**Venus** (♀) is by nature cold and moist, but so tempered that, especially at its morning rising, it pours out a generative dew upon mortals, by which not only living creatures are adapted for manifold generation, but green things are also disposed toward various conceptions. Its significance is all beauty and every charm, ornate clothing, dress worked with threads of gold or silver, or honored with the purple of Tyrian murex <note>a highly prized and expensive purple dye made from sea snails in antiquity</note>. Then baths, dyes, and scented balsams; grace, jesting, the Muses <note>the goddesses of the arts</note>, and the rich applause in a choir. It also signifies primarily beautiful maidens and their playful betrothals, loves, elegies, lovers' quarrels, deceits, complaints, and then peace and the renewal of love. It also signifies banquets, temptations, and sweet treats or desserts <note>original: "tragemata, siue bellaria"</note>, and whatever is sweet and pleasurable in taste; both lawful and unlawful sexual unions, debauchery, incest, adultery, and other things of that kind. It also signifies the mutual affection of men, piety, faith, trust, and the highest humanity toward all. From the condition of the body, however, it signifies plumpness rather than leanness, but adorned with a charming grace—yet weak and often fatigued by ill health. Among the arts, it signifies painting, the trade of perfumes, and whatever is practiced with wonderful and subtle skill. But of the body parts, together with Mars (♂), it governs the nostrils.

Mercury (☿)
Parts of the body.

**Mercury** (☿) is indeed of a mixed nature, easily adhering with a promiscuous agreement of mixture to that planet with which it is mixed or joined by some aspect; however, it is by nature rather cold and dry. Its significance is childhood, intellect, reason, eloquence, pleasant deception, and playful theft. Then logical arguments, syllogisms, sophisms <note>original: "enthymemata, syllogismi, sophismata"; technical terms for types of philosophical reasoning</note>, poetry, music, and the investigation of the stars and the whole of Mathematics <note>original: "Matheseos"; in this context, the term encompasses both math and the "divine science" of astrology</note>. It signifies faithful men, prophets, soothsayers, augurs, and those honored with the divine interpretation of the fates; also merchants, ambassadors, and orators, but those who often deceive with fraudulent cunning. It also signifies the nightly study <note>original: "lucubrationem"</note> of any very sharp art, the discovery of hidden and secret things, smooth speech, sound counsel, delights, pleasures, ambitions, profits, and public taxes—and whatever is sought for the sake of glory rather than utility. Then simulated reconciliation, a doubtful and entangled affection, yet a mild compassion of mind, an ungrateful modulation of the voice; but in every sharp workmanship of any art, it signifies a skillful hand and a most adaptable intellect, both for the wonderful discovery of hidden things and for their very swift completion. Of the body parts, it governs the mouth, the tongue, and the hands which aid human speech.

It signifies light merchants of things, especially of watery goods, business...

## THE LORDS OF THE TRIPLICITIES AND THEIR QUALITIES. CHAPTER XI.

Now, for you, Mavortius <note>original: "Mauorti". Referring to Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman consul and statesman to whom the author, Firmicus Maternus, dedicated this work.</note>, our glory, we shall organize the lords of the triplicities <term>triplicities: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term>, so that nothing regarding the condition or eminence of these stars might seem to be omitted. Since the twelve signs represent four natures distributed through three intervals, it follows that three signs share each nature. For since the figure of an equilateral triangle is equal and consistent within itself and marks three boundaries of the circle—namely Aries (♈), Leo (♌), and Sagittarius (♐)—it divides the twelve parts into four triplicities. From this kinship of nature, we may add something to the dignity of the stars. Divine and masculine stars shall preside over the diurnal <note>pertaining to the day</note> and masculine triplicities, while nocturnal and feminine stars preside over the nocturnal and feminine ones, because they possess greater evidence of harmony in that classification.

<margin>
The Fiery Triplicities.
</margin>
Of the **Fiery Triplicity**—that is, Aries (♈), Leo (♌), and Sagittarius (♐), which is diurnal, masculine, and Northern—the first of the lords is the Sun (☉) by day, and the second is Jupiter (♃) by night; however, Saturn (♄) is the participant in both.

<margin>
The Earthly.
</margin>
Of the **Earthly Triplicity**—that is, Taurus (♉), Virgo (♍), and Capricorn (♑), which is nocturnal, feminine, and Southern—the first of the lords is Venus (♀) by day, the second is the Moon (☽), and by night it is the reverse; however, Mars (♂) is the participant in both.

<margin>
The Airy.
</margin>
Of the **Airy Triplicity**—that is, Gemini (♊), Libra (♎), and Aquarius (♒), which is diurnal, masculine, and Eastern—the first of the lords is Saturn (♄) by day, the second is Mercury (☿), and by night it is the reverse; however, Jupiter (♃) is the participant in both.

<margin>
The Watery.
</margin>
Finally, of the **Watery Triplicity**—that is, Cancer (♋), Scorpio (♏), and Pisces (♓), which is nocturnal, feminine, and Western—the first of the lords is Venus (♀) by day, the second is Mars (♂), and by night it is the reverse; however, the Moon (☽) is the participant in both. These are all the powers of the stars, which, if you compare them well after careful consideration, you will be able to unravel through no obscure divination what they have decreed in each birth-chart <term>genitura: a birth chart or horoscope</term> by their fatal decree.

### THE NATURE, FORMS, AND QUALITIES OF THE SIGNS. CHAPTER XII.

We have spoken of the limits and kinds of the signs; now we must explain their nature, forms, qualities, subjects, and risings <term>risings: originally "anaphoris," referring to how the signs appear over the horizon</term>, so that we may impart the complete knowledge of this art to you through the clearest possible expositions.

<margin>The nature and quality of Aries.</margin>
Aries (♈) is a masculine sign in the heavens, equinoctial, royal, fiery, strong, and truthful. It is a four-footed sign, semi-corporeal <note>meaning it has two aspects or parts to its form</note>, with weak eyes, and is wandering. It is called *krios* <note>original: "κρὶος"</note> by the Greeks. It is untamed, harmonious, impure, and lustful; it is the house of Mars (♂) and the setting <note>detriment</note> of Venus (♀). The exaltation of the Sun (☉) is around the 19th degree, while the fall of Saturn (♄) is around the 20th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by the Sun (☉) by day and by Jupiter (♃) by night. It is called equinoctial because, in this sign, the Sun balances the hours of night and day with equal moderation; for this reason, it is called the "equinoctial tropic" <note>original: "τροπικὸν ἰσημερινὸν"</note> by the Greeks. For when the Sun is in Aries, it balances the diurnal and nocturnal hours equally, so that the day <margin>The Ram.</margin> has twelve hours and the night has twelve. The Greeks call it *krios* <note>meaning Ram</note> because when the Sun is within it, it "judges" between day and night—the word for "to judge" being *krinein* <note>original: "κρὶνειν"</note>—and because, being placed between winter and summer in that sign, the Sun is itself judged again. It is called "tropic" <note>from the Greek word for "turning"</note> because the Sun, positioned in that sign, creates the spring season; for spring begins when <margin>The beginning of spring.</margin> the Sun enters the first degree of that sign. It is called fiery because whoever has it in the Ascendant of their birth chart will lean toward a fiery and choleric nature. This sign is situated in the North wind.

<margin>Taurus (♉)</margin>
Taurus (♉) is a feminine sign in the heavens, Northern, earthy, melancholic, fixed, and single-bodied. It is four-footed, domestic, faulty, productive of few children, lustful, and has a diminished voice. It flourishes in the South; it is oblique, heavy, focused on a single business, uneven, irrational, easy-going, and associated with maimed limbs. It is the house of Venus (♀) and the setting of Mars (♂). The exaltation of the Moon (☽) is around the 3rd degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and the Moon (☽) by night. This sign is situated in the South wind. It signifies a bitter taste, the colors green and white, four-footed animals, those with cloven hooves, the fifth climate <note>a geographical zone</note>, cultivated lands, average men, and all ailments of the neck.

<margin>Gemini (♊)</margin>
Gemini (♊) is a masculine sign in the heavens, common, two-bodied, two-footed, rational, and has a beautiful voice. It is winged, sterile, flourishes in the West, and is midway between light and heavy. It is focused on two businesses, even, Northern, acquiring, and emptying. It is the house of Mercury (☿) and the setting of Jupiter (♃). Its triplicity is ruled by Saturn (♄) by day and Mercury (☿) by night. This sign is situated in the East wind. It also signifies a sweet taste, a mixed and temperate color, rational animals, monkeys, and all songbirds. It governs the sixth climate, as well as all high and sunny places where bird-catching is especially practiced. It also signifies nobles, astronomers, and all troublesome ailments of the shoulders.

<margin>Cancer (♋)</margin>
Cancer (♋) is a feminine sign in the heavens, movable, semi-corporeal, irrational, many-footed, and wild. It is without voice, faulty, productive of many children, and nocturnal. It flourishes in the North and is watery, phlegmatic, focused on a single business, and midway between light and heavy. It is uneven, Northern, solstitial, lowly, deceitful, and weak. It is the house of the Moon (☽) and the setting of Saturn (♄). The exaltation of Jupiter (♃) is around the 15th degree, and the fall of Mars (♂) is around the 28th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and Mars (♂) by night. This sign is situated in the Southwest wind. It also signifies a sharp and salty taste, the colors white and pale, aquatic animals, and serpents. It governs the seventh climate, stagnant or flowing waters, average men, and all ailments of the heart and diaphragm.

<margin>Leo (♌)</margin>
Leo (♌) is a masculine sign in the heavens, fixed, single-bodied, four-footed, and irrational. It is midway between domestic and wild, lustful, and flourishes in the East. It is fiery, choleric, has a moderate voice, is light, focused on a single business, even, diurnal, Northern, direct, truthful, and strong. It is the house of the Sun (☉) and the setting of Saturn (♄). Its triplicity is ruled by the Sun (☉) by day and Jupiter (♃) by night. This sign is situated in the North wind. It also signifies a bitter and sharp taste, a saffron color leaning toward redness, wild and fierce animals, the fifth climate, and all places of dignity and laborious ascents, such as camps, government buildings, and palaces. It signifies princes, leaders, powerful and wealthy men, and all ailments of the chest and stomach.

♍ ♍ Virgo is a feminine sign in the heavens, common <note>also called "mutable," representing the end of a season</note>, bicorporeal <note>double-bodied</note>, rational, two-footed, of a beautiful voice, winged, sterile, flourishing in the South, heavy, of two businesses <note>referring to dual interests or occupations</note>, earthy, melancholic, odd-numbered, northern, honest, beautiful, generous, easy, direct, nocturnal, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Mercury (☿), the setting <note>detriment</note> of Jupiter (♃); the exaltation of Mercury (☿) is around the fifteenth degree, and the fall of Venus (♀) is around the twenty-seventh degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and by the Moon (☽) by night. This sign is placed in the Southern wind. It also signifies a styptic <note>astringent or mouth-puckering</note> taste; the colors white, purple, and *leucotheum* <note>a pale or clear white</note>; rational animals and birds; the fifth climate; and all places that are cultivated and flowering. It represents wise and industrious men, as well as jesters, and all ailments and sufferings of the belly.

♎ ♎ Libra is a masculine sign in the heavens, mobile <note>also called "cardinal," marking the start of a season</note>, semi-corporeal, rational, domestic, two-footed, of a beautiful voice, of few children, flourishing in the West, medium between light and heavy, airy, sanguine, of one business, even-numbered, Southern, equinoctial, direct, diurnal, strong, and truthful. It is the house of Venus (♀), the setting <note>detriment</note> of Saturn (♄); the exaltation of Saturn (♄) is around the 20th degree, and the fall of the Sun (☉) is around the 19th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Saturn (♄) by day and by Mercury (☿) by night. This sign is placed in the East wind <note>original: "Subsolano"</note>. It also signifies a sweet taste; the colors green and *leucotheum*; flying animals, especially large ones; the fifth climate; and all places on the tops of mountains, or those that are sown and cultivated. It also represents merchants, judges, diviners, and obedient men, as well as all ailments of the kidneys and vertebrae.

♏ ♏ Scorpio is a feminine sign in the heavens, fixed, single-bodied, irrational, wild, many-footed, of many children, lacking a voice, flourishing in the North, watery, phlegmatic, of one business, odd-numbered, Southern, direct, nocturnal, heavy, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Mars (♂), the setting <note>detriment</note> of Venus (♀); the fall of the Moon (☽) is around the third degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and by Mars (♂) by night. This sign is placed in the Southwest wind <note>original: "Aphrico"</note>. It also signifies a salty <note>original: "falsum," often meaning salty in this context</note> and insipid taste; the colors green, red, and *leucotheum*; reptilian and poisonous animals, as well as marine and aquatic ones; the third climate; places that are sometimes garden-like and cultivated, but sometimes foul and deserted. It represents doctors (though some are fakes and unlearned) and mediocre men, as well as all ailments of the groin.

♐ ♐ Sagittarius is a masculine sign in the heavens, common, bicorporeal—of which the first part is rational and the other irrational—of a beautiful voice, four-footed, lustful, of few children, flourishing in the East, though its second part has a diminished voice; it is light, fiery, choleric, strong, of two businesses, even-numbered, Southern, direct, diurnal, truthful, partly domestic and partly wild. It is the house of Jupiter (♃), the setting <note>detriment</note> of Mercury (☿). Its triplicity is ruled by the Sun (☉) by day and by Jupiter (♃) by night. This sign is placed in the North wind <note>original: "Aquilone"</note>. It also signifies a bitter taste; the color red or saffron; rational animals, horses, birds, and serpents; the second climate; all well-watered places, mountains, and gardens, and whatever contains some pleasantness in itself. Finally, it represents judges, worshipers of God, merciful men, interpreters of dreams, prophets, and all ailments of the thighs.

♑ ♑ Capricorn is a feminine sign in the heavens, mobile, semi-corporeal, irrational, four-footed, domestic, vicious, of few children, chaste, of diminished voice, oblique <note>referring to its rising at an angle to the equator</note>, earthy, melancholic, flourishing in the South, heavy, of one business, odd-numbered, Southern, solstitial, easy, nocturnal, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Saturn (♄), the setting <note>detriment</note> of the Moon (☽); the exaltation of Mars (♂) is around the 28th degree, and the fall of Jupiter (♃) is around the 15th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and by the Moon (☽) by night. This sign is placed in the Southern wind. It also signifies a bitter and styptic taste; the color black or *leucotheum*; four-footed animals and some aquatic ones; the first climate; garden-like and well-watered places, springs, and rivers, as well as pastures, animal stalls, and the dwellings of obscure people. It represents rude and lowly men, yet some of profound character and melancholics, as well as all ailments and sufferings of the knees.

♒ ♒ Aquarius is a masculine sign in the heavens, fixed, single-bodied, rational, two-footed, of a beautiful voice, of few children, flourishing in the West, medium between light and heavy, even-numbered, of one business, Southern, oblique, diurnal, truthful, strong, airy, and sanguine.

### THE RISING OF THE SIGNS ACCORDING TO DIFFERENT
### CLIMATES. CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>First and second climate</margin>
Having explained the types and forms of the signs, and having described their nature with diligent reasoning as it was handed down to us by the most learned teachings of the Greeks, we ought to show in the following section in what year <note>original: "quoto anno"; though "year" is written, this refers to a technical unit of time used in astrological timing or degrees of ascension</note> each sign rises in a birth chart. We shall demonstrate the use of this through a brief definition. They rise at various times and days, and according to the different climates <note>latitudes or geographical zones</note>. Therefore, we show by this calculation which signs rise in which climates and at what time.

In the first climate, which is that of Ethiopia, and in the second climate, which is that of Babylon, and in all other regions that lie beneath these climates, the signs rise in this course of time: Aries (♈) rises in the 20th year, Taurus (♉) in the 24th, Gemini (♊) in the 28th, Cancer (♋) in the 32nd, Leo (♌) in the 36th, Virgo (♍) in the 40th, Libra (♎) likewise in the 40th, Scorpio (♏) in the 36th, Sagittarius (♐) in the 32nd, Capricorn (♑) in the 28th, Aquarius (♒) in the 24th, and Pisces (♓) likewise in the 20th year.

<margin>Third climate.</margin>
In the climate that passes through Alexandria and the other regions that lie beneath this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the 19th year, Taurus (♉) in the 23rd, Gemini (♊) in the 27th, Cancer (♋) in the 32nd, Leo (♌) in the 36th, Virgo (♍) in the 40th, Libra (♎) in the 40th, Scorpio (♏) in the 36th, Sagittarius (♐) in the 32nd, Capricorn (♑) in the 27th, Aquarius (♒) in the 23rd, and Pisces (♓) likewise in the 19th year.

<margin>Fourth climate.</margin>
In the climate of Athens and the other regions that lie beneath this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the 18th year, Taurus (♉) in the 23rd, Gemini (♊) in the 27th, Cancer (♋) in the 32nd, Leo (♌) in the 36th, Virgo (♍) in the 41st, Libra (♎) in the 41st, Scorpio (♏) in the 36th, Sagittarius (♐) in the 32nd, Capricorn (♑) in the 27th, Aquarius (♒) in the 23rd, and Pisces (♓) likewise in the 18th year.

<margin>Fifth climate.</margin>
In the climate of the City <note>Rome</note> and the golden regions that lie beneath this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the 17th year, Taurus (♉) in the 22nd, Gemini (♊) in the 27th, Cancer (♋) in the 32nd, Leo (♌) in the 37th, Virgo (♍) in the 42nd, Libra (♎) likewise in the 42nd, Scorpio (♏) in the 37th, Sagittarius (♐) in the 32nd, Capricorn (♑) in the 27th, Aquarius (♒) in the 22nd, and Pisces (♓) in the 17th.

<margin>Sixth climate.</margin>
In the climate of the Hellespont and the other regions that lie beneath this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the 16th year, Taurus (♉) in the 22nd, Gemini (♊) in the 27th, Cancer (♋) in the 32nd, Leo (♌) in the 37th, Virgo (♍) in the 42nd, Libra (♎) likewise in the 42nd, Scorpio (♏) in the 37th, Sagittarius (♐) in the 32nd, Capricorn (♑) in the 27th, Aquarius (♒) in the 22nd, and Pisces (♓) in the 16th year.

<margin>Seventh climate.</margin>
In the climate of the North and the other regions that lie beneath this climate, Aries (♈) rises in year 15, Taurus (♉) in 21, Gemini (♊) in 29, Cancer (♋) in 32, Leo (♌) in 37, Virgo (♍) in 41, Libra (♎) likewise in 41, Scorpio (♏) in 31, Sagittarius (♐) in 33, Capricorn (♑) in 27, Aquarius (♒) in 21, and Pisces (♓) likewise in the 15th year. These are the risings of the signs, by which the individual stars are moved toward their own efficacy.

### THE SUBJECTION OF THE SIGNS TO THE WINDS.
### CHAPTER XIV.

It is also appropriate for us to know which signs are subject to which winds; for this knowledge is especially necessary in the *apotelesmata* <note>the study of astrological effects or predictions; original: "apotelefmatis"</note>. Subject to the North wind (*Aquilo*) are the signs Aries (♈), Leo (♌), and Sagittarius (♐). To the South wind (*Auster*) are Taurus (♉), Virgo (♍), and Capricorn (♑). To the East wind (*Apeliotes*, which we call *Subsolanus*) are Gemini (♊), Libra (♎), and Aquarius (♒). To the Southwest wind (*Aphricus*, which is called *Lips* <note>original: "λίψ"</note> by the Greeks) are Cancer (♋), Scorpio (♏), and Pisces (♓).

### Twelfth-parts. CHAPTER XV.

Now I shall briefly show the method by which you may seek out the twelfth-parts <note>original: "duodecatemoria"; these are sub-divisions of a zodiac sign where each 30-degree sign is divided into twelve 2.5-degree sections.</note>. For some believe they can find the entire substance of a birth-chart <note>original: "genituræ"</note> through these, and they suggest that whatever is hidden in the celestial decree can be brought forth from the twelfth-parts. What these twelfth-parts actually are is taught by this example: whichever star’s twelfth-part you wish to find, multiply its degree by twelve; then, divide the total and assign them to the individual signs, beginning from the sign in which that star is located. Wherever the final number falls, that sign will show you the location of the twelfth-part.

But so that you may understand more clearly, we shall also give an example of this matter. Suppose the **Sun** <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> is in **Aries** <note>original symbol: $\Upsilon$</note> at 5 degrees and 5 minutes. Twelve times 5 degrees makes 60 degrees. Likewise, twelve times 5 minutes similarly makes 60 minutes, and these 60 minutes make 1 degree. Through this, the total becomes 61 degrees. From these, give 30 to **Aries** (where we said the **Sun** was), and 30 to **Taurus** <note>original symbol: ♉</note>; the **Sun's** twelfth-part is found to be in the 1st degree of **Gemini** <note>original symbol: ♊</note>. 

Therefore, look to see that the full **Moon** <note>original symbol: $\mathbb{D}$</note> does not send its twelfth-part into the terms <note>original: "fines"; specific segments of a sign ruled by a planet</note> of **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> during the day, nor its minutes (that is, when she is waning) into the terms of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>; nor should **Mars** be setting, nor **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> in a sign of **Mars**, nor **Mars** in a sign of **Venus**. Consider these positions by terms, decans <note>ten-degree sub-divisions of a sign</note>, and conditions <note>the sect or state of the planet</note>, to see whether they receive the power to help or to harm.

<margin>The wonderful kindness of the star of Jupiter.</margin>
For the kindness of **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> fails when its benevolence is hindered by the weakness of the sign, the degrees, the decan, or a change in its condition. But the malice of **Saturn** grows more strongly when it receives a greater power for harm, provoked by the quality of its place, the terms, the decan, the sign, or the condition of all these together. The other stars act in a similar way. One thing, however, must be known: although the star of **Jupiter** is benevolent, it cannot resist the attack of **Mars** and **Saturn** alone if they constrain it with violent radiation <note>aspects or beams of light cast from one planet to another</note>. 

Indeed, humans would be immortal if the kindness of **Jupiter** were never overcome in their birth-charts. But because the Creator God <note>original: "artifex deus"</note> made man in such a way that his substance would dissolve after a certain span of life had passed, it was necessary that—while **Jupiter** (through whom life and a saving protection are granted to men) is held back—the malicious and destructive power of the baleful stars should remain with increased malice to extinguish the human being. Thus, attacked by malevolent radiations, the framework of the body is dissolved.

->THINGS TO BE CONSIDERED REGARDING<-
->THE HOROSCOPE. CHAPTER XVI.<-

<margin>n</margin>
Now let our attention be turned to the explanation of the pivots <note>original: "cardines"; the four most important points in a chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli</note> and all the places. For when all these have been diligently found by us, we must next find the individual decrees of a person, through which the entire substance of their life is divided. For now, we shall speak broadly <note>original: "platice"; looking at whole signs rather than specific degrees</note>; a little later, when we come to the books on astrological effects <note>original: "apotelesmatum"</note>, we shall show with degree-precision <note>original: "partiliter"</note> the method by which individual places can be gathered through secret inquiries. For he who is being instructed must first be taught broadly, so that once he is composed and shaped by these clearer and lighter matters, he may then follow the more secret parts of the birth-chart with more confidence. 

When the place itself has been found by its specific degree, one must consider what sort of place it is, in what sign, in whose terms it lies, and which stars are there, so as to see what testimony they provide. This must also be considered most carefully: the ruler of the sign of that place—where is he positioned? In what sign or in what terms is he? This matter must be sought out most diligently: whether he is adorned by the testimonies of benevolent stars, or whether he is struck by the attack of malevolent ones. Now let us return to the broad definition of the places, so that we may explain the order of the pivots and the other places.

### THE PIVOTS AND THEIR SUCCESSORS. CHAPTER XVII.

One must read carefully concerning the eight places <note>The "Octotopos" or eight-house system was an older tradition before the twelve-house system became standard</note>; the definition of the eight places is therefore as follows. The "broad" place of life is in that sign in which the **Horoscope** <note>the Ascendant, or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is established. 
The place of money or hope is in the second sign from the **Horoscope**. 
The sign of siblings is in the third. 
The sign of parents is in the fourth. 
The sign of children is in the fifth. 
The sign of health is in the sixth. 
The sign of the spouse is in the seventh. 
The sign of death is in the eighth. 
We have shown all these starting from the **Horoscope** by this definition of names: life, hope, siblings, parents, children, health, spouse, death.

But let it be enough to have spoken of these things broadly, as we said above, for the sake of providing the basic instructions for a student. Later, indeed, we shall take care to explain how these places are shown by a precise definition of their parts.
<margin>What is said of men is to be understood for women.</margin>
Truly, you ought to know this: that those things which we say regarding the birth charts <note>original: "genituris"</note> of men, these same things also operate in the birth charts of women—knowing this, however, that the star **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> indicates the Wife, and the star **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> indicates the Husband.

## THE PIVOTS OF THE BIRTH CHART. CHAPTER XVIII.

<margin>Four pivots.</margin>
In birth charts there are four pivots <note>original: "cardines," literally the hinges or poles upon which the chart turns</note>: the Rising, the Setting, the Midheaven (MC), and the Bottom of the Midheaven (IMC). These places are usually called by these names by the Greeks: *Anatole*, *Dusis*, *Mesourania*, and *Hypogeion*.
<margin>The Rising.</margin>
The Rising <note>original: "Ortus"</note> is the part of the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopus"</note> which, at the time of every birth, first emerges from the eastern region and is drawn out through the next 30 degrees; this is called *Anatole* <note>original: ἀνατολή</note> by the Greeks.
<margin>The Setting.</margin>
The Setting <note>original: "Occasus"</note> is that part of the sky situated exactly opposite the Ascendant in the seventh place. It is called the "Western Diameter" <note>original: Διάμετρον Δυτικόν</note> by the Greeks. So that you may understand this more easily: count 180 degrees from the degree of the Ascendant through the other signs, and in whatever sign the 181st degree is found, the Setting of the birth chart is established in that sign or degree.
<margin>Midheaven (MC).</margin>
The Midheaven <note>original: "Medium Coelum"</note> is the tenth sign from the Ascendant, though sometimes the Midheaven is also found precisely in the eleventh sign from the Ascendant. So that you may understand this more clearly: count 170 degrees <note>note: the Latin text "clxx" (170) is likely a printer's error for "cclxx" (270), which would correctly lead to the 271st degree mentioned next</note> from the degree of the Ascendant through the signs that follow; in whatever sign the 271st degree is found, this has obtained the Midheaven, which is called *Mesourania* <note>original: μεσουράνια</note> by the Greeks.
<margin>Lower Midheaven (IMC).</margin>
The Bottom of the Midheaven <note>original: "Imum Coelum"</note>, which is called *Hypogeion* <note>original: ὑπόγειον</note> by the Greeks, is established in the fourth place from the Ascendant. To understand this easily: count 90 degrees in order from the degree of the Ascendant, and where the 91st degree falls, there the place of the IMC is positioned. These are the four pivots of birth charts and decrees, which we must always gather with careful reasoning so that we may explain the entire substance of fate with the truest pronouncements.

## THE FOUR SECONDARY PLACES. CHAPTER XIX.

After these four pivots—that is, after the Rising, Setting, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven—there are four other places in birth charts which have the next and secondary power: these are the Goddess, the God, Good Fortune, and the Good Spirit. To this day, they are named by the Greeks as *Thea*, *Theos*, *Agathe Tyche*, and *Agathodaimon*. The "Goddess" is the third place from the Ascendant—that is, the third sign from the Ascendant; this place, as we said, is called *Thea* <note>original: θεὰ</note> by the Greeks. The "God" is that sign which is established directly opposite this sign on the diameter—that is, the ninth sign from the Ascendant; this place is called *Theos* <note>original: θεὸς</note> by the Greeks. "Good Fortune" is located in the fifth sign from the Ascendant, a place called *Agathe Tyche* <note>original: ἀγαθὴ τύχη</note> by the Greeks. The "Good Spirit" is located on the diameter of this sign—that is, in the eleventh place from the Ascendant; this place is called *Agathodaimon* <note>original: ἀγαθοδαίμων</note> by the Greeks.

## THE SLUGGISH AND CAST-DOWN PLACES OF THE FIGURE. CHAPTER XX.

The remaining four places are said to be sluggish and "cast-down" <note>original: "deiecta," meaning weakened or unlucky</note> because they are joined in no fellowship with the Ascendant. Of these four remaining places, the first is that which is established in the second sign from the Ascendant; this place is called the "Lower Gate" <note>original: "inferna porta"</note> or *Anaphora* <note>original: ἀναφορὰ, meaning "rising up"</note>. Whatever place is on the diameter of this sign—that is, in the eighth sign from the Ascendant—is called *Epikataphora* <note>original: ἐπικαταφορὰ, meaning "falling down"</note> or the "Upper Gate." The very last places are those of Bad Fortune and the Bad Spirit. "Bad Fortune" is established in the sixth sign from the Ascendant. The "Bad Spirit" is placed in the twelfth sign from the Ascendant. The Greeks call Bad Fortune *Kake Tyche* <note>original: κακὴν τύχην</note>, while the "Bad Spirit"—that is, the place in the twelfth sign from the Ascendant—they call *Kakodaimon* <note>original: κακοδαίμονα</note>.

## THE ORDER OF THE PLACES IN THE FIGURE. CHAPTER XXI.

Now we ought to know which of these twelve places take precedence and which follow—that is, which places are first and which are second—so that we can gather everything with careful reasoning. The Ascendant precedes the Setting; the Midheaven is placed before the Lower Midheaven; the 11th place (the Good Spirit) is preferred to Good Fortune (the 5th); the 9th (the God) is preferred to the 3rd place...

It provides the Greek terminology and mathematical methods for locating these points relative to the Ascendant.</summary>

place—that is, the **descent** <note>original: ἐπικαταφορὰ (*epikataphora*), referring to the 8th house falling away from the descendant pivot</note> is placed before it—that is, the 8th place from the Ascendant; the **rising up** <note>original: *anaphorae*, the 2nd house which "rises up" after the Ascendant</note> is placed before **bad fortune** <note>original: *mala fortuna*, the 6th house</note>; and the **bad spirit** <note>original: *malo dæmoni*, the 12th house</note> is placed before the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*</note>. All these things must be known so that when we come to the **astrological judgments** <note>original: *apotelefmata*</note>, by mixing and tempering them all together, we may confirm our opinions with the faithful logic of truth.

## THE POWERS OF THE TWELVE PLACES. CHAPTER XXII.

<margin>First place</margin> <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'N' featuring a seated figure in a landscape with classical architecture in the background.</image-desc>Now we must explain the significations of the twelve places individually, beginning from the Ascendant, so that once all have been set out in order, the obscurity of confusion may be illuminated and the things that follow may be more clearly understood.
The first place is that part in which the Ascendant is established; in this place, the life and spirit of humans are contained, and from this place the foundations of the entire **birth chart** <note>original: *genitura*</note> are known. This place extends its powers from that part where the Ascendant is found through the remaining 30 degrees. It is, moreover, the first pivot and the framework and substance of the entire birth chart, which provides the entrance for the rest.

<margin>II</margin> The second place from the Ascendant is established in the second sign; it takes its beginning from the 30th degree of the Ascendant and extends its powers through the remaining 30 degrees. From this sign, the increases of hope and possession are known. It is, however, a **lazy place** <note>original: *piger locus*; ancient astrologers called houses "lazy" or "idle" if they did not form a major geometric aspect to the Ascendant, making them less effective</note> and alienated from the Ascendant; for this reason, it is also called **Hell’s Gate** <note>original: *inferna porta*</note>, because it is joined to the Ascendant by no radiation, nor is it mixed with any aspect.

<margin>III</margin> The third place is that which is established in the third sign from the Ascendant, which, taking its beginning from the 60th degree of the Ascendant, ends at the 90th. From this place, we shall speak of all things concerning brothers and friends. The name for this place is **Goddess** <note>original: *dea*</note>. Furthermore, this is the first place of travel <note>original: *peregrinantis*</note>; it is joined to the Ascendant by a slender fellowship, for it is seen to look back at the Ascendant from a **sextile** <note>original: *hexagono*</note> aspect.

<margin>IIII</margin> The fourth place from the Ascendant—that is, the **Bottom of the Sky** <note>original: *imum cœlum* or IC</note>—is established in the fourth sign from the Ascendant, whose beginning proceeds from the 90th degree and reaches to the 120th. This place shows us parents, inheritance, substance, foundations, movable goods, and whatever pertains to hidden or stored-away ancestral wealth. This is a pivot of the birth chart; it is called the "Bottom of the Sky" because it is established in **opposition** <note>original: *diametro*</note> to the **Midheaven** <note>original: M C, *Medium Coeli*</note>. But this place is joined to the Ascendant by the greatest fellowship, because it looks back from the **square** <note>original: *quadrato*</note> of the Ascendant and is seen by a square aspect from the Ascendant, as is clear to one who investigates.

<margin>V</margin> The fifth place from the Ascendant is established in the fifth sign from the Ascendant, because, taking its beginning from the 120th degree of the Ascendant, it extends to the 150th degree. From this place, the number of children and the quality of the family line are found. It is called **Good Fortune** <note>original: *bona fortuna*</note>, because it is the place of **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>. But this place also is joined with the Ascendant by the greatest fellowship, and sometimes a part of the Midheaven is established in the opposition of this sign; for this reason, it is associated with the Ascendant by the greatest connection, because it is seen from a **trine** <note>original: *trigono*</note> aspect from the Ascendant and receives its rays.

<margin>VI</margin> The sixth place is established in the sixth sign from the Ascendant, which, taking its beginning from the 150th degree of the Ascendant, extends to the 180th. In this sign we shall find the cause of defects and health; the place is called **Bad Fortune** <note>original: *mala fortuna*</note> for this reason: it is the place of **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>. This place is also "lazy," because it is joined by no fellowship with the Ascendant; but sometimes the malice of the place itself is relieved if a star is located in that place and other stars found in the tenth place from the Ascendant (the Midheaven) are joined to it by a prosperous radiation which helps it.

<margin>VII</margin> The seventh place is established in the seventh sign from the Ascendant, because, having proceeded from the 180th degree, it extends to the 210th and ends there. Its beginning is established at the 180th degree. In this place is another pivot of the birth chart; it is called the **Setting** <note>original: *occasus*</note> by us, but by the Greeks, as we said above, it is called **Dusis** <note>original: Δύσις</note>, which is the pivot positioned opposite the pivot of the Ascendant. From this place, let us seek the quality and quantity of marriages. This place is joined to the Ascendant by a violent fellowship, and is seen from the Ascendant in **opposition** <note>original: *diametro*</note>.

<margin>VIII</margin> The eighth place is established in the 8th sign from the Ascendant, because, having proceeded from the 210th degree from the Ascendant, it extends to the 240th degree and ends there. This place is called the **descent** <note>original: ἐπικαταφορὰ, *epikataphora*</note>. It is a "lazy" place because it is not joined to the Ascendant by any fellowship. From this place, the quality of death is found. It is fitting for us to know, however, that no star rejoices in this place except only the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, but only in nocturnal birth charts; for if in this place, in a nocturnal birth chart, a waxing Moon is found, and she is so placed without fellowship or radiation of malevolent stars, and **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> looks upon her from a sextile or trine in the house...

...his own house, or in the house of Venus ♀, or in the house of Mercury ☿, or in the house of Jupiter ♃, or in the bounds <term>bounds: also known as 'terms' (fines), these are specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term> of the aforementioned stars, it decrees the greatest means, wealth beyond measure, magnificent glory of power, and promises clear honors of nobility.

The **ninth place** is located in the 9th sign from the Ascendant; its measure begins at 240 degrees and extends to 270 degrees. It is the place of the day and of the Sun ☉ <note>In ancient astrology, the 9th house was specifically associated with the Sun and called "God"</note>. In this place, we find the sects of men; it concerns religions and travels abroad <note>original: *peregrinationibus*</note>. This place is joined with the Ascendant by a very great radiation, for it is seen from the Ascendant in a trine aspect <term>trine: a harmonious 120-degree angle</term> and receives its rays.

The **tenth place** is located in the 10th sign from the Ascendant, taking its beginning at 270 degrees and extending to 300, where it ends. This place is principal, and more sublime in power than all the cardines <term>cardines: the 'pivots' or four most powerful angles of a chart</term>. This place is called by us the **Midheaven** <note>original: *MC* or *Medium Coeli*</note>, but by the Greeks the *mesouranema* <note>original: μεσουράνημα</note>, for it is situated in the middle part of the entire world. In this place, we find life, spirit, all actions, fatherland, domicile, and one's entire manner of living, as well as the arts and whatever is granted to us through the benefit of the arts. From this place, we perceive the vices of the mind by an easy method; the power of this place is joined in fellowship with the Ascendant, because it is seen from the Ascendant in a square aspect <term>square: a 90-degree angle, often representing visible action or challenge</term>.

The **eleventh place** is located in the 11th sign from the Ascendant, starting at 300 degrees and extending to 330. We call this place the **Good Spirit** <note>original: *bonus daemon* or *bonus genius*</note>, but the Greeks call it the *agathos daimon* <note>original: ἀγαθὸς δαίμων</note>. In this place, the Midheaven degree is frequently found; it is the place of Jupiter ♃, and it is joined to the Ascendant in no small fellowship, for it sees the Ascendant in a sextile aspect <term>sextile: a 60-degree angle, called a 'hexagon' in the original Latin</term> and is seen by it, receiving its rays.

The **twelfth place** is located in the 12th sign from the Ascendant, starting at 330 degrees and extending to 360. This place is called the *kakodaimon* <note>original: κακοδαίμων</note> by the Greeks, but by us the **Bad Spirit** <note>original: *malus daemon*</note>. From this place, the quality of enemies and the condition of slaves are shown to us by clear indication; we also find vices and illnesses in this place. Furthermore, this is a "lazy" place <note>original: *piger*, meaning it cannot 'see' the Ascendant and thus lacks its vitalizing influence</note>, because it is joined in no fellowship with the Ascendant. It is the place of Saturn ♄. Indeed, Saturn shows the father in both a man’s and a woman’s birth chart; the Moon ☽ shows the mother, Venus ♀ the wife, and Mars ♂ the husband.

## THE NAMES AND EFFECTS OF THE TWELVE PLACES. CHAPTER XXIII.
<note>original title: *Locorum XII Nomina Apotelesmataque*</note>

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'N' featuring a mythological scene within a square border.</image-desc>

Now that we have described the qualities, names, and substance of the 12 places, we ought to briefly show these same places by their signification. Let the Ascendant be our beginning, whose starting point the other places follow. It is fitting that these places be called by these names: **Life, Hope (or Brothers), Parents, Children, Health, Spouse, Death, Religion (or God), Midheaven, Good Spirit, and Bad Spirit.** Through these names and through these places, the substance of the entire birth chart <note>original: *genitura*</note> is sought. Once you have inspected these diligently, conceived them in your mind, and joined everything in that fellowship, observe which stars possess those places, and also diligently inspect the conditions of the day-stars and night-stars.

<margin>Beneficent stars</margin> But also consider what kind of testimony the **beneficent stars** <note>original: *stellæ beneuolæ*, usually Jupiter and Venus</note> provide in each place, and which places the **malefic stars** <note>original: *maleuolæ*</note> strike with their radiation. For whatever place the beneficent stars look upon—whether they are located in that same place, or in a trine or sextile aspect—all those things we said should be sought after will turn out happily.

<margin>Malefic stars</margin> If, however, without the testimony of the beneficent stars, only the malefic stars are either located there or strike these same places from a square or diameter <term>diameter: an opposition aspect of 180 degrees</term>, then according to the quality of each place, everything we touched upon in the earlier part of our discourse... is weighed down by frequent calamities of misfortune.

<margin>Mixed stars</margin> If both beneficent and malefic stars look upon a place with equal radiation, the happiness is diminished and the misfortune is mitigated, and the whole substance of the place is composed by a moderate balance, so that they may be freed from the harming malefics by the saving protection of the beneficent stars.

<margin>The star's place must be considered</margin> Also inspect which star is located in which place, whose house or bounds it possesses; and if it is located in a foreign house, inspect its lord <note>The 'lord' is the planet that rules the sign another planet is currently sitting in</note>, what place in the birth chart it occupies, and whether it is in the primary pivots <note>cardines</note>, or in the secondary places, or in the lazy places; and whether it is in its exaltation <note>original: *altitudine*</note> or its fall <note>original: *deiectio*</note>, and in which signs it rejoices, or in which it is saddened by a certain natural pain. For if the lord of the sign is well [placed]...

<margin>Observation of the birth chart <note>original: *Genitura obseruanda*</note>.</margin>
...if a star is positioned in a part of its own happiness, even that star about which we inquire borrows from the joy of its host. But if the lord of that sign is for some reason dejected <term>dejected: a planet in a weak position, such as its 'fall' or in an unfavorable house</term>, even that star about which we inquire—though it may be placed in an advantageous location in the birth chart and firmly established to provide something by easy logic—is hindered by the shared dejections of that star which is the lord of the sign. You can easily understand this from our own human actions. For if, for the sake of hospitality, you enter the domicile or house of some friend or host, and the master of the house is uplifted by happy increases of fortune, you also exist as a sharer in that happiness; for you borrow the joy of gladness from the successes of your host. But if your host is deformed by wretched squalor and entangled in the dejected accidents of misfortune, the shared torments of pain and ill-fortune will consume you as well. Thus the stars, when the lords of the signs are well-placed, uplift the inhabitant and guest of their house to the condition of their own status, arranging them with an equal measure of fellowship, and they shape the power of the guest according to their own liberty.

<margin>The practice of astrology <note>original: *Matheseos usus*</note>.</margin>
Seek also, if it is a diurnal <term>diurnal: belonging to the day</term> birth chart, to what extent the stars which rejoice in diurnal charts are positioned, and to what extent those which harm diurnal charts are present. For if the stars which rejoice by day possess the principal places in a diurnal chart and are found in the primary cardines <term>cardines: the four 'pivots' or angles of the chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term>, they decree the greatest increases of happiness. But if the stars which we said rejoice by night possess the principal places or the primary cardines of the birth chart in a diurnal chart, they indicate infinite misfortunes with continuous calamities. We must also observe this in nocturnal <term>nocturnal: belonging to the night</term> birth charts, but with the order of power reversed. For if, in a nocturnal birth chart, the stars or the forms of the celestial images which we said rejoice by night possess the principal places or the primary cardines, they decree the greatest increases of happiness in a similar way. If, however, in nocturnal charts, those stars which we said rejoice in diurnal conversation possess the principal places or the primary cardines, they cause the entire ornament of happiness to be entangled in the falling accidents of misery. If all these things are collected with diligent reasoning—and if you join together the mixtures of the benevolent and malevolent stars, the power of the places and signs, and the powers of the degrees with an equal comparison of conjunction—you will designate the whole man, from his first until his final day, and his entire life and hope, and also his brothers, parents, children, health, spouse, death, sect <note>original: *sectam*; refers to the individual's philosophical or religious following</note>, actions, honors, travels, domicile, foundations, substance, and the accusations and dangers from friends and enemies, with a simple explanation of the definition. We have said enough of these things for now in this book of instruction; but when we come to the *apotelesmata* <term>apotelesmata: the study of the predicted effects or outcomes of the stars</term>, we shall first speak of everything broadly <note>original: *platice*</note> and then with subtle interpretation, showing all things with clear designation, lest any trepidation of doubt should hinder the knowledge of pronouncing judgment.

## The Qualities of Birth Charts: Which are Noble and Which are Mediocre. CHAPTER XXIV.

It is also fitting for us to know that a birth chart is "mediocre" which has one star (besides the Sun ☉ and Moon ☽) situated in its own domicile <term>domicile: the zodiac sign over which a particular planet has 'rulership' or 'home' status</term> and placed in the principal locations of the birth chart. He is also uplifted by "middling" happiness who has two stars placed in their own domiciles in opportune locations of the chart. He who has three will be happy and powerful beyond measure. Moreover, he who has four stars established in their own domiciles will approach the happiness of the gods; the substance of the human race does not allow for a number beyond this. But he who has no star established in its own domicile will always be unknown, ignoble, and entangled in wretched actions.

## ALL ASPECTS OF THE STARS. CHAPTER XXV.

<margin>Opposition <note>original: *Diametrum*</note>.</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'E' featuring a woodcut illustration of a seated figure, possibly an astronomer or astrologer, holding an instrument and looking upward, set within a square frame.</image-desc>First of all, we must also teach what is an opposition <note>original: *diametrum*</note>, what is a trine <note>original: *trigonum*</note>, what is a square <note>original: *quadratum*</note>, what is a sextile <note>original: *hexagonum*</note>, what is "cast away" <note>original: *abiectum*</note>, and also what is a right trine, what is a left, what is a right sextile, and what is a left. An opposition <note>original: *diametrum*</note> is Aries ♈ and Libra ♎; the opposition of Taurus ♉ is Scorpio ♏, and Scorpio's is Taurus ♉, and all other signs in a similar way. But so that you may find this not only with your eyes but also by calculation, we teach it briefly by...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions on the aspects (geometric relationships) between signs in a birth chart, building on the previous page's discussion of planetary rulers and the condition of the "host" signs. ->B O O K   S E C O N D<-

<margin>Trine <note>original: *Trigonum*</note>.</margin>
...by way of example: from one sign to another, whatever is the seventh sign, that is the diameter <note>original: *diametrum*; in modern astrology, this is the 'opposition' aspect</note>. This is always a malignant and threatening radiation <note>The author uses 'radiation' to describe the way planets cast their influence or 'aspect' across the circle of the zodiac</note>. A trine <note>original: *trigonum*</note> is that which is the fifth sign from where we begin; this is taught by the following example: from Aries ♈︎ to Leo ♌︎ is a trine, and similarly from Taurus ♉︎ to Virgo ♍︎, and so through all the signs—whichever sign is the fifth, that is a trine. We must also know what is a right-handed trine and what is a left-handed one. The right-handed <note>original: *dextrum*</note> is that which is behind the sign from which we start, while the left-handed <note>original: *sinistrum*</note> is that which is ahead. For example, the right-handed trine of Aries ♈︎ is Sagittarius ♐︎, while the left-handed is Leo ♌︎; and in the same way, the right-handed trine of Leo ♌︎ is Aries ♈︎, and the left-handed is Sagittarius ♐︎. For Sagittarius ♐︎, the right-handed trine is Aries ♈︎, and the left-handed is Leo ♌︎. Seek the trines in this way for all the other signs: this is a prosperous and happy radiation.
<margin>Right-handed and left-handed trines.</margin>

<margin>Square <note>original: *Quadratum*</note>.</margin>
A square is the sign which is the fourth from the one we start with, as shown by this example: the square of Aries ♈︎ is the sign Cancer ♋︎, and of Cancer is Libra ♎︎, and of Libra is Capricorn ♑︎, and of Capricorn is Aries ♈︎. But as for which square is right-handed and which is left, you will find it by the same logic we used for trines. For whichever sign is behind is the right-handed square—such as Capricorn ♑︎ for Aries ♈︎—and the left-handed is Cancer ♋︎. Thus in all other squares: that which is behind is right-handed, and that which is ahead is left-handed. This is a threatening radiation, composed of malicious power and full of the bile of enmity.

<margin>Sextile <note>original: *Hexagonum*</note>.</margin>
Sextiles <note>original: *hexagona*</note> are the same as trines, but of lesser power. A sextile is, therefore, the third sign from the one we begin with; for example, Gemini ♊︎ is the sextile of Aries ♈︎. But lest there be any controversy, we provide examples of this too. The right-handed sextile of Aries ♈︎ is Aquarius ♒︎, and the left-handed is Gemini ♊︎. So it is in the other signs: that which is behind is right-handed, and that which is ahead is left-handed. However, those sextiles are more powerful which have tropical <term>tropical: the 'turning' signs marking the solstices and equinoxes (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn)</term> or double <term>double signs: also known as bicorporeal or mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces)</term> signs in the middle; those separated only by solid signs <note>original: *signis solis*; likely referring to fixed signs</note> are ineffective.

### THE KINSHIP OF THE SIGNS TO ONE ANOTHER. CHAPTER XXVI.

We have already said by what logic radiation joins trines, squares, oppositions, and sextiles to the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the *horoscopos*, or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>. Now we must briefly explain why we have shown certain places to be joined to the Ascendant in the fellowship of radiation, while others are turned away from the Ascendant and in a certain way alien—which we have not without reason called "idle" <note>original: *pigra*; these are the 'inconjunct' houses (the 2nd, 6th, 8th, and 12th) that do not form a major geometric aspect to the 1st house</note>.

<summary>This page defines the major astrological aspects—opposition, trine, square, and sextile—explaining their mathematical distances, their handedness (right vs. left), and their general influences. It also introduces the concept of "idle" signs that lack a geometric connection to the Ascendant.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical mathematical explanation of astrological aspects, specifically why certain geometric relationships (60, 90, 120, and 180 degrees) create a "fellowship" between signs based on their division of the 360-degree circle. It then transitions into Chapter XXVII, which introduces melothesia—the ancient practice of assigning the twelve signs of the zodiac to specific parts of the human body for medical and predictive purposes.</meta>

# B O O K

As we have said, we must explain all these things clearly, so that this book of instruction may be fortified with the full substance of Astrology <note>original: *Matheseos*; here referring to the "science" of the stars</note>. All signs are joined together, bound to one another in turn. Learn briefly why we have said this. We have said that all signs have 30 degrees <note>original: *p.*, abbreviation for *partes* (parts/degrees)</note>. If, therefore, you multiply these 30 degrees twelve times, you make one number: you complete 360 degrees, which are divided through all the bodies of the twelve signs. From this, a proximity of connection associates all signs with one another. Therefore, whichever signs, when joined by the number of their degrees, make 360 degrees, they are joined to one another by a radiation <note>The "look" or "aspect" a planet casts</note> of equality and fellowship.

<margin>The Sextile <note>original: *Hexagonum*</note></margin>
The Sextile we have mentioned before, and now we indicate it in detail. From the position of the Ascendant <note>original: *horosc.*, the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, whatever is at 60 degrees, that shows the side of a Sextile. Thus, if you mix 60 six times, you get the full number of 360 degrees. Therefore, he who fulfills the total number of 360 degrees by joining six complete partitions is joined by an equal fellowship.

<margin>The Trine <note>original: *Trigonum*</note></margin>
The Trine indeed—that is, the fifth place from the Ascendant and from others, whether it be a right-handed or left-handed trine—we have said is joined in the greatest fellowship with the Ascendant or with others. But let us briefly explain by what logic this happens. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, if we have tripled 120 degrees, we will complete the first full number of 360 degrees. By this radiation of connection, that place is joined to the Ascendant; indeed, all trines are joined to each other by this radiation of fellowship.

<margin>The Square <note>original: *Quadratum*</note></margin>
We have also said that the Square is joined to the Ascendant by a very powerful fellowship of radiation. I shall briefly show the reason for this connection as well. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, we establish this place at 90 degrees; thus, by quadrupling 90 degrees, we complete the full number of 360 degrees. See how appropriately the square is a worthy side, because the number 90, quadrupled, completes the entire substance of 360 degrees; for this reason, it received the name "Square." This is the logic in all squares.

<margin>The Opposition <note>original: *Diametrum*</note></margin>
We have said that the Opposition is joined with the Ascendant in a fellowship of radiation, and I will explain the logic of this connection. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, we establish this place at 180 degrees. If, therefore, we double 180, we make the full number of 360 degrees. Since two complete numbers—that is, 180 joined twice—restore the complete substance of 360 degrees, these places are joined to one another by the greatest radiation of fellowship. This is the radiation in all oppositions. But those places which are so positioned that their degrees, by neither doubling, tripling, nor quadrupling, can complete the full number of 360 degrees, are joined by no radiation of fellowship with the Ascendant, nor with any other sign that falls in such a way. Because of this, whatever sign is found outside this number is called **idle** and **cast off** <note>original: *pigrum, & abiectum*; modern astrology refers to these as "inconjunct" or "averse" signs</note>.

### THE DOMINIONS OF THE SIGNS OVER THE HUMAN BODY. CHAPTER XXVII.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop cap 'E' featuring classical figures and botanical motifs.</image-desc>
We must explain which parts of the human body the 12 signs hold, for this is exceedingly profitable for outcomes <note>original: *apoteleſmata*; the predicted results of a birth chart</note>, especially when we wish to find the location of a health condition or a defect. The head of a person is in the sign of Aries ♈, the neck in Taurus ♉, the shoulders in Gemini ♊, the heart in Cancer ♋, the chest and stomach in Leo ♌, the belly in Virgo ♍, the kidneys and vertebrae in Libra ♎, the genitals <note>original: *natura*</note> in Scorpio ♏, the thighs in Sagittarius ♐, the knees in Capricorn ♑, the shins in Aquarius ♒, the feet in Pisces ♓. And thus, through these signs, all the members of a person are divided.

## THE GIVER OF HUMAN LIFE. CHAPTER XXVIII.

Now we must explain which star decrees how many years—more if it is well-placed, but fewer if poorly situated. When you have diligently inspected the "Giver of Life" <note>original: *dator vitae*; the planet responsible for determining the life span, often called the *Hyleg* in later traditions</note>, that is, the lord of the birth chart, and you have seen in what place it is positioned, in what sign, and in which degrees <note>original: *p.*, abbreviation for *partes* (degrees)</note>; and if you have likewise examined the lord of that very sign in which the Giver of Life is located—in what place, sign, and degrees it sits; and also the Moon, to the extent that she and the benevolent stars regard the Giver of Life—you will be able to define the quality of an easier life. For if the Giver of Life itself is placed in a good house, a good sign, and in good degrees, the full number of years is decreed, especially if the Sun (in a daytime birth) or the Moon (in a nighttime birth) supports the Giver of Life with a prosperous radiation <note>original: *radiatione*; the "look" or "aspect" one planet casts upon another</note>.

<margin>Saturn ♄</margin> Therefore, if Saturn is the Giver of Life and decrees the full number of years, he grants 57 years; if in a medium state, 43 years and six months; but if he decrees poorly, he grants 30 years, or 20 months, or 30 days and 12 hours.

<margin>Jupiter ♃</margin> If Jupiter is the Giver of Life and decrees well, he grants 79 years; if in a medium state, 45 years and six months; if poorly, 12 years, or 12 months, 12 days, and 12 hours.

<margin>Mars ♂</margin> If Mars is the Giver of Life and decrees well, he grants 66 years; if in a medium state, 40 years and six months; if poorly, 15 years, or 15 months, and 12 hours.

<margin>Sun ☉</margin> If the Sun decrees well, he grants 120 years; if in a medium state, 69 years and six months; if poorly, 19 years, or 19 months, 19 days, and 12 hours.

<margin>Venus ♀</margin> If Venus decrees well, she grants 82 years; if in a medium state, 45 years and six months; if poorly, 8 years, or 8 months, and 12 hours.

<margin>Mercury ☿</margin> If Mercury decrees well, he grants 76 years; if in a medium state, 48 years and six months; if poorly, 20 years, or 20 months, and 12 hours.

<margin>Moon ☽</margin> If the Moon decrees well, she grants 108 years; if in a medium state, 66 years and six months; if poorly, 25 years, or 25 months, 29 days, and 12 hours.

If, therefore, the Lord of Life or Giver of Life (that is, the lord of the birth chart) is in his own house, his own exaltation <note>original: *altitudine*; the sign where a planet's power is maximized</note>, or within his own bounds <note>original: *finibus*; specific sub-divisions of a sign</note>, and the stars of his own condition offer him good testimony—that is, they look upon him with a good radiation—and those stars that offer testimony are themselves well-placed, the greater number of years is decreed. However, they decree a medium age especially if the Giver of Life is indeed in his own bounds or houses, or in the rising sign or his own dignity, but is nevertheless hindered by malevolent radiations, or placed in a fallen position, or fortified by the testimony of no other star.

## THE TIME-LORD. CHAPTER XXIX.

The Greeks called the "Lord of Time" the *Chronocrator* <note>original: *Chronocratorem*; from the Greek *chronos* (time) and *kratōr* (ruler)</note>. In daytime births, the Sun takes the beginning of the times and divides them among the others; in nighttime births, the Moon does so. You should not admit any other method, because this is approved by everyone. When the Sun is the Lord of the times, he holds dominion for 19 years and 9 months. In the same way, when the Moon is the Lady of time, she will hold it for 10 years and 9 months. In a daytime birth, the Sun takes the first decade <note>a ten-year period</note>; the second is taken by whoever is found in the second place in the birth chart following the course of the signs; the third by whoever comes after the second, and so on for the rest. We teach this by example so you may understand more clearly: if in a daytime birth the Sun is found in Aries ♈, he himself will be the lord of the decade, and likewise in whatever other sign he may be. Whoever is in Taurus ♉ will be in the second place; whoever is after Taurus will be third, and so on for the others in this manner. We shall do the same for nighttime births, beginning from the Moon. But whoever has been allotted the decade, although he is the lord of the whole time, he nevertheless divides the entire substance of the decade among all the stars, beginning from himself and then handing it over to those placed in order, first giving it to whoever is found second in the theme <note>the horoscope or chart layout</note>.

### THE DIVISION OF TIMES. CHAPTER XXX.

We shall now briefly show how great the distribution of times is. The Sun <note>☉</note> receives 19 months, the Moon <note>☽</note> 25, Saturn <note>♄</note> 30, Jupiter <note>♃</note> 12, Mars <note>♂</note> 15, Venus <note>♀</note> 8, and Mercury <note>☿</note> 20. We will explain what happens in this distribution of times in the books on astrological outcomes <note>original: *apotelesmatum*; the study of the effects or "outputs" of the stars</note>, showing what each star decrees when it receives time from another star. For all things that come to us, whether good or bad, we gather from this reckoning of times: the end of life is found this way, as well as the substance of the whole birth, and everything the order of the stars has decreed. We find the annual progression <term>profection</term> <note>A technique where the chart is "advanced" by one sign per year to see which planet rules the current year of life.</note> by very easy calculations: for it always takes its beginning from the Ascendant <note>original: *horosc.*, the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>. The first year will be in the sign where the Ascendant is established, the second in the second sign, the third in the third, and so on in order. Others do this same thing from the Sun in a daytime birth, and from the Moon in a nighttime birth, and this method is reasonable.

### THE DIVISION OF YEARS INTO DAYS. CHAPTER XXXI.

The days of the whole year are also divided among the individual stars. I will take care to show how they are divided and where they take their beginning, so that we may know when sicknesses, weaknesses, profits, losses, joys, or pains occur. For when the benevolent stars <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> receive the days, we are freed from every evil; but when the malevolent ones <note>Saturn and Mars</note> do, then sudden cases of misfortune attack us. Therefore, in whatever sign the year falls <note>referring to the annual profection mentioned above</note>, the ruler of that sign receives the first days, and after it the others, according to how they are positioned in the birth chart. I will also teach how many days each star is allotted: the Sun has fifty-three days, the Moon seventy-one, Saturn eighty-five, Jupiter thirty, Mars thirty-six, Venus thirty-three, and Mercury fifty-seven. Within this span of days, we can find everything that happens to us—but first, the quality of the signs and houses must be examined. For if a star is well-placed and it receives the time, months, or days, and it is benevolent, it decrees all good things. If, however, a malevolent star receives the time, months, or days and is poorly placed, it decrees misfortunes according to the quality of the astrological houses. Thus, by handling everything with prudent inquiry, you will be able to explain the whole substance of a most true birth chart.

### THE RESULTS OF ANTISCIA. CHAPTER XXXII.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'E' featuring ornate floral scrolls and foliage inside a rectangular frame.</image-desc>
From all these established teachings—since we postponed the treatise on antiscia <note>original: *antisciorum*; from the Greek "shadow-opposite." These are pairs of degrees that are equally distant from the solstice points (0° Cancer/0° Capricorn) and are thought to have a hidden sympathetic connection.</note> a little while ago—we must now explain this topic, so that nothing seems to have been omitted by us in this instruction. The antiscia of the Greeks were handed down to us by mastery. I do not want anyone to suspect that this treatise does not exist among the Greeks, for Ptolemy <note>original: *Ptholomæus*</note> follows no other reasoning except that of antiscia. And Antiochus, when he says that Libra does not "see" Aries because of the earth that is in between, touches upon the reasoning of antiscia as if through a mirror. Dorotheus of Sidon <note>original: *Dorothius Sydonius*</note>, a most prudent man who wrote about astrological outcomes in the truest and most eloquent verses, explained the reasoning of antiscia with clear statements, specifically in his fourth book. Now I will briefly explain the method by which antiscia are calculated. We begin the start of the antiscia either from Cancer and Capricorn, or from Aries and Libra.

BOOK 2

Thus Cancer reflects into Gemini, and Gemini back into Cancer; Leo into Taurus, and Taurus back into Leo; Virgo into Aries, and Aries back into Virgo; Libra into Pisces, and Pisces back into Libra; Scorpio into Aquarius, and Aquarius back into Scorpio; Sagittarius into Capricorn, and Capricorn back into Sagittarius. Therefore, if any stars in the arrangement of a <term>birth chart</term> <note>original: *genitura*; the map of the heavens at the moment of birth</note> do not "see" one another <note>In astrology, "seeing" refers to planets being in "aspect" (specific geometric relationships like squares or triangles).</note>, one must ask whether they are joined to each other by a shared radiation through an <term>antiscium</term> <note>From Greek *anti* (opposite) and *skia* (shadow); a point reflected across the solstice axis.</note>. For when they cast an antiscium in such a way that they join by a trine, square, opposition, or sextile radiation through that reflection, they decree outcomes just as if they were placed in that arrangement naturally. All matters involving the blending of radiations are completed in this way. When you have done this, you will be able to very easily discover everything sought within the fates of men. This is a hidden logic, confirmed by the natural consensus of the reflections, which I shall take care to explain at another time. However, you can learn how much power the force of the reflections has and how much their logic operates from this birth chart which I set forth below.

For the man in whose birth chart the Sun was in Pisces, the Moon in Cancer, Saturn in Virgo, Jupiter in Pisces in the same degree as the Sun, Mars in Aquarius, Venus in Taurus, and Mercury in Aquarius—at the same degrees as the Sun—and with the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: *horoscopus*; the sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note> in Scorpio: the father of this birth chart, after a double ordinary consulship, was sent into exile. Furthermore, the subject himself was likewise sent into exile on a charge of adultery, but was finally snatched from exile and first appointed to the administration of Campania. Then he was raised to the proconsulship of Achaia, and afterward to a similar proconsulship of Asia, and finally, by the consensus of all the fathers <note>The Senate.</note>, he was promoted to the Prefecture of the City of Rome. He converted a fortune that was previously bitter and adverse into one that was prosperous and fruitful.

<margin>
This birth chart does not correspond to reason or astronomical calculation. For Venus cannot be in Leo <note>The main text says Taurus, but this marginal critic likely spotted an error in the source manuscript or calculated that Venus cannot be that far from the Sun.</note> [while] Mars and the Sun are at 15 degrees of Pisces, to say nothing of Venus for the moment.
</margin>

For any man ignorant of the logic of reflections, if he saw the Sun with Jupiter at the same degrees in the <term>Fifth House</term> <note>original: *quinto loco*; known as the "House of Good Fortune."</note> from the Ascendant—that is, in "Good Fortune"—he would pronounce that the father was blessed, happy, and powerful, and other such things. But regarding his exile and the constant plots against him, he could pronounce nothing unless he turned his attention to the logic of the reflections. You remember we said that Pisces casts an antiscium into Libra, and Libra back into Pisces. Thus, the Sun and Jupiter, being positioned together in Pisces, cast a reflection into Libra—specifically into that sign in which the Sun is "humbled" and "cast down" <note>Astrological "Fall," where a planet's power is weakened.</note>, and into the <term>Twelfth House</term> <note>original: *xii locum*; the house of hidden enemies and misfortune.</note> of the birth chart, known as the <term>Evil Spirit</term> <note>original: *cacodæmona*.</note>. This reveals an ignoble paternal lineage and decrees a famous exile for the father himself. Indeed, Jupiter—whose force and power the radiation of the reflection transferred from the sign of Pisces to the sign of Libra—[acts] as if he were in the Twelfth House, that is, in the Evil Spirit...
