BOOK SECOND

<sig>d 4</sig>
<meta>catchword: error</meta>

...in the **House of the Evil Spirit** <note>original: *cacodæmone*; the 12th House, associated with enemies and misfortune</note>, had been positioned there through an **antiscium** <term>antiscium: a point reflected across the solstice axis (Cancer/Capricorn)</term>, he stirred up many enemies for both himself and his father, and caused those enemies to prevail. Behold also another factor which decreed exile for the father: for **Saturn**, positioned in **Scorpio**, sees the **Sun** by an **opposition** <note>original: *de diametro*; a 180-degree aspect, usually considered hostile</note>, and his reflection regarded the reflection of the **Sun** by a radiation of opposition; for being positioned in **Aries**, he sent his reflection into **Virgo**. Therefore, his reflection positioned in **Aries**, and the reflection of the **Sun**, which was sent into **Virgo**, became contrary to one another through an opposition; by a decree of the highest rank, they caused him to be sent into exile, because the reflections of **Saturn** and the **Sun**, positioned in cosmic signs, saw each other by opposition. 

Indeed, by what logic he himself was made an exile, or what logic made him an adulterer (for this was the crime charged against him), is shown by this reasoning. We have said that the **Sun** sends its reflection into **Gemini**; thus the **Moon**, positioned in **Leo**, sent her reflection into **Gemini**, which reflection **Mars**, positioned in **Aquarius**, regarded from the right side. This is destructive whenever he receives the light of the waxing **Moon** from any side; for being made superior with many bodily defects, he finally made this same man an exile. 

But **Mars** himself, positioned in **Aquarius**, sends an reflection into **Scorpio**, in which sign the degree of the **Ascendant** <note>original: *horoscopus*; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> had been located. First, he struck the part of life—that is, the **Ascendant**—while positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** <note>original: *IMC* or *Imum Coeli*; the 4th House, the lowest point of the chart</note> with a violent radiation. Second, he regarded the **Moon** (whose reflection was positioned in **Scorpio**) while she was full, with a **trine** <term>trine: a harmonious 120-degree aspect</term> radiation. Third, his reflection sat in the degree of the **Ascendant**. Fourth, the reflection of **Mars**, which he had sent into the **Ascendant**, the **Moon** (positioned in **Cancer**) saw by a trine. Thus, from all sides, the waxing **Moon**, struck by the rays of **Mars**, oppressed him with many illnesses and finally made him an exile. And unless **Jupiter**, positioned in **Pisces**, had seen the **Ascendant** by a trine, he would never have been freed from exile; and unless the **Moon** in her exaltation (for the exaltation of **Jupiter** is **Cancer**) had similarly seen the **Ascendant** by a trine, he would have died a **violent death** <note>original: *biothanatus*; one who dies by execution, suicide, or accident</note>.

<margin>The third day is to be observed in birth charts.</margin>
But we have said that such benefits of **Jupiter** fail in the earlier parts, because on the third day the **Moon**, positioned in **Leo**, full of light, collided with the rays of **Mars** by opposition. For this day—that is, the third—operates in a very great way in birth charts. As to what radiation made him an adulterer, I shall take care to explain this as well.

**Mars**, positioned in **Aquarius**, sent his reflection into **Scorpio**. Thus **Venus**, placed in the **Setting** <note>original: *occasu*; the 7th House or Western horizon</note> of the birth chart, found the reflection of **Mars**. For **Venus** is wretched and entangled in many calamities if, being placed in the Setting, she is struck by the violent radiation of **Mars**. Furthermore, the reflection of **Venus** sent into **Leo** regarded **Mars** (positioned in **Aquarius** in the **Lower Midheaven**) by opposition. But from the bottom of the sky, **Mars**, without the logic of the reflection, joins **Venus** by a **square** <term>square: a 90-degree aspect, usually indicating tension or conflict</term> radiation. Thus, by all reasonings—through themselves and through their reflections—in the principal **angles** <note>original: *cardinibus*; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> of the birth chart, **Venus** and **Mars** attack each other with either square or opposing radiations in the matter of their union. This logic made him guilty of the charge of adultery.

<margin>**Saturn** and **Mercury** in exchanged houses.</margin>
**Mercury**, positioned in **Aquarius** (that is, in the house of **Saturn**) without the testimony of **Jupiter**, and **Saturn** in the house of **Mercury**, having **exchanged houses** <note>A condition known as mutual reception, where two planets occupy each other's signs</note>, make him a confidant of secret writings. And the **Moon**, positioned in her own house full of light, decrees the greatest honors for him in the **Ninth House**. This is especially because in a nocturnal birth chart, having followed the power of her own condition, she held the leadership in decreeing honors. **Saturn** and **Mercury**, through their exchanged houses, also decree such learning and great knowledge of literature that his speech and style may be compared to the ancient authors. Because **Venus** sent her reflection from **Taurus** into **Scorpio**—that is, into the house of the **Sun** and into the **Midheaven** <note>original: *MC* or *Medium Coeli*; the 10th House of career and public reputation</note>—the Emperor pronounced sentence against him regarding those crimes. Whose birth chart this is, O **Lollianus**, our glory, you know best. Having thus treated all these things, you will find how great is the power of the reflections. If anyone follows this with diligent discipline, the intention of his conjecture will never fail him when treating the fates of men.

# BOOK II

...approach with fearful trembling. Be modest and sober, content with little food and few possessions, lest the base greed for money bring infamy upon the glory of this divine science. Take care that, by your conduct and purpose, you surpass the conduct and purpose of even the good priests. For it is necessary for a priest of the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, and of the other gods through whom all earthly things are governed, to always prepare his mind in such a way that he is proven worthy of such great ceremonies by the testimony of all men. You shall indeed give your answers publicly, and say this beforehand to those who are about to ask: that you will speak with a clear voice about all things they inquire about, lest someone should perhaps ask of you something which is not permitted to be asked or spoken. Beware that you never respond to anyone questioning the state of the Republic or the life of the Roman Emperor; for it is not right, nor is it permitted, that we speak of the state of the Republic with wicked curiosity. Moreover, he is a criminal and worthy of every punishment who, when questioned, speaks concerning the fate of the Emperor, because

<margin>
Nothing is to be answered concerning the Emperor.
</margin>

you will neither be able to say anything about him, nor find it out. For it is fitting for you to know that even the haruspices <term>haruspices: diviners who interpreted the will of the gods by inspecting the entrails (exta) of sacrificed animals</term>, whenever they are questioned by private citizens about the state of the Emperor and wish to answer the inquirer, always find the entrails destined for this purpose and the arrangement of the veins to be disturbed by a tangled confusion. Indeed, no astrologer <term>mathematicus: in this period, the term specifically referred to an astrologer rather than a modern mathematician</term> has ever been able to define anything true regarding the fate of the Emperor. For the Emperor alone is not subject to the courses of the stars, and he alone is the one in whose fate the stars have no power of decree. Since he is the lord of the whole world, his fate is governed by the judgment of the Supreme God; and because the entire earthly space of the world is subject to the Emperor's powers, he himself is also established in the number of those gods whom the Principal Divinity has appointed to create and preserve all things. This reason also disturbs the haruspices; for whatever deity is invoked by them, because it is of lesser power, it cannot explain the substance of the greater power which exists in the Emperor. For he whom all talents, all ranks, all the wealthy, all the noble, all honors, and all powers serve, by the license of a divine and immortal lot, is placed within the principal ranks of the gods. 

Therefore, if anyone should inquire anything concerning the Emperor, I do not want you to disturb him with a fierce or harsh response, but persuade him with gentle speech that no one can find anything regarding the life of the Emperor, so that, warned by your persuasions, he may lay aside that madness of recklessness and correct the error of his mind. Yet I do not wish for you to report him if he asks something wickedly, lest when he is subjected to a capital sentence because of the illicit desires of his mind, you appear to have been the cause of his death, which is foreign to the purpose of a priest. Let there be a wife for you, a home, an abundance of honorable friends; let there be frequent access to the public; be separate from all contentions; undertake no harmful business, nor let the increase of money ever tempt you. Be removed from every heat of cruelty; never rejoice in the quarrels of others, or in capital and pestilential enmities, but let quiet moderation please you in every conversation. Flee seditions, flee always turbulent struggles; bind the loyalty of friendship with strong bonds; take care that in all acts your faith remains incorrupt; never pollute your conscience with false testimonies; never practice the lending of money at interest, lest a wretched increase of money be squeezed out for you from the necessities of others. Neither promise nor demand an oath of faith, especially if it is demanded because of money, lest the divine protection of the deities seem to be implored for the sake of a miserable pittance. 

To men who wander, especially those joined to you by the bond of friendship, show the right way of living, so that, formed by your instruction, they may be freed from the errors of their past life, and that you may be able to correct the ruined desires of men not only by your answers but also by your counsel. Never be present at nocturnal sacrifices, whether they are called public or private, nor confer in secret with anyone, but openly, as I have included above, practice the discipline of this divine art in the sight of all. I do not want you to explain the vices of men too plainly in your treatment of nativities <term>genitura: a birth chart or the configuration of stars at the moment of birth</term>, but whenever you come to this point, suspend your answer with a certain fearful modesty, lest you seem not to speak of, but to reproach, that which the evil course of the stars has decreed for a man. Separate yourself always from the allurements of spectacles <note>meaning the theater, chariot races, or gladiatorial games</note>, lest someone think you a supporter of any faction; for it is fitting for the priests of the gods to be separate and estranged from depraved allurements of plea[sure...]

...the allurements of pleasures. Having attained the true science of divinity in defining the fates of men and explaining the course of life, may you be instructed not only by readings but by the judgments of your own mind, so that more may be conferred upon you by the divinity of your mind than by the mastery of lessons.

## THE MATHESIS OF JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS JUNIOR, OF SENATORIAL RANK, TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANUS, BOOK III.

### P R E F A C E.

<margin>Man is made of four elements.</margin>
The discourse of the Mathesis <term>Mathesis: a Greek term meaning "learning" or "science," specifically used here for the art of astrology</term>, which belonged to the definition of astrological predictions, is now transferred into sentences so that, with all things revealed and demonstrated which the divine seers have published, the entire discipline of this wisdom may be most fully introduced through us to men who are students of this kind of art. Therefore, it is necessary for us to know first of all, Lollianus—our great honor—that the God who is the fabricator of man perfected the form, stature, and whole substance of man according to the image and likeness of the world, with nature as his guide. For he composed the body of man just like that of the world from a mixture of the four elements—namely, fire, water, air, and earth—so that the tempered conjunction of all these might adorn a living being into a form of divine imitation. He set forth man by the craftsmanship of divine fabrication in such a way that, by the force of nature, he brought together the power and substance of all elements in a small body, preparing a lodging—fragile though it may be, yet similar to the world—for that divine spirit which descends from the celestial mind to sustain the mortal body. For this reason, five stars, and also the Sun <note>original: ☉</note> and the Moon <note>original: ☽</note>, sustain man as a sort of smaller world <term>minor mundus: the microcosm; the theory that the human being is a miniature reflection of the universe</term> by their fiery and eternal motion, so that the living being made in imitation of the world might be governed by a similar substance of divinity. Wherefore those divine men, Petosiris and Necepso <note>Legendary Egyptian figures to whom many early astrological texts were attributed</note>, who are worthy of all admiration and whose wisdom approached the very secrets of divinity, also handed down to us the birth chart of the world by a divine mastery of science. They did this to show and demonstrate that man, formed according to the nature and likeness of the world, is sustained forever by the eternal companions of perpetuity through the same principles by which the world itself is ruled and contained.

### THE CHART OF THE WORLD. CHAPTER I.

<margin>perhaps Anubis.</margin>
Thus they wished this to be the birth chart of the world, following Aesculapius and Anubius <note>original: Anubium</note>, to whom the most powerful deity Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> committed the secrets of this science. For they established the Sun <note>original: ☉</note> in Leo <note>original: ♌</note> at 15 degrees, the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> in Cancer <note>original: ♋</note> at 15 degrees, Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> in Capricorn <note>original: ♑</note> at the fifteenth degree; Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> in Sagittarius <note>original: ♐</note> at the fifteenth degree; Mars <note>original: ♂</note> in Aries <note>original: ♈</note> at the fifteenth degree, Venus <note>original: ♀</note> in Libra <note>original: ♎</note> at the fifteenth degree, Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> in Virgo <note>original: ♍</note> at the fifteenth degree, with the Ascendant <note>original: horoscopo</note> in

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Thema Mundi" or the mythical birth chart of the universe, which Firmicus Maternus uses as the foundational template for all human astrology. It explains how the planets aspect the "Luminaries" (the Sun and Moon) based on their gendered signs and geometric relationships.</meta>

<header>BOOK</header>

...at the fifteenth degree. Thus, according to this birth chart and these conditions of the stars, and according to the testimonies which they offer to this birth chart, and according to these principles, it is intended that the fates of men be arranged. This is just as it is contained in that book of Aesculapius which is called the *Myriogenesis* <note>original: "μυριογένεσις" — meaning "The Ten Thousand Births" or "Infinite Origins"</note>, so that nothing in the individual birth charts of men should seem foreign to this birth chart of the world. Let us see, therefore, which star provided testimony to the Luminaries <term>Luminaries: The Sun and Moon, the primary sources of celestial light</term>, to what extent, and by what method of their radiation. For the Luminaries are the Sun (☉) and the Moon (☽).

Now, Saturn (♄) joins himself first to the Moon (☽), for he followed her condition. He follows the condition of the Moon because, being positioned in a feminine sign <note>Capricorn</note>, he received the rays of the Moon—who is also in a feminine sign <note>Cancer</note>—across a diameter <term>diameter: an astrological aspect of 180 degrees, known today as an "opposition"</term>. But indeed, when that same Saturn in this birth chart made his transition to the sign of Sagittarius (♐︎), he joined the Sun (☉) again with a similar radiation. He is thus aligned with the condition by which the Sun is composed; for being positioned in a masculine sign, he associates himself with an equal testimony of radiation when he regards the Sun across a diameter with a radiation similar to that of the Moon.

By this same logic, Jupiter (♃) is positioned in Sagittarius (♐︎), and by offering a trine testimony <term>trine: an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</term> to the Sun, he first joined himself to the Sun's condition. For this reason, being positioned in a masculine sign and associated with the Sun (who is in a sign of the same gender), he follows the Sun's power first. However, when he makes the transition to Pisces (♓︎), he will join himself to the Moon (☽) again in an equal condition; for in a similar manner, being placed in a feminine sign, he regards the Moon—who is positioned in a sign of the same gender—through a trine with an equalized radiation of condition.

In a similar way, the star of Mars (♂), being positioned in Scorpio (♏︎), offers testimony to the Moon (☽) via a trine because he is in a feminine sign. But when he comes to Aries (♈︎), transitioning to the testimony of the Sun (☉), he is placed in a masculine sign and joins the Sun with a trine radiation.

But this logic is changed in the case of Venus (♀). For being positioned in Libra (♎︎), although that sign itself is masculine, she nevertheless offers testimony to the Moon (☽) through a square <term>square: an aspect of 90 degrees, often indicating tension or dynamic action</term>. Yet when she makes the transition to Taurus (♉︎), being positioned in a feminine sign and regarding the Sun (☉) with a square radiation, she will again offer testimony to him.

Mercury (☿), however, they intended to be "common" <note>meaning neutral or adaptable</note> in this birth chart. He offers testimony neither to the Sun nor the Moon through square, trine, or diameter, nor does he join himself to the Sun or Moon by radiation. Instead, he is said to take pleasure in the Sun during the day if he is a "morning star," but in the Moon during the night if he is an "evening star." All these things we have discussed are intended to be observed in the birth charts of men, and they believe that a man's fate cannot be discovered unless these radiations are sought out with a keen inquiry...

## THE WORLD BIRTH CHART (MVNDI THEMA):

## BOOK THREE

...collected by reasoning. But lest the mythical tales of men deceive you, and lest anyone think that this birth chart was composed by the wisest men without cause, everything must be explained by us specifically, so that the wise reasoning behind this secret may be made known through diligent exposition. <margin>The uncertain origin of the world.</margin> This was not the actual birth chart of the world; for the world did not have a fixed day of its origin, nor was anyone present at that time when the world was formed by the reason of the divine mind and provident spirit. The reach of human fragility could not extend itself so far as to easily conceive or explain the origin of the world through reason, especially since a great <term>Apocatastasis: The cyclic restoration or renewal of the universe <note>original: "ἀποκατάστασις"</note></term>—that is, a reintegration—is completed over a space of three hundred thousand years through <term>Ecpyrosis: Destruction of the world by fire <note>original: "ἐκπύρωσιν"</note></term> or through <term>Cataclysm: Destruction of the world by flood <note>original: "κατακλυσμὸν"</note></term>. <margin>The restoration of the world.</margin> For the restoration is usually brought about by these two origins; for a flood follows a burning—that is, a <term>Cataclysm</term> follows an <term>Ecpyrosis</term>. For things consumed by fire could be reborn in no other way, nor be recalled to their former face and form, unless the mixtures and the joined dust of the ashes conceived the collected fertility of all generative seeds. But so that there might be an example for astrologers <note>original: "mathematici" — in this period, the term specifically referred to those who calculated horoscopes</note> to follow in the birth charts of men, the divine men fashioned this "birth chart of the world" through wise reasoning. It is pleasing, therefore, to explain the inventions of this divine composition, so that the reasoning of this admirable conjecture may be revealed through the study of mastery.

<margin>The ages, as they followed one another.</margin> Therefore, they wished to establish Saturn (♄) so that he might join himself first, and hand down the leadership of the ages. And this was not without merit. Because the first origin of the world was uncultivated and harsh, and wild in its rustic social dealings; and because rude men, having entered the first and unknown footsteps of light, were abandoned by the reason of established humanity, they wished this rustic and harsh time to belong to Saturn (♄). Thus, in imitation of this star, the quality established at the beginnings of life would endure in rustic dealings and the sharpening of inhuman ferocity.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
After Saturn (♄), Jupiter (♃) received the power of the ages; for the Moon (☽) is joined to him in this second place, so that, having abandoned the horror of the former squalor and set aside the ferocity of rustic dealings, a more cultivated life of men might be returned with purified morals.

<margin>Mars (♂)</margin>
In the third place, indeed, Mars (♂) joined himself to the Moon (☽) and handed over to it the power of the ages, so that mortality, having entered the right path of life and being composed with a certain moderation of its inhumanity, might conceive all the ornaments of arts and manufacturing.

<margin>Venus (♀)</margin>
After Mars (♂), Venus (♀) received the time of dominion, so that the discipline of men, growing by degrees, might also conceive the ornaments of wisdom. Therefore, they wished this time—in which learned speech refined the morals of men, and in which men were formed by the natural freedom of individual disciplines—to belong to Venus (♀). Thus, being joyful and protected by the majesty of a salutary divinity, they might govern their wandering acts by the mastery of providence.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
Indeed, they thought the final period should be given to Mercury (☿), to whom the Moon (☽) joins herself at the very last. What can be found more subtle than this arrangement? For once rustic pursuits were purified, arts discovered, and disciplines composed, the focus of the human race was sharpened through various acts. And because a noble character in man cannot maintain a single course of life, from various institutions and confused morals, the wickedness of malice grew; and at this time, the race of men discovered and handed down the shame of life's crimes through villainous machinations. For this reason, they thought the final period should be handed to Mercury (☿), so that in imitation of that star, the human race might conceive power once full malice was discovered. Therefore, from these things which were done in order, and from those whoever caused the change of succeeding times in man, the birth chart of the world was composed by the interpretation of divine conjecture, and thus far the origin and course of the human race is handed down to us.

And this was so that it might be an example to follow in the birth charts of men. However, lest anything seem to have been omitted by us, all things must be explained which prove that man was formed in the imitation and likeness of the world. Indeed, we have said—and it is proven by all—that the <term>Apocatastasis</term> is brought about through <term>Ecpyrosis</term> and <term>Cataclysm</term>. So too is the human substance of the body dissolved by a similar logic when the course of life is complete. For as often as nature, through the heat of internal fire, evaporates the overly loosened body of man with floods of humors, it is always either cooked away by ignited heat or dissolved by excessive sweating. Not otherwise do the most wise interpreters of the medical art [report] the substance of the human race by a natural pro...

### BOOK THREE

...they announce that it cannot be dissolved, unless either moisture dissolves the fire, or with heat once again dominating, the fire—extinguished deep within the marrow—should dry out. Thus, in every way, following the imitation of the world, artisan nature composed man, so that whatever either dissolves or forms the substance of the world would also both form and complete man.

### THE FIRST OF THE SIGNS. CHAPTER II.

We must now explain why they wanted the beginning of the twelve signs to start from ♈ <note>Aries</note>; I did not explain this in the book of instructions because this question could not have been clarified unless the birth chart of the world had been shown, which I ought not to have explained in that book, lest that exposition—with its obscure interpretation—disturb the unrefined minds of the students. Therefore, reconsidering the birth chart of the world, which we said was most prudently composed by the wisest men, I found the <term>Medium Coeli: The Midheaven or the highest point of the chart <note>original: "M C"</note></term> of that birth chart to be placed in Aries. For this reason, because the Midheaven frequently—indeed, always—holds the leadership in all birth charts, and because this place is the first above the crown of the head, and because we gather the foundations of the entire birth chart from this place, the beginning was opportunely given to all signs from this sign. This is especially true since the greatest part of the stars, as well as both "luminaries"—namely the ☉ <note>Sun</note> and ☽ <note>Moon</note>—sent their rays into this sign. From this, it was agreed among all nations that the beginning of the stars should commence from this sign. Now that these things have been said and shown, we must define through the individual places of the birth chart what each star, once established, decrees. And although some think this is a <term>platice: A general or broad arrangement <note>original: "platicam"</note></term> <margin>perhaps broad.</margin> arrangement, the skill of the speaker nevertheless arranges it with the easy guidance of instruction, lest the astrologer, as if established in darkness, be disturbed by the falling confusion of error. But although these things are thought by some to be defined in a <term>Platonic: Relating to the ideal or philosophical system of Plato</term> manner, many things in this book are said in a similar way. For then the stars will have their efficacy if they are positioned equally in their individual places.

# THE DECREES OF SATURN THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER III.

<margin>The first place of Saturn in birth charts.</margin>
<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'S' containing a seated figure, possibly a scholar or a personification of Saturn, set within a landscape with floral ornamentation.</image-desc>When Saturn is positioned by day in the <term>horoscopus: The Ascendant or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>, that is, in that part in which the Ascendant is, he will cause the birth to be brought forth with a very loud cry. This god, however, always causes those born by day in any of the <term>four cardines: The four angles of a chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli)</term> to be the first born, or the first to be nurtured, or causes those brothers born before them to depart. He also makes people puffed up and uplifted by a spirit of pride. If, however, with ♄ <note>Saturn</note> established by day in the Ascendant, ♂ <note>Mars</note> should possess another angle of the birth chart, or be in the <term>anaphora: The house immediately following an angle</term> of an angle, it signifies the arrival of many evils. For he will cause the greatest dangers and the ruin of the inheritance; frequently, indeed, if no benevolent star placed in a good location of the birth chart joins itself to them by the radiation of its light, <margin>Violent deaths.</margin> and if it receives the rays of a waxing ☽ <note>Moon</note> or the ☉ <note>Sun</note>, it makes <term>biothanati: Those who die a violent or unnatural death <note>original: "biothanatos"</note></term>. But if ♄ <note>Saturn</note> is established in the part of the Ascendant by night, the one who has him thus will be hindered by the greatest illnesses and always weighed down by great labor. To some, indeed, he will give activities involving water, yet in such a way that they are always worn down and oppressed by laborious dealings.

<margin>II</margin>
Established in the second place from the Ascendant, ♄ <note>Saturn</note> causes grave ailments and the greatest reversals. He is also the slayer of the wife and children, and the stirrer of the greatest and frequent turmoils; moreover, he dissipates the paternal and maternal substance. He makes the one who is born slower in all actions, and for some, he even imposes lifelong physical infirmities. If, with ♄ <note>Saturn</note> thus established, ♂ <note>Mars</note> is in any angle of the birth chart, and sees the ☉ <note>Sun</note> by <term>quadrate: An aspect of 90 degrees</term> or by <term>diameter: An aspect of 180 degrees (opposition)</term>, or regards a waxing ☽ <note>Moon</note> in a similar way, he will make them wretched, poor, and destitute, and those who must commit their bodies to daily labors. If, however, he is in this place by day, he will give increases to the inheritance slowly and step-by-step. But he renders them hidden, secretive, and poor in spirit, always denying that they have anything. To some, indeed, he grants the supports of life from aquatic activities or from damp businesses.

### BOOK THREE

...thieves, but those whom a prosperous outcome never follows in their theft. If, however, with these positions as they are, <term>Mars <note>original: "♂"</note></term> joins <term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> in any manner, he will make the individuals accusers, informers, wicked, malevolent, envious, and malicious, and they will always perish by a wretched death.

<margin>IV</margin>
In the fourth house from the <term>Ascendant <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth; original: "horoscopo"</note></term>, if Saturn is positioned to the exact degree—that is, in the <term>Imum Coeli <note>The "Bottom of the Sky," the lowest point of the chart representing home, roots, and the father; original: "I M C"</note></term>—and if he holds this place during a day birth, he will make those who are greedy for money, guardians of gold and silver. If, however, he is in this place during a night birth, he dissipates the paternal inheritance and causes the early death of the father; he will also cause serious illnesses, cold shivers of the body, and will make the person always disreputable during their weak years. If the <term>Moon <note>original: "☽"</note></term> regards him from a <term>square <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note></term> or <term>opposition <note>An aspect of 180 degrees</note></term>, or if she is in the same degree in which he is positioned, he will cause sterility of children, and forces the one who is born to adopt others' children as his own, or makes him a guardian of orphans; and from hidden pains, they are deformed by the vice of perpetual ill health. He renders the mother of the newborn a widow quickly, and inflicts heavy illnesses upon her from women's troubles, and causes her to be fatigued by perpetual stomach pains and many anguishes.

<margin>V</margin>
In the fifth house from the Ascendant, if Saturn is positioned there by day, he will make kings and leaders, and bestows the greatest insignias of power. If, with Saturn so placed, the <term>Sun <note>original: "☉"</note></term> is found in the part of the Ascendant, and he receives the conjunction of a waxing Moon, he grants perpetual happiness and decrees the ornaments of the greater powers. If, with Saturn so placed, it is not the Sun but <term>Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note></term> in the Ascendant, he will make magistrates of lesser rank, to whom the government of individual cities is entrusted, and he will make them masters of a very great inheritance, so that they can sustain others from their own wealth. If neither the Sun nor Jupiter is in the Ascendant, but he only receives the conjunction of the waxing Moon and is positioned in the fifth house, he will give substance and inheritances; however, these men will frequently be without a wife, or joined in marriages unworthy of themselves. If Saturn holds this place of the birth chart by night, in the process of age, he assigns a portion of happiness to the man in some small domain, but he makes his youth inconsistent; he also demonstrates the man to be slow and lazy in all acts. Some, if a waning Moon joins him, he causes to lose their inheritance and to perish with miserable tearing apart whatever was previously acquired.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the sixth house from the Ascendant, Saturn dissipates the entire inheritance, for he is always badly positioned in that place; he will also cause illnesses, especially if a waning Moon joins him, or if she regards him from an opposition, or if she is in square to him while waning. For he will make men unhappy, disreputable, and wanderers, who clearly can never stay in one place. If, however, Mars regards Saturn so positioned either from a square or opposition, or if he is with him in the same sign, he will cause hidden bodily pains, or those suffering from consumption <note>tuberculosis</note> or dysentery; and if no radiation of a benevolent star mitigates them so positioned, he will cause those who are born to perish unhappily from these illnesses.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the seventh house from the Ascendant—that is, in the setting <note>The Descendant or western horizon</note> to the exact degree—if he is a "morning star" <note>Rising before the sun</note> in a day birth, he will be good, and decrees the greatest substance to men, but only when they have entered the threshold of old age; for positioned thus, he bestows a very great age of life. He makes them guardians of money, but indicates hidden pains of the bodies, for he makes them hemorrhoidal or contracted with the pain of the nerves <note>possibly sciatica or gout</note>. If, however, he is an "evening star" in this place, he causes fistulas around the anus and likewise hemorrhoids, especially if Mars regards him so positioned by any radiation; he also makes them rheumatic, and those in whom abscesses frequently arise, and whom the accidents of wives always shake, being crushed by the heavy bitterness of pain.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the eighth house from the Ascendant, if Saturn is placed there by day, as time proceeds, he bestows increases of inheritance; for some, if positioned in this place he is in a sign of Mars or in the <term>terms <note>Specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note></term> of Mars, he decrees money from the deaths of others. If, however, he is positioned in this place by night, he will cause the overthrow of the inheritance, if the Moon regards him with a square or opposite radiation. It is also bad if, with Saturn so positioned, the Moon is positioned in his house and regards him with preceding radiations. But if Mars regards the Moon so placed with Saturn from any side by any radiation, he will make <term>biothanatos <note>original: "biothanatos"; refers to those who die a violent, premature, or unnatural death</note></term>. But if Mars, and likewise Jupiter, the Moon, and Saturn are all placed as we have said and regard each other with opportune radiation, he will make men good, and of good life and reputation, but always unstable regarding the affections of a wife; moreover, a "good radiation" is <term>trine <note>original: "trigonica"; an aspect of 120 degrees</note></term> or <term>sextile <note>original: "hexagona"; an aspect of 60 degrees</note></term>.

### IX. In the ninth house from the <term>Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopo"</note></term>, <term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> positioned for a day birth will make famous magicians, or renowned philosophers, or temple priests who are always most celebrated for their expertise in magic. Depending on the nature of the signs, he also creates <term>haruspices <note>Priests who practiced divination by inspecting entrails</note></term>, prophets, <term>mathematicians <note>original: "mathematicos"; in this era, the word specifically referred to astrologers</note></term>, and those who are always brilliant in true interpretation, whose answers are given as if from a certain divine authority. He makes some always persevere in temple worship, and occasionally makes them leaders of religions and divine interpreters of dreams; he also frequently produces <term>long-haired philosophers <note>original: "philosophos capillatos"; a reference to the traditional ascetic appearance of certain philosophical schools like the Stoics or Cynics</note></term>. If, however, he is positioned in this house for a night birth, he will cause the wrath of the gods and the hatred of emperors, especially if the <term>Moon <note>original: "☽"</note></term> with diminishing light is brought toward him for whatever reason. Greater evils from the gods or the Emperor are decreed for the one born thus if <term>Mars <note>original: "♂"</note></term> regards the <term>Moon <note>original: "☽"</note></term> and <term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> from any side. These things are mitigated if a ray of <term>Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note></term> reaches him from a favorable location, or if he is in his own <term>terms <note>Specific degrees within a sign ruled by a planet</note></term>, or in the house of <term>Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note></term> or the <term>Sun <note>original: "☉"</note></term>, or in his <term>exaltation <note>The sign where a planet's power is most intensified</note></term>, provided he is joined to Jupiter by a <term>trine <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</note></term> aspect.

### X. In the tenth house from the Ascendant—that is, to the exact degree in the <term>Midheaven <note>The highest point of the chart, representing career and public life; original: "M C"</note></term>—<term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> will make Emperors, generals, and praetorian prefects. If Saturn is thus placed in the locations where he is exalted, and the <term>Sun <note>original: "☉"</note></term> is in the degree of the Ascendant, and Saturn is in the Midheaven as we said before, and he is found during a day birth, he will make honorable men of good character, such as wealthy farmers whose possessions always lie near the sea, rivers, or forests. He will also grant great wealth, much glory, and inheritances from important persons, especially if <term>Mars <note>original: "♂"</note></term> is joined to him by no aspect. But if Mars regards him in this position with a very strong conjunction, he will grant these things we mentioned to a lesser degree. If, however, he is found in the Midheaven during a night birth, he decrees misfortunes and causes the loss of the patrimony; he will deny marriage and children, especially if he is found in a malevolent star, sign, place, or terms.

<margin>Saturn by night in the <term>angles <note>The four most powerful points of a chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses; original: "cardinibus"</note></term></margin>
But if a benevolent star—that is, <term>Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note></term> or <term>Venus <note>original: "♀"</note></term>—regards him thus positioned at night with a good aspect, it grants some part of those things we just said were denied. But specifically, the star of <term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> positioned in any of the angles during a night birth decrees the greatest evils for the life-chart: it kills the wife, strikes down the children, and always announces the bitter pains of bereavement. If, thus positioned, he receives a conjunction of the waning <term>Moon <note>original: "☽"</note></term>, the one who has Saturn so placed will be so worn down by the weight of poverty that he will scarcely have food for daily life, especially if the Moon, positioned in a feminine sign and failing in light, joins herself to Saturn. If Saturn so positioned receives a waxing Moon, he decrees inequality in life, so that for the one who has Saturn thus, there is not one similar course of life, but it always turns with changeable diversity. If, however, the star of <term>Mercury <note>original: "☿"</note></term> associates with Saturn thus positioned, he will grant the greatest sharpness of heart and a long-lasting substance of life, especially if he is the master of the birth or the giver of life. But if he is opposed to the one who is master of the birth or the giver of life, he subtracts thirty years from those years that were decreed, and also decrees worse evils whenever he is placed against the master of the birth, whom

### THE DECREES OF JUPITER THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL 
### STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER IV.

<term>Jupiter <note>original: "IVpiter"</note></term>, if he is positioned exactly in the first angle in the degree of the <term>Ascendant <note>original: "horosc."</note></term>, especially in those signs in which <term>Jupiter</term> rejoices, or in his own houses, and also if he is in his own <term>stations <note>points where a planet appears to stand still</note></term> or in his exaltation, he will always make men who are noble, glorious, great, and leaders of cities. According to the scale of the birth chart, he makes them good, charming, benevolent, joyful, and wealthy—especially if he is found in the degrees of the <term>Ascendant</term> during a day birth, and if no malevolent star looks upon him from any side while he is thus positioned. For if malevolent stars look upon <term>Jupiter</term> so positioned with a hostile ray, everything <term>Jupiter</term> has decreed is for the most part diminished. If, however, he is found in the degree of the <term>Ascendant</term> during a night birth, he will cause the person to be born first among brothers; or if someone was born before him, <term>Jupiter</term> will in the meantime separate that person, perhaps even in distant regions and places, so that the subject himself may hold the leadership in his father's house. He also makes them well-nourished and places the parents in the greatest happiness. But if a malevolent star stands against <term>Jupiter</term> positioned thus at night, it dissipates all paternal and maternal substance. <term>Jupiter</term>, when placed in the <term>angles</term> of a birth chart, will always either cause the subjects to be born first, or cause their older brothers to be removed in the meantime, so that the subject himself (as I said above) may alone hold leadership in the father's house. If the <term>Moon <note>original: ")"</note></term> is increasing and joins with <term>Jupiter</term> by any ray while he is in the <term>Ascendant</term> by day or night, he will produce the greatest administrators, governors of cities, and those often put in charge of the greatest affairs.

<margin>II</margin>
In the second house from the <term>Ascendant</term>, <term>Jupiter</term> decrees inheritances from strangers and will cause the person to be adopted by strangers. He will give lordship over the great possessions of high-ranking nobles, if <term>Venus <note>original: "♀"</note></term> is also well-positioned and joins him with a good ray. But if <term>Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note></term> looks upon <term>Jupiter</term> in this association from any side, the person will frequently change their status and be transferred from good circumstances to bad. And it will be that he who has <term>Saturn</term> thus will always be changeable throughout his whole life with various diversities, such that at one moment he abounds in riches, and at another he is weighed down by the burden of poverty.

<margin>III</margin>
In the third house from the <term>Ascendant</term>, <term>Jupiter</term> is neither good nor bad, but is always composed with an even moderation; thus, sometimes the patrimonies of such persons are dissipated, but at other times inspired riches are bestowed upon them.

<margin>IIII</margin>
In the fourth house from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The text here identifies the "fourth house" as the <term>Midheaven <note>original: "M C" or "Medium Coeli"</note></term>, which is usually the 10th house; Firmicus is likely counting the "angles" or "cardines" in a specific order</note> positioned exactly by day, he makes men of the highest legal standing: either lawmakers, interpreters of the law, or legal experts. He also makes lovers and breeders of beasts of burden, according to the quality of the signs. He produces messengers of kings, generals, or judges, and those to whom the care and concern of the first public couriers are mandated, and those who are sent here and there in frequent travel by public command of princes, generals, or judges. He will also make them known to princes, attached to public acts, and those who commit themselves to the protection of the gods and ask the gods for remedies, and those who show the direct path to others by frequent signs. Most who have <term>Jupiter</term> thus have foreknowledge of the future and frequently hold the greatest honors in temples. Others, according to the quality of the signs, find treasures. For <term>Jupiter</term> positioned thus always decrees a happy old age until death. If, however, <term>Jupiter</term> so positioned is placed in <term>opposition <note>original: "in diametro"</note></term> to the <term>Sun <note>original: "☉"</note></term>, he makes the father noble and glorious, but he will dissipate the father's inheritance around middle age, and gather it again afterward. Moreover, he who has him thus will be both slower in sexual union with women and separated from the affections of his children. If, however, he is found thus at night, he will make men of moderate substance, and in the process of time, he will render them even more fortunate.

**V** In the fifth house <note>The "fifth place" from the Ascendant, historically associated with children, creativity, and good fortune.</note> from the <term>Ascendant <note>original: "horosc."</note></term>, **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> being positioned decrees great increases of good fortune; for it makes the person who is born thus honored in public magistracies, especially if he is found in his own <term>houses <note>The zodiac signs a planet rules; for Jupiter, these are Sagittarius and Pisces.</note></term>, or in his <term>boundaries <note>original: "finibus"; specific degrees within a sign assigned to a planet.</note></term>, or in his <term>exaltation <note>original: "altitudine"; the sign where a planet's power is most intensified; for Jupiter, this is Cancer.</note></term>, or in the house of the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"; the sign of Leo.</note>. But if, with Jupiter thus placed, the **Sun** joins him with a favorable aspect, he will produce leaders who even possess the power of life and death. If, without **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, with Jupiter thus placed, **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> join him from any part, he will make royal financial administrators. But if, without all these, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> alone joins him from any part, he will make people adorned with the grace of flowing prosperity; for if, as we said above, he is positioned thus with the **Sun**, the one who has this in his chart will always be distinguished by royal power, and his pronouncements will be such as if divine teachings were being brought forth by a man joined to God. Furthermore, the one who has him thus will have a strong body and sturdy bones. And if he receives a conjunction with the "wind" <note>Likely referring to the Moon's latitude or its directional movement in the sky.</note> of the waxing **Moon**, he will procreate humans of almost divine and immortal substance. 

One must always observe, if Jupiter is thus located, by which "wind" the **Moon** travels as she is carried toward him; for this calculation is difficult to gather. For if Jupiter is positioned in the North, and the **Moon**, receding from the South, joins him while waxing and in full light—specifically with Jupiter positioned in the fifth house from the <term>Ascendant</term> and in those signs in which he rejoices, or in his own houses, or in his exaltation, provided it is a day birth—he will create invincible Emperors who hold the steering oars of the entire world, especially if, with Jupiter thus located in those signs in which he rejoices or is exalted, the **Sun** joins him by a <term>trine aspect <note>original: "trigona radiatione"; an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note></term>. For Jupiter rejoices by day when adorned by the Sun's light, especially if he is positioned in his morning rising. But if Jupiter, placed as we have said, receives a waning **Moon**, he will make people of respectable character, raised up by the grace of moderate dignity, and upon whom the burden of poverty never falls. If, with Jupiter thus placed, without any conjunction of the "winds" which we mentioned, the waxing **Moon** joins him by a simple aspect, he will make administrators, men of consular rank, and frequently even ordinary consuls, especially if it is a diurnal birth chart. But if **Venus** joins him in a partnership of light, he decrees long years and a great span of life; he will also give children of both sexes, or twins, especially if Jupiter himself is the ruler of the birth chart, or ruler of the Ascendant’s part, or ruler of that sign in which the lord of the birth chart is located.

<margin>Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note> does not rejoice in nocturnal birth charts.</margin>
But if, in a nocturnal birth, he is located in opposition to the giver of life <note>The "Hyleg" or planet responsible for determining the length of life.</note> (for Jupiter does not rejoice in nocturnal births), he takes away twelve years from whatever age was decreed. Moreover, if in a nocturnal birth, **Mars**, **Venus**, or the **Moon** show themselves to him in an opposing course, he will cause the one born thus to be entangled in the greatest vices, according to the nature and substance of the signs. For in **human signs** <note>Signs depicting humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius.</note>, positioned thus, he will make them lustful and perverse regarding their loves with insane desire, doing those things which women are accustomed to do. But in **quadruped signs** <note>Four-footed signs like Aries, Taurus, or Leo.</note>, positioned thus, he will make hunters and lovers of wild beasts, and those whom the desert woods always delight, entangled in constant labors. In **terrestrial signs**, he will make herbalists and those wishing to know more than the substance of human nature allows. In **watery signs**, however, he makes fishermen and those whose livelihood is found around the river, sea, or marshes—laborious men indeed, often living by these arts. If, with Jupiter thus placed in a nocturnal birth, the **Moon** recedes from him while those we mentioned resist him, he will make a life of inequality; for the one who has him thus will fall into frequent miseries. But he will be tempered from this evil to some degree if, with him thus placed, the receding **Moon** joins **Venus** by a favorable aspect. But if, with Jupiter thus placed, the **Moon** receding from him has a conjunction with no star, he decrees the greatest misfortunes, labors, and misery. If, however, with Jupiter thus placed, the **Moon** receding from him and in a sense fleeing, should cast herself by a square or diameter <note>Opposition (180 degrees).</note> into the rays of **Mars**, he will create <term>victims of violent death <note>original: "biothanatos"; a Greek term for one who dies an unnatural or violent death.</note></term>, according to the natural form and substance of the sign. For if **Mars** regards the **Moon** receding from Jupiter by the diameter (as we have said) in a nocturnal birth, he will cause brawls, dangers, and always great struggles with inferiors. Whence, by night in this sign, Jupiter frequently decrees bad hardships and calamities.

<margin>The sixth house is always perilous.</margin>
For the sixth house <note>The "Sixth Place" was traditionally known as the House of Bad Fortune, associated with illness and labor.</note> has its own particular claim to malice, and whatever star is in that place will always borrow the greatest power for decreeing evils from the vice of the location.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the seventh house <note>The "Seventh Place" or Descendant, representing marriage and partnerships.</note> from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."</note>, **Jupiter** being positioned—that is, exactly upon the setting point—in a day birth, certainly, will make men affluent and wealthy, and he decrees spans of long and blessed old age. But in a night birth, he particularly overturns the place of children and the spouse; for it is necessary that they lose a most dear and compliant wife, and see the miserable death of beloved sons or daughters. If, however, he is found in that place of the birth chart during the night, the one who has him so will achieve increases in his inheritance as his age increases; he will be of moderate substance, however, and of such means that nothing is lacking for him to live well and blessedly.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the eighth house <note>The "Eighth Place," associated with death and the resources of others.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Jupiter** being positioned frequently undermines the inheritance, creates great enemies, and frequently stirs up seditions from the people; he makes men occupied always with malicious ages of life. He also makes them ignoble, and rejoicing with a foolish boldness—people who are backwards, and whose fury may even proceed as far as insanity, especially if, with **Jupiter** so placed, a malevolent star should possess any angle <note>The "angles" are the four most powerful points of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart. <margin>IX</margin>
In the ninth house <note>The "Ninth Place," associated with travel and religion.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Jupiter** being positioned, if it is a day birth, will make the one who is born say whatever things are to come, and renders him always an interpreter of the gods. Some also achieve priesthoods; for others, he causes some gift to be conferred from the temples, but sometimes he also causes losses, and fevers of the body and mind. If, however, he is positioned in that place by night, he makes men who always dream false dreams, and who frequently lie about the gods, and who promise themselves some hope from the lots of the gods; and they think it most important that they are always vexed by this in their lives.

<margin>X</margin>
In the tenth house <note>The "Tenth Place," the Midheaven or Zenith, representing career and reputation.</note> from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" / "Medium Coeli"</note>—positioned exactly during the day, he will make leaders of public business and the top ten of the greatest men, and those upon whom the greatest honors are conferred by the people; famous men also, and those who always wish to exert themselves for the sake of ostentation, but whom he renders luxurious. He also decrees the greatest felicities when positioned thus, if no malevolent star, positioned in the **Midheaven**, resists him. But if a malevolent star resists **Jupiter** so placed in the **Midheaven**, whatever of dignity, honor, or riches was bestowed upon them in the first stage of life is all diminished, scattered, and utterly overturned in the later life, unless the setting—that is, the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—should be protected by the omen of another benevolent star. If, however, he is positioned in the tenth house by night, he makes them honorable in character, indeed, but those who are quickly deceived, and whose inheritance perishes and flows away with frequent and swift dissipation.

<margin>XI</margin>
In the eleventh house <note>The "Eleventh Place," the House of the Good Spirit, associated with friends and hopes.</note> from the **Ascendant**, positioned during the day, he decrees the greatest felicities and bestows great riches; he also gives the most famous powers, and decrees the **fasces** <note>Symbols of high Roman magisterial office.</note> and proconsular command, if the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> join him with a good radiation, and if the **Moon**, receding from the South while **Jupiter** is positioned in the North, joins him while full—that is, if she is carried toward him in such a course as we described in the fifth house. But if **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is contrary to **Jupiter** so positioned, being placed in the 8th house of the birth chart, he will make them rejoice in great and potent felicities and be refined with the greatest riches, but he will change everything—whatever of honors or dignities was conferred upon them—into an incursion of miseries and unhappiness.

<margin>XII</margin>

### THE DECREES OF MARS THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY, CHAPTER V.

<margin>The first place of Mars.</margin>
**Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> positioned exactly <note>original: "partiliter" - meaning precisely by degree.</note> in the **Ascendant**, in a nocturnal birth and in masculine signs, will create military men. However, if he is positioned exactly in the **Ascendant** as a morning star, without the radiation of **Jupiter**, he will make men who are overly generous, wishing to give away more than the substance of their patrimony allows, so that they seem to be spendthrifts, yet they always make their actions known through reason. But if, during the night, the **Ascendant** is positioned in the house of **Mars** <note>The "houses" of Mars are Aries and Scorpio.</note>—specifically in a masculine sign—and **Mars** is found in that same sign (that is, in the **Ascendant**), and **Jupiter** is with him exactly in the same sign or looks upon him with a solid radiation, he will make leaders of wars to whom the entire army is committed. He shall render them masters of life and death, whose arrival cities or provinces always greatly dread; they shall be fortunate, strong, and grave, and their anger is always brought forth with great indignation. But such a position does not permit one to love a spouse or children with dear affection. In a day birth, however, if he is found exactly in the **Ascendant**, he makes men who are clever, audacious, furious, and wanderers, but always unstable in all things; whatever they dare, they can complete by no reasoning, but whatever they have obtained always slips from their hands. The patrimonies of those who have **Mars** thus are also dissipated. Indeed, they lose the substance of their entire life, and even their wives and children, nor is anything of their paternal substance reserved for them; rather, these things perish in their early years. But if **Jupiter**, being so placed, should look upon **Mars** during the day while **Mars** is positioned in his own house, or in his exaltation <note>original: "altitudine"</note>, or in his own bounds, by a **trine aspect** <note>original: "trigonica radiatione" - an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered very harmonious.</note>, or if he is with him exactly, the evils of **Mars** are mitigated from every side. But I also know, as I have found in many birth charts, that with **Mars** positioned in the **Ascendant**, many who were given into exile have administered **public affairs** <note>original: "res pub."</note> well and vigorously, and have been well-deserving of them.

If, with **Mars** so positioned, **Jupiter** joins him with a good radiation, being himself positioned either in his own house or in his own bounds, they escape from all dangers, and are thoroughly redeemed from captivity and transferred back from slavery to liberty—though at times they will not have the necessities of life. If, however, he is found thus during the night, he makes soldiers or athletes, but he is accustomed to easily deceive them through a continuation of dangers. Dangers will be present in a similar way if **Jupiter** and **Venus**, as we said above, join him with good radiation.

# BOOK #

<margin>Mars does not destroy his own house.</margin>
If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is positioned in the **setting** <note>original: "occasu" - the descendant or 7th house, where the sun sets.</note> and looks toward the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc." - the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> through a **diameter** <note>An aspect of 180 degrees, also called an opposition.</note>, he will not cause a **violent death** <note>original: "biothanatum" - from the Greek for one who dies by force or unnaturally.</note>; for in this case **Mars** does not destroy his own house, but instead he makes people **short-lived** <note>original: "ὀλιγοχρόνιους" (oligochronious)</note>, provided that the **Ascendant** and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are not protected by the aid of **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>. But if the **Ascendant** is not in a house of **Mars**, he renders them short-lived, especially if he regards the **Moon**—positioned in the **Ascendant** or at the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" - the Medium Coeli, the highest point of the chart.</note>—with her full light through a **square** <note>An aspect of 90 degrees.</note> or a **diameter**.

But generally, **Mars** established in the **seventh place** from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **setting** during the day or night—causes **violent deaths**, and this according to the quality of the zodiac signs. However, he decrees this evil more strongly and more clearly in the signs of others <note>Signs not ruled by Mars.</note>; for if he is found in this place, he then causes pains and lacerations of the body, and either casts the person down from heights, or kills them, or weighs down those held in prison and chains with perpetual and deadly calamities. In **nocturnal births** <note>Charts for people born at night.</note>, however, he will cause pains and fevers from all actions, but he frequently inflicts wounds from **iron**, and causes those very wounds to be treated by the fiery burning of **cauteries** <note>Hot irons used by ancient doctors to seal wounds.</note>. He also causes hidden and immense bodily pains, especially when he himself is the **Lord of Times** <note>The planet ruling a specific period of the native's life.</note>, or if he possesses the spans of time divided to himself by a **full Moon**. If **Mars** is established in the **seventh place** while **Saturn** <note>original: "ħ"</note> is exactly in the **Ascendant** or at the **Midheaven**, and the **full Moon** moves toward **Mars**, or a **waning Moon** moves toward **Saturn**, misfortunes of great evils and deadly calamity are decreed: for then come accusations, then chains, then prisons, then condemnations, and then capital sentences are brought against him. For he is either thrown to the **beasts**, or cast down from **precipices**, or crushed by a **collapse**, or torn apart by **domestic plots**, or killed by **bandits**, or perishes in a **shipwreck**. But these things are decided by the nature and quality of the signs: for **Mars** positioned in **earthy signs** causes one to be thrown to wild beasts; in **solid signs**, to be crushed by a collapse or cast down a precipice; in **watery signs**, to be submerged in a shipwreck; but positioned in **human signs** <note>Signs depicting humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>, he causes one to perish by the **sword**. If the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is in **diameter** with him, or with him in the same sign, or in another **pivot** <note>original: "cardine" - the four main angles of the chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> of the birth chart, he causes them to be **burned alive**, so that in every way, positioned in this place, he destroys the person with miserable calamity and the mournful atrocity of a bitter life. But

<margin>**Mars** in the 7th pursues the place of the spouse and children.</margin>
before the final day of life, whoever has **Mars** in the **seventh place** of the birth chart will have their life driven by **fire, iron, violence**, or by **torments** or **homicides**. Furthermore, **Mars** established in the **seventh place** most vehemently persecutes the place of the **spouse** and the **children**.

**VIII** In the **eighth place** from the **Ascendant**, **Mars** established during a **day birth** either denies the resources of **patrimonies** <note>Inherited estates or family wealth.</note>, or causes those who have a patrimony to lose it through miserable **proscription** <note>The public identification and seizure of property by the state.</note>. If he has the **Sun** and the **Moon** in **diameter** to him, he decrees **blindness** through the extinguishing of the eyes. Positioned alone in this sign, he causes **poverty, distress, fevers, turmoils, seditions**, and **dangers**. If, when **Mars** is so positioned, the **Moon** is in the **ascent** of the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **second place** from the **Ascendant**—and the **Moon** joins herself to them with no radiation <note>Aspect or influence.</note>, but is rather estranged from them and does not see the **Ascendant**, he causes **violent deaths**, yet according to the nature and substance of the signs. For in **human signs**, as we said, if he is so positioned, the person will be killed by men with a **sword**, or will be slain by **pirates**, or **bandits**, or **household members**. Therefore, whoever has **Mars** thus will either kill or be struck by the sword by the sentence of a judge, being convicted of various and diverse crimes. Frequently, however, when positioned thus with the **Moon**, as we said, without the testimony of **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> or **Jupiter**, he makes **gladiators**, but those who perish in the sight of the people by a cruel and atrocious death. In **terrestrial signs**, he will cause one to be killed in **deserted places**, though first troubled by a multiple continuation of dangers. In **four-footed signs**, positioned with this radiation of the **Moon** we mentioned, he causes one to be submerged in **rivers, lakes**, or the **sea**, or causes those killed by pirates to be scattered by the waves and tides. In **solid signs**, he kills those who have fallen from **precipices**. In **fiery signs**, he causes them to be **burned**. During a **night birth**, however, positioned in this sign—that is, in the **eighth place** from the **Ascendant**—he will make people **clever, dangerous**, and **sharp-tongued**. He places those who have **Mars** thus in **public** or **distinguished acts**, but nonetheless decrees a **violent** or **sudden death**, just as those who are accustomed to perish from **apoplexy** <note>A sudden stroke or loss of consciousness.</note>. But if **Jupiter** regards **Mars** so positioned by any radiation, or if he is with him, these evils we have mentioned are mitigated for the most part. But if **Jupiter** is found likewise in the **Ascendant**, and the **Ascendant** itself is in a house of **Jupiter** or **Venus**, and that prosperous star joins itself to **Jupiter** by radiation and opposes the violence of **Mars** we have described, all these deadly calamities are changed for the better. For the mournful falls and the miserable inconveniences of misfortunes always decreed by **Mars** in this and other places are changed...

### BOOK THREE ###

...and they grow mild, if the impulses of **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> are most happily mitigated by the favorable testimony of **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>.

<margin>IX</margin>
**Mars** established in the **ninth place** <note>The 9th house, traditionally associated with travel, religion, and philosophy.</note> from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."</note> during the day will be favorable regarding life and glory. And if **Jupiter** is positioned in the **Ascendant** while **Mars** is in the ninth place, it makes men happy and those who may easily achieve all things. But if found during the night, with **Mars** in the ninth place and **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant**, it grants the greatest power of administration and the **right of the sword** <note>original: "ius gladii" — the legal authority to sentence people to death.</note>, and it causes the one so born to lead an army. Frequently, however, when positioned thus, he decrees troubles during travel. But if established in the ninth place in a house of **Mercury** <note>original: "☿" — Gemini or Virgo.</note> or **Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra.</note>, he makes for learned and famous orators. If, however, he is either in his own house, or in the house of **Saturn** <note>original: "♄" — Capricorn or Aquarius.</note>, or in his **exaltation** <note>The sign where a planet's influence is strongest; for Mars, this is Capricorn.</note>, and **Jupiter** is not placed in the **Ascendant**, he will make men who are terrifying to the gods and who condemn all kinds of perjurers. Moreover, they will be terrifying to all demons; the wicked spirits of demons flee their approach. Those who labor <note>meaning those possessed or suffering from spirits.</note> are freed by such men, not by the power of words, but by their mere presence; and even if it be a violent demon that shakes the body and soul of men, whether <margin>Exorcists.</margin> it be of the air, the earth, or the underworld, it will flee at this man's command, because it will be terrified by his precepts with a certain veneration. These are they who are called **exorcists** by the common people. But such a man will be one who has **Mars** in the ninth place, as we have said: he is easily able to purge and completely free a laboring man from every spirit of malignant demons by the authority of his command.

<margin>X</margin>
**Mars** established in the **tenth place** from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" — the highest point in the sky at the moment of birth.</note>—exactly in a nocturnal birth, if he is found in a masculine sign, in his own home or that of **Jupiter**, or in the kind we have mentioned, or in his exaltation: he will indeed make men who are dangerous and often deceived in various ways, but nonetheless governors, leaders, lords of life and death, and terrifying tribunes in provinces and cities. But if established in the **Midheaven** during the night in the kind of sign we have mentioned, and he receives the conjunction of the incoming **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, while **Jupiter** occupies another **angle** <note>The four critical points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart—and if he himself is nonetheless in his own house, or his exaltation, or his own **bounds** <note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by specific planets.</note>—he will produce powerful men, leaders, and lords of the whole world. But if the star of **Jupiter** deserts **Mars** when he is so positioned, and does not join him by any aspect, nor is found in the other angles of the birth chart, he will nonetheless produce armed men, commanders, tribunes, or leaders of a smaller place or of great provinces; and though they are established in a place of lesser dignity, they nonetheless possess the sword and the power of life and death. But if, with **Mars** thus established as we said, **Jupiter** is also positioned in the other angles of the birth chart in the signs and parts we mentioned, and **Saturn** is established in another angle of the birth chart, they will indeed be kings, emperors, powerful men, and greatly terrifying—the destroyers or builders of cities—but they will be **short-lived** <note>original: "oligochronii" — from the Greek meaning "of little time."</note>. Some, moreover, perish by an evil end; established in foreign places, they lose their life and kingdom alike, or die while placed under the power of another. If, however, **Mars** is found in the **Midheaven** in a feminine sign, namely in the sign of any star or his own or **Jupiter's** during the night, he will nonetheless make men shining with the highest honor; but in a masculine sign during the night, and established in the **Midheaven** in a feminine sign, he denies children. If, however, he is found in this place during the day—that is, in the **Midheaven**—he will make ineffective men, whom it befits to be hindered in all acts by various means; he also decrees the greatest losses and the loss of inheritance. He will also cause proscriptions and condemnations. For to some he indicates the burden of travel, on others he imposes the greatest necessities, others he compels to flee, for others he decrees exile, and others he causes to perish abroad or in exile far from their fatherland.

<margin>XI</margin>
**Mars** established in the **eleventh place** from the **Ascendant** decrees many good things, grants increases of inheritance, and gives love from the people. Frequently he even gives the insignia of the highest dignity, if **Jupiter** regards him so positioned with a favorable aspect while the **Moon** is waning, or if he is with him, or joins him in a **trine** <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> association; for then he makes judges possessing the **right of the sword** with the insignia of the greatest dignity.

<margin>XII</margin>
**Mars** established in the **twelfth place** from the **Ascendant**, if found in this place during the day, decrees the greatest illnesses, involves one in evil vices, and causes frequent plots from slaves; he makes such a person one whom slaves always desire to harm, and through his many slaves, he spreads infamy in all things. Frequently, moreover, on account of certain imprisoned persons, or those placed in custody...

But all these things are mitigated if **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, thus positioned, is found in a nocturnal birth chart <note>An astrological chart for someone born at night.</note>. We ought to hope in all birth charts and in all positions that **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are always favorable to **Mars** by any aspect and from any location. For then his impulses grow weak in whatever part they may be, when mitigated by the testimony of these stars.

But we must also hope that **Jupiter** does not occupy any pivot <note>The "pivots" (cardines) are the four most powerful houses: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart during the day. For if he is found by degree in some pivot during the day, he vents his rage in various ways against the one who is born. If **Mars** is positioned in a pivot and **Jupiter** joins him during the day, or if **Mars** is found in another pivot during the day and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> possesses another pivot of the birth chart, he will make

men who die a violent death <note>original: "biothanatos" — a term for those who die by execution, accident, or suicide.</note>, or who bring death upon themselves. If, however, **Mars** is established in a pivot during the day and **Venus** is found in another pivot, he causes the native to be wearied by the constant allurements of evils, and he makes them either the killers of their wives or those who bring death upon themselves. 

If **Mars** possesses any pivot of the birth chart during the day and **Venus** is established in another pivot, he will make the natives heart-sufferers <note>original: "cardiacos" — in ancient medicine, this referred to a dangerous condition involving heart palpitations or severe stomach distress.</note> and condemned by whatever means. If **Mars** is found in any pivot during the day and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in another pivot, he makes them always stripped of possessions in some way. If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> joins him with a similar aspect and with increasing light, he causes violent deaths and strikes down their mothers with a bitter death. But if the **Moon** is separated from him, and he himself is found in any pivot without the conjunction of any star during the day, he decrees the greatest illnesses, defects, sicknesses, and weaknesses. 

He rejoices, however, in always joining himself with the waning **Moon** and **Venus**.

For we have shown in the *Book of Institutions* (as you remember) that these three stars—that is, **Mars**, the **Moon**, and **Venus**, as well as **Saturn**—belong to the same condition <note>original: "conditionis" — referring to the astrological "sect" or group of planets that function better at night.</note>. Great dangers of Mars and Mercury in two pivots.
