For whatever evil exists in human affairs, all of it is decreed from that conjunction of stars. 

We must also remember that **Mars** established in the pivots during the day always denies offspring if the "Place of Children" <note>A specific mathematical point or house in the chart relating to family.</note> is found in his sign. For being established in the pivot himself, because he is the lord of that place, he will deny children. But if the Place of Children is found in another's house, and the lord of that sign is with **Mars**, or if the **Moon** regards him from an opposite or square aspect, he will deny children. 

If, however, by night he himself is the **Giver of Life** <note>original: "dator vitae" — the planet responsible for determining the native's lifespan.</note>, he grants a very long span of age. But if in a daytime birth, he causes those positioned in the first stage of life to perish. If another is the Giver of Life and **Mars** resists him through a square or opposite aspect, he will subtract fifteen years from the life that had been decreed. If he receives the **Moon** positioned in the middle between himself and **Saturn**, he weakens and cuts off a part of the body according to the nature of the sign in which the **Moon** is found. If he sees a waxing **Moon** through an opposite or square aspect, he will either kill those who are born immediately or cause them to be abandoned <note>original: "exponi" — the practice of leaving unwanted infants in the elements.</note>. But to grasp his power fully, you must diligently seek out the **twelfth-part** <note>original: "δωδεκατημόριον" (dodekatemorion) — a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign used for precision.</note> of **Mars** and its **terms** <note>original: "fines" — specific sub-divisions of signs ruled by different planets.</note> with skillful reasoning.

### THE DECREES OF THE SUN THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER VI. ###

**THE SUN** established in the degree of the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horoscopo"</note> will give difficult brothers. However, in a masculine sign, in his own house or **exaltation** <note>The sign where a planet's influence is at its peak; for the Sun, this is Aries.</note>, joined by the aspect of a favorable star and protected by good ones, he grants the emblems of great nobility. But if malefic stars approach the rays of the **Sun** when he is established in the **Ascendant**, they largely deprive the eyes of their sight. 

But because we have said that he decrees the greatest strokes of luck, we must explain everything in detail. When the **Sun** is established in the degree of the **Ascendant** in those parts we mentioned during the day, he will make **Emperors** and **Kings**; but if his power is slightly impeded, he will make **Consuls** and **Proconsuls**, and grant ordinary magistracies. If **Mars** aspects the **Sun** thus positioned, or if he is positioned with him, he decrees leadership, empires, and powers, but with the greatest envy and with great dangers, obstacles, fights, and difficulties. ...is found <note>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing from a discussion of the Sun's placement.</note>, specifically in a masculine sign, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☾"</note> is also in one of the pivots of the birth chart <note>The "pivots" (cardines) are the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>, at full light, or in the <term>anaphoras</term> <note>The houses that "rise up" after the pivots; also known as succedent houses.</note> of the pivots, it will cause the native to rule the whole world, or will establish them in such an administration of power that their authority—even if they are not the sovereign or king—shall be extended across the reaches of the entire world. 

But if **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is in the Midheaven <note>original: "M C"</note> or in the Descendant <note>the western horizon</note>, with the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> positioned as we have said, and the **Moon** is found with **Mars**, or in the Midheaven, at full light, or in the eighth house of the birth chart, it makes those born under this sign leaders, or kings, or administrators who are <term>biothanatos</term> <note>A Greek term for those who die a violent or unnatural death, such as by execution, accident, or suicide.</note>; or, having been captured for some reason, it will cause them to be struck down by an evil death, according to the nature and substance of the signs. It will also sometimes cause them to be stripped of their honors and cast down from all power. 

But even if **Mars** is not joined with the **Moon** in the way we described, but is found alone in the pivots of the birth chart, or in their <term>cataphoras</term> <note>The houses that "fall away" from the pivots; also known as cadent houses.</note> or <term>anaphoras</term>, while the **Sun** is established in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "horosc." (horoscopus)</note> as we said before, nonetheless those who are born will be leaders, or kings, or administrators who become captives or <term>biothanatos</term>, or are deposed from power with the greatest disgrace. 

However, if the **Sun** is found in the degree of the <term>ascendant</term> and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> likewise possesses the Midheaven, it similarly produces kings, leaders, and very powerful administrators. But if the **Sun** is so placed, and **Saturn** is found in the second house from the <term>ascendant</term> or in the eighth, and the **Moon** is at full light in other pivots, or in the second house from the <term>ascendant</term>, or in the eighth with **Mars**, it makes the natives kings, leaders, or administrators who are <term>biothanatos</term>, exiles, and captives. 

If indeed the **Sun** alone is found in the degree of the <term>ascendant</term> in the signs we mentioned (for this is worth remembering), and **Mars** is found in the <term>anaphora</term> of the **Moon**, and the **Moon** is established in the other pivots or their <term>anaphoras</term>, it will similarly make those born kings, leaders, or administrators who are <term>biothanatos</term>, or it will force them to be deprived of this honor. 

But if the **Sun** is found in the degree of the <term>ascendant</term>, and the **Moon** is found in the other pivots of the birth chart, or in their <term>anaphoras</term> or <term>cataphoras</term>, and **Mars** joins itself to them by no aspect <note>original: "radiatione"</note>, but the star **Jupiter** is either established with the **Sun** in the degree of the <term>ascendant</term>, or found in the other pivots, or in their <term>anaphoras</term> or <term>cataphoras</term>, those who are born will hold the rudders of the whole world as kings, destroying some cities and raising up others. 

If, however, **Mars** is so positioned that he looks upon the **Sun**, the **Moon**, and **Jupiter**, or is positioned with them, or is found in the pivots, or established in their <term>anaphoras</term> or <term>cataphoras</term>, he will cause evil deaths for those we have described; he also decrees defects and illnesses according to the nature of the signs and those parts of the body which we have said are divided among the signs. 

If, with all these positioned as we have said, **Saturn** is found in their <term>anaphoras</term> or in the <term>cataphoras</term> of the pivots, they will not have an empire as great as we described, yet it will make them men of the greatest power, or famous judges, or commanders of great legions, or tribunes—effective and terrible men, yet not persevering in these dignities and powers; for it will either make them captives, or drive them into exile, or cause them to perish easily as <term>biothanatos</term>. 

When the **Sun** is positioned in the sign of the <term>ascendant</term> <term>platically</term> <note>original: "platiue/platice" — meaning by sign rather than by exact degree.</note>, it makes those born free-born and noble. Also, with the **Sun** positioned <term>platically</term> in the sign of the <term>ascendant</term>, if **Jupiter**, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are in the other pivots of the birth chart, it will make great men, for whom the greatest happiness of goods is prepared by their parents, and who from their earliest age grow in good and prosperous circumstances, so that they are always far from the onset of poverty. 

But if, with all these so positioned, **Saturn** looks upon them from a <term>trine</term> <note>original: "trigono" — an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very favorable.</note> or a <term>sextile</term> <note>original: "hexagono" — an aspect of 60 degrees, also favorable.</note>, or even if he is positioned together with them, perpetual happiness is decreed for them. 

But if all are so positioned—that is, the **Sun** in the sign of the ascendant, **Jupiter**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** in the pivots, and **Saturn** in a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> or in the same place with them—and **Mars** looks upon them with this aspect, or is positioned with them, or sees them all from a <term>square</term> <note>original: "quadrato" — a 90-degree aspect, usually difficult.</note> or from an <term>opposition</term> <note>original: "diametro" — an 180-degree aspect.</note> and joins himself to this mixture of stars, he will make very great judges, powerful men having the power of life and death, but also thieves, predators, and those who seize the property of others by a greedy instinct of desire. Nevertheless, after great plunder, robberies, and immense crimes, this makes them exiles or <term>biothanatos</term>. 

If the **Sun** is found in the sign of the ascendant by night, it causes the native to be born of a lowlier sort. But if by night, with the **Sun** established in the ascendant, **Saturn** or **Mars** look upon it through a <term>square</term> or <term>opposition</term>, or are together with it, and it joins itself to them by whatever aspect...

<margin>II</margin> When the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **second house** <note>The "second place" from the horoscope (Ascendant) traditionally governs wealth and livelihoods.</note> from the Ascendant, it makes people who seek their inheritance through their own efforts, and who are pleasant and good throughout their lives. However, if **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> or **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> look upon the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> in this position with a favorable **aspect** <note>original: "radiatione"</note>, either from a **trine** <note>an angle of 120 degrees</note> or a **sextile** <note>an angle of 60 degrees</note>, or if they are placed in the same sign with it, it will grant some sudden goods and no small increase in happiness. Indeed, it will cause men who were lowly and cast down to be raised to a public increase in dignity. But this is granted to them only through great labor and with the greatest difficulty, and often with the voluntary loss of their inheritance. Therefore, whoever has the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> positioned in this way should desire nothing and dare no great thing, since he should know that with the **Sun** so placed, he is unhappily hindered in all his actions.

<margin>III</margin> When the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **third house** from the Ascendant, it decrees a bad death for the father. However, they will be slow to acquire a wife and children. But if, in the third house of the birth chart, the Sun is placed in its own house, or if **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are there, or if it is in its own **exaltation** <note>The "height" or sign where a planet's power is most intensified.</note> or the exaltation of **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or **Mercury**, it will produce religious people and worshippers of the gods. These are people who dedicate statues of the gods (including those they have made themselves) with religious consecrations, and who preside over the construction of temples by order of princes or judges. But if it is placed in other signs, as we have said, it results in lowly offices in temples, or some form of servile service. <margin>IV</margin> When the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned specifically in the **fourth house** from the Ascendant, if it is struck by any aspect from **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> or **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, it decrees first the death of the father and the ruin of the entire family line, or the loss of the entire inheritance. <margin>V</margin> When the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **fifth house** from the Ascendant, it makes people lovable, honored, and those who easily obtain all things, and to whom everything is granted through the protection of friends. Furthermore, those who have the **Sun** and **Jupiter** in this way will be established alongside kings for the sake of their learning and mastery, if the star of **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> joins them. **Mercury** will also do this if he is found far from the rays of the **Sun**, and if **Mars**, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, **Jupiter**, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> gaze upon him in his position with a good **aspect** <note>original: "radiatione"</note> without envy.

<margin>11th</margin>
The **Sun** positioned in the **eleventh house** from the **Ascendant** makes people happy and noble, whose fathers are decorated with the greatest splendor of honor; in the course of time, they will receive increases in happiness and dignity. If, however, the **Sun** is found in the eleventh house and malevolent stars are with him or joined by some ray, they will not harm his actions or honors, but the persistence of a bitter decree will affect only the area of children.

<margin>12th</margin>
The **Sun** positioned in the **twelfth house** from the **Ascendant** will make people low-born and frequently slaves or captives; it also decrees the death of the father, the loss of the entire inheritance, a sad life, and serious illnesses. Even if a benevolent star is found with the **Sun** in that place, it will nevertheless cause great lack of nobility. If a malevolent star is found with the **Sun** in this place, it decrees perpetual illnesses, great defects, and lifelong servitude. If the **Moon** (☽) should join her, they will achieve positions of administration and glory, though accompanied by great envy. <margin>VI</margin>
In the **Sixth House** <note>The House of Health and Service, often associated with challenges or "falling" away from the Ascendant.</note>, if **Venus** is established by day or by night, she will grant ignoble wives, or widows, or those who are infirm and never obedient to their husbands—provided that no other planet is found in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" (Medium Coeli); the highest point in the sky at the time of birth, representing career and public reputation.</note>. If, however, a woman has the planet **Venus** located in the sixth place of her birth chart, she will suffer great difficulties and great dangers in childbirth; for she will either miscarry frequently, or endure a difficult labor, or the fetus will be brought forth by physicians after being torn apart within her womb. But if **Venus** is established in the sixth place from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."; the rising sign.</note> in a nocturnal birth, and some planet is found in the **Midheaven**, she will make the subjects pleasing and graceful, with wives who are obedient to them; happiness will be granted to them, and they shall achieve everything they desire. <margin>VII</margin>
In the **Seventh House** <note>The House of Marriage and Partnerships.</note>, if **Venus** is established in her own sign <note>Taurus or Libra.</note> by night, she will grant a happy old age; however, she grants a wife later in life and decrees that children are difficult to obtain for those who have **Venus** positioned so. Furthermore, she will cause them to labor under the greatest infamies regarding sexual matters <note>original: "rebus uenereis"; matters of Venus, referring to sex or love affairs.</note>, according to the nature and quality of the sign. If **Saturn** (♄) should look upon **Venus** and **Mars** so positioned in the signs we have mentioned—either by square, opposition, or being located together—women who have **Venus** in this planetary association will be impure and unchaste, and will consort with other women for the sake of lust. These vices will be stronger if this planetary mixture occurs in **Capricorn** (♑) or **Aries** (♈).

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the **Eighth House** <note>Commonly associated with death, inheritance, and shared resources.</note>, if **Venus** is established in a daytime birth, she will grant a wife late; and when she does, it will be one who is either low-born, a widow, sterile, or deformed by some heavy foulness. But if **Jupiter** (♃) is with her, or if a malefic planet looks upon **Venus** and **Mercury** (☿) in this place (either by square or opposition, or if found with them in this place), the entire patrimony of the native is dissipated or stripped away by some manner of proscription. Their death is said to come through "gonorrhea" <note>original: "gonorream"; in ancient medicine, this referred to a "flow of seed" or involuntary loss of semen, thought to be a wasting disease.</note>, or through contraction, spasm, or apoplexy. If, however, she is found in this place by night, she will make them wealthy and grant happiness through the death of great women; death for these individuals is decreed to be swift, without pain or any torment.

<margin>IX</margin>
In the ****Ninth House** <note>The House of Travel, Religion, and Philosophy.</note>, if **Venus** is established in a daytime birth, she will cause the native to be struck by the constant intervention of a certain spirit <note>original: "dæmonis"; not necessarily an evil demon, but a guiding or haunting spirit.</note>; she will also cause them to remain in temples in a filthy state, and to walk about in such a manner forever, never cutting their hair, and wishing to announce things to men as if spoken by the gods—such as those who are accustomed to prophesy in temples. **Venus** thus positioned also frequently produces interpreters of dreams. These traits will be stronger if **Saturn** (♄) looks upon **Venus** with some radiation. But if she is found in this place in a nocturnal birth, she will make them divine worshippers of the gods, who study sacred rites and religions. To some, she grants offices and gifts from the temples. If, however, in a night birth, **Mars** (♂) and **Saturn** (♄) look upon her by opposition or square, or are positioned together with her, they will cause the native to be agitated by women, or to have heavy misfortunes brought upon them by women, to whom they themselves are always ungrateful—especially if she is found in tropical signs with this planetary society. 

If, however, the planet **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon **Venus** so positioned from a **trine** <note>120 degrees apart.</note> or **sextile** <note>60 degrees apart.</note>, or is found with her, it will make them beloved by women, charming, and pleasing; they will easily obtain everything from them and will dominate their wife's affairs. Some will take up the care of women or act as their managers; others with **Venus** thus positioned will persevere in the palaces of kings or the houses of powerful men for the sake of manufacturing those things which are necessary for the adornment of women.

**Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly in the degree of the horoscope <note>The "horoscope" here refers to the Ascendant or 1st House, representing the self and physical body.</note>, in those signs in which he rejoices during a daytime birth, will produce philosophers, masters of the grammatical art, geometers, those who often treat of celestial matters, or those who are so suited to this that they can perceive the presence of the gods. Or, he makes them experts in sacred letters, and frequently orators and lawyers, especially if he is found in this place, or in his own signs, or in other local places. If **Mercury** (☿) is so positioned, and the **Sun** (☉) or **Saturn** (♄) or **Jupiter** (♃) look upon him in a daytime birth, they will make great men who are crowned with sacred and glorious lineages; they also make such men to whom the greatest business of emperors is entrusted. But if **Mercury** (☿) is so positioned and **Mars** (♂) looks upon him from a square or diameter <note>Aspects of 90 degrees or 180 degrees, traditionally considered harsh or challenging.</note>, so that he is found exactly with him in the horoscope, he will cast down the one so born with a manifold succession of evils; for the evils that arise from this conjunction of **Mercury** (☿) and **Mars** (♂) cannot be defined or described.

If **Mercury** (☿) is found exactly in the horoscope in a nocturnal birth, he will make them divine in their senses, and people who always achieve everything they want through the easiest reasoning; he also renders them honest and grave in character. He also makes them overseers of accounts, or those who handle the business of contracts, or grain, or taxes, or trade, or banking, or moneylending, and such matters. Positioned thus at night, he also frequently makes interpreters for Emperors or the most powerful judges, but he decrees all these things according to the difference and quality of the signs.

<margin>The varied nature of Mercury.</margin>
But because we have said that **Mercury** (☿) joins itself to all things by an easy radiation, and is good with the good and equally evil with the evil, we must now explain what it decrees in nativities <note>original: "genituris" — birth charts or the act of being born.</note> when in the company of each planet. For by day, if positioned with **Jupiter** (♃) and with the **Sun** (☉) in favorable places of the birth chart, it decrees the greatest happiness. If, however, it is found with **Mars** (♂) by day, it will cause the greatest calamities of misfortune; by night, it is likewise changed by the same reasoning. For with **Mercury** (☿) and the **Moon** (☽) it is good, but with the **Sun** (☉) it decrees the greatest evils and misfortunes. To teach this more clearly, we must explain everything specifically. But first, one must diligently seek the twelfth-part <note>original: "δωδεκατημόριον" (dodekatemorion) — an astrological technique where each 30-degree sign is divided into 12 parts of 2.5 degrees each.</note> of **Mercury** (☿) and its bounds <note>term: "fines" — specific degree-ranges within a sign ruled by different planets.</note>, so that you may reach all the secrets of the birth chart.

->MERCURY WITH THE SUN THROUGH THE TWELVE<-
->STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER IX.<-

<margin>The first place of Mercury with the Sun.</margin>
If **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) by day exactly <note>original: "partiliter" — by exact degree.</note> in the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopo" — the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note>, it will produce kings, leaders, and powerful men; but by night, it will render the father degenerate and ignoble, and these people will be learned in the public arts but secretive and wretched, according however to the quality and nature of the signs.

<margin>II</margin>
In the second house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it decrees the increase of patrimony and designates leadership in certain actions by its happy radiation.

<margin>III</margin>
In the third house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it will produce soothsayers, interpreters of dreams, divine physicians, augurs, astrologers, mathematicians <note>In this era, "mathematicus" was a common term for a professional astrologer.</note>, and those who always predict the future, and whose art and practice are very easily brought to the notice of all.

<margin>IIII</margin>
In the fourth house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it will produce ignoble and secretive people, or those skilled in illicit arts, yet honorable and serious. If they are so positioned in the fourth house of the birth chart, it must be greatly considered in which sign they are placed and who is the lord of that sign; for it is especially dangerous if, in this place, **Mercury** (☿) is found with the **Sun** (☉) while positioned in the house of **Saturn** (♄).

<margin>V</margin>
In the fifth house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it will produce noble people and those who easily accomplish everything, but they are dangerous and do not have perpetual happiness, and they deceive and trick many men by easy reasoning.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the sixth house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it will produce ignoble, enslaved, industrious, and lazy people, whose fathers are unknown, orphans, slow in actions, and who can achieve nothing—and this is if no star is found in the tenth house from the Ascendant. If, however, some star is found in the tenth house from the Ascendant, divine signs of nobility and glory are conferred, especially if a benevolent star is also positioned in that same place.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the seventh house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant—that is, in the setting <note>The 7th house is the West, where the sun sets.</note>—if found in this place by day, it will cause the greatest affairs and powers to be entrusted to those so born, but at last it will cause them to perish by an unnatural death. If, however, it is positioned exactly in this place by night, it will cause them to suffer many evils while toiling, seeking food through daily labor, and always occupied in evil and sordid actions; for their arts will be either sordid, or filthy, or of a heavy odor, from which perpetual vigils are required of the workers, such as tanners, fullers, wool-workers, painters, cooks, and those similar to these; yet it will make them astrologers, though certainly prone to vice in their early age.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the eighth house, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with the **Sun** (☉) exactly from the Ascendant, it will produce weak and prone to vice men, and those who deceive by easy reasoning: also victims of unnatural death, and those who frequently fall into insanity.

### ->MERCURY WITH THE MOON, THROUGH THE TWELVE STATIONS OF THE HEAVENS. CHAPTER X.<-

<margin>The first station of Mercury with the Moon.</margin>

However, various hindrances will sometimes happen to them from such a cause.

## MERCURY WITH SATURN THROUGH THE TWELVE 
### STATIONS OF THE HEAVENS. CHAPTER XI.

<margin>Mercury with Saturn in the Ascendant</margin> **MERCURY** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree in the area of the **Ascendant**, in a daytime birth <note>original: "diurna genitura"</note>, will produce hoarders of money, advocates, legal experts, or scribes, but they will be sluggish and those who quickly fail. If, however, they are positioned in this place by night, they will make slaves or captives out of free-born men, as powerful vices hand them over to serve for the sake of captivity. But if they are found in a feminine sign in a nocturnal birth, they will produce eunuchs, or men without seed who are unable to perform the sexual act—likewise shameful, infamous, unchaste, and effeminate <note>original: "cinaedos"—a term used in antiquity for men who did not conform to traditional gender roles, often with a derogatory social connotation.</note>.

<margin>II</margin> In the second house from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree in a daytime birth will make herbalists, doctors, and those through whom health is restored to men; they will also be wealthy and famous in their actions. However, depending on the quality of the signs, they will frequently be orators or agents of powerful men. But if they are found in this place by night, it will produce beggars, the insane, the destitute, or temple slaves; frequently they will cause men to be accused and placed in custody—always mournful, however, and without children, and weak in some part of the body, or it will make them entangled in certain crimes and vices.

<margin>III</margin> In the third house from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree will produce divers, those lifting water from deep wells, gardeners, managers of small villas, or undertakers <note>original: "pollinctores"—those who prepared the dead for the funeral pyre or burial</note>, and tomb-keepers, guardians of dead bodies, or doorkeepers of sepulchers.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the fourth house from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) and **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree will make masters of illicit and hidden arts, or those privy to them, and those who seek their daily life from evil arts. But some having **Mercury** with **Saturn** thus will either be in custody or be condemned for some reason; however, all actions are found according to the nature and quality of the signs, and according to the logic of the other stars.

<margin>V</margin> In the fifth house from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree will make those who frequently change their dwellings; but it will make overseers of provisions, or of grain, or of certain places, and prefects of gems, pearls, or spices, or of metals, and sculptors of sacred objects.

<margin>VI</margin> In the sixth house from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned at the exact degree, if found in this place by day, will make those knowledgeable in many doctrines and powerful in the teaching of hidden arts, and those who wish to know everything that exists in human affairs; but they will be truly ambitious and envious, and those entangled in many vices and illnesses. By night, however, those positioned in this place will produce authors of forged documents <note>original: "falsarum litterarum"</note>, the wicked, the malicious, the malevolent, sorcerers, and those who are always entangled in the greatest evils and necessities. ### MERCURY WITH MARS THROUGH THE TWELVE STATIONS OF THE HEAVEN, CHAPTER 13

<image-desc>Decorative ornamental drop cap 'M' featuring a figure amidst architectural scrollwork and foliage.</image-desc>

<margin>Mercury with Mars in the Ascendant</margin> **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂), if positioned in the degree of the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>—specifically in a daytime birth chart <term>genitura: a birth chart or nativity</term>—will produce people who rise in status <note>original: "anaphoricos", which can also refer to the astrological Second House</note>, those with heart ailments <term>cardiacos: referring to stomach or heart distress</term>, the short-lived <term>oligochronios: having a brief lifespan</term>, and the unhappy. For he will cause them to be falsely condemned or to die a violent death <term>biothanatos: one who dies by execution, suicide, or an unnatural end</term>, either due to women, the enticements of love, hidden writings, or sorcery. But if they are found by night at the exact degree <term>partiliter: at the same numerical degree within a sign</term> in the **Ascendant**, they will produce great men, leaders of great religions, generals, protectors, heralds, or attendants, the highest administrators of emperors, and those upon whom the greatest happiness is bestowed following the outcome of battles. If, however, **Saturn** (♄) should aspect them when they are so positioned by night from a square <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful.</note> or from an opposition <note>An aspect of 180 degrees, suggesting conflict.</note>, he will make them dangerous people who are very often deceived and hindered in all their actions; for **Saturn** so positioned makes men sluggish and weighed down by every burden of unhappiness.

<margin>II</margin> In the second place <note>The house of wealth and resources.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂) positioned at the exact degree in a daytime birth will cause children to be exposed <note>The ancient practice of abandoning unwanted infants in a public place.</note>. If they are raised, he will make them fugitives for some reason, frequently exiles, and sometimes captives; he will cause many to be stripped of their property by proscription <note>State-sanctioned seizure of property.</note>. He entangles some in grave illnesses and physical defects; he will cause others to die a violent death, especially if one or both planets are radiated by the light of the full **Moon** (☽). But if they are found thus by night, they make men of evil mind, malicious, obscure, fearful, and those who are deceived in all their actions. Yet he will make their activities multifaceted, for they will be tax collectors <term>publicani: private contractors who collected Roman taxes</term>, toll-gatherers, or imperial agents <term>curiosi: high-level government inspectors or spies</term>; some they will render mentally insane or frantic.

<margin>III</margin> In the third place <note>The house of siblings and travel.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂) positioned at the exact degree will cause one to have the substance of life from sacrifices or festive activities. Such people will be those who predict the future and who are always found in temples, but they will be terrifying to everyone with whom they do business; even if they know nothing or do nothing, they will nonetheless, in the process of time, obtain many increases in happiness.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the fourth place <note>The house of home, family, and the end of life.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂) will make people lazy and humble in all their actions and in every fortune, and those who engage in constant enmities with their parents or relatives, such that the greatest losses and traps are always brought upon them by those very people. They will be legal guarantors <note>Those who take responsibility for another's debts.</note> and, as a result of this, will be shattered by the greatest dangers and fall into humility and poverty. When this happens to them, they will be the authors of certain illicit arts, whence they are caught as intermediaries or accomplices in certain evils and are entangled in the greatest snares of danger, so that they are punished by a sentence of condemnation. Others, placed in these calamities, are overwhelmed by the onslaught of great and long-lasting illness, especially if the **Moon** (☽) aspects them while so positioned from an opposition or a square. However, if in the fourth house of the birth chart **Mercury**, **Mars**, and the **Moon** are found thus by night, they also produce governors, tribunes, generals, powerful men, and administrators—but for the most part, these people perish shamefully by a violent death.

<margin>V</margin> In the fifth place <note>The house of children and pleasure.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂) positioned at the exact degree renders people strong, manly, athletes, and undefeated in all contests, but they will be moved to various places for the sake of a home. The greatest favor of food and grain will be granted to them from the treasury or public stores. He makes them superior in every contest and utterly terrifying to their adversaries.

<margin>VI</margin> In the sixth place <note>The house of health and service.</note> from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) and **Mars** (♂) positioned at the exact degree, if they are in these places by day, decree the greatest ill health and defects. They also cause one to be placed in custody and to have knowledge of prison, and to be condemned by whatever accusation; for they are either attacked, or informed upon, or bound by the false deceptions of crimes. They are attacked or informed upon either by slaves, or through slaves, or by slavish men, or by those who are placed in custody because of some crime, so that they perish with the greatest torture, violence, and atrocity—especially if the full **Moon** (☽) aspects them from any part while they are in these places. If, however, they are positioned in this place by night, they make people entangled in many debts and high interest on loans <term>foenore: the charging of interest on money</term>, causing anxiety of mind and thefts. They render them lazy in all acts and produce the greatest accusations and heavy envy, but which either from slaves...

In the seventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with **Mars** (♂) by exact degree <term>partiliter: at the same numerical degree within a sign</term>, and they are found in this place during a daytime birth, they compel those who have this alignment to kill their own woman or wife with their own hand. They will cause them—either because of a woman, a wife, or the desires of some perverse love—to kill themselves or others, or because of some such crime, to be placed in public custody or in prison, and to be condemned based on that accusation. But generally, whoever has **Mercury** (☿) and **Mars** (♂) thus, will commit homicides and meet deaths according to the quality of the signs. For they will either be muggers, robbers, assassins <term>sicarii: daggermen or contract killers</term>, or pirates, or similar to these, and those caught in these crimes are punished by the severe execution of a lasting sentence. In a nighttime birth <term>genitura</term>, however, those so positioned will be cheated by women in unjust acts, or be joined to viragos <note>original: "viraginibus" – women who behave with masculine strength or aggression</note>, and father children by them, and finally and always be involved in great and most wicked vices.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the eighth place from the **Ascendant**, if **Mercury** (☿) is found positioned with **Mars** (♂) by degree in a daytime birth, he will make such people unable to achieve anything they desire, but rather dangerous individuals who lose their entire inheritance fundamentally. They may be inventors or executors of wicked deeds, also torturers, or executioners, or traitors of their own people, acquiring for themselves the greatest substance of fortune and wealth from these arts; but a violent death will come to them, either with certain heavy tortures, or they will die suffering from the heavy vice of insanity.

<margin>IX</margin>
In the ninth place from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) positioned with **Mars** (♂) by degree will make people unjust, irreligious, and perjurers; nevertheless, they may be ministers of the gods even with this error of mind, but they will be those who despoil and strip the very gods they serve, so that they might turn the control of temples into their own plunder. From these misfortunes, their money is so dissipated that they are shaken by the heavy interest of usury; but also by some pledge or guarantee <term>fideiussione: a legal surety or bail</term>, they are oppressed by heavy types of losses or condemnations. But **Mercury** (☿) with **Mars** (♂) decrees diverse and manifold types of acts or administrations, for this variety arises according to the quality and substance of the signs. In the sixth place from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, **Mercury** (☿) positioned with **Venus** (♀) by exact degree <term>partiliter: at the same numerical degree within a sign</term>, in a birth chart for a long life, determines the resources of one's substance through accounts, or business dealings by calculation, or through training, or even from the revenue of the gods <note>Likely referring to income from temple service or religious endowments</note>, especially if, with them so positioned, some star is found in the tenth house of the birth chart; but these men will obtain a wife with difficulty. For they will be lustful, and because of that matter, somewhat infamous. But if a star is there, it will make those who seek much through their own labor; for they will be travelers, merchants, governors, shipmasters, and smiths of gold. If, however, **Mercury** is an evening star in this place and found with **Venus**, he will make them sensible, ingenious, musicians, or makers of instruments, or dyers of colors, or merchants of spices, gems, or pearls; some he will make perfume-sellers <term>myropolas: sellers of ointments or perfumes</term>, or inventors of medicinal pigments, and frequently overseers of mines, so that from these activities, the greatest support of resources or riches may be conferred upon them.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the seventh place from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) positioned with **Venus** (♀) by exact degree determines the defects of hidden health; for it will make them suffer from liver disease <term>epaticos</term>, or frenzy <term>phreneticos</term>, or melancholy <term>melancholicos</term>, and things similar to these; they are also always alienated from the affection of a wife, and infamous until the final time of their life. If, however, it is found in this place with **Venus** by night, the greatest substance of riches will be conferred upon them by women or wives, and by the gradual process of age they will obtain great honors and the insignias of the greatest happiness, especially if, when they are so positioned, **Mars** (♂) and **Saturn** (♄)—and specifically **Saturn**—should look upon them from no direction. For if **Mars** and **Saturn** are joined by some aspect <term>radiatione: an astrological aspect or "beaming"</term> to them while so positioned, all these things we have mentioned will be turned into the contrary.

<margin>VIII</margin>
<margin>viii</margin>
In the eighth place from the **Ascendant**, **Mercury** (☿) positioned with **Venus** (♀) by exact degree, if both are evening stars in a day birth, will render men ineffective and cut off <term>apocopos: literally "cut off," often meaning eunuchs or those who are impotent</term>, and those who can achieve nothing. They also make those who are always lustful, entangled in business, defective in mind and body, and who obtain marriage with difficulty; for they will be sterile and unable to produce offspring. They will die from either spasms <term>spathici</term>, or wasting disease <term>colobici</term>, or apoplexy <term>apopletici</term>, or frenzy <term>phrenetici</term>. If, however, **Mercury** as a morning star is positioned with **Venus** in this place, it will produce those who learn much and know all things, even inventors of things, and those who obtain whatever they wish most easily, and perceive the increase of their inheritance through the passage of time.

<margin>IX</margin>

For they will make either priests, or those positioned in temples who predict the future, or diviners <term>aruspicis</term>, or astrologers <term>astrologos</term>, augurs, or magicians <term>magos</term>, or those who are accustomed to explain all things.

<margin>X</margin>

**XI** In the eleventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, **Mercury** and **Venus** positioned together will produce those who handle the business of women, and to whom the assets of women are entrusted. **XII** In the twelfth place from the **Ascendant**, if **Mercury** and **Venus** are found there in a daytime birth, they will produce lovers and those suffering from the vice of scandalous passions. These people will be conspicuous and known to all for these affairs, yet the stars will compel them to be completely carried away by these vices; and, having been condemned by such a reputation, they will perish as a **biothanatos** <term>biothanatos: one who dies a violent or unnatural death</term>. If, however, they are found in this place in a nighttime birth, they will suffer many persecutions from unworthy women, or they may acquire prostitutes through the instinct of love with a man acting as a middleman, and they will be occupied with multiple legal proceedings arising from these acts. They are the sort who frequently fall away from their intended purpose, and who are often deceived in their accounts—whether in their actions, business, or resources—or are accustomed to being defrauded by traps. Having finished with the specific decrees for **Mercury** in conjunction with all the planets, let us now return to where we left off: the decrees of the **Moon**, through the individual houses.

### THE DECREES OF THE MOON THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY, CHAPTER XV.

<margin>Read in this [place], or certainly the first, or in this place. <note>original: "In isto uel certe primo, uel hoc loco legēdum." This is likely a philological note regarding a textual variant.</note></margin>

**I** The **Moon** positioned by exact degree <term>partiliter: at the same numerical degree within a sign</term> in the **Ascendant** in a night birth—if found full and in the signs in which she rejoices—decrees great increases in fortune and makes one always superior to one’s brothers in both age and merit. If, however, she is found by exact degree in the fifth place during a day birth, she will produce captains of great ships. But if, with the **Moon** so positioned, **Saturn** occupies another angle of the birth chart—that is, if they regard each other from a square or a diameter <term>aspects of 90 or 180 degrees</term>, or if they are found together—they will produce pirates, famous for the atrocity of their cruel savagery, or judges presiding over inaccessible places. If, when the **Moon** is so placed with malefic stars, no benevolent star regards her, she will cause those born then to be exposed <note>A reference to the Roman practice of infant exposure</note>, or she decrees no length of life for them, but causes them to perish immediately, or threatens an evil end to life and a violent death.

**II** The **Moon** positioned in the second place from the **Ascendant** in a night birth will make people famous and conspicuous in their actions, but also lustful and devoted to the pleasant delights of luxury; they are those to whom a greater ancestral inheritance is granted over the course of time. If, however, she is found in this place during a day birth, she will either kill the parents immediately, or divide the child from the parents, or cause the parents to be separated by a dissolved marriage, and the ancestral inheritance to be diminished by various kinds of losses. Such people who have the **Moon** thus are also occupied by constant travels, and they divide their activities across many places, but their life is always subject to someone else. If, however, she is in this place with her light diminished <note>waning</note>, and **Saturn** is positioned in this part or in the sign of the **Ascendant**, she causes blindness from sudden wounds to the eyes. But if, with the **Moon** so positioned, **Mars** is found in the degree or sign of the **Ascendant**, he will cause pains in the joints, dislocations, or fractures; others he weakens with the persistence of hemorrhoids.

**III** The **Moon** positioned in the third place from the **Ascendant** indicates an ignoble mother, or one polluted by some stain of infamy. If, however, she is found in this place with **Jupiter**, she provides nourishment to those who have her thus, either from the treasury or from the public grain supplies. If **Jupiter**, positioned with the **Moon** in this place, joins himself to **Mercury** by some radiation <note>an astrological aspect</note>, they make high priests of some very great goddess, or priests of a most powerful religion, or those who organize or correct public religious rites. If, however, **Venus** is then found with the **Moon** in this place, they will have business involving pigments, spices, wine, or flowers. But if, in a night birth, the **Moon** is found in this place with **Saturn** alone, she will make people slow, who achieve nothing of what they desire, and who utter sacrilegious words regarding religions, and upon whom the wrath of the gods brings the greatest misfortunes. If, however, the **Moon** is found in this place during a day birth with **Mercury** and **Mars**, she will produce sacrilegious people, unjust plunderers of temples, the impious, the irreligious, murderers, and thoroughly evil men.

<margin>VII</margin> When the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **Descendant** <term>occasu: the western horizon where stars set</term>—if in a nighttime birth she is found exactly in this place, in those signs in which she is exalted or rejoices, and with increasing light, and if **Jupiter** (♃) or **Venus** (♀) aspects her with favorable rays, she will grant a happy old age, profit from women, and decree suitable marriages. If, however, she is oppressed in this place by the rays of malevolent planets, especially in a daytime birth and diminished in light, she will give a wife late in life; and when she does give one, she will be low-born, a widow, sterile, or deformed with a heavy foulness, or the marriage will please him in no way.

<margin>VIII</margin> When the **Moon** (☽) is found exactly in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**, she will give a man an inheritance from the dead, but death is decreed for him quickly and without great pain or torment. But if **Mars** (♂) or **Saturn** (♄) aspects her from a **square** or **opposition** <note>original: "de quadrato, siue diametro"</note>, it will grant destruction and a fall from one's usual status, and when so positioned, she frequently creates "lunatics" <note>This term historically referred to those with epilepsy or mental health struggles believed to be influenced by the moon's phases.</note>.

<margin>IX</margin> When the **Moon** (☽) is positioned exactly in the ninth house from the **Ascendant** in a daytime birth, it will cause the one who has the **Moon** (☽) so to dwell meanly in temples, and to be those who wish to announce something to men as if spoken by the gods. If, however, she is found in this place in a nighttime birth, she will make divine worshippers of the gods and those who study sacred rites and religions, and to some she grants offices or gifts from the temples; but she will also give many anxieties and travels through various regions. And if this is the house of **Mercury** (☿), she will give **astronomy**; if of **Venus** (♀), songs and joy; if of **Mars** (♂), the work of arms and instruments; if of **Jupiter** (♃), divine worship and knowledge in the law; if of **Saturn** (♄), the knowledge of **alchemy** <note>original: "scientiam alchimiæ"</note>; if of the **Sun** (☉), foresight regarding livestock; but if it is the sign of **Cancer** (♋)—her own house—she will give knowledge of all things that come from the water.

<margin>X</margin> When the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the tenth house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **Midheaven** <term>M C: Medium Coeli, the highest point of the chart</term>—if she is found exactly there in a nighttime birth, in those signs in which she is exalted or rejoices (that is, with increasing light), and if **Jupiter** (♃) protects her with favorable rays, she will produce the greatest emperors or powerful administrators, to whom the **power of life and death** <note>original: "uitæ & necis potestas"</note> is easily entrusted; she also gives ordinary consulships when so positioned. If, however, she precedes or follows the degree of the Midheaven, yet is positioned in the nearest place and neighboring degrees, she will produce leaders, tribunes, and administrators; but if she is positioned generally <term>platice: within the same zodiac sign but not at the exact degree</term> in the same sign in which the Midheaven is located, she makes them great in all actions and adorned with various kinds of happiness. If, however, with the **Moon** (☽) so positioned, **Saturn** (♄) occupies another angle of the birth chart, she decrees envies and misfortunes by frequent account. In a daytime birth, however, the **Moon** (☽) positioned in the Midheaven makes those whose lives and actions are mediocre, but who are accustomed to being frequently deceived in their calculations. If the **Moon** (☽) is so positioned by day and the **Sun** (☉) is found exactly in the **Ascendant** in his own house or exaltation, or in the house of **Jupiter** (♃), he will make great and powerful administrators of the largest provinces or cities, and consuls, but terrible in the very administration of their duties. But even with the **Moon** (☽) and **Sun** (☉) so positioned—that is, the **Sun** (☉) in the **Ascendant** in the signs we have mentioned and the **Moon** (☽) in the Midheaven—and if **Jupiter** (♃) protects both together, or one of the two, with a favorable ray, he will make emperors most powerful in happiness and justice...

<margin>XI</margin>
When the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the eleventh house from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, she decrees the same things that we showed she does in the fifth house in the preceding sections.

<margin>XII</margin>
When the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the twelfth house from the **Ascendant**, she decrees a brief span and duration of life in a nighttime birth. However, if **Jupiter** (♃) and **Venus** (♀), or one of them, is found similarly in the **Ascendant**, she decrees the privilege of some power along with happiness. But if **Mars** (♂) and **Saturn** (♄) are similarly positioned in the **Ascendant**, or if even one of the two is there while the **Moon** (☽) holds the twelfth house, she decrees many evils and misfortunes, as well as grave accidents and illnesses. In a nighttime birth, moreover, she will cause defects for the person themselves as well as for the mother. If, however, no planet is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and the Moon is found alone during the day in the twelfth house from the **Ascendant**, she decrees the loss of inheritance, wretched actions, and wandering. But if she is found in this place during the night in a similar way, she will cause people to be born who are wretched, humble, or of a lowly or servile class, but who are hardworking and always occupied in heavy tasks; their body or mouth may be defiled by a foul stench, and they are frequently accustomed to being deceived and endangered, or they may contract some defect from the hardships of travel.

But also inquire diligently into the **twelfth-part** <note>original: Δωδεκατημόριον (duodecatemorion), a 2.5-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of the **Moon** (☽) and its "bounds" <term>fines: specific degrees within a sign ruled by different planets</term>; for whatever is concealed in the birth chart <term>genitura: the configuration of the stars at the moment of birth</term>, and is generally hidden by the arrangement of the stars, the entire **twelfth-part** and its bounds reveal and demonstrate. For if you note the efficacy of the twelfth-parts—especially from the bounds in which they were found—and use them to explain the entire substance of the **astrological outcomes** <note>original: apotelesmatum</note>, you will certainly never be deceived. For the Babylonians attribute the sum of all decrees to the twelfth-parts, although Ptolemy attributes them to the **Antiscia** <term>Antiscia: "shadow-points" or mirror positions across the solstitial axis</term>; we, however, attribute them to both.

### THE DECREES OF THE MOON IF SHE IS FOUND IN THE PLACE OF FORTUNE. CHAPTER XVI.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial S featuring a human figure surrounded by swirling leafy vines and flowers.</image-desc>
Since our work has progressed this far, so that after the decrees of all the planets through the individual stations of the sky, we have finally arrived at the **Moon** (☽), let us—before the end of this book is closed—discuss something regarding the application of the same **Moon** (☽) to the **Place of Fortune** <term>Locus Fortunae: a mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity and fate</term>, since she is the principal mistress of the life of mortals. Therefore, if the **Moon** (☽) is found in the **Place of Fortune**, and she is so positioned that she is moving toward **Jupiter** (♃), or is with him, she decrees the glory and happiness of administrative leadership. If, however, she is positioned with **Venus** (♀) in this place, or if she is moving toward **Venus** (♀), she bestows the honors we have mentioned with a charming grace. But if, positioned in this place and waxing in light, she is moving toward **Mercury** (☿), or is with him, she makes people blessed, powerful, and exceedingly wise, and those who achieve honors, glory, dignity, and the substance of an inheritance by the happiness of their natural talent or by the grace of learning. If, however, she is positioned in this place while waning and is moving toward **Mercury** (☿) or is with him, she decrees illnesses, vices, malice, and malignity.

But if, positioned in this place in a daytime birth, she is moving toward **Mars** (♂), or is with him, she will make people hardworking, wretched, and seeking their daily sustenance from fire, or iron, or from some heavy weight of daily life. If, however, positioned in this place in a nighttime birth, she is moving toward **Mars** (♂) or is with him, she decrees military service, glory, power, and leadership in these acts; she also makes athletes according to the quality of the signs, but those who are preferred over others by merit of their courage.

But if, positioned in this place in a nighttime birth and waxing in light, she is moving toward **Saturn** (♄) or is with him, she diminishes the paternal and maternal inheritance, and will cause the mother to be either a widow or one who perishes by a bad death with illness and vice. The people themselves she makes wretched and hardworking in their early years, but happy as their age progresses. If, however, during the day, waxing in light, she is moving toward **Saturn** (♄) or is with him, she will cause the one so born to be quickly bereaved by the death of parents, and she compels the inheritance to be scattered by wretched tearings-apart; but nevertheless, happiness and increases in inheritance are conferred upon them as age progresses. In the night, similarly, when she is waning in light, she decrees these same things by a similar reasoning.

If, however, positioned in this place during the day and diminished in light, she is moving toward **Saturn** (♄) or is with him, she decrees the hardships of vices, illness, a bad death, and proscription <term>proscription: the legal seizure of property or being declared an outlaw</term>. If the **Place of Fortune** is found in the tenth house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the **Midheaven** <note>original: M C (Medium Coeli)</note>—or in the eleventh house (the place where the degree of the Midheaven is found by the most frequent calculations), and the **Moon** (☽) is found there waxing in light, and if she is so moving toward **Saturn** (♄), or if she is with him, and the **Sun** (☉) is similarly positioned in the **Ascendant**, [she makes them] happy, blessed, glorious,

In all birth charts, however, it is proper for you to observe the course of the **Moon** (☽), not only on the same day that the person first enters the light of life, but we must also investigate with careful reasoning on the third day which star the **Moon** (☽) joins, or with what radiation, or from whom she is receding and toward whom she is moving. For on that day, the first nourishing food <note>original: "alimenta nutricia" — likely referring to the first breastfeeding or weaning rituals which were astrologically timed</note> is administered to the newborn. Therefore, one must inquire on the third day whether she is diminished or full of light, and to what extent the benevolent or malevolent stars regard her. For on the third day, just as on the first, she decrees all things by a similar logic; if these details are collected with diligent inquiry, we can never be troubled by erratic confusion in explaining the fates of men. Lest we seem to have omitted anything, let us briefly explain this treatise in the opening of the following book.

# THE MATHESIS OF JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS THE 
# YOUNGER, A SICILIAN OF SENATORIAL RANK, TO MAVORTIUS
## LOLLIANUS. BOOK IV.
### P R E F A C E .

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring a man holding an instrument, possibly a quadrant or compass, within a square frame with classical ornamentation.</image-desc>
While I was practicing as a legal advocate, the conflicts of court cases and—if I may put it this way—the snarling strife of "dog-like" <note>original: "caninae" — a common Roman metaphor for the vicious, biting nature of courtroom litigation</note> litigation held me back. From this pursuit, nothing else was brought to me daily except a heap of dangers and a heavy burden of envy. For I always trusted myself to resist with upright constancy those factional men whom power-hungry wickedness delighted, or those who, driven by the instinct of greedy desire, clung to the wealth of others, or those who appeared terrifying to wretched men through fear of the courts. Because of this, the spiteful malice of envy and the hatred of wicked men prepared a storm of danger for me on account of their depraved desires. 

I therefore abandoned this pursuit, lest by watching over the interests of others while the consensus of ignorant and indebted men grew stronger, I should entangle myself in the greatest plots and the risks of the greatest dangers. While these men raged against me always and without pause, fighting with a bitter continuation of hatreds, I displayed a pure and faithful defense for those who were suffering and anxious in various affairs, for no other reason of restoration than a liberal spirit, having looked down upon the profits of the forum. 

Now, therefore, being established in leisure and freed from the battles of courtroom contests—having also, in a way, stripped off the snares of envy—and since the power of spite and robbery (or rather, brigandage) has been left to wicked and treacherous men, I have written these books for you, Lollianus, freed from every care of anxiety. Thus, separated from earthly social interaction, I might apply myself to celestial and divine discussions to purge, in some part, the vices of the soul which I had contracted from social interaction with corrupt men.

# BOOK FOUR

In this book, therefore, we will first explain what we promised in the later parts of the third book: that is, all the appearances and forms of the **Moon** (☽), her conjunctions and separations <note>original: "defluxiones," referring to the Moon moving away from one planet toward another</note>, and whatever pertains to the power of that deity. We will also carefully treat the Place of Fortune, the Spirit, and the lord of the birth, whom the Greeks call the *oikodespotēs* <gloss>master of the house or ruler of the chart</gloss>. I shall also explain the efficacy of the planet that decrees one’s actions <note>referring to the planet governing profession and public life</note>, and I will show the full and empty degrees and their decrees, as well as the masculine and feminine degrees. After this, the **Moon** (☽) will again take up the final sections. For everything that **Mercury** (♿) handed down to Aesculapius <note>Aesculapius is the Latin name for Asclepius, the god of healing, who in Hermetic tradition received wisdom from Hermes/Mercury</note> and Enichnus <note>likely a reference to the legendary astrologer Anubio</note>; everything that Petosiris and Necepso explained; everything that Abraham, Orpheus, and Critodemus published, as well as all the other masters of this art—all these things I have read and collected. I have compared their diverse and contrary opinions in these very detailed books, making this divine science known to all Romans. My goal was to take what seemed most difficult to some because of the "narrowness of the Latin language" <note>A common complaint among Roman scholars who felt Latin lacked the technical precision of Greek</note> and, by showing the versatility of our Roman tongue, explain it with true and clear interpretations.

We promised, therefore, at the beginning of this book to explain all the courses of the **Moon** (☽) and what she decrees, and by what logic. For the entire substance of the human body belongs to the power of this deity. For after the vital breath has received the perfected human being and the spirit of the divine mind has infused the body, the **Moon** (☽) sustains the form of the composed body according to the quality of her course. Thus, we must gather her course with prudent inquiry so that we can explain the entire substance of the human body. Otherwise, human nature cannot subsist unless the body is constructed as a firm defense to support life. Those people are mistaken who think that only life and the reason of the spirit should be treated in all birth charts—that is, the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> and the **Midheaven** <term>Medium Coeli: the highest point of the zodiac at the moment of birth</term>. For while the substance of life and the spirit are found from these places, we must also find the course of the **Moon** (☽) degree by degree with wise and skillful inquiry.

For God, the creator of man, when he composed this living being with a divine and singular logic of craftsmanship, bound the divinity of the immortal soul within the chains of a mortal and earthly body. He did this so that the soul—diffused within and bound by the command of a great necessity—might govern the fleeting fragility of the body serving it through the license of divine power. Therefore, the soul will not have a sound receptacle, nor can it connect itself to its surroundings or unfold the substance of its divinity, unless the body has been strengthened by a sound and incorrupt frame to receive the soul. In this way, soul and body are joined by an equal logic of necessity, sustaining each other with the powers and strengths of their own natures. Thus, they represent the human being, composed of a partnership of divine and earthly union, as a work perfected in sound appearance and form. Therefore, we must know which parts of the human body the **Moon** (☽) has taken up and what has been assigned to her powers.

<margin>The power of the Moon.</margin> For we feel both the increases of the waxing **Moon** (☽) in our bodies and the losses of her waning light. For the marrow in the human body grows when the **Moon** (☽) waxes; but when she begins to be empty and destitute of light, the marrow languishes with the exhaustion of a thinned body. The human body even fails as the **Moon** (☽) wanes, and is again cleansed by the solemn completions of the waxing **Moon** (☽). Thus, every substance of the earthly body is governed by the providence of this deity. Located in the lower regions of the heavens and allotted the command of the Earth due to her proximity, she sustains all bodies animated by the inspiration of the divine mind through the manifold variety of her course. She runs through all the signs with swift speed and joins herself to all the stars in constant conjunctions. From these contrary mixtures and disparate nourishments, the substance of the composed work is changed; she both creates and conceives all the bodies of living beings, and dissolves them once they are born.

One must labor, therefore, to greatly seek out that substance in every birth chart where the **Moon** (☽) is positioned. For the more the **Moon** (☽) moves herself with swift agitations and joins herself to all the stars with faster haste, the more we must collect her course with diligent contemplation. For the first day and the third day decree by the same logic, and the seventh and eleventh days also demonstrate the substance of the whole life through the **Moon** (☽). Even the lord of the birth and the giver of life are learned from the conjunctions of the **Moon** (☽) in the birth chart; even the final day of life is known from the logic of the **Moon** (☽). Furthermore, she demonstrates the "lord of times"—whom the Greeks call the *chronokratōr* <gloss>time-lord or ruler of specific periods of life</gloss>—along with the **Sun** (☉). For in nocturnal births, she herself takes up the beginning and the lordship of the times,

FOURTH. 89

In day charts, however, the **Sun** (☉) is the primary focus; we will explain its nature and where its influence prevails in the later books. Although we have already described its many types and forms in the book of institutions <note>referring to an earlier introductory text</note>, we will now briefly explain them again. We must frequently revisit the more difficult concepts so that through repeated study, we may more easily master these complexities. The **Moon** (☽) is therefore either synodic <note>original: "synodica," referring to the New Moon when it is in conjunction with the Sun</note>, full, halved <note>original: "dichotomos," the first or last quarter</note>, crescent-shaped <note>original: "monoides"</note>, or gibbous <note>original: "amphicyrtos," meaning "curved on both sides" or more than half full</note>; through these changing forms, she completes the monthly cycle of her light. Therefore, we must diligently inspect these increases or losses of her light and the changing appearances of her various forms—first on the day of birth when treating the nativity <term>genitura</term> <gloss>the configuration of the stars at the moment of birth</gloss>, and again on the third day. We must look at which planets she joins and from which she flows away <note>original: "defluat," the astrological concept of separation where the Moon moves out of aspect with a planet</note>, how she connects herself to second conjunctions after the first, which ones she precedes in joining, when she is carried through the heights, and which stars she regards with a trine <term>trigonica</term> <gloss>an aspect of 120 degrees</gloss>, a square <term>quadrata</term> <gloss>an aspect of 90 degrees</gloss>, or an opposition <term>diametra</term> <gloss>an aspect of 180 degrees</gloss>. We must observe when and toward which stars she moves while full or while her light is diminished, how she is joined to the stars of her own condition, when she joins in a synodic union in the same degree, and when the **Sun** (☉) seizes and hides her in his own orb. By exploring and treating all these factors, we may achieve full scientific knowledge for pronouncing judgments on the births of men.

## THE APPLICATION OF THE MOON TO THE REMAINING PLANETS, BUT FIRST HER PASSAGE FROM SATURN TO THE OTHER WANDERING STARS: CHAPTER 1.

<margin>The Moon joined with ♄</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) applies herself to the star of **Saturn** (♄) while increasing in light and joins him in that fellowship, or if she is carried toward **Saturn**, she decrees widowhood for the mother and constant eye pain for the woman. She causes the subjects to be detained in the service of temples, but she causes their inheritance to be scattered by various losses; yet again, in the course of time, she leads them to seek another substance for their estate through their own labor. If, however, she is joined to **Saturn** while failing and diminished in light, she will make the parents either low-born, or slaves, or drowned in the squalor of wretched unhappiness. Furthermore, the mothers of some will be weighed down by physical weakness, or she will certainly cause them to die by a violent death <note>original: "biothanatas," a Greek-derived term for an unnatural or violent death</note> while the children are still in their younger years. It also makes the subjects themselves either defective and weak, or short-lived <note>original: "oligochronios"</note> and perishing by some evil end—especially if she is found in this conjunction in the "necessary places" of the birth chart, or if they are joined to one another in the Ascendant <term>horoscopus</term> by a degree-specific <note>original: "partili," meaning an aspect occurring within the same degree</note> radiation.

<margin>♃</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) applies herself to the star of **Jupiter** (♃) while increasing in light and joins him in that fellowship, or is carried toward him, she will make the subjects happy, famous, wealthy, and masters of many great estates and vast possessions. Those having the **Moon** in this position even predict the future, either by the natural divinity of their own mind, by the warning of the gods, from oracles, or from the venerable discipline of some art <note>likely referring to the "art" of astrology itself</note>. If, however, the star of **Mars** (♂) regards the **Moon** from a square or opposition while she is in this conjunction, all these benefits are diminished, accompanied by the greatest danger to life. But if she is in this conjunction while diminished in light, she will cause the subjects to be adopted, or to have been previously exposed <note>referring to the Roman practice of "exposure," where unwanted infants were left in public places</note> and later returned to their parents; they will seek inheritances for themselves through their own efforts, and gradually, through the passage of time, they will grow in wealth and possess some degree of glorious power. But these things are fulfilled only if **Mars** (♂) does not see the **Moon** (positioned either waxing or waning) from an opposition or square. If **Mars** regards the **Moon** in the way we described, he will make them exposed children and weighed down by the burden of perpetual slavery, or he will cause them to be born of a slave mother or a weak one; or they themselves will certainly be weak in some part of the body and burdened by the wretched weights of unhappiness—especially if **Mars** regards this conjunction in a day chart, or **Saturn** (♄) in a night chart, but **Saturn** only when the **Moon** is failing and diminished.

If the **Moon** (☽) applies herself to the star of **Mars** (♂) while increasing in light and joins him in fellowship, or is carried toward **Mars**, and it is a night chart, she will make the subjects clever, dangerous, and violent, but those who are often deceived in their calculations; their lives are given over to the greatest dangers, yet they are effective and accomplish everything, being either dedicated to arms or assigned to athletic contests—especially if they are positioned in the primary places of the birth chart. 86 B O O K

If it is a daytime birth <term>genitura</term> <gloss>the configuration of the stars at the moment of birth</gloss>, and the **Moon** (☽) and **Mars** (♂) join in this way, it will cause debility or amputations in every part of the body. For some, it harms the eyes; for others, it weakens the stomach through a continuation of hidden defects. It makes some short-lived <term>oligochronios</term> <gloss>from the Greek for "brief time"</gloss> or causes them to die a violent death <term>biothanatos</term> <gloss>one who dies by execution, suicide, or accident</gloss>. But the stars decree all these things according to the specific nature of the zodiac signs. Depending on the angles <term>cardines</term> <gloss>the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</gloss>, they produce various outcomes. According to the houses that follow the angles <term>anaphoras</term> <gloss>the "succedent" houses that rise after the angles</gloss>, and according to those signs which we have said are "alien" to the associations of the Ascendant <term>horoscopus</term> <gloss>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</gloss>, a diverse variety of decrees is found. In those signs which we called alien to the Ascendant's associations—that is, in the sixth or the twelfth house from the Ascendant—if the Moon joins Mars while increasing in light, it will diminish marriage and separate parents. Once the parents are deceased, it will cause the individual to be exhausted by the miseries of orphanhood. For some, the body is cut by the laceration of iron; for others, such wounds arise that no medicine can heal them unless they are freed by burning cauteries. However, it bestows skills that always involve either fire or iron, though it makes others into soldiers who are weighed down by the eternal burden of military service. But in the fifth or eleventh house from the Ascendant, or in the second, eighth, or in the Ascendant itself, if the Moon is carried toward Mars during the day, it decrees defects of the sides, a short span of life, and causes violent deaths (<term>biothanatos</term>). If, however, it is a nighttime birth and the Moon is waning in light as it moves toward Mars in the aforementioned places, it will make people great, powerful, terrifying, and effective, such that they may subjugate the greatest cities by the license of some power—especially if this is found in the primary angles of the birth chart. But if this is found in the principal places of the birth chart during the day, it dissipates the paternal inheritance and kills the parents themselves by debility or a violent death; nevertheless, it will make the individuals public artisans or soldiers, though entangled in illnesses or vices, and it frequently decrees the greatest dangers and an end by violent death.

<margin>The Sun (☉)</margin> If the **Moon** (☽) is carried toward the **Sun** (☉) and joins it by a specific degree of radiation, in whatever chart it may be, it will make people dangerous, miserable, and cast down from meager resources; throughout their whole life, they will be prostrated by the dejection of a humble social standing. Sometimes it produces those who suffer from spasms <term>spathicos</term> <gloss>likely referring to spasticity or convulsive disorders</gloss> and those who are weakened by constant health defects. It makes others "fallers" <term>caducos</term> <gloss>a historical term for those with epilepsy</gloss>, for others it decrees the hardships of mental alienation, and for many others it decrees bouts of insanity <term>insanias</term>.

Always, however, in every configuration of her rising, if the Moon is carried toward Venus, it will make people entangled in the vices of perverse loves, for which they are struck by constant infamy. They will be impure, lustful, and always burning with immoderate desire for the love of women, and an incestuous passion will always inflame them toward wicked unions.
