If, however, the Moon moves toward Venus in a woman's birth chart, she will always be restless with envious resentment; she will be driven by depraved desires toward promiscuous lusts and will conceive a longing for incestuous and illicit passions. For then, by the merit of their learning and the splendor of their eloquence, the greatest honors are conferred upon them. These are the men who, by the power of their eloquence, restrain the fickle minds of the people when they are turbulent and stirred up to sedition; they can soothe furious minds, irritated by the indignation of hopeless madness, through the freedom of their speech. It also causes the management of money to be entrusted to them through constant interactions. 

If, however, a waning **Moon** (☽) is carried toward **Mercury** (☿), it makes men who are malicious, wicked, criminal, unstable in their desires, wavering in error, and who multiply all their plans and always keep them suspended in erratic hesitation. For directing its course through various signs, it causes the first age to be entangled in miserable and various cases of misfortune. 

But when it has shaken the mind and body with a heavy continuation of misfortunes, and broken their youth with many dangers, and dragged them here and there in miserable wandering, then it decrees increases of many goods and the greatest happiness, so that as much as was taken from the early years by misfortunes, so much is granted to the later happiness. ### ->THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM THE PLANETS, TOWARD OTHER PLANETS, AND FIRST THE SEPARATION FROM SATURN TOWARD THE OTHER WANDERING STARS. CHAPTER II.<-

<margin>The Moon (☽) is carried from Saturn (♄) to the Moon (☽).</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from **Saturn** (♄) and joins herself to the star of **Saturn**, or is carried toward **Saturn**, and if she is waxing <note>original: "crescens" — increasing in light</note> when joined in this society, she will make men who are wealthy, rich, well-supplied, famous, noble, and placed in charge of great peoples or cities; to some she grants the greatest inheritances, to others treasures, and to others truly the greatest gifts. If, however, she is waning in her light <note>original: "minuta luminibus"</note>, she decrees no such thing, but makes men who are agents, curators, or those to whom the protection of private property is handed over, and those who linger in foreign business dealings. She also makes pilots, shipmasters, or tax-collectors, and those whose actions involve the law of contracting near the water, yet in such a way that only a small substance is gained from these arts.

<margin>Mars (♂)</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) separates from **Saturn** (♄) and joins **Mars** (♂) while full of light, she decrees sicknesses and defects, and causes the person to perish in early youth. If, however, she is waning in her light, she decrees torments of long and extreme sickness for the mother, and causes her to be bound by certain vices; she also inflicts the danger of a bad death upon her, such as dying while constantly vomiting blood. As for the children born under this, she causes them to be exhausted by the weariness of misery and orphancy, or causes their parents to be separated by perpetual discord. Furthermore, she squanders the paternal and maternal inheritance through various ravages, and constantly inflicts wounds of the sword upon them. She decrees such sicknesses that, for the sake of healing, the remedy of <term>cauterization</term> <gloss>branding or burning the skin for medical purposes</gloss> or burning is applied. She will also cause constant labors in the "hidden arts" <note>likely referring to magic or alchemy</note>, or make them fulfill their life’s duty while submerged in the pains of long sickness. Or, she makes them <term>biothanatos</term> <gloss>those who die a violent or unnatural death</gloss>, perishing by various kinds of death: for they either perish drowned by floods, or burned in fire, or they hang themselves by a noose, or cruelly extinguish themselves with a sword by their own hand.

<margin>Sun (☉)</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) separates from **Saturn** (♄) and moves toward the **Sun** (☉), she decrees the greatest misfortunes and the greatest calamities. She will also make men who are insane, <term>lunatic</term> <gloss>affected by the phases of the moon</gloss>, epileptic, dropsical, or afflicted with <term>elephantiasis</term> <gloss>a skin disease, often used historically for leprosy</gloss>. She perpetuates these misfortunes with stubborn persistence, and the person who is under such a nature and constellation is entangled in these snares of calamity until the final day of life.

<margin>Venus (♀)</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) separates from **Saturn** (♄) and joins the star of **Venus** (♀), and she is waxing in light, she will make men who are great, noble, powerful, happy, wealthy, and rich; yet they are also cruel with great power, lustful, and struck by heavy infamy because of these things. If, however, she is waning in light, she decrees the perverse allurements of loves, or causes them to be entangled in impure and shameless lusts, or decrees shameful acts in constant succession. Nevertheless, she makes these same people seeking and possessing the greatest resources of substance, through which, with the protection of money, the greatest happiness and power are obtained.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) separates from **Saturn** (♄) and joins the star of **Mercury** (☿), and if she is waxing in light, she makes men who are obscure, hidden, silent, and aware of secret and "forbidden letters" <note>original: "illicitarum literarum" — often referring to magic or prohibited religious texts</note>, or those occupied with celestial religions, or those interpreting the courses of the stars through skilled calculations. She will also make them managers of business dealings, public masters of the liberal arts, or orators shining with the splendor of eloquence, or doctors adorned with the testimony of all. If, however, she is waning in light, she either hinders the sound of the voice or dulls the ears; it also causes the bodies of those who have this aspect to waste away with wretched exhaustion. For she makes them <term>melancholic</term> <gloss>suffering from an excess of black bile, believed to cause gloom or madness</gloss>, jaundiced, splenetic, consumptive, dropsical, pleuritic, and constricted by a tumor of the bladder with a narrow passage and bitter inconvenience of pain.

### THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM JUPITER TOWARD THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER III.

<margin>The Moon (☽) from Jupiter (♃) to Mars (♂).</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from **Jupiter** (♃) and is carried toward **Mars** (♂), and if it is a nocturnal birth <note>original: "nocturna genitura"</note> with a waxing **Moon**, and she is thus joined in association with **Mars**, it creates great and powerful men who obtain vast cities or regions by their own strength; however, she decrees the power of this authority to be accompanied by anxieties and dangers. Yet these individuals will not be without some physical defect or health condition; they are the sort who easily endure all hardships, especially if **Mars** is found in the principal places of the birth chart. But if **Mars** is situated in "dejected" <note>lower-power or poorly aspected</note> places and the **Moon** is carried toward him in this way, she decrees the "fiery arts" <note>professions involving fire or metalwork</note>, but makes the individuals themselves humble and cast down, and frequently decrees illnesses, defects, and the dangers of a bad death. 

If, however, the waxing **Moon** separates from **Jupiter** by day and associates herself with the star of **Mars**, she will make men who are outcasts, servants weighed down by the wretched burden of beggary, entangled in defects and illnesses; their servitude will be like captivity, and they may lose their lives by a violent death. 

If the **Moon** is waning <note>original: "deficiens" — decreasing in light</note> in a nocturnal birth, separating from **Jupiter** and carried toward **Mars**, she will make men foremost and famous; and if **Mars** is found in the principal places of the birth chart and the **Moon** is diminished in light in a nocturnal birth, separating from **Jupiter** toward **Mars**, she will make judges, leaders, and those to whom the highest command of power is entrusted. But if **Mars** is found in dejected places of the birth chart and the **Moon** is carried toward him as we described, she will make soldiers, athletes, and those who seek the sustenance of life through fire and iron, or she will make surgeons. 

If, however, the **Moon** is waning by day and, separating from **Jupiter**, is carried toward **Mars**, she dissipates the paternal and maternal inheritance, destroys the parents in their early years, and imposes the burden of extreme beggary; she inflicts the defect of bitter pain upon others, making them sometimes servants, sometimes captives, and often victims of a violent death <note>original: "biothanatos" — those who die by execution, suicide, or accident</note>, especially if, while the **Moon** is so moving, **Mars** is found in the "pivots" <note>the four main angles/houses</note> of the birth chart, or in its ascensions <note>original: "anaphoris"</note> or declensions <note>original: "cataphoris"</note>; for then all the things we have mentioned will occur, if **Mars** is joined in this association under these conditions.

<margin>The Sun (☉)</margin>
If the **Moon** separates from **Jupiter** and is carried toward the **Sun** (☉), she ruins the paternal and maternal inheritance through various distractions, alienates the children from their parents, and places them in far-off travels; she makes some exiles, others fugitives, and imposes servitude on some and the burden of captivity on others, especially if either the **Sun** or the **Moon** is found in the house of **Saturn** (♄).

<margin>Venus (♀)</margin>
If the **Moon** separates from **Jupiter** and is carried toward **Venus** (♀) while waxing or full of light, she will make the parents shine with the noble authority of power and achieve the greatest influence; however, she forces the child to be alienated from his own people and quickly makes him an orphan. Nevertheless, she also decrees power, glory, and nobility for the individual himself, though she grants all these things as age progresses, and decrees an increase of the greatest happiness through wives. She will also make these men charming, pleasing, and witty, and those to whom the greatest power is acquired through grace or beauty. 

But if the **Moon**, separating from **Jupiter**, is carried toward **Venus** while diminished in light, and is in the principal or necessary places of the birth chart, she decrees infinite increases in happiness. The person in whose birth chart she is so found will be exceedingly fortunate; for she decrees honors, powers, the *fasces* and *praetextas* <note>The "fasces" (bundles of rods) and "praetexta" (purple-bordered toga) were the ultimate symbols of Roman high office and legal authority</note>, and the insignia of magnificent power, and those to whom this merit of dignity is conferred by their parents. In the first stage of life, she also decrees dignities and the ornaments of the greatest power, and causes increases of wealth and happiness to be conferred upon the wife and the women of the family.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
If the **Moon**, full of light, separates from **Jupiter** and is carried toward **Mercury** (☿), she makes "critics"—that is, good, kind, and glorious judges; for they will be either collectors of fiscal payments, or those placed in charge of religious matters, or interpreters of the law. From these opportunities, the greatest happiness and greatest riches are conferred upon them, so that this happiness perseveres through the entire span of life. 

If, however, the **Moon** is diminished in light and separates from **Jupiter** toward **Mercury**, she will create a livelihood from letters or some discipline, or from granaries or business dealings; or, for those seeking support from these things, they will obtain certain inheritances. Others truly find things, while some will deny things entrusted to them, so that from this perfidy <note>dishonesty or breach of trust</note> they may acquire the protections of a patrimony for themselves.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
If the **Moon** separates from **Jupiter** and is carried toward **Saturn** (♄), and is waxing or full of light, she will cause the individual to be adopted by strangers, or will make them the fathers of another's offspring, or the tutors or guardians of minors...

->THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM THE SUN TOWARD<-
->THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER V.<-

<margin>The Moon is carried from the Sun to Venus.</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Venus** (♀), and it is a daytime birth <term>diurnal genitura: a birth occurring between sunrise and sunset</term>, she will make the subjects sterile and unable to produce offspring. They will find it difficult to be joined in matrimonial affection; for they marry wives who are either sterile, elderly, or female slaves—who are likewise sterile—or they pursue the shameful and wretched intercourse of boys <note>The author here reflects ancient Roman moral legalisms regarding social status and sexuality</note>, for which reason offspring of children is denied to them forever. They will surely be bound by the perverse vices of loves, or devoted to impure and shameful desires, and always occupied in servile pursuits and actions. Nevertheless, they acquire great resources and seek the greatest means of life through their own efforts, attaining increases in happiness as time progresses. 

But if by night the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Venus** (♀), she decrees many wives and makes the children common, pleasing, and well-received; she involves the subjects in great deeds and decrees great resources, for they will be noble, shining with the greatest splendor of glory. She will also make them commanding, powerful, and wealthy, and to whom the greatest happiness is granted, especially if **Saturn** (♄) has not struck them with a square or diametrical radiation <note>referring to harsh astrological aspects of 90 or 180 degrees</note>. These forms of happiness and these honors are decreed if this conjunction occurs in the necessary places of the birth chart.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Mercury** (☿), and it is a daytime birth, it makes them dangerous in life and actions, of bad character, and always perverse through sacrilegious error, even denying divinity; such people would even deny things entrusted to them. But if by night the **Moon** (☽) separates from the **Sun** (☉) and moves toward **Mercury** (☿), she produces public notaries <note>original: "tabelliones publicos"</note> and those who seek the means of life through writing; however, because of this study, they will be honored in their cities and preferred above all men of the same business by everyone's judgment. Often, however, if **Jupiter** (♃) regards them with a trine aspect <note>original: "trigonica radiatione" — a harmonious 120-degree aspect</note>, they undertake the care and protection of the city. They will be inventors of difficult writings or of a certain wisdom, or devoted to celestial religions and entrusted with the secrets of divinity; or they may cling to the actions of hidden or illicit writings. Some find hidden things, while to others a secret inheritance is granted, provided that **Jupiter** (♃) and **Saturn** (♄) together are absent from their company.

<margin>Saturn</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Saturn** (♄), and it is a daytime birth, she dissipates the inheritance, enriches the parents, but inflicts upon the subjects the hardships of wretched bereavement; yet in the process of time, she decrees for them the greatest capacity of substance, grants increases of great happiness, and bestows ownership of many estates. But if by night the **Moon** (☽) separates from the **Sun** (☉) and moves toward **Saturn** (♄), she decrees bereavements, diminishes inheritances, and decrees the hardships of bad travels; she also causes serious vices and heavy illnesses, or causes them to be entangled in cases of serious and violent dangers, from which they are scarcely saved.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Jupiter** (♃), and it is a daytime birth, the marks of fortune and happiness are bestowed by the parents; for some will obtain regions and others the greatest cities, while some will be adorned with the happiness of benefits beyond measure. But if by night the **Moon** (☽) separates from the **Sun** (☉) and moves toward **Jupiter** (♃), she will make those who acquire a substance of resources through their own efforts, but who are devoted to constant travels. She deceives these people in their early youth, but when they have advanced in age, they attain glories, good and suitable commendations, and the support of resources.

<margin>Mars</margin>
If in a daytime birth the **Moon** (☽) is separating from the **Sun** (☉) and moving toward **Mars** (♂), she strikes down the parents with a swift death, so that the one born is weighed down by the burden of bereavement. Often the parents perish in this conjunction as "biothanati" <note>original: "biothanati" — those who die a violent or unnatural death</note>; for the subjects, she decrees defective blindness of the eyes, or makes them weak with an amputated part of the body, or kills them in their early youth; or if she does none of these things, she nevertheless causes them to perish as "biothanati." But if by night the **Moon** (☽) separates from the **Sun** (☉) and moves toward **Mars** (♂), she makes them violent, cruel, and those who always commit dangerous crimes, or makes them entangled in vices or illnesses. Their actions however...

But if this conjunction occurs in "dejected" <note>original: "deiectis locis" — places in the chart where planets are traditionally considered weak or poorly positioned</note> places without the testimony of any beneficial star, it diminishes the inheritance, makes the subjects orphans, humbles their life, corrupts them, decrees ill health, or certainly causes them to die as *biothanati* <term>biothanatos: one who dies a violent or unnatural death</term>. ->THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM VENUS TOWARD<-
->THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER VI.<-

<margin>The Moon from Venus to Mercury.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'A' containing a classical scene with three figures; one figure appears to be a woman being presented to or addressing a seated male figure, while a third person observes in the background.</image-desc>As the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀), if she is waxing or full of light and is carried toward **Mercury** (☿), she makes protectors or agents of noble women, and those who, through the protection of women, receive some rank of promotion. They will be, however, either dyers, or dealers in pearls, or inventors of years <note>original: "annorum inuentores" — likely chronologists or calendar-makers</note>; they are frequently renowned as musicians, or doctors, or leaders and masters of athletes, but they are lustful and subject to constant desires of love, yet they are pleasing and lovable regarding sexual unions. But if the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀) while diminished in light and is carried toward **Mercury** (☿), it decrees vices, impurities, and ill health, and will create various and manifold occupations. For she will make either orators, or torturers, modelers, and sculptors, or those who prepare pigments and discoverers of colors, or pharmacists, or tavern-keepers, and those who take on the care and anxiety of others' pleasures.

<margin>Saturn</margin>
As the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀), if she is waxing and full of light and is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) in a nocturnal birth, she will give a wife who is either an older woman or a public woman <note>original: "publicam mulierem" — a prostitute</note>, whom he will bring into the partnership of the marriage bed; or she will be someone from his own relatives, yet in such a way that through the protection of the spouse, he achieves a leading place of honor, increases in dignity, and signs of promotion. But if the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀) while full of light in a daytime birth and is carried toward **Saturn** (♄), she makes those devoted to the worst cravings of lust and vicious pleasures, and those who are struck by frequent infamy because of their lustful acts. They will surely be base, wanderers, and miserable in their slave-like lowliness—renters of prostitutes or certainly their pimps. If this is a woman's birth chart, she will be a public prostitute who seeks the support of her life in a public place through the loss of her bodily modesty. 

But if the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀) in a nocturnal birth while diminished in light and is carried toward **Saturn** (♄), she will make them either sterile, or eunuchs, or high priests of Cybele <term>archigallos: the chief priest of the goddess Cybele, known for self-castration</term>, or hermaphrodites, or certainly those who are compelled to endure "womanly things" <note>original: "muliebria pati" — a Roman legal and social euphemism for the passive role in same-sex intercourse</note> by the heat of wretched lust; they will therefore be short-lived <term>oligochronii: those destined for a short life</term> or *biothanati*. 

But if the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀) while diminished in light and is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) during the day, she will make them vicious and weak, and those whom a "malignant humor" <note>referring to the ancient medical theory of the four humors; here specifically black bile or phlegm associated with Saturn</note> always plagues. However, she will give occupations involving water, but will cause them to be exhausted by wretched continuations of labor. For they will either be compelled to lift water from deep wells in daily toil, or be ordered to constantly clean pits and sewers, or they will be gardeners—but miserable and poor ones—or sailors, or water-carriers, or fishermen, or hunters. But the quality of the [zodiacal] signs will frequently provide these different acts. For she will make ox-drivers, herdsmen, water-bearers, shepherds, and those who are ordered to clean or wash the stalls of beasts of burden; she also frequently makes guardians of tombs, or even those who prepare the dead <note>original: "pollinctores" — those who prepared bodies for funerals</note>, who take up the care of people to be buried by the judgment and consent of all. But she decrees these things according to the variety of places or signs, about which we have also spoken most fully in other *apotelesmata* <term>apotelesmata: astrological effects or outcomes</term>.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
As the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀), if she is carried toward **Jupiter** (♃) while waxing in light, she will make men who are great, powerful, noble, and in charge of cities. Some, however, she causes to be raised up by the protection of women; they will surely be pleasing, charming, lovers of women, and those who achieve everything they desire for the sake of their beauty. But if the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀) while diminished in light and is carried toward **Jupiter** (♃), she will grant support of wealth from women, and make those to whose parents, from their earliest age, happiness and glory are granted; for she will give inheritances to some, and compel others to find the greatest profits, or she decrees honored offices of sacred rites in temples.

<margin>Mars</margin>
As the **Moon** (☽) departs from **Venus** (♀), if in a daytime birth she is carried toward **Mars** (♂) and the **Moon** (☽) is full of light or waxing, she decrees the ruin of wretched calamity by the impulse of some love, and for this reason indicates a grave danger of perils, such that it leads even to the custody of prison and the crime of condemnation, and because of this, they perish by a *biothanata* death. Others she will cause to be plundered, others to be subjugated, and others to suffer wretched captivity...

But as soon as they have left the first time of youth, with the passage of age, they will easily obtain and possess increases in inheritance and whatever they have desired.

->THE DEPARTURE OF THE MOON FROM MERCURY TO THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER VII.<-

<margin>The Moon from Mercury to Saturn.</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽), departing from **Mercury** (☿) while full of light, is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) and it is a daytime birth, she makes people who are either always stammering, or deaf, or she will obstruct their words with a slow sound of the voice. They will have careers, however, either from accounting, or teaching, or from trading, or travels, or from the interpretation of words; others always suggest celestial secrets <note>likely referring to astrologers, diviners, or theologians</note>, others take up the care of guarding a prison and its protection, so that the supports of life are sought from these activities. But if by night the **Moon** (☽), full of light, is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) after departing from **Mercury** (☿), she will cause them to be always exhausted by constant labors near water, and will make them workers devoted to everlasting labors, and those who are accustomed to hire out their body for some work, seeking the supports of life with hardworking shoulders and backs. Others she places in custody, others she thrusts into prison, others she opposes to public trials, others she condemns, others she will cause to perish oppressed by the filth of prison and the lot of public guards, defiled and deformed—especially if this conjunction occurs in the signs of malevolent stars <note>referring to Mars or Saturn</note>. But if the **Moon** (☽), waning in light, is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) after departing from **Mercury** (☿) by day, she will make beggars, the poor, those covered in rags, and those submerged in the calamity of wretched want; she makes some serve in temples, and compels others to wander. She frequently makes lunatics, or those oppressed by the vices of "sacred diseases" <note>original: "sacrarum ualetudinum" — a common historical term for epilepsy</note>, as well as those who are "falling" <note>original: "caducos" — another reference to epileptic seizures</note> and insane from the commotion of misery. But if the **Moon** (☽), waning in light, is carried toward **Saturn** (♄) after departing from **Mercury** (☿) by night, she either causes them to be abandoned <note>original: "exponi" — the historical practice of infant exposure/abandonment</note>, or imposes the filth of wretched slavery, or imposes the burden of bitter captivity; she even decrees the greatest illnesses and vices, or destroys them in the first age of time, or will cause them to be condemned for some reason; but if none of these things happen, she nonetheless causes them to perish by unnatural deaths.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If the **Moon** (☽), departing from **Mercury** (☿) while full of light, is carried toward **Jupiter** (♃), she will make men great and powerful, and those to whom the letters and secrets of emperors are entrusted, or those who guard royal wealth and treasures with the protection of their loyalty, or those who have the power of commanding or arranging in a royal house. She also makes many teachers and messengers of kings, as well as temple wardens <term>neocoros: an official in charge of a temple</term>, or prophets, or leaders of priests, whence the greatest marks of happiness are bestowed upon them from these honors or opportunities, and from these activities they acquire increases of powerful riches. But if the **Moon** (☽), waning in light, is carried toward **Jupiter** (♃) after departing from **Mercury** (☿), she either puts them in charge of accounts, or makes them managers of the business of high-interest loans, or makes them agents and the sort to whom public or fiscal documents are entrusted, or she puts them in charge of public or fiscal weights, or makes them judges of private lawsuits; and from these activities, she decrees the greatest increases of resources and grants great marks of happiness,

If the **Moon** (☽), departing from another planet, is carried toward **Mars** (♂) in a daytime birth <term>genitura: a birth chart or nativity</term>, and the **Moon** (☽) is waxing or full of light, she makes men who are irreligious, perjurers, and deceivers, whose malice grows every single day toward every kind of crime. But if it is a nocturnal birth, and the **Moon** (☽), being full or waxing, is carried toward **Mars** (♂), she will produce leaders, tribunes, and soldiers—but terrible ones, elevated by tyrannical powers—or governors of cities, or defenders, or those who never persist within the bounds of just power but always give offense in various ways. Thus, they run riot in parricidal insanity through various instincts of madness in every way; but these things are decreed according to the variety of the places and the signs. Their death will always be violent and afflicted; for because of slaves, or persons reduced to custody, or condemned men, a grave crisis of danger is brought upon them, and because of this, they—frequently condemned themselves—perish by a public execution.

If the **Moon** (☽), waning in light in a daytime birth, is carried toward **Mars** (♂), she will make forgers, sorcerers, housebreakers, thieves, or accomplices and receivers of bandits; for which crimes they are either placed in custody or condemned by a severe sentence. Others also become public executioners, entrusted with the duties of public punishment, or court reporters in personal lawsuits, such that they handle such duties; or they become assistants to such condemned men, or they become guards of the public prison from this conjunction.

If, however, this conjunction is in the house of **Mercury** (☿) or **Mars** (♂), she will make lovers of arms or the wrestling-ground, and those who handle the duties of public business. If this conjunction is in the house of **Jupiter** (♃), she will make tribunes, leaders, or those in charge of great legions, or governors of cities or provinces. If, however, this conjunction is in the house of **Saturn** (♄), she decrees heavy, wretched, or wicked duties; for she will make either torturers or executioners, or informers, or hunters of wild beasts, or such Marsians <note>A people of ancient Italy famous for being snake-charmers</note> who are accustomed to hunt vipers, or masters of rural herds or wild beasts. She will make others fishermen or fowlers; others she compels to raise water from the deepest wells with constant labor, others [masters] of wild places,

-> THE MOON'S DEPARTURE FROM ALL PLANETS TOWARD NONE. CHAPTER VIII. <-

<margin>The Moon departing from Saturn.</margin>

The **Moon** (☽) departing from **Saturn** (♄), if she is carried toward none, but directs her course through the void <note>This refers to the "Void of Course" Moon, where the Moon makes no further major aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign</note>, and is waxing or full of light, she squanders the inheritance with miserable tearing-apart, and makes them alienated from their parents, or this happens in their youth because their parents have been killed; she also frequently renders them lazy, or keeps them occupied in long-distance travels. But if she is diminished in light, she will cause a constant coldness around the belly, which the Greeks call *shivering-belly* <note>original: "φρικoκόιλιoν" (phrikokoilion)</note>; she also renders them suffering from infinite imbalances of phlegm, making them thin, splenetic, dysenteric, dropsical, pleuritic, or suffering from difficulty urinating <term>dysuricos: someone suffering from painful or difficult urination</term>, and those who are tortured by the hidden pains of ailments, though she decrees these things according to the nature of the signs.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions from Book 4 regarding the Moon’s influence. While the previous page discussed the Moon moving from one specific planet to another, this page details the effects of the Moon "moving into the void"—meaning she departs from a planet and makes no further planetary connections before leaving her current zodiac sign.</meta>

<margin>Jupiter ♃</margin> The **Moon** (☽) departing from **Jupiter** (♃), if she is carried toward no other planet but directs her course through the void <note>original: "per uacuum"; in astrology, this is often called "void of course," meaning the Moon makes no further major aspects before changing signs</note>, and if she is full of light, she will through constant travel make people wanderers and poor, those who in the course of time lose all the ornaments of their good fortune. If, however, she is diminished in light <note>waning</note>, she creates abandoned children, captives, and those whose lives are weighed down by the burden of slavery; some will be entangled in many vices and illnesses, while others become short-lived <term>oligochronii: from the Greek for "those who live a short time"</term> and die in a brief span of time.

<margin>Mars ♂</margin> The **Moon** (☽) departing from **Mars** (♂), if she is carried toward no other planet but directs her course through the void, and if she is full of light, she dissipates the family inheritance and destroys the parents in the first stage of life, or strikes them with some defect or the danger of a bad death. As for the individuals themselves, she either casts them down from high places or decrees the greatest dangers from four-footed animals, as well as defects and illnesses; some she makes victims of a violent death <term>biothanatos: a Greek term for one who dies a "forced" or unnatural death, such as by execution or suicide</term> by public sentence. If, however, she is diminished in light while departing from **Mars** and is carried toward nothing, she causes people to be alienated and separated from their families and scatters their inheritance through various losses; or she gives them laborious crafts, such as those involving fire and iron, or makes them wretched soldiers.

<margin>Sun ☉</margin> The **Moon** (☽) departing from the **Sun** (☉), if she is carried toward no other planet but directs her course through the void, she will make people poor and unhappy, wanderers, vagabonds, and those who always dwell in servile activities. Others, aspiring to various activities, she will cause to abandon whatever they have begun out of a specific kind of despair. But in the process of time, the sting of this misfortune is mitigated, and the wretched destruction of the presiding calamities is partially changed; once the burden of poverty is set aside, a small support for life is obtained, and they are compelled to aspire to certain activities.

<margin>Venus ♀</margin> The **Moon** (☽) departing from **Venus** (♀), if she is increasing in light <note>waxing</note> and is carried toward no other planet but directs her course through the void, she will make people passive in sexual intercourse and never persevering in the love of their wives, but rather those who are always turned aside by incestuous embraces. She also makes these same people destitute, poor, and those who seek the daily supports of life by submitting their shoulders to hard labor. If, however, she is diminished in light, she makes them prone to vice, shameful, poor, and weighed down by a constant burden of miseries, always entangled in dishonorable and wretched arts and activities.

<margin>Mercury ☿</margin> The **Moon** (☽) departing from **Mercury** (☿), if she is carried toward no other planet but directs her course through the void, and is full of light, she makes grammarians, orators, doctors, musicians, and those who, through the changeability of their skill, know the courses of the stars as witnesses. She also makes those who handle the duties of lending money and business, from which occasions they may attain glory and substance, though only after the passage of time. If, however, she is diminished in light, she decrees defects arising from the bodily humors, or indicates a grave crisis of danger from water; in some she harms the mind, in others she binds the tongue <note>speech impediments</note>, in others she obstructs the ears, but she makes all of these people strangers to literature. She makes others prophesy, but in temples; others she brings to the eternal guardianship of temples; and others she makes their slaves and ministers.

### GENERAL DECREES OF THE MOON, AND
### THEORETICAL NOTES, CHAPTER IX.

<image-desc>A decorative letter 'N' featuring a moon in the sky above a small landscape.</image-desc>

Now all the types of conditions must be explained which the **Moon** (☽) completes in her swift course, so that we may seem to have explained everything both specifically and generally. If the **Moon** applies herself to **Saturn** (♄), she makes the parents wretched; but if **Mars** (♂) joins her, she renders both parents humble but indicates various miseries for the father. This is especially true if she moves from **Mars** to **Saturn**—that is, if **Mars** and **Saturn** sharply possess both her sides <note>this refers to a condition called "besiegement," where a planet is trapped between two "malefics"</note>. If, however, she moves from **Saturn** to **Mars**, she causes these same things but to a moderate degree. She decrees defects for women when **Saturn** attacks the Moon with his rays. She makes people "moon-struck" <note>lunaticos: historically referring to epilepsy or mental illness believed to be triggered by the phases of the moon</note> if the Moon's configuration or phase is compared to the likeness of **Saturn**, and if **Mars**, **Jupiter**, and **Venus** are in signs foreign to them. If, however, **Jupiter** (♃) and **Venus** (♀) look upon all these conjunctions or departures (through which wretched ends are decreed for men) with a favorable radiation <note>a positive aspect, like a trine or sextile</note>, the outcomes of the evil decrees and the wretched calamity are mitigated. A person will be happy, and exceedingly happy, and adorned with the brilliance of wisdom alongside all prosperity, if—in those places in which she rejoices—the **Moon** joins herself to the rays of **Jupiter** or **Venus** (or to one of the two) without the hostile radiation of **Mars** or **Saturn**. For then happiness, then substance, then honors, then all the ornaments of life are decreed. The Moon rejoices in the Horoscope <note>the Ascendant or 1st House</note>, or in the fifth, or in the eleventh place from the Horoscope, in conjunctions with **Jupiter** or **Venus**.

But if it is in the eighth house of the nativity <note>The eighth house was traditionally associated with death and inheritance</note>; in a nocturnal birth, and in those signs in which the planet rejoices, when it is supported by the testimony of **Jupiter** (♃) or **Venus** (♀), it decrees the greatest happiness. Therefore, whatever place you wish to treat in the birth chart—whether concerning nature, the type of nourishment, parents, siblings, marriage, offspring, or the final day of life—you must diligently inspect the **Moon’s** (☽) course, her conjunctions <term>conjunction: when two celestial bodies appear in the same sign</term>, her separations, her heights and lengths, and which conjunctions follow her. For in every birth chart, we must hope that the **Sun** (☉) does not receive the conjunction of the **Moon** (☽) approaching him. For after the Moon, receding from the diameter <note>original: "de diametro"; referring to the opposition or Full Moon</note> of the Sun, begins to feel the loss of her light and hastens toward the assembly <note>original: "synodum"; the conjunction of Sun and Moon (New Moon)</note>, she decrees destruction in whatever form that light takes, according to the measure of each person. For if her radiation is strong, she decrees strong evils and the destruction of great misfortunes; if the radiation is middling, the destruction of evils is tempered. But if she is failing, and approaches the very rays of the **Sun** (☉) and is in a way glued to his orb and snatched from human sight <note>This refers to the Moon being "combust," or hidden by the Sun's brilliance</note>, then she decrees more powerful evils and the destruction of all calamities, according to these interpretations which we have marked in the preceding part of this book.

If, however, she is freed from the conjunctions of the **Sun** (☉), and during the day she joins **Saturn** (♄) while adding numbers to her course <note>moving faster than her average speed</note>, she decrees increases of great goods and great happiness. But if **Jupiter** (♃) joins her with similar radiation, the symbols of all goods are granted beyond the measure of happiness; for the person in whose birth chart the **Moon** (☽) and **Jupiter** (♃) are found this way will be happy, and exceedingly happy. But if she is with **Mars** (♂), as we have said, she decrees the destruction of great evils, for they will be victims of violent death <term>biothanati: from the Greek for those who die by execution, suicide, or other unnatural means</term> according to the nature of the signs; but these evils are moderately mitigated if **Mars** (♂) is found in a feminine sign. 

If indeed she is joined by this radiation with **Venus** (♀) in the Midheaven <term>MC: Medium Coeli, the highest point in the chart</term>, she decrees a good marriage, especially if she is distant from **Jupiter** (♃) in her conjunctions. But if this conjunction occurs in other places of the birth chart, she decrees a good life, but makes them have intercourse with their own kin <note>interpreted as incest or marriages within the family circle</term>. If **Mars** (♂) views this conjunction, he decrees illicit unions with wretched desire. But if this conjunction is with **Mercury** (♿), she decrees infinite and even unheard-of evils, with constant affliction. Whence we ought to pray and ask with the highest prayers that the **Moon** (☽) never joins **Mercury** (♿) with such radiation. 

If, however, by night, while diminished in light, she joins **Saturn** (♄) while he is retrograde or stationary, she decrees great unhappiness; for some, according to the nature or power of the places, perish as victims of violent death <term>biothanati</term>, but these misfortunes are mitigated in some part if **Saturn** (♄) is found in a feminine sign. If **Jupiter** (♃) joins her by night with this radiation, he makes them abundant in all goods. If the **Sun** (☉) is joined with similar radiation, it decrees the marks of great happiness, but these are made greater if the **Sun** (☉) adds to his speed. But if **Venus** (♀) joins with this radiation, either in the Midheaven, the fifth house, the eleventh house from the Ascendant <term>horoscopus: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, or in the Ascendant itself, matters concerning marriage will be good, provided **Saturn** (♄) has struck them with no radiation. They will be even happier if **Venus** (♀) was retrograde when she affected the principal places. If **Mercury** (♿) is joined with similar radiation, he usually makes natural philosophers <note>original: "physicos"; those who study nature or medicine</note>, but he decrees stronger goods when this conjunction occurs by night; for all goods decrease and all evils grow from these stars if the birth chart is diurnal <note>a daytime birth</note>.

# AN EXPLORATION OF BOTH GENERAL AND SPECIFIC FORTUNE. CHAPTER X.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'L' featuring a man in a gown and cap standing in a field with a village in the background, pointing upward toward a stylized sun or star in the sky.</image-desc>

**H**AVING explained the course of the **Moon** (☽) and shown it with diligent reason, let the intention of our discourse be transferred to the definition of the promised work—that is, to a brief explanation of **Fortune**. For we cannot sufficiently explain a person's entire substance <note>meaning their wealth and physical standing</note> unless this place has been collected with the most diligent reasoning. For just as we seek in the Ascendant <term>horoscopus</term> who is in that place, who is setting, who is in the Midheaven <term>MC</term>, who is in the depths of the sky, or who is in the other places, and even where the lord of the sign in which the Ascendant is constituted is placed; so also we must collect the **Place of Fortune** by similar reasoning. In which place it may be, I will show by an easy method; when you have found it, you will inspect the associations and radiations of all the stars, and then you will be able to explain that entire place with a true and faithful judgment. In every nocturnal birth, therefore, having counted from the **Moon** (☽) to the **Sun** (☉), and in a diurnal birth from the **Sun** (☉) back to the **Moon** (☽), whatever the number of signs may be, count that many signs starting from the Ascendant...

...the last sign holds the number, it demonstrates the place of fortune itself. But this is the general <term>original: "platica"; a calculation based on whole zodiac signs rather than specific degrees</term> calculation, which we have set down so that nothing might seem to have been overlooked by us. However, the precise <term>original: "partiliter"; a calculation based on exact degrees (parts)</term> Lot of Fortune is gathered by this method, which you should follow in every discussion; for a true definition will be produced from the astrological forecasts <note>original: "apotelesmatis"</note> whenever each individual place is gathered by the precise degree-based method. 

In this way, you will explain life, hope, brothers, parents, children, health, a spouse, death, journeys or religion, actions, friends, enemies, and all other things required for the substance of human life with true definitions. However, we shall explain all these things when we come to the interpretation of the "Barbarian Sphere" <note>The "Sphaera Barbarica" refers to non-Greek astrological traditions, often Egyptian or Babylonian</note>, which the divine **Abraham** and the most prudent **Achilles** <note>In ancient astrology, Abraham was often cited as a legendary founding authority; Achilles refers to Achilles Tatius, an astrological writer</note> attempted to discover through the truest methods and pass down to us.

<margin>How the Lot of Fortune is to be found.</margin>
Therefore, the Lot of Fortune, of which we have begun to speak, is gathered by this precise degree-based method. If you are handling a daytime birth <note>original: "diurnam genituram"</note> and seek the Lot of Fortune, investigate it especially by this method: Beginning from the degree of the **Sun** (☉), count the degrees of all the signs up to that sign in which the **Moon** (☽) is, including the degrees of the **Moon** (☽) itself. Whatever the total sum of all these degrees makes—adding also the degrees of the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> if necessary—collect it. Starting from the **Ascendant** with that sum, divide it toward the following signs, giving thirty degrees to each individual sign. In whichever sign the last degree of the total number falls, that sign will show you the Lot of Fortune and its substance.

But in a nighttime birth, beginning from the degree of the **Moon** (☽) and proceeding in a similar way through the following signs up to the degree of the **Sun** (☉), collect the total degrees of the signs, adding also the degrees of the **Ascendant** if necessary. Make one sum of the number, which you will divide through all the signs starting from the **Ascendant**—giving, as we said, thirty degrees to each sign—and in whichever sign the last degree of the total number falls, that sign will intimately show you the Lot of Fortune.

From this place, the quality of life, the substance of one's patrimony <note>original: "patrimonii"; inherited estate</note>, and the course of happiness or unhappiness is shown. Love, and how one's passions are affected regarding women, is learned from this place; the nature of one's upbringing and desires is also sought from the substance of this place. This place also demonstrates by an easy method one's fatherland or the "square sides" <note>referring to the houses at 90-degree angles</note> of that location. 

It is also called (as **Abraham** says) the "Place of the Lunar Sign." You should see, therefore, who is the ruler of that sign, and who is the ruler of that specific degree—that is, in which planet's "bounds" <term>original: "finibus"; a subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> that degree is—and in what location both the ruler of the sign and the ruler of the degree are found. Note in which places of the birth chart they are established: whether in the "pivots" <term>original: "cardinibus"; the most powerful houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th)</term>, or in the second houses, or in the "fallen" houses; whether in their exaltations, their own houses, or their depressions. See if the ruler of the sign itself looks upon the Lot of Fortune with favorable aspects from its current location. 

If both rulers are together in pivots, then, when you have collected all these things with diligent reasoning—and if it is a nighttime birth, attend again to the degrees of the **Moon** (☽), or if a daytime birth, the **Sun** (☉)—see who is the ruler of those degrees. If the **Sun** (☉) is the ruler, see if he himself looks upon the Lot of Fortune with a pivotal aspect. If the ruler of the **Sun's** (☉) degrees is found, and he is well-positioned in the birth chart—either in the signs in which he rejoices, or in which he is exalted, or in whose house he resides—he decrees a happy birth. If the **Sun** (☉) is placed here with the **Moon** (☽) and looks upon the Lot of Fortune, a greater happiness is decreed by the multiplied radiation. 

If **Jupiter** (♃) is also returned here in a broad aspect to Fortune and is established in the pivots, even so, a multiplied happiness is decreed. But if there is not one single ruler of the sign in which the Lot of Fortune is located and its degrees, and neither the **Sun** (☉) nor the **Moon** (☽) obtains that leadership, then the planet which has the greatest power in the decision [takes charge]. If this planet is benevolent and found in benevolent signs, or in its exaltation or own house, and is placed in the principal pivots of the birth chart and sees the Lot of Fortune from a pivot, it decrees a great and noble birth. But it only does this if it is precisely placed in the pivots. For if it is found generally in the places we mentioned, it decrees a middle-class birth, so that the person is neither excessively happy nor depressed by the narrowness of poverty. 

If, however, both fall well—both the ruler of the sign in which the ruler of Fortune is located, and the ruler of that degree where the final part was found—and they are established in good signs (that is, in places where they rejoice, are exalted, or in their own houses)...

## THE PLACE OF THE SPIRIT, REVEALED BY PRECISE INVESTIGATION. CHAPTER XI.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'L' with floral and foliate motifs.</image-desc>

We calculate the Place of the Spirit <note>original: "Locum dæmonis"; also known as the Lot of the Spirit, the spiritual counterpart to the Lot of Fortune.</note> by this method, which we have added to this book because **Abraham** <note>The biblical patriarch, often regarded in antiquity as a legendary master of astrology.</note> showed by similar reasoning that it belongs to the Sun; and it was unfair that the place of the Sun be separated from the place of the Moon. It is calculated by this method: in a daytime birth, you should collect the degrees of all signs from the degree of the Sun to the degree of the Moon, and distribute this entire sum starting from the horoscope <note>The Ascendant</note> through the following signs; and into whichever sign the last degree falls, that sign shall show you the Spirit. In a nighttime birth, however, collect the degrees of all signs from the Moon to the Sun, and distribute all that sum starting from the horoscope through the following signs; and into whichever sign the last degree falls, it will show the Spirit. 

This place is called "Action" and the "Substance of the Soul," for from it we find all action and the increase of all substance we seek; it also shows what sort of affection a woman has toward a man. Moreover, this place and its square sides <note>The "quadrate" aspects or houses at 90-degree intervals from the Lot.</note> demonstrate the fatherland to us by clear reasoning. See, therefore, whether malefic or benefic stars look upon this place, and you will know the astrological results explained by the testimonies of the individual stars.

## THE LORD OF THE BIRTH CHART, AND HIS FATAL DECREES. CHAPTER XII.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' containing a classical figure or face surrounded by foliage.</image-desc>

The Lord of the Birth Chart, whom the Greeks call the *master of the house* <gloss>original: "οἰκοδεσπότην" (oikodespotes)</gloss>, you should investigate how to identify in this way: for he himself possesses the sum of the whole birth, and from him the individual stars obtain their decreed diligence. If he is well-placed—either in the signs in which he rejoices, or in those where he is exalted, or in his own homes—and the birth chart is of his condition, and he is neither struck by the harmful radiation of malefic stars nor deprived of the protection of beneficial stars, he decrees all good things according to the quality of his nature, and likewise a full number of years. But if he is hindered by malefics and deserted by benefics, all his effectiveness fades and weakens. I will therefore explain how you may find him, after first making known all the opinions of the ancients. 

For some wished to identify the Lord of the Birth Chart by this reasoning: saying that the lord is the one who, placed in the principal places of the birth chart, is found in his own signs or bounds. But others sought the lord of the birth from the Sun and Moon, saying that the Lord of the Birth Chart is that star in whose bounds the Sun and Moon are found—that is, so that the Sun has the reckoning in a daytime birth, and the Moon in a nighttime birth. Others, however, said he was the lord who was found to be the master of the Moon's latitude. Still others said the lord was he whose—

If Saturn (♄) is found to be the Lord of the Birth and is opportunely placed in the nativity, and the waxing Moon (☽) decrees the lordship to him, he will make men puffed up in spirit, elevated by honors, rarely laughing, and long-preserving their anger. They will be good men of sound counsel, whose faith is always proven by right judgment, and who complete all business by the reasoning of correct judgment; but regarding their wives and children, they will always be of an estranged affection. They will also be solitary and at leisure for themselves, taking little food but delighting in much drink. In body they will be thin, small, pale, sluggish, of a cold nature, and those who are accustomed to handling food constantly; they are those whom a malignant humor <note>Refers to the "Four Humors" of ancient medicine; Saturn is associated with "black bile" or melancholy.</note> always attacks, and whom an internal pain, once gathered, tortures with constant belching. Their life, truly, will be full of malice, labor, and anxiety, entangled in constant pains of the soul, having the support for their life near water or in a watery place. 

But if he himself, having been made Lord of the Birth, is either in his own house, or in his own bounds <term>original: "fines"; specific degrees within a sign ruled by a planet</term>, or in the house or bounds of Jupiter (♃), or in the house of the Sun (☉), and it is a place of a daytime birth, he makes them famous and noble in life, and decrees every happiness according to the power of those places. If, however, he is in the bounds of Mars (♂) or in his house, or if he is found in the house of the Moon (☽), he will make them sad, laborious, squalid, humble, and [yet] boastful, and those who are constantly stained by mournful sadness. These evils will be stronger if it is a nighttime birth and if a Moon (☽) diminished in light <note>A waning Moon.</note> decrees the lordship to him; for then the head is stripped of hair by thinning, or he makes them shamefully bald with falling hair, or those whose eyes are hindered by sudden blindness, or whose sight is lost through constant cataracts. He also makes men pleuritic, dropsical, gouty, epileptic, or spastic, especially if—having been made Lord of the Birth and placed in that dejection of signs or parts—he receives the rays of a failing Moon (☽). 

But if benevolent stars <note>Specifically Jupiter and Venus.</note> join with good radiation the planet holding the lordship while placed as we described, then either the protection of some god or skillful medicine will cure these ailments. If, however, a malignant star <note>Specifically Mars.</note> shines upon Saturn placed as we described, these evils we have mentioned are increased with a maximum growth of calamity. He will cause deaths from long and grave sickness, which will be brought about by a vicious flooding of the humors; they will die, moreover, in damp or watery places, or in hidden and unknown spots. But if he is in the house or parts of Mercury (☿), he will make men slanderers, poisoners, perjurers, and enemies of their own brothers and parents.

If Jupiter (♃) is found to be the Lord of the Birth, he will make men of great spirit, seeking great things, who are always trusted, and who are always puffed up toward great acts. More is given to them than their inheritance or the capacity of their power might demand; in all their acts they are commanding, noble, glorious, honest, lovers of elegance, joyful, and those who desire to be delighted by every reason. They take a great deal of food, loving many people and making many friends; they are simple and always accustomed to doing good. The body, however, is composed with a modest moderation, and the form of the body itself will be clean and beautiful; they will be fair, indeed, and adorned with beautiful eyes and a head of thick hair, placing their footsteps with a firm gait. Their life will be glorious, notable, and full of happiness, and they will obtain everything whatever they desire; but these men also adorn themselves with good conversations and...

## THE DECREES OF THE SUN AND MOON, WHEN THEY ARE
## JOINED WITH THE LORD OF THE
### NATIVITY, CHAPTER XIII.

We ought to know, as we have understood above, that the Sun (☉) and the Moon (☾) never receive the lordship of a nativity <term>genitura</term> <gloss>the birth chart or the moment of birth itself</gloss>. But when the lords of the nativity have been placed within their bounds <term>fines</term> <gloss>specific degrees within a zodiac sign governed by a particular planet</gloss>, or when joined with them by a favorable radiation, or placed in their houses <term>domiciles</term> <gloss>the zodiac signs where a planet is most powerful</gloss>, and they themselves are established in the bounds of the lord of the nativity, or placed in its houses and look upon its place, beholding it with certain radiations, they decree that much of their own nature is communicated to it. And although there may be another lord of the nativity, it contributes a great deal from its fellowship of radiation with the Sun (☉) and Moon (☾). Therefore, I shall briefly explain what the Sun decrees with the lord of the nativity, with an equal power of fellowship; thereafter I shall touch upon what the Moon likewise determines when placed with the lord of the nativity, with a brief axiom of speech. For however much they each decree in a determined space of time, we have touched upon it more than sufficiently and specifically in the previously tasted book of instructions.

<margin>
The Sun with the lord of the nativity
</margin>
If the Sun (☉), therefore, is joined with the lord of the nativity by this radiation of which we spoke, it contributes these things according to the powers of its nature, out of its own benevolence, along with the other things which the lord of the nativity has given. For it makes men full of faith, but inflated not a little by a certain spirit of pride; yet they are wise, and compose all things with a spirit of moderation and equity. They are humane, religious, and those who always cherish their fathers with an undiminished love. It also makes them stout of body, and those whose head shines with yellow hair. It also makes farmers, and those seeking an inheritance by their own virtue—effective, prudent, and those who are always delighted by the watery nature of regions. It also makes such people who complete all their acts with the greatest honor. But these people will be separated from the affections of a wife and children. Regarding vices and illnesses, it causes frequent burning by fire around the eyes and other parts of the body. But it decrees the outcome of death in foreign places, as violent and public. The Sun increases the length of life, however, if it is well-positioned and holds the bounds of the nativity, and if the radiations of malevolent stars do not hinder it.

<margin>
The Moon
</margin>
If the Moon (☾) is joined with the lord of the nativity by this radiation of which we spoke, it most generously confers these things upon the native <note>the person for whom the chart is cast</note> out of its own benevolence, according to the powers of its nature, along with the other things which the lord of the nativity has given. For it makes men stable, honored, orderly, honest, large in body, yet it decrees a body sufficiently proportioned according to its quality; for it makes them well-built, but whom an honorable beauty of body graces. They take much food, but delight in little drink. Their life, however, will be unequal, and will change according to the reason of the times, so that their inheritance is both constantly increased and, in turn, diminished by constant loss. It also makes them constantly move about in watery places. But it always makes their affections leaning toward their wife, children, and mothers, and it makes them [separated] from paternal affections...

## GENERAL APHORISMS
### ON THE LORDS OF THE NATIVITY. CHAPTER XIV.

<image-desc>A square woodcut decorative initial 'C' depicting a seated figure, likely a scholar or philosopher, amidst classical architectural elements and foliage.</image-desc>
When, therefore, the Lord of the Nativity <term>Dominus Geniturae</term> <gloss>The planet that rules over the birth chart and governs the person's life</gloss> has been found by a skillful investigation from the course of the Moon, we ought not to look at it alone with a single reasoning, but to form an image from all the temperaments <note>the blending of different planetary influences</note> of the stars. For when one star is with another, or when it provides its testimony <term>testimonium</term> <gloss>a supportive astrological relationship or position</gloss>, it either increases or diminishes everything according to its nature. For the Lord of the Nativity, instructed by the radiations <note>the 'rays' or light cast by one planet onto another</note> of others, judges from the individual stars—whichever of them provide testimony to it—and from the power of the place and sign; having borrowed diligence, it composes its own efficacy from the radiation of others. If, therefore, the planet is malevolent, it is mitigated by the prosperous radiations of benevolent stars, and its entire malice is changed into uprightness and away from wickedness; whence, although it may be ready to harm by its own malignancy, nevertheless, from the testimony of good stars, a certain benevolent grace is somehow instilled in it, especially if it has been met by the prosperous radiation of all the benevolent stars. For a benevolent star always mitigates both the sign and the place, even if it is bad. If, therefore, there are many in which there is a salutary protection, the Lord itself receives the image of a salutary will; for it takes up a better desire for judging if, by the company of good stars, it has changed its will to do harm. Then, indeed, misfortunes and heavy falls are corrected again by prosperous acts; then those accused and placed in grave dangers are freed either by the sentences of judges or by the pardons of princes; then, finally, God heals illnesses, and all evils are suppressed in the very attempts of misfortunes. But if a malevolent star alone receives the license of ruling, it rages against the person with bitter continuity, and exercises its powers and license with the command of great necessity. Likewise, on the other hand, benevolent stars—if they have not been hindered by the threatening rays of malevolent stars—decree all the ornaments of happiness and dignity. But if the ray of malevolent stars attacks them, they can decree nothing of the promised happiness. Thus we must always diligently inspect the mixtures and radiations of all, for otherwise the substance of the whole fate cannot be explained, unless all these things have been collected by diligent inquiry.

We must also gather by skillful study <note>original: "lucubratione"; literally "working by lamplight"</note> whether, when a malevolent star has obtained the lordship of the nativity, it is placed in opportune places of the nativity, or in idle or cast-down ones, or whether it is established in its own house or height <term>exaltation</term> <gloss>a specific zodiac sign where a planet's power is most intensified</gloss>. From all these things, when they have been composed by diligent comparison, and when you have collected everything from the nature of the stars and signs and from the powers of the places or angles <term>cardines</term> <gloss>the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</gloss>, you will be able—from the license of divine conditions—to explain this entire topic with the truest and most certain sentences. This topic contains the entire sum of the nativity, and shows the end of life and the whole substance of the decree. Therefore, when you begin to treat a nativity, and have looked through the whole course of the stars with diligent reasoning, and have seen the power of the places and angles, and have collected everything by specific degree <note>original: "partili ratione"</note>, being positioned at the very beginnings of the astrological outcomes <term>apotelesmata</term> <gloss>the predicted effects or 'results' of the stars</gloss>, you ought to gather nothing else in the primary place except the length of life by diligent reasoning, and frequently inspect the power of the Lord of the Nativity. For when the Lord of the Nativity decrees a narrow span of living with certain well-ordered stars, whatever the well-placed stars had decreed is changed by the untimely arrival of death from Mars (♂) alone. Therefore, you must discuss the length of life from the Sun (☉), the Moon (☽), and from the degree of the Horoscope <note>the Ascendant or rising sign</note>, and—what is most important—from the Lord of the Nativity, by diligent reasoning; all of which, although spoken of scatteredly in this work, [will be treated] specifically in a single book, which [I have written] about the Lord of the Birth...

<header>->FOURTH BOOK<-</header>

...and about the time-lord <term>chronocratore</term> <gloss>the planet that rules over a specific period of a person's life</gloss>, we have written and explained these matters to our dear Marinus. Therefore, we must work with all the skill of our attention so that, once the span of life has been found through the Lord of the Nativity and the division of time has been assigned to individual stars by the time-lord, we may be able to explain all the decrees of fate. Among other cycles, this must be especially observed: that the seven-year and nine-year periods, running in a multiplied ratio through the whole time of life, always affect a person with various risks of danger by a certain natural and hidden logic. For this reason, the 63rd year is called the "man-breaker" <note>original: "androdas"</note> because it receives the sum of both numbers equally; for nine times seven years make 63, and again seven times nine make 63 years in a similar way. Because the course of both numbers meets in this year in an equal ratio, it always imposes a great risk of danger. For if the seven-year and nine-year periods—which are called "hebdomatic" <note>original: "hebdomatici"</note> and "enneatic" <note>original: "enneatici"</note> by the Greeks—always indicate grave dangers to men, what will the 63rd year do, which completes the multiplied sum of both numbers bound to each other? For this reason, it was called "androdas" by the Egyptians, because it breaks and weakens all the substance of life. Therefore, among the other dangers decreed by malevolent stars according to the risings <term>anaphoras</term> <gloss>the way signs of the zodiac ascend over the horizon</gloss> of the signs and their threatening radiation <term>aspects</term> <gloss>the geometric angles between planets</gloss>, we must also gather these by diligent reasoning. In those dangers, and in these which we calculate from the seven-year or nine-year logic, we must also look at the time itself to see what risk of danger is imminent, and whether the Moon (☽) and the lords of the times and the birth chart are regarded by benevolent stars with an equal radiation. For if Jupiter (♃) and Venus (♀) are found in suitable places in the birth chart—either in the Horoscope <term>Ascendant</term> <gloss>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</gloss> or looking upon the Moon with an exact aspect, or seeing the lord of the times and the birth—they relieve the threatening attacks of dangers with the healing protection of benevolent stars and free men from imminent perils. However, there is not just one kind of danger: for the whole risk of dangers is brought either from accusations and delays, or from ambushes and voyages, or from travels and losses and the loss of inheritance, or from sicknesses and venereal matters, and the weakness of the body, or from beasts and ruins, or from mud and precipices. Therefore, when you see what kind of danger is in a place, look (as we said before) how the Horoscope or the Moon is regarded by benevolent stars, and from what place; and similarly the lord of the birth and of the times. Then, once you are certain about the substance of life, you may see by what means the risks of imminent or pressing danger may be avoided. You must also look at that star which will stir up the danger—that is, the one in which the lord of the times is located, in what place or sign and in what parts of the birth chart it is established—and especially then when it decrees danger; and similarly, to what extent benevolent stars regard it. For if the star that causes danger is found in good places, or in those signs and bounds <term>terms</term> <gloss>specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet</gloss> in which it rejoices, and is regarded by benevolent stars and well-placed in the birth chart, it mitigates the risk of imminent danger. But if it is otherwise, and it has received the power permitted to it to do harm, it involves the person in the inextricable snares of miseries, so that imminent death or danger can be avoided by no reasoning or foresight.

### THE PLANETS SIGNIFYING THE ACTIONS OF OUR LIFE. CHAPTER XV.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'N' within a square frame featuring leafy/floral scrollwork.</image-desc>
Now, however, we must investigate who decrees whatever actions for individual men, the place of which we must determine with diligent reasoning. Now, those who decree the actions of men are Mars (♂), Venus (♀), and Mercury (☿). But from these three, that one decrees the actions who is either in the Midheaven <term>Medium Coeli</term> <gloss>the highest point of the sky in a birth chart</gloss>, or in the right trine <term>aspect</term> of the Midheaven, or in the left, or who is found in those cardinal points in any person’s birth chart.

<margin>Mars determines actions.</margin>
If, therefore, Mars (♂) has decreed the actions and is well-placed, and is joined by a favorable aspect to benevolent stars in a nocturnal birth, he gives arms, leadership, glory, the authority of the sword, and decrees the insignia of the greatest powers, according as the power of the decree raises itself; or certainly he brings fame through the bright and noble arts of fire and iron, and places the person before all knowledge by a clear judgment of nobility. But if he is established in sluggish and dejected places, and in those signs in which he does not rejoice, he decrees certain honest arts, but with a lack of nobility. But if, with Mars thus placed, the benevolent stars provide their rays, then from the action or work, whatever was decreed,
