<header># BOOK II</header>

...that [Mars] decrees both a certain glory and the resources of one's substance. But if Mars ♂ has been deserted by benevolent stars <note>Jupiter and Venus are considered "benevolent" or lucky stars</note>, yet still holds the power of decreeing one's actions, and malevolent stars look upon him, he will make the subjects subordinates, hardworking, and those who spend more than they can earn from their labors to support their lives.

<margin>♀ Venus</margin> But if Venus ♀ has decreed the actions, and it is a daytime birth, and she is in her own house or her own "bounds" <term>fines</term> <gloss>specific degrees of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet</gloss>, or positioned exactly in the Ascendant <term>horoscopus</term>, or in the Midheaven <term>M C</term> <gloss>the highest point of the chart</gloss>, or in the eleventh or fifth houses from the Ascendant, or placed in those locations in which she rejoices, she decrees great actions and the insignia of great glory. This is especially true if Jupiter ♃ looks upon her from a trine aspect <note>original: "trigonica radiatione," an auspicious 120-degree angle</note> while she is so positioned, or if a waning Moon ☽ <note>original: "minuta luminibus"</note> is carried toward her. For she will establish the person in such freedom of power that one who has Venus so placed may be compared to kings or emperors. For then she decrees golden crowns, then purple-bordered togas <term>praetextas</term> <gloss>the robes worn by high-ranking Roman magistrates</gloss>, and the palm-embroidered robes <term>palmatas</term> of consuls or proconsuls.

She will also, according to the measure of the climate and the birth, create people of noble power: directors of gymnasiums <term>gymnasiarchas</term>, provincial priests—always famous and noble—whose insignia of honor are carried across the spans of the whole world. She also renders them pleasing, lovable, charming, and just, such that everyone desires to benefit them in whatever way possible; they are also granted great marks of happiness by women or wives.

However, if she is not in these favored places, signs, or bounds, but in those of others, she will give honest and "clean" crafts; for she creates goldsmiths, gilders, gold-leaf beaters <term>bractearios</term>, silversmiths, musicians, organ-makers, and painters. But if she is found in "dejected" <note>weak or unfavorable</note> places, she will create hosts, cooks, tavern-keepers, perfume sellers <term>myropolas</term>, and those who are accustomed to sell garlands composed of various flowers on festive and sacred days, and whatever things are necessary for joy or delight. 

But generally, if a benevolent star is with the one who decrees the action, or looks upon it with a trine aspect, it decrees glory, fame, and nobility to the action itself, and grants the greatest increases of resources. The more benevolent stars that contribute their rays and associations to the one decreeing the action, the greater the increases of happiness they confer, and they add a name of greater glory from that action—especially if those benevolent stars providing testimony are found in their morning rising and moving in a direct course. 

But if, without the testimony of benevolent stars, malevolent stars alone look upon the planet decreeing the action, they decree a lowliness of life and subordinate, laborious actions; they render such people as are struck by constant infamy arising from those very actions. But if both malevolent and benevolent stars agree in equal measure toward the one decreeing the action, they all act according to their own decreeing nature; however, those that join themselves with a stronger aspect <note>original: "radiatione"</note> will be more powerful.

<margin>☿ Mercury</margin> If indeed Mercury ☿ has decreed the action, and is positioned in the principal places (as we said before regarding Venus and Mars), and is in his "height," his bounds, or his own house, he decrees kings, or those placed over judges, or those to whom royal accounts are entrusted, or teachers of emperors, or actions similar to these by every reasoning—yet according to the nature of the signs and the power of those stars which lend him their testimony. 

He also creates orators, architects, mathematicians, astrologers, and diviners <term>auspices</term>, which he also decrees according to the quality of the signs. For when positioned in "fixed" signs, he decrees the greatest judgments and reasonings. In "tropical" <note>turning</note> signs, he decrees offices involving changes or interpretations. In "equinoctial" signs, he places one over public weights and measures. In "double-bodied" <note>mutable</note> signs, he creates wise people, astrologers, and clever inventors, and decrees everything that seems similar to these arts and disciplines. 

Therefore, we ought to know this generally: that whenever Mercury decrees the action, if he is adorned by the testimonies of benevolent stars, he decrees glory, the advancement of honors, and insignia of the greatest authority. Conversely, malevolent stars decree rejections, lowliness, miseries, and infamies. But in these very decrees, there is no small difference based on the nature of the stars: Mars ♂ providing testimony will make them authors who are bold, dangerous, quickly moved, and who deceive by every logic, though they may now subdue others by the license of some power. Saturn ♄, however, will make them mild, deep, silent, and haughty, and those who do everything with dissimulation. 

You must observe this also in the other two stars <note>Jupiter and Venus</note>. When all these things have been collected by you with skillful reasoning, you will be able to explain the entire substance of a most true decree, and thus depict the character of men so that, from your answers, all the features of the body may be seen as if in a painting, and the hidden disposition of their character and mind may be found no less clearly.

<header>BOOK FOUR</header>

### THE THIRTY-SIX DECANS OF THE SIGNS, AND THEIR DECREES. CHAPTER XVI.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'E' featuring a woodcut illustration of a seated figure in a landscape, possibly representing an ancient scholar or deity.</image-desc>

As I am about to explain the secrets of this venerable teaching—which the divine ancients spoke of with the greatest trepidation and left shrouded in the ambiguities of obscurity, lest the published divine science reach the knowledge of profane men—let whatever they said be made known in this treatise with the simplest reasoning, provided the mind is attentive, calm, and not occupied by other concerns. We have already stated in the previous book of instructions that each individual sign has three <term>decans</term> <gloss>spirit-rulers who each govern a portion of a Zodiac sign</gloss>. These decans are of great divinity and power, and through them all successes and misfortunes are decreed. Thus even Necepso <note>A legendary Egyptian Pharaoh and priest-astronomer often cited in Hellenistic texts</note>, the most just emperor of Egypt and an excellent astronomer, gathered all vices and illnesses through these decans. He showed which decan caused which illness, because one nature is conquered by another, and one god by another; therefore, from these contrary natures and contrary powers, he discovered the remedies for all ailments through the mastery of divine reason. Thus, thirty-six decans possess the entire circle of the Zodiac, and this multitude of gods or decans is divided through the number of the twelve signs. But although there are three decans in each sign, they are not established in all thirty degrees <note>original: "partibus"</note> of those numbers; rather, through each sign, the three decans possess certain degrees and leave others behind. Therefore, the degrees in which the decans are found are "plenary" <note>full or occupied</note>, while those which the number of decans never reaches are "vacuous" <note>empty</note>.

Whoever, therefore, has the Sun ☉ and Moon ☽ and the five planets in plenary degrees in their birth chart <term>genitura</term> will be like a god, uplifted by the protection of the greatest majesty. However, it can never happen that the Sun, Moon, and the five planets are all positioned in plenary degrees in a human birth. Those who have one star (besides the Sun and Moon) in plenary degrees will be of moderate status; those who have two approach every kind of happiness; those who have three perceive the ornaments of happiness multiplied beyond measure; and those who have four attain the power of royal happiness. Beyond this number, stars never possess plenary degrees in any birth chart. However, those who have neither the Ascendant <term>horoscopus</term>, nor the Sun or Moon, nor any star in plenary degrees will be miserable, always destitute and poor, and subjected to a continuation of miseries at every turning point of happiness. 

Indeed, in all locations and stars, you must diligently inspect this reasoning: if the Ascendant is in plenary degrees, they will be powerful in the virtue of their life, the balance of their mind, the health of their body, and the power of their authority. Those who have the Ascendant in vacuous degrees will be miserable in body, dejected in mind, with weak strength, always serving those more powerful, subjected to their equals, and losing their freedom of authority in all business. By similar reasoning, if the degree of the Midheaven <term>M C</term> <gloss>the highest point in the sky at birth</gloss> is found in vacuous degrees, it provides a vacuous efficacy to its decree; but if it is in plenary degrees, it decrees all things whole and uncorrupted, as this location is accustomed to provide. In the same way, the Lot of Fortune <note>a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity</note>, the lord of the birth, and even that planet which we previously designated as the "provider of action"—for all of these, even if they are placed in favorable houses of the birth chart, lose their license and power if they are not established in plenary degrees. But if they possess plenary degrees, they decree all that we have promised with uncorrupted power. 

I will therefore explain the plenary and vacuous degrees so that no stain of envy may defile the secrets of this discipline; I will also set forth the names of the decans in the Egyptian language, so that we may make known to you everything we promised, beginning primarily with Aries ♈. For those degrees in which you find the names of the decans are plenary, while those which the decans have left bare and uncultivated are vacuous.

♈ Plenary and vacuous degrees of the decans.

| | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | place | degrees | 1 | vacuous |
| 2 | place | degrees | 5 | Aficcan |
| 3 | place | degrees | 8 | vacuous |
| 4 | place | degrees | 3 | Senacher |
| 5 | place | degrees | 9 | vacuous |
| 6 | place | degrees | 4 | Asentacer |

There are therefore 12 plenary degrees in Aries ♈, and 18 vacuous.

<header>BOOK FOUR</header>

# MASCULINE AND FEMININE PARTS OF THE SIGNS,
## CHAPTER 17.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap 'N' depicting a figure, possibly a sea deity like Neptune, amidst ocean waves.</image-desc>
Now, I shall reveal the masculine and feminine parts of the signs. For there are both masculine and feminine parts contained within masculine signs, and likewise within feminine signs. It is from these parts that one discovers whether a birth <note>original: *genitura*; referring to the natal horoscope or the child itself.</note> will be masculine or feminine. Thus, there are 197 masculine parts and 163 feminine parts <note>These "parts" refer to the 360 individual degrees of the zodiac.</note>. How they may be most easily distinguished, I shall explain specifically through the following table.

♈ **Aries:** From the 1st even to the 7th are masculine parts; from the 8th even to the 12th are feminine; again, from the 13th even to the 16th are masculine; from the 17th even to the 22nd are feminine; and from the 23rd even to the 30th are masculine.

♉ **Taurus:** From the 1st even to the 7th are masculine parts; from the 8th even to the 19th are feminine; and from the 20th even to the 30th are masculine.

♊ **Gemini:** From the 1st even to the 17th are masculine parts; from the 18th even to the 23rd are feminine; and from the 24th even to the 30th are masculine.

♋ **Cancer:** From the 1st even to the 2nd are masculine parts; from the 3rd to the 7th are feminine; from the 8th to the 10th are masculine; from the 11th to the 12th are feminine; from the 13th to the 18th are masculine; from the 19th to the 20th are feminine; from the 21st to the 27th are masculine; and from the 28th to the 30th all parts are feminine.

♌ **Leo:** From the 1st even to the 5th are masculine parts; from the 6th to the 7th are feminine; from the 8th to the 15th are masculine; from the 16th to the 26th are feminine; and from the 27th even to the 30th are masculine.

♍ **Virgo:** From the 1st even to the 7th are masculine parts; from the 8th even to the 22nd are feminine; from the 23rd to the 24th are masculine; and from the 25th to the 30th are feminine.

♎ **Libra:** From the 1st even to the 5th are masculine parts; from the 6th to the 10th are feminine; from the 11th to the 21st are masculine; from the 22nd to the 28th are feminine; and from the 29th to the 30th are masculine.

♏ **Scorpio:** From the 1st even to the 4th are masculine parts; from the 5th even to the 10th are feminine; again from the 11th to the 12th are masculine; from the 13th to the 19th are feminine; from the 20th to the 27th are masculine; and again from the 28th to the 30th are feminine.

♐ **Sagittarius:** From the 1st even to the 2nd are masculine parts; from the 3rd to the 5th are feminine; from the 6th to the 12th are masculine; from the 13th to the 23rd are feminine; and from the 24th even to the 30th are masculine.

♑ **Capricorn:** From the 1st even to the 8th are masculine parts; again from the 9th even to the 12th are feminine; from the 10th <note>This is likely a transcription error in the original text; logically it should follow the 12th degree.</note> even to the 19th are masculine; and from the 20th even to the 30th are feminine.

♒ **Aquarius:** From the 1st even to the 9th are masculine parts; again from the 10th to the 12th are feminine; from the 13th even to the 19th are masculine; and from the 20th even to the 30th are feminine.

♓ **Pisces:** From the 1st even to the 10th are masculine parts; again from the 11th to the 20th are feminine; from the 21st even to the 23rd are masculine; and from the 24th to the 30th are feminine.

# THE DECREES OF THE MOON, WITH EACH OF THE PLANETS
## AT THE CARDINAL POINTS. CHAPTER XVIII.

<note>The "Cardinal Points" (cardines) refer to the four most powerful angles of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven.</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'E' with foliage and architectural elements.</image-desc>
Having explained all these things and demonstrated them with careful reasoning, I shall hasten toward the end of this book. However, because we spoke much of the Moon’s ☽ course at its beginning, we shall also close its final parts with a similar conclusion, so that the most powerful divinity of the Moon <note>original: "potentissimum Lunae numen"</note> may be seen to have given this book both its beginning and its end. Therefore, I shall explain in general, through the truest and most manifest maxims, what the Moon ☽ decrees when positioned with the other stars at the cardinal points, so that in the fifth book we may thereafter disclose the remaining secrets of divine mathematics without ill-will.

<margin>Moon with the Sun in the Ascendant</margin>
If the Moon ☽ is found with the Sun ☉ exactly <term>partiliter<gloss>to the specific degree</gloss></term> in the <term>horoscopus<gloss>the Ascendant, or the degree rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term>, in those signs in which she rejoices or is exalted, or in her own domicile, and is already freed from the Sun’s ☉ rays <note>This refers to being "combust," where a planet is too close to the Sun to be seen; here, she is safely away from that effect.</note>, she makes the parents illustrious and adorned with the splendor of wealth. She signifies this same thing for the father when positioned with the Sun ☉ in the <term>M C<gloss>Medium Coeli, or Midheaven</gloss></term>. In the setting <note>the West</note>, however—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the <term>I M C<gloss>Imum Coeli, or Lower Midheaven</gloss></term>, if she is placed exactly with the Sun ☉, she makes the parents either slaves, or miserable, low-born, outlaws, or beggars; yet she decrees these things according to the quality of the signs or degrees. But if Mars ♂ should behold the Moon ☽ so positioned with a threatening <term>radiation<gloss>an aspect or beam of light</gloss></term>, and is in exact opposition to both, he weakens the body with a severe defect and frequently indicates blindness of the eyes. If indeed the Sun ☉ and Moon ☽ should be in the same degrees together with Mars ♂, he casts down both the parents and the individuals themselves into a miserable humility of dejection, decrees a violent death, and indicates a most wretched end.

<margin>Saturn ♄</margin>
If the Moon ☽ is found exactly with Saturn ♄ in the Ascendant, she will cause the children to be first-born or the first to be raised, but she will impose the miserable weight of widowhood upon the mothers. For she either causes them to be detained in the service of temples, or indicates a grave crisis of health arising from the private and feminine parts. She decrees this same thing in the Midheaven if she is found exactly with Saturn ♄ in that place. In the setting, however—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, she makes the mother oppressed by the filth of slavery, and renders the children themselves either captives or separated from their parents; yet she decrees all these things according to the quality of the signs and degrees.

<margin>Jupiter ♃</margin>
If the Moon ☽ is positioned exactly with Jupiter ♃ in the Ascendant, she makes the mother adorned with the splendid stock of nobility. She renders the natives themselves religious and possessing foreknowledge of future things; they will be bright of face, noble, and powerful. She decrees this same thing when positioned with Jupiter ♃ in the Midheaven. In the setting, however—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, when positioned exactly with Jupiter ♃, she squanders the paternal wealth, but afterward, either by the protection of friends or from the inheritance of relatives, these individuals will obtain the greatest resources of substance. In all things, however, you must frequently inspect the power of the degrees and places, as we have said.

<margin>Mars ♂</margin>
If the Moon ☽ is found exactly with Mars ♂ in the Ascendant, she shows a foreign mother or a weak one, and weakens the stomach or the eyes of those born. If it should be a daytime birth, she renders them weak in the whole body or amputates a part of the body. She promises this same thing in the Midheaven. In the setting, however—that is, the seventh place from the Ascendant—or in the [Lower] Midheaven, if she is found with Mars ♂, she makes them leave their fatherland and dwell in foreign regions. If indeed Mercury ☿ is found with them, she will make thieves, pirates, murderers, looters of temples, sacrilegious persons, and those who always incur the crime of forgery, and because of these things, they are often punished by public execution; yet all things, as we have frequently said, are discerned according to the quality of the signs. If Saturn ♄ should behold them with any radiation, he will make them bound in public custody or prisons or by the bonds of chains, so that a hostile gluttony of crimes always defiles them, and he places them in such necessity that they even beg for food from their enemies; some, however, persisting in custody and chains, even complete the span of their life there. But if Jupiter ♃ should behold all these from any part, he causes them to be assigned to servile and humble duties in temples.

<margin>Venus ♀</margin>
If the Moon ☽ is found exactly with Venus ♀ in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven, she will make them well-known, noble, and those upon whom the greatest marks of power are conferred. In the setting, however—that is, in the 7th place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, they show a humble maternal lineage, but they are those who never lack the support of life, though in early age they are always struck by various infamies. In all signs,

The Moon ☽ with Mercury ☿, if found <term>partiliter<gloss>to the exact degree</gloss></term> in the <term>horoscopus<gloss>the Ascendant, the degree rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> or in the <term>M C<gloss>Medium Coeli, or Midheaven</gloss></term>, will make people famous and noble through their mastery of letters, and fit for every office of trade. Let it suffice for us to have said these things in the final parts of this book; for this final discourse has worked to recall to your memory the effect of all the preceding discussions.

### THE THEORY OF THE MOON’S CONJUNCTION AND SEPARATION. CHAPTER XIX.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'N' with floral patterns and a central figure.</image-desc>
Now we ought to indicate by what reasoning the Moon ☽ <term>defluat<gloss>separates or flows away</gloss></term> by degree, and by what she is joined, which the Greeks call <term>synapheia<gloss>συναφείας—conjunction or application</gloss></term> and <term>aporrhoia<gloss>ἀπορροίας—separation or emanation</gloss></term>. For in all signs, she separates from many and is joined to many by her radiation. First, therefore, look at whatever sign she is in and in which planet's <term>bounds<gloss>fines—specific degree-ranges within a sign ruled by a planet</gloss></term> she is found; for departing from that one, she is carried toward the one whose bounds she enters next in the same sign. Then look to see how the lord of those bounds regards her, or in what place he is positioned; once the reasoning of the preceding <term>apotelesmatum<gloss>astrological effects or outcomes</gloss></term> is understood, you will be able to explain the whole fate of a person with true pronouncements. Look also, in the third order, at whose planetary degrees she enters, for from these she also conceives the power of decreeing; and thus proceed until she reaches the very last degrees of the sign, so that you may find specifically everything pertaining to the Moon’s ☽ efficacy.

It should also be known that in all signs, whenever the Moon ☽ possesses the final degrees, she is carried toward no one, for she is hindered by the obstacles of the approaching sign. But again, placed in the first degrees of a sign, she separates from no one, and then only the efficacy of conjunction is sought. For all the power of the preceding degrees is left behind from that boundary which exists between two signs, and it arises from the first part of the sign into those following; and this is a <term>partile<gloss>degree-based</gloss></term> conjunction and separation of the Moon ☽. For we speak <term>platice<gloss>broadly or by whole sign</gloss></term> from the signs as a whole, but in every treatise, we ought to treat everything by degree-based reasoning. 

Wherefore, again and again, we meet you with these same warnings: that whenever you treat a <term>genituram<gloss>a birth chart or nativity</gloss></term>, you should inspect the whole body of the decree together. Compose everything from the logic of the individual stars; inspect diligently the power of the places and degrees; compare the birth-sign with the qualities of the places; look at the conditions, and likewise consider the courses and forms of the stars, as well as the separations and conjunctions of the Moon ☽ with diligent reasoning. For in this way, whatever house you treat, you will be able to explain with the truest pronouncements if you collect all these things with skillful investigation.

Now, however, let the remaining treatise be transferred to the beginnings of the fifth book, so that once all necessary things are explained, the reasoning of our entire discussion may be transcribed toward the degree-based effects and the <term>barbaric sphere<gloss>the Sphaera Barbarica, a collection of non-Greek constellations and astrological lore</gloss></term>. But because the first part of our work is now settled and we approach the second principal part—which is also divided into four members like the first—we shall briefly list the parts of each in a short summary so that you may more easily understand what is to be treated in each of them.

<margin>Subject of the fifth book.</margin>
The fifth book, therefore, will make known what the <term>cardines<gloss>cardinal points or "hinges" of the world</gloss></term> decree; that is, what the <term>horoscopus</term> and the other three cardinal points promise when positioned in any sign, and how the <term>horoscopus</term>, found in individual minutes, is said to show the entire substance of a life. It will also explain in which planetary bounds the <term>horoscopus</term> is found, by whom the lord of those bounds is aspected, what the <term>horoscopus</term> itself threatens, or what the stars decree when placed in certain signs, bounds, decans, or houses, and it will explain the virtues of the twelve signs.

<margin>VI</margin>
The sixth book is about the four bright and royal stars of the signs; about the trine, square, opposite, or hexagonal <note>sextile</note> radiation of the stars; about stars positioned together, either attacking or elevating the rays of others; and likewise about the diversity of the rays of the Moon ☽ or Sun ☉. It covers what the stars decree when placed in various places or bounds and occupied by the rays of others, as well as the <term>ephodos<gloss>Greek: ἔφοδος—inquiry or planetary transit</gloss></term>, and the division of time.

<margin>VII</margin>
The seventh book will dispute the state of life, the quality of death, and the vices of men; it will discuss parents (and which might die first), all the accidents of life's affairs, and the nativities of kings.

# FIFTH [BOOK]. 115

The eighth and final book will treat the ninetieth part from the <term>horoscopus<gloss>the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> and the part of the Moon ☽; it will discuss signs that "see" and "hear" one another <note>an astrological concept where signs in certain geometric relationships are said to perceive each other</note>, and which parts are located in the various members of the signs' bodies. It will also cover what things arise in specific places of the signs, what kind of man the <term>horoscopus</term> creates depending on the part in which it is found, or what it decrees. It will explain which are the "bright parts" of the signs, and show that the decreed "license" <note>referring to the power or range of influence</note> of the <term>horoscopus</term> cannot be found unless all things and mixtures are considered, and the decrees of all the <term>numina<gloss>divine powers or planetary deities</gloss></term> are weighed.

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS JUNIOR, OF SICILY, A MAN OF SENATORIAL RANK, TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANUS, PROCONSUL: THE MATHESIS. BOOK V.

#### P R E F A C E.

<image-desc>A large ornamental drop cap 'M' containing a woodcut illustration of a scholar or clerk seated at a desk, surrounded by decorative floral patterns.</image-desc>

**M**avortius, we have laid the greatest foundations of our promise, and our discourse has advanced, growing through each individual step toward maturity. For we have demonstrated through a clear explanation of speech all those things which seemed difficult to some and were wrapped in many winding paths of obscurity. Therefore, if a capable mind, moved by the desire of a burning soul, has drunk in the preceding books, and if it has been conceived under a favorable radiation of the stars, let it reach the divine secrets of this science. Once initiated into all the disciplines of this same knowledge, it will receive the entire order of divine interpretation, so that it may be able to both discover and explain the fates of men. But the listener expects something more from us; for the principles of the preceding books were formed in such a way that the substance of a still greater work is required beyond what we have already written. Therefore, lest I deceive the desire of a longing mind with a false promise, having set aside all the bitterness of envy and cast away all the sluggishness of sloth, I shall come before the accumulated secrets of the **Mathesis** <note>original: "Matheseos"; here meaning the sacred science of astrology</note>, so that in these very beginnings, my steady intention is not abandoned to the vice of envy or malicious silence. Thus, we return the work we promised in full, specially disclosing all things to your wisdom. But let not this discourse be left naked of divine protection, lest the envy of some malevolent opponent attack these efforts.

<margin>Invocation.</margin>
You, whoever you are, God, who continues the course of the sky with swift haste through each individual day, who makes the waves of the sea perpetual with ever-moving agitation, who has strengthened the earth's solidity upon an immovable foundation, who has refreshed the labor of earthly bodies with the riches of the night, who returns the grace of the sweetest light once our strengths are restored; You, who sustain the fragility of the body by the inspiration of a divine mind, who quicken all the substance of your work with the salutary breaths of the winds, who pour forth the waves of springs and rivers in tireless necessity, who return the variety of the seasons in the fixed courses of the days—You alone are the governor and prince of all, the sole commander and Lord, whom the entire power of the <term>numina<gloss>divine beings</gloss></term> serves, by whose will the perfection and substance of the work consists, whose incorruptible nature adorns the entire substance of eternity. You are father and mother alike; You are to yourself both father and son, bound by a single bond of necessity. To You we stretch out suppliant hands, You we worship with trembling prayer. Grant pardon that we attempt to explain the courses of Your stars and their efficacies; let it be Yours, for some divine power or other has driven us to this interpretation. With a pure mind, set apart from every earthly association and purged from the stain of all outrages, we have written these books for your Romans, lest—if every art of the disciplines were transferred elsewhere—this work alone might seem to have existed to which the Roman genius had not aspired. And you, the courses of the eternal stars; and you, Moon ☽, the mother of human bodies and the leader of all stars in action, who in your monthly courses both take away and return the light; and you, Sun ☉, best and greatest, who arrange all things through each day by the moderation of your majesty, through whom an immortal soul is distributed to all living things by divine disposition, who alone open and close the gates of heaven, at whose judgment the order of the fates is arranged: Grant pardon, that our slender discourse reaches the secrets of your divinity. For it was not sacrilegious greed nor the heat of a profane mind that recently drove us to this study, but a mind strengthened by divine inspiration has attempted to explain all that it had learned, so that whatever divine things the ancients from the Egyptian...

### SIMPLE DECREES OF THE CARDINAL POINTS WITHOUT THE TESTIMONY OF ANY PLANET. CHAPTER I.

<margin>The Ascendant in Aries ♈︎</margin>
Mavortius, my pride, the naked substance of the signs themselves, even without the presence of any star, possesses a very great power of decreeing by its own nature, and this operates in many nativities. But this effectiveness is found only in the <term>cardines<gloss>the four "pivots" or angles of a birth chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</gloss></term>. For the cardinal points, even if they are left "without the gods" (that is, without the testimony of the planets), nevertheless receive the power of decreeing from their own nature. So that you may understand this more clearly, I will demonstrate it briefly by the authority of reason itself. 

If the <term>horoscopus<gloss>the Ascendant, or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> is found in Aries ♈︎, then the <term>Midheaven<gloss>Medium Coeli or MC; the highest point of the chart</gloss></term> will be in Capricorn ♑︎, the <term>Descendant<gloss>the western horizon</gloss></term> in Libra ♎︎, and the <term>Lower Midheaven<gloss>Imum Coeli or IMC; the lowest point of the chart</gloss></term> in Cancer ♋︎. I shall explain in general what the man himself and the remaining three cardinal points decree when the <term>horoscopus</term> is in Aries ♈︎. It decrees a long youth for the one born, denies him brothers, or preserves only one out of many, but even that one it weakens with the bitterness of some defect; his name is always pursued with hatred, and his paternal substance (inheritance) does not remain in the same state, but is now squandered and scattered, now gathered back together after being dissipated. To some he will seem safer because of his excessive generosity, but to others the inconsistency of his liberal nature will be displeasing. He will grant his favors to the ungrateful, so that equal thanks are never paid back to him. He will certainly be changeable, and his head will always be fatigued by various pains. 

If, likewise, the Midheaven is in Capricorn ♑︎, it persistently decrees the ornaments of a certain glory, and makes many flatter him with a kind of humility. He will be placed in charge of certain businesses and letters, as one who supplies the sustenance of daily life for many, and supports the resources of others through his own management. He will be ingenious in many necessary matters, and one to whom the secrets of hidden religions are entrusted, who easily penetrates into celestial mysteries—especially if the star of Jupiter ♃ should look upon this place from any part, or if he is found within it. 

The third cardinal point, that is the Descendant, also claims for itself the license of decreeing. If this is found in Libra ♎︎, it decrees a life spent in constant conversation within a royal house, or establishes the person in public acts. However, the one born will have a life changeable in some unequal part, such that unhappiness always follows every happiness, and misfortune follows prosperity; sometimes he is called back from the highest rank of dignity to the lowest by a falling humility, for the spite of envy will attack all his brilliance. This is especially true if Jupiter ♃ does not see the <term>horoscopus</term> by a <term>trine radiation<gloss>an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very favorable</gloss></term>, or if he is not stationed within it, for then these evils grow stronger. 

The fourth cardinal point will be the Lower Midheaven, which, when Aries is the <term>horoscopus</term>, is always in Cancer ♋︎. This makes people famous and adorned with the ribbons of crowns, for whom statues and images are decreed. But if Jupiter ♃, stationed in the <term>horoscopus</term>, looks upon this place, or is found in the place itself, certain of his relatives will be adversaries to him because of himself or because of someone close to him. He himself will be unshaven and filthy with the grime of his hair, yet always wealthy with an abundance of necessities, especially if Jupiter ♃ is found in any cardinal point.

♉︎ If the <term>horoscopus</term> is found in Taurus ♉︎, the one who has it so will be fatigued by a long continuation of labors. Whatever he has acquired in his early age he will always lose, though afterward he will accumulate what he lost with an increase of joy; he will have the ornament of good fortune and will see his enemies prostrated in a state of wretched humility. 

If the Midheaven is in Aquarius ♒︎, the one born will always be occupied in the grace of friendships with powerful men and will have his life in public acts. He will always be involved in "watery" businesses <note>original: "aquosis negociis"—likely referring to maritime trade, irrigation, or liquids</note> and will be one who is never struck by the envy of an accusation. He will, however, have increases in wealth as well as losses. 

If the Descendant is found in the sign of Scorpio ♏︎, it makes people sensible in all the dealings of life, with the office of management nourishing those of others; they may lose their first wife through the intervention of death. If it is a woman, she will likewise lose both husband and son. 

If the Lower Midheaven is found in Leo ♌︎, it creates those who seek the support of their patrimony through their own labor, and who, through constant skills, attain the greatest abundance of substance, which remains with them in an order of perpetual happiness.

### THE DECREES OF THE HOROSCOPE IN THE ASSOCIATION OF ALL THE PLANETS. CHAPTER II.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' featuring a figure in a landscape with foliage.</image-desc>

<margin>The Horoscope in the bounds of Saturn ♄</margin>
If the horoscope is found in these bounds, it will always make people lazy and slow, obscured by a deep silence of mind, evil, malicious, and those who are always separated from every grace of goodness. Their plans will always have slow effects, and they will pursue everyone with various kinds of hatred, holding their anger with perpetual indignation. But if the horoscope is positioned in the bounds of Saturn, and **Saturn** himself is found in those same parts, he denies them brothers, or if any are born, he strikes them down with a miserable death, or decrees the misfortune of perpetual childlessness, so that the offspring of children is always denied to them.

If, however, **Venus** ♀ is found in those same parts, it will make them filthy regarding sexual intercourse, and they will always desire the things of others with envious greed. 

If, however, **Mercury** ☿ is found in those same parts, it will make them filthy in all social interactions, and those who frequent prisons and are handed over to public custody, or who are always involved in miserable dangers because of a crime. 

If, however, the **Moon** ☽ was increasing or full of light in those parts, it will render them vain in mind and body; but if she was diminished in light, she corrupts the whole body with malignant humors, and either makes them dropsical, or deformed with a leaden paleness, or certainly decrees detestable insanities.

### THE DECREES OF SATURN THROUGH EACH SIGN OF THE ZODIAC, CHAPTER 3

<margin>Saturn in Aries (♈)</margin>
If **Saturn (♄)** is found in **Aries (♈)** and it is a daytime birth, in early life it causes one to be entangled in evil and unhappy deeds and to be constantly hindered in all things. But when **Saturn (♄)** has completed its first cycle—that is, the first thirty years—it diminishes the inheritance from both father and mother; whatever is received from these resources, the individual will always diminish or lose, and they will be worn down by constant losses and recurring damages. However, after the planet has taken away the resources of the original estate, with the passage of time it will cause another inheritance to be granted to him. These individuals will certainly be sickly and prone to danger, and as they run into their "seventh-year" or "ninth-year" cycles <note>original: "hebdomaticos, uel enneaticos annos"; these are "climacteric" years (multiples of 7 or 9) which ancient astrologers believed brought significant life risks</note>, they will undergo heavy trials of danger. They will be overwhelmed by these perils unless they are liberated at that time by the protection of a benevolent planet. 

And if **Saturn (♄)** itself is the <term>Lord of the Geniture<gloss>the planet that holds primary influence over the birth chart</gloss></term>, in the first stage of life the individual will be at odds with his wife, and through dissenting quarrels, he will avoid marrying a virgin. His wife will be separated from him quickly, either by sudden death or by divorce. **Saturn (♄)** thus positioned will also give either a widow as a wife, or one who has been "defiled" by another, or one who has had children by another husband, or one whom the stain of some disgrace defames. But it only decrees such a wife when a "transiting" <note>original: "parodicus"; referring to the movement of planets over time</note> **Saturn (♄)**—that is, the temporal planet—or the **Moon (☽)** looks upon him from a <term>square<gloss>an aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</gloss></term>, or if they look back at him from **Leo (♌)** or **Libra (♎)** with a <term>trine radiation<gloss>an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</gloss></term>. For when **Saturn (♄)** is so positioned, whatever wife he has obtained, the planet makes her obedient to him, and she will persevere in her affection for him with integrity until the final span of life. He will also obtain children whenever **Saturn (♄)** is found in the manner we described; for then he will successfully receive offspring, especially if, while **Saturn (♄)** is in **Aries (♈)**, **Jupiter (♃)** and the **Moon (☽)** look upon him with some radiation. If this is not the case, he will either lose the children he received or the planet decrees he shall have none at all. But if **Saturn (♄)** returns to **Aries (♈)** from a high place, it threatens heavy danger and embitters brothers with the harsh hatred of enmities.

<margin>Taurus (♉)</margin>
If **Saturn (♄)** is found in **Taurus (♉)**, it will make individuals who grow in all their actions by their own strength, but they will diminish whatever they received in their early life. Subsequently, through their own efforts, they will seek out great resources of substance for themselves. In their early youth, however, they will be weighed down by various instabilities and will be subject to others, and out of necessity, they will flatter more powerful men. They will have difficult times at first, being worn down by heavy illness and suffering many hardships of life due to a lack of necessities. In the first stage of life, they will also suffer from the festering of wounds and ulcerations, and they will be bound by certain great vices. After being oppressed by great illnesses and then liberated from these dangerous inconveniences, they will obtain a long span of life. 

Nevertheless, all the father’s substance will be scattered, and they will receive nothing remaining from the father's or mother's estate through their own labors. **Saturn (♄)** positioned thus also causes the mother to be weighed down by the loss of the patrimony and the narrowness of poverty, even approaching the misery of beggary, unless the planet **Venus (♀)**, providing testimony to **Saturn (♄)** with good radiations, relieves the hardships of the mother's unhappiness. Nor is this testimony of **Venus (♀)** alone sufficient, unless the **Moon (☽)** and **Jupiter (♃)** also look upon the birth with a prosperous radiation. In their own proper places and by their own merit, the greatest signs of happiness are conferred, but they are weighed down by the burden of unhappiness for as long as it takes **Saturn (♄)** to complete its first circuit of the zodiac. 

Dangers will be brought upon them either from legal cases, illnesses, or foreign travels. They will also face grave danger in their ninth year, or the fourteenth, twenty-fifth, or thirty-second. But if, at the time of these dangers, they are liberated by the protection of benevolent planets, they escape the crisis of impending death and receive a life span of up to sixty-three years. For in these times, they will face ambushes, legal cases, and losses. But if they have the protection of benevolent planets at the time of danger, they are liberated from all of them. Before the thirty-second year, **Saturn (♄)** never allows them to take wives, nor will virgin wives be given to them; and if they are given, the children they receive from them will be lost, and their loves will be for those who belong to others. They will frequently obtain foreign wives or those "defiled" by others. Wives will be given most especially when, after the thirtieth year, **Saturn (♄)** enters **Cancer (♋)**, or when it is positioned in **Virgo (♍)** or **Libra (♎)**.

<margin>♊</margin>
If **Saturn (♄)** is found in **Gemini (♊)**, in early life he causes one to be entangled in dangers and illnesses, and to suffer easily through all manner of crises; but truly, those crises which are inflicted in the "seventh-year" or "ninth-year" cycles <note>original: "hebdomaticis, uel enneaticis annis"; these are the climacteric years, multiples of seven or nine, which ancient astrologers believed marked major turning points or dangers in a human life</note> will be the most perilous. For they will have disturbances and feuds, and will often be occupied in great labors, and will obtain nothing of significance from their father’s or mother’s substance. Instead, they will be weighed down by the burdens of labor and unhappiness for as long as it takes for **Saturn (♄)** to pass through **Cancer (♋)**, **Libra (♎)**, **Aries (♈)**, and their squares. Then, indeed, they will make progress in all things when **Saturn (♄)** resolves its first <term>station<gloss>the point where a planet appears to stand still before changing direction</gloss></term> in **Leo (♌)** or **Sagittarius (♐)**. **Saturn (♄)**, positioned in **Gemini (♊)**, also causes vices, and decrees the greatest adversaries in legal cases and contests; it will also grant swift and frequent losses of <term>patrimony<gloss>inherited wealth or estate</gloss></term>, so that the individual is tossed about by various conflicts. But when they come to the extreme crises of life, afterward, in great business and power, he will make them appointed by someone’s command, and they will associate with famous and powerful men for the sake of honor. They will then be famous and noble in all their actions, and will travel abroad constantly, moving to various regions; however, a virgin wife will not be given to such a person. But if the testimony of **Jupiter (♃)** should perhaps grant a virgin wife, they will be separated from her either by divorce or by the crisis of death. Furthermore, they will be without children, or will raise only one son. But when **Saturn (♄)** approaches the sign of **Virgo (♍)**, then they will be happy, glorious, and wealthy; yet they will obtain a widow as a wife, with whom they will persevere without any strife or quarreling. Many matters will also be entrusted to them, but they will deny many, and will have many feuds with more powerful men; they will be endangered by these men unless the star **Jupiter (♃)**, running well in the birth chart at that time, mitigates the danger of those crises. For one who has **Saturn (♄)** thus will not always be "great," but will be an opponent to powerful men, always applying the protection of inferiors to themselves. Such a person will frequently be placed in "free custody" <note>original: "libera custodia"; a form of house arrest or detention where the person is not in a dungeon but is still restricted</note>, and will also grow out their hair, either because of someone's friendship, or because of an inconvenience or misfortune, or because of the miserable torments of someone's death or loss. But when they have been shaken by various dangerous crises, then they will be lifted up by such prosperous happiness that they obtain both praise and estates, and a sudden inheritance comes to them; then they also obtain riches, power over the greatest lands, and sublime lordships.

<margin>♋</margin>
If **Saturn (♄)** is found in **Cancer (♋)**, like a "crab among crabs," they will be entangled in seditions, legal cases, and in many contradictions; whatever they have obtained from father or mother, they will always lose through miserable tearing-away. They will have dangers from some disturbance or from illnesses, and most especially in the seventh and ninth climacteric years, and for as long as they are passing through twenty-three years of age; for up until this age, they will always be exhausted by the greatest dangers. But if, at the time of these dangers, benevolent stars hold the mastery of the times, or if the **Moon (☽)** regards them with a prosperous radiation, or if the <term>Lord of the Geniture<gloss>the planet with the most influence over the life path in a chart</gloss></term> is a benevolent star and is well-placed, the crises of the coming dangers are mitigated. For if at the time of the dangers, as we have said, the birth chart is aided by benevolent stars, there will nonetheless be losses of parents for the person born, or of brothers, or damages from the conflicts of legal cases; but from all these dangers they will nonetheless be liberated. However, when **Saturn (♄)** is in its own houses, then it decrees losses, then storms, dangers, illnesses, and legal cases with persistent reason; and when it is found in the <term>diameter<gloss>the opposite sign, 180 degrees away</gloss></term> of its own houses, it threatens these same things by similar reasoning.

In "double" signs <note>original: "geminis uero signis"; referring to Gemini, Pisces, Sagittarius, etc., or specifically to the degrees of Gemini</note>, when it is present, it will always agitate those born, and entangle them in sudden anxieties and dangers; for then it indicates both misfortunes and will shake them with a continuation of those evils for as long as it passes through the sign of **Cancer (♋)**. But when **Saturn (♄)** is in the <term>tropical parts<gloss>the degrees associated with the solstice</gloss></term> of **Cancer (♋)**, then it will cause the loss of patrimony and place them in such great straits that the humanity of others must sustain them; for then there will be shameful seditions and various crises of life. But when **Saturn (♄)** has passed the tropical parts of **Cancer (♋)**, the preceding evils will be lightly put to rest, and they will be separated from anxieties, cares, and all dangers. <margin>Leo (♌)</margin> If **Saturn (♄)** is found in **Leo (♌)**, those born will be buffeted by constant envy. But when Saturn (♄) has shaken them with the storm of an earlier time, then thereafter he decrees for them joy arising from a vice <note>original: "ex uitio" — this may refer to a previous failing or an unconventional habit that becomes a source of happiness</note>, and from the grace of marriage, according to the measure and substance of the birth chart <term>geniturae<gloss>the specific configuration of the stars at the moment of a person's birth</gloss></term>, which the other stars will have decreed by their own authority, strengthened by their conjunctions or aspects.

### JUPITER’S DECREES THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL
### SIGNS OF THE ZODIAC. CHAPTER IV.

<margin>♈︎ Jupiter in Aries</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' featuring a male figure holding a staff or scepter amidst architectural and floral motifs.</image-desc>
If Jupiter (♃) is found in Aries (♈︎), whatever those born under this sign possess in their early years is disturbed in every action, as long as they fulfill the contradictions of the birth chart. But when these times have been completed, then honors, then happy actions, good times, a place for progress, and the management of the greatest affairs are decreed; then, furthermore, they are joined in friendship with powerful and great men, or, being established in great and royal houses, the duties of powerful administration are entrusted to them. Then they obtain the greatest inheritances <note>original: "patrimonia" — family estates or ancestral wealth</note>, and receive the power of command, and are relieved by the greatest increase of joy from wives or children. Finally, the emblems of power and signs of honor are conferred; then they are allotted the governance of men and authority; then in all legal cases and the contests of litigation they emerge as victors, and whatever they have considered in silent thought, all of it is completed by the easiest means. For Jupiter (♃) makes men adorned with the proclamation of goodness, but who have a certain mark around the mouth. They will be masters of others' estates, but religious in the worship of the gods, and keeping the precepts of all with faith, and those who are directed by more powerful men or kings to the duties of great administration, being commanding in all actions and strong—but those whose early times are difficult, yet afterwards, shaped by the constant warning of the gods, they complete everything prosperously, especially if he [Jupiter] looks upon those positioned in the principal places of the birth chart, and not in the fallen ones—Saturn (♄), or Mars (♂), or the Sun (☉), or Mercury (☿), or Venus (♀), or the Moon (☽)—with a trine aspect <term>trigonica radiatione<gloss>an aspect of 120 degrees, traditionally considered the most harmonious and beneficial relationship between planets</gloss></term>.

<margin>♉︎</margin>
If he is found in Taurus (♉︎), whoever has him so placed will be in the greatest glory and power. But after Jupiter (♃) has fulfilled his times—since in those first times they were shaken by a heavy storm of dangers, and since they were occupied in sicknesses, services, and legal cases, and since, furthermore, they suffered contentions with more powerful men, losses, labors, and injuries—then they will have prosperous outcomes in all affairs; then they obtain glories and the friendships of the powerful, and then the powerful will entrust the secrets of their lives to them. They will sail upon the great sea or on rivers; they will also associate with sterile or infamous men, who nonetheless serve religion. But for these people, the protections of life are provided by women, and through them they will obtain the emblems of great dignity and the highest honors. They will, however, be just, strong, and showing love to their friends; there will be free speech in them, and they will defend their friends strongly. But they will be reckless in every struggle of competition, and strong, and those who desire never to benefit themselves but always their friends; however, their friends often turn out to be ungrateful to them. They themselves, also falling quite often, are corrected again. They will also be the sons of two fathers or two mothers—one by nature, the other by accident <note>original: "per accidens" — likely referring to adoption, fosterage, or a second marriage by a parent</note>. But in the beginning they will have joys from wives, and later sorrows from children. Likewise, they will benefit many, having the greatest signs of happiness. But all these things Jupiter himself decrees according to the measure of the birth chart.

<margin>♊︎</margin>
If he is found in Gemini (♊︎), whoever has him so placed will be in the greatest glories and powers, known in friendships and always adorned with grace; yet while they seek many things, they lose these same things again, and their goods vary with constant change. For in the first period of life they will be in dissensions, and in many affairs and losses, in distress and sicknesses, and they will have constant sorrows regarding wife and children, until they have completed the forty-fifth year of age. For within this span of the birth chart’s time, whatever they have, they will squander. But when this time has passed <note>original: "fuerit diuersum" — literally "has become different"</note>, then they will have reputations, then the support of resources. In the first period, however, they will be at odds with their wives, but afterwards [prosperous]...

But this is primarily decreed once Saturn has first passed through the locations of the birth chart. But a little later, they are weighed down by such an oppression of all adversities that life scarcely delights them. In the end of their life, however, they will attain joys once again.

### THE DECREES OF MARS THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL SIGNS OF THE ZODIAC, CHAPTER VI.

<margin>Mars in Aries ♈</margin>
♈ <image-desc>Decorative drop cap M featuring a seated figure in a classical room setting.</image-desc> If Mars is found in Aries, whoever has him so will be thieves, loud, fraudulent, and quarrelsome, always striving to exalt themselves above others. These people will, however, attain some happiness in their early years; they will be leaders of armies and governors of peoples, always ready for arms, whereby they deter others by their bravery or their ferocity. But this will be especially so when Saturn has first passed through the locations of the birth chart; for before this time, they will be flighty and hindered by the snares of love—though they always remain adorned with weapons, seeking to strike fear into others and to be always revered by them.

<margin>Mars in Taurus ♉</margin>
If Mars is found in Taurus, whoever has him so will be made bold, reckless, and spendthrifts who fulfill their desires regardless of right or wrong <note>original: "fas, aut nefas" — divine law or forbidden acts</note>. Entangled in the charms of women, they will frequently stir up brawls and lawsuits, and sometimes even homicide. For this reason, they will be exhausted by many misfortunes. They will also be of a most shameful and foul appearance, continually devoted to jokes and throwing games <note>original: "iaculationibus" — likely referring to games involving the throwing of dice or javelins</note>. But as soon as Saturn has completed his first circle, if they have corrected their deeds and left behind their former way of life, they will be able to rejoice in a better decree for the remainder of their age.

<margin>Mars in Gemini ♊</margin>
If Mars is found in Gemini, whoever has him so will be devoted to military service; they will be those who discover many stratagems in war through their art and ingenuity. They will not, however, be so reckless or bold, but rather those who desire to punish enemies with concealed weapons, searching out their secret crimes with watchful sagacity. Now, perhaps, they will sometimes attain great marks of honor among kings and princes. But when Saturn has passed through the first locations of the birth chart, they will be made poor and perhaps physically impaired, and they will scarcely be able to provide the necessary supports of life for themselves in a sufficient manner.

<margin>Mars in Cancer ♋</margin>
If Mars is found in Cancer, whoever has him so will be knights <note>original: "equites" — also refers to the Roman social class of horsemen/cavalry</note> and those who delight in the firing of catapults and siege engines. They will breed horses and beasts of a malicious nature. They will also be soldiers involved in military business, whereby they may sometimes acquire honor and much fear from others. They will, however, be of a most foul appearance or strange form, such that everyone mocks them at first. But when Saturn has passed his first circle, they will be intent upon the faculty of medicine and especially surgery; they will follow magical incantations with the greatest zeal, investigating various hidden poisons.

If Mars is found in Leo, whoever has him so will be powerful, bold, and strong men, and those who delight especially in equestrian spear-throwing. Yet they will be sad of face...

<margin>Mars in Taurus ♉</margin>
In Taurus, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be men of the ugliest and most foul appearance, of the gravest anger—yet holding it within their chests for a very long time—and those who are always borne with a bold spirit toward any matters at all, even those unattempted by others, and especially toward homicides. But when Saturn reaches the second trine of the birth chart, they will perhaps come to blindness and some injury of the limbs; they will also be poor, prone to vice, obscure, and hindered by bad business, and those who can scarcely provide themselves with the necessary nourishment of life.

<margin>Mars in Gemini ♊</margin>
In Gemini, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be men of good appearance, beautiful form, and devoted to delights, but those who are especially delighted by arms and labor at javelin-throwing from horseback. Truly, when Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, they will be affected by several sorrows, from which perhaps no small blows and losses will come to them. But when Saturn himself has come to the other trine of the birth chart, then they will be engaged in humorous banquets and joyful companionships; then they will practice jests and songs, most happily enjoying the tranquil quiet of life.

<margin>Mars in Leo ♌</margin>
In Leo, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be powerful men, strong, bold, and those who easily dominate all their enemies. They will also be of high name and excellent reputation, and those who guard their goods with wise moderation; but this will be especially when Saturn first passes the trine of the birth chart. For before this time, they will be poor, envious, hateful, workers of evil, and serving as common soldiers. They will also be so devoted to women that, having cast aside all honesty of shame, they may sometimes attempt to offer them violence, and more often, being angry, they will engage in quarrels with them.

<margin>Mars in Sagittarius ♐</margin>
In Sagittarius, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be soft, effeminate, and very lazy and sluggish in their actions, with a indeed feminine voice, weak also, and rejoicing in women's apparel. But when Saturn first passes the trine of the birth chart, then they will be bold, strong, magnanimous, and occupied in great business, and those who, by their strength and magnanimity, are easily feared by all. They will nevertheless be bold and joyful, but those who study to accomplish their deeds through laws and equity rather than by violence, from which they may acquire great glory for themselves.

<margin>Mars in Capricorn ♑</margin>
In Capricorn, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be royal men, noble, powerful, honored by the greatest trophies and many kinds of victories, and those who involve themselves chiefly in such business which others would not dare to undertake with such easy reason. But this will be especially when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart; for before this time, such happiness is not so <note>decernuntur</note> decreed, although they may always be joined in the friendly company of illustrious men, and they always apply their mind to arduous matters that are entirely hidden from others.

<margin>Mars in Aquarius ♒</margin>
In Aquarius, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be evil, treacherous, nefarious, <term>litigious<gloss>original: "uitilitigatores," those who find pleasure in malicious lawsuits or arguments</gloss></term>, and those who attempt to sow dissensions and discords among everyone, and always instigate others so that, violating human society, they study to bring constant insults upon men. But when Saturn first passes the <term>decan<gloss>a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</gloss></term> of the birth chart, then they will devote their effort to breeding horses, stirring up wars, and attacking enemies. But a little later, they will fall into defects of the limbs and blindness of the eyes, from which they may be forced to serve others, and have no further liberty in their life.

<margin>Mars in Pisces ♓</margin>
In Pisces, if Mars is found, whoever has him so will be jesters, crafty, and followers of women, and those who desire to fulfill all delights of both their body and their mind. They will nevertheless be diviners, prophets, dream-readers, and those who perform such wonderful things by magical operations that for that reason they are honored by all, and even feared by many. These things, moreover, will be when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart; for before this time, they will be killers of men, and, having preserved no equity of the law, overcomers of those opposing them.

<margin>The Sun in Aries ♈︎</margin>
If the <term>Sun<gloss>original: "Sol" (☉)</gloss></term> is found in Aries, whoever has it so will be people of varied fortune; for sometimes they rise from lowly origins to the heights, and at other times they are cast down from being lords and princes to a humble and sad state. But these people will especially delight in wrong-doing, cruelty, and savage victory. However, as soon as <term>Saturn<gloss>original: "♄"</gloss></term> has passed the first <term>trine<gloss>an astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, forming a triangle in the zodiac</gloss></term> of the <term>birth chart<gloss>original: "genitura"</gloss></term>, and if the Sun is in the <term>angles<gloss>the four pivotal points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</gloss></term> or their <term>succedent houses<gloss>original: "anaphoris," the houses immediately following the angles</gloss></term>, and not weighed down by the threatening <term>aspects<gloss>original: "radiatione," the "rays" or influence sent from one planet to another</gloss></term> of <term>malefics<gloss>planets considered to have a negative influence, typically Mars and Saturn</gloss></term>, they will increase their wealth. They will be granted such journeys by princes in which they may seek out honor and advantage. But if the Sun is struck by the aspect of malefics, they will suffer evils from kings.

<margin>Taurus ♉︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Taurus, whoever has it so will be the kind of people who, in order to increase their treasures, will always be engaged in battles. To satisfy the <term>lust<gloss>original: "venerem," referencing the goddess Venus, the ruler of Taurus</gloss></term> by which they are troubled, they will attempt to increase their money in whatever way they can, even through unjust means. But as soon as Saturn has completed the first circuit of the birth chart, and if the Sun is fortified by the favorable aspect of <term>benefic<gloss>planets considered to have a positive influence, typically Jupiter and Venus</gloss></term> stars, they will then begin to obtain benefit and glory from kings and princes. But if the Sun is weighed down by the threatening aspect of evil stars, they will obtain sorrows, anxieties, and unexpected toils from those same kings.

<margin>Gemini ♊︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Gemini, whoever has it so will be princes or leading men, but of meager spirit and little power. Yet these people will desire to rule everything according to their own will, adhering to no one's advice; for that reason, they will lose their reputation and their status. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, and if the Sun is positioned in favorable places and fortified by the prosperous aspect of benefic stars, these people will have a great profit from social partnerships and will obtain the greatest joy on account of their children. However, the opposite will happen if malefic stars hinder the Sun.

<margin>Cancer ♋︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Cancer, whoever has it so will be people especially devoted to jesting, songs, games, and storytelling; they are lovers of beautiful ornaments and those who, because of such pleasures of theirs, utterly despise the reconciliations and partnerships of men. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, they should then fear their enemies, for they will indeed be easily overcome by them and will be established in many toils. If, however, the Sun is positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and is not weighed down by the threatening aspect of malefics, all these evils will be lessened.

<margin>Leo ♌︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Leo, whoever has it so will be kings, princes, and powerful men who trust in both arms and their own power. They desire to utterly overcome everyone and to rule over all, and to obtain all their wills and desires by whatever means. They will be the kind of people who always bring back profit and gain from all their business, along with the highest praise from everyone. This is especially true if the Sun is positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and is entirely free from evil stars. But when Saturn reaches the third trine of the birth chart, then many ailments and sorrows will befall them.

<margin>Virgo ♍︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Virgo, whoever has it so will be famous and high-ranking people, endowed with a certain admirable natural talent. But being intent only on games, stories, and jesting, they love banquets, songs, and fellowships, and devote their time to all delights, perfumes, and pleasures. Nevertheless, they obtain substance most abundantly through their talent and learning. And this happens especially when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart, and if the Sun is in favorable places, fortified by the protection of benefic stars. But if it is struck by the aspect of malefics, they will never be able to fulfill their vows.

<margin>Libra ♎︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Libra, whoever has it so will be powerful men and princes, but who, having lost their empire or their happy condition, may flee as exiles and fugitives, trembling at the sight of their enemies. Nor will they have anyone in whom they can trust or to whom they can safely commit their lives. This occurs as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart and the Sun has been weighed down by the aspect of malefics in the chart. For before this time, perhaps in their early age, they will make many journeys, from which they will most happily obtain some glory and profit.

<margin>Scorpio ♏︎</margin>
If the <term>Sun<gloss>original: "☉"</gloss></term> is found in Scorpio, whoever has it so will be handsome people, of well-proportioned body and well-dressed, of great name and fame, and those who delight in fine clothing. They will also be the sort who obtain honor and esteem from kings, acquire many inheritances, and increase their patrimony, so that they are feared by others. This occurs especially when <term>Saturn<gloss>original: "♄"</gloss></term> has first passed the <term>trine<gloss>an astrological aspect of 120 degrees</gloss></term> of the <term>birth chart<gloss>original: "genituræ"</gloss></term>; for before this time, being established in many labors and partnerships, they shall obtain the greatest profits from some violent pillaging <note>original: "uiolenta quapiam populatione"; this likely refers to spoils of war or aggressive business tactics</note>, and especially if the Sun is not regarded by the threatening <term>aspects<gloss>original: "radiatione," literally "radiations" or rays sent between planets</gloss></term> of <term>malefic stars<gloss>original: "maleuolæ ftellæ"</gloss></term>.

<margin>Sagittarius ♐︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Sagittarius, whoever has it so will be powerful and decorated with great marks of honor, but they will be people who bring much loss to others, and without any reason or equity, they may strip others bare even unto death by plundering; whence some sadness, the detractions of many, and anxieties may also befall them, and they may sometimes lose their children. This occurs especially when Saturn has first passed the trine of the birth chart, and the Sun has been weighed down by the threatening aspects of malefics; for before this time, they will be joyful, quite fortunate, and fertile with very beautiful offspring.

In Capricorn, if the Sun is found, whoever has it so will be kings of great fame and high name, who strive to prevent all evils threatening those of lower status, and do not permit the more powerful to rage against the people. But as soon as Saturn has passed the trine of the birth chart, then sicknesses, pains, and sadnesses are decreed, as well as a diminishing of honor and fame, and the loss of patrimony. For they will be made into the sort who seek the company of even viler men, and being joined in such society, they perform such things that disgrace and infamy follow them in many ways.

<margin>Aquarius ♒︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Aquarius, whoever has it so will be men commanding others, but of modest name and meager fame, and who have few faithful clients. For these men will be of their own will, commanding such things of their servants which often exceed their condition, whence they find few who are obedient to them. Many anxieties, labors, and illnesses will also happen to them and their associates, perhaps for this reason, and they will suffer many losses and perhaps even the destruction of their substance once adversaries are stirred up. But when Saturn has passed the <term>second trine<gloss>the second 120-degree milestone in Saturn's cycle around the birth chart</term> of the birth chart, they will devote their efforts to <term>matrimony<gloss>original: "rei uxoriæ," literally "matters of a wife"</gloss></term>.

<margin>Pisces ♓︎</margin>
If the Sun is found in Pisces, whoever has it so will be men devoted to games, jesting, and songs—lazy, quiet, idle, doing no work, but only following their own whims; neither regarding honesty of character nor baseness, but being entirely of bad character and a bad nature, whence many labors, many losses, and distresses will often occur. And this especially when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart; for before this time, being admitted only to these delights, they might perhaps be able to obtain good fortune, which they then turn into bad by their own fault.

## THE DECREES OF VENUS THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL SIGNS OF THE ZODIAC, CHAPTER VII.

<margin>Venus in Aries ♈︎</margin>
If <term>Venus<gloss>original: "♀"</gloss></term> is found in Aries, whoever has her so will be sad, solicitous, and anxious people, corrupted in both body and mind, poor, and beggars, and those whom many obstructions of diverse calamities shall harm. They will also be of much thought and various wandering, and often held by impure love; and especially if <term>Mars<gloss>original: "♂"</gloss></term> regards Venus so placed with some aspect. But when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart, and Venus is fortified by a prosperous aspect from <term>Jupiter<gloss>original: "♃"</gloss></term>, this bad fortune is mitigated somewhat, and promises better outcomes thereafter.

<margin>Taurus ♉︎</margin>
If Venus is found in Taurus, whoever has her so will be noble men and of a high heart, of great esteem and fame, intimates of kings and princes, and perhaps instructors of royal sons, and who always have familiarity with the leaders and noble men. And this especially if Venus, placed in suitable locations of the birth chart, is regarded by a prosperous aspect from Jupiter. But when Saturn has passed the second trine, some rumors shall arise against them, whence they may lose their acquired fame and perceive the greatest damages to their resources.

<margin>Gemini ♊︎</margin>
If Venus is found in Gemini, whoever has her so will be good people, having goodwill toward everyone, and who strive with a certain great heat of piety to help all people, and especially the poor and the afflicted. These will also be wise, shrewd, ingenious, eloquent, and handsome, and of a delightful appearance, most pleasing to everyone, and especi—
