<margin>Cancer ♋︎</margin> In Cancer, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be people intent only on feasts, banquets, and social circles, seeking gems, little stones, and other ornaments of this kind; they are lovers of beautiful clothes, and those who very often give themselves with their whole heart's affection to every kind of pleasure. This is especially true if, when Venus is established in favorable places of the birth chart, Jupiter regards her with a prosperous aspect. When Saturn has passed the trine of the birth chart—but before this time—they will be weighed down by some anxieties and labors, through which they suffer the greatest detriments to their life.

<margin>Leo ♌︎</margin> In Leo, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be poor people, neglected, flawed in body, of a diverse and varied nature, always intent on certain evil deeds, and who, being for the most part established in differing fortunes, are often exhausted by frequent labors. But as soon as Saturn has passed the trine of the birth chart, and if Venus has been fortified by the benign aspect of Jupiter, all these things are thoroughly diminished of their stain. For then, living for the most part among noble men, they both restore their reputation and obtain some assistance for their resources.

<margin>Virgo ♍︎</margin> In Virgo, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be people who are always sad, anxious, worried, and mournful, and those who, being flawed in body and mind, associate for the most part with needy and low-born men. This occurs especially when Saturn has first passed the trine of the birth chart, and Venus or <term>Mercury<gloss>original: "☿"</gloss></term> has been struck by the adverse aspect of malevolent stars. But when Saturn has passed the second trine, and Venus or Mercury has been fortified by the prosperous aspect of benevolent stars, then, with all evils driven away, a favorable fortune will at some point begin to breathe upon them a little.

<margin>Libra ♎︎</margin> In Libra, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be equitable and just people, but lovers of legal judgments or military honors; those who, compelled by a cause involving a woman, are oftentimes forced by arms to drive out adversaries, and from this they may suffer no small inconveniences of adversity. This happens especially when Saturn has passed the second trine of the birth chart; for before this time, they will be intent on jests, games, and songs, and entangled in feminine loves, from which, although they may sometimes incur many labors, they will nevertheless perceive many delights of pleasure.

<margin>Scorpio ♏︎</margin> In Scorpio, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be choleric, litigious, proud, and haughty in spirit, and those who always follow after lawsuits, discords, and quarrels, desiring by any means whatsoever to obtain the desires of their will. These people, having no respect for honesty or equity, will attempt to violently wrench desired things from the hands of others; for this reason, they will not care even to descend at times to the killing of men <note>original: "intersectiones etiam hominum," literally the "cutting down" or "slaughter" of people.</note>. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, having at last turned toward the reason of equity, they will strive to change the habits of their former life for the better.

<margin>Sagittarius ♐︎</margin> In Sagittarius, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be javelin-throwers, archers, and those who take the greatest delight in martial games of this kind; for this reason, they will perhaps be pleasing to noble men, whose constant company they will always enjoy. From this, they will be able to acquire some support for their life, and obtain fame and a glorious name among others. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, being entangled in evil and wicked associations, whatever they had obtained in their early youth, they lose it all through a certain wretched infamy and the tearing away of adverse fortune.

<margin>Capricorn ♑︎</margin> In Capricorn, if Venus is found, whoever has her so will be honest, peaceful, and cheerful people, lovers of jesters, songs, and fellowships, of good stature and beautiful appearance, and those who are most delighted by banquets and love beautiful and adorned things. This is especially so when Saturn has first passed the trine of the birth chart; for before this time, they will be joined especially to shameful people, from whom they may obtain disgrace and infamy rather than honor, particularly if Saturn regards Venus, established in weakened places of the birth chart, with a threatening and adverse aspect.

<margin>Aquarius ♒︎</margin> In Aquarius, if Venus is found, those who have her so will be people devoted only to fowling <note>The hunting or trapping of wild birds.</note> and hunting, but in other matters lazy, sluggish, idle, and melancholy, and who know themselves to have no [good skills]...

### THE DECREES OF MERCURY THROUGH EACH OF THE SIGNS OF THE ZODIAC. CHAPTER VIII.

<image-desc>A decorative initial letter 'M' depicting a classical scene, likely involving figures in a pastoral or mythological landscape.</image-desc>

<margin>Mercury in Aries ♈</margin>
If <term>Mercury<gloss>original: "☿"</gloss></term> is found in Aries, whoever has him so will be evil, litigious, brawlers, contentious, murderers, and those who, with various shouts, always attempt to oppose everyone shrewdly and insidiously; for that reason, they frequently fall into the greatest losses and calamities. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, and if Mercury is fortified by the prosperous aspect of benevolent stars, they are forced to lay aside something of their former ferocity, whence they may prepare some friends for themselves, from whom they may obtain the necessary supports of life.

<margin>Taurus ♉</margin>
In Taurus, if Mercury is found, those who have him so will be jesters, singers, and those who delight in games, stories, banquets, and gluttony; they will be sluggish, slow, idle, and devoted only to the belly and to pleasures. They will, however, be crafty, ingenious, and sagacious, and those who execute many things by the strength of their talent. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, and Mercury is hindered by the rays of malevolent stars, then labors, then anxieties, then many inconveniences are decreed, from which many losses may come to them.

<margin>Gemini ♊</margin>
In Gemini, if Mercury is found, whoever has him so will be men of sharp sense, ingenious, and sagacious, but always prone to evil, and who always apply their eloquence and industry to lawsuits, brawls, dissensions, and discords. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, then losses and detriments, then calamities and wants are decreed, and this especially in the <term>climacteric years<gloss>original: "hebdomaticis, uel enneaticis annis," referring to years based on the numbers seven and nine, which ancient physicians and astrologers believed were turning points in life</gloss></term>, in which they will sometimes come to such a great lack of things that they are forced to miserably beg for the necessary supports of life from others.

<margin>Cancer ♋</margin>
In Cancer, if Mercury is found, whoever has him so will be sad, solicitous, anxious, and daily occupied in many thoughts; they will, however, be crafty, shrewd, cunning, caviling, and full of deceits and snares, with which they always attempt to falsely attack and overcome others; they will also perform evil deeds, from which they often fall into great infamy and detriments. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, having laid aside their evil character and deceitful works, they will be converted to a better life, and for a short time will enjoy a prosperous decree of fortune.

<margin>Leo ♌</margin>
In Leo, if Mercury is found, whoever has him so will be soldiers, giving their efforts primarily to military matters; they will love wars and battles, in which they will especially prevail, from which they will achieve honor and glory with the greatest usefulness. They will also be so greedy for victory that they often attempt to violently snatch it from the hands of enemies, beyond what is fair and just. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, they will be led into some sorrows and labors, from which they perceive the greatest hindrances to life, especially if Mercury is hindered by the rays of malevolent planets.

<margin>Virgo ♍</margin>
In Virgo, if Mercury is found, whoever has him so will be strong, industrious, and sagacious, breeders of horses, hawks, falcons, and other birds pertaining to fowling, and likewise of dogs, mastiffs, and <term>greyhounds<gloss>original: "uertagorū," a type of swift hunting dog</gloss></term>, and those suited for hunting. They will also hold men and soldiers, and all the equipment pertaining to military service, and most of all...

<margin>Capricorn ♑</margin>

But when the first trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, and if Mercury is aided by the prosperous rays of Jupiter or <term>Venus<gloss>original symbol: ♀</gloss></term>, being somewhat relieved from such great calamities, they will seek out a few small gains and the meager supports of life by which they may live miserably until death.

<margin>Aquarius ♒</margin>
If Mercury is found in Aquarius, whoever has him thus will be astronomers, augurs, soothsayers, magicians, accountants, interpreters of dreams, and those who, moved by a certain divine frenzy, predict future things to the nations, whereby they achieve both a name among the people and many supports for life. They will also be those who always labor in the investigation of hidden things, treasures, metals, and other secrets. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, being most occupied with these things, they will come into some obstacles of life.

<margin>Pisces ♓</margin>
If Mercury is found in Pisces, whoever has him thus will be beautiful, sharp, intelligent, most equitable followers of laws and judgments, of charming appearance, well-composed in body and limbs, taking great joy in fine garments, eloquent, articulate, and learned in many sciences; for this reason, they are honored by all, from whom they seek many supports of wealth, especially if a prosperous aspect from Jupiter looks upon Mercury so placed. But when the second trine of the birth chart has passed Saturn, then, occupied with some disturbances, they will come into several obstacles of life.

...of great name and much fame, of charming appearance, composed manners, and who bring their business to completion with always modest counsel; tranquil, quiet, cheerful, of good complexion, and those who are greatly beloved by the people—especially if the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is so placed in **Taurus** <note>original: ♉</note> or **Gemini** <note>original: ♊</note> and looks upon it with a prosperous radiation. But when **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> has passed according to the <term>trine<gloss>An astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, often marking significant life cycles</gloss></term> of the <term>birth chart<gloss>original: genituræ</gloss></term>, especially in the <term>ninth<gloss>original: enneaticis</gloss></term> or <term>seventh<gloss>original: hebdomaticis</gloss></term> years, being entangled in some adversities, they will encounter the greatest impediments of life.

<margin>Gemini ♊ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Gemini**, whoever has it thus will be poor, wretched, and unhappy, of foul appearance, physically impaired, and handling their affairs and business without any counsel or moderation; from which they produce both disgrace for themselves and often many losses of resources. These people will also be base, abject, of rustic manners, foul and dressed in filthy clothing, of meager sustenance, and utterly despised in all things. Yet they will be of good sense, sharp wit, and sufficiently industrious for all actions if they wish, and this especially when Saturn has fulfilled the trine according to the birth chart; for before this time, occupied with better business, they will lead a sufficiently milder life.

<margin>Cancer ♋ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Cancer**, whoever has it thus will be kings and princes, of great and high name, good fame, exalted rank, and ample dignity; powerful, rich, wealthy, and those whom many willingly obey. They will also be of beautiful appearance, charming face, tall and lovely body, and to be feared with a certain benevolence. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, they will become somewhat irritable, harsh, hard, and severe, and who, often venting rage upon others, encounter some impediments of life. But once that time has passed, having become pious and just again, they will obtain the greatest marks of honor.

<margin>Leo ♌ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Leo**, whoever has it thus will similarly be kings and princes, decorated with a beautiful lineage of honors, rich, opulent, and wealthy. But they are puffed up with a certain hostile spirit of pride, by which they exercise much cruelty and savagery toward their subjects; wherefore they turn the hearts of the people against them in a certain irritable sedition, so that for that reason they despise them and refuse to obey their commands. For which reason, as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, they will turn to a better way of life, so that they may win over the hearts of the people. But returning at last to their first actions, they will lead a miserable and despised life.

<margin>Virgo ♍ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Virgo**, whoever has it thus will be sad men, solicitous, anxious, of many thoughts, and of various wanderings, seeking how they might provide the sustenance of life for themselves. They will, however, be of good intellect, sharp wit, and composed through the practice of many arts. But on account of their bad fortune, always disfigured by the tearing of their clothes, and serving many with their songs and storytelling so that they might seek a living therefrom. But when Saturn has passed according to the trine of the birth chart, and Taurus and the Moon have been fortified by the radiation of benevolent stars, they will restore their life by a better decree of the fates.

<margin>Libra ♎ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Libra**, whoever has it thus will be nobles and leaders of cities, rich, wealthy, and powerful; but who, having left behind all their business, turn—sluggish and idle—only to the relaxation of the mind. They are always watchful for games, jesting, songs, and dances, and pleasures of this kind; they consort with playful women and harlots, and for that reason suffer the loss of honor, fame, and even their resources. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, occupied with many adversities, they will fall into great labors, distresses, and anxieties, so that they are compelled, even by force, to abandon their previous way of life.

<margin>Scorpio ♏ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Scorpio**, whoever has it thus will be evil men, harsh, cruel, and those who are exhausted by many anxieties, pains, and distresses; ignorant, inexperienced in human affairs, of thick wit, and who, because of their ignorance, are often led into many errors, from which great detriments sometimes come to them and their own. But as soon as Saturn has passed the first trine of the birth chart, being somewhat relieved and taught by the experience of things, they will find wretched subsidies for life. In their ninth <note>enneaticis</note> and seventh <note>hebdomaticis</note> years, however, they will suffer such inconveniences of calamity that, being set in adversities, they will often desire death with an afflicted heart.

<margin>Sagittarius ♐ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon is found in **Sagittarius**, whoever has it thus will be kings and princes, or leaders of cities; rich, powerful, wealthy, of good sense, and of the best counsel and judgment, lovers of laws and justice. But they are inexperienced in letters, sluggish, lazy, idle, and those who concerning things, or their empire...

### THE DECREES OF THE PLANETS IN THE TERMS OF OTHERS, AND FIRST SATURN. CHAPTER X.

<margin>Saturn in its own places.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative historiated initial 'S' depicting a figure in robes seated at a table or desk, surrounded by floral flourishes.</image-desc>
If **Saturn** <note>original: Saturnus</note> is found in its own house or <term>decan<gloss>A ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</gloss></term> <note>original: decano</note>, and it is a daytime birth, it makes men who always seek the friendship of noble men, kings, and princes, joined with them in constant conversation of commerce and habit. If, being so placed, it is found in the <term>Horoscope<gloss>The Ascendant, or the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</gloss></term> <note>original: horosc.</note>, and the <term>Lot of Fortune<gloss>A mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity</gloss></term> <note>original: locus fortunae</note> is joined to it in a similar partnership, it decrees the greatest abundance of resources. <margin>Jupiter ♃</margin>**Saturn** if found in the house or decan of **Jupiter**, and it is a daytime birth, decrees a happy state, plenty of substance, and a multitude of honors. For then they prosperously nourish children, love their wives, and enter into societies and secret councils of noble men, from which they acquire an honored name and fame for themselves. But if it is a nighttime birth, it decrees discord with noble men, and enmities and contentions with the leaders of the city; it also threatens the mournful death of the father.

<margin>Mars ♂</margin>**Saturn** if found in the house or decan of **Mars**, in both a daytime and a nighttime birth, makes men harsh, crude, severe, and who are never moved by any inclination of piety or mercy; also grave, wrathful, and often thinking many things both in their own deeds and those of others—difficult indeed, intractable, proud, and insolent, but who conciliate close friendships and necessities especially with similar princes and soldiers.

<margin>Sun ☉</margin>**Saturn** if found in the house or decan of the **Sun**, and if it is a daytime birth, decrees full honors and riches for the father, then a memorable name and excellent fame, which is also extended to posterity in like measure; yet they will suffer from moist illnesses, and [will die a violent death]...

<margin>Jupiter in its own places.</margin>

If **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> is found in its own house or decan and it is a daytime birth chart, it makes men fortunate, wealthy, and honored, upon whom the greatest signs of honor are bestowed—provided no malevolent star gazes upon it with a threatening aspect. It also makes them pleasing and beloved to princes, and preferred for some magisterial office among them. However, if it is a nighttime birth chart, it diminishes something of this happy decree and causes them to be exhausted by some labors.

<margin>♄</margin>

They will be narrow-hearted and greedy for profit, for the sake of which they consider neither labors nor even shameful deeds, from which they often suffer bad consequences.

<margin>♂</margin>

This is especially true if the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> or **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, placed in the angles of the birth chart, gaze upon them with a benevolent aspect and confirm them by their own decree.

<margin>☉</margin>

If, joined in such a partnership, it is placed in the angles of the birth chart or their anaphoras, it perhaps makes them decorated with royal power—either they are kings themselves, or vicars of kings and princes. If it is a nighttime birth chart, something of this happiness is diminished.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> is found in the house or decan of **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> and it is a daytime birth chart, it makes men honored in the houses of princes, either managing their councils or collecting taxes, from which they acquire the greatest benefits for themselves. # THE DECREES OF MARS IN THE BOUNDS OF OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER XII.

<margin>Mars in his own places.</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial M depicting a robed figure seated in an architectural setting with columns and foliage.</image-desc>
If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in his own house or decan, in both a daytime and a nighttime birth chart, it will make men proud, bold, cruel, and prone to anger, who strive to bring all the concepts of their mind to completion. These people, however, will squander the wealth of their parents, and for this reason, they will perhaps lose their older brothers. They will also be fierce, reckless, impetuous, and adorned with no gift of piety or religion, but rather driven mad by a certain license of their own recklessness.

**Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>: If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in the house or decan of **Saturn**, in both a daytime and a nighttime birth chart, it will make men handsome, swift, and agile in running, and as easy as they are industrious in all their works. However, they will be melancholic and seekers of hidden things, such as treasures, tombs, gold and silver, hidden metal, and finally all things that are foreign to the common custom of men. Nevertheless, their younger brothers, by the fatal decree of the stars, will destroy their wealth.

**Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>: If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in the house or decan of **Jupiter**, likewise in either type of birth chart, it will make men noble, great, and haughty, joined to the intimate society and goodwill of kings and princes, from whom they obtain not only marks of honor but also the means of life. But if **Jupiter** is positioned in the house of **Mars**, or regards him with a favorable alignment, it will make them noble leaders of armies and many military forces, from which they will achieve a great name and glory for themselves.

**The Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>: If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in the house or decan of the **Sun**, in both a daytime and a nighttime birth chart, it makes men who destroy themselves, wasting their father’s wealth and utterly squandering their own honor and reputation. To lead their lives, they will practice some craft involving iron <note>such as blacksmithing or soldiering</note>; however, they will suffer from a serious ailment in the eyes and stomach, from which they may die either a sudden or a <term>violent death<gloss>original: biothanata morte</gloss></term>. If **Saturn** is also found in the same place, he will confirm all these things with a more stable decree.

**Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>: If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in the house or decan of **Venus**, likewise in either type of birth chart, it will make men lustful, incestuous, debauchers, and adulterers, who either violate female relatives or, by doing them wrong, pursue the wives of others. But such men, as soon as they see the cruel intent of their women, will either join themselves in marriage to prostitutes, or they will die by the sword or fire, or perhaps be taken away by some betrayal of enemies in a violent death.

**Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>: If **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in the house or decan of **Mercury**, also in either birth chart, it will make men sensible, clever, and cunning, who, surpassing their associates by their own shrewdness, gain much through deceits and snares. They will, however, be of good thought and understanding, and they will labor for a long time with both skill and genius, so that...

### THE DECREES OF THE SUN IN THE DOMAINS OF THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>The Sun in its own places</margin>
If the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> is found in its own house or decan, and it is a daytime birth chart, it makes kings—rich, great, and strong—who conquer great wealth and glory from others, especially if, thus positioned, they are placed in the <term>angles<gloss>original: cardines; the four most powerful points in a horoscope</gloss></term> of the birth chart or their <term>succedent houses<gloss>original: anaphoris; the houses immediately following the angles</gloss></term>. If it is a nighttime birth chart, it decrees the father's sorrow and a sudden death; however, it often makes men travelers who nonetheless find advantage and utility in their travels.

<margin>Saturn</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it makes men of high heart and deep thought, who always seek out great and hidden things with wise inquiry; these will be stable and constant in all their works, never ceasing from what they have begun until they achieve the desired end. If it is a nighttime birth chart, all these things are decreed by a lighter fate, and men are rendered inconsistent in their works.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, in either birth chart, it makes men gentle, faithful, and greater and more worthy within their lineage, but who do not watch much over wealth and profits, especially if the **Moon** is also in the same place, joined in close association. These people will also be extremely lustful, desiring the wives of their kinsmen, nor will they think it shameful to have intercourse with their own mother or stepmother. The same lust is decreed in a woman's birth chart.

<margin>Mars</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it decrees liver pain and such illnesses from which death itself is feared; it also causes the father to die a <term>violent death<gloss>original: biothanatū</gloss></term>, especially if there is such an <insert>unfavorable</insert> association of rays <note>astrological aspects between the planets</note>; however, it makes men quite rich and opulent, as well as industrious and successful in their business. If it is a nighttime birth chart, all the aforementioned evils will be diminished, nor will they rage with such a harsh decree.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, in both a daytime and a nighttime birth chart, it makes men divine, soothsayers, astronomers, interpreters of dreams, and those who foretell the future by some heavenly mystery; seekers of hidden things, truth-tellers, good, faithful, and those who delight in various journeys and travels. They will, however, be somewhat irritable and <term>choleric<gloss>possessing an angry or fiery temperament</gloss></term>, and suffering from <term>moist qualities<gloss>an imbalance of bodily humors, such as excess phlegm</gloss></term> to such an extent that they often suffer ills from them.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, in a daytime birth chart, it makes men of much knowledge and good works, clever, secretive, faithful, and greatly beloved by nobles, but for the most part sickly and suffering from moist illnesses. If it is a nighttime birth chart, it renders them poor and wicked in their first age, performing evil deeds, but afterwards makes them rich and involved in magic tricks, though they are often fatigued by illness of the eyes and stomach.

<margin>Moon</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it makes men worthy, honored, and amiable, obtaining many insignia of magistracies and honors, and who are joined to kings and princes in the familiarity of close relationship. These people, however, often weighed down by moist qualities, fall into various and troublesome illnesses. If it is a nighttime birth chart, all these things occur nonetheless, but are decreed with a certain restricted influence.

### THE DECREES OF VENUS IN THE DOMAINS OF THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER XIV.

<margin>Venus in her own places <note>original symbol: ♀</note></margin>
If **Venus** is found in her own house or <term>decan<gloss>a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</gloss></term>, in both a daytime and a nighttime <term>birth chart<gloss>original: genitura</gloss></term>, she decrees a multitude of joys, an increase in happiness, and the rewards of good fortune. They will, nevertheless, be fortunate in the rest of their works and always beloved by everyone.

<margin>Saturn <note>original symbol: ♄</note></margin>

<margin>Jupiter <note>original symbol: ♃</note></margin>

They will, however, be hateful to their parents because of this, but they will pursue their own wives with a great intensity of love, and from this they will prepare for themselves gladness and joy.

<margin>Mars <note>original symbol: ♂</note></margin>

These men will also be pursuers of other men's wives, or of public prostitutes, or of female slaves; for this reason, they will either abandon their own wives or cruelly kill them.

<margin>The Sun <note>original symbol: ☉</note></margin>

They will, however, be lovers of noble girls especially; frequently because of them, they fall into many losses and damages, and even into the highest infamy, and perhaps into dangers of death which can only be avoided with the greatest difficulty.

<margin>Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note></margin>
If **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> is found in the house or decan of **Mercury**, in either birth chart, she will make men exceedingly lustful, and pursuers especially of boys or of small girls. They are those who study to serve women with every art and ingenuity, from which many inconveniences might perhaps come to them.

<margin>The Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note></margin>

For such men will be those who, held back by no reason of kinship or blood relation <note>a reference to incestuous inclinations</note>, are led toward whatever affections their appetite dictates. These men, intent on many things, will never persist in a stable purpose in any one undertaking.

### THE CONCLUDING INSTITUTIONAL INSTRUCTION OF THIS FIFTH BOOK, CHAPTER 17.

All these things, Mavortius—our glory—have been specially made known to you, nor has anything been omitted by us which the seers of the divine race and the interpreters of this discipline <note>the "discipline" refers to astrology</note> have brought forth with the study of prudent skill and learned speech. But this, which we have frequently said, we emphasize to your own prudent attention: that you must compare the entire force of the stars, the mixtures of all the signs, and the efficacy of the <term>parts<gloss>the specific degrees of the zodiac</gloss></term> according to the powers of their locations in turn. Do not seek to explain the entire substance of a <term>birth chart<gloss>original: genitura</gloss></term> from the course of a single star; rather, first join the <term>horoscope<gloss>the Ascendant or Rising Sign</gloss></term> with the powers of the twelve <term>places<gloss>the twelve astrological houses</gloss></term>, and also compare the stars with each individual star. Seek to find which star is joined to the horoscope by what <term>radiation<gloss>the light or "aspect" sent from one planet to another</gloss></term>, and to what extent the powers of the constellations either attack or uplift their own stars. Consider also what forms the natural appearance of the signs or parts attributes to individual stars, and what the authority of the individual places and <term>angles<gloss>the four most powerful points: Rising, Setting, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven</gloss></term> decrees. 

When all these things have been collected through wise inquiry, and the substance of the birth chart has been inspected, then bring forth your judgments on individual matters. But first, with a balanced comparison, you must diligently inspect the forms, the <term>Lots<gloss>mathematical points in a chart, like the "Lot of Fortune"</gloss></term>, and even the <term>rising times<gloss>original: anaphoras; refers to the order signs rise or the timing of life periods</gloss></term> of the signs. For the entry of **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> into the places of **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> does not always decree wives, nor does entry into the place of children grant children; rather, it grants these things to those for whom the original substance of the birth chart has already decreed wives or children. Nor does **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> always look back with threatening radiations when circling from the setting of the horoscope. Nor does **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> always decree grave crises of danger with general malicious cruelty when coming from the part of the horoscope. 

Instead, for whomever dangers were decreed from the substance of the entire birth chart, it is then—when they have advanced from the rising times of the signs and become the <term>Lords of the Times<gloss>planets that "rule" a specific period of a person's life</gloss></term>—that the sequences of all dangers are carried out. Therefore, as these factors are mixed by very frequent movement through the powers of individual parts, they ought to instruct your mind—formed by divine instruction—with skillful conjecture. For frequently **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> changes the condition of a bad sign by its goodness, and the healthy hospitality of a good part weakens the malice of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>. You should not expect a crisis from a bad house when a healthy star regards it, just as the threatening rays of malevolent stars are broken by the opportunity of their location. For in the birth charts of men, the mixture of places, parts, signs, and stars composes everything. If you collect all these with balanced moderation, you will be able to explain the entire fate of a man with the truest judgments. But, this book being finished, let our discourse transfer to the principles of the sixth book; for there I will make known to you all the mixtures of the stars with the truest interpretations, so that once that book is explained, our purpose may transfer—with good omens <note>original: bonis auibus, literally "with good birds"</note>—to the specific interpretation of <term>astrological outcomes<gloss>original: apothelesmatum</gloss></term>.

# THE MATHESIS OF JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS
## THE YOUNGER, OF SICILY, A MAN OF SENATORIAL RANK <note>original: V. C., for Vir Clarissimus</note>, TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANUS,
### PROCONSUL. BOOK VI.
#### PREFACE.

FREQUENTLY, Mavortius, our glory, our discourse has advised you concerning the mixtures of the stars. You need seek nothing else in all your judgments, nothing in the substance of the decrees, if you have grasped the efficacy of the mixed tempering—especially since in the birth charts of men, the first angles do one thing, and the second angles do another. For the first angles possess the horoscope and the <term>Midheaven<gloss>the highest point of the chart</gloss></term>; the second ones receive the <term>Imum Coeli<gloss>the lowest point of the chart, or "bottom of the sky"</gloss></term> and the setting. From the always varying and contrary power of these four angles, it is known...

<meta>Catchword: ...known (gnoscitur)</meta>

<summary>Firmicus Maternus concludes Book Five by warning that no single planet determines a fate, urging the astrologer to synthesize the "mixtures" of all chart factors. He then opens Book Six by introducing the specialized power of the four primary chart angles (Cardines).</summary>
<keywords>Mavortius Lollianus, planetary mixtures, astrological houses, horoscope, Ascendant, Midheaven, Imum Coeli, Lords of the Times, anaphoras, birth chart interpretation</keywords>

--- Page 169 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the twelve astrological "places" (houses), specifically how their relationship to the Ascendant (Horoscope) determines the strength of the planets. It marks the transition into the main technical instruction of Book Six, focusing on the "Royal Stars"—specific degrees of the zodiac that grant supreme power and imperial dignity.</meta>

...the substance of every birth chart is known. All stars, according to the powers of their own natures, decree one thing when positioned in the primary **angles** <note>The four "cardines" or pivots: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven.</note> and another in the secondary ones. However, the fifth and eleventh places from the **horoscope** <note>The "horoscope" here refers to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note>—that is, the places of Good Fortune and Good Spirit—are signs of "lazy" locations; because they disagree with a sluggish humility, they are joined to these lazy and dejected places by no sharing of reason. Instead, the ninth and third places from the horoscope obtain the true efficacy of decreeing, for these locations join the horoscope in a very great partnership of society.

But the second and eighth places from the horoscope are separated from the shared partnership, as every bond with the horoscope is dissolved. The sixth and twelfth places from the horoscope are excluded by all reasoning of society and are attacked by the falling humility of their dejection. From this variety of locations, then, the power of the stars is either raised up or falls away, just as we showed in the preceding explanation; for in the third book we specifically included what each individual star decrees when positioned in each place.

But you, implore with whatever prayers you can, that the course of either **benefic** <note>well-willing planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> or **malefic** <note>ill-willing planets like Saturn and Mars</note> stars never occupies the sixth or twelfth place from the horoscope, nor even the second and eighth, in the decrees of men. For these locations are always occupied by the hostile radiations of all the stars; indeed, whatever constellation of stars settles in these places either loses the healing protection of its own goodness or, if it is a malignant star, it worsens the power of its malice more strongly toward doing harm. Malefic stars are even strengthened in these places when the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is positioned there, and they decree—generally and without any remedy—the ruins of misfortunes. Benefic stars, however, being closed off in the hidden humilities of these places, lose the healing protection of their own power.

Furthermore, the changeable condition of the stars works one way in **diurnal** <note>daytime</note> and another in **nocturnal** <note>nighttime</note> birth charts. They also possess various powers of decreeing when the individual stars are joined to one another by **trine**, **square**, or **opposite** <note>original: "diametra"</note> radiation. For from this, the entire society of "mixtures" is tempered; from this, the total power of the decrees is inspected. For the stars, always positioned opposite to one another according to their nature or condition, compose the fates of men with an equal moderation of variety. 

Therefore, Mavortius—our glory—I will now explain to you this substance of the mixtures, so that you may have the full discipline of this divine wisdom to the end. But before our discourse approaches the explanation of the mixtures, I will tell you a few things about the royal powers of the **bright stars** <note>Specific fixed stars considered to have great influence</note>, so that the beginnings of this book, adorned with the explanations of the August constellations, may proceed under a more fortunate omen.

### THE ROYAL STARS OF THE SIGNS AND THEIR DECREES, CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' with intricate floral and scrollwork designs.</image-desc>

We find clear stars, shining with the radiation of August majesty, in all the signs, but the royal ones are in four: namely, in **Taurus** <note>original symbol: ♉</note>, **Leo** <note>original symbol: ♌</note>, **Scorpio** <note>original symbol: ♏</note>, and **Aquarius** <note>original symbol: ♒</note>. In which parts <note>degrees</note> of these you may find the August light, I shall show in a brief discourse.

The fifth degree of **Leo** has a star shining with lucid splendor. If the **Moon**, increasing in light, is found in this star while the horoscope or the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C," the highest point in the chart</note> is presiding exactly over the angle, it decrees kingdoms and the greatest power of empires. 

The twentieth degree of **Aquarius** is also decorated with a similar splendor of majesty; for if the **Moon** is in the ascendant in this star, full of light, and possesses the primary angles of the birth chart, it decrees in a similar way the insignia of royal power and imperial dignity.

Also, the fifteenth, twenty-seventh, and thirtieth degrees of **Taurus** are equally adorned with the light of majesty. For if the **Moon** is found in the fifteenth degree of **Taurus**, it decrees an increase of most powerful and affluent substance, provided it possesses the primary angles of the birth chart. If the **Moon** is found in the twenty-seventh degree of **Taurus**, it decrees great insignia of dignity and makes such men as sustain the lives of great populations by their own power, giving to the people whatever is zealously requested, and consecrating magnificent and famous gifts to temples, so that they may be honored by these perpetual splendors of glory. 

The thirtieth degree of **Taurus**, as we said, also flashes with the divine light of majesty. For if the **Moon** is found in this degree, it decrees the insignia of great power and license; for if it is found positioned in this degree in the primary angles, it decrees leadership, empires, and kingship—especially if, while the Moon is increasing in light, prosperous **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> looks upon it with its radiation. For then, raised up by the license of their power and possessing dominion of both sea and land, they shall successfully lead an army wherever they wish. The seventh degree of **Scorpio** will also effect these same things, for a similar splendor of majesty [adorns] that same part...

# THE RADIATIONS OF THE PLANETS, AND THEIR DECREES; AND FIRST, THE TRIGONAL RADIATION OF THE PLANETS. CHAPTER II.

All stars, if they look upon each other in a trigonal radiation <note>A "trine" aspect, where planets are 120 degrees apart (four signs away from each other). In ancient astrology, this was considered the most harmonious and beneficial relationship.</note>, whether they are **benefics** <note>Well-willing planets: Jupiter and Venus</note> or **malefics** <note>Ill-willing planets: Saturn and Mars</note>, are always compared to prosperous temperaments of mixtures. Indeed, the wickedness of the malefics is mitigated by this radiation, while the most salutary benefits of the benefics are strengthened.

## SATURN IN TRINE WITH THE OTHER PLANETS. CHAPTER III.

<margin>Saturn in trine with Jupiter</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative initial letter S containing scrolling foliage and floral motifs.</image-desc>If Saturn <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined with Jupiter <note>original: "♃"</note> in a trigonal radiation, and this conjunction avoids being corrupted by lazy or dejected places <note>The "bad" houses of the chart (the 6th, 8th, and 12th) which were thought to weaken planets.</note>, and both are in signs in which they rejoice, or one of them positioned in his own house <note>The zodiac sign a planet "rules," such as Capricorn for Saturn or Sagittarius for Jupiter.</note> looks upon the other with a trigonal radiation, and they are associated with the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horoſc."</note> by an exact radiation <note>original: "partili radiatione" — meaning an aspect that is accurate to the same degree, not just the same sign.</note>, they decree the riches of infinite wealth with great happiness. This is especially true if one of them receives the light of the waxing Moon <note>original: "☽"</note>; then Saturn grants the dominion of infinite and great possessions, then he decrees sacred sowings, pastures, and wooded glades. He makes such men that kings commit all the duties of their actions to them and frequently impose the gift of an illustrious embassy upon them. These men, however, are fatigued by excessive misfortunes from the falls of their sons; either losing their sons, they are forced to nourish the offspring of others, or they certainly receive back their own sons after a long space of time, having been raised by others. For if Mars either strikes this mixture with a threatening radiation, or if it is a nocturnal birth chart, all these things we have said are diminished. ### JUPITER WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
#### THE TRINE ASPECT, CHAPTER IV.

<margin>Jupiter with Mars in trine.</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of dejection, they decree the greatest commands of dignity and a great freedom of power. They render such men as complete all their actions with the most successful reasoning, decreeing duties of the highest administration and making them those upon whom frequent honors are conferred by the judgment of kings.

<margin>Sun</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of dejection, they decree the greatest increases in nobility and copious protections of flowing riches. They also bestow the marks of great glory, create the greatest joy from the successes of children, and always adorn and honor the life with the clear status of dignity.

<margin>Venus</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to **Venus** by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of dejection, they decree the greatest grace of truth. They always associate the person with all good men through lovable conversation and induce a faithful love for their wives. However, the increases of inheritance and the marks of dignity are granted to them entirely through the help of friends or wives.

<margin>Mercury</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to **Mercury** by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of dejection, they make men who are gifted, wise, and formed by the sharpest power of talent, who execute all business with successful actions. They cause them to be preferred above all men by merit of magnificent and most powerful dignity, and they perfect them so that in all their acts they are always praised and well-pleasing. They will also make them scribes, set over public and fiscal accounts, handling public duties without any blame, and organizing royal necessities by their own arrangements. Others they will cause to aptly understand the secrets of the celestial stars.

# SIXTH BOOK

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "Iupiter" or "♃"</note> should be joined to the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> by a trine aspect <term>trine: an auspicious astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, forming a triangle</term>, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart <term>genitura: a person's birth chart or horoscope</term> and removed from all the weaknesses of their Fall <term>deiectionum humilitatibus: refers to the "Fall," the specific zodiac sign where a planet’s power is most diminished</term>, and if the Moon is full of light, they will make men famous, distinguished by a reputation for nobility, and bearing witness to a good name. Depending on the rest of the birth chart’s substance, they grant some the permit for the most powerful administrations, place others in command of the army, and entrust others with the judgments of the greatest provinces. But these same men they make noble through upright and incorruptible judgment, so that their integrity is honored by an always untainted freedom of power.

### MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### THE TRINE ASPECT, CHAPTER V.

<margin>Mars with the Sun in trine.</margin>

If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> should be joined to the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of their Fall, they decree signs of the greatest power and highest dignity, especially if in a nocturnal birth the Sun is positioned on the right side of Mars; then powers of glorious license and commands of honors are decreed. If, however, while these are so positioned, **Jupiter** should look upon them with a favorable aspect from another side of the triangle, and the Moon’s ray should reach all these while she is positioned at the primary angles <term>cardinibus: the four most powerful points in a chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term> and in a good place, then they entrust the greatest administrations of the army and decree infinite signs of dignity with the power of the greatest license. But these effects will be stronger if Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter are positioned in masculine signs.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **Mars** should be joined to **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of their Fall, they decree daily profits from a steady continuation of gains, and they bring about a prosperous marriage alliance from this conjunction; such people will be those who always conduct themselves with pleasing honor, yet are uplifted by a proud spirit of power; but always seeking many marriages, they will attain these very things by the easiest means.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If **Mars** should be joined to **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of their Fall, they make men wise and, in all actions, guided by the successful reasoning of their counsels; they are those whom a prosperous outcome always follows in every business conversation, and who can mitigate the narrow straits of all necessities by the authority of their advice; they are sharp, effective, and handle the duties of reasoning, accounting, or literature.

<margin>Moon</margin>
If **Mars** should be joined to the **Moon** by a trine aspect, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all weaknesses of their Fall, and the Moon is waning in light <note>original: "minuta luminibus"</note> and it is a nocturnal birth, they decree all the ornaments of happiness and, in all acts, they bestow prosperous outcomes with constant successes. They also cause them to attain everything they desire by the easiest means. But if **Jupiter** should look upon this mixture of Mars and the Moon with his own aspect, they will surely promise the greatest men from such a stellar configuration; they will likewise decree commands of the greatest dignity, and bestow glory and the license of great power. They will produce such men that they may be worthily compared to the first magistrates in the state <note>original: "rep." for "republica"</note>, who have dominion over many peoples, by whose counsels the deeds of princes are handled, and who have the highest power and veneration among nations. If, however, the Moon is full of light, amidst these prosperities they nevertheless weaken the body with the constant affliction of various illnesses, and sometimes, by their fatal radiation, they exhaust them with many troubles and the hindrances of disturbances.

# VENUS WITH THE MOON ALONE, IN TRINE CHAPTER VII.

If **Venus** is joined to the **Moon** by a trine radiation <term>trine: an auspicious astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart</term>, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowliness of their Falls <term>dejectionum: refers to the "Fall," the specific zodiac sign where a planet’s power is most diminished</term>, and the Moon is lessened in light <note>original: "minuta luminibus," meaning a waning moon</note>, and if it is a nocturnal birth, then the signs of the highest happiness are decreed through them. # MERCURY WITH THE MOON ALONE, IN TRINE CHAPTER VIII.

If **Mercury** is joined to the **Moon** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowliness of their Falls, they decree all things according to the variety of the signs <note>The specific zodiac signs where the planets are located</note>. To some, they assign eloquence of speech; to others, they decree from this aspect distinguished signs of the arts; to others, they hand down the sweet sound of music. They make others painters, but of the sort whose distinguished nobility always introduces their arts. To others, they decree the power of arms; to others, they hand down the discipline of joy and gladness. Others, singing with sweet modulation, they assign to popular pleasures; but all these they always recommend to the faithful judgment of the people. Others they make into those handling the duties of merchants. But they explain all these things according to the testimonies of the other stars and according to the strengths of the houses and signs. However, which trines are "right" and which are "square" was explained in the second book.

# THE SQUARE RADIATION OF ALL THE PLANETS CHAPTER IX.

Now I shall tell you the decrees of the square radiation <term>square: a challenging astrological aspect of 90 degrees, often associated with tension or conflict</term>. This fellowship is always composed of a strong and threatening star, for from that conjunction, the power of malevolent stars is increased, and the protections of benevolent ones are sometimes overcome. For the threatening radiation, along with the diametrical conjunction <note>An opposition, or 180-degree aspect</note>, always rages with equal power in the perpetration of evils.

# SATURN IN SQUARE WITH THE OTHER PLANETS CHAPTER X.

<margin>Saturn and the Sun</margin>
If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined to the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> by a square radiation <term>square radiation: an astrological aspect where two planets are 90 degrees apart, usually considered tense or difficult</term>, and Saturn itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Sun positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction weakens the marks of the preceding lineage. It always indicates grave illnesses from a bitter coldness of the humors <term>humors: the bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, black bile, yellow bile) believed in ancient medicine to control health and temperament</term>, and it equally cuts off and shatters the patrimony and all actions. <margin>Saturn and Venus</margin>
If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined to **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> by a square radiation, and Saturn itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Venus positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction indicates a heavy burden of beggary after the patrimony has been squandered. Nevertheless, they love their husbands with a faithful and uncorrupted affection, so that a conjugal grace associates them both in turn, but they may attempt to hide their love with a certain dissimulation.

<margin>Saturn and Mercury</margin>
If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined to **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> by a square radiation, and Saturn itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Mercury positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction decrees destruction from the first day of birth. It equally attacks all thoughts of the mind and all orders of counsel, and always pursues all actions with a cold numbness <note>original: "frigido torpore"</note>. It also makes the person always subject to the powers of others, handling secondary ministries of business in their actions, but it indicates the greatest storms of envy for them. For some, it will cause a stuttering sound of the voice from a bound tongue; it makes others deaf with dull ears. These vices also persist unless they are mitigated by **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> moving away from the bad testimony of Saturn. But if Mercury is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon Saturn positioned in the inferior place with a square radiation, nothing good indeed is decreed from this society of conjunction, but the shamelessness of the preceding misfortunes is somewhat mitigated.

<margin>Saturn and the Moon</margin>
If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined to the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> by a square radiation, and Saturn itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Moon positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction will make the body fatigued by malicious humors. It will make them separated from all actions by lazy numbnesses of the mind, and will render them such that they can never dare to perform any actions. Moreover, this conjunction always dissipates the maternal substance with miserable tearings, so that it causes sudden parricidal <note>original: "parricidalia," here meaning "clashing with a parent"</note> contests of enmity by sons against their mothers. But if the Moon is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon Saturn positioned in the inferior place with a square radiation, this conjunction prostrates the person with a miserable death. It surrounds the person with a bitter continuation of dangers from birth and indicates destruction from malignant humors. It will cause the person to be fatigued by various misfortunes of errors, and always indicates losses of marriage and honor. Unless this conjunction is supported by the protection of other stars, it exasperates bitter defenses of hatred in the heart of the wife, and makes the person destitute of all protections from friends and children.

It will cause some to be involved in military duties, others it will assign to royal houses, and it will decree for them the offices of noble and public acts. It will cause them to be elevated by these official businesses, so that they attain these affairs with the greatest increase of dignity; but they will never be able to well-preserve the resources of their father’s estate. Furthermore, this conjunction always indicates constant griefs from the misfortunes of their sons, or certainly will cause them to have children late in life. If, however, **Mars** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Jupiter** placed in a lower position with a square radiation: this conjunction sharpens every fiery impulse of the mind, and will cause one to always sin through various errors throughout life. Without cause, it forces men to endure the inconveniences of great labor, but this labor is obtained either from public or royal affairs; and more than this, it decrees with a hostile fervor the dangers of evil insinuations and bitter accusations.

<margin>The Sun</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> by a square radiation, and Jupiter itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Sun positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: by both his own and his father’s merit, this conjunction decrees marks of dignity, but it also grants increases and promotions of good and great honors. It always introduces the person with the testimony of good recommendations, so that many are subject to them by merit of their dignity. If, however, the **Sun** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Jupiter** placed in a lower position with a square radiation: this conjunction will make a man adorned with the bright splendor of nobility, but it will cause his patrimony to be registered by a wretched confiscation <note>original: "publicatione"; the public seizure or forfeiture of private property to the state</note>, and it will stir up threatening crowds of misfortunes and evil enemies.

<margin>Venus</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> by a square radiation, and Jupiter itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Venus positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction always associates the person with the friendships of many. By the protection of women, it causes both actions and profits to be conferred by the same means, and it always adorns the whole substance of life with honorable dignity; it also makes these people observe the religions of the gods with devoted veneration. If, however, **Venus** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Jupiter** placed in a lower position with a square radiation: from this conjunction, it decrees the allurements of loves, and regarding the care of the body, it always indicates ornate clothing and decrees the luxurious desires of the will. But as often as they have attained the prosperous joys of happiness, so often will the decrees of these fates be changed into the opposite, and their joy will slide down into something worse.

<margin>Mercury</margin> If **Jupiter** is joined to **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> by a square radiation, and Jupiter itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Mercury positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: from this conjunction, offices of writing or the liberal arts <term>liberal arts: the traditional curriculum of higher education, including grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy</term> are decreed. They are put in charge of accounts and calculations; their patrimony and activities are also conferred through some form of public defense. If, however, **Mercury** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Jupiter** placed in a lower position with a square radiation: this conjunction will create sufficient resources of wealth, but these people always hinder themselves in every action, avoiding all good things as if they were evil because of an unknown fear of the mind. They will be such that whatever they desire to attain even with great prayers, they would despise the whole of it—even if it fell to them by chance—with a stubborn judgment of the mind. They are people who neither desire any benefits to be conferred upon them by others, nor do they themselves try to obtain any good for themselves.

### MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### IN SQUARE ASPECT — CHAPTER XII.

<margin>Mars square the Sun.</margin>
If **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is joined to the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> by a square radiation, and Mars itself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Sun positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction omits no occurrence of misfortunes, but always opposes all opportunities for advancement and ranks of promotion with a malignant composition. If, however, the **Sun** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Mars** established in a lower place with a square radiation: a wretched end is prepared for both the father and for the person born from this conjunction. A heap of misfortunes is added, and they decree various inconveniences of calamities; for it stirs up seditions, announces battles, and excites fearsome dangers of public censure. Furthermore, it destroys the foundations of a sound mind and of wise counsel, and always imposes the wretched weight of blindness upon the eyes. These dangers are more strongly provoked in a long-lived birth chart, especially if this conjunction is joined by a threatening radiation to the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, or if Mars, positioned in the descendant or occupying the **Midheaven** <term>M C: Medium Coeli, the highest point in the sky at birth, signifying career and public life</term>, aspects the Sun, which—positioned on another angle—receives the light of the waxing Moon. For then, it scatters those prostrated by public censure with wretched mutilations; then also, with limbs torn by popular fury, the honor of a proper burial is denied, so that in life and after death, the danger of censure persevering, the outcome of the calamity is increased. Even in a nocturnal birth, these same things are carried out by a similar order of reasoning.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **Mars** is joined to **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> by a square radiation, and he himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Venus positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction decrees all manner of evils. For then it indicates quarrels and accusations and fearsome dangers; then losses strike the man because of a woman. If this conjunction occurs in **tropical signs** <term>tropical signs: the signs of the solstices and equinoxes—Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term>, then with the man's body becoming effeminate, the impurity of all unchastity grows strong. Then men will suffer the passions of feminine lusts; then, with the shipwreck of their modesty and reputation, they are polluted by the stains of shameless impurity. They will even compel their own wives to commit adultery and surrender their wives' modesty to foreign embraces with the endurance of a prostitute; they force a marriage joined under bad omens to serve foreign lusts with the wretched necessity of calamity, or with the mind of a pimp, they willingly acknowledge the hidden adultery of the wife. If these are women, they endure this necessity of a prostituted body through the husband with a constant, bitter grief of mind. If, however, **Venus** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **Mars** established in a lower place with a square radiation: she decrees these same things by a similar reasoning, but those who have Venus so placed exercise their crime secretly, so that the wicked commerce of prostituted modesty may be protected by the hidden impurities of lusts, and a bad conscience may conceal whatever was perpetrated by the vicious desires of the mind. This is especially true if **Jupiter**, either positioned with them or looking by a **trine radiation** <term>trine radiation: an auspicious aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart</term>, aspects one of them.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If **Mars** is joined to **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> by a square radiation, and he himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Mercury established in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction decrees the fearsome outcomes of all evils. It always weakens the man with a harmful continuation of troubles and always opposes all his acts with various contrariety. With malignant tumors, it will always cause these same people to be poorly introduced to their goals; it also stirs up bitter accusations...

And if perhaps anything of happiness was promised by the benign radiation of other stars, they always study to turn it away by their own wickedness, and daily they think of disturbing their spouses and almost the entire family with varied insults. If, however, this conjunction is also struck by the adverse radiation of malevolent stars, it will be shaken by a detriment that is worse in proportion to the power of those who have provoked this left-hand association of stars with a threatening ray. But if **Mars** and the **Moon** are so unhappily established, and associated in an adverse confederation in dejected places of the birth chart, and the testimony of benevolent stars is present, although their radiation will be of little use, nevertheless something of the superior evils is occasionally diminished, especially if such benevolent stars are in a good state, or rejoicing in some power of their own.

### THE SUN SQUARE WITH THE MOON ALONE — CHAPTER XIII.

<image-desc>A square woodcut decorative initial 'S' containing a dark, detailed illustration of figures in a landscape, possibly celestial or mythological in nature.</image-desc>
If the **Sun** is joined to the **Moon** by a square radiation, whether they preside cardinally <term>cardinally: placed in the most powerful houses of the chart, like the ascendant or midheaven</term> on the right or left side: if the access of prosperous happiness from the rays of other stars is added to the decrees for the men, the greatest actions, a suitable substance of life, and signs of glorious dignity are conferred from always prosperous recommendations; and frequently, with the laudable applause of good men, the business of magistracies and royal offices are granted, not without great profit. If, however, malevolent stars, without the protection of benevolent ones, contain this society of the Sun and Moon with a malignant radiation: the greatest crises of life and the inconveniences of misfortunes are decreed, which, unless someone overcomes them with the skillful prudence of the mind, occasionally lead a man to the highest calamity. But if, with the rays of malevolent stars thus joined and unhappy aspects added, the **Moon**—full of light—is carried toward **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, and **Jupiter** receives the conjunction of the waxing **Moon**: signs of nobility [are granted], yet with the greatest envy...

### VENUS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS IN SQUARE CHAPTER XIV

If **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is joined to **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> by a square radiation, whether either of them possesses the right or left square, they decree all things in equal measure; for that conjunction promises distinguished, amiable, and worthy duties in some art, or a discipline of great learning is handed down from that conjunction, so that from this duty of instruction they may follow the joy of a clear social life. However, because of these loves, the malicious talk of envious people spreads the mark of infamy.

If **Venus** is joined to the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> by a square radiation, and the **Moon**—possessing the superior part of the right square—looks upon **Venus** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, that conjunction decrees the greatest gains of wealth. But for men, it always inflicts various losses because of women, or imposes a weight of infamy. 

If, however, **Venus** is made superior and possessing the right side, looking upon the **Moon** established in the lower place with a square radiation, she increases the greatest happiness with always-prosperous growth, and decrees better things than the goods that came before. This conjunction also honors their actions, life, and social conduct, and preserves the incorrupt love of a wife; it also decrees pure and good affections of spouses, benefits full of joy, the insignia of a distinguished art, an honorable order of life, and the grace of sweet speech with the greatest happiness. Nevertheless, it indicates sexual unions with others <note>original: "alienos concubitus"</note> with impatient desire; it grants their mothers the honorable glory of chastity, but these men obtain compliant wives from the manumission <term>manumission: the legal act of freeing a slave; here implying the wives may be former slaves</term> of others.

### MERCURY WITH THE MOON IN SQUARE CHAPTER XV

<margin>I cannot know by what reasoning a square aspect of **Venus** and **Mercury** happens, for the greatest distance by which they can be separated from each other is 75 degrees, unless you wish to understand this broadly <term>broadly: "platice," an astrological term for aspects that are not mathematically exact but fall within a certain range or "orb"</term>.</margin>
If **Mercury** is joined to the **Moon** by a square radiation, and he himself, possessing the superior part of the right square, looks upon the **Moon** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, he indicates from that conjunction those who are wisely adorned and endowed with learned eloquence and honorable speech; but a crisis is frequently brought to them from popular sedition. 

If, while **Mercury** is so constituted, a malevolent star is made superior and looks upon them with a square radiation—so that it looks at the **Moon** from an opposition <note>original: "de diametro"</note> and at **Mercury** from a square—it imposes the fear of a false accusation. In that crime, it causes those detected to be either placed in custody, or thrust into prison, or to undergo chains or exile by the observation of a public sentence. 

If, however, the **Moon** is made superior and possessing the right side, looking upon **Mercury** established in the lower place with a square radiation, that conjunction will make them unstable with a levity of mind, and will shift their plans here and there with varying thought, so that their mind never uses the logic of a single counsel. 

The authority of the Fates brings forth these decrees in the births of men from the square radiation and from the square sides day by day; you must look into these diligently in every treatise, especially since this same square change of the stars causes even the decrees of the laws to be changed. But with these explained, I will specifically mention the effects of the oppositions <note>original: "diametrorum"</note> as well. Which are right squares and which are left, we have said most clearly in the book of instruction.

### THE OPPOSITION RADIATION OF ALL THE PLANETS CHAPTER XVI

Now I will explain to you the decrees of the opposition <note>original: "diametræ"</note> radiation, which association is always composed of a threatening star, and most of all destroys the condition and nature of the stars, and forces them for the most part to tend toward unhappiness. For the opposition radiation always attacks itself with contrary power and rises from a hostile kind of association; and, just like the square, it is always a threatening radiation.
