# [BOOK] SIX. 179

...found from the place of the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: 'horoscopus'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, in this way also the misery of blindness and of the loss of light is decreed.

The Sun (☉) and the Moon (☽), if they are joined in a **tropical sign** <term>Tropical sign: The signs of the solstices (Cancer and Capricorn) or equinoxes (Aries and Libra)</term> by a **conjunction** <note>original: 'synodica radiatione'</note>, and if the Moon is deprived of all the splendor of her light, and Mercury (☿) is with them, they decree the greatest wisdom, a brilliant intellect, and knowledge of many things, but accompanied by blindness of the eyes and weakness of the body.

If the Moon (☽), Saturn (♄), and Mars (♂) are positioned equally in the **equinoctial signs** <note>Aries and Libra</note>, they stain the whole body with certain marks, or disgrace it with white patches <note>likely referring to vitiligo</note>; or surely a creeping **impetigo** <term>Impetigo: a skin infection; here used generally for spreading skin diseases</term> will possess the human body, or the form of the body will be changed by small falling scales <note>psoriasis</note>, or a long-lasting **scabies** <term>Scabies: a contagious skin condition causing intense itching</term> will shake the man, or certainly **leprosy** will defile him with a shameful appearance.

If Mercury (☿), Saturn (♄), and the Sun (☉) are positioned together in the seventh house from the Ascendant—that is, in the **Setting** <term>Setting: 'occasu'; the Descendant or 7th house, representing the western horizon</term>—and the Moon (☽) is joined with Mars (♂) in an equal partnership of degrees in the sixth house from the Ascendant, they either render men lame, or weak with amputated hands, or they surely make them insane, suffering greatly from the vice of a "falling mind" <note>likely epilepsy or severe mental collapse</note>.

Now to you, **Mavortius** <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman aristocrat and consul to whom Firmicus dedicated this work</note>, our glory, I shall show a humorous decree, by the example of which you will be able to define similar **nativities** <term>Nativity: 'genitura'; a birth chart</term>. That deformed and weak Greek, whose fused bodily form **Homer** announced to us in his divine poems—whom the wise man <note>referring to Odysseus</note> chastised with a severe rebuke amidst the laughter of all—had his decree composed by this reckoning: The Ascendant was established in Aquarius (♒︎). In the **twelfth house** <note>original: 'in ♄'; the 12th house was traditionally associated with Saturn</note> from the Ascendant, the Sun (☉) and Saturn (♄) were joined with an equal power of degrees. Jupiter (♃), however, was positioned in the **Anaphora** <term>Anaphora: the 2nd house, which 'rises' after the Ascendant</term> of the Ascendant, and Mars (♂) possessed the sign of Capricorn (♑︎) in the ninth house from the Ascendant along with the Moon (☽). Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) were established in the Ascendant itself—that is, in Aquarius (♒︎). This decree of the nativity showed us **Thersites** <note>In the *Iliad*, Thersites is described as the ugliest and most insolent of the Greeks at Troy</note>; for he was powerless, weak, ridiculous, and always impatient with rambling loquacity. Thus, the birth chart prescribed for us demonstrates all these things.

# BOOK [SIX]

The Moon (☽), Saturn (♄), and Venus (♀), if they are positioned in the seventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: 'horoscopus'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>—that is, in the **Setting** <term>Setting: 'occasu'; the 7th house or Descendant, representing the western horizon</term>—will make men with the softness of an effeminate body, *cinaedi* <note>original: 'cinædos'; a Roman term for men perceived as effeminate, often used to describe those who took a passive role in same-sex relations</note>, and those who imitate the endings of ancient myths by dancing often on stage. But if Mars (♂), positioned in the **IMC** <term>IMC: 'Imum Coeli'; the 'Bottom of the Sky' or 4th house, representing the lowest point of the chart</term>, watches them with a **square aspect** <note>original: 'quadrata radiatione'; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note>, he will make them impure and prone to every vice of lustful disgrace, and those who are always joined with their own wives in shameless and impure intercourse. If, however, Jupiter (♃) from the **MC** <term>MC: 'Medium Coeli'; the 'Midheaven' or 10th house, representing the highest point of the chart</term> watches all these planets positioned in the Setting with a square aspect, he will make them, along with all those vices, lovers of boys and infamous sodomites.

If Jupiter (♃), Saturn (♄), and Venus (♀) are positioned exactly in the MC, joined to each other by an equal degree, and Mars (♂) positioned in the IMC watches all of these with an **opposition** <note>original: 'diametra radiatione'; an aspect of 180 degrees, where planets face each other from opposite sides of the zodiac</note>, they create lovers of boys, but those who restrain this vice of lust at the cost and expense of their own bodies.

If Jupiter (♃), Venus (♀), and Saturn (♄) are placed together in the seventh place from the Ascendant—that is, in the Setting—an inheritance will be granted from the death of a wife; but the men themselves will be shaken by a long continuation of illness, and the birth of children is decreed to be difficult for them.

If Venus (♀) is positioned in the MC, and the Moon (☽), Saturn (♄), and Jupiter (♃) are placed with her, they decree foreign wives, but wives who are wealthy with a great flow and abundance of riches.

If Saturn (♄) is positioned in the Ascendant, while Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) are placed in the seventh place from the Ascendant, they deny children; but if this arrangement is swapped—that is, if Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) are in the Ascendant and Saturn (♄) positioned in the Setting watches them with an opposition—they decree the same thing.

If Mars (♂) and Venus (♀) are placed together in the IMC, and Saturn (♄) possessing the degree of the MC strikes these same planets with an opposition, he decrees a woman of advanced age as a wife, but they themselves will also be joined with their wives in impure intercourse.

If Venus (♀) is placed in the MC and Saturn (♄) is joined to her in an equal degree, while the Moon (☽) is positioned in the IMC and watches them with an opposition, he decrees wives who are either sterile or certainly of advanced age, so that children are forever denied from that union.

If Venus (♀) is positioned in the fifth place from the Ascendant, and Mars (♂) is joined with her in an equal degree, he decrees either sisters or the daughters of sisters as wives.

If Saturn (♄) is positioned in the MC, and Jupiter (♃) and Mars (♂) join him in that same place, they cause every kind of sadness to be provided by wives, so that they can never feel the joy of marital grace.

If Venus (♀) is placed in her evening rising in the seventh place from the Ascendant—that is, in the Setting—and Saturn (♄) is positioned in the degree of the MC, he will make the men sluggish toward Venus <note>Meaning impotent or lacking sexual desire</note>; but he will also make the women cold toward intercourse, with their desire for Venus lulled to sleep and all the substance of their lust extinguished.

If Mars (♂) and the Moon (☽) are joined in the MC in an equal degree, and Venus (♀) and Mercury (☿) positioned likewise watch them from the IMC with an opposition, this decree in a man’s birth chart will create public **Galli** <note>original: 'gallos'; the castrated priests of the goddess Cybele</note>; but it will render the women prostitutes, destitute of any protection of honest shame.

If Saturn (♄) and Jupiter (♃) are positioned together in the IMC, or placed in the Setting (the seventh place from the Ascendant), they impose a heavy weight of sadness from the misfortunes of children. But if Mercury (☿) is found with them in those same places, and Venus (♀) placed in the same spot is joined to them in an equal degree, they will make the women sterile; and the males, destitute of manly desires, they will separate from all intercourse. If indeed they are positioned in a **tropical sign** <note>The signs of the solstices and equinoxes: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> (as we have said), they make the natural body of a woman fused with an uncorrupted opening <note>Likely referring to a physical deformity or an imperforate hymen</note>. If, however, Mars (♂) is also found with all these, he will make castrated *Galli* serving in the ceremonies of the sacred rites.

If Mars (♂) and the Moon (☽) are positioned together in the Ascendant, and with them so placed, Mercury (☿) possesses the degree of the MC, and Saturn (♄) positioned in the Setting watches them with an opposition, while Venus (♀) watches with a square aspect, they cause children established in tender age, still wailing in the laps of their nurses, to die by quite immature fates.

If Venus (♀) is positioned in the MC, and Mars (♂), Saturn (♄), and Jupiter (♃) are joined to her in an equal degree, they cause children to die before the sight of their fathers by miserable and bitter necessities of death.

If Mars (♂) is found in the IMC, and Saturn (♄) is positioned in the Setting, and Venus (♀) is positioned in the Ascendant—with Mars (♂) joined by a square and Saturn (♄) by an opposition—from this fellowship of the stars, a swift death is prepared for a beloved wife.

# [BOOK] SIX

If **Jupiter** (♃) is found in the **Setting** <term>Setting: 'occasu'; the 7th house, representing the western horizon</term>—that is, in the seventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: 'horoscopus'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>—and **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) are joined in the Ascendant by an equal degree, they will deny children. But if **Mercury** (☿) and **Jupiter** (♃) are positioned in **angles** <term>Angles: 'cardinibus'; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful points in a chart</term> and look upon each other in an **opposition** <note>original: 'diametra radiatione'; an astrological aspect of 180 degrees</note>, and **Venus** (♀) is in the Ascendant so that one is in the Setting, another in the **MC** <term>MC: 'Medium Coeli'; the Midheaven or 10th house</term>, and another is positioned in the **IMC** <term>IMC: 'Imum Coeli'; the Bottom of the Sky or 4th house</term>, they cause male children to perish by wretched and atrocious deaths. But if **Jupiter** (♃) is positioned in any angle and looks upon **Saturn** (♄) positioned in the opposite angle with an opposition, the birth of children is denied by this star.

If the **Ascendant** is positioned in **cardinal** <term>Cardinal signs: 'tropicis signis'; Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term> or **mutable signs** <note>original: 'duplicibus'; signs like Gemini or Virgo that represent transitions</note>, and in its degree **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) are joined by an equal degree, and **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon the Ascendant and them with an opposition, they make men either **epileptics** <note>original: 'epilenticos'</note> or certainly always insane with a backwards mind.

If **Venus** (♀) is positioned exactly in the Ascendant, and **Saturn** (♄) is positioned in the **IMC**, and is joined to **Venus** (♀) by a **square aspect** <note>original: 'quadrata radiatione'; a 90-degree aspect</note>, it will make men assigned to the service of temples. These men, through a hidden instinct of divinity and a changed state of mind, are possessed by the power of an ever-present religion; they predict the future to those who ask, and thus find the nourishment for their daily life from that profession.

If the **Ascendant** is positioned in **Virgo**, and in the same sign **Jupiter** (♃), **Saturn** (♄), **Mars** (♂), **Mercury** (☿), and **Venus** (♀) are all placed together, while the **Sun** (☉) is in **Pisces**—that is, in the Setting—looking upon all these we have mentioned with an opposition, and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the **succedent** <term>Succedent: 'anaphora'; the house following an angle, here the 2nd house</term> of the Ascendant in the sign of **Libra**, but the **Moon** (☽) is [also] placed in **Aquarius** <note>The Latin text here contains a contradiction or scribal error, placing the Moon in two different signs (Libra and Aquarius) simultaneously</note>, and all are positioned in their own **bounds** <term>Bounds: 'finibus'; specific segments of a sign ruled by a particular planet</term>, the decree of a most powerful emperor is shown by this birth chart.

If **Jupiter** (♃) is positioned in the Ascendant, and the **Moon** (☽) is either moving toward the **Sun** (☉) or flowing away from it, they decree a humble life, heavy defects of health, bitter crises of danger, and the onset of wretched calamity from that fellowship of conjunction. But if the **Sun** (☉) is found in the Setting, and the **Moon** (☽) flows away from it, they accomplish these same things in a similar way.

If the **Sun** (☉) is positioned in **Aries** or **Capricorn**, and the **Ascendant** is joined with it in an equal degree, while **Mars** (♂), **Saturn** (♄), and **Jupiter** (♃), positioned in favorable places of the birth chart, look upon each other with a **trine aspect** <note>original: 'trigonica radiatione'; a 120-degree aspect, usually considered beneficial</note>, they will make tyrants: cruel, terrible, and effective men who always go about with cruel ferocity in the slaughter of men and the punishment of the wretched.

If the **Moon** (☽) is found in the Ascendant, and either **Saturn** (♄) or **Jupiter** (♃) positioned in the Setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—looks upon it with an opposition, the conscience of the one who has them thus will be polluted and thoroughly contaminated by a hidden homicide.

If the **Sun** (☉), **Mars** (♂), and **Mercury** (☿) are joined in an equal degree in the Setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in a cardinal sign, this fellowship of stars creates a murderer and a thief, always drenched in human blood and armed with every kind of cruelty. If indeed **Saturn** (♄) is found with them, he shows us the doom of death; for such a man, caught in these crimes, is cruelly raised on a cross, nailed to the gallows by the severe sentence of a judge.

If **Jupiter** (♃) is found in those degrees in which **Andromeda** <note>The constellation of Andromeda</note> is positioned, and **Saturn** (♄) receives the conjunction of the approaching **Moon** (☽), the greatest disadvantages of unhappiness are decreed from that conjunction. But if **Mars** (♂) looks upon the **Moon** (☽) positioned as we said with an opposition, he causes men caught in wicked thoughts to be raised on a cross.

If **Venus** (♀) is positioned in **Taurus**, and **Mars** (♂) holds those degrees in which the **Pleiades** <note>A prominent star cluster in Taurus</note> are placed, and the **Moon** (☽) is full of light, and **Jupiter** (♃) and **Mars** (♂) are either joined with her by an equal degree or, having become superior from a square side, look upon her with a threatening aspect, the one who has them thus will perish captured by bandits, struck by the point of a threatening sword. If, however, **Venus** (♀) is found in **Taurus** with the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the **MC** full of light and is struck by a square aspect, it will accomplish this same thing we said in a similar way. But if the **Ascendant** is found in **Sagittarius**, and **Mars** (♂) is positioned in **Leo** and looks upon the Ascendant from the **IMC** with a threatening aspect, he will cause death by the sword. But if the **Ascendant** is found in **Scorpio**, and in **Sagittarius**—that is, in the **IMC**—he looks upon the Ascendant from a square with a threatening aspect, even so, he will cause death by being struck with a sword. However, it should be known that if the **Ascendant** is placed in **Aries** or in **Scorpio**, and **Mars** (♂) is found in the Setting or in the **MC**, with even a slight testimony of benevolent planets, he decrees nothing evil—especially if it is a nocturnal birth chart—for **Mars** (♂) always protects his own house and never destroys it when positioned in the Setting.

->[BOOK] SIX<-

If the **Ascendant** <note>original: 'ℋ' used here as an abbreviation for Horoscopus</note> or the **South Node** (☋) <note>original: 'Cauda Draconis'; the descending node of the Moon, often considered a point of depletion or misfortune</note> is positioned in the Ascendant, and the **houses of Saturn** <term>houses of Saturn: Capricorn and Aquarius</term> are located in the **Setting** <term>Setting: 'occasu'; the 7th house, representing the western horizon and the end of life</term>, and **Saturn** (♄) himself is placed in the **Midheaven** <term>Midheaven: 'M C' or 'Medium Coeli'; the 10th house, representing one's public life and peak of fate</term>, it will cause men to die of **dropsy** <term>dropsy: 'hydropicos'; a condition of swelling caused by excess fluid, often associated with Saturn in ancient medicine</term>. But if these signs we mentioned hold the Ascendant and the **South Node** (☋) is positioned in the Midheaven, it will cause men to die by poison. If, however, with those signs rising, **Jupiter** (♃) is found in the Midheaven, a sudden death is decreed amidst cups and tables, and among the joyful noise of banquet-guests, arising from **indigestion** <note>original: 'cruditate'; literally 'raw humors' or undigested food</note> or excessive drink. But if, with those same signs rising, **Mars** (♂) and the **Sun** (☉) are positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** <term>Lower Midheaven: 'I M C' or 'Imum Coeli'; the 4th house, representing the roots, the home, and the hidden end of things</term>, they are either killed by the sword or consumed by the heat of fire. If, however, **Venus** (♀) is found in these rising signs and the **Moon** (☽) is in the Midheaven, it will cause men to die shaken by **sacred diseases** <term>sacred diseases: 'sacris aegritudinibus'; a historical term for epilepsy, thought to be an affliction from the gods</term>.

If **Venus** (♀) is found in **Cancer** (♋) or **Pisces** (♓) in the Lower Midheaven, she will cause one to fulfill the duty of a wretched life, either oppressed by faulty humors or submerged in rushing waves.

If **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) are placed together in the **eighth house** from the Ascendant <note>The 8th house is the house of death and "other people's money"</note>, they will produce wicked thieves who desire the property of others with a depraved greed of mind; those who, possessed by an immoderate madness of mind and the vice of avarice, always pursue the estates of others with unjust desires.

If the **Sun** (☉) is found in the Ascendant and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the Setting, and **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂) are either with the Sun or placed equally with the Moon, and one of the malevolent stars is positioned with either the Sun or the Moon, and another malevolent star holds one of the following **angles** <term>angles: 'cardines'; the four pivotal points of the chart (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses)</term>, the one who has such a conjunction of stars will be **exposed** <note>original: 'exponetur'; referring to the ancient practice of child abandonment/exposure</note>.

If **Mars** (♂) is positioned in the Ascendant and **Mercury** (☿) is placed in the Midheaven and joined by a **square aspect** <term>square aspect: 'quadrata radiatione'; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually indicating tension or conflict</term>, it will produce public and malicious accusers. But if **Mercury** (☿) is found in the Setting and **Mars** (♂) is placed in the Lower Midheaven, and Mercury looks upon him with a square aspect, it will produce bandits, specifically those who are frequently bloodied by human gore.

If the **Ascendant** <note>ℋ: Horoscopus</note> is found, and **Saturn** (♄) is placed in any **post-ascension** of an angle <term>post-ascension: 'anaphora'; the house immediately following an angle, such as the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th house</term>, and the **Moon** (☽) and **Jupiter** (♃) are positioned in a **debilitated place** <note>original: 'deiecto loco'; a house that does not "see" the Ascendant, like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note> by their exact degree, those who are born live only as long as the Moon can quickly complete its course past Jupiter. But if the Moon is joined to **Jupiter** (♃) by a faithful aspect, they live as long as it takes Jupiter to pass the first angle he encounters. However, if the rays of the Moon are unstable, they live for as many days (as we said before) as the Moon is found with Jupiter. But if (as we said) **Mars** (♂) or **Saturn** (♄) is positioned, and with **Jupiter** (♃) placed in a debilitated place, the **Moon** (☽) is found in a primary angle—that is, in the Ascendant—they will, because of **Mars** (♂), produce **short-lived infants** <term>short-lived: 'oligochronios'; a Greek term for those who die in infancy</term> with a bad turning-point of death. If, however, **Saturn** (♄) is found in the Midheaven and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the Lower Midheaven, joined to Saturn by an **opposition** <note>original: 'diametra radiatione'; an aspect of 180 degrees</note>, and **Mars** (♂)—either positioned in the Setting or the Midheaven—looks upon the Moon with a threatening aspect while possessing the same degrees as the Moon, he immediately **bursts the narrowness of the womb** <note>original: 'uteri-angustias rūpit'; implies a fatal or violent birth</note> and delivers the occurring offspring to death. But if the **Sun** (☉) is found in the Ascendant and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the Setting, joined to the Sun by an opposition, and **Mars** (♂) or **Saturn** (♄) is positioned with one of them—that is, with either the Sun or the Moon—or if while one is with them, the other holds any other angle, the one who is born will be **exposed**.

If the **Sun** (☉) is found in the **seventh house** from the Ascendant, and **Saturn** (♄) is placed in the **twelfth** from the Ascendant, looking at the Sun with an opposition, and the **Moon** (☽) and **Mars** (♂) are also in the twelfth house joined with Saturn in an equal fellowship of degrees, and they themselves are opposed to the Sun by a diameter, they will produce **weaklings** and **paralytics** <note>original: 'parilyticos'</note>, whose entire body, with the structure of their sinews loosened, is disgraced by broken and dissipated strength.

If **Saturn** (♄), **Mars** (♂), and the **Moon** (☽) are positioned together, joined in an equal fellowship of degrees in the **twelfth house** from the Ascendant, and **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon them with a **trine aspect** <term>trine aspect: 'trigonica radiatione'; a harmonious 120-degree aspect</term>, or is positioned in the Setting or the **third house** from the Ascendant, and the **Sun** (☉) holds the Ascendant by degree, this **birth chart** <term>birth chart: 'genitura'</term> demonstrates a cruel tyrant to us.

If **Mercury** (☿), **Venus** (♀), **Saturn** (♄), and **Mars** (♂) are arranged in an equal aspect in the **eleventh house** from the Ascendant, they produce a luxurious man who, with lavish expenses, is entangled in lustful desires.

If **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) are placed together in the **fifth house** from the Ascendant, and **Saturn** (♄) being in a superior position looks upon them with a square aspect, or is positioned with them joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, he will produce **counterfeiters**, or those who imitate public money with the deceptive arts of the foundry. But if, with these planets so positioned, the **Moon** (☽) gives some consent in the following years, he will produce murderous bandits. But if **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) hold the fifth house from the Ascendant, and the **Moon** (☽) is diminished by **Saturn** (♄), or certainly by the **South Node** (☋) or a full **Mars** (♂)...

->[BOOK] SIX<-

...if [the Moon] strikes [the Sun] with an **opposite ray** <term>opposite ray: 'diametra radiatione'; an astrological aspect of 180 degrees, usually considered very difficult</term>, for the crime of forgery, they decree a public death, so that those fallen into this vice are punished by the severe sentence of a judge. But if the **Sun** (☉) is positioned in the **Ascendant** <note>original: 'horosc.'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, and **Mercury** (☿) is placed with him, and **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂) are positioned in the **Setting** <note>original: 'occasu'; the 7th house or western horizon</note> and look upon the **Sun** (☉) with an opposite ray, they will cause those caught in the crime of forgery to be **crucified** <note>original: 'in crucem tolli'; literally 'to be raised onto a cross'</note>; nor can the good testimony of **Jupiter** (♃) mitigate this danger, but with his healing protection ignored, the threatening rays of the malevolent stars decree a public and violent death in every way.

If **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂) are positioned in the **Ascendant** at the same degree, and the **Sun** (☉) and **Mercury** (☿) are placed together in the **Setting** and look upon them with an opposite ray, from this partnership of radiation, either a foot or a hand is amputated. But later, when they have been worn down by this mutilation of the body, they also encounter a miserable and fatal death.

If in the same sign of the **Ascendant**, the **Lot** <note>original: 'pars'; refers to a calculated mathematical point in the chart, often called a 'Part' or 'Lot'</note> is found exactly between **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂), it shows the mournful fall of a dismal misfortune; for the birth being blocked within the mother's womb, the mangled creature <note>original: 'laniatum pecus'; a harsh term here used for the fetus</note> is torn apart by miserable lacerations, so that with the parts of the womb being dismembered, all the limbs are brought forth by the help of a **cruel skill** <note>original: 'crudelis artificii'; likely referring to a physician performing an embryotomy to save the mother</note>.

If the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in a **double sign** <term>double sign: 'duplici signo'; also called bicorporeal signs, such as Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</term> and holds the degree of the **Midheaven** (MC), and **Saturn** (♄) is in the **Setting** and in the **Lower Midheaven** <note>original: 'IMC'; the 4th house or bottom of the sky</note>, it will make people **epileptics** <term>epileptics: 'caducos'; literally 'the falling ones'</term>. But if the **Moon** is in conjunction with the **Sun**, and **Mars** (♂) is positioned equally with her, and all of them hold the degree of the **Midheaven**, and **Mars** (♂) is rising in the morning, and **Saturn** (♄) is positioned either with them or in the **Setting**, it will produce epileptics by a similar reasoning, who, changed by an insane madness of the mind, lose the right order of life. If, however, with **Mars** (♂), the **Moon** (☽), and the **Sun** (☉) positioned as we said, **Saturn** (♄) is found in the **Midheaven** and looks upon them positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** with an opposite ray, a miserable death will overtake those oppressed by a vice of the mind and thrown headlong from heights. But generally, if **Mars** (♂) and **Saturn** (♄) are positioned together in **double signs** and are found together in the **Setting**, they decree these same things by a similar reasoning as was said above.

If the **Ascendant** is found with the **Sun** (☉) in **Gemini** (♊), and in the **Midheaven** (that is, in **Pisces** ♓) the **Moon** (☽) is placed, and in the **Lower Midheaven** (that is, in **Virgo** ♍) **Mars** (♂) is positioned—occupying the western angles—so that being placed in **double signs** they possess all the angles of the birth chart, they will also produce epileptics from this partnership, raging with a heavy disease.

If **Jupiter** (♃) is positioned in a **double sign** and holds the **Midheaven** angle, and **Saturn** (♄) placed in the **Lower Midheaven** looks upon him with an opposite ray, and **Jupiter** (♃) is joined to **Saturn** (♄) in a bond of partnership, they seek an inheritance by the title of **adoption** from strangers, so that they become the sons by law of those to whom nature had denied their own children.

If **Mars** (♂), **Saturn** (♄), and **Venus** (♀) are joined in the **Midheaven** in an equal partnership of degrees, and **Mercury** (☿) approaches them as a fourth witness, it will make **prostitutes** <note>original: 'meretrices'</note> who, through the loss of their traded modesty and for the sake of a prostituted body, seek a miserable profit every single day. If, however, this should be the birth chart of a male, he will be entangled in the womanly vices of lust by the heat of an effeminate madness.

If the **Sun** (☉) and **Mars** (♂) are found together in the **Ascendant**, and **Saturn** (♄) positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** looks upon them with a **square ray** <term>square ray: 'quadrata radiatione'; an aspect of 90 degrees, considered a source of tension and conflict</term>, and the **Moon** (☽) is placed in the **Midheaven** looking upon **Saturn** (♄) by the opposite and the **Sun** (☉) and **Mars** (♂) by the square, it always stirs up the **parricidal hatred** of parents toward children and a deadly slaughter.

If **Jupiter** (♃) is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and **Jupiter** <note>This repetition of Jupiter is likely a scribal error for another planet, possibly Mercury or the Moon</note> is placed in the sixth house from the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** (☽) with **Mercury** (☿) and **Venus** (♀) possesses the degree of the **Midheaven** in an equal partnership of conjunction, that union decrees the insignia of **distinguished nobility**.

If the **Ascendant** is found in **Aries** (♈), and **Mars** (♂), **Saturn** (♄), and **Venus** (♀) are there together, and the **Sun** (☉) is also in the same sign, it decrees a slave or an old woman as a wife, or certainly one who is humble and destitute of all protection of dignity. But if **Mercury** (☿) approaches these so positioned, he brings public prostitutes to the marriage of the bridal bed. If, with all these positioned as we said, the **Moon** (☽) is found in the **Midheaven**, they compel those possessed by an incestuous heat of madness and a wicked greed of the mind to come to the beds of their own daughters.

If **Mars** (♂) and the **Sun** (☉) are positioned in a **tropical sign** <term>tropical sign: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs marking the turning points of the seasons</term> and are found in the **Setting**, and **Mercury** (☿) joins them as a third in the same place, it will make a **bandit** <note>original: 'latronem'</note>, but one who, practicing banditry in foreign places, is stained with human blood; yet he, being discovered in the same crime, is punished by a severe sentence.

**Mercury** (☿), the **Moon** (☽), and **Venus** (♀), if they are positioned together in the **eleventh place from the Ascendant** <note>The 11th House, traditionally called the 'Good Spirit,' associated with friends and gains</note>, and if it is the feminine sign of **Cancer** (♋︎), and **Mars** (♂) looks upon them with a **trine aspect** <term>trine aspect: 'trigonica radiatione'; a harmonious planetary relationship of 120 degrees</term>, they create musicians who strike lyres made either of glass <note>original: 'harenarios'; literally 'sandy,' possibly referring to glass or a specific material used in instrument making</note> or bronze with a sweet melody.

**Mercury** (☿), **Mars** (♂), **Venus** (♀), and the **Moon** (☽), if they are positioned together in the **Ascendant** or in the **Midheaven** <note>original: 'M C'; the 10th House, representing career and public standing</note>, will produce dancers and pantomimes adorned with the grace of beauty. But if **Jupiter** (♃), being so positioned, looks upon them with a favorable aspect, he grants these very people glory from the judgment of the public, especially if **Saturn** (♄) provides a good testimony to them in this position.

The **Moon** (☽) in **conjunction** <term>conjunction: 'synodica'; when two celestial bodies appear in the same degree of the zodiac</term> with the **Sun** (☉), if found in the eleventh place from the Ascendant, and **Jupiter** (♃) is positioned together with them, but **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂) look upon them with different aspects—such that one is in a **square** <term>square: 'quadrato'; a difficult 90-degree aspect</term> and the other in **opposition** <term>opposition: 'diametro'; a 180-degree aspect</term>—and one of them is positioned in an **equinoctial sign** <note>Aries or Libra</note>, they decree **elephantiasis** <note>A term used in antiquity for severe skin diseases or leprosy</note> and a long, chronic sickness lasting until the final day of life.

If **Saturn** (♄) or the **Moon** (☽) is positioned lowly in a part of **Aquarius** (♒︎), or **Mars** (♂) is there, and **Saturn** (♄) looks upon this same part from an **opposition**, it will make children who are separated from their parents.

If the **Moon** (☽) is found in the **Pleiades** <note>A star cluster in the shoulder of Taurus</note> of **Taurus** (♉︎), or in the **Nebula** <note>The Praesepe or 'Beehive' cluster</note> of **Cancer** (♋︎), or in the **Mane** of **Leo** (♌︎), or in the **Forehead** of **Scorpio** (♏︎), or from the eighth to the tenth degree in **Sagittarius** (♐︎), or in the **Spines** of **Capricorn** (♑︎), or in the **Cord** <note>The band connecting the two fish</note> of **Pisces** (♓︎), or in the **Head** of **Aries** (♈︎), and if she is **waning in light** <note>original: 'minuta luminibus'; referring to the Moon losing brightness as it approaches the Sun</note>—that is, with all the splendor of her light spent—and either **Saturn** (♄) or **Mars** (♂) looks upon her with any aspect, she will create blind people. If, however, in these signs and in the places we have mentioned, she holds one of the **angles** <term>angles: 'cardinem'; the four most powerful points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> of the birth chart, then with the entire substance of the eyes destroyed, the miserable disaster of blindness is brought about. But if the **Moon** (☽) is full of light and still increasing in splendor, she will not make them blind, but she always inflicts either impaired vision, or ill health, or a scar or mark upon the face, so as to disfigure the face despite a generally honorable appearance.

If **Jupiter** (♃), **Saturn** (♄), and **Mars** (♂) are found exactly by degree in the **Midheaven**, and in the third place from the Ascendant **Mercury** (☿) and **Venus** (♀) are joined in an equal partnership of degrees, while **Saturn** (♄) holds the eighth place from the Ascendant, and the **Sun** (☉) is in **Gemini** (Ⅱ), and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned either in her own **house** <note>Cancer</note> or in her **exaltation** <note>Taurus</note>, this decree will produce a hero, a brave man, and a killer, who with a victorious right hand creates heaps of enemies in extraordinary slaughter.

If the **Ascendant** is found in **Taurus** (♉︎), a tropical sign <note>Taurus is usually a fixed sign; the author may be following a specific tradition or referring to its position relative to the seasons</note>, and the **Moon** (☽) is positioned in the twelfth place from the Ascendant, while **Jupiter** (♃) and **Venus** (♀) are joined in an equal partnership of degrees and incline toward the **Ascendant** or the **Midheaven**, and **Mercury** (☿) and **Venus** (♀) possess the **Midheaven** by equal degrees, this birth chart demonstrates the soul of a malicious prostitute. She invites many to her bed because of her beauty, but she will be led through foreign lands and will be entangled in frequent legal cases and great accusations. Public custody will also take her, and she will endure frequent disturbances and injuries. She will also miscarry twin sons; but for the sake of profit and lust, she will even barter her shame to two brothers, and will invite both father and son to her bed; for she will do all these things with an immoderate heat of lust and an unbridled greed for money. But when she enters the time of middle age, she will then return to her **homeland**, and she will take a foreign youth, poor and unworthy, as a companion for her marriage bed; and having been joined to a vehicle of manumission <note>original: 'vehiculo manumissionis'; likely a metaphor for a low-status marriage or a formal release from her previous life</note>, she will arrive at the final day of her life in miserable necessity.

### GENERAL RULES FOR EVERY BIRTH (THE EPHODOS). CHAPTER XXXII.

Having explained all these things which the mixture of planetary temperaments reveals, and having arranged them by diligent reasoning, I shall hasten, **Mavortius** <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman aristocrat to whom this work is dedicated</note>, our glory, to the end of this book. But there is still that which is required for the full substance of this work, and I will now show it to you through a most true exposition. For we cannot otherwise come to the secrets of the **astrological art** <note>original: 'matheseos'; the study of the stars</note> which the seventh book will contain, nor to the **barbaric sphere** <note>The 'Sphaera Barbarica' refers to non-Greek, often Egyptian or Babylonian, star lore discussed in Book VIII</note> which the body of the eighth book shows you, unless all things that pertain to the foundations of the entire science have first been collected by diligent tradition. We shall show, therefore, what you should seek in which place, and to what extent. For the square place from the Ascendant <note>The 4th House</note> does not show parents or the life of parents alone, nor does the seventh show only the spouse, nor the fifth only children, nor the eleventh only friends, nor the sixth only illnesses. Therefore, because we have promised that we would say everything, receive the reasoning full of truth and faith, so that you may be able to collect all these things by diligent consideration; lest, being occupied with vague definitions <note>original: 'platicis'; refers to 'platick' or wide/non-exact astrological aspects</note>, you lose the integrity of the truth, but rather find it most certainly.

<meta>This page transitions from the general planetary mixtures of the previous book into Book VI, specifically focusing on the "Lot of the Father"—a mathematical point in the birth chart used to determine the father’s status, character, and lifespan. ->### BOOK SIX ###<-

<margin>If **Saturn** (♄) is under the rays of the **Sun** (☉) <note>meaning the planet is so close to the Sun it is hidden by its light</note>, take 1 degree from the Sun to Saturn; in a night birth, do the reverse. Hali, part 4, chapter 16.</margin>
Therefore, if you wish to calculate the place of the father by the method of degrees, and it is a daytime birth, count the number of all degrees from the degree of the **Sun** (☉) to the degree of **Saturn** (♄)—that is, all the signs from the Sun to Saturn. When you have the total sum, begin counting from the degree of the **Ascendant** <note>original: 'horosc.'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> and distribute this number across all the signs, giving thirty degrees to each sign. The sign in which the last degree falls will show you the place of the father. However, in a nighttime birth, count from the degree of **Saturn** (♄) to the **Sun** (☉) and do the same. When you have found the sign of the father through careful calculation, you shall describe the father's substance <note>his social and financial standing</note> based on the nature of that sign. Observe also how this same sign is honored by the rays of the **benefic stars** <note>the helpful planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>. For if either benefic stars are in the sign of the father, or if they look upon it with a favorable aspect, the father's happiness is confirmed. But if **malefic stars** <note>the challenging planets, Saturn and Mars</note> do this, we are told that everything regarding the father will be the opposite. Look also into this sign to see whether benefic or malefic stars are present, and how the ruler of that sign is positioned in the birth chart—in what sign, in what **bounds** <term>bounds: 'finibus'; specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term>, and whether it stands in the primary or secondary **angles** <term>angles: 'cardinibus'; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</term>, or in places where it rejoices, or in sluggish and cast-down places. From all these things, you will find what kind of father the person had, all of which I shall explain in detail.

<margin>The father's place in **Saturn** (♄).</margin>
If the father's place is found in a sign of **Saturn** (♄) <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, seek where Saturn himself is positioned in the birth chart. For if it is a daytime birth and Saturn is found in that same place, or in its own degrees, or in signs where he is **exalted** <note>referring to Libra, where Saturn’s influence is strongest</note>, or in places where he rejoices, and if he is in his **morning rising** <note>appearing in the sky before the Sun</note>, increasing in number, and if he looks upon the place of the father with a favorable aspect, he will make the father grave, modest, mature, and respected for his calm severity. He will be a cultivator of fields, one whose greatest ancestral protection comes from the fruits of the earth, and who is raised up by great promotions. But if it is a nighttime birth, and Saturn is in cast-down places, or in weakened angles, or in his **debility** <note>places where the planet's power is diminished</note>, or if he is **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward</note> or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** (☉), he makes the father hardworking, lowly, dread-inducing, gloomy, always hesitating with sluggish efforts; he may even be a slave, of slave-like character, or stained by the filth of the most shameful servitude.

<margin>**Jupiter** (♃)</margin>
If the father's place is found in a sign of **Jupiter** (♃) <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, and Jupiter is positioned in that place, or in signs where he is exalted, or in the primary angles, or in the fifth or eleventh house, and is increasing in number and in his morning rising, and looks upon the place from a **trine or sextile aspect** <note>original: 'trigono uel hexagono'; harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, it shows a father adorned with the fortunate insignia of high office. But if Jupiter is in secondary angles, or in cast-down and sluggish places, or retrograde, or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** (☉), it will demonstrate that the father was entirely mediocre.

<margin>**Mars** (♂)</margin>
If the father's place is found in a sign of **Mars** (♂) <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, and it is a daytime birth, and Mars is in that place, or in the angles, or in the fifth or eleventh house from the Ascendant, or in the eighth or third, and is in his morning rising and proceeding in direct motion, he will make the father austere and reckless, entangled in various labors and dangers, short-lived, and always caught up in backwards desires. If Mars, so positioned, sees the father's place from a **square or opposition** <note>original: 'quadrato uel diametro'; challenging aspects of 90 or 180 degrees</note>, he will cause the father to suffer a **violent death** <term>violent death: 'biothanatum'; an unnatural or sudden end</term>. However, if it is a nighttime birth, and **Saturn** (♄) or **Venus** (♀) looks upon the place of the father or mother with a favorable aspect, these things we have mentioned are mitigated in some part; he then makes the father upright, military, and severe, one who is always delighted by arms and iron, and according to the status of the birth, makes him either a prince or a leader.

<margin>**Sun** (☉)</margin>
If the father's place is found in the sign of the **Sun** (☉) <note>Leo</note>, and it is a daytime birth, seek in which sign or house of the birth chart the Sun is placed. For if the Sun is in that sign itself, or in his **height** <note>exaltation, which for the Sun is Aries</note>, or in the primary angles, or in the fifth or eleventh house from the Ascendant, it shows a father wealthy with flowing riches, adorned with the greatest marks of dignity, and bringing home the glory of great happiness. But if he is in cast-down places, or in secondary angles, or in his debility, and is deprived of help from benefic stars while being attacked by the rays of malefic stars, all these things we have said are greatly diminished—especially in a daytime birth, for then he strikes down the father with a swift death among other misfortunes.

<margin>**Venus** (♀)</margin>
If the father's place is found in a sign of **Venus** (♀) <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, one must seek where the star of Venus is located; for if she is in that place, or in the primary angles, or in signs in which she rejoices, or in which...

-># BOOK VI #<-

->### CHAPTER [CONTINUED] ###<-

in which <note>referring to Jupiter, implied from the previous page's context</note> it is exalted, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **Ascendant** <note>original: 'horosc.'; the first house of the birth chart</note>, and if it is rising in the morning and increasing in its number <note>referring to the planet's speed or numerical degree progression</note>, and positioned in these places or signs, and if it regards the place of the father with a prosperous **aspect** <note>original: 'radiatione'; the way planets "look at" or influence each other across the zodiac</note>, it decrees for the father the greatest marks of honor and the most excellent charm of grace. If, however, it is in weakened places, or in those signs in which it is debased, or is **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** (☉), it will show us a mediocre father.

☿ If the place of the father is found in a sign of **Mercury** (☿), seek in what place **Mercury** (☿) is located. For if it is in that very place, or in its **exaltation** <note>original: 'altitudine'; the sign where a planet's power is heightened</note>, or in its own house, or in its own terms, or in those **angles** <note>original: 'cardinibus'; the four most powerful points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> and places in which it rejoices, and if it is rising in the morning and increasing in number, it will make the father dedicated to all the duties of business, and one to whom the greatest profits are frequently granted, and who always loves his children with tender affection. If, however, a prosperous aspect from the **benefic stars** <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> assists **Mercury** (☿)—that is, the lord of the paternal place—greater increases than those we have mentioned will follow. But if **Mercury** (☿) is in weakened places, or in those angles where it does not rejoice, or in its own debasement, and is retrograde, or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** (☉), the decrees of the preceding happiness are changed, and all that we have said will apply to the father only slightly and mediocrely.

☽ If the place of the father is found in a sign of the **Moon** (☽), seek in what place of the **nativity** <note>original: 'geniturae'; the birth chart</note> the **Moon** (☽) is positioned. For if it is in that very place, or in those signs in which it is exalted, or in the principal angles, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **Ascendant**, and it is full of light, and it is a nighttime birth, and the benefic stars regard it with a prosperous aspect, and it is separated from all associations with **malefic stars** <note>Mars and Saturn</note>, it will make the father famous, clear-headed, and wealthy, and one to whom inheritance and dignity are always granted. But if the **Moon** (☽) is in weakened places, or in the secondary angles, or in its own debasement, and is destitute of the protection of benefic stars, and the aspect of malefic stars attacks it, and it is a daytime birth, or the Moon itself is diminished in light, and **Saturn** (♄) regards it, or **Mars** (♂) when it is full, all the things we said before are for the greatest part diminished; and the father becomes either an exile or a <term>biothanatus</term> <note>original: 'biothanatus'; one who dies a violent or unnatural death</note>, with straying character, not knowing the right path of life. But in this matter, as we said before, you ought to always inspect the mixtures, grants, and aspects of all the stars with diligent reason, so that when all have been mixed and composed with a wise joining of temperament, you may be able to explain the place of the father with true judgments. Seek out that **Lot** <note>original: 'Partem'; a mathematical point in the chart</note> itself also diligently, and see who is the lord of the Lot and where he is positioned, for he himself by his own nature colors the place. Moreover, you must observe this method of <term>predictions</term> <note>original: 'apotelesmatum'; the outcomes or judgments of astrology</note> in the following places as well; for in the place of the mother, and of brothers, and of the wife, and of children, and of health and vices, you must temper all things with very frequent observations of the aspects, so that once the radiation of all stars has been perceived, and the power of the places and signs collected, as well as the Lots and their **bounds** <note>original: 'finium'; subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note>, you may be able to explain everything with true judgments. But although we may gather the locations in others according to these same predictions, generally in nativities, the **Sun** (☉) is placed in the position of the father, though we find it better by this specific calculation.

<margin>The place of the Mother.</margin>
If you wish to calculate the place of the mother by a specific method, and it is a daytime birth, beginning from the degree of **Venus** (♀) and proceeding through the following signs, count all the degrees up to the place of the **Moon** (☽); and when the sum of all degrees is collected, beginning from the **Ascendant**, you will distribute them all across the following signs. In whatever sign the final degree falls, this sign will show you the place of the mother in a daytime birth. But if it is a nighttime birth, beginning from the degree of the **Moon** (☽), collect the degrees up to **Venus** (♀), and you will perform the rest by a similar method. When you have thus collected this place by specific calculation, you will investigate everything just as we said you should do for the place of the father—namely, the aspects of the benefic and malefic stars, the powers of the places and signs, and the mixtures and temperaments of the degrees. When you have compared all these with a balanced evaluation, you will be able to explain the place of the mother with true judgments.

<margin>Hali <note>Haly Abenragel, 11th-century astrologer</note> has it: by day and night from **Saturn** (♄) to **Jupiter** (♃).</margin>
If you wish to find the place of brothers by a specific method, and it is a daytime birth, beginning from the degree of **Saturn** (♄), count up to the degrees of **Jupiter** (♃). Whatever the count may be, beginning this same sum from the degree of the **Ascendant**, distribute it through the following signs. In whatever sign the final degree of the whole number falls, this sign will show you the place of the brothers. But if it is a nighttime birth, you will count the number of all degrees from **Jupiter** (♃) to **Saturn** (♄) in a similar manner, and thus beginning from the **Ascendant**, you will perform this same task by similar reasoning. When therefore you have collected the place of the brothers by this specific calculation, look here...

[...Observe] this same place <note>referring to the 'Place of Brothers' discussed at the end of the previous page</note> to see how much the **malefic** <note>original: 'maleuolæ'; planets considered traditionally difficult, like Saturn and Mars</note> and **benefic** stars <note>original: 'beneuolæ'; planets considered traditionally helpful, like Jupiter and Venus</note> regard it; see also the power of the sign, and in what place of the **nativity** <note>original: 'genituræ'; the birth chart</note> this sign is seen to be positioned. For if benefic stars are found either in that sign itself, or are established in favorable places of the nativity—and are located in those signs in which they **rejoice** <note>a specific state where a planet's influence is strengthened by its zodiacal position</note>, or in which they are **exalted**, or in their own houses—they decree a share of many and good brothers. 

But if malefic stars do the same, and are destitute of the testimony of benefic stars, they do the opposite. If, however, both benefic and malefic stars regard this same place with an equal power of association, they both give brothers and take them away. But you shall handle all things according to the kinds of stars: for masculine benefic stars will give males, while feminine benefics give females; the malefic stars also perform the same, and thus all things are fulfilled according to the power of the individual stars.

<margin>Hermes, according to Alcabitius <note>Alcabitius was a 10th-century astrologer; this marginal note likely comes from a later scholar referencing medieval Arabic astrology</note>, took 2 to **Saturn** (♄); by day and night the Lot of Marriage in a woman’s nativity is seen to be taken from the **Sun** (☉) to **Venus** (♀) according to the saying of Hermes, which **Hali** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> also proves in Book 5, Chapter 6. Otherwise, the Lot of Marriage and the Lot of Fortune would be the same. This can also be seen in Alcabitius, in the fifth difference concerning the Lots.</margin>
But generally, as we said in the book of instruction, the third place from the **Ascendant** <note>original: 'horosc.'; the first house of the chart</note> shows brothers, but let us seek it specifically by degree.

If you wish to find the place of the spouse specifically by degree, calculate from the degree of **Saturn** (♄) to the degree of **Venus** (♀), and whatever sum the calculation makes, divide that same amount starting from the **Ascendant** through the following signs; and in whatever sign you find the final degree, this will show you the place of the spouse in a daytime nativity. In a nighttime nativity, however, you shall calculate starting from **Venus** (♀) to **Saturn** (♄), and similarly divide the collected number of degrees starting from the **Ascendant**; and in whatever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the place of the spouse in a nighttime nativity. 

Others calculate from the **Sun** (☉) to **Venus** (♀) in both daytime and nighttime nativities, and count the same amount from the **Ascendant**, calculating similarly in both male and female nativities; and we ourselves have also proved this in many nativities. Therefore, when you have collected the place of the spouse by this method which we have described, first look into the power of the sign: whether it is **fixed** <note>original: 'solidum'; signs like Leo or Taurus that represent stability</note>, **double-bodied** <note>original: 'duplex'; mutable signs like Gemini or Pisces representing change</note>, or **tropical** <note>original: 'tropicum'; cardinal signs like Aries or Cancer representing new beginnings</note>. In the second order, you shall seek in what place of the nativity the **lord** <note>the planet that rules that specific zodiac sign</note> of the sign is located. Thirdly, seek this second place in which the **lord of the terms** <note>original: 'finium dominus'; the planet ruling the specific subdivision of degrees within a sign</note> is located, to see how much the benefic or malefic stars regard him. 

For when benefic stars possess that same sign in which the place of the spouse was found, being positioned in favorable places of the nativity and cast down by no lowliness, but following the power of their own condition, they will give glorious and wealthy wives, and those who are always joined by bonds of harmony. In such cases, marriages to many wives are not decreed, for whatever wife they have obtained, the marriage lasts until the final day of life with great joy and charm. You will be able to find the types of marriages and the deaths of wives from the failing nature of the signs and from their differences. If, however, malefic stars have done the same, all things become contrary to these: for then humble and inglorious wives are decreed; then also dissensions in marriages, then bitter types of grudges, then even the wretched disturbance of discord is perpetrated; then the spouses themselves are sterile, then they are adulteresses; but you will be able to explain all these things according to the powers of the stars.

<margin>The Lot of Marriage in a woman’s nativity.</margin>
If, however, you wish to find the place of the husband in a woman’s nativity, and it is a daytime birth, calculate from **Mars** (♂) to **Venus** (♀); in a nighttime birth, from **Venus** (♀) to **Mars** (♂). You shall perceive this by the same reasoning, [counting] the same amount from the **Ascendant**; and in whatever sign the final number of the portion comes to, this sign will show you the place of the husband. You will be able to know what kind of husband he is by the same reasoning which we used for women in the nativities of men. You ought to remember, however, that generally **Venus** (♀) always indicates the wife, and **Mars** (♂) the husband.

<margin>**Venus** (♀) shows the wife, while **Mercury** (☿) shows the husband.</margin>
**Venus** (♀) and **Mercury** (☿) always show us the place of children; for whichever of them is positioned earlier in the nativity, you shall calculate starting from that one to the other, and divide the collected sum of all the degrees starting from the **Ascendant** through the following signs. In whatever sign the final degree falls, this sign will show you the place of children. We teach by this example how it is that "whichever is earlier," as we said: If **Venus** (♀) is in **Aries** (♈) and **Mercury** (☿) is in **Gemini** (♊), **Venus** (♀) is found to be earlier; therefore, you shall calculate starting from **Venus** (♀) up to **Mercury** (☿). But if in a similar way **Mercury** (☿) is before, and **Venus** (♀) is in the later signs, you shall give the beginning of the calculation from **Mercury** (☿). If they are established in one sign, you shall come from the one starting earlier to the other which is found in the later degrees of the same sign. If they are found in the same degrees, you shall start from that one whose minutes precede. But if they are in the same minutes, then, omitting this, [calculate] from **Jupiter** (♃) to **Venus** (♀) in a daytime...

-># BOOK VI #<-

<margin>Read this as "Of the Condition"; for not only are the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> said to be "conditionary," but also the planets, which the Arabs call **Haiz** <note>original: 'Haiz'; a term for a planet being in its preferred "sect"—for example, a daytime planet being above the horizon during the day</note>. That is, when a diurnal planet is above the earth by day, or a nocturnal planet is below the earth at night.</margin>
[...by day] but in a nocturnal birth you shall calculate from **Jupiter** to **Saturn**, using the same methods. Therefore, when you have gathered the place of children by precise degree calculation, examine in a similar way how much the **benefic** stars <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> or the **malefic** stars <note>Saturn and Mars</note> regard this place. You must also consider the **condition** <note>original: 'condationis', likely 'conditionis'</note> of the stars with the most diligent reasoning, as well as the nature and power of the zodiac sign itself. For if benefic stars regard this place, being positioned in favorable areas of the **nativity** <note>the birth chart</note> and in supportive signs, they decree children according to the power of the locations and signs; but the malefic stars do the opposite. Yet sometimes even the malefic stars themselves decree children, if the birth falls under their own **condition**—that is, **Saturn** in a day birth, and **Mars** in a night birth. Children are decreed according to the nature of the signs. However, we ought to know this: if the place of children is found in a **double sign** <note>original: 'duplici signo'; signs like Gemini or Pisces</note>, the man will have children from two wives; but if it is a **solid sign** <note>original: 'solidum'; a Fixed sign like Leo or Taurus</note>, the man will have children from one wife, and the woman from one husband. If the malefic and benefic stars regard the place of children in equal measure, they both give offspring and take them away. Or, if the power of the benefic stars overcomes the hostile rays of the malefic stars, a certain weakness will be inflicted upon the children received, or certainly the children will be separated from the parents by a great feud. In this place, as in all others, you should perceive the mixtures and temperaments of the stars with diligent reasoning, as well as the nature of the signs and the specific powers of the places coming from the **ascendant** <note>original: 'horosc.'; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>. But generally, the **fifth house** <note>original: 'quinta sedes'</note> shows the place of children, as well as the ruler and nature of that sign, and the testimonies of the benefic or malefic stars.

If you wish to find the **place of defects and health** <note>the Lot of Ailments</note> by precise degree, in a day birth you shall calculate from **Saturn** to **Mars** and project the same distance from the ascendant; in a night birth, calculate from **Mars** to **Saturn** and project the same from the ascendant. In whatever sign the final number of collected degrees falls, this sign will show you the place of defects and health. Generally, however, the **sixth sign** from the ascendant shows destruction. Therefore, you shall define the defect of health primarily from the nature of the sign. For in the book of instruction, we said which parts of the body each individual sign rules. In the second order of importance, you shall look to see how the benefic and malefic stars regard this same place. For if benefic stars, positioned in their own houses or in their **exaltations**, regard this place with a prosperous radiation, they will free the person from every onset of illness. But if malefic stars regard this place with a threatening radiation, they decree bitter defects of health along with miserable calamity; they perform these things according to the nature of the signs and their own power. For **Mars** decrees blows, minor bodily wounds, falls from heights, ruins, and destruction of the wretched from those very accidents; but **Saturn** decrees the onset of pestilent humors, spasms, tremors, dimness of sight, and miserable dangers from water, and things similar to these. If a ray from the benefic stars reaches the malefic stars that are decreeing these things, all these evils are mitigated. But if this place is possessed by malefics and left naked of all protection from benefic stars, perpetual defects of health and fatal outcomes of calamities are decreed. Furthermore, **Mars** will cause harm within fifteen years, **Saturn** within thirty, and the **Sun** within nineteen. If there are two acting together who cause harm, once the years of the defined time for both are calculated, each of these stars will decree the onset of the expected defect or illness at both times, according to its own nature.

If you wish to find the **place of Cupid** <note>the Lot of Desire or Passion</note> by precise degree, in a day birth you shall calculate from the **Lot of Spirit** <note>original: 'parte dæmonis'</note> to the **Lot of Fortune**, and project the same from the ascendant; in a night birth, you shall calculate from Fortune to Spirit by the same reasoning, and project the same from the ascendant. When you have gathered this place by degree calculation, the nature of all your desires and cravings will be demonstrated to you from the sign and the testimonies of the stars. How you may find the Lot of Fortune and the Lot of Spirit, we have explained in the fourth book.

If you wish to find the **place of necessity** <note>original: 'Necessitatis locũ'; associated with constraints or poverty</note> by degree calculation, in a day birth you shall calculate from Fortune to Spirit. In a night birth, from Spirit to Fortune, and project the same from the ascendant. When you have gathered this same place by this method, you shall define everything about that place according to the quality of the signs and stars.

If you wish to gather the **place of honors** by degree calculation, you shall always calculate from the **tenth house** to the **Sun**, and project the same from the ascendant. Whichever sign receives the final degree will show you the insignia of honors, both from its own nature and from the accidental testimonies of all the stars.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Military Service** by the method of degrees, you shall always calculate from **Mars** <note>original: '♂'</note> to the **Sun** <note>original: '☉'</note>, and then project the same distance from the **Horoscope** <note>The Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>. In whichever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the outcome of military service according to the nature of that sign and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to find the **Place of Foreign Travel** by degrees, you shall always calculate from the **Sun** to **Mars**, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the outcome of travel according to its nature and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to calculate the **Reputation of One's Esteem** by the method of degrees, you shall calculate from the **Sun** to the **Midheaven** <note>original: 'MC'; the highest point in the sky at the time of birth</note>, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the reputation of one's esteem according to its nature and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to find **Bodily Virtue** <note>Strength or physical excellence</note> by degrees, you shall calculate from the **Sun** to **Jupiter** <note>original: '♃'</note>, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**; you should handle all other matters by a similar method, for all decrees will be shown to you according to the nature of the signs and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to calculate the **Substance of Possessions** by the method of degrees, you shall always calculate from **Venus** <note>original: '♀'</note> to **Jupiter**, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, you will find the order of one's possessions from the nature of that sign and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Accusation** by the method of degrees, you shall always calculate from **Mars** to **Saturn** <note>original: '♄'</note>, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the outcome of accusations according to its nature and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Adversaries and Enemies** by the method of degrees: for a birth during the day, calculate from **Mars** to **Mercury** <note>original: '☿'</note>; for a birth at night, calculate from **Mercury** back to **Mars**, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, it shows the enemies based on its nature and the testimonies of the planets.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Friends** by the method of degrees: for a birth during the day, calculate from **Jupiter** to **Venus**; for a birth at night, from **Venus** to **Jupiter**, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, it will show you the friends you seek by a most true method based on its nature and the testimonies of the planets.

The **Place of Glory**: at night from **Venus** to **Jupiter**, but by day the opposite. **Nemesis** <note>The Lot of Retribution or Fate</note>: at night from **Fortune** to the **Moon** <note>original: '☽'</note>, but by day the opposite. **Power**: at night from **Saturn** to the **Sun**, but by day the opposite.

**The Foundation** <note>original: 'Basis'</note>: at night from **Fortune** to the **Spirit** <note>original: 'genium'; the Lot of Spirit</note>, but by day the opposite. However, if **Venus** has reached thirty degrees, whether by night or by day, you shall calculate by degrees from the **Spirit** to **Fortune**.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Slaves** by the method of degrees, you shall always calculate from **Mercury** to the **Moon**, and then the same distance from the **Horoscope**. In whichever sign the final degree falls, this will demonstrate the nature of one's servants according to its own nature and the testimonies of the planets.

### XXXIII. THE DIVISION OF TIME OWED TO THE TIME LORD.

<note>The 'C' is a decorative drop cap.</note>
We have begun to impart to you, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom this book is dedicated</note>, the secrets of astrology <note>original: 'matheseos'</note> through the most true path of definitions. However, the seventh book will show you a most full treatment of all these things, so that you may find everything without any difficulty through the easiest and most true inquiries. To complete this book, I will add this: I shall show you which planet, when it becomes the master of a period of time, divides the entire substance of ten years and nine months for itself and the other planets, and what it decrees for each according to that method. As for how the Master of Time—whom the Greeks call the **Time Lord** <note>original: 'chronocratora'; Greek: <term>χρονοκράτορα</term></note>—may be found, we have shown this by a clear method in the book of instructions. Research this matter diligently so that you may have the outcomes and ranks of all dangers explored.

When you have gathered all these things with diligent reasoning, you will then find what he does when he is the Master of Time. For if dangers were decreed by him in the birth chart, he then carries out whatever he had previously decreed. If of the world...

determines in the birth-chart; then it pursues the wretched offspring of children with cruel power. If it has decreed widowhood, then it dissolves the marriage either through death or discord. If it decrees accusations, then it stirs up crowds of enemies; if illnesses, it inflicts the defect of wretched calamity; if losses, then it shatters the inheritance with various lacerations. To **Jupiter** <note>original: '♃'</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: '♄'</note> assigns twelve months from its own time, if it has been made the Lord of the Times. To the **Sun** <note>original: '☉'</note>, Saturn assigns nineteen months from its ten-year period if it has been made the Lord of the Times; but when the Sun receives the time assigned to him by Saturn, he stirs up legal cases and contentious struggles with quarreling, but these cases are for the most part brought regarding the ownership of houses or estates, especially if it is a nighttime birth; but he also decrees danger to the father and causes a loss of dignity.

To **Venus** <note>original: '♀'</note>, Saturn assigns eight months from its ten-year period if it has been made the Lord of the Times; but when Venus receives the time assigned to her by Saturn, she indeed separates it from all misfortune, so that the shock of a preceding crisis—which the malice of another planet might have committed—is corrected by a salutary remedy. But if he himself decrees a marriage, a widow is then joined to the wife by the nuptial bond.

To **Mercury** <note>original: '☿'</note>, Saturn assigns twenty months from its ten-year period if it has been made the Lord of the Times; but when Mercury receives the time assigned to him by Saturn, he excites the dormant animosities of old legal cases, and causes the hidden insults of contentions to be inserted and stirred up again by revived legal actions.

To the **Moon** <note>original: '☽'</note>, Saturn assigns twenty-five months from its ten-year period if it has been made the Lord of the Times; but when the Moon receives the time assigned to her by Saturn, she will stir up illnesses from **vicious humors** <note>An imbalance of the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, or will strike with the greatest crisis of danger from water, or will cause one to be disturbed by the announcement of new lawsuits, so that this entire time always brings on various dangers and various anxieties. But this is if the Moon is full of light; if however she is waning and, in the birth-chart, is struck by the radiation of Saturn, she decrees the hardships of a most unhappy death along with wretched calamities.

## JUPITER'S DECREES WHEN HE IS THE LORD OF THE TIMES ##
## CHAPTER XXXV ##

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' at the beginning of Chapter XXXV, featuring a square woodcut frame with floral ornamentation around the letter.</image-desc>

If Jupiter has been made the Lord of the Times—that is, when the order of times has come to him—he is also granted ten years and nine months, but this entire period is divided by him in a similar fashion. Therefore, he himself must also be inspected when he is the Lord, to see how he is positioned in the birth-chart, and in which signs and degrees he is placed, and whether he is established in the first or second **angles** <note>The primary "power centers" of a chart, such as the Ascendant or Midheaven</note>, or indeed in lazy and cast-down <note>Cadent houses, which were considered weak or ineffective</note> places, and whether it is a daytime or nighttime birth. From all these things, we shall find the effectiveness of his decrees when he is the Lord of the Times. For whatever has been decreed by Jupiter in the birth-chart, he delivers when he has acquired the lordship of the times; but you must observe this in all the other planets as well, as we said concerning Saturn. For all planets, whatever they have decreed in the birth-chart—whether prosperous or evil—will fully carry it out when they have obtained the lordship of the times.

To Jupiter, therefore, since ten years and nine months have been granted, he first claims twelve months for himself from all this time. In these twelve months, which Jupiter has thus assigned to himself, he decrees the glory of happiness and joys according to the measure of the birth-chart, especially if he himself was the Lord of the Nativity; for then, to whomever marriage or children have been decreed, if the person's age permits
