...has admitted <note>This sentence continues from the previous page's description of Jupiter's influence</note>, since he himself will be the lord of the times, he will perform his duties with the greatest reason; he grants glories and honors, as well as increases of patrimony <note>Inherited estate or wealth</note>, as we have said, according to the measure of the person's birth-chart.

To **Saturn** <note>original: '♄'</note>, **Jupiter** <note>original: '♃'</note> assigns thirty months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. But when Saturn receives the time assigned to him by Jupiter, he will make men always be dulled by a sluggish way of life, so that they fail in all actions with the inactive numbness of cold; this occurs if it is a nocturnal birth <term>Nocturnal birth: A birth that occurs at night, which changes the "sect" or power dynamics of the planets</term>, and if Saturn is not well-placed in the birth-chart.

To **Mars** <note>original: '♂'</note>, Jupiter assigns fifteen months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Mars receives the time assigned to him by Jupiter, he changes the entire order of life and business; whatever was being handled in the preceding arrangement of affairs, he transfers to another order of life, so that at this time the institutions of the prior office are deserted, or he will certainly do harm through various crises.

To the **Sun** <note>original: '☉'</note>, Jupiter assigns nineteen months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Sun receives the time assigned to him by Jupiter, he will cause all secrets of life to be made public, and all acts to be overturned by various means; he also leads the mind through different types of anxieties with various thoughts. He even dissipates whatever was composed before, so that with everything disturbed and confused, the mind is divided by various types of worry; but these effects are diminished in a daytime birth.

To **Venus** <note>original: '♀'</note>, Jupiter assigns eight months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Venus receives the time assigned to her by Jupiter, if she is the mistress of a nocturnal birth, or if Jupiter himself <note>is well-placed</note>, she brings about marriages and decrees prosperous times with the benefit of happiness. In a daytime birth, however, he indicates moderate and constant allurements of love, especially if Venus herself has moved the nature of the place or sign, or changed her own nature.

To **Mercury** <note>original: '☿'</note>, Jupiter assigns twenty months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Mercury receives the time assigned to him by Jupiter, he decrees such actions from which the greatest benefits of profit are conferred, and he grants the protection of many great friendships, and assigns increases of prosperous reason in all duties, so that from all actions, prosperous benefits of both profit and happiness are conferred with favorable fortune.

To the **Moon** <note>original: '☽'</note>, Jupiter assigns twenty-five months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Moon receives the time assigned to her by Jupiter, he decrees the rest of tranquil serenity and the greatest increases of happiness—but this is according to the substance of the birth-chart. For then the pain of preceding misfortunes is mitigated by various kinds of comforts; then the hardships of poverty are relaxed; then health constrains the defects of illnesses; then the fear of dangers is countered by prosperous protections; then in all disputes over causes, judgments are delivered according to one's wishes. Then pain is broken, then anxiety is changed, so that with the filth of preceding misfortunes wiped away, a pure and clean time of happiness approaches, especially if Jupiter looks upon a Full Moon <note>original: "Lunam plenam luminibus," literally "a Moon full of lights"</note> with a prosperous radiation in the birth-chart.

### THE DECREES OF MARS WHEN HE SHALL BE THE LORD OF THE TIMES. CHAPTER 36.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'M' containing a seated figure in classical robes within a landscape featuring trees and a clear sky.</image-desc> If **Mars** has been made the lord of the times, or when he comes to the lordship of the ten-year period, all this time is divided by him according to the same methods. In this likewise, just as with Saturn and Jupiter, you must inspect everything by a similar reasoning: namely the sign, the degree, the condition, the place, and the testimony <note>The "testimony" refers to the aspects or "looks" other planets give to Mars</note>, so that you can find and judge everything through clear investigations.

Mars, therefore, when he is the lord of the times, retains fifteen months for himself from his ten-year period, in which he decrees the greatest actions indeed (according to the substance of the birth-chart), but with prior disturbance, so that in those very acts, of whatever kind they may be, a varied risk of dangers arises, especially if he should be the lord of a daytime birth.

To **Saturn**, Mars assigns thirty months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Saturn receives the time assigned to him by Mars, he imposes the sluggish weight of slowness in all dealings, so that they always conduct all business more slowly; he also makes the time ineffective and filthy...

Therefore, when Jupiter receives the time assigned to him by Mars, he decrees all the benefits of prosperity and will always complete business with a successful outcome; he also bestows profits and all types of professional duties. He grants rest to those who labor, health to the sick, security to the anxious, return to those who wander, an end to litigation, and abundance to those established in hardship.

To the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, **Mars** assigns nineteen months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Sun receives the time assigned to him by Mars, he decrees the greatest risks of danger from constant calamity and disturbs the entire order of life with a wretched transformation. To **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, **Mars** assigns eight months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. But if they are in a square aspect <term>Square: A challenging astrological angle of 90 degrees</term> to each other in the birth-chart, they then cause adulteries to be committed; yet they hide this crime with the testimony of Jupiter. With **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> and the **Sun**, however, they cause the crime to be made public, even with a wretched risk to one’s life.

To **Mercury**, **Mars** assigns twenty months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Mercury receives the time assigned to him by Mars, he will cause dangers to be stirred up from certain writings, or will always inflict wretched loss from some theft; however, he will cause enemies to be scattered by frequent legal accounts. But if they are in a square or an opposition aspect <term>Opposition: A celestial angle of 180 degrees, where planets face off from opposite sides of the zodiac</term> to each other in the birth-chart, then they indicate a crime of sorcery <note>original: maleficiorum</note> or of counterfeit money, especially if Venus is found in the "bounds" <note>The "bounds" or "terms" are specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</note> or the house of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>.

To the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, **Mars** assigns twenty-five months from his ten-year period, if he has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Moon receives the time assigned to her by Mars, she will always cause the greatest risks of danger to be brought in, especially if she is full of light <note>i.e., a Full Moon</note>. For then dangerous spaces of time are decreed; then flights, then exiles, then wretched risks of danger are stirred up; then men are thrust into custody or a public prison; then fires, then fevers, then heavy loss with a wretched tearing apart of the inheritance is decreed; then a heavy fall into sickness is always brought on. But if, in the birth-chart, they are in a square or opposition aspect with the testimony of Jupiter, then without doubt they cause either a bloody, or a mournful, or a sudden death. But if Saturn is found with the Moon in the birth-chart, and the Moon receives the time assigned to her by Mars, even then the destruction of a bitter death is brought in from the preceding dangers—though these dangers reach their outcome according to the varieties of the zodiac signs.

## THE DECREES OF THE SUN WHEN HE HAS BEEN MADE THE LORD OF THE TIMES. CHAPTER 37.

<image-desc>An ornamental woodcut initial 'S' decorated with stylized leaf and floral motifs.</image-desc>
If the **Sun** has been made the lord of the times, you ought to look into all things regarding him by a similar reasoning as we have said for the others: namely, the mixtures, the temperaments, the sign, the place, and the degrees <note>original: partes</note>, so that from a comparison of all these things you may find the entire order of the decrees. But even by the Sun himself, all this time which has been allotted is divided by very similar reasonings.

Therefore, when the Sun has been made the lord of the times, he keeps nineteen months for himself from his ten-year period. In these nineteen months, nothing prosperous should be expected from him, but rather we must expect all types of misfortunes, which are nevertheless mitigated in some part in a daytime birth <note>A "diurnal" birth, where the Sun is above the horizon, making the Sun more naturally favorable</note>. They are calmed by the testimony of Jupiter, but they are provoked by Saturn and Mars, especially if the Sun himself was poorly placed in the man’s birth-chart.

From his ten-year period, the **Sun** assigns thirty months [to Saturn], if the Sun has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when **Saturn** receives the time assigned to him by the Sun, he indeed threatens a pestilential and deadly destruction in a nighttime birth; but in a daytime birth, he decrees increases of the greatest happiness, though still according to the substance of the birth-chart...

**Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> assigns fifteen months from his ten-year period to the **Sun**, if the Sun has been made the lord of the times. **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> assigns twenty months from his ten-year period to the **Sun**, if the Sun has been made the lord of the times. The **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> assigns twenty months from her ten-year period to the **Sun**, if the Sun has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Moon receives the time assigned to her by the Sun, she disturbs the person's whole life with a constant and unstable variety, so that whatever was established in former times is taken away again for more urgent reasons. This time will be changeable due to various inequalities, so that hardships are relieved by sudden riches, and those very riches are followed again by the hardships of poverty.

### THE DECREES OF VENUS WHEN SHE IS THE LADY OF THE TIMES, CHAPTER XXXVIII.

<image-desc>A large decorative capital letter 'V' begins this chapter, featuring intricate floral patterns and vines within a square border.</image-desc>

To **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> also, a space of ten years and nine months is granted. When Venus is the lady of the times, you must observe everything in her with the same reasoning that we have shown should be observed in the others. Out of this whole time, she claims only eight months for herself, in which she raises marital affections with the greatest grace of beauty; she also decrees joy with the highest security, especially if she was the ruling planet of that birth chart.

**Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> assigns thirty months from his ten-year period to **Venus**, if she has been made the lady of the times. Therefore, when Saturn receives the time assigned to him by Venus, he either stirs up grave disagreements with a woman through his own indignation, or separates a man from his wife, either by death or by certain legal rivalries.

**Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> assigns twelve months from his ten-year period to **Venus**, if she has been made the lady of the times. Therefore, when Jupiter receives the time assigned to him by Venus, he decrees a good and joyful time, but he will stir up certain scandals <note>original: *infamias*, referring to loss of reputation or public disgrace</note> within it.

**Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> assigns fifteen months from his ten-year period to **Venus**, if she has been made the lady of the times. When Mars receives the time assigned to him by Venus, he decrees many evils and frequent inconveniences of pain. Then he also always agitates the mind with the various allurements of loves, and because of the hard torments of love, he always imposes a heavy sorrow on the soul, so that because of these vices of a wandering mind, legal crises also frequently occur. Troubles and dangers also occur because of very bad wives—either brought upon by them or involving them—for either the crime of adultery arises, or a certain love conceived with impure and dishonest thoughts.

The **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> assigns nineteen months from his ten-year period to **Venus**, if she has been made the lady of the times. Therefore, when the Sun receives the time assigned to him by Venus, he will make men always flee from their own wives, and this with risk to their lives <note>original: *capitis periculo*, literally "danger of the head" or capital punishment/status</note> and the loss of inheritance. If, however, a prosperous ray from Jupiter is added, they are merely separated by the necessities of travel.

### THE DECREES OF MERCURY WHEN HE IS THE LORD OF THE TIMES. CHAPTER XXXIX.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap letter 'M' depicting a man in 16th-century attire standing in a landscape.</image-desc> To **Mercury** also, a space of ten years and nine months is granted; in this, however, we must gather everything by a similar reasoning as with the other stars. Therefore, when he himself is made the lord of the times, he reserves twenty months for himself from his ten-year period, in which he decrees all good things from constant good fortune. He ensures that a prosperous outcome follows all actions, especially if he is the lord of the birth chart <note>the planet ruling the Ascendant or the primary ruler of the horoscope</note> and is well-placed within that chart.

**Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> assigns thirty months from his ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Saturn receives the time assigned to him by Mercury, he decrees the deaths of household members from a constant calamity of misfortunes, such as parents, relatives, patrons, and those who were accustomed to being of use to us.

**Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> assigns twelve months from his ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Jupiter receives the time assigned to him by Mercury, he decrees truly quiet days, separated from all the noise of business; and in this very quiet, he always provides the greatest benefits of praise and joys of happiness. He even decrees children for those who have none, if the logic of the birth chart permits it.

**Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> assigns fifteen months from his ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Mars receives the time assigned to him by Mercury, he will stir up enemies, bring accusations, and decree lawsuits from new legal notices—which, however, the good testimony of Jupiter may mitigate.

The **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> assigns nineteen months from his ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Sun receives the time assigned to him by Mercury, he always indicates the greatest losses of inheritance and the greatest anxieties for the mind.

**Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> assigns eight months from her ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when Venus receives the time assigned to her by Mercury, she decrees good benefits from constant good fortune, along with security, perfect quiet, and, according to the measure of the birth chart, profitable gains.

The **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> assigns twenty-five months from her ten-year period to **Mercury**, if Mercury has been made the lord of the times. Therefore, when the Moon receives the time assigned to her by Mercury, she decrees the greatest illnesses and the greatest vices of lingering diseases; but these are according to the nature of the place and the sign, unless Jupiter mitigates them with his good testimony.

### THE DECREES OF THE MOON WHEN SHE IS THE LADY OF THE TIMES. CHAPTER XXXX.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap letter 'L' depicting a man in classical or Renaissance garb sitting or reclining.</image-desc> To the **Moon** also, a space of ten years and nine months is granted; in this, as in all the other stars, you must treat everything with diligent reasoning. From this ten-year period, the Moon reserves twenty-five months for herself; in these, if she is so placed that she is waning in light <note>original: *minuta luminibus*</note> and moves toward Saturn, or if she is full and moves toward Mars, she decrees death in every way. But if she is full of light and adorned by the testimonies of the benefics <note>the "helpful" planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</note>, she decrees modest increases in inheritance, though with the greatest labors. For the times of the Sun and Moon always have bad endings, especially if the malevolent stars <note>Saturn and Mars</note> look upon them with a threatening and unfortunate radiation <note>an astrological aspect</note>.

**Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> assigns thirty months from his ten-year period to the **Moon**, if she has been made the lady of the times. Therefore, when Saturn receives the time assigned to him by the Moon, if the Moon is waning, he decrees wretched deaths and miserable endings of dangers arising from corrupted humors <note>unbalanced bodily fluids</note>, or from water, or from shipwrecks. But if she is full, he indeed causes these same things, but gives the ability to escape.

**Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> assigns twelve months from his ten-year period to the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, if she has been made the mistress of the times. Therefore, when Jupiter receives the time assigned to him from the Moon, he decrees all good things with joy and cheerfulness, especially if the Moon is full of light <note>a Full Moon</note>; for then perils, then fears, and then sicknesses are put to rest. At that time, according to the measure of the birth chart <note>original: *genituræ*</note>, increases in happiness proceed, and adverse matters tend toward prosperity.

**Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> assigns fifteen months from his ten-year period to the **Moon**, if she has been made the mistress of the times. Therefore, when Mars receives the time assigned to him from the Moon, if the Moon is full, he decrees the greatest disturbances and seditions; and if in the birth chart he is seen in a square <note>original: *quadrata*; an aspect of 90 degrees</note> or diameter <note>original: *diametra*; an opposition of 180 degrees</note> aspect from the Moon, he decrees a bloody end of calamity.

The **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> assigns nineteen months from his ten-year period to the **Moon**, if she has been made the mistress of the times. Therefore, when the Sun receives the time assigned to him from the Moon, he indicates fires, burnings, sicknesses, and the miserable exhaustion of burning fevers; but a favorable testimony from **Jupiter** will mitigate all these things.

**Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> assigns eight months from her ten-year period to the **Moon**, if she has been made the mistress of the times. Therefore, when Venus receives the time assigned to her from the Moon, if it is a daytime birth, she decrees the harshness of sterility; but if it is a nighttime birth, she grants the greatest increases in profits, especially if the Moon is diminished in its splendor and light <note>a waning or New Moon</note>.

**Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> assigns twenty months from his ten-year period to the **Moon**, if she has been made the mistress of the times. Therefore, when Mercury receives the time assigned to him from the Moon, he decrees "cold" sicknesses <note>likely referring to ailments thought to be caused by cold humors, like phlegmatic diseases</note> with the greatest bodily weakness.

By these reasonings, Mavortius, our glory, the sum of the times is divided. But I do not wish for abrupt judgments to be brought forth in determining these treatises. For frequently, if a benevolent star receives its assigned time but then has a malevolent star with it during that period which regards it in a square or diameter radiation, it loses the decree of its goodness to the power of the malevolent star. You will find this same thing in a malevolent star by a similar reasoning: for if a malevolent star receives its assigned time, and a benevolent star—either positioned alongside it or arranged in a favorable radiation—mitigates it, the entire decree of misfortunes is relieved by the healthy protection of the benevolent star.

Thus, the discipline of this completed work has been revealed to you so that it may be understood, nor is there anything else yet to be required; for we have related in a teachable discourse everything with which we ought to instruct unrefined minds. Since we have now reached the very threshold of secrets through these first initiations of the ceremonies, we ought to hear the remaining things with an intent mind, lest—with ears set in boredom and rejecting these words—we introduce the opinions of wandering treatises. Thus, with the sixth book completed, let all the zeal of speaking be transferred to the secrets of the seventh book with good omens <note>original: *bonis auibus*, literally "with good birds"</note> and a lucky star.

# THE MATHESIS, BOOK VII, BY JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS JUNIOR, OF THE RANK OF CLARISSIMUS VIR <note>V.C. stands for *Vir Clarissimus*, a title denoting a high-ranking Roman senator</note>, TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANUS, PROCONSUL.
## PREFACE.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'C' featuring a seated infant or cherub-like figure within an ornate frame of leafy vines and floral patterns.</image-desc>

When Orpheus opened the ceremonies of the rites to unknown men, he required nothing else from those he was initiating in the first vestibule except the necessity of an oath, and he demanded it with a certain terrible authority of religion, lest the secrets of the discovered and composed religion be betrayed to profane ears. But even Plato frequently kept the *Timaeus* <note>Plato’s famous dialogue on the creation of the universe</note> close to himself, lest he ever disclose the venerable commentaries of secret discussions to the unskilled; for all these things suffer a loss when they are thrust upon ruined and desperate minds. Among the Pythagoreans, our Porphyry <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on the life of Pythagoras</note> also consecrated the religious feast of our soul with silence. Whence I also, following the law of these men, bind you with an oath, Mavortius our glory, by the god who is the fabricator of the world, who [created] all things by necessity...

...[God] cultivated with the necessity of perpetuity, who fixed the sun and the moon, who arranged the courses and orders of all the stars, who constrained the waves of the sea within certain boundaries of the earth, who kindled fire for its eternal substance, who suspended the earth placed in the middle with equalized moderation, who composed humans, wild beasts, birds, and all kinds of living creatures with the divine majesty of his craftsmanship, who waters the earth with perennial springs, who causes the blasts of the winds to vary with a certain moderation of necessity, who, for the fabrication of all things from the four elements, perfected everything from contrary and repugnant things in a balanced diversity, who ordained the rising and setting, and the immortality of eternal perpetuity of all earthquakes through the descent and ascent of the soul—lest these venerable common things be disclosed to profane or unskillful ears, but only to those whom an incorrupt mind has established in the right order of living by the chaste and modest protection of the mind, whose faith is unimpaired, whose hands are separated from every wickedness of crime—to those, namely, who are upright, modest, sober, and temperate, so that the complete knowledge of divination <note>Here "divination" refers specifically to the scientific study of astrology (*mathesis*).</note> may instill itself into those decorated with only the pure splendor of the mind. ### CHARTS OF THE EXPOSED OR UN-NURTURED INFANTS CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>A square decorative woodcut initial letter 'V' depicting a scene with several figures in a landscape, possibly from a classical or mythological narrative.</image-desc>

**T**herefore, if the benevolent stars <note>The "benefics," usually Jupiter and Venus.</note> do not see the face <note>original: *vultum* (OCR reads *votum*); refers to the aspect or appearance of the rising sign.</note> of the **Horoscopus** <term>horoscopus: the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, and the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is positioned on any **angle** <term>cardine: one of the four cardinal points of a chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, or Nadir)</term>, and **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> and **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> are in the seventh place from the **Horoscopus**—that is, positioned in the setting <note>The Western horizon or Descendant.</note>—those born are immediately **exposed** <term>expositus: the Roman practice of abandoning an unwanted infant in a public place</term> by their mothers. But if the **Horoscopus** is in those signs which have short times <note>Signs of "short ascension," which rise more quickly over the horizon.</note>, and **Mars** is in the seventh place from the **Horoscopus** (in the setting), while the **Moon**, waning in light, is carried toward **Saturn**, or if full, toward **Mars**, the newborn infant will likewise be exposed. Furthermore, if the **Lord of Fortune** <note>The planet that rules the sign containing the "Part of Fortune."</note>—that is, the lord of that sign in which the **Lot of Fortune** is found—and the lord of that sign in which the part of the **Horoscopus** is established, are hidden **under the rays** <term>sub radiis: a planet so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up" or hidden</term> of the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, or if **Saturn** and **Mars** are located in those signs which we mentioned before in a nocturnal birth, the newborn infant will be exposed. 

But if the **Moon** is found in the **Horoscopus**, or in the setting of the **Horoscopus**, and **Mars** and **Saturn** are joined by a **diameter radiation** <note>An opposition aspect of 180 degrees.</note>, or if one malefic is found on the conceptional **Sun**, whoever is born will be exposed. If, however, the **Sun** and **Moon** look upon each other with a diameter radiation, or if they are **square** <note>A 90-degree aspect.</note>, provided they make these configurations on the **angles**, and malefic stars are positioned together with both—that is, if the **Sun** is in the **Horoscopus** and the **Moon** is in the setting, or the **Moon** is in the **Horoscopus** and the **Sun** is in the setting, and **Mars** is with one and **Saturn** with the other—at the very moment of birth, the infant, placed in narrow straits, is extinguished by suffocation. But if the superior malefic stars, having become active, look upon the **Moon** with a threatening radiation, even the mother incurs a grave danger of death during the birth itself. 

If the **Sun** is found in the **Horoscopus**, and the **Moon**, full of light, is carried toward **Mars** in whatever sign, while **Saturn** is positioned on some **angle**, he who is born will die after being exposed. But if the **Moon** is found with **Mars** on any **angle**, and the **Sun** with **Saturn** is established in the opposite position, and the testimony of **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> is lacking to all of these, he who is born will either be exposed or will immediately perish along with the mother. If the **Moon** is found on any **angle**, and **Mars** looks upon it from any other **angle** with a diameter radiation, or is found with it in the same part, and **Saturn** holds another **angle** of the birth chart or is positioned in the **anaphora** <term>anaphora: the house immediately following an angle, also known as a succedent house</term> of an **angle**, he who is born will be exposed. 

If, however, the star of **Jupiter** is found on any **angle**, and **Mars** looks upon it from a superior position, he will cause the exposed infants to be either found or returned, especially if **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> looks upon them with any radiation. If the **Sun** with **Saturn** is found in the **Horoscopus**, and the **Moon** is established in the **Midheaven** <note>original: M C (Medium Coeli)</note>, and **Mars** is positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** <note>original: I M C (Imum Coeli)</note> and looks upon the **Moon** with a diameter radiation, he who is born will be exposed; but if the **Sun** is established in the **Horoscopus** and the **Moon** in the **Midheaven**, with **Saturn** in the setting and **Mars** in the **Lower Midheaven**, he who is born will perish immediately upon being exposed, or the mother will die along with him. But what is always and generally appropriate to observe: if the **Sun** and **Moon** are established on any **angles**, and **Mars** and **Saturn** look upon them with a diameter radiation, or one by diameter and the other by square, the newborns will either be exposed or perish immediately, or the mothers will be destroyed with them in a miserable death. # SEVENTH [BOOK]

In the <term>epicataphora <note>The ninth house, which "falls away" or declines from the Midheaven.</note></term>, if the ☽ <note>Moon</note> is struck by one of them [the malefic planets Saturn or Mars] by either an opposition or a square aspect, or if it is positioned exactly with them, the one born under this sign will be exposed. If, however, while these things are so arranged, a benevolent star [a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus] receives the conjunction of the approaching ☽, those who were exposed will be taken in by others, and having been restored to freedom, they are raised in the place of sons. If the ☽ is found in the <term>horoscopus <note>The Ascendant or first house.</note></term>, and ♂ <note>Mars</note> is in the twelfth house from the horoscopus, while ♄ <note>Saturn</note> is positioned in the <term>anaphora <note>The second house, which "rises up" after the Ascendant.</note></term> of the horoscopus, and the ☉ <note>Sun</note> regards them with any aspect, a "beast"—cut limb-from-limb by doctors within the mother’s womb—will be brought forth. If, however, the ☽ is so positioned and has one malevolent star in the preceding sign and another in the following sign, and the star following the ☽ is regarded by the ☉ with any aspect, the one born will be exposed, or will perish immediately upon birth. If the Lord of the <term>nativity <note>The planet that rules the entire birth chart.</note></term> or the Lord of the sign in which the <term>Place of Fortune <note>The Part of Fortune, a calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and fate.</note></term> is found, are located in the twelfth, sixth, second, or eighth house from the horoscopus, and no favorable aspect of the benevolent stars regards them, nor is the Lord of the nativity positioned within its own <term>bounds <note>Specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets.</note></term>, the one born will be immediately exposed. But if any malevolent star sees either the [ruling] star or the horoscopus, and every aspect of the benevolent stars is absent from them, those exposed will indeed be torn apart by dogs.

If the Lord of the nativity is found in the <term>tropical signs <note>Also known as cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn.</note></term>, and is positioned in dark and lowly places, and the ☽ regards it with an opposition aspect, and the malevolent stars are joined to the ☽ by square or opposition in an equal degree of fellowship, those born will be thrown into the sea or a river and will perish immediately. When the ☉ and ☽ possess the thirtieth degree of any sign, the one born will possess no span of life. If, indeed, the malevolent stars regard the ☉ and ☽ positioned in the thirtieth degree from a square or opposition, the one born will be exposed and, torn by dogs, will be extinguished.

But if the ☽ and ☉ are found in the fifth house from the horoscopus in the same degree, and the benevolent stars regard neither them nor the horoscopus with a favorable aspect, the one born will be exposed; if the malevolent stars regard them, the exposed child will be consumed by dogs. If, however, as we have said, they are positioned in the tropical signs without the testimony of benevolent stars, the newborn will immediately perish in water. In a nativity, if neither the ☉, nor the ☽, nor the horoscopus, nor the Place of Fortune are regarded by a favorable aspect of the benevolent stars, the one born will be exposed. If the ☽ is <term>synodic <note>At the New Moon (conjunction with the Sun).</note></term>, so that she loses all the substance of her light, and no benevolent star regards her with a favorable aspect, the one born will be exposed. If a malevolent star sees the ☽ so positioned, they will either be stillborn or, once born, be torn by dogs.

If all the stars, along with the ☉ and ☽, are found in the sixth or twelfth house from the horoscopus, the one born will be exposed. # THE [SEVENTH] BOOK

If the Lord of the sign is in the <term>anaphora <note>The second house, which "rises up" after the Ascendant.</note></term> and regards it with an opposition, and ♂ <note>Mars</note> regards either the <term>horoscopus <note>The Ascendant or first house.</note></term> or the ☽ <note>Moon</note> from a square aspect, and no benevolent star sees any of these, the child who is born will be exposed and perish immediately. ### THE NATIVITIES OF TWINS AND THEIR SEX, CHAPTER II.

If ♃ <note>Jupiter</note> and ♀ <note>Venus</note> are positioned together in the <term>horoscopus <note>The Ascendant, or the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term>, and the horoscopus itself is in a <term>double sign <note>Bicorporeal or "double-bodied" signs like Gemini, Sagittarius, or Pisces, which were thought to represent duality.</note></term>, and the ☽ <note>Moon</note> is also in any <term>cardine <note>A "pivot" or "angle"—the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart.</note></term>, while the ☉ <note>Sun</note> has another star joined to it in the sign where it is, there will be a birth of twins, or the person born will have twin children. One must observe, however, that no malevolent star, being in a superior position, regards them; for if it regards one of them, whichever was conceived first will either die during birth or be aborted before birth.

But if the ☽ is not found in the cardines nor in a double sign, yet ♃ and ♀ are found together in the horoscopus in a double sign as we said before, and the ☽ or ☉ is placed with some other star, twins will be born. If the ☽ is found with the ☉ or with ♃, and the ☉ has another star joined to it, and being positioned in double signs they regard each other by any aspect, and if the horoscopus is found in a double sign and has any star joined to it, twins will be born. But if the ☽ is found in the signs of ♊ <note>Gemini</note> or ♐ <note>Sagittarius</note>, and ♃ and ♀ are positioned in the horoscopus or in the <term>setting <note>The Descendant, or the 7th house.</note></term> from the horoscopus, twins will be born. If the ☽ is found in a double sign and the ☉ is positioned in a cardine, or if the ☉ possesses the second sign from the ☽, or if it certainly holds a double sign placed with ♃ or ♀, twins will be born, or they will have twin children.

Whether they will be born of the male sex or the female sex, we shall gather by this reasoning: if the ☉, the ☽, and the horoscopus are positioned in masculine signs and the testimonies of masculine stars are added—that is, ♃, ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, or ♂ <note>Mars</note>—males will be born. If, however, ♀ alone does this same thing, being positioned in a feminine sign, while the ☉, ☽, and horoscopus are joined in the manner we have described, twins of different sexes are procreated. If ♂ and ♄ are positioned in their own <term>houses <note>The specific zodiac signs ruled by those planets (e.g., Aries for Mars, Capricorn for Saturn).</note></term> and see the ☉, ☽, and the horoscopus, and no ray of the benevolent stars reaches them, they will either be aborted or, being born prematurely, will perish immediately. If, however, with all things positioned as we said, the rays of both benevolent and malevolent stars reach them by this reasoning, whichever of the twins comes out first will perish. If the ☽ is found in any cardine, specifically in the second sign, and a benevolent star is positioned together with it, and the horoscopus is in a double sign, or with the second [sign], or with ♃ or ♀, or in the third or fifth [house], twins will be born. If the lord of that sign in which the specific <term>place of children <note>A mathematical point or "Lot" in the chart used to predict offspring.</note></term> is found is in a double sign, and the fifth place from the horoscopus is positioned in a double sign, and the ☽ is likewise placed in a double sign and ♃ or ♀ regards it by any aspect or is found together with it, twins will be born.

### THE NATIVITIES OF SLAVES OR CAPTIVES, CHAPTER III.

If the ☽ regards ♂ through an <term>opposition <note>An aspect of 180 degrees, often considered difficult or confrontational.</note></term>, or if one regards by opposition and the other joins the ☽ by a <term>square aspect <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, indicating tension.</note></term>, a slave will be born, especially if the ☽ is found in the <term>IMC <note>Imum Coeli, the "Bottom of the Sky" or 4th house.</note></term> or in the setting. If, however, ♃ regards these so positioned with a favorable aspect, he will attain the rewards of freedom. If the ☉ and ☿ <note>Mercury</note> are positioned together in the <term>MC <note>Medium Coeli, the "Midheaven" or 10th house.</note></term>, and a malevolent star positioned in a cardine regards the ☽ with an opposition aspect, the one born will be the son of a slave woman. If, however, ♃ regards those we mentioned with a favorable aspect, he will be subject to a free-born woman. If the <term>Place of Fortune <note>The "Lot of Fortune," a significant calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and fate.</note></term> is found in the sign of a malevolent star, and ♂ is in that same sign, that nativity will be servile. ### CHAPTER VII: THE BIRTH OF EUNUCHS AND HERMAPHRODITES

If the ☉ and ☽ are found in feminine signs, whether positioned together or in different places, and ♀ is positioned in a feminine sign within some cardine, while the ☽ and ♂ are positioned exactly in any cardine, they will produce either eunuchs or hermaphrodites. ### CHAPTER IX: BIRTH CHARTS OF CHILDREN AT ODDS WITH THEIR FATHERS

If in a birth chart ♂ <note>Mars</note> or ♄ <note>Saturn</note> is found in the fourth house from the <term>horoscopus <note>The Ascendant or 1st House.</note></term>, and the ☉ <note>Sun</note> is in the eighth, either the son will be alienated from the father, or they will have legal disputes because of their rivalries. But if ♂ <note>Mars</note> is found in the rising house of the horoscopus, or in the rising house of the <term>Midheaven <note>The 10th House, abbreviated here as M C.</note></term>, this same thing happens by a similar logic. Furthermore, if ♂ <note>Mars</note> is found exactly in the horoscopus or in the Midheaven, and the ☉ <note>Sun</note> is established in the descendant <note>the "setting" or 7th house</note> or in the <term>lower Midheaven <note>The 4th House, abbreviated here as I M C.</note></term>, this same result will be produced. If, however, these malefic positions we mentioned are shared with the ☽ <note>Moon</note>, quarrels of enmity are stirred up between mother and sons, especially if the ☽ <note>Moon</note> regards ♄ <note>Saturn</note> in this way. But whoever has the ☉ <note>Sun</note> in the <term>terms <note>Specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note></term> of ♂ <note>Mars</note> in a daytime birth, or in a nighttime birth has ♄ <note>Saturn</note> and the ☉ <note>Sun</note>—if indeed ♂ <note>Mars</note> by day or ♄ <note>Saturn</note> by night regards them with a square or opposite radiation, and no aspect of a <term>benefic star <note>Usually Jupiter or Venus.</note></term> mitigates this—the sons will kill their own fathers; if the ☽ <note>Moon</note> is found in this condition, they will kill their mothers. If the ☉ <note>Sun</note> is established in the terms or houses of malefic stars and is placed in the sixth or twelfth house from the horoscopus, and a malefic star regards it while so positioned with a square or opposite radiation, it will cause sons to be disinherited by their fathers. But if a benefic star regards the ☉ <note>Sun</note> so positioned from any side, the severity of the father's animosity is mitigated. If the ☉ <note>Sun</note> is found in the rising house of the horoscopus, or in the eighth house from the horoscopus, the son will not indeed be disinherited by the father, but he will cause the paternal inheritance to be squandered in some manner. If, as we said, benefic stars regard the ☉ <note>Sun</note> so positioned, only a few of the paternal resources will perish; the ☽ <note>Moon</note> will produce this same effect regarding mothers or maternal inheritances. Moreover, if the ☽ <note>Moon</note> is so positioned in a birth chart, holding either the 15th or 17th degree in a <term>tropical sign <note>The signs marking the solstices and equinoxes: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn.</note></term>, and malefic stars regard her with a square or opposite radiation, the maternal substance is squandered. But if the ☉ <note>Sun</note> and ♂ <note>Mars</note> are together in any pivot in a tropical sign, they cause paternal resources to be squandered. If a benefic star regards them so positioned, something of the paternal resources is preserved; and the ☽ <note>Moon</note> will perform this same thing similarly in a maternal birth chart when so positioned.

If this happens to the ☽ <note>Moon</note>, we say the mother dies first. But if, with these arranged as we said, ♂ <note>Mars</note> regards ♄ <note>Saturn</note> with a square radiation, the father will die a violent death <note>original: "biothanatus" - one who dies by violence or against nature</note>, perhaps by the order of a prince. For what we said regarding the ☽ <note>Moon</note> suffering this in a nighttime birth means the mother will similarly die; but then these evils grow stronger if, with things so arranged, the benefic stars are either in <term>dejected places <note>Cadent houses that do not aspect the Ascendant, often the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses.</note></term> or hidden under the rays of the ☉ <note>Sun</note>. ### THE NUMBER OF SIBLINGS BORN TO ANYONE CHAPTER XIII.

Calculate the distance from ♄ <note>Saturn</note> to ♃ <note>Jupiter</note>, and [add] the same amount from the <term>horoscopus <note>The Ascendant or 1st house.</note></term>; whichever sign the final number falls into indicates to you the number of brothers and sisters. If, however, <term>malefic <note>Harmful planets, usually Saturn or Mars.</note></term> stars aspect this place, the siblings will perish or become mortal enemies; if <term>benefic <note>Helpful planets, usually Jupiter or Venus.</note></term> stars, they will increase in number. But if ♄ <note>Saturn</note> is found <term>by degree <note>original: "partiliter" — meaning at the exact degree, rather than just in the same sign.</note></term> in the horoscopus, and those degrees belong to ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, all the siblings will die within the years of their youth. Others count from ☿ <note>Mercury</note> to the ☉ <note>Sun</note>, and the same amount from the horoscopus, and thus define the "place of siblings," using the same reasoning for the rest of the location; this method also has effectiveness in <term>apotelesmata <note>original: "apotelesmatis" — the Greek term for astrological predictions or outcomes.</note></term>.

### BIRTHS OR CHARTS OF INCESTUOUS PERSONS CHAPTER XIV.

In a man’s birth chart, count from ♄ <note>Saturn</note> to ♀ <note>Venus</note> if it is a daytime birth, and the same amount from the horoscopus. In a nighttime birth, do the opposite. This sign (as we have frequently said) shows you the "place of the wife." Again, calculate the place of siblings from ♄ <note>Saturn</note> to ♃ <note>Jupiter</note>, and the same from the horoscopus. If, therefore, the place of the spouse, thus calculated by degree, falls into the place of the siblings, they obtain their own sisters or near-kin as wives; you will find the same in the birth charts of women.

But if ♀ <note>Venus</note> and the <term>Lord of the Geniture <note>The planet that rules the entire birth chart.</note></term> are found together in the same sign, it decrees sisters or kin as wives. But if the place of the spouse, calculated by degree, is found in the signs of the mother or father (these also being gathered by degree), it decrees mothers, stepmothers, or nurses as wives. You will find the same in the birth charts of women, especially if ♂ <note>Mars</note>, ♀ <note>Venus</note>, or ☿ <note>Mercury</note> aspect these same places.

And since we have begun to speak of incestuous marriages, let us examine these further, setting others aside. If in a birth chart ♄ <note>Saturn</note> is found in the sign or <term>terms <note>Subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by specific planets.</note></term> of ♃ <note>Jupiter</note>, while ♀ <note>Venus</note> and ☿ <note>Mercury</note> are in the sign of ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, and ♂ <note>Mars</note> and the ☽ <note>Moon</note> aspect them so placed with a <term>square <note>A 90-degree aspect, often considered stressful or intense.</note></term> radiation, these people will have intercourse with either their mothers or stepmothers. If ☿ <note>Mercury</note> is joined to them, they will have intercourse with sons or daughters, or with stepchildren.

But if the ☽ <note>Moon</note> is found with the ☉ <note>Sun</note>, ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, and ♂ <note>Mars</note> in the house of ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, they will have intercourse secretly with a mother, stepmother, or father. If all these are found in the <term>seventh house <note>The house of marriage and partnerships.</note></term> from the horoscopus, the man will take his mother as a wife after the father’s death, or after the mother’s death, the daughter will do the same with the father. If ☿ <note>Mercury</note> is found with them, women take their sons as husbands, and men take their daughters as wives. But if the ☽ <note>Moon</note>, placed in the final degrees of ♋ <note>Cancer</note>, is moving toward ♃ <note>Jupiter</note>, or is in the house of ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, and ♀ <note>Venus</note> is similarly found in the house of ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, and ♄ <note>Saturn</note> in the house of ♀ <note>Venus</note>, this same thing is brought about.

If ♀ <note>Venus</note> is found with ♂ <note>Mars</note> in the sixth house from the horoscopus, it will make both men and women adulterers. But if they are placed in the house of ♄ <note>Saturn</note>, and joined with ♄ <note>Saturn</note> himself in the same sign by an exact partnership of degrees in the seventh house, in a woman's chart they make public prostitutes; in a man's birth, it is decreed that they either have prostitutes as wives, or they are joined in the desire of impure lust with <term>public "cinaedi" <note>original: "cinædis publicis" — a term for men who took a passive role in sexual acts, often associated with public entertainment or scandal.</note></term>, and they become <term>Socratic pederasts <note>original: "Soctatici pædicones" — a reference to the Platonic/Socratic tradition of older men loving younger men, though here used in a disparaging astrological sense regarding "active" same-sex desire.</note></term>.

### BIRTH CHARTS OF THE UNCHASTE, THE IMPURE, AND THE STERILE. CHAPTER XVI.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'M' featuring ornate floral and scrollwork patterns inside a square frame.</image-desc>

If ☿ <note>Mercury</note> and ♀ <note>Venus</note> are positioned together in the 19th degree of ♉ <note>Taurus</note>, they will make people who are impure with the mouth <note>original: "impuros ore" — a reference to oral sex, which was highly stigmatized in Roman culture.</note>. ->THE NUMBER OF WIVES AND HUSBANDS CHAPTER XVII.<-

In all nativities <note>original: "genituris" — birth charts.</note>, if $\Venus$ is found in double-bodied <note>original: "duplicibus" — also known as bicorporeal signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note> or tropical signs, and the lords of those signs in which she is placed are similarly positioned in double-bodied or tropical signs, they decree many wives for men and many husbands for women. If, however, $\Venus$ is positioned in neither tropical nor double-bodied signs, and the $\Moon$ <note>Moon</note> regards her in a similar condition, it decrees one wife for a man and one husband for a woman. But if $\Venus$ is placed in tropical or double-bodied signs and sees the $\Moon$, it decrees many wives for men and many husbands for women. In these same nativities, if $\Saturn$ <note>Saturn</note> is found with $\Venus$ in the same sign, and if $\Saturn$ has more degrees <note>original: "partes" — degrees of the 30-degree zodiac sign.</note>, he decrees one wife; if $\Venus$ has more, [he decrees many]. You will find this same rule in the nativities of women. If $\Venus$ is positioned in the setting <note>original: "occasu" — the 7th house or the West, representing marriage.</note>, she will grant a wife who has been defiled by others, or they will cohabit without marriage contracts <note>original: "tabulis matrimonialibus" — legal marriage documents.</note>. If $\Mars$ sees her, they will take wives known for adultery. If, however, $\Venus$ is so arranged in $\Taurus$ <note>Taurus</note> or $\Libra$ <note>Libra</note>, she will grant noble-born <note>original: "ingenuas" — free-born citizens of good standing.</note> wives, but in the other signs, ignoble ones. If $\Venus$ is found in the <term>Midheaven <note>original: "MC" or Medium Coeli; the highest point of the chart representing career and public status.</note></term> and the $\Moon$ regards her with a trine radiation <note>A 120-degree aspect, considered very harmonious.</note>, and she also has the testimony of the other stars, she decrees one wife. But if she is found in any other sign, count from $\Venus$ herself to that sign in which the degree of the spouse is found; however many signs there are from $\Venus$ to the sign of marriage, that many wives are decreed. You will find the same regarding husbands in feminine nativities. Some approve of this calculation, but to be honest, it is not at all approved by us.

->THE MUTUAL AFFECTION OF SPOUSES CHAPTER XVIII.<-

If the degree of the wife is found specifically <note>original: "partiliter" — by exact degree rather than just by sign.</note>—using the method we showed in the previous book—and if it is found in a sign of $\Jupiter$, the man will be separated from all the allurements of lust. If, however, it is in the house of $\Saturn$, it will make them lustful; but if $\Saturn$ sees this place, he makes the men stern toward their women. But if it is found in a sign of $\Mars$, and $\Mars$ or $\Jupiter$ regard this same place, or one of them is in the place and the other regards it, it will make men always love their wives with faithful affection. If this place is found in a sign of $\Mercury$ <note>Mercury</note>, and $\Mercury$ sees the place or is positioned there, it will make fickle lovers; the $\Sun$ <note>Sun</note> makes them noble <note>original: "regios" — literally 'kingly'.</note>, the $\Moon$ pleasing and lovable. If the $\Moon$ is found with $\Mars$ in the house of $\Saturn$, and $\Saturn$ regards them with a diametrical or square radiation, it makes men without wives, without children, and consumptive <note>original: "phthisicos" — suffering from a wasting disease like tuberculosis.</note>. ->THE TIMES OF BETROTHALS OR NUPTIALS CHAPTER XIX.<-

But if the lord of the sign is so placed that it does not regard the sign of the spouse by any radiation, but another star is positioned in that sign, marriage is decreed when the "first times" of that star are completed. If no star is positioned in that sign, a wife is decreed after the <term>anaphora <note>The rising or ascension of a sign or planet; the timing based on the movement of the heavens.</note></term> of that sign. But there is another more subtle method composed of exact degree calculations. Calculate the numerical substance of all the stars and make one sum of the total number; starting from the sign in which the degree of the spouse was found, divide this sum among the other signs, giving thirty degrees to each. Into whichever sign the final number falls, when $\Jupiter$ reaches that sign, then the marriage is decreed. ### THE NATIVITIES OF THOSE WHO KILL THEIR OWN WIVES CHAPTER XX.

IF $\Venus$ <note>Venus</note> is found in the house of $\Mars$ <note>Mars</note> and in his bounds <note>original: "finibus" — the "terms" or specific degrees within a sign ruled by a planet.</note>, and $\Mars$ is placed in the house of $\Venus$ or her bounds, and he regards the $\Moon$ <note>Moon</note>—placed in her own signs or bounds and full of light—with a diametrical radiation <note>An opposition aspect of 180 degrees.</note>, the husbands will kill their own wives with their own hands. If, however, in the nativity of a woman, $\Mars$ is found in the Midheaven <note>The 10th house or highest point of the chart.</note> placed in his own house or degrees, and he regards $\Venus$ with a diametrical radiation, the husbands will perish, having been killed by their wives. But the testimony of $\Jupiter$ <note>Jupiter</note> mitigates all these things and turns them toward a better outcome.

### THE NATIVITIES OF THOSE LACKING LITERACY CHAPTER XXI.
IF the $\Sun$ and $\Mercury$ are positioned together so that, being placed in one sign, they are joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, and the $\Moon$ does not regard them with any radiation, or certainly if $\Mercury$ is not established in the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopo" — the 1st house.</note>, they will produce people who are illiterate and most unrefined.

### THE NATIVITIES OF GLADIATORS OR ATHLETES CHAPTER XXII.

IF $\Jupiter$ is positioned in the bounds of $\Mars$, in whatever sign he may be, and $\Mars$ is in the bounds of $\Jupiter$, and if they are positioned in the angles <note>original: "cardinibus" — the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> and regard each other by a square <note>90 degree</note> or diametrical radiation, and the birth is by day, with the $\Sun$ in places dejected from the Ascendant <note>original: "deiectis" — the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, considered weak.</note>—or similarly the $\Moon$ in a nocturnal nativity—famous gladiators will be born. If $\Mercury$ is found in the bounds of $\Jupiter$ in whatever sign he may be, and $\Jupiter$ is similarly in the bounds of $\Mars$, and $\Venus$ regards both of them by any radiation, athletes will be born. If these planets are positioned in the angles, they will be athletes who are victors in every clash of the games. If, however, the testimony of $\Venus$ and $\Mars$ is present, wrestlers <note>original: "palęstritæ"</note> or masters of athletes will be born, but such as would never commit themselves to actual contests. If $\Mars$ is established in the bounds of $\Venus$, and $\Venus$ in turn in the bounds of $\Mars$, and the testimony of $\Mercury$ and the $\Moon$ is brought together by any fellowship of radiation, and $\Venus$ alone provides testimony, it will produce runners. But these effects grow stronger if the Lot of Fortune and the Place of Activity <note>Specific points in a chart calculated for success and career.</note> are found in an angle and are joined to the preceding fellowship of the stars.

### THE NATIVITIES OF LAWYERS OR ORATORS CHAPTER XXIII.
IF $\Mercury$ is found in his own bounds or the bounds of $\Mars$, and is established in dejected places, and $\Mars$—positioned in the house or bounds of $\Mercury$—regards him with any radiation, it will produce lawyers and orators. If, however, $\Mercury$ is positioned as we have said in a daytime nativity, but is not in dejected places, and $\Mars$—positioned in the angles and in those parts we mentioned—regards him with a favorable radiation, he will produce great and famous orators.

### THE NATIVITIES OF PODALYRIAN PHYSICIANS CHAPTER XXIIII.
<note>Podalyrian refers to Podalirius, a mythical Greek physician and son of Asclepius.</note>

If they have exchanged their bounds, so that $\Mars$ is in the bounds of $\Venus$ and $\Venus$ in the bounds of $\Mars$, and a favorable testimony from $\Jupiter$ is added to them, they will be ingenious physicians. If, however, $\Jupiter$ is not joined to them, they will be cooks.

But you shall define all these things, as we have frequently said, according to the variety of the signs.

To know whether they will persevere in their decreed crafts, I will show you by a brief reasoning: see in which sign **Mercury** is placed, and inquire after the lord of that sign, and ask whether he himself is well-situated. For if he is well-situated, the person will remain in those crafts, and the greatest profits will follow from them. But if he is poorly placed, they will labor in their duties without the fruit of their craft, and, exhausted by the toil, they will frequently abandon those same arts.

### THE FATAL NATIVITIES OF THE DAMNED CHAPTER XXVI.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial letter S with scrolling foliage and vine patterns.</image-desc>

IF the place of necessity <note>The "Lot of Necessity," an astrological point associated with constraints, legal battles, and unavoidable fate.</note> is found in the house of **Mercury**, the **Moon** <note>☽</note> in the house of **Saturn** or **Mars**, and **Mercury** regards **Mars** or **Saturn** in a square or diametrical radiation <note>A 90-degree or 180-degree aspect, usually considered difficult.</note>, or if they are situated with it in any pivot <note>original: "cardine" — one of the four main angles of the chart.</note>, or in the rising <note>anaphoris</note> or falling <note>epicataphoris</note> houses of the pivots, or in the horoscope, or in the place of fortune, or in the place of necessity—they will cause the person to be condemned in any manner. 

If indeed the place of necessity is found in the place of **Mercury**, or in the house of the **Moon**, or in the house of **Mars** or **Saturn**, and is positioned exactly <note>original: "partiliter" — to the specific degree.</note> in some pivot of the nativity, and any of those stars we mentioned is found in the rising or falling houses, it will cause condemnation in a similar way. These condemnations are to the mines, public works, exile, or the arena <note>original: "ludi" — literally "the games," referring to being sentenced to the gladiatorial schools.</note>. 

But if the place of necessity is found in the houses of those stars we mentioned, and some of them are in the rising or falling houses while others are in the pivots, they will cause the crime of a just condemnation to be imposed. If, however—with all these arranged as we have said—**Jupiter** is situated in the Midheaven <note>MC - the highest point of the chart.</note> and meets the malevolent stars with a favorable radiation, he will mitigate the dangers of all condemnations. For then, after a certain space of time, by the judgment of the Emperor, they will be liberated from the aforesaid condemnations and restored both to their dignities and their homeland. 

But if **Jupiter**'s testimony is denied to all these, it will cause those justly condemned to be subjected to the punishment of severe retribution. If the lord of the sign in which the place of necessity was found is situated in the house of **Mars**, **Saturn**, or **Mercury**, and is in the horoscope or placed in that same place of necessity, it will bring about condemnation. But if the place of necessity itself and its own lord are situated in the aforesaid places, it will similarly cause one to be condemned. 

If, however, the place of necessity is found in the house of **Mercury**, and **Venus** is situated in any pivot, while **Mars** and **Saturn** are in the rising or falling houses of the pivots, they will bring about condemnation. If, with all these things arranged as we have said, the **Moon** is found either in the pivots or in the rising houses of the pivots, those condemned will die a violent death <note>original: "biothanata morte" — a death that is unnatural, premature, or forced.</note>. 

If the place of necessity is similarly found in the house of **Mercury**, and **Mars** and **Venus** are placed in the house of **Saturn** or **Mars**, or found in the rising or falling houses of the pivots, with **Mars** and **Saturn** situated exactly in the pivots and **Jupiter** being estranged from them, a sentence of just condemnation will be delivered with the consent of all. If the place of necessity falls into the place of fortune, or if the lord of the place of fortune is found in the place of necessity, or the lord of necessity in the place of fortune, it will cause a sentence of just condemnation to be pronounced against the accused.

# SEVENTH BOOK

### VARIOUS MORTAL EXITS AND THE UNCERTAIN END OF LIFE. CHAPTER XXVII.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap 'S' featuring ornate scrolling foliage within a square frame.</image-desc>

If the **Sun** <note>☉</note> is found in watery signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>, and in that same sign or place **Mars** <note>♂</note> is positioned exactly with the **Moon** <note>☽</note>, or if it is placed together with the **Moon** in the eleventh or sixth house from the horoscope <note>The Ascendant</note>, with **Saturn** <note>♄</note> regarding the horoscope by an opposite aspect <note>original: "per diamettrum" — an aspect of 180 degrees</note>, the native will be <term>biothanati</term> <note>From the Greek "biothanatos," referring to someone who dies a violent, unnatural, or premature death.</note>; for they will either perish by hanging from a noose or meet their final destruction by drowning in water. 

If the **Moon** is found in the eighth house from the horoscope, joined in exact partnership with **Saturn**, and no benevolent star <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> is positioned at a cardo <note>One of the four "pivots" or "angles" of the chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note>, death will be caused by an excessive loss of blood. But if, with these planets so arranged, a benevolent star is found in another cardo, those who were despaired of will recover through medical remedies. 

If the **Moon** is found with **Mars** in the seventh house from the horoscope, it will cause death by <term>hemorrhoids</term> <note>In ancient medical-astrology, this often referred generally to severe internal or external bleeding/ruptures.</note>. Generally, however, **Saturn** in a nocturnal birth, or **Mars** in a diurnal birth, when positioned in the seventh house from the horoscope, causes eruptions of blood from hemorrhoids. But if the <term>Lot of Fortune</term> <note>A mathematical point calculated from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant representing luck and physical fate.</note> is found in their signs in the seventh house from the horoscope, they will suffer the defects of ill health by being cut with iron <note>Ancient terminology for surgery.</note>. If, with these factors so arranged (as we have said), a benevolent star provides a favorable testimony through its radiation, they will be freed from that illness after being cut with iron. 

However, if both—that is, **Saturn** and **Mars**—are positioned in the seventh house from the horoscope, and the horoscope itself or the Lot of Fortune is placed in those signs we mentioned (that is, of **Mars** or **Saturn**), or if one of them is placed in the seventh house and the other regards it by a square or opposite radiation, they will perish after being cut by physicians. 

If the **Moon** is found in the setting <note>The 7th house, where the sun sets.</note>, and **Mercury** <note>☿</note> and **Mars** are joined to her in exact partnership and positioned in the **Midheaven** <note>The 10th house, the highest point of the chart.</note>, they will produce murderers and patricides <note>Those who kill their fathers.</note>, or those who, by a wicked instinct of madness, are stained with the blood of a brother; but after being struck by the infamy of such crimes and made public through hatred and threatening accusations, the stars will cause them to perish by the severe punishments of judges. 

If the **Moon** and **Mars** are positioned in the ninth house from the horoscope, and the **Sun** and **Mercury** are in the third, they produce sacrilegious people and temple-robbers; but those who, because of this crime, are punished by the severe sentence of a judge. If, however, the **Sun** with **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** is positioned in the eleventh house from the horoscope, and the **Moon** is placed in the third house without the testimony of **Jupiter** <note>♃</note>, they will die as <term>biothanati</term> because of the aforementioned crimes. 

If the **Sun** is found in the horoscope, and **Mars** and **Saturn**, joined by equal degrees, are positioned in the twelfth house from the horoscope, and they regard the **Moon** (placed in the sixth house) with an opposite radiation, they will make the natives violent-dying slaves. 

If the horoscope is found in a sign of **Saturn** or **Mars**, and the Lot of Fortune is positioned exactly in the horoscope, and **Mercury** is joined with it in an equal partnership of degrees, while **Saturn** and **Mars** are positioned in the seventh house from the horoscope, they will produce epileptics, yet ones who die a violent death. 

If the **Moon** is placed exactly in the **Midheaven**, and **Mars** is placed exactly in the horoscope, while **Saturn** is positioned in the <term>anaphora</term> <note>A "rising" or "succedent" house that follows after a cardinal angle.</note> of the **Moon**, it will cause a violent death. Furthermore, if **Mars** and **Saturn** regard each other by a square radiation, and **Mars** is positioned in any cardo, and one of them sees the **Moon** by either a square or opposite radiation, or is found with her, it will cause a violent death. But if the **Moon** with **Mars** is found in the eighth house, and the **Sun** in the seventh, while **Saturn** is in the Midheaven or any other cardo, it will cause a violent death. 

If **Mars** and **Saturn** are found in the eleventh house, or if one of them is placed in that house while the other is positioned with the **Moon** or regards her with a square radiation, and **Mercury** or **Venus** <note>♀</note> is joined by any radiation, it will cause the insane, epileptics, and those who die violently. This will be even worse if **Mars** is found in the eleventh house and **Saturn** in the fourth. 

If the **Sun** is discovered in the eighth house, and the **Moon** is placed exactly in the Midheaven, and the horoscope or the Lot of Fortune is in a sign of the **Sun** or the **Moon**, it will produce the insane and those who die a violent death. 

If the <term>Lot of Desire</term> <note>A mathematical point similar to the Lot of Fortune, associated with passion and eros.</note>, **Mars**, and **Saturn** are joined by degree, and this place is positioned in any cardo of the birth, and **Venus** regards those we mentioned by any radiation, they will produce deaths by hemorrhoids. If they see the **Moon**, they will make them <term>lunatics</term> <note>Literally "moon-struck"; referring to those with mental illness or epilepsy believed to be affected by the moon's cycles.</note>. If they see **Mercury**, they will cause those caught in falsehoods or counterfeit money to perish by a violent death. But if **Jupiter** regards all these as they are so positioned, they are delivered from all these dangers.

# BOOK SEVEN

From their rising <note>original: "anaphora" — a succedent house, specifically the house following a cardo</note>, they will likewise cause those afflicted in the eyes to die violent deaths <note>original: "biothariatos interfire," likely a corruption of "biothanatos interire"</note>. But if the **Moon** <note>☽</note> is found with **Mars** <note>♂</note>, and **Saturn** <note>♄</note> is positioned with the **Sun** <note>☉</note> in the Midheaven <note>original: "MC" or Medium Coeli, the 10th house</note>, this will cause spasms, or epilepsies, or insanities, or a departure by violent death. 

If indeed the **Moon** and **Sun** are found in the cardines <note>the four "pivots" or angles of the chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, and **Mars** and **Saturn** exist in their own houses, or are positioned in other cardines, they cause the natives to die violent deaths <term>biothanatos</term>. 

If **Mars** or **Saturn** are found in the Place of Fortune, and a conjunction <note>original: "synodus"</note> occurs in the fifth or eleventh house from the horoscope <note>the Ascendant</note>, they will bring about a violent death. 

If **Mars** with the **Moon** are in the twelfth house from the horoscope, and **Saturn** or the **Sun** are in its rising <note>original: "anaphora"</note>—that is, in the second house from the horoscope—they cause the native to die a violent death; frequently, they are even cut at the very moment of birth and brought forth bit by bit from the mother's vitals, especially if they are found in the same degrees. 

If the **Moon** is found in the Midheaven, and some malevolent star is positioned in any cardo, and another [malefic] regards the **Moon** by an opposite aspect <note>original: "diametra radiatione"</note>, or if it similarly approaches the horoscope, or if it is found in the fifth or eleventh house from the horoscope, it will cause violent deaths; for those born thus either throw themselves down from heights <note>original: "praecipitant"</note> or lay hands upon themselves, yet the diversity of the deaths is fulfilled according to the nature of the zodiac sign. 

If the **Moon** is found in the eighth house from the horoscope, and **Mars** is placed in his own house and positioned exactly in the horoscope, and **Venus** <note>♀</note> or the **Sun** are joined to him in equal or nearby degrees, and the **Moon** receives a conjunction exactly with either **Mars** or **Saturn**, the natives will die torn apart by the habits of wild beasts. 

If the **Moon**, diminished in its light, is found in the eighth house from the horoscope, it will cause violent deaths, but of such a kind where they meet a wretched end by drowning while naked. 

If the **Moon** is found in the setting <note>the 7th house</note>, and **Saturn** in the sixth house from the horoscope, and the Place of Fortune is located in the house of **Saturn** or the **Moon**, it will cause the natives to die of dysentery. 

If the **Moon** is found in the horoscope, and **Saturn** with **Mercury** <note>☿</note> is positioned in the seventh house from the horoscope, they will make the natives foolish, sluggish, dull-witted, and prone to falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note>. But if, with these so ordered, **Mars** is found in any cardo, he will render them dull-witted and epileptic, but also subject to violent death. 

If **Saturn** is found in the third or ninth house from the horoscope, and **Mars** regards him with a square aspect <note>original: "quadrata radiatione"</note>, he will make them leaders of great affairs or actions, but he will dissipate whatever marriage is gathered by them; they will also have the greatest illnesses, and being stationed in foreign places, they will be bound by many evils; he even weakens the parents of some, or certainly causes them to die violent deaths. 

But if **Mars** is found with one of them, and the **Moon** is either with them or regards them by a square or opposite aspect, it will make them sacrilegious, plunderers of temples, leaders of bandits, murderers, and dying by an evil death. 

If the **Sun**, **Saturn**, and **Mercury** are found in the Midheaven, they will cause accusations and dangers to be brought in from hidden or forged letters, or from counterfeit money. But if **Mars** regards them with a square or opposite aspect, or is found with them, he will make them bandits and murderers, yet also exiles and fugitives. If, however, with these so ordered, **Jupiter** <note>♃</note> is found in another cardo, after some time they will be freed from these calamities and transferred to the grace of great power. 

If, however, with all these so positioned, the **Moon** is found either in some cardo, or in the succedent <note>anaphoris</note> or cadent <note>epicataphoris</note> houses, after all this, they will die by a violent death. 

If **Mercury** and **Saturn** are positioned in the sixth or twelfth house from the horoscope, they will be set over ineffective and wretched accounts, but this will also make them always slow and languid in all things. If indeed **Jupiter** regards these with a square or opposite aspect, it makes them criminals, bandits, perjurers, informers, and traitors of their own people; some are indeed handed over to dangers or prisons because of slaves or condemned men, especially if **Mars** regards the **Moon** by any aspect. 

If **Saturn** is found in the eighth house from the horoscope, or in the second house <note>the "anaphora" of the horoscope</note>, and the **Moon** is positioned in the succedent or cadent houses, and **Mars** is found in the seventh house from the horoscope, he will make them removed from all care for religions. But if, with these so ordered, **Saturn** and the **Moon** are found in square or opposite places to them, they will make them plunderers of temples, and those who, because of this, are punished by a public death. 

But if, with these so ordered, **Jupiter** and **Venus** are found with them, they will make them priests, prophets, and temple wardens <term>neocoros</term> <note>From the Greek "neokoros," an official in charge of a temple and its contents.</note>, but nonetheless dying a violent death. 

If the **Moon** with **Mars** is found in the setting <note>the 7th house</note>, such that **Mars** precedes in degrees, and **Saturn** and **Mercury** are positioned together in the Midheaven, they will cause violent deaths. But the death is also recognized according to the nature of the signs. For if positioned in tropical or watery signs, they either kill by dropsy <note>edema/fluid retention</note> or cause them to be submerged in waves or rivers. In double <note>mutable</note> or solid <note>fixed</note> signs, however, positioned as we have said, they cause them to be epileptic but dying a violent death.

## -> YOUNGER, THE SICILIAN, OF SENATORIAL RANK [[notes: "V.C." in the original stands for "Vir Clarissimus," a formal title for a member of the Roman senatorial order]], TO MAUORTIUS LOL- <-
