#### -> PREFACE. <-

[[insert: Large decorative woodcut initial **N** containing a landscape/mythological scene]] **N**OTHING else, while we are in this brevity of life, must be worked upon by us, Mauortius our glory, except that—the stain of the earthly body having been purged, and all vices (if it can be done) or at least most of them having been cut away—we might return the incorrupt divinity of the soul, polluted by no contagion of crimes, to God our creator. We must not, unmindful of the divine craftsmanship, lose the soul as if it were cast down a precipice, entangled in the vicious snares of lusts. For this is what the earthly body works toward every single day: that it might always bind its own divine spirit—preoccupied by the depraved pleasures of desires and deceived by flattering solicitation—to its own fleeting fragility, so that the soul, submerged and sunk down, can never find the beginnings of its own origin, but instead, cast forever into darkness and filth, it might blush at the origin of its own majesty with certain tremblings of concealment [[notes: This reflects the Neoplatonic belief that the soul feels "shame" when it forgets its divine origin and becomes too focused on the physical world]]. For we ought to think of nothing earthly, especially since we know that God our maker, by the moderation of divine craftsmanship, made us in such a way that the form of an upright body—set apart from every lowly dejection—should see nothing else first, once the sharp sight of the eyes is opened, except the [[notes: Sun]] and [[notes: Moon]], the stars, and the most beautiful and immortal domicile of all these: the world itself. For nature composed other living creatures in such a way that, sunk down toward the earth and cast forth by a certain fleeting lowliness of this world, they might cling to earthly dealings with both soul and body. But us, He perfected by a certain great moderation of necessity, so that the fragility of the body might claim one thing for itself in us, and the divinity of the immortal soul another; namely, that the body, which we seem to have in common with the beasts, might be subject to the command of the soul’s divinity. Considering therefore the beginnings of our origin, and our soul being strengthened by the protection of its own majesty, we ought so to conduct ourselves that the soul, summoned by the authority of its own name, might always think and do something worthy of its author. Thus, being so instructed and formed, it might find the right and incorrupt path of immortality when it is about to return to its origin, and not, with wandering steps and sliding, trembling footprints, be dissolved into the vices of earthly fragility by eternal errors. Look therefore, Mauortius, our glory, with the eyes of a parent [[notes: An affectionate term for a mentor or patron]]; let your soul always gaze upon the heaven and that most beautiful fabric of divine work. For then our mind, shaped by the recollection of its own majesty, is freed from the depraved allurements of bodies, and having stripped off the inconveniences of mortality, it strives with a hurried step toward its author, seeking nothing else but divine matters through every moment of the hours, with a sagacious and ever-watchful inquiry. These teachings will therefore give us whatever small notion of divine science they can, and will lead us to the secrets of our origin; for by always being occupied in divine disputations, and joining our soul to the celestial powers, and initiating it into divine ceremonies [[notes: Firmicus uses the language of mystery religions to describe the study of astrology]], we are separated from the desires of all depraved cravings. This greatly accomplishes the goal that—having despised all things which in human affairs are thought to be either bad or prosperous—we might return our soul, composed of natural virtue and authority, incorrupt and unimpaired to its origin. For when we have learned the inconveniences of birth, the fear of imminent evils is removed by this: that we know they are

Nor do we dread the denounced dangers of evils, if our mind has strengthened itself to receive these things through the remembrance of its own majesty [[notes: "Majesty" here refers to the divine or cosmic origin of the human soul, a common Stoic and Neoplatonic theme]]. Neither are we seized by the advantages of fortune, nor lifted up by the marks of high rank, since we know that all of this was promised to us by the proclamation of the decree [[notes: The "decree" refers to Fate or the immutable laws of the stars]]. Thus we are able to remain always composed with steady reason, neither crushed by misfortunes nor raised up by the joy of prosperity. Therefore, that which I believe remains for these books, I shall take care to explain; for I have reserved another time for the explanation of the *myriogenesis* [[notes: A complex astrological theory involving the specific influences of each of the 10,000 subdivisions of the zodiac]]. Now, however, at the beginning of this book, we shall set forth which signs "see" each other, for all of this pertains to the interpretation of the *sphæra barbarica* [[notes: The "Barbaric Sphere" refers to non-Greek astronomical traditions, such as Egyptian or Babylonian star charts, often featuring extra-zodiacal constellations]]. We shall also state the measurements of all the parts, and we shall add which parts are found in the bodies of the signs, and also what the ninetieth part effects, which is called *ἐννενηκοντάμερος* [[notes: Greek: *ennēnekontameros*]] by the Greeks, so that with all these things explained, we may more easily master the *sphæra barbarica* and perceive the power of the effective license of the bright stars.

->### *Εννενηκοντάμερος, OR THE NINETIETH PART CH. I*<-

# P
Rimarily, therefore, I shall dispute concerning the ninetieth part, which is called *ἐννενηκοντάμερος* by the Greeks. This matter is both unknown to most and seems to have been treated lightly by the few who have; for even Petosiris [[notes: A legendary Egyptian priest and sage, often cited as a foundational authority in Hellenistic astrology]] wished (as it seems to me) to hide this treatise out of envious spite. For in all nativities [[notes: Latin *genituris*, referring to the birth chart]], the ninetieth part must be sought out with wise inquiry, for from it is gathered the end of life, death, misfortunes, dangers, prosperity, and the entire substance of the nativity. Proceeding from the horoscopos [[notes: The Ascendant, or the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], seek the ninetieth part through the other signs, and when you have found it, foresee in which sign it sits—that is, whether it is found in the domicile of a benevolent or malevolent star. See also how the lord of that sign is positioned in the nativity. Look carefully also to what extent benevolent stars "regard" [[notes: "Regarding" or "aspecting" refers to the geometric angles stars make with one another]] that part; for each star looking upon this part fulfills everything according to its own nature. For malevolent stars [[notes: Usually Saturn and Mars]], if they are alone, will bring ruin; if they are benevolent [[notes: Usually Jupiter and Venus]], they decree the greatest marks of prosperity; but if benevolent and malevolent are there together, that which was decreed by each is tempered. Seek also in whose lordship and power the part itself lies—that is, in whose "terms" [[notes: *Fines*, or specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets]]—and similarly where the lord of that part is positioned. Thus you will fulfill all things according to the nature of the star and the power of the place, for all things, both bad and prosperous, fulfill the nature of the sign. You should seek this same thing similarly from the ☽ [[notes: Moon symbol]] and from the progression from that part in which the ☽ was found, so that you may have the 90th part. You should also gather all things in that part by similar reasoning: what kind of sign it is, what kind of part, who is the lord of the sign and the part, in what place the lords are, and in which signs they are located, and by what radiation both benevolent and malevolent stars regard that part. And if the ☽ is waxing, see to what extent ♂ [[notes: Mars symbol]] regards this; and if she is waning, likewise. For all things fulfill according to the power of their nature, whether they regard the part with the threatening radiation of a malevolent star, or support it with the prosperous testimony of a benevolent one. For thus you will find the departure of death, thus the order of life, and finally the whole substance of the human nativity.

# THE THEORY OF SIGNS THAT SEE AND HEAR EACH OTHER. CHAP. II.

**N**ow I shall briefly explain which stars [[notes: "Stars" (stellae) here refers to the zodiac signs]] see others, and which hear them. Aries (♈︎) does not see Leo (♌︎), but hears him; Leo, however, sees Aries, but does not hear him. Aries both sees and hears Cancer (♋︎) equally, but Cancer does not see Aries, though he hears him. Taurus (♉︎) and Leo both see and hear each other, and similarly Leo treats Taurus. Gemini (♊︎) and Virgo (♍︎) see and hear each other faintly; Virgo sees Gemini faintly, but hears him most fully. Cancer and Libra (♎︎) both see and hear each other equally. Libra and Scorpio (♏︎) neither see nor hear each other, but Scorpio both hears and sees Leo equally. Scorpio looks at Sagittarius (♐︎) from an angle [[notes: "ex obliquo," likely referring to a non-major aspect]], but does not willingly hear him; Sagittarius both hears and sees Virgo equally. Libra and Scorpio both hear and see each other, and Libra is both heard and seen by Saturn (♄) [[notes: In this context, Saturn (♄) is often used as a shorthand for the signs he rules, particularly Capricorn or Aquarius]]. Aquarius (♒︎) does not see Scorpio, but hears him; in the same way, Scorpio does not see Leo or Aquarius, but hears them. Sagittarius and Pisces (♓︎) neither see nor hear each other. But Pisces and Sagittarius both see and hear each other equally [[notes: The text here appears to contradict itself or describe a specific asymmetrical relationship common in ancient "antiscia" or "reflection" theories]]. Pisces do not see Gemini, but they do hear them. Saturn and Aries neither hear nor see each other. Aquarius and Taurus look at each other from an angle and hear each other. Gemini and Libra both see and hear each other; similarly, Libra both hears and sees Gemini. Sagittarius and Leo both see and hear each other. Virgo indeed looks at Capricorn (♑︎), but does not hear him. Capricorn sees Aquarius, but is not herself seen by Aquarius; however, they hear each other mutually and equally. Scorpio indeed sees Pisces but does not hear them; similarly, Pisces see Scorpio but do not hear them. Sagittarius and Aries are so placed that they can neither see nor hear each other. Saturn and Taurus can neither hear nor see each other. Aquarius and Gemini indeed see each other, but are entirely separated in hearing. Pisces and Cancer do not indeed see each other, but they do hear. We have discussed these secrets of the matter so that you might receive the complete forms of the arrangement and know how the signs are disposed in the zodiac circle; for these twelve signs are not placed in a fixed order or degree, nor are they positioned so that those rising in a later place always look upon the preceding or following signs. For I have published this treatise, excerpted from the **books of Abraham** [[notes: Likely referring to Abraham Ibn Ezra, a 12th-century scholar whose astrological works were highly influential in the Renaissance]], to show you this not through mere arguments, but through the reality itself, so that our discourse might make known to you through clear interpretations those things which we have spoken.

♐︎ The first and second parts are located in the head; the three following in order are in the face; the two that follow the preceding parts are placed in the mouth of ♐︎ [[notes: Sagittarius, the Archer]]; the three following are in the neck; the two succeeding in the left hand; three others in the bow; two in the front feet; three in the back; and two in the equine belly [[notes: Sagittarius is depicted as a centaur, hence the 'equine' reference]]. In the hind feet, reaching down to the hooves, three follow; the 26th and 27th are located in the nature of ♐︎; the two following are placed in the right hand; and the 30th alone is located in the tail.

♑︎ The first and second parts are located in the horns; the three following are in the head; the sixth and seventh are placed in the face; and the three following in order are established in the mouth. Indeed, in these parts which are in the mouth of ♑︎ [[notes: Capricorn, the Sea-Goat]], if anyone should have the ☽ [[notes: Moon]] there, even if it is adorned by the testimonies of benevolent stars, it will nonetheless make men of impure speech and defiled by the stain of feminine lusts. Women, too, if they have the Moon in these parts of ♑︎, will all be possessed by the vice of unchaste desire. The eleventh is located in the heart of ♑︎; the twelfth and thirteenth in the neck; the two following in the shoulder blades; the three succeeding in the right hand; the two following these in the back; the three following in the belly; the four succeeding on each side; and the three final parts are located in the tail, reaching to the very end of the fin of ♑︎.

♒︎ The first and second parts are placed in the head; the three following in the face; the sixth and seventh in the back; the three following in order are located in the chest; the eleventh and twelfth in the right hand; the three following in the ♒︎ [[notes: Aquarius, the Water-Bearer]] river [[notes: The stream of water pouring from the urn]]; the 16th and 17th in the left hand; the two following in the sides; another two in the belly; the three succeeding ones extend to the very ends of the feet; another three in the kidneys; and the final three are located in the ♒︎ pitcher [[notes: The Latin 'cantaro' refers to the water jar or urn]].

♓︎, of which one fish turns toward the South and the other toward the North: the first and second parts are located in the mouth of the Southern ♓︎ [[notes: Pisces, the Fishes]]; the third, fourth, and fifth in the head of the same ♓︎; two in the jaws; the three following in order are placed in the neck; the eleventh and twelfth are found in the furthest spine; the three following in order are received by the back of the same ♓︎; and we find the sixteenth, seventeenth, and eighteenth in the cord of ♓︎ [[notes: The 'linum' is the cord or ribbon connecting the two fish]]. In that ♓︎ which turns toward the North, the nineteenth and twentieth are placed in the head; the twenty-first and twenty-second in the mouth; the three following in the chest; and the three following in the neck. In the tail, the two newest are located. But the three final parts of ♓︎, which are between the ☊ [[notes: The Dragon's Tail, or South Node]] and ♓︎, are always clouded by a dark mist; for this reason, if anyone has either the ☉ [[notes: Sun]] or ☽ [[notes: Moon]] in these parts without the testimony of benevolent stars, they will be oppressed either by perpetual blindness or by wretched debilities of the body. From this division of the parts, therefore, when you begin to seek the location of vices and health, you will be able to find all this most clearly and easily. For that divine Necepso [[notes: Necepso was a legendary Egyptian Pharaoh to whom early astrological works were attributed]], so that he might find remedies for health, explained this topic most diligently in clear treatises, as far as the divine genius of such a great man was able; I will take care to explain the interpretation of this book to you at another time, Mavortius [[notes: Lollianus Mavortius, the high-ranking Roman official to whom this work is dedicated]], our glory.

One part of a sign, therefore, has twenty-one thousand and four hundred stadia [[notes: A 'stadium' was an ancient unit of distance, roughly 185 meters or 600 feet]]; if you compute this number through thirty parts together, you will know from that calculation that the space of one sign has six hundred and forty-two thousand stadia.

-> THE BOOK <-

-> ### THE FIRST PREDICTIONS OF THE BARBARIAN SPHERE ### <-
-> ### CHAPTER V ### <-

[[notes: The "Barbarian Sphere" refers to a tradition of constellations and astrological degrees thought to originate from non-Greek sources, such as the Egyptians or Babylonians.]]

**A**ccept now, Mavortius—our great honor—the most complete teaching of this work, which was unknown to many Greeks and nearly all Romans, and toward which our own genius has aspired until this very day. For even those divine men and high priests of the most holy religion, Petosiris and Necepso [[notes: Legendary figures traditionally credited with the invention of Hellenistic astrology; Necepso was a mythical Egyptian pharaoh and Petosiris his priest]], one of whom held the rudders of the empire, were unable to discover what we are about to publish, even though they explained everything pertaining to the discipline of this art with most diligent and true interpretations. But lest a long-winded speech extend our orderly arrangement, I will briefly set forth for you the decrees of the promised work.

Twelve signs occupy the zodiacal circle, as we said in the book of instruction. Along the sides of these signs, other stars are attached, but these never desert their assigned places with an erratic course; instead, possessing the spaces handed down to them, they are turned with an unchangeable motion as the world runs its course. These stars, located in the neighboring regions of the signs, rise with the twelve signs and set with them, always preserving the unchanged order of their course. Antiquity applied the names of ancient fables to these stars. Aratus [[notes: A Greek poet famous for the *Phaenomena*, a didactic poem about the stars]], a most eloquent poet, followed the number of these constellations in Greek, while in Latin, Caesar [[notes: Referring to Germanicus Caesar, who translated Aratus]] and that glory of eloquence, Tullius [[notes: Marcus Tullius Cicero]], did the same; however, they published only their names and risings, but not the authority of their *apotelesmata* [[notes: From the Greek *apotelesma*, meaning the "effects" or "outcomes" of the stars; essentially, astrological predictions]]. Thus, it seems to me that they brought forth the study of skillful speech not out of any knowledge of astrology, but rather carried away by poetic license. We, however, having looked into the reasoning behind all the *apotelesmata*, have found that these stars also claim much for themselves in the births of men. Therefore, so that we may explain what we promise, we shall designate both the places and the names of the stars, so that the whole truth of the *apotelesmata* may be gathered: which stars decide the fate if, being positioned in the morning rising, they hold the ascendant or the setting.

-> ### THE BRIGHT CONSTELLATIONS RISING AND SETTING ### <-
-> ### WITH ARIES [[notes: Represented by the symbol Y]] CHAPTER VI ### <-

**I**N the tenth degree of Aries [[notes: The symbol Y is used throughout as shorthand for Aries, the Ram]], the Ship [[notes: The constellation Argo Navis]] rises. If anyone is born when this part is rising—that is, if the birth breaks forth at its rising—he will be a pilot, a shipmaster, or a boat-builder, and one who desires to involve the entire span of his life in maritime affairs or duties.

On the left side of Aries, specifically in the tenth degree, Orion rises. Therefore, if Orion is exactly in the ascendant, he will make men conspicuous for the swift mobility of their bodies, and whose minds, involved in various anxieties, always seethe with wide-awake thinking. These men often change their residences, houses, and seats, and will run through everyone’s thresholds with morning *greetings.
[[margin: Perhaps *dances*.]] [[notes: The translator notes a possible correction from *salutationibus* (greetings) to *saltationibus* (dances), suggesting these people are socially hyperactive or literally performers.]]

In the fifteenth degree of Aries, toward the north, the Charioteer [[notes: The constellation Auriga]] rises. He who is born at the rising of this star will be either a charioteer, a tamer of horses, or one who leaps across four-horse teams, or who, standing on the back of horses, supports himself with wonderful balance, and especially one who, riding a horse, practices military maneuvers. At the rising of this star, Salmoneus and Bellerophon [[notes: Heroes of Greek mythology associated with chariots and horsemanship]] are said by ancient authors to have been born.

In the twentieth degree of Aries, toward the north, the Kid [[notes: *Hoedus*, part of the constellation Auriga]] rises, which the Charioteer carries. Whoever is born under this star promises one thing on the surface but hides another thing secretly in their character. For they have an austere face, a long beard, and a stubborn brow, so that they seem to imitate the lifestyle of Cato [[notes: Cato the Younger, famous for his rigid Stoic morality]] entirely; but they lie about all of this with a fake display of emotion. For they are by nature petulant, always lewd in their desires, and most lustfully involved in pleasures, and they always seethe secretly with the enticements of love. They will also be separated from every duty of virtue, being timid, weak, and those who shudder at every danger of battle. Furthermore, these men, frequently captured by their lusts and occupied with the pursuit of "perverted" love [[notes: *Praeposteri amoris*, often used in this period to refer to non-traditional or socially discouraged sexual orientations]], are forced to bring death upon themselves. Also born from this star are shepherds of sheep, but those who, playing on a rustic pipe, produce the sweetest melodies of a country song.

-> In Aries <-

[[summary: Firmicus Maternus introduces the astrological influence of non-zodiacal constellations (the Barbarian Sphere), criticizing poets for ignoring their predictive power. He then details the specific fates of those born under the degrees of Aries when the Ship, Orion, the Charioteer, and the Kid are rising.]]

[[keywords: Firmicus Maternus, Mathesis, Astrology, Aries, Orion, Auriga, Argo Navis, Barbarian Sphere, Petosiris, Necepso, Roman Astrology, Fixed Stars]]

[[meta: This page continues a technical discussion of the "paranatellonta"—stars or constellations that rise or set alongside the primary zodiac signs—specifically concluding a section on Taurus and transitioning from rising stars (ascent) to setting stars (descent).]]

# ->EIGHTH<- [[page number: 217]]

In the thirty-seventh [[notes: A zodiac sign traditionally contains only 30 degrees. The author may be using a different counting system or this is a printer's error for the 27th degree.]] degree of Taurus (♉) the **Hyades** rise. Whoever is born at the rising of this constellation will be restless, turbulent, and a man of the people; one who always stirs up the common folk with rowdy seditions, inflaming their minds with loud and furious arguments. He is an enemy of peace and quiet, desiring internal and domestic wars with a furious passion of the mind. Yet, from this constant state of anxiety, various profits often arise for him. This constellation also produces ox-drivers, shepherds, herdsmen, and keepers of sheep.

In the thirtieth degree of Taurus (♉), which is the part that always shows the whole sign above the earth, the **Goat** [[notes: This refers to the star Capella in the constellation Auriga.]] rises, which the myth-making poets claim provided nourishment for the infant Jupiter. Whoever is born under this constellation will be anxious with excessive trepidation of the mind, and their bodies will be constantly plagued by tremors. They will be overwhelmed by slight disturbances and will be shaken by a heavy onset of fear even at minor news. Nevertheless, they will be curious about all things, desiring to hear whatever is new with an impatient passion, so that they always pursue every novelty with a curious longing and strive to understand it.

And because we have now said enough, and more than enough, regarding what these stars do at their rising, we must speak in the following place of what they decree when positioned at their setting. For just as darkness is the opposite of light, so is death to life. Therefore, life will be found in the rising, but death in the setting. Thus, if the rising is in the **horoscope** [[notes: In ancient astrology, the "horoscope" refers specifically to the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.]], the setting will be diametrically opposite the horoscope—that is, in the seventh place from the horoscope.

If the **Ship** [[notes: The constellation Argo Navis.]] is therefore positioned precisely at the setting, and the malevolent stars [[notes: Usually referring to Saturn and Mars.]] regard this place by an opposite or square radiation [[notes: "Aspects" in astrology; a square is 90 degrees and an opposition is 180 degrees, both considered stressful or "hard" angles.]], they decree the bitter misfortunes of shipwrecks. But if **Saturn** (♄) himself is placed in that star, they will perish by drowning in the sea or in rivers.

If **Orion** is found at the setting of the birth chart, such men will be born whose minds are always driven by various anxieties. These men, sent on an embassy by their fellow citizens and while stationed in that very office, will die abroad; they carry to the underworld the slight solace that this office was given to them by their citizens. To them are also decreed perpetual honors, images, titles, and the insignia of honorable statues.

If the **Charioteer** (*Auriga*) is found at the setting of the birth chart, and the ray of the malevolent stars attacks it, they are thrown from four-horse chariots and scattered by wretched manglings, so that with a broken body they suffer the bitter misfortunes of death; or, struck by lightning, they are overwhelmed by a sudden death; or they are raised upon a cross; or their legs are broken by the public vengeance of the judges. If the **Kid** (*Hoedus*) of the Charioteer is found at the setting, and **Saturn** (♄) regards it with a square or opposite radiation, those born die in the very moment of life; or, being placed in the very light of birth, they are strangled as the mother’s strength fails; or a bitter death is brought upon them by swelling of the throat. But if **Mars** (♂) is found with that same star at the setting, and is destitute of all testimony from the benevolent stars, he will cause those born to be executed, or to be sacrificed at an altar under the observations of a fearsome religion.

If the **Hyades** are found at the setting, and the ray of the malevolents attacks that place, a sudden and unhoped-for death is decreed. For they will perish utterly, overwhelmed by turbulent seditions and torn apart here and there by the hands of the common people, so that the authors of their death can neither be found nor named.

If the **Goat** is found at the setting, they will have the means of substance from rural estates, but they will be struck by heavy envy on account of injured religions [[notes: Likely meaning a violation of sacred rites or sacrilege]]; they will also have wealth either gathered from shipwrecks or acquired from rivers.

For the vices of petulance always exalt these people—smeared with ointments and given over to excessive wine-drinking—who, in banquets and gatherings of men, strike at the lives of others with the freedom of bitter speech. They will certainly be inclined toward every deed of lust, and they who [rely] on false [[margin: Pleiades.]] speech...

...with biting words in their speech, they are accustomed to provoking laughter among men. They will also always have a bright and polished appearance, ready with carefully chosen clothing. Their curled hair is always twisted with purple dye [[notes: "In ostro" refers to Tyrian purple, a sign of luxury and vanity]]; furthermore, by using applied false hair, they feign a manufactured and composed beauty, softening the form of their whole body with various kinds of pigments. If the Pleiades—that is, the sixth part of ♉ [[notes: 6 degrees of Taurus]]—are found in the setting position and are radiated by malefic stars, those born under this sign will perish in a shipwreck. But if benefic stars, together with the malefics, behold this same place with equal radiation, a pleasant death will come to them without any lamentation, either from Venusian pleasure or from excessive food, amidst banquets and wine cups.

If the Ascendant is in the "fixing of the hoof" of ♉, and the ☽ [[Moon]]—or the benefics and malefics equally—behold this same place with equal radiation, they make a painter, but one whom this study ennobles with celebrated honor. If, however, without the testimony of the benefics, the malefics alone behold this place with a threatening radiation, famous gladiators will be born; these are men who, after many palms of victory and innumerable wins in that pursuit of combat, die with an intrepid heart by a threatening and drawn sword, even amidst the great applause and favor of the spectators.

If the setting position is found in the "fixing of the hoof" of ♉, whether benefic or malefic stars behold that place, those born under this constellation will suffer, not without danger, from the tension of violent lust [[notes: *Tentigine* refers to a physical manifestation of lust or priapism]].

[[margin: The Hare.]]
**I**N the seventh part, the Hare [[notes: The constellation Lepus]] rises. Those born under this constellation will possess such lightness of body that when they begin to run, driven by their own speed, they seem to surpass the birds. If the ☽ [[Moon]] is with ♂ [[Mars]], it produces *pyctomacharios* [[notes: From the Greek, meaning those who fight with fists; boxers or certain gladiators]]. If ☿ [[Mercury]], it produces jugglers or ball players. If ♀ [[Venus]], it produces pantomimes or mimes [[notes: In the Roman world, these were performers who acted out stories through gesture and song]]. If ☿ [[Mercury]] and ♀ [[Venus]] are together, they produce masters of new arts and of exceeding diligence, especially if the testimony of the "Dialis" radiation [[notes: Referring to Jupiter, the star of Zeus/Diespiter]] assists them in all these *apotelesmata* [[notes: Astrological outcomes or predictions]] we have mentioned. But if ♄ [[Saturn]] sees this place through a square or diameter [[notes: Harsh astrological aspects of 90 or 180 degrees]], it will produce fugitives who, moving their hearths to distant regions, will separate from their homes through a sudden impulse of spirit and be divided from them.

If the Hare is found in the setting position and has the testimony of both benefic and malefic stars together, as we said in the preceding outcomes, they will seek the means of life with great labor. If, however, only the testimony of malefic stars is added, they will die utterly consumed and torn apart by wild beasts.

If ♄ [[Saturn]] does this same thing, they will be devoted to every pursuit of fishing, so that by exquisite fishing methods, they may even capture sea monsters.

[[margin: Argion [[notes: Likely referring to Procyon in the constellation Canis Minor, the 'Before-the-Dog' star.]]]]
In the 20th degree of Gemini (♊), Argion rises. When this star is rising, those who are born will be removed from the actual practice of hunting; instead, they will either manufacture or provide tools for hunters, such as nets, spears, arrows, and whatever else pertains to the equipment of that pursuit. They will also breed dogs that track the dens of wild beasts and their hidden lairs with prophetic noses, as well as all animals that assist in hunting.

If, however, this constellation is setting, and Mars (♂) regards this place with a square or diametrical radiation [[notes: 'Square' (90°) and 'diametrical' (180° opposition) are considered harsh or difficult astrological aspects.]], and is deprived of the favorable testimony of Jupiter (♃), they will perish torn apart by the bite of a rabid dog, suffering a similar madness of fury. They will shun the sight of water and shudder at the swallowing of any drink, so that with parched throats, they even fear the water they long for; or certainly, while laying snares for wild beasts, they will be torn apart and scattered by their bites.

-> ### CHAPTER X: BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH LEO (♌) ### <-

[[margin: Canicula [[notes: 'The Little Dog,' commonly known as Sirius, the Dog Star.]]]]
### **I**N the first degree of Leo (♌) rises Canicula, which is called *Seirios* (σείριος) by the Greeks. Whoever is born when this star is rising will apply an unbridled mind to every pursuit of perverse wickedness. They will be devoid of all grace of humanity—men who gladly follow every pursuit of violence: furious, wrathful, terrible, and menacing, whom all men alike will both hate and fear. Furthermore, they will be high-spirited and puffed up with a muscular flow of speech, driven by reckless talk toward every kind of insult. These people, stirring up new legal quarrels, have hearts that throb with frequent agitation, and a voice that—as the throat swells—imitates the barking of dogs. Often, moved by impulse and fury, they either chatter their teeth or constantly whet them as if grinding them down. But if Mars (♂) regards this place, these traits we have mentioned grow even stronger. Such men never fear the secrets of the woods; indeed, they despise the bites of all wild beasts due to their mental ferocity, so that dangers are frequently brought upon them by both beasts and fires. Furthermore, if malevolent stars [[notes: Usually referring to Saturn or Mars.]] radiate upon this place while the Moon (☽) is also aspecting Saturn (♄), there will be born hunters, *arenarii* [[notes: 'Arenarii' were low-ranking gladiators who fought wild animals in the arena.]], and those who fight with bristly beasts in cages in the sight of the people; also gladiators, and those gifted with such bodily speed that they seem able to catch hares in a race.

If, however, this constellation is found to be setting, and Mars (♂) is either in that exact place or regards it with a menacing radiation, they will be eaten by wolves, or torn apart by dogs or wild beasts, ending their lives in wretched mutilation.

[[margin: Crater [[notes: The 'Cup' constellation, often associated with the god of wine, Bacchus.]]]]
In the 30th degree of Leo (♌) rises Crater. He who is born when this constellation is rising will love well-watered fields and springs; he will divert streams or rivers from their channels to other places. He will also be a lover and cultivator of vineyards, one who grafts fruitful shoots onto fruitful trees, or who, shearing boxwood trees, shapes them into the forms of beasts, or makes green porticos with vines bent into a circle. But such a man will gladly drink wine without the admixture of water [[notes: Drinking wine undiluted was considered a sign of excess or 'barbarism' in the Greco-Roman world.]]. If the radiation of favorable stars decrees these actions, he will trade in liquid goods.

If, however, this constellation is found to be setting without the testimony of a malevolent star, the person born will die of drunkenness amidst feasts and cups. But if the radiation of malevolent stars is added, he will die submerged in a wine vat, or a well, or he will be found dead in a river, a lake, a swamp, or the sea, or certainly in a pool or a bath.

[[margin: Corona [[notes: Corona Borealis, the Northern Crown.]]]]
**I**N the 5th degree of Virgo (♍) rises Corona. Whoever is born under this star will be occupied with various pleasures of luxury and devoted to the study of feminine arts. He will be an inventor of flowers and garlands, one who clings to the pleasant delights of gardens, desiring scents, ointments, and spices with studious greed. He will cultivate his body with the allurements of beauty and may secretly practice debauchery and adultery, rushing with a prone spirit of lust toward the beauty of maidens and the beds of boys.

If, however, this star is found to be setting, and either **Saturn** [♄] is in that very place, or gazes upon this same part from another location with a threatening ray [[notes: An "aspect" or "ray" refers to the geometric angle between celestial bodies, believed to transmit their influence]], or if other malevolent stars do this, they decree destruction for the movements of the life, and they shall kill the person in their first youth. For they will cause the individual to be struck down by public execution and left unburied, to be torn apart by the habits of wild beasts, dogs, or birds.

[[margin: **Spica.**]]
In the tenth degree of Virgo, **Spica** [[notes: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo, traditionally associated with the harvest]] rises. Whoever is born under this star will always be devoted to rural duties and joined to the cultivation of fields with an endurance for labor; he is one who, with new seeds, produces a renewal of crops every single year, and who stores many fruits in barns for the support of life. If there are also excellent testimonies from the stars [[notes: "Testimonies" refer to favorable planetary alignments]], they make pastry chefs, confectioners, and men of similar trades.

If, however, this star is found to be setting, they will be troubled either by the excessive heat of the weather, by the narrows of garrisons, or by raids. But if **Saturn** [♄] regards this place with a threatening ray, he will cause the native to be weighed down by the wretched burden of poverty, so that through every stage of life he is naked in ill-hanging rags; and thus Saturn leads him to the very end of life, seeking food through the protection of public pity, so that he completes the duty of life with torment of the mind as well as the body. But if **Mercury** [☿] should radiate upon this place, because of a grain supply that is intercepted, poorly distributed, or stolen through the fraud of greed, the native will be struck by a heavy blow and torn apart by the envy of a raging populace, so that with limbs mangled by the hands of the people, he demonstrates a terrifying example of a bitter death to others.

### -> CHAPTER XII <-

[[margin: **Sagittarius.**]]
In the eighth degree of **Sagittarius** [↗] rises [the star] †. Whoever is born in this sign will be a shooter of arrows, one who strikes even flying birds with a certain special moderation of skill, or who, intrepid, pierces fish with a trident or a point even within the stretches of the waves.

If, however, this star is found to be setting, and both benevolent and malevolent stars regard this same place with an equalized radiation, the natives—having been established in the army and positioned in the battle line—die at last, slain by a hostile right hand among the bitter heaps of the enemy, bloodied with their infinite blood. But if **Venus** [♀] alone, with **Mercury** [☿] standing by, should see this place, or if she is found in it, she will make such men as sell themselves to the spectacle of death for the sake of another’s favor, through the loss of their bartered blood [[notes: This likely refers to gladiators or mercenaries]]. If, however, **Saturn** [♄] should do this, they are led into the *ludus* [[notes: The *ludus* was a training school for gladiators]] by the sentence of a judge. For in this part, the **Styx** is said to be; and there is no doubt that the Styx is here on earth, for those who do not fear celestial things shudder in their minds at those things which, having fallen from heaven, are applied to the sustenance of earthly bodies.

[[margin: **Haedus**]]
In the 15th degree of **Libra** [♎] [[notes: The source uses the symbol for Libra, though "Haedus" (The Kid) is a star usually associated with the constellation Auriga]], **Haedus** rises. When this sign is rising, whoever is born will always be of a flickering mind and an anxious purpose; entangled in various thoughts, he may never enjoy rest with the grace of security. He will also be assigned to the service of magistrates, either as a scribe, a courier, or handling the duties of public taxes. Yet he will be bound by wanton habits and backwards desires of love, devoted to wine and feasts; he is one who prefers the favor of public banquets, is fit for dancing, and learns the theatrical arts with a studious passion.

If, however, this star is found to be setting, and malevolent stars regard this place with a threatening ray, they will either cast the person down through precipices and thus they shall perish, or, practicing leaping, the wretches are broken by the fall of their hanging body in an unlucky misfortune of death. Or, seeking the beds of girls in the blind night and demanding them with an excessive fire of impatience, when they have traveled through unknown places and climbed upon roofs to lie in wait for the sleep of husbands, they die, deceived by a headlong slip. But if benevolent stars regard this place, they die unhappily as "dysphorici" [[notes: From the Greek *dysphoros*, meaning "hard to bear"—referring here to those suffering from extreme distress or agitation]] and wretches.

# **I**
n the 5th degree of Sagittarius (♐), Arcturus rises. When this sign is rising, whoever is born will be the sort of person who [[margin: *Arcturus.*]] guards the secrets of friends with faithful silence. When this constellation is rising, whoever is born will either catch birds, [[margin: *Cygnus.*]] or trade them, or through ingenious study, will teach the sound of the human voice to birds, or will studiously breed various birds, especially wood-pigeons.

-> BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH CAPRICORN (♑) <-

# **I**
n the first degrees of Capricorn (♑), Ophiuchus [the Serpent Bearer] rises. When this is rising, those born will be Marsi [[margin: *Ophiuchus.*]] [[notes: The Marsi were an ancient Italic people famous for their supposed immunity to snake bites and their skills as healers and snake charmers.]], who—naturally—overpower pestilential snakes by numbing and soothing their fangs.

In the 8th degree of Capricorn (♑), the Dolphin [Delphinus] rises. When this constellation is rising, whoever is [[margin: *Delphinus.*]] born will be gripped by a passion for swimming. But with the testimony of Saturn (♄), he will be a diver; with Mars (♂) and Mercury (☿) however, he will be an acrobat, a leaper, a balancer, or certainly distinguished by an innate agility of running [[notes: The Latin lists several specific Greek-derived terms for types of stage performers and acrobats common in Roman entertainment.]].
But if this constellation is found to be setting, and Saturn (♄) looks upon this place with a threatening aspect, he will be unluckily submerged in the sea or in a river by whirlpools and storms.
In the 10th degree of Capricorn (♑), the Lyre rises. Whoever is born when this constellation rises will be just, [[margin: *Lyra.*]] upright, eager, and fit for every duty of equity, and avengers of crimes, to whom public trials and judicial inquiries are entrusted. But if Saturn (♄) looks upon this place with any aspect, they will be torturers and executioners, who pursue bad men with a ready zeal.
But if this constellation is found to be setting, they will perish torn by public tortures, or consumed by fires, or by legal execution, especially if Mars (♂) looks upon this place.
In the 15th degree of Capricorn (♑), Cepheus rises. Whoever is born when this constellation rises will be [[margin: *Cepheus.*]] grave, austere, and feared for a terrifying severity, always shaping their expression based on the integrity of their character—people who follow the Stoic sect with true devotion. For such among the ancients were the Catos [[notes: Refers to Cato the Elder and Cato the Younger, legendary symbols of Roman morality and discipline.]]. Such in our times was Lollianus [[notes: Likely Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius, a contemporary high-ranking official and consul in 355 AD.]], who by merit of his severity, even attained the insignia of an ordinary consulship. But if in this place Venus (♀) and Mercury (☿) are witnessing...

->## BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH [[note: Eagle/Aquila symbol]]<-
->## CHAPTER XVI<-

[[margin: **The Eagle.**]]
   In the twelfth degree [[notes: The Latin "parte" (part) refers to a degree of the 360-degree zodiacal circle]] of [[note: Eagle/Aquila symbol]] the Eagle rises. Whoever is born during the rising of this constellation will find the means of their life through the slaughter of men and through spoils; they will also capture and likewise tame wild beasts. Furthermore, they will be brave soldiers who, endowed with the highest virtue, would follow the enemy even with a bare chest, believing it to profit their praise greatly if they despise death with a calm boldness. But if benefic stars [[notes: "Benevolent stars" usually refers to Jupiter or Venus]] look upon this place with a favorable radiation, their fatherland will be liberated by them; indeed, they will even found other cities and, having conquered and subjugated nations, they will triumph wonderfully. But if Mars (♂) or Saturn (♄) looks upon this place, it will make them prefects, tribunes, ministers of emperors, attendants of kings, and those to whom the care of the empire or the guarding of arms is entrusted by their faith.
   But if this star is found in the setting, it will make those born at the first light of life unhappily suffocated—

[[margin: **Cassiopea.**]]
   In the twentieth degree of [[note: Eagle symbol, likely an error in the original text for the zodiacal degree of Aquarius]] Cassiopea rises. Whoever is born under this constellation will be goldsmiths, gold-leaf beaters, gilders, modelers, pearl-merchants, and those who handle all these arts with ingenious skill, and from these they will obtain the greatest means of life.
   But if this star is found in the setting, those born will either perish from a falling building [[notes: "Ex ruina" specifically suggests the collapse of a structure, a common urban danger in the Roman world]] or will die by being murdered.

->## BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH PISCES (♓)<-
->## CHAPTER XVII.<-

[[margin: **Andromeda.**]]
   In the 12th degree of Pisces (♓) Andromeda rises. Whoever is born during the rising of this constellation will always range about with cruel ferocity against men; for they will be either ministers of public punishments, or guards of prisons, or executioners, and those to whom the duties of killing men are entrusted. But if a benefic star, joined with malefic ones, looks upon this same place, it will make them overseers of workhouses [[notes: "Ergastulis" were private prisons or Roman slave-labor camps]] or of mines.
   But if this star is found in the setting, and malefic stars look upon this place, they will cause the person to be thrown to wild beasts or raised upon a cross. But if the favor of benefic stars is added to such an arrangement of malefic ones, they will cause them to be given to the gladiatorial school or to be bound in perpetual chains and shackles.

[[margin: **The Charioteer.**]]
   In the 20th degree of Pisces (♓) the Charioteer rises [[notes: Known in Latin as *Heniochus* or *Auriga*]]. Whoever is born during the rising of this constellation will be diligent charioteers, drivers, horsemen, wagon-drivers, scouts, and sometimes even doctors—but specifically those who compose remedies for sick men and cattle very aptly from herbs.
   But if this star is found in the setting with malefic stars, the person will either be cured after being thrown by the kick of a horse, or will perish overturned by a vehicle or weakened, or shaken by a miserable mangling of the body and limbs.

[[margin: **The Kneeler.**]]
   In the final degrees of Pisces (♓) the Kneeler rises, who is called *en gonasin* [[notes: ἐν γόνασιν]] by the Greeks. [[notes: This is the constellation Hercules, who was often depicted as a man on one knee.]] Whoever is born during the rising of this constellation will be fugitives, crafty, equipped with various deceits, liars, and those who attack men with various snares and always range about with unbridled boldness. But with the testimony of Mars (♂) and the Moon (☽), they will be tightrope-walkers, mountain-climbers, string-walkers, and those who practice such things.
   But if the star is found in the setting, they will be endangered by various snares. But if Mars (♂) radiates upon this place, they will also be unhappily burned alive.

[[margin: **The Sea Monster.**]]
   In the last part of Pisces (♓), toward the left, rises the beast which is called *orphos* [[notes: ὀρφὸς]] by the Greeks. [[notes: Likely referring to Cetus or a similar sea creature.]] Whoever is born during the rising of this constellation will be fishermen, but of the larger fish. For these will catch seals, sharks, swordfish, tunas, or crocodiles. Or they will have occupations involving salt, salted meats, or fish sauce [[notes: "Liquamine" refers to *garum*, the fermented fish sauce ubiquitous in Roman cuisine]], and they will trade in these.
   But if this star is found in the setting, and Mars (♂) radiates upon this place, while swimming in a river or the sea, they will be mangled by crocodiles or beasts of this kind.
   Now, when the North rises, which is between Pisces (♓) and Aries (♈)—that is, between the beginning and the end of the world—which is fixed in one place and located at the very summit of the world, twisting it with its perpetual speed,

...whoever is born [under these conditions] will be tamers of wild beasts, who associate with bears, bulls, or lions—once their ferocity has been laid aside—in human settings.
[[margin: The Snake. [[notes: Referring to the constellation Draco (the Dragon or Snake), located near the North Pole.]]]]
But if this constellation is found in the north during its setting, with **Mars (♂)** witnessing, they will perish most cruelly by wild beasts.
The "Tail of the Snake" is that which is placed between the two Bears [[notes: Ursa Major and Ursa Minor]], flowing in the manner of a river that glides along with smoky twists. Whoever is born under this constellation will be "Marsi" [[notes: The Marsi were an ancient Italian people famous for their skills as snake-charmers and herbal healers]], or those who are accustomed to preparing healthy remedies for men from poisons made from the pigments of herbs.
But if this constellation is found in its setting, they will perish struck by the bite of serpents, or certainly by drinking poison.
[[margin: The Swan.]]
The Swan [[notes: The constellation Cygnus]] also pertains to this part of the sign. Whoever, therefore, is born while this constellation is rising will be discoverers of metals, who pursue hidden veins of gold and silver and other species with skillful investigations; these people will also be made masters of the mint.
But if this constellation is found in its setting, and **Mars (♂)** is in that same place, or in diameter [[notes: Opposition (180 degrees)]] or square [[notes: An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered difficult or tense]], they will either burn to death in a house fire or be cremated by the avenging flames of a public judicial sentence.
[[margin: Those born during an earthquake.]]
Furthermore, at the end of these decrees, we ought to know this: if at that hour in which the birth is completed, there is either an earthquake or it thunders in the heavens, whoever is born then will always be trembling and unstable of body. He will be one who, with a doubting step and trembling feet, expects and fears the ruin of overhanging rooftops at every moment of the day. His eyes will flicker, and he will shudder at the burning gaze of all; his very words will not keep a certain order, but the hindered sound of his voice will hiss out a trembling murmur, so that with a tightened throat, his words always fail him at the very moment of utterance. For such people will always think the heavens are thundering, the earth is moving, and everything is forever collapsing, so that—preoccupied by the terrors of a falling world—they lose the order of a proper life. These, **Mavortius** [[notes: Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman aristocrat to whom this work is dedicated]], our glory, are the principles of the "Barbaric Sphere"; this is the discipline of the Chaldean work which we promised.

-># PREDICTIONS OF THE BARBARIC SPHERE<-
->## BOOK TWO, CHAPTER XVIII.<-

### **N**ow, however, I shall translate the entire treatise following the parts of the Barbaric Sphere, which in some part imitates "Myriogenesis" [[notes: From the Greek for 'origin of ten thousand,' a technique for interpreting the specific influence of every individual degree of the zodiac]]. For whatever Myriogenesis pronounces concerning individual minutes, we shall do concerning individual degrees. Therefore, the "Horoscope" [[notes: Here meaning the Ascendant, the specific degree rising on the eastern horizon]] must be placed as a pointer, so that the true degree, collected by skillful computation, allows the prediction to be brought forth with a faithful pronouncement. Otherwise, whatever has been promised will be entirely overshadowed by the vice of error and deceptive lies. Now, therefore, we shall embrace the powers of all the signs and their predictions, according to the Barbaric Sphere, through their individual degrees in a brief discourse.

->## MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF ARIES ($\Upsilon$), CHAPTER XIX.<-

### **I**f the first degree of **Aries ($\Upsilon$)** is found in the Horoscope, and the ray of benevolent stars [[notes: Usually Jupiter or Venus]] approaches, there will be born kings, leaders, and those who lead their army prosperously.
If the second degree of **Aries ($\Upsilon$)** is found in the Horoscope, they will be stubborn, thieves, and those who always rage with a backward fury, or who transfer their household to foreign nations. But if, with the Horoscope settled in this degree, **Mars (♂)** has testimony, and the **Moon (☽)** sees him from a square or diameter, once their aforementioned crimes are discovered, they are punished by public execution.
If the third degree of **Aries ($\Upsilon$)** is found in the Horoscope, they will be deaf, one-eyed, and dulled by a stupid foolishness.
If the fourth degree of **Aries** is found in the Horoscope, they will be thieves, but [exhausted by the business].
If the fifth degree of **Aries** is found in the Horoscope, they will rule over a great people and judge the greatest matters; by the merit of their dignity, they will be preferred above all. For they will be just, upright, sober, and those who protect the religions of their fathers with the greatest veneration; they will die adorned with every proclamation of goodness.
If the sixth degree of **Aries ($\Upsilon$)** is found in the Horoscope, he will be a friend of kings, or of powerful judges, adorned with the insignia of illustrious dignities, and one who carries about him all the ornaments of glory. Either the merits of a certain art will commend him, or another will be put in charge of military offices; all these, however, will perish not by a violent death, but by their own natural death.

The seventh degree of ♈ [[gloss: Aries]], if found in the horoscopus [[notes: The 'horoscopus' refers to the Ascendant, the specific degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], with the testimony of ♃ [[gloss: Jupiter]], will make an athlete; however, with ♂ [[gloss: Mars]], it makes one hunchbacked and a *biothanatus* [[notes: A Greek-derived term meaning one who dies a violent, shameful, or premature death]].

The eighth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus with the testimony of malevolent stars [[notes: Usually Mars or Saturn]], will produce athletes, but those whom the merits of illustrious virtues ennoble. These people, however, after many honors, will perish by a violent death. But if the ray of benevolent stars [[notes: Usually Jupiter or Venus]] reaches this degree, they will be prophets, bearing the greatest signs of divinity in their souls.

The ninth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscopus, slaughters those placed in it in their first age [[notes: childhood or early youth]] with a violent death.

The tenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make people treacherous, irreligious, and impure, who, oppressed by various ailments of vice, die in their first age.

The eleventh degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus with ♃ either positioned in that degree or joined to it by a trine [[notes: An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious]] and partile radiation [[notes: An exact aspect to the same degree]], will make a person powerful and bearing the marks of magnificent dignity; one whom a faithful bond of friendship joins to kings and powerful men. It makes him wealthy, affluent, and possessing great spans of lands and estates; it will also make him a famous leader, heaped with every honor of dignity, adorned with prosperous testimonies of fame, and one who will die a natural death [[notes: Literal: "by his own death," as opposed to execution or accident]].

The twelfth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus with ♃ and ♀ [[gloss: Venus]] positioned in that same degree, with the testimony of the ☽ [[gloss: Moon]], or if the ☽ regards this same degree with a trine radiation, will make people adorned with the bright splendor of nobility, who—being also wealthy and long-lived—die by a praised kind of death.

The thirteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make people sterile, to whom the always-desired offspring is denied; these will die overtaken in middle age.

The fourteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make a businessman, but one provided with flowing riches; also a moneylender at the public tables [[notes: Similar to a banker or state financier]], collecting great reserves of wealth, known to all and always conspicuous. This place also makes weavers, or those who handle wools and purples [[notes: Purple dye was a sign of extreme luxury and status]] with constant mastery of their art.

The fifteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make one polluted by the shameless stain of lust, and always bound to impure vices; also a *cinaedus* [[notes: A term used in antiquity for a man considered effeminate or sexually passive, often carrying social stigma]] condemned by public infamy. If it is a woman, a similar lust for impurity will strike her.

The sixteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will cause one to be tortured by constant intestinal pains; such a person will also die in agony. If it is a woman, she will fulfill her life's final duty while laboring in childbirth.

The seventeenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make a fowler [[notes: a bird-catcher]], a hunter, or a breeder of birds or wild beasts. But if the testimony of ♂ reaches the horoscopus, he will be torn apart by wild beasts or by dogs and die.

The eighteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make a mule-driver or a shepherd of mules, but this man will die a miserable death, struck by a small beast, or a *phalangium* [[notes: A type of venomous spider]], a field mouse, or a scorpion.

The nineteenth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will cause those placed within the first porch of life [[notes: early childhood]] to perish.

The twentieth degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, and if the prosperous testimony of ♃ reaches it, or if ♃ is positioned in it, will make a person wealthy, adorned with many and famous offspring, and protected by the support of many brothers. But the merits of a faithful friendship also join this same man to kings or powerful men. He will be a worshiper of the gods, adorned with every proclamation of goodness: good, benevolent, just, long-lived, happy in old age, and one who dies his own death.

The twenty-first degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus with the same star we mentioned [[notes: Jupiter]], will decree the same fate.

The twenty-second degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus with the same star we mentioned, will decree the same fate.

The twenty-third degree of ♈, if found in the horoscopus, will make one scrofulous [[notes: afflicted with 'struma', a swelling of the lymph nodes often linked to tuberculosis]], possessed by the stain of ulcerated spots, or certainly marked by the contagion of elephantiasis [[notes: Could refer to leprosy or the condition now known as elephantiasis]].

The twenty-fourth degree of Aries (♈︎), if found in the [[notes: The *horoscopus* refers to the Ascendant, the specific degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.]] horoscope, will make men prone to the pleasures of Venus, and always troubled by the urges of lust.

The twenty-fifth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will make a person a goldsmith, a gilder, or certainly a stonemason.

The twenty-sixth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will make a man so timid that at every moment of the day he will be terrified by vain and foolish suspicions.

The twenty-seventh degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will produce a wool-worker, a builder, or a weaver of wool.

The twenty-eighth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will make a cleaner of latrines and sewers, or someone condemned by a judge’s sentence to some form of public labor.

The twenty-ninth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will make a barber, and one who is in charge of cutting the hair of men.

The thirtieth degree of Aries, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are insane, [[notes: The Latin *caducos* refers to those with "the falling sickness," or epilepsy.]] epileptics, the delirious, and those who are short-lived.

->### CHAPTER XX. THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF TAURUS.<-

# P
he first degree of Taurus (♉︎), if found in the horoscope, will make divinely inspired prophets, but specifically those who are accustomed to prophesy within temples.

The second degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make porters of dung, and cleaners of latrines and sewers.

The third degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make famous stage-performers who, having participated in [[notes: *Sacris certaminibus* refers to the "Sacred Games" (like the Olympic or Pythian games), where winners were awarded prestigious crowns.]] sacred contests, obtain the most beautiful insignia of crowns.

The fourth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are quick to anger and threatening over any slight cause.

The fifth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope—if [[notes: ♂ is the symbol for the planet Mars.]] Mars is positioned there or joined by a threatening ray [[notes: In astrology, a "ray" refers to an aspect or geometric relationship between planets.]]—will cause death resulting from serious injuries.

The sixth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make [[notes: The Latin terms *exoletos*, *irrumatores*, and *cinædos* describe specific roles in Roman sexual culture that carried heavy social stigma or "infamy."]] debauched men, devoted to every vice of impurity: "irrumators," "cinaedi," and those who are always struck by heavy infamy.

The seventh degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make [[notes: *Haruspices* and *Augurs* were official Roman diviners; the former read the entrails of animals, while the latter interpreted the flight of birds.]] Haruspices, Augurs, and diviners of such arts.

The eighth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will cause people to be advanced by new and sudden honors, yet they will die suddenly.

The ninth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make men base, infamous, and polluted by the stain of all vices.

The tenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make men bad, malicious, and spiteful, who are shaken by the hardships of every misfortune, and who finally die as [[notes: *Biothanati* were those who died a "violent death," which in the ancient world included suicide, execution, or accidents.]] *biothanati*.

The eleventh degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will cause the body to be spoiled and swollen by malignant humors, and the person will die of dropsy.

The twelve degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make miserable men who are consumed by fires and perish by an ill-fated death.

The thirteenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make overseers of athletes and famous masters of the wrestling schools.

The fourteenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make a body possessed by foul odors, such that a miserable person always reeks of a [[notes: *Hyrcini fœtoris* literally means the "stench of a he-goat," a common Roman insult for bad body odor.]] goat-like stench, and for this reason is shunned by everyone.

The fifteenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make liars, separated from all trust in the truth; they will also be gluttonous, serving the drunken lusts of the belly and the throat.

The 16th degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make men defiled by the shame of every crime.

The 17th degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make blacksmiths and those who work bronze with their hands.

The eighteenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make slaves and humble men, [[notes: *Artocopos* is a Latinized Greek term for a bread-maker or specialty baker.]] bread-makers or bakers.

The nineteenth degree of Taurus, if found in the horoscope, will make people sterile, to whom children are always denied.

->## THE MYRIOGENESIS [[notes: "Ten thousand origins," a term for the specific influences of individual degrees]] OF THE PARTS OF GEMINI CHAPTER XXI.<-

rima [[notes: Decorative initial 'P']] The **first part of Gemini (♊)**: if it is found in the horoscope and **Saturn (♄)** looks upon it with any radiation [[notes: any astrological aspect]], it will produce the powerful and the great, the first of their province, and those to be feared with the greatest honor by their citizens, but perishing by the indignation of the prince.
   If the **second part of Gemini** is found in the horoscope, and **Jupiter (♃)** is positioned with it, or **Saturn (♄)**, and especially if the **Moon (☽)** is placed in favorable locations of the birth-chart, or is carried toward them full of light, it will produce leaders who lead armies of horsemen or infantry, to whom the command of ships is entrusted, who also subject very many men, who see places unknown to them, and to whom clear insignia of power are given even in remote and far-flung regions. If the **third degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create priests, or leaders of sacred rites, or even prominent minor rulers.

If the **fourth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create people of the greatest physical beauty and distinction, whose beloved beauty commends them to kings, so much so that the kings' desires are always burning with love for them.

If the **fifth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create nobles who are always uplifted by a high spirit of pride.

If the **sixth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create inspired prophets [[notes: The Latin *vates entheos* suggests poets or seers possessed by a divine frenzy]], who sing their poems through a certain divine power.

If the **seventh degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create jailers and guards of the public watch.

If the **eighth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, and **Mercury** (☿) also holds a place there, it will create musicians. If **Mars** (♂) is there, it will produce trumpeters, but those who die pierced through in war.

If the **ninth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, it will create laborers, ceiling-decorators [[notes: *Lacunarios* refers to craftsmen who made ornate, coffered ceilings]], and those burdened by a perpetual weight of misfortune.

If the **tenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create men who die consumed by pain in the lungs.

If the **eleventh degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create *hoplomachi* [[notes: A type of gladiator armed with a spear and shield, modeled after Greek hoplites]] and those who gladly practice gladiatorial games.

If the **twelfth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, the men will die by the piercing of a weapon, while the women will perish in childbirth.

If the **thirteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create men who die of dropsy [[notes: *Hydropici* refers to edema or the abnormal accumulation of fluid in the body]] with a swollen belly.

If the **fourteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, it will cause people to perish by a miserable death, having fallen from a high place.

If the **fifteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create men who are bath-attendants, low-ranking household slaves, and assistants.

If the **sixteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create pantomimes [[notes: In the Roman world, these were solo dancers who acted out mythological stories through gesture and movement]], whose striking physical beauty and soft, delicate hearts always win them many lovers.

If the **seventeenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create men notable for both the beauty and size of their bodies, but who are truly modest and, because of this, friends of good men.

If the **eighteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create the exercises of athletes, assigned always to the services of the wrestling school.

If the **nineteenth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, it will create men destined to die by the sword. If **Saturn** (♄) is in that part, it will create water-carriers, exhausted by perpetual labors. However, if the **Moon** (☽) is placed in the "scaly signs" [[notes: These are signs associated with aquatic creatures, such as Pisces or Capricorn (the Sea-Goat)]] and is moving toward **Mars** while full of light, or toward **Saturn** while waning, it will produce lepers [[notes: *Elephanticos* refers to elephantiasis or similar skin-disfiguring diseases, often grouped with leprosy in antiquity]].

If the **twentieth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, it will create men who hold the rudders of the people [[notes: Meaning they are governors or leaders]] and to whom beautiful judgments are entrusted, but they will die a violent death.

If the **twenty-first degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Saturn** (♄) present and the **Moon** (☽) well-placed, it will make men wealthy with flowing riches, and noble friends of kings; yet they will be fathers of few sons and brothers of few brothers; these men, however, will die at a great age.

If the **twenty-second degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create lyre-players and musicians who will bear the greatest marks of nobility for this reason, or whom a bond of friendship joins to kings; yet such a person will die a violent death [[notes: *Biothanata* is a Greek-derived term used in astrology for a death that is unnatural, premature, or violent]].

If the **twenty-third degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant, it will create men vigorous in virtue and noble in war, whom everyone commends with the testimony of a prosperous reputation, but such a man dies without children.

If the **twenty-fourth degree of Gemini** is found in the Ascendant with **Mars** (♂) present, or aspecting this place from a diameter or a square [[notes: *Diameter* refers to an opposition (180 degrees); *quadrato* refers to a square aspect (90 degrees)]], it will cause people to perish by falling from a height, so that they either die with broken feet or perish torn apart by wild animals or beasts.

If the twenty-fifth degree of Gemini [[note: Gemini is the third sign of the zodiac, symbolized by the Twins]] is found in the Ascendant [[note: The "horoscopus" or Ascendant is the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], it will produce priests, soothsayers, prophets, and those joined to kings in faithful friendship. But if Saturn is in that degree, it will produce catamites and those who take the passive role in sex [[note: The Latin *cinædos* and *pathicos* refer to historical Greco-Roman sexual categories often associated here with social stigma or legal misfortune]], but who ultimately perish under the king's indignation.

If the twenty-sixth degree of Gemini is found in the Ascendant, it will produce sacristans, guardians of temples, temple servants [[note: *Hierodulos*, from the Greek for "sacred slave"]], and those assigned to sacred duties.

If the twenty-seventh degree of Gemini is found in the Ascendant, it will produce epileptics, the mentally impaired, and the insane, who are ultimately short-lived.

If the twenty-eighth degree of Gemini is found in the Ascendant, it will produce litigious and argumentative people who are always involved in lawsuits and disputes. But if Mars is in this degree, or regards this place by a square or diameter aspect [[note: A "square" is a 90-degree angle and a "diameter" or "opposition" is 180 degrees; both were considered stressful or "hard" aspects in ancient astrology]], he will cause them to be torn apart by dogs and to die without leaving an inheritance to children.

If the twenty-ninth degree of Gemini is found in the Ascendant while the Moon is present, it will produce nobles and those of illegitimate birth, but they will die in their youth.

If the thirtieth degree of Gemini is found in the Ascendant, it will produce hunters, specifically those who are enrolled for the pleasures of princes.

In the "line" of Gemini [[note: likely referring to a specific decan or boundary within the sign]], whoever has the Ascendant there while Mars is also found in that place will be bitten by a beast or a viper and will unfortunately lose a thigh or a foot.

->### CHAPTER XX: THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF CANCER ###<-

[[insert: Decorative initial I decorated with floral/scroll patterns]] Whoever has the Ascendant between the "eyes of the Cancer" [[note: Referring to specific stars in the constellation Cancer, likely near the Praesepe cluster]] will be one-eyed or deprived of all sight in the eyes.

If the first degree of Cancer [[note: Cancer is the fourth sign of the zodiac, associated with the summer solstice in antiquity]] is found in the Ascendant while the Moon is present, it will produce businessmen and nobles; however, if Saturn is present, it produces sailors, fishermen, tavern-keepers, innkeepers, and the like.

If the second degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce men distinguished by great power and nobility, but also violent men who possess the property of others through factious greed; these men, however, will travel on long journeys where they will fail due to sudden death.

If the third degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce hardworking businessmen who never stay in one place.

If the fourth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce men who always attack their enemies with every kind of controversy, and who become superior to them in every contest.

If the fifth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce men whose eyes are afflicted by "stalk-like" wounds [[note: *cauloſis uulneribus*, likely referring to growths or specific types of ocular lesions]].

If the sixth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce men whose eyes are always turned with a distorted gaze [[note: likely referring to strabismus or crossed eyes]].

If the seventh degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce men who have swellings or tumors on the head. But if the Moon is moving toward the Ascendant, it will produce the cunning and the impious. Yet, if Mars casts his rays upon the Moon and the Ascendant, he will produce bandits who roam with cruel ferocity; these will be raised on a cross or, condemned by public trial, will perish by a most cruel death.

If the eighth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce the blind. For in this degree and the fourth, there is a nebula [[note: This refers to *Praesepe* (the Beehive Cluster), a fuzzy patch of stars in Cancer. In ancient medicine and astrology, nebulae were frequently blamed for blindness or poor eyesight because they appeared "cloudy"]], of which we have frequently made mention in this book.

If the ninth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce sailors and ship-pilots—those who, of course, steer ships across every sea with the restraint of skilled craft.

If the tenth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce such men who accomplish all things through effective social interaction.

If the eleventh degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce fishermen and those who are continually occupied in the waters.

If the twelfth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce hardworking men who seek their living through constant sweat.

If the thirteenth degree of Cancer is found in the Ascendant, it will produce studious men who are always occupied with books and diligent late-night study.
