->## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF VIRGO ♍ CHAPTER 24.<-

# **P**
If the **f**irst degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, and the Moon ☽ is full of light and provides a favorable testimony to the Ascendant, it will make men distinguished by great nobility, who by merit of their literary skill are always in the company of the king or queen, and who have very many people established under their power. But if Mars ♂ casts his rays on this place, it will create *cinaedi* [[notes: *Cinaedi* were men perceived as effeminate or passive in sexual roles, a term often used as a social or moral critique in Roman society]], who finally die unhappily in damp places.

If the second degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, it will create beautiful priests, prophets, *haruspices* [[notes: *Haruspices* were diviners in ancient Rome who interpreted the will of the gods by inspecting the entrails of sacrificed animals]], and also religious men distinguished by great nobility; powerful men, possessing the greatest insignias of divinity.

If the third degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, it will create merchants who enrich many by their industry.

If the fourth degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, it will create country-folk who are exhausted by continuous labors in tilling the earth.

If the fifth degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, it will effect the same things we said the second degree of this sign decrees.

If the sixth degree of Virgo ♍ is found in the Ascendant, it will also work the same as what we said is decreed in the second degree of this sign.

If the seventh degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, with the Moon ☽ waxing or positioned in the Ascendant, it will create priests, or *uspices* [haruspices], diviners, religious men, and the powerful, who always suppress their adversaries with the highest authority. But if Jupiter ♃ and Mercury ☿ cast their rays on this place, they will create leaders who lead an army against barbarians. If indeed Mercury ☿ provides testimony, he creates overseers of treasures and moneylenders. But whenever Saturn ♄ comes to this place, they will be established in great poverty. However, if Jupiter ♃ alone is found in this place, all the marks of happiness will be decreed for them. If the Moon ☽ is waxing in light and Jupiter ♃ provides his rays, they are joined to the powerful in faithful intimacy by merit of their beauty. But if Venus ♀ is found in that very place, it will create women who are prostitutes and wicked.

Under **Spica** [[notes: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo, representing the ear of grain held by the Maiden; it was historically considered a very powerful and generally fortunate influence]] itself, if the Ascendant is found, it will create bakers, but those who hold leadership among their colleagues.

Near **Spica**, if the Ascendant is there, it will create unhappy, poor, and miserable men, established in the greatest penury.

If the eighth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create religious, just men, distinguished by magnificent nobility, who are both adorned with flowing riches and rejoice in a beautiful offspring of sons, and die in advanced age.

If the ninth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create wrestlers, and those who in all contests always obtain the beautiful marks of victory crowns.

If the tenth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create thieves, always foul with an unbridled desire for possessing.

If the eleventh degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create athletes, but those who obtain the marks of glorious nobility; rich indeed, and husbands of wealthy women, but who finally die a violent death.

If the twelfth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create religious men carrying the greatest marks of dignity, also prophets and priests, and governors of great temples, cities, or provinces, to whom the judgments of the people are frequently entrusted; but for these, they will suffer the greatest sorrows from the misfortunes of their sons.

If the thirteenth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create *citharoedi* [[notes: Professional performers who sang while playing the *kithara*, a professional version of the lyre]], singers, and hymn-writers, melodious with strings.

If the fourteenth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create musicians who soothe the ears of men with their songs.

If the fifteenth degree of Virgo is found in the Ascendant, it will create elegant men who often seek the company of virgins, but they will have a defect in the thigh, such that blood thickened by faulty humors [[notes: In ancient medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile). An imbalance or "vitiation" of these was thought to cause specific physical ailments or temperaments]] will frequently disturb them.

The sixteenth degree of ♍ [[notes: Virgo, the Maiden]], if found in the Ascendant [[notes: The *horoscopus* or "horoscope" refers to the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, considered the most important point in a natal chart]], will create great men who often manage many affairs, but who finally die a violent death [[notes: *Biothanata morte* refers to a death that is unnatural, violent, or premature]].

The seventeenth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create gladiators assigned to public entertainments.

The eighteenth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create blessed men, even high priests, learned men, and friends of kings, who are always loved by women. But if ♂ [[notes: Mars, the planet of war and violence]] should be in this same degree, or in its setting [[notes: "Setting" refers to the western horizon, the point opposite the Ascendant]], he will cause them to perish in a public execution or die a violent death because of a woman.

The nineteenth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create architects, builders, masons, or marble-workers.

The twentieth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create musicians and cithara players [[notes: The cithara was an ancient Greek and Roman stringed instrument similar to a lyre]], even those who sing poems with sweet modulation; however, these men will pursue the patronage of protectors, always securing favor for themselves among men through loving service.

The twenty-first degree of Virgo, if found in the Ascendant—that is, in the "extreme foot" [[notes: Ancient astronomers often described degrees by their position on the "body" of the constellation's figure]]—will create men who involve themselves in many types of business, and to whom legal judgments are frequently entrusted, or who always seek the friendship of judges.

The twenty-second degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant—which is the degree of the "outer boundary"—will create men harassed by a demon [[notes: *Daimon* in this context could refer to a malevolent spirit or a specific type of mental affliction]]. But if ♂ should be in this same degree, or in its setting, he will cause them to be captured by pirates and perish at sea.

The twenty-third degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create sailors and those who traverse the seas with constant labors.

The twenty-fourth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create men exhausted by the persistent labors of life.

The twenty-fifth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create litigious men who are moved to lawsuits for any trivial cause.

The twenty-sixth degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create men of good character, shining with praiseworthy discipline.

The twenty-seventh degree of ♍, if found in the Ascendant, will create the idle and the lazy, who engage in no activity in life.

The twenty-eighth degree of Virgo, if found in the Ascendant, will create wealthy men, very rich with many possessions.

The twenty-ninth degree of Virgo, if found in the Ascendant, will create religious men of holy mind, always intent upon divine matters.

The thirtieth degree of Virgo, if found in the Ascendant, will create fools and the insane, who use no reason at all.

-> ### CHAPTER XXV: THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF ♎ <-

[[notes: *Myriogenesis* is a Greek-derived term meaning "the origin of ten thousand," referring here to the specific influences of each of the 360 degrees of the zodiac.]]

**P**rinted in the first degree of ♎ [[notes: Libra, the Scales]], if it is found in the Ascendant, it will create a man with a beautiful body, adorned with the grace of a lovable beauty. If, however, ♄ [[notes: Saturn, the planet of restriction and discipline]] should be in this degree, he will keep the entire body healthy and unharmed.

The second degree of ♎, if found in the Ascendant—because there are many stars in this degree, some of which are masculine and some feminine—it must be noted that if anyone has their Ascendant in these masculine stars, he will be a noble singer of hymns to whom the secrets of the gods are entrusted. If, however, it is in the feminine stars, he will be a *cinaedus* [[notes: A *cinaedus* was a Roman term for a man who took a "passive" or "effeminate" role, often a public performer; the text suggests a person of charm but social stigma]], yet always loved because of his wit and dear to everyone.

The third degree of ♎, if found in the Ascendant, will create priests who are just, holy, and long-lived in a happy age.

The fourth degree of ♎, if found in the Ascendant, will create cithara players and musicians adorned with sweet-sounding voices.

The fifth degree of ♎, if found in the Ascendant, will create the rich and the wealthy, and those who are always occupied in legal judgments.

The sixth degree of ♎, if found in the Ascendant, will create wealthy men who manage many business duties.

If the seventh part of ♎ [[notes: Libra]] is found in the horoscope [[notes: the "horoscope" here refers specifically to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], with ♂ [[notes: Mars]] present, it will cause them to be captured by pirates and perish by a cruel death; or, torn apart by wars, it will compel them to die a wretched death.

If the eighth part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make bath-keepers, menial servants, and attendants of the waters.

If the ninth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make gamblers, well-known by the common people. This part also renders one very skilled in letters and learning.

If the tenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make passive homosexuals and catamites [[notes: the Latin terms *pathicos* and *cinaedos* refer to men who took a passive role in sexual encounters, which carried significant social stigma and "infamy" in Roman law and custom]], struck by public infamy. But if this is the birth-chart of a woman, she will be a prostitute with passive lustful desires.

If the eleventh part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make those with dropsy [[notes: *hydropicos*, an archaic medical term for edema or the abnormal accumulation of fluid in the body]], swollen, and destined to perish from this death.

If the twelfth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make men who are involved in legal judgments and known to everyone.

If the thirteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make them religious and just, and those to whom public judgments are entrusted, and whom kings always love with friendly affection; these also, in advanced age, shall die a natural death [[notes: literally "die their own death," meaning a peaceful death from natural causes rather than violence]].

If the fourteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make sculptors who fashion the likenesses of the gods with wondrous artistry.

If the fifteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make a queen without sons, short-lived [[notes: *oligochroniam*]], and destined to perish by a violent death [[notes: *biothanatam*]].

If the sixteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make merchants, but specifically those who always bring in foreign wares.

If the seventeenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope—namely in the northern part—and with the ☽ [[notes: Moon]] well-placed, full of light, and moving toward benevolent planets, it will make men of letters, and scribes of kings, or those to whom the office of dictating [[notes: an official who composed or dictated formal documents]] is committed; and for that reason especially, they will be conspicuous with the great honor of nobility.

If the eighteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will cause one to be raised on a cross by order of the emperor, or to be tortured in his presence, or to be hanged by order of the prince; but all this will happen only when ♂ [[notes: Mars]] is found in that same part.

If the nineteenth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will cause men to be captured and dragged away in a sudden raid of enemies.

If the twentieth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope—namely in the northern part—it will make physicians, conspicuous for the most celebrated nobility of their art. But if ♂ [[notes: Mars]] is found in that part, he will deal with measures and weights, but it will make the man die without children or heirs.

If the twenty-first part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make geometers and men of mathematics, but it will render them short-lived.

If the twenty-second part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, with ♂ [[notes: Mars]] present, it will cause them to perish by a cruel death, having fallen from a high place.

If the twenty-third part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make a king, who nevertheless, though leaving many survivors behind, shall die by the sword.

If the twenty-fourth part of ♎ is found in the horoscope, it will make merchants who bring foreign wares by ship. But if ♂ [[notes: Mars]] is found in that same part, or in the setting position [[notes: the *occasus*, or the western horizon/Descendant]], these same men shall be slaughtered after being captured by pirates at sea.

If the twenty-fifth part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make blacksmiths, or those who always work with metallic things.

If the twenty-sixth part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make weavers and loom-workers, but whose minds are shaken by the malady of insanity.

If the twenty-seventh part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make incense-sellers, or pigment-sellers, or pharmacists.

If the twenty-eighth part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make priests and temple ministers, but wealthy ones.

If the twenty-ninth part of Libra is found in the horoscope, it will make them religious, just, benevolent, and adorned with every goodness.

-> ## CHAPTER XXVI. THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF SCORPIO (♏︎) <-

If the first degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make enchanters who are able to soothe pains by the power of words.
[[margin: p]] If the second degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make foul men, often polluted by the squalor of prostitution.
If the third degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make men who are dwarfs, hunchbacked, deformed, and ridiculous.
If the fourth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will similarly make dwarfs, but those assigned to the delights of kings or emperors [[notes: Referring to the historical practice of keeping "court dwarfs" as entertainers or companions in royal households]].
If the fifth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, and the **Moon** (☽) is well-positioned, it will make men noble, just, and religious, who, being distinguished by excellent family connections, shall have many children. If, however, they are of a scholarly or interpretive profession, they will derive their life's sustenance from it; they will be royal scribes, handling literary duties, whom the loyal friendship of kings shall ennoble.
If the sixth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make priests who are rich and have many children, but these frequently die through the indignation of kings or princes.
If the seventh degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will cause men to perish having been torn by the cruel bite of beasts.
If the eighth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make men artisans, laboring in the work of the mechanical arts. But they are destined to die struck by either an asp or a viper.
If the ninth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make cultivators of gardens who are always devoted to their care.
If the tenth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make such men who die while still in their early youth.
If the eleventh degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make **inspired** [[notes: The Latin *entheos* suggests being "filled with God" or divinely possessed]] priests, giving true answers to those who seek them.
If the twelfth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make servants of temples, or those assigned to the service of the saints.
If the thirteenth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, and the **Moon** (☽) is established in any **angle** [[notes: The "cardinal" points or angles of a birth chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions]], it will make judges who carry the greatest marks of dignity, even judging the sentences of other judges, and having the highest power over human life and death. But this power is decreed for them until their 30th or 35th year. These will also have wives and children, but in the 27th, 42nd, and 58th years of their life, they will encounter **climacterics** [[notes: Critical turning points or "dangerous years" in a person's life according to ancient medicine and astrology]] and dangers; if these are extended to the 66th year, they will then utterly perish. Nevertheless, they will suffer a certain vice in life, and finally die by the sword, or iron, or in water, or by some other sudden death.
If the fourteenth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make men unstable in their senses, and using no reason at all.
If the fifteenth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make men idle, sluggish, and lazy, who weary themselves with no action in life.
If the sixteenth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make bakers. But if the Moon is in any sign with a bright star, they will be judges, prevailing with great license and power. If, however, **Mars** (♂) is found in a **place of dejection** [[notes: A "fall" or "depression," a sign where a planet's influence is considered weakened or corrupted]], it will make **executioners** [[notes: The Latin *spiculatores* refers to scouts or guards who often doubled as executioners]], who cut off the necks of men with a drawn sword.
If the seventeenth degree of Scorpio is found in the horoscope, it will make goldsmiths, gilders, gold-leaf makers, and those who work in gold.
If the eighteenth degree of Scorpio (♏︎) is found in the horoscope, it will make men wickedly torn by beasts.

Elated by this excessive increase in good fortune, they may even contemplate rebellion to seize the empire. For they will be bold and reckless, leaving surviving sons after their death, though they themselves may die by fire or by offending the king.**

**If the twenty-second degree of Scorpio—that is, the first left foot in Scorpio—is found in the Ascendant, it will create cultivators of gardens. If the second, it causes death by beasts; if the third, it produces barbers. If the fourth, it causes one to be killed by pirates or torn by beasts and slain in damp places.**

### -> CHAPTER XXVII. THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF SAGITTARIUS ($\text{\Sagittarius}$) <-
[[notes: "Myriogenesis" refers to a system where every individual degree of the 360-degree zodiac is assigned a specific destiny or character trait.]]

[[gloss: P]] **The first degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope [[notes: In ancient astrology, the "horoscope" refers specifically to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], will make people noble, religious, and just, and those upon whom the greatest marks of glory are conferred. But if a benevolent star [[notes: Usually referring to Jupiter or Venus]] is positioned in this degree, it will create kings, or those close to kings, who carry out all their business effectively.

**The second degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men furious, perjurers, treacherous, and even sacrilegious.

**The third degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will cause one to lose an eye, by whatever means or manner.

**The fourth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make guardians of monuments, undertakers, and embalmers [[notes: The Latin *pollinctores* were those who prepared bodies for the funeral pyre]].

**The fifth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make people impure, immodest, wretched, and polluted by the stain of foul infamy.

**The sixth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, makes people dwarfs, hunchbacks, those with varicose veins, the disabled, and ultimately *biothanatos* [[notes: A Greek-derived term used in Latin astrology for those who die a violent or unnatural death]].

**The seventh degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men just and religious, to whom public judgments are entrusted, such that they may pass sentences upon the judgments of others.

**The eighth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, with Jupiter ($\text{\Jupiter}$) present, will make people long-lived and religious, and foremost among their kin; they will have many sons, and be interpreters or teachers of kings, as well as scribes and those handling the duties of sacred letters, from which—in the course of their lives—marks of happiness may be conferred upon them, and they shall fail by a good death.

**The ninth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make astrologers, prophets, diviners, those who are inspired [[notes: *Entheos*, meaning possessed by a god]], and worshipers of the gods.

**The tenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make athletes, heavy-armed gladiators [[notes: *Oplomachos* were a class of gladiators who fought with a large shield and a spear or sword]], and those who are always training with the sword.

**The eleventh degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men who, struck down in a hostile war, perish cruelly.

**The twelfth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men dangerous and reckless, who, by a perverse fire of greed, will willingly approach every wickedness.

**The thirteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make those possessed by a patricidal [[notes: The urge or madness to kill one's own parents or close relatives]] fury, likewise dying as *biothanatos*.

[[notes: The original text omits the 14th degree and provides two different entries for the 15th degree.]]

**The fifteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make lyre-players devoted to public pleasures, but who have a defect in the eye.

**The fifteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make mechanics who, while making instruments necessary for war, themselves die wretchedly in battle.

**The sixteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, with Mars ($\text{\Mars}$) present, a man will indeed die mangled by a spear, while a woman will perish in childbirth.

**The seventeenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make athletes. But if Mars ($\text{\Mars}$) provides testimony [[notes: An astrological term meaning the planet "aspects" or looks toward this degree]], it will make hunters. If Jupiter ($\text{\Jupiter}$), it will make most fit keepers of horses.

**The eighteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make thieves, perjurers, malicious and spiteful people, childless, and *biothanatos*.

**The nineteenth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men *pancratiasts* [[notes: Athletes who competed in the *pancratium*, an ancient Greek combat sport combining wrestling and boxing]] and athletes, but dying without children.

**The twentieth degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, and ridiculous.

**The twenty-first degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, will make men who consume much food and who deny the property of others [[notes: Likely meaning they embezzle or refuse to return what is held in trust]].

**The twenty-second degree** of Sagittarius, if found in the horoscope, with Jupiter ($\text{\Jupiter}$) present, will make great and powerful men, possessing the lowest reaches of the earth. For these will be such that armies of infantry and cavalry are committed to them, to whom even naval battle is often entrusted. In which also many wars...

...they will form [a plan/government] and will even subjugate barbarian cities, some of which they will restore, while others they will utterly destroy. They will also have children and wives, though these will have defects and scars in necessary [[notes: likely meaning "intimate" or "private"]] places; they themselves, while warring in foreign lands, will die a **biothanatus** [[notes: from the Greek *biothanatos*, meaning a violent or unnatural death, often considered a cursed fate in antiquity]].

**The twenty-third degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope [[notes: the *horoscopus* refers to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], will cause one to perish in deserted and hidden places, torn apart by wild beasts.

**The twenty-fourth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make one a tamer of horses or a charioteer. If, however, Jupiter (♃) is in that same place, it will make them royal charioteers or mule-drivers, but those who achieve the highest marks of glory for this reason. But if Mars (♂) is testimony there, it will cause them to perish by a violent death.

**The twenty-fifth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make one a drunkard and intoxicated, especially if Mars (♂) is found in that same part. If, however, Venus (♀) offers testimony, it will make them **cinaedi** [[notes: a derogatory term for men who were perceived as effeminate or passive in sexual roles]], who are condemned by public infamy; the women, however, will be harlots.

**The twenty-sixth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make those polluted by a corrupting contagion [[notes: likely referring to disease or moral vice]]; the women, however, will be **viragines** [[notes: "viragos" or women who take on masculine roles/traits]], harlots, and devoted to every crime of lust.

**The twenty-seventh degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will cause men to pass away by a miserable death in deserted places. If Mars (♂) is found in that same part, it will make them **oligochronios** [[notes: short-lived]] and unhappy, and those who die from a sharp blow.

**The twenty-eighth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make donkey-drivers and muleteers and those who are entangled in constant labors.

**The twenty-ninth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, captives, and objects of ridicule.

**The thirtieth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make **physicos** [[notes: natural philosophers or physicians]] without favor and envious, whose death is caused by wild beasts. If Mars (♂) is in that same part, they will be short-lived and childless.

In the final line of Sagittarius, and above the tail, those who are born will be potters. Those born below the tail will be one-eyed and cross-eyed, but very swift runners, though subjugated under the power of others. These people will often be disturbed by "blood" [[notes: likely referring to a sanguine temperament or blood-related ailments]], and they will have long faces, but they will pass away by a miserable death, torn by a four-legged animal. On the right side of Sagittarius rises the **Argo Navis** [[notes: The Ship Argo constellation]], and on the left, the **Dog** [[notes: Canis Major, containing the star Sirius]].

Those who have their horoscope in the **Ship** will be ship-owners or captains of ships, or merchants, but those who sail to the West. But if Mars (♂) looks upon this same place, they will be killed by pirates while returning to the East.

Those who have their horoscope in the **Dog** will be litigious and noisy. If, however, Mercury (☿) is found in that same place, they will be excellent advocates, friends of kings, and distinguished orators.

Those who have their horoscope in the mouth of the Dog will lead a base life with a "polluted mouth" [[notes: possibly meaning foul-mouthed, prone to slander, or practicing oral sex, which was stigmatized]], but puffed up with an abundance of flowery speech.

-> ### CHAPTER 28: THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF SATURN (♄) <-

[[meta: Large decorative initial P]]
**T**he **first degree of Saturn** [[notes: "Saturn" here represents the sign he rules, Capricorn]] if found in the horoscope, will make one a king and a prince, and one upon whom the greatest signs of power are conferred.

**The second degree of Capricorn**, if found in the horoscope, will produce teachers of waging war, and those to whom the arrangement of battles is entrusted; but these will die unhappily by a violent death.

**The third degree of Capricorn**, if found in the horoscope—with Mars (♂) present and the Moon (☽) well-placed—will make men great and powerful, and those who possess the greatest "power of the sword" [[notes: *ius gladii*, the legal authority to sentence people to death]], but who always exercise their judgments severely and cruelly. For these will be cruel, ingenious, bold, and killers of many; they will also be leaders of great armies, but they will die in battle.

**The fourth degree of Saturn** [[notes: Capricorn]], if found in the horoscope—with Mercury (☿) present—will make musicians or artisans, but those who pursue women with "preposterous" [[notes: perverted or contrary to nature]] loves of lust, and they shall be negligent in all things. If, however, the Moon (☽) is well-placed, it will make scribes and nobles, to whom the duties of great affairs are entrusted, as well as wealthy, just, and religious men who die at a great age.

**The seventh part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope, will make curious craftsmen, whose noble skill commends them, and friends of kings. However, with the testimony of malevolent stars [[notes: Such as Mars]], doctors will also be born in this part.**

**The ninth part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope while Mars is present, will make men fail in the first stage of life [[notes: Meaning they may die young or face early misfortune]]. But if Venus provides testimony, he will make moneylenders and rich men, but those who die because of their own money.**

**The tenth part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope while Mars is present, will make adulterers, but with a lovely grace of beauty, who nevertheless corrupt the wives of their friends with a perverted desire of love. Truly, they are never caught and exposed in that crime; rather, they are granted the greatest supports of life through some skill. Yet they themselves will obtain wives corrupted by adultery, and finally, at the very end of their lives, they will fail by a sudden death.**

**The eleventh part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope, will make craftsmen who are gilders and gold-leaf makers, and those who practice such things.**

**The twelfth part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope, will make an athlete of great virtue [[notes: Or strength]], but one who dies a "biothanatus" [[notes: A Greek-derived term meaning one who dies a violent, unnatural, or premature death]].**

They will also be perjurers and corrupters of lusts, yet they may sweetly sing the measures of songs with a thin voice, and for the most part deceive everyone with a faked simplicity; they are foul-mouthed, noisy, and those who obtain no joy from either wives or children. Furthermore, in the process of age, they will be limping in their feet, and will obtain their life's support from commerce or from the public treasury.**

They will, however, be negligent, and those who delight in many banquets. But if Mercury is found in that place, having been promoted by domestic recommendation, they will arrive at the friendships of kings.**

**The fifteenth part of Saturn, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, and ridiculous.**

-> #### CHAPTER XXIX: THE GENESIS OF THE MYRIAD PARTS OF AQUARIUS ♒ <-

**The first degree of Aquarius ♒**, if found in the horoscope with Jupiter ♃ and Saturn ♄ present, or looking upon the horoscope with a trine aspect [[notes: A "trine" or *trigonica radiatio* is an astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, generally considered a very harmonious and powerful influence.]], and with the Moon ☽ well placed, will make great and glorious kings, who are also *polychronios* [[notes: From the Greek *poly-chronios*, meaning "long-lived"]], possessing the circle of all the lands, and to whom the greatest power is decreed in the passage of time; yet they shall perish in water.
**The second degree of Aquarius ♒**, if found in the horoscope, will make artisans of the arts pertaining to ornament or painting; they shall die their own natural death, leaving surviving children.
**The third degree of Aquarius**, if found in the horoscope with Jupiter ♃ present, or looking upon the horoscope with any aspect, will make men great and powerful, possessing many lands; however, they may suffer the loss of their inheritance, yet by their own strength they shall attain the greatest resources of wealth. They shall also conquer their own people and be inclined toward every deed of cruelty, rejoicing in the slaughter of many men. They will have sons by handmaidens, but will lose them at an immature age. They will be removed from all sadness; they will displease everyone and disparage everyone, so that for this reason all their friends avoid them. They will furthermore be gluttons, consuming much food, but possessing much land and attaining many marks of power in the process of time. But when they have entered the threshold of old age, their bodies weakened by their previous labors, they will cultivate the fields.
**The fourth degree of Aquarius ♒**, if found in the horoscope, will make worshipers of the gods who deliver judgments on the opinions of others; nevertheless, they shall perish unhappily by a *biothanata* [[notes: A Greek-derived term used in Latin astrology to denote a violent or unnatural death]] death.
**The fifth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the horoscope, will make such men as end their lives unhappily by the noose [[notes: i.e., by hanging]].
**The sixth degree of Aquarius ♒**, if found in the horoscope, will make drawers of water, burdened by the wretched weight of labor, or perhaps noble athletes.
**The seventh degree of Aquarius**, if found in the horoscope and if Venus ♀ is joined to it by any aspect, will make men long-lived, rich, and just, who prosper greatly in old age; they shall finally die their own death, leaving surviving children.

If the thirtieth degree of Aquarius is found in the Ascendant [[notes: The 'horoscopus' refers to the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], and if Saturn ♄ is positioned there with the Moon ☽, joined by whatever aspect [[notes: 'Radiatione' refers to the geometric angles or 'aspects' (like square or trine) between planets]], it will make the individuals noble and long-lived; in the course of time, all the marks of happiness shall be bestowed upon them. Some will also cross the great sea for the sake of business. However, they will certainly be without children of their own, holding their stepchildren in the place of sons. Outside of these specific degrees of Aquarius, there rise together with the sign: the Scythe, the Wolf, the Hare, the Lesser Aquarius [[notes: Likely referring to a specific group of stars within or near the constellation]], and the Altar.

Those born under the **Scythe** shall be plowmen who, cultivating the fields, gather great stores of grain.

Those born in the **Mouth of the Wolf** shall be dancers, but if Mars ♂ bears witness [[notes: 'Bearing witness' means the planet is in a position to influence that part of the sky]], they shall be miserably devoured by dogs.

Those born in the **Wolf** itself shall be deceitful, thieves, cruel, and murderers, who strike both their own kin and strangers with a cruel, wild atrocity; but these, dying as *biothanati* [[notes: A Greek-derived term used in astrology for those who die a violent, premature, or unnatural death]], shall be left even in their graves to the beasts.

In the **Left Foot of the Wolf**, if Mars ♂ bears witness, those born there will be struck by bandits and will suffer a severe weakening of the feet.

In the **Right Foot of the Wolf**, those born there will become frantic [[notes: Likely 'phrenetici', referring to a state of delirium or madness]] and will die in the first stage of life.

In the **Head of the Lesser Aquarius**, those born there will wander much through deserted places and live within them; perhaps some will be dedicated to the practice of fowling [[notes: The hunting or trapping of birds]].

In the **Right Hand of the Lesser Aquarius**, those born there will be masters of horses. But if benevolent stars bear witness, they shall be made charioteers or the King's mule-drivers.

In the **Belly of the Lesser Aquarius**, those born there will be cultivators of gardens, moneylenders, and hardworking, but they will be *biothanati* [[notes: Again, referring to a violent or unnatural end]].

In the **Right Foot of the Lesser Aquarius**, those born there will die unhappily in watery and damp places.

Those born in the **Altar** shall obtain the necessities of life from sacrifices, yet they shall perish consumed by fire.

In the **Pouring of the Water** [[notes: Referring to the stream of water flowing from Aquarius's urn]], those born there will be wealthy from their earliest years and possessors of many goods, but they will squander their paternal inheritance through various extravagances. They will be generous, but many people will frequently be ungrateful toward them. Nevertheless, in the progress of their life, they will achieve the greatest increases in both inheritance and dignity, and they shall see their enemies subdued in every way.

Those born in the **Hare** will be poor, unhappy, timid, and wanderers, striving for their labors in vain.

### -> CHAPTER XXX: THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES IN PISCES <-

[[notes: 'Myriogenesis' refers to the specific influences of each of the 360 degrees of the zodiac. The term implies 'ten thousand origins'.]]

**P**irist degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, it will make people inquisitive and composed, obtaining the means of life from distinguished resources; they may take up children from the union with sisters or relatives, acquired through incestuous intercourse.

Second degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, it will make men of a grating mind, suspicious and jealous.

Third degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, it will make people impure, entangled in the vices of lust and polluted by the squalor of harlotry, whose lives are always vexed by public infamy.

Fourth degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, it will make *cinaedi* [[notes: A term for men perceived as effeminate or who take a passive role in same-sex relations, often carrying heavy social stigma in Roman culture]] of effeminate character; it will make women prostitute their modesty in a common trade of lust.

Fifth degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, and if Mercury ☿ and Venus ♀ are joined to it by any aspect, it will make people wealthy, noble, and long-lived, who obtain their livelihood through some art. These people will also be introduced to kings, and having advanced to a good old age with surviving children, they will die well.

Sixth degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, it will make men who die being cruelly torn apart by beasts.

Seventh degree of Pisces: If found in the Ascendant, with Mars ♂ present, it will cause them to be torn apart either by beasts on land or by "fishes" [[notes: Likely referring to sea monsters or sharks]] in the water.

**The eighth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope [[notes: In historical astrology, the "horoscope" usually refers specifically to the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.]], with **Venus (♀)** and **Mercury (☿)** present, will make men who are religious, just, and long-lived; they will handle the duties of the learned, be known to kings, and serve as their scribes. They will die at an advanced age, leaving surviving children.

**The ninth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, decrees the same as we said was decreed in the eighth part above.

**The tenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, with the **Moon (☽)** well-positioned and present there, will make men great, powerful, and known to everyone. They will be connected to kings, traveling through many lands and sailing the great sea. These men will even be placed in charge of *Liburnians* [[notes: Fast, agile warships used originally by the Liburnians of the Adriatic and later the Roman Navy.]] and entrusted with naval command; they will be victors and superiors in battle. They will also possess the greatest merit of love and grace, being just and religious, but they are always restless regarding female intercourse [[notes: Implying a high or uncontrollable sex drive.]]. Though they perform great deeds and obtain all they desire, they will die a *biothanatus* [[notes: From the Greek 'biothanatos,' referring to a violent, unnatural, or premature death, such as execution or suicide.]] through the deceit or anger of a king.

**The eleventh part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men who are torn by wild beasts in desert places and lose their nature [[notes: Likely a reference to emasculation or loss of physical integrity.]], or they will die as *biothanati* in damp lands in their youth, without children or heirs.

**The twelfth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make fishermen, but they will be "phrenetic" [[notes: Afflicted with 'phrenitis,' a historical medical term for delirium or mental inflammation.]] and will die in their youth.

**The thirteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, with **Venus (♀)** and **Jupiter (♃)** present, will make men rich and noble, following some art to obtain the substance of their life. If, however, **Mercury (☿)** is joined to it by any radiation [[notes: "Radiation" refers to an aspect, or a specific geometric relationship between planets.]], it will make merchants or *pigmentarii* [[notes: These were people who dealt in "pigments," which in the ancient world included pharmacists, perfumers, and painters.]], yet they will be rich and happy, and die with surviving children.

**The fourteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men upon whom the greatest insignia of dignity are conferred, but they will be killed in watery or damp places, or by pirates.

**The fifteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, with **Mars (♂)** present, will make men who wander through the deserts of the earth and sail through unknown seas; for these men will always be tormented by labors and will spend their lives upon ships.

**The sixteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men rich and long-lived, and foremost among their other kinsmen.

**The seventeenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, makes men who sing songs with sweet melody. If, however, **Mars (♂)** is found in that same part, these men will hang themselves with a noose.

**The eighteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men bold and great consumers of food, but sickly.

**The nineteenth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make orators and advocates, distinguished by an abundance of learned speech. If a benevolent star [[notes: Usually Jupiter or Venus.]] lends its testimony to it, they will be in the royal house, commanding many things, always adorned with great modesty, gravity of character, and honorable conversation, and beloved by everyone.

**The twentieth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men who wander through many nations, but if **Mars (♂)** offers testimony to it, they will be captives and slaves in their youth.

**The twenty-first part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men murderers, and those who are easily moved to brawls by their bile [[notes: In the theory of the Four Humors, "yellow bile" was thought to cause irritability and anger.]].

**The twenty-second part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men shameless, and indeed defiled by every kind of foul lust.

**The twenty-third part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make *aucupes* [[notes: Fowlers or bird-catchers.]] and those who obtain the substance of life only from birds.

**The twenty-fourth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make men who, while sailing the sea, end their lives there.

**The twenty-fifth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, will make goldsmiths, engravers, painters, and those who are nourished by these arts.

**The twenty-sixth part of Pisces (♓)** if found in the horoscope, with **Mars (♂)** and **Saturn (♄)** offering testimony, will make bath-keepers, *mediastini* [[notes: Menial servants or drudges, often working in the city or in bathhouses.]], and sailors; also those to whom the duties of mechanical engineering are entrusted, but they will be unhappy and die as *biothanati*.

-> B O O K  E I G H T <-

If the twenty-seventh degree of Pisces [[notes: ♓]] is found in the ascendant [[notes: The 'horoscopus' refers to the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], it will make fugitives, wandering through many lands, but who may perish pierced by a thorn [[notes: Could also imply a sting or a sharp point]].

If the twenty-eighth degree of Pisces is found in the ascendant, with **Mars** [[notes: ♂]] present, it will make men who are torn apart by wild beasts in damp and watery places.

If the twenty-ninth degree of Pisces is found in the ascendant, and if **Jupiter** [[notes: ♃]] and **Venus** [[notes: ♀]] are placed in that same degree, and the **Moon** [[notes: ☽]] is well-positioned, it will make men noble and wealthy, who, living happily through their whole lives, finally pass away by their own natural death.

If the thirtieth degree of Pisces is found in the ascendant, it will make men who have their life upon the sea, and who, always entangled in laborious affairs, lead a life of the greatest toil.

In the extreme tail of Pisces—that is, in the line which divides Pisces and Aries [[notes: ♈]]—those who are born while **Mars** is present will be mutilated and severed [[notes: The Latin *apocopi* specifically suggests being castrated or having limbs cut off]]. In northern Pisces, the Stag and the Hare rise; however, in the southern part, Cetus, the sea monster, rises.

In the horns of Cetus, those who are born with **Mars** present will be commanders of arms and leaders of an army, who, fighting abroad, finally die in battle.

In the mouth of Cetus, those who are born will be of Mars [[notes: Meaning they possess a Martian temperament—aggressive or martial]]; they will track down and capture serpents, but they will be *biothanati* [[notes: This Greek-derived term refers to those who die a violent or untimely death]].

In the feet of the Stag [[notes: *Ceruus*]], those who are born will be great wanderers and will finally pass away by a violent death.

In the Hare [[notes: *Lepus*]], those who are born will be skilled pilots, to whom the rudders of ships are entrusted.

In the tail of Cetus, with **Mars** present, those who are born will lose their lives by a cruel death, torn apart by beasts.

In two parts of Cetus, with **Venus** and **Mercury** [[notes: ☿]] present, those who are born will be subject to powerful men, and advancing from there, they will achieve increases in their station of life. Others, however, will be servants, but they will be led to great dignity through the honorable and liberal merit of their service and the kindness of their patrons.

In three parts of Cetus, those who are born will sail and encompass many lands; but if **Mars** is found in that same part, they will die murdered by pirates.

## -> THE THIRD PART OF THE FOREIGN SPHERE <-
### -> ON THE FORECASTS, CHAPTER 31 <-

[[meta: Historiated initial I decorated with floral patterns.]]

**I**n many signs, we have said in the sixth book that there are bright stars, shining with royal majesty of light. Therefore, what the ascendant determines in those degrees in which bright stars are found—just as we spoke regarding the **Moon** in that same sixth book—I shall now likewise take care to explain.

In the eleventh degree of Aries, a bright constellation is shown; those born in this degree, with **Jupiter** present or joined to it by a trine aspect [[notes: *trigonica radiatione*—an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious]], will be great leaders, powerful, and friends of kings, possessing much and vast land, raised up by the honorable testimony of their reputation, and who die by their own natural death.

In the horns of Taurus [[notes: ♉]]—that is, in its 30th degree—is a bright star; those who are born in it will be kings or commanders.

In the right horn of Taurus, those who are born will be great princes, to whom command of both the navy and the infantry is committed; they are fearsome, hardworking, and liberators of many cities from the sieges of wars. These men, though born unique, shall be without children; public titles, images, and statues shall be decreed for them, but they will later die from the offense of kings. In which star of **Mars**, however, these same things are decreed, our sixth book has already shown you.

In the second degree of Leo, a clear star is found; those who are born in it will be powerful kings, possessing a double kingdom, but for whom, as often as **Saturn** [[notes: ♄]] and **Mars** come to that same star, as many times shall stirred-up battles be brought against them.

In the thirteenth degree of Virgo [[notes: ♍]] is a clear star; those who are born in it while the **Moon** is present and bright will be powerful, having great power of life and death, and to whom the greatest part of the empire is committed.

In the nineteenth degree of Virgo there is likewise a clear star; those who are born in it while the **Moon** is present and well-placed will be powerful. If **Jupiter** is joined to it by a prosperous aspect, they will be very close to the king, possessing divine honors, outstanding and good, but negligent for a little while, and to whom death comes from the indignation of the king.

-># B O O K  E I G H T.<-

In the twenty-second degree of Sagittarius [[notes: ♐]], there are certain bright stars. For those born while Jupiter [[notes: ♃]] is positioned in this sign, they shall be great and powerful, possessing much land; they shall lead armies of infantry and cavalry, and to them shall be entrusted naval warfare. They shall also be victors in all battles, subjugating barbarians; they shall restore some cities and overturn others. However, they shall have a wife afflicted in the essential parts of her body [[notes: This likely refers to reproductive health or a physical disability]], but they themselves, with their children surviving them, shall die while fighting bravely in battle.

In the third degree of Capricorn [[notes: ♑]] is a bright star. For those born with Mars [[notes: ♂]] and the Moon [[notes: ☽]] also well-placed in this sign, they shall be great and powerful, holding the highest power of life and death. Yet they shall be cruel, rejoicing in much slaughter. Nevertheless, they shall be leaders of armies, gifted, high-minded, and bold, though they shall ultimately die in war.

In the first degree of Aquarius [[notes: ♒]] is a bright star. For those born when Jupiter and Saturn [[notes: ♄]] are joined in a favorable aspect, with the Moon well-placed, they shall be great and glorious kings, religious, just, and long-lived; to them also, in their earlier years, the greatest imperial power shall be granted with the highest glory.

In the tenth degree of Pisces [[notes: ♓]] is a bright star—specifically in the Southern Fish. For those born here with Venus [[notes: ♀]] present and the Moon well-ordered, they shall be great and powerful, known to kings, and shall travel through many lands and navigate the great sea. To these also shall be committed the command of Liburnian galleys [[notes: *Liburneum*—a fast, light warship used by the Roman navy]] and naval forces; they shall be victors in battles, beloved by all, just, and religious, but prone to the company of women. They shall nonetheless achieve many things and command greater powers, though they may ultimately die condemned by the hatred or anger of a king. Indeed, these are the pronouncements of the **Barbaric Sphere** [[notes: The *Sphaera Barbarica* refers to astrological systems of non-Greek origin, such as Egyptian or Babylonian, which Firmicus integrated into his work]] concerning individual degrees, which we have explained to you most clearly.

->### CHAPTER XXXII. THE GENERAL INTERPRETATION OF THE WHOLE WORK.<-

You will not be able to explain a birth chart [[notes: *Genitura*]] fully and with integrity unless everything has been compared according to the balanced mixtures and traditions of the stars—which you remember me saying very frequently. For when the cold of other stars is set against the fiery stars, and the frost of the cold is tempered by the burning heat of the fire, this mixture is rendered according to reason. Therefore, all things must be gathered according to the powers of the locations and the stars. For a star suffers a loss of its power when it is placed in "fallen" or "humble" places [[notes: These are technical terms for 'debility,' where a planet is in a sign that weakens its influence]], but it rejoices (as we have often said) when placed in a leading position, in its "exaltation," or secondly, in its "bounds." When, therefore, all things have been gathered by this precise calculation, we must inspect the whole body of the birth chart, so that by collecting the fates of men from the powers of all the stars, we may be able to explain whatever has been decreed with true judgment.

->### CHAPTER XXXIII. THE PERORATION OF THE ENTIRE PREVIOUS WORK.<-

Accept therefore, Mavortius [[notes: Lollianus Mavortius, a high-ranking Roman official and Firmicus’s patron]], our glory, what we promised you (albeit with great trepidation of spirit): namely, these seven books, composed according to the order and number of the seven stars [[notes: Although there are eight books, the first is an introductory defense of astrology, leaving seven for the technical discipline]]. For the first book only took up the defense of our patronage; in the remaining books, we have delivered the discipline of a new work to the Roman people. You, however, having been cautioned by my previous warning and bound by the religious authority of an oath, must guard these books with a pure spirit and a pure mind, lest the knowledge of this work be disclosed to unlearned and sacrilegious ears. For the nature of divinity wished, from the beginning, to be hidden and concealed by many coverings, lest it be easily accessible to all, and lest the origin of its majesty be cheapened if opened to everyone. It is fitting that we also do this in these books: namely, that their reading should be open only to the religious, but always denied to the profane and sacrilegious, lest we pollute the hidden commentaries of the ancients with somewhat wicked publications. Therefore, hand these down only to your sons, whom you have trained from their earliest years to every duty of virtue; hand them also to your friends, whom a faithful bond of love has joined to you, and whom you know follow the examples of your virtue. Let it suffice that we have produced the skill of these books for you alone; we entrust them to you, we believe in you, we consecrate them to you. You are the true interpreter, the faithful guardian, the religious priest; you alone, by the merit of your virtues, will be able to adorn that which we have perfected through sleepless care and the labor of both mind and body, and with the greatest anxiety and trepidation.

->## JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS JUNIOR, OF SICILY, *VIR CLARISSIMUS* [[notes: A title of senatorial rank]].<-
->## TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANUS, PROCONSUL.<-

# CL. PTOLEMY
## OF PELUSIUM, ALEXANDRIAN
## THE FOUR-PART TREATISE.

### ->P R E F A C E.<-

[[insert: Large decorative initial R decorated with floral and figure motifs]]
**O**F THE MATTERS, Syrus [[notes: Syrus was the person to whom Ptolemy dedicated his major works, including the *Almagest*; little is known of him historically]], in which the perfection of the science of the stars consists, we find two to be the greatest and most principal. Of these, the first which precedes, and is the more powerful, is the science which demonstrates the configurations of the sun and moon, as well as the five wandering stars [[notes: The "wandering stars" are the five planets visible to the naked eye: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn]], which occur by reason of their own motions, and their relationship to one another and to the earth. The second, however, is the science by which the changes and effects which happen and are completed on account of the natural configurations of their orbits are explained within those things which they surround. But since the first of these two is a science unto itself and unmixed with the other, it is necessary that the investigator of science seek and learn it for its own sake, and here receive the fruit, even if he does not learn the second science. Since, therefore, it is manifest that this is so, the volume of the first science by itself has already been completed by us [[notes: A reference to his previous work, the *Almagest*, which dealt with mathematical astronomy]], in which we proceeded rationally according to our ability. In this book, we shall explain the second science, which is by no means explainable by itself, just as physical reason requires. It is necessary, moreover, for its investigator to follow this intention: that he proceed in it by a straight path and a truthful way. Yet he should not wish to compare the method of attaining this science to the method by which the other is attained—which is always of one and the same mode—for he will disparage and reject this science if he compares them. For a brief delay in the accidents of matter [[notes: Ptolemy argues that because earthly matter is messy and constantly changing, astrology cannot be as "perfect" or predictable as the mathematical movement of the stars]], in which this science is concerned, is the occasion of change in this second science. For this matter never perseveres in the same state; therefore, one attains a perfect knowledge of this science only with great difficulty. For this reason, however, it should not be cast aside by anyone out of laziness, but rather he should strive to know what is possible to be known from it. It is indeed plain that the environment which surrounds us is the cause of most accidents and changes happening in this world. Since, however, it is the habit of many to despise things that are difficult to investigate, some—through blindness of mind and lack of skill—have accused and cast aside the first part of the science, while others have done so to the second. The reason distracting them toward these views is perhaps this: either they are like those who, because they cannot know something due to its excessive difficulty, think that others cannot know it at all; or perhaps like those who, although they are able to know, reject it because it easily slips from the memory. For these reasons, therefore, they held this science in contempt and reckoned it as nothing. We, however, before we manifest the particulars of this science, shall briefly strive to prove what is contained in it, and what can be known of the science of prognostication [[notes: Prediction or "fore-knowing"]], and what fruit follows; and from these two points we shall begin to explain how much it is that we can attain from this science.

->*The method of attaining the science of prognostication.* **Chap. II.**<-

[[insert: Decorative initial V with floral/scroll design]]
**S**INCE a certain power exists in the substance of the ether [[notes: The OCR reads "alathir," a Latinization of the Arabic *al-athir*, meaning the Aether or the "fifth element" that makes up the heavens]], which, reaching as far as earthly things, compels—indeed, forces—them to change, and since these same things likewise naturally undergo change from the two primary materials placed below the lunar circle, which are fire and air, which the motion of the ether surrounds and changes; and it surrounds the other things themselves, namely water and earth, and each of their plants, and changes them by its own changes; we believe it is a matter of doubt to no one, because the sun and the air work upon all earthly things. And that not only do alterations come to the earth from the four seasons of the year, but also in 
[[margin: A]] living creatures...

# ->CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY<-

...the conceptions of animals [[notes: The Latin *mantium* is a fragment of *animantium* (living beings/animals) continued from the previous page]], the fruits of trees, the rising of waters, and the mutations of bodies, but also from the daily rotation in which it is daily contained. For because of this rotation, the earth grows hot and becomes cold, dries out and becomes moist in one and the same way, according to the similar patterns formed according to their positions relative to our **zenith** [[notes: The point in the sky directly above an observer]]. From the **Moon** also, because she is closer to the Earth, a great force is bestowed upon us, by which changes are brought to many things, both animate and inanimate. For the flooding and receding of rivers occur according to the waning and waxing of the moon. The tides of the sea are also altered by her rising and setting. Likewise, plants and animals, in whole or in part, experience growth and decay following her waxing and waning. The revolution of the **erratic stars** [[notes: "Erratic stars" (*stellae erraticae*) refers to the planets, which appear to "wander" against the background of the fixed stars]] and the fixed stars also produces heat, winds, and snow in the air surrounding us in many ways. Therefore, according to the **complexion** [[notes: In this context, "complexion" refers to the specific combination of qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) present in the atmosphere]] of that air, alterations happen to things situated upon the earth. And according to their configurations relative to one another, which they receive from their conjunction and the mixing of their strengths, various changes of things occur. 

Beyond this, the efficacy of the **Sun** always prevails over the others in the variations of things that proceed more regularly. Truly, others sometimes assist it and sometimes hinder it, which occurs more evidently and frequently in the Moon—as in her conjunction, her **dichotomy** [[notes: The "dichotomite" refers to the first or last quarter moon, when the disk appears exactly half-illuminated]], and the full moon. In the other stars, however, this happens in a circuit of longer time and with more hidden significance, according to the hours of their occultation [[notes: When a planet is hidden by another body or the sun's light]], apparition, and their declination toward any latitude. Since, therefore, the work of the stars is of this nature, it is necessary that what they perform by their motions appears not only in manifest things, but also in the very beginning of the birth of seeds and fruits, so that their forms and modes are designated [[margin: the power of the stars]] according to the qualities of the air at that very hour. 

For this reason, farmers and keepers of livestock, who are highly experienced, can grasp what is to come through the blowing of the winds at the hour of the animals' mating and the sowing of seeds. Generally, we also recognize that universal things, which are declared through the configurations of the Sun, the Moon, and the stars, are clear and open. Indeed, those skilled in this art frequently recognize their prognostications through experiments with the Sun. Even those effects of the stars which occur with the greatest force, and which are accustomed to happen naturally, are predicted by the unlearned—and even by certain animals. For we see very many animals signify the variations of the seasons of the year and the changes of the winds, which are called *aulia*. We do not doubt that this happens because the cause of these significations is most frequently the Sun. 

However, those things which occur with lesser force are predicted only by those with frequent experience, such as individual changes of winter air and long-term winds predicted by sailors. It is manifest that these things happen through the configurations of the Moon and the fixed stars with the Sun. But because people have remained ignorant of the locations of the stars, the hours of the predicted events, and the motions of the erratic stars (which greatly assist the knowledge of the aforementioned things), they have many times been deceived in this science. Since this is so, if anyone should have knowledge of the motions of all the stars, the Sun, and the Moon—so that he truly knows the places and hours in which their configurations are formed—and should he not forget their natures (which he has learned through the experiments of many ages, even if he does not know their substantial essences), but recognizes the effects they perform, such as that the Sun heats, the Moon moistens, and similarly for the rest; and if he is capable of knowing this in a natural way, and grasps the manner of significance in their mixing through good estimation: what could then prohibit him from always knowing the future changes of the air, so that he predicts it will be now warmer, now more moist? 

Likewise, through the qualities of the air, he could grasp the qualities of the natures of all men, so that he might discern the qualities of the body and the soul, and perceive their future occurrences at certain hours. Furthermore, when the surrounding air and the nature of bodies are in such-and-after-such a state, he will predict what is conducive to health and the better action of bodies, and when it is the opposite, he will judge it to be so. From these stated things and others like them, it is manifest that we can reach the goal of this work. Those who have said that this science is to be blamed and set aside have had some reasons, however frivolous... 
->Of which<- [[notes: "Quarum" (Of which) is the catchword, indicating the first word of the following page.]]

[[summary: This page argues for the physical validity of astrology (astrometeorology) by linking celestial movements to weather, tides, and biological cycles. Ptolemy asserts that if a practitioner understands the motions and qualities of the planets, they can predict environmental changes and their subsequent effects on human health and character.]]

[[meta: This is the first page of the first book of the treatise. The text serves as an introductory defense of astrology and celestial prognostication against its critics, establishing the methodology and justifying the potential for human error.]]

-># BOOK I. 1<-

The first of these is the great deception of those who do not regard this science with authority, even though examining it requires great industry in many ways. Therefore, many have formed the opinion that its results happen by chance, even when this science has proven true. However, their reasoning is inappropriate, for this deception occurs not through a weakness in the art itself, but through the recklessness of those examining it. Indeed, the second reason is this: there are many who, in order to make a great profit, took the prognostications of other teachings and falsely ascribed them to this science. Many have been deceived by these people and were driven to the opinion that because they predicted many things through this science, they exceeded the natural limits of what could be known. Consequently, their work was the reason many people disparaged not only what cannot be known through it, but even that which is truly knowable. This reason, like the first, is inappropriate, for philosophy [[notes: In this period, "philosophy" often included the study of nature, physics, and the heavens]] should not be looked down upon because of the ignorance of fools. It is also clear that even good and accurate researchers of the sciences are sometimes deceived—not for the aforementioned reasons, but because of the nature of the subject itself and their own weakness—since they are unable to grasp the complexities inherent to this science. It also happens generally that we do not arrive at a true knowledge of any quality of this matter, but only an estimated one. This is especially true regarding that which is gathered from many and dissimilar things. It also happens that the configurations of the wandering stars [[notes: *erraticarum stellarum*, referring to the planets]] were recorded in ancient times; it is through those ancient configurations that we consider the configurations of our own times which resemble them. Based on their effects, we judge what the men of ancient authority, the observers of things, discovered through the configurations of their own times—which perhaps resemble our configurations much or little, owing to their long orbital cycles. But that these configurations should resemble them so perfectly that everything in the heavens and on the earth should return to exactly what they were then is by no means possible. Nor could this be claimed by anyone, unless they were a foolish mocker who confessed to know perfectly what no one could ever perfectly achieve, or someone claiming to have reached a point of knowledge that no mortal life is long enough to attain. For these reasons, we are sometimes deceived in the hours of our prognostications, because the examples through which we learn do not perfectly match the cases we are judging. For when we investigate atmospheric phenomena in the air, we find them difficult to discern because discovering the causes present in the air is a heavy task, even if we grasp the causes originating from the celestial bodies. And when we speak about the births of men according to the choosing of powers, we perceive in this many significant reasons which by themselves compel things to vary. For differences in "seeds" [[notes: *Seminiū*, referring here to heredity, lineage, or the biological nature of the parents]] and the qualities of parentage are of great help; for although any region and the air of that same region may be of one and the same type, a single difference in seeds possesses the power to form the image appropriate to its species—such as the seed of a man, a horse, or other beasts. Furthermore, the places of birth change things with a great mutation; for even when the seeds are of one species, such as the seed of men, and the qualities of the air are the same, they will be assigned many great differences in body and soul according to the differences of the regions in which they are born. To you also, the various customs and manners of people will in some way assist in their future individual alterations. But since not everything will agree with the conditions found in the air (though the force of the air is great in these things), it is a source of great help if those who prophesy only through the movements of the upper bodies are not [merely] aided by them; those who investigate only through the stars that which they cannot know perfectly will sometimes be deceived. Therefore, since this is the case, this entire science should not be disparaged and destroyed just because we are sometimes deceived in it. Just as the skill of sailors, who frequently err while navigating, is neither disparaged nor rejected by us, so we ought rather to remain more attentive and diligent in this study. For they promise us arduous and inestimable things; let us not doubt that which is possible to observe through it. Likewise, it is not fitting that we investigate all things through it, but only that we investigate through proper inquiry. We also say it is necessary that we grasp their subject matter, and not interpose that which is unsuitable. For just as we do not find fault with physicians when they seek the causes of illnesses and the qualities of the sick, so it should not be troublesome for us to investigate the materials, regions, foods, and all the past accidents [[notes: *accidētia*, a philosophical term meaning non-essential characteristics or events that happen to a subject]].

->**A 2** [space] **Utility**<-

[[summary: This page introduces the study of celestial science, defending it against skeptics by explaining that errors arise from human incompetence, greed, and the immense complexity of changing planetary positions and heredity, rather than flaws in the science itself.]]
[[keywords: astrology, celestial science, planetary configurations, heredity, prognostication, defense of philosophy, human error]]
