-> ### BOOK II. [[page number: 21]] <-

-> ### *On application, and separation, and other virtues. Chap. XXIV.* <-

[[margin: † That is, application.]]
[[margin: † That is, separation.]]

**T**he general rule of this chapter is that planets which precede, and those which seek a conjunction with another, are in their † **application** [[notes: Latin *alictisal*, from the Arabic *al-ittisal*. In astrology, "application" occurs when a faster-moving planet approaches an aspect with a slower one, indicating an event that is about to happen.]], unless there is a great distance between them, exceeding the sum of half the bodies of the two planets [[notes: This refers to the "moieties" or orbs of the planets; if they are too far apart, the influence is considered inactive.]], whether the **application** is by conjunction or by any of the aforementioned aspects. For this reason, it is useful to consider their latitude in the **application** of their conjunction. Similarly, it is also worthwhile to consider their latitude in the † **separation** [[notes: Latin *alnisigref*, from the Arabic *al-insiraf*. This indicates an aspect that is moving apart, representing an event that has recently passed.]] of their conjunction. In **application**, however, it is superfluous to observe the other aspects here, because all their rays are always extended to the center of the earth, and there they are joined from every side. It is also manifest from what has been said that the powers of all planets must be investigated from their own proper natures, from the [Zodiac] signs, and also from the aspects they hold in relation to the Sun, as well as the angles [[notes: The four "angles" of a chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli—are the most powerful points in a horoscope.]], according to the method described for all these things. Regarding the quantity of these powers, we should know that when they are oriental [[notes: Rising before the Sun in the morning.]] and their proper motion is increasing, they will be as strong as they can be. When their motion is decreasing and they are occidental [[notes: Setting after the Sun in the evening.]], they will be as weak as they can be. The same also happens to them according to the quality of their horizons. For when they are in the **midheaven** [[notes: *Medium Coeli*, the highest point of the path of the stars.]], or when they ascend toward the **midheaven**, they are strongest; but they gradually decline from strength according to their distance from the **midheaven**. For when they are at the very eastern point of the horizon [[notes: The Ascendant.]], they are not as strong, and in the west, even less so. And when they are beneath the earth in opposition to the **midheaven** [[notes: The *Imum Coeli*, or "Bottom of the Sky".]], or between the west and the angle of the earth, they are even less strong. Similarly, they are said to be strong when they have an association with the **ascendant** [[notes: The degree of the Zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.]] not from this, but from another figure [[notes: An aspect or configuration.]]. However, when none of these are present, they will be weak and considered to have no strength.

# ->CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPAR-<-
## ->TITE, BOOK II.<-
### ->*On the general division of this science. Chap. I.*<-

**T**hus, regarding those things in which the principles are sustained, and which must be used in the inquiry of particular prognostications, those things which have been generally set forth by us are sufficient. Now, however, as the discourse is continuous, the particulars which are perceived by this method of prognosticating shall be subjoined after the aforementioned things, in which we shall follow a direct path suitable to natural things. We shall say, therefore, that because the prognostication of the stars is divided into two parts, which are its greater and more powerful divisions: the first and more universal part is that which concerns what will happen in regions and lands, and it is called the **Universal** part; the second part, which is less universal than the former, is that by which what will happen to each individual is perceived, and it is named the **Science of Nativities** [[notes: Also known as Genethlialogy, or birth-chart astrology.]]. I have thought it worthy to prioritize the Universal part, because this universal [fate] is altered by circumstances that are stronger and greater than the particular. Therefore, because weak natures are contained under stronger ones, and particulars under universals in all their qualities, it is necessary that those who seek to observe particulars should first make haste to observe those things which are more universal and of greater cause. And since among these universal observations, some indicate the general state of regions, others of lands; some also indicate the greatest and most general impediments, such as wars, plagues [[notes: Latin *mortalitates*, referring to mass death or epidemics.]], famines, earthquakes, floods, and similar things; while others show lesser impediments than these, which occur at certain hours, such as the years, the changes of seasons, the increase and decrease of heat and cold and winds, their intensity and remission, the abundance of rain and droughts, and similar things. And because that which precedes from these two parts is the knowledge of those things which generally happen in regions, and of great impediments, on account of the aforementioned causes. In the knowledge of these things, we properly use two methods, one of which is the similarity of the signs and stars in each **climate** [[notes: "Climate" in ancient geography referred to latitudinal zones of the earth, each supposedly influenced by different celestial configurations.]], and the other is the signs in various hours and similar [times].

[[summary: This page concludes Book I by explaining how a planet's strength is determined by its motion and position in the sky, then introduces Book II, which focuses on "Universal" or Mundane astrology. Ptolemy argues that broad events like wars and plagues are more important to study than individual horoscopes because they overrule personal destiny.]]

| [[margin: Northern peoples.]] | **S**urely there are certain properties of nations which occur generally along parallel lines and the angles of the earth, because of their similarities with the circle of the signs [[notes: The Zodiac]] and with the Sun. In each of these universal parts, however, there ought to be particular qualities, arising from the qualities of the soul and natural customs. ### -> On the similarity of regions with triplicities and stars. Cap. III. <-

**S**ince, therefore, the figures of the triplicities [[notes: A "triplicity" is a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same astrological element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).]] which are formed in the circle of the signs are four, as was shown in the preceding sections: we have said that the triplicity of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius is between the north and the west, of which the first lord is Jupiter, for he is northern, and Mars is associated in lordship with him, since he is western. Indeed, the triplicity of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn is between the south and the east, of which the first lord is Venus, because she is southern, and Saturn is associated with her in lordship, for he is eastern. Moreover, the triplicity of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius is between the north and the east, of which the first lord is Saturn, since he is eastern, and Jupiter is associated with him in lordship, for he is northern. Also, the triplicity of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces is between the south and the west, of which the first lord is Mars, for he is western, to whom Venus is associated in lordship, because she is southern. Since these things are so, and the place of our habitation is divided into four parts, which are equal in number to the triplicities, its latitude is divided by a line that passes through our sea [[notes: The Mediterranean]], and begins from the place called the Passage of Hercules [[notes: The Strait of Gibraltar, traditionally the western limit of the world]], and reaches to the river which is called Citicon, and is on the mountain ridge which follows it from the eastern part, and by this line is divided that which is between the north and the south. Its longitude, however, is divided by the line that passes through the western river, and through the sea which is called Aggion Nabartis, and through the pool which is called Mantis [[notes: Likely referring to the Maeotian Marshes or Sea of Azov]], and this line divides that which is between the east and the west. These four quarters agree in arrangement with the triplicities. Therefore, the first quarter of the habitable place, which is placed between the north and the west, is in that part of the lands which are called Felitogalatiæ, and they are the lands which are generally called Europe. The quarter, however, placed in opposition to that one, between the south and the east, is in the part of the lands which are called eastern Ithosiæ [[notes: Ethiopia]], and it is the southern part of the lands called Asia Major. The third quarter, indeed, established between the north and the east, is located in the part of the lands called Sefume, and is in the northern part of Asia Major. The fourth, however, which is placed in opposition to this between the blasts of the western and southern winds, is arranged in the part of the lands called † western Ithosiæ, which [[margin: Otherwise the deserts of Libya.]] are generally named † Languages [[notes: This likely refers to the "tongues" or diverse tribes of North Africa]]. [[margin: Otherwise Inoquia]] Likewise, in each of these aforementioned quarters, that which is contained from its parts around the middle of the whole habitable earth, its order—with respect to that quarter of which it is a part—is contrary to the disposition of the same quarter with respect to the whole habitable earth. For in the quarter which is called † Vrukin, which with respect to the whole habitable earth is established [[margin: Otherwise Europe.]] between the north and the west, the order of that which is around the middle of the earth approaches the angle which is in opposition to that angle in which this quarter is shaped, and it is the south-eastern. This same thing will undoubtedly happen in the other quarters, so that each of these quarters is assimilated to two triplicities opposite to one another. Also, its parts which are around the middle of the earth are assigned to that which that part approaches, which also is assigned to the contrary of that which that quarter generally approaches. Other parts of it, however, will agree with the general quality of that quarter. It is also necessary that with the stars of the triplicity of the quarter itself, they be taken in similarity to the star which has lordship in the other triplicities. And it is necessary that in every habitation, the stars be taken which rule only that triplicity in each quarter, except in those parts which are toward the middle of the habitation, in which the star Mercury will be taken with the stars that rule the triplicities, since he is of a common and mixed nature. It is necessary therefore according to this order, that the parts which are be- [[margin: The first quarter]] tween the north and the west of the habitable earth—that is, that quarter which is called Vruben—[correspond to] the triplicities...

...triplicity which is associated with the North and West, which triplicity is gathered from Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. Generally, the masters of this triplicity will be Jupiter and Mars, provided they are **vespertine** [[notes: "Vespertine" refers to planets appearing as "evening stars," setting after the sun]]. The general nations inhabiting these parts are the people of the lands of Britain, Galatia, Germany, Bastarnia, Italy, Gaul, Apulia, and Sicily, Tyrrhenia, Celtica, and also Spain. It is therefore natural that many of the men of these regions, because of the lordship of this triplicity and their ruling stars, are not easily humbled, but instead call out for liberty. They long for arms, they are industrious and warlike, and they are skilled in governance, as well as being neat, clean, and magnanimous. 

And since Jupiter and Mars are associated in their lordship—being vespertine—and because the first parts of this triplicity are masculine while the latter parts are feminine, it happens that these nations are not jealous regarding their women, but rather think little of sexual intercourse with them. Instead, they have a greater appetite for sodomitic vice [[notes: A historical term used by the translator to describe same-sex male relations, which Ptolemy attributed to the specific planetary alignments of these regions]], and they are more prone to jealousy in that regard. He who commits this does not think he has done anything shameful; nor does the one upon whom it is committed think he has been made effeminate or soft, nor does he think it should be postponed at all. They are also accustomed to daring acts of courage and are occupied with good works and fidelity; they love their kin, and they do not neglect anything that is good, honest, and praiseworthy.

[[margin: The second.]] But the second quarter, the southern one, is a part of Greater Asia. Its constituent parts—the regions of India, the Arbalui, Gedrosia, Parthia, Babylonia, and the islands and regions of Assyria—all of which are situated in the south-eastern part of the whole habitable world, must be likened to the triplicity which is between the South and the East, composed of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. The lords of these regions are Venus and Saturn, when they are **matutinal** [[notes: "Matutinal" refers to planets appearing as "morning stars," rising before the sun]]. Wherefore the natures of those inhabiting these regions imitate the natures of these two lords. For they worship Venus and call her *Asis*, and they call Saturn the *Bright Sun*. 

There are also some among them who foretell the future; they guard and accurately observe the generative organs, holding them to be for divining, because they are likened to the aforementioned stars which are naturally generative in the same way. They also venerate their parents. They are hot-blooded men who engage much in venereal acts [[notes: Acts related to Venus; i.e., sexual acts]] and are more preoccupied with them than is proper. They are deceivers, dancers, and players of musical instruments. Their bodies are also inclined toward fleshiness; they paint and adorn themselves because of Venus, yet their customs are also full of gravity because of Saturn. Manifestly and not in secret—because of the matutinal figure—they have intercourse with women, yet they strongly abhor sodomitic vice, and thus it happens that many of them procreate children from their own wives. In this, they also demonstrate courage in their hearts, likened to the matutinal rising; and because the virtue that rules their bodies is in their hearts, they are likened to the strength of the Sun. They are also, for the most part, soft and effeminate in their way of dressing, in their grooming, and in all things pertaining to the body, because of the qualities of Venus. Yet they are also magnanimous and strong warriors, because Saturn is oriental [[notes: Rising in the east before the Sun]]. 

Furthermore, when these regions are divided, those who are from the regions of Parthia and Media will be likened to Taurus and Venus. Therefore, the inhabitants of these lands use garments having venereal [[notes: Bright or alluring]] colors with which they cover the whole body except the chest, and they are generally effeminate and delicate. But those who are likened to both Virgo and Mercury are the Babylonians and the inhabitants of the islands and the regions of Assyria. For this reason, these people are skilled in the sciences and are observers of the motions of the stars. Those who are likened to Capricorn and Saturn are the Indians and Gedrosians; therefore, they are deformed and filthy, and the qualities of their souls are most ferocious.

[[margin: The third.]] Now, the third quarter is in the northern part of the lands of Greater Asia. Its parts contain Armenia, Hyrcania, Media, Bactria, the regions of the Amazons [[notes: The Latin *mulierum regiones* refers to the legendary "regions of women"]], and the lands of the Scythians. These are the northern and eastern parts of the whole habitable region, and they are likened to the triplicity between the North and the East, which the signs of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius compose. Its lords are Saturn and Jupiter, when they are oriental. Therefore, the inhabitants of these regions worship Jupiter and the Sun. To them, gold and... -> ### BOOK II. <- [[page number: 25]]

**Riches** flow to them in abundance, and their actions are shining and beautiful, just as they ought to be; likewise, they are wise, seekers of the divine, and observers of the qualities of their own souls. They do not turn aside from truth and justice; they are liberal [[notes: "Liberal" here means generous or possessing the qualities of a free-born person]], of good intellect, unchanging, and they abhor wickedness. Their friendship is sincere and incorruptible; for the sake of their kin and for things worthy of praise and honor, they give themselves over easily to death. They are chaste and abstinent, they favor the finest clothing, they give grand gifts, and their deeds are illustrious. These qualities are mostly offered by the fellowship of **Saturn** and **Jupiter** in these regions, because the planets are "oriental" [[notes: In astrology, "oriental" refers to planets that rise before the sun, believed to increase their outward activity and masculine influence]].

Thus, we compare these regions to the "triplicity" [[notes: A grouping of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; here, the Water signs]] which lies between the South and the West, consisting of **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**, in whose dominion **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** are associated. For this reason, many inhabitants of these regions worship **Venus**, calling her by many different names in their various lands. They name **Mars** as "Ideus" [[notes: Likely a reference to Mars of Mount Ida, or a specific local deity syncretized with the Roman god of war]] and by certain other names to which they ascribe many secrets. 

They are industrious men, yet unfortunate in their miseries and prone toward wickedness; they are hired for battles and expeditions, as well as for robberies and highway robberies. They are considered among the ranks of servants and die in battles because of the dominion of **Mars** and **Venus** over them, since these planets are oriental. Likewise, the "exaltation" [[notes: The zodiac sign where a planet’s influence is thought to be strongest]] of Mars is in a trine aspect to Venus—specifically in the sign of **Capricorn**. **Venus**, however, is exalted in a trine aspect to Mars, which is the sign of **Pisces**. Because of this, their wives love them with their whole hearts and are truly well-reconciled to them; they stay constantly in their own homes, are capable of great labor, and are reduced to servitude; generally, they are very hardworking and oppressed. 

Now, those among these people who are in the regions of **Bathionia**, **Ferogia**, and **Felogica** are likened to **Cancer** and the **Moon**. Therefore, many of their inhabitants are men of fear and humility. Because of the "oriental" Moon and the masculinity of that same figure [[notes: Though the Moon is usually feminine, its position here suggests a more active, "masculine" role]], there is a sense of utility, dominion, and segregation in many of their wives—much like the women who are called **Amazons**, who [[margin: Amazons.]] flee from marriage with men and love weapons. They are also mindful of their fathers; from the cradle, their right breasts are cut away for the sake of military expeditions, which they uncover when they go to war, so that the female nature is thought to be minimal in them. 

But those who inhabit the parts of **Syria**, **Cumachia**, and **Canadochia** are likened to **Scorpio** and **Mars**. For this reason, many of them are unstable, deceivers, traitors, and capable of great labor. 

The men of **Ludhia**, **Fiilia**, and **Macholia** are likened to **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. Therefore, they are properly men of much money, good society, and of liberality and faithfulness in trade and all their business.

The remaining fourth part is in the region called by the general name **Lynoy** [[notes: Likely "Libya," which in ancient geography often referred to the entire African continent]], [[margin: The fourth quarter.]] whose parts contain the regions of **Numidia**, **Iarsinodia**, **Africa**, **Cadbania**, the place of **Cemunitis**, **Harmantia**, **Mauritania**, **Hatolia**, and **Metagonata**—all of which are situated in the south-western part of the entire habitable world. They are likened to the triplicity between the South and the West, which is gathered from **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. The masters of this quarter are **Mars** and **Venus**, since they are "vespertine" [[notes: Planets that set after the sun, often associated with a more internal or "feminine" influence]]. Because of the fellowship of these two planets in many of these regions, it happens that a King and a Queen from the same mother rule together over them—the man ruling the men, and the woman ruling the women—and they always observe this custom of lineage. 

Their natures are very hot and they are overabundant in sexual union, so much so that their marriages are made through force and rapine. Often, their King exercises the sexual act with others' brides before their own husbands do, and among some of them, wives are held in common. They also desire paintings and ornaments, and they adorn themselves in the feminine fashion because of **Venus**; yet their minds are manly, crafty, ready to serve, diviners, traitors, and deceivers, fearing no danger because of **Mars**. 

Among these, those in the parts of **Numidia**, **Iarsinodia**, and **Africa** are properly likened to **Cancer** and the **Moon**. For this reason, they are men of society and trade, and of great fatness. Those who are in the part of the lands of **Metagonica**, **Mauritania**, and **Hatolia** are properly likened to **Scorpio** and **Mars**. Therefore, the qualities of their souls are feral; they are despisers, litigants, and great eaters of meat, not fearing danger and valuing life as nothing—so much so that some of them [kill] others for no [reason]...

...lead them to kill with the sword. But those who dwell in the region of Fadhaniae [[notes: Likely a corruption of Parthia or a related eastern province]], the place of Cemunitis Harma neboiae, are likened to Pisces and Jupiter. For this reason, the qualities of their souls are liberal; they are clearly lovers of work, givers of thanks, and god-fearing men. Many among them are not brought low, on account of Jupiter whom they venerate and call **Hamon** [[notes: This refers to Amun-Ra, the Egyptian deity whom the Greeks and Romans identified with Zeus/Jupiter]]. Other parts of this fourth quarter, which are toward the middle of the inhabited world, are the lands of Cyrenaica, Marmarica, Egypt, Tabneis, Auefis, Taragae, Dhiticae, Dhamae, Aramae, and Lumemedae, which are the lands of Alhabai and Media. All these regions toward the North-eastern part of this quarter are likened to the triplicity [[notes: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element]] which is between the North and the East, composed of the signs of **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius**. In its dominion, **Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury** are associated, since in the dominion of these regions, the five wandering planets [[notes: The "wandering stars" or planets known to the ancients]] are more frequently associated when they are evening stars [[notes: "Vespertini" refers to planets that set after the sun, appearing in the western sky after sunset]]. Their inhabitants love God and venerate the truth; they adhere to the matters of the Creator, bewail their funerals, and bury and hide their dead under the earth because they are "evening stars." Their customs are diverse, and the qualities of their souls, their actions, and their laws are many. When someone rules over them, they are obedient and humble, and then a certain faint-heartedness and humility of speech prevails in them. However, when they themselves rule over others, their souls are agreeable and their thoughts are very grand. The men take many wives, and the women likewise marry many men; they are very anxious concerning the acts of Venus [[notes: A euphemism for sexual activity]], they cohabit even with their own sisters, and they procreate many children with men; their wives conceive quickly, just as all things grow and increase greatly in their regions. Indeed, the souls of many of the men are soft and effeminate. Some of them even hold the generative organs in low esteem [[notes: A reference to the practice of castration or asceticism noted by Ptolemy in certain Middle Eastern and North African cultures]], on account of the association of **Venus** and the malefics [[notes: "Infortunaru" likely refers to the "infortunes" or malefic planets like Saturn or Mars]] in an evening quality. Among these are those in the western part, called Curmanta and Marmarica, who are closely likened to the sign of **Gemini** and **Mercury**; therefore, their inhabitants are men of deliberation and intellect, and of sharp genius in all things, especially in the investigation of the sciences of philosophy and divine matters. They are diviners, using secrets and hidden things; generally, they are also strong and firm in the doctrinal sciences. But the men of Zays, Auofis, Coraxae, and Turicae are likened to **Libra** and **Venus**; for this reason, their natures are hot, and they are travelers and merchants, and their regions are fertile and abundant. Yet those who cultivate the lands of Adhamae, Aramae, and the lands of Alhabas Mediae are likened to **Aquarius** and **Saturn**. Therefore, they are great eaters of flesh and fish, and they move themselves from barren places to fertile ones. Their life is likened to the life of wild beasts and animals.

->### How to arrive at the predictive science of general future events. Chapter IV.<-

**A**FTER this observation of the aforesaid things, it is necessary that we pursue in our speaking how we may know how to predict universal future events in a general way; and we shall set forth those future things which happen generally in lands and regions, of which this is the first account: the stronger occasion of these accidents occurs only from the eclipsing conjunction and "prevention" [[notes: *Praeuentione* refers to the Full Moon occurring just before a conjunction/New Moon]] of the Sun and Moon, as well as from the places of the motions of the planets in those very hours. Certain of these predictions of universal accidents are "discourses of place"; that is, that which must be set forth to know in which of the regions and lands the significations of a particular eclipse will fall. The stations of the wandering stars [[gloss: planets]] at each time of their station—I mean of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—when they stand still and their significations are observed, are also noted. Others indeed are to speak of time; that is, that the hour of the signification and the quantity of its duration must be foreknown. Others however are to speak of kind [[gloss: genus]]; that is, that we ought to know in what category the future accidents will occur. Certain others are to speak of the species of the future; and this is the last of the parts, through which we shall grasp the mode of the future, how it may be.

->### Concerning the knowledge of the regions in which future accidents will occur. Chapter V.<-

**F**IRST indeed, what we have proposed to relate is the first species of predictive speaking: namely, concerning place. But how one arrives at the knowledge of it, we shall indicate here. For in the eclipses, conjunctions, and preventions of the Sun and Moon, and especially in that which is more manifest, we ought to observe the place of the eclipse in the zodiac. Also the regions which are likened to that triplicity [[notes: A grouping of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, such as Fire, Earth, Air, or Water]]. We must also observe the lands which are likened to the sign of the eclipse, whether through the Ascendant of the hour of their foundation and through the places of the luminaries [[gloss: the Sun and Moon]] in that hour, or through the place of the midheaven in the birth chart of him who then ruled over them. It must also be known that in whatever regions or lands we find this likeness which we have mentioned, in all of them the future significations will come to pass, especially in that which is likened to the same sign of the eclipse, and in which the eclipse is seen above the earth.

->### Concerning the time of future accidents. Chapter VI.<-

**W**E shall grasp the second species of prediction, through which the hour of signification and the quantity of duration is known, in this manner: since one and the same eclipse, which occurs at some time, is not seen in all regions at the same hour in an equal way, nor is the degree to which the Sun is eclipsed, nor even the duration of that eclipse's time, equal in all lands.

[[margin: Eclipses.]] Let us determine the eclipse hour, which will occur in each of the places having a share in the future event, and let us likewise set the angles according to the altitude of the pole [[notes: i.e., the geographical latitude]], just as we do in the casting of nativities [[notes: birth charts]]. After this, let us observe for how many equal hours the darkness of the eclipse will extend in each of the lands. For when we have knowledge of these, we shall know that the coming events of a **Solar eclipse** will last for as many years as there were equal hours of its duration, but for a **Lunar eclipse**, for as many months. Because the beginning of these hours, and the total span of their space, is apprehended only according to the proportion of the location of the eclipse to the angles [[notes: the four cardinal points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]]: when the location of the eclipse is in the **eastern part** of the horizon, it will signify the beginning of the future event in the first four months after the hour of the eclipse. The state of its intensity will appear in the first third of the total span of time in which the significations of that eclipse occur. If, however, it is in the **Midheaven** [[notes: the highest point of the sun's path]], it signifies that it will be in the second four months, and in the middle third. But if it is in the **western part** of the horizon, it designates that it will occur in the final four months and in the third and last part. Furthermore, the particular increases and decreases of future events are gathered from the conjunctions and preventions [[notes: syzygies, or the alignments of the Sun and Moon]] which occur between these times, when they are in places that are the causes of future events, or in some place having a relationship in the figure with them. This is also gathered from the places of the motions of the planets through which future events happen to be—namely, whether they are **oriental** or **occidental**, or **stationary**, or **rising** at the beginning of the night—and as assigned in the figure to the signs which are the causes of future events through aspect or in the other manner aforesaid. For when they are oriental or stationary, they will increase the future events; but when they are occidental or exist under the rays [[notes: "under the rays" refers to a planet being so close to the sun that it is invisible]], or are rising in the evening and retrograde, they will diminish the future events.

...[continuation from previous page] similarly. Likewise, if they [[notes: "they" refers to the celestial configurations or signs]] bear the likeness of wild beasts, that which is to come will happen among the wild beasts of the forest which are harmful to men. If they represent the forms of domestic animals, it will without doubt be found among the domestic animals which men use and by which they are assisted at every time of their lives—that is, among horses, oxen, flocks, and similar creatures. 

Likewise, that which is placed among the figures of wild animals toward the northern region specifically signifies sudden changes in the Earth. However, that which is figured toward the southern region shows alterations of the air that bring fear to no one. For when the locations of the stars which govern the arrangement are in figures having wings—such as in Virgo, Sagittarius, the Hen, and the Flying Vulture [[notes: "Gallina" (the Hen) and "Vulture" refer to the constellations Cygnus and Lyra or Aquila, which were often identified this way in medieval star catalogs]]—it is manifest that the future event will occur among winged creatures, and especially those which are eaten by men. 

But if it should be in the figures of swimming animals, it will happen among fish and all aquatic animals. If it is in figures representing sea animals, such as Cancer, Capricorn, and the Dolphin, it will occur among the creatures of the sea and the ships of the ocean. But if it is in the figures of river animals, such as Aquarius and Pisces, it will appear in the animals of rivers and springs. And if it is in the figure of a Ship [[notes: Referring to the constellation Argo Navis]], it will be seen in both types. 

Similarly, if it occurs in any of the solstitial or equinoctial signs, the significance will generally be in the matters of the air and in the seasons appropriate to each of them. Specifically, however, their meanings will appear in those things which grow from the earth. For when it is in the vernal [[notes: Spring]] equinoctial sign, the significance will be found in the fruits of trees when they begin to sprout, such as in vineyards and fig trees and their contemporaries. 

If it is in the summer solstitial sign, it signifies future events occurring in fruits when they are gathered and stored; additionally, in the regions of Egypt, the specific significations will be shown in the rising of the Nile. If, however, it is in the autumnal equinoctial sign, the significations will be in the seeds when they are sown, and in herbs and similar things. But if they are in the winter solstitial sign, their meanings will come to pass in vegetables and in what appears among birds and fish. 

Furthermore, when they are in any of the equinoctial signs, they signify future events in churches and in houses established for the honor of God. If, however, they are in any of the solstitial signs, they will judge the changes of customs [[notes: Or "morals" (morum)]] among those dwelling in that region. If they are in fixed signs [[notes: The "Fixed" signs are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, associated with stability]], they will demonstrate future events in foundations and buildings. And if they are in common signs [[notes: The "Common" or "Mutable" signs are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces, associated with change]], they will portend future events happening to men and kings. 

Similarly, when the hour of an eclipse [[vocabulary: eclypsis]] is located specifically toward the east, it will designate future events in fruits, in those whose years are of youth, and in foundations. If it is in the mid-heaven [[notes: The "Medium Coeli," the highest point in the sky]], which is above the earth, the significations will appear in churches and powerful people, and in those who are of middle age. But if it is in the west, the signified events will happen in customs and variations of behavior, in those whose years are of old age, and even among the dead. 

The knowledge of the magnitude of the portion in which the future events of the subject kind will appear is determined from the quantity of the darkness of the eclipse, and from the proportion of the stars which are the causes of the future to the location of the eclipse. For if they are in evening figures in a solar eclipse, or in morning figures in a lunar eclipse, the future events will happen in a smaller part of that kind; and when they are in opposition across the diameter, the future will embrace half of that kind. But if in a solar eclipse they are in morning figures, and in a lunar eclipse in evening figures, they signify that the future will happen in the greater part.

[[meta: This page continues the Latin translation of Claudius Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos* (The Four Books), commonly known by its Latin title *Quadripartitum*. This section focuses on the specific astrological influences of the planets when they act as the sole "ruler" of a period.]]

-> ## CL. PTOLEMY'S QUADRIPARTITUM <-

The Sun and Moon take the lead and rule over the other stars. Therefore, they are the causes for the entire work and the arrangement of the stars, as well as the strengths of the "almudhebir" [[notes: From the Arabic *al-mudabbir*, meaning the "governor" or "ruler" of a specific astrological period or chart]] stars and their weaknesses. Indeed, the meeting of the mixture of these ruling stars with one another signifies the qualities of future events. We shall now begin to describe the properties of the works of each of the "erratic stars" [[notes: The "wandering stars," or planets]]. But so that our narration may be more complete, we think a certain general principle should be set forth first: namely, that when we show the mixtures of any of the five wandering stars in a general sense, we must know that their work will be likened to their own nature—whether the star itself is of a named quality in itself or not—because there are certain fixed stars and certain places in the circle of signs [[notes: the Zodiac]] whose mixtures are likened to the mixtures of that planet. And if it were possible that stars could lack names in this way, we would still show their natures and qualities. Because we also observe their mixtures, we must not only observe the mixtures of the wandering stars with one another, but also the mixtures of their natures with the fixed stars and with the places of the zodiac, according to what we have explained regarding their similarities with the fixed stars.

Therefore, when Saturn alone is the lord of the disposition,
[[margin: **Saturn alone as the lord of the disposition.**]]
he will generally be the cause of destruction occurring from cold. His specific work, when events occur among men, will be to generate long illnesses, consumption [[notes: *Phthisis*, typically referring to tuberculosis or a wasting of the lungs]], and harms that arise from the humors [[notes: In ancient medicine, the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile—which determined health and temperament]] and from the collection of humors: quartan fevers, flights, stupors, anxieties, sadness, fears, and death, especially among those who are already advanced in years. But when future events occur among animals which men use most, there will be a hindrance due to their scarcity, and in those that are found at that time, diseases and bodily detriments will occur. Also, in the men who use them, illnesses similar to the illnesses of those animals will arrive, and they shall die. If, however, it happens in the qualities of the air, there will be extreme cold with ice and mists; there will be harms in the air and deadly qualities; it will be thickened with clouds and darkened; snows and the blowing of winds will be unsuitable and destructive, from which many beasts that harm men will be procreated. But in the sea and in rivers, wintry air and the sinking of ships will commonly occur. Traveling on them will be difficult; there will be scarcities and destruction of fish. In the sea, specifically, there will be ebbs and flows. In the rivers, specifically, there will be great floods and water damage. Likewise, in the fruits of the earth there will come diminishment, scarcity, and damage, especially in those which men necessarily require; their damage will be through worms created in vegetables, or through locusts, or through flooding, or through an overabundance of rain, or through cold, or things similar to these, such that from this, a "caristia" [[notes: A Latin term for a period of high prices or scarcity, often leading to famine]] will sometimes arise, by which occasion men will die.

However, when Jupiter alone is the lord of the disposition,
[[margin: **Jupiter.**]]
he will generally increase things. His own work among men is the heightening of ranks, the improvement of status, a healthy fleshiness [[notes: indicative of good health and prosperity in the ancient world]], a quality of health and security, the increase of things which men need, a suitable habit of bodies and souls, rewards, and kingship, prizes, the increase of royal matters, the fame of one’s name, and magnanimity; and generally, he is the cause of good fortune. Among the beasts which men frequently use, they will increase sufficiently; but those which are contrary to these will die and be annihilated. The air, however, will be tempered and healthful, and with many moist winds, the fruits of the earth will increase; navigation on the sea and the foundations of rivers will be healthful during the season, with many fruits and things of this sort.

And when Mars alone is the governor, he will generally be the cause
[[margin: **Mars.**]]
of all damage which happens because of dryness; this is the universal work of Mars. His particular works among men are fights and many wars among the same...

# ->CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM<-

[[notes: The *Quadripartitum*, also known as the *Tetrabiblos* (Four Books), is the foundational text of Western astrology, written by the 2nd-century scholar Claudius Ptolemy.]]

And since the explanation of all these things can be understood generally in many ways according to any configuration of accidents, let this specific study be left to those who listen, who must inquire into and observe the particulars within it. Indeed, we must observe these likenesses of the stars—through which they signify future events for regions and lands—in the following way. Therefore, when the "fortunes" [[notes: Beneficial planets like Jupiter or Venus]] are present and are assimilated to the places where future events will occur, and if the stars are in their *haiz* [[notes: *Haiz* is an astrological term referring to a planet being in its preferred "sect" (day or night) and in a sign of its own gender]], and if stars contrary to their *haiz* do not rise above them, their natural work will be of greater strength. Likewise, when they are not assimilated to those places, and stars contrary to them rise above them, their strength will be diminished. 

Furthermore, when their combination is harmful and they rule the work of the future, if they are assimilated to the places where future events will occur, and stars contrary to their *haiz* rise above them, they will alleviate the harm. But if the disposition of those regions does not belong to them, and if stars assimilated to those regions do not rise above them, the work of their harmful combination will happen more intensely. Indeed, general accidents [[notes: Events affecting whole populations, like plagues or wars]] happen more frequently to people in whose births (*nativities*) the necessary places—that is, the places where the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and Moon]] and the angles of the chart are located—are also the locations of the causes of general accidents, such as the locations of eclipses or the places opposite to them. This will be more severe and most difficult to guard against when those same parts of the eclipse locations are the same as the locations of one of the luminaries in the birth chart, and following this, when those parts are opposite to them.

---

## ->On the colors of eclipses, and on tailed stars, and similar things. Chapter IX.<-

**I**n future universal matters, it is fitting for us to observe the colors appearing at the hour of an eclipse—that is, the colors of the luminaries themselves and of those things seen around them, such as what are called *haleisi*, *halela*, and similar phenomena [[notes: These terms, often corrupted from Arabic translations, refer to optical phenomena like halos, parhelia (mock suns), or light pillars]]. Therefore, when they are black or somewhat green, they signify those things we have said imitate the nature of Saturn. When they are white, they are said to signify the things of Jupiter’s nature. If they decline toward redness, they designate things of the nature of Mars. If they appear golden in color, they indicate things following the nature of Venus. But if they are of diverse colors, they signify things of the nature of Mercury. 

Furthermore, if that color embraces the entire body of the luminary or the things around it, the future event will happen in the majority of regions; but if it occupies any one part of the luminary or its surroundings, the event will occur only in that part which is directly in line with the portion where the color appeared. 

[[margin: Comets.]] Likewise, it is fitting that we observe the "tailed stars" [[notes: *Caudatas stellas*, the literal Latin term for comets]] which appear at the hour of an eclipse or at another time, as well as other universal portents like those called *haleisi*, *abbocat*, *halhaueni*, and similar things. Their natures are assimilated to the natures of Mars and Mercury which we spoke of before; they produce wars, fires, and the kind of conditions that cause things to be set in motion, and the accidents that happen because of them. We shall also recognize the places in which these future events will occur from their locations in the circle of the zodiac and from the places directly in line with the tailed star. We shall grasp the type of future significance and its substance from the form of that appearance which then appears. From the duration of that appearance, we shall know the span of the future event. Furthermore, from their affinity with the Sun, the hour the future event begins will be indicated. For when they appear more in the morning, the future event will happen suddenly; when they appear more in the evening, the future event will happen slowly.

## ->On the beginning of the year. Chapter X.<-

**A**fter the aforementioned universal method of knowing future things in regions and lands, it remains to add the particulars—that is, those things that happen in the seasons of the year. It is necessary to show the time which is called the beginning of the year in this way: the start of the Sun’s return in each revolution...

For the solution to that [problem], it ought to be nearly so because of its power, and its name is plain and clear. But in a circle, no one thinking [logically] could find an absolute beginning; yet in the circle of the Zodiac, a beginning can by no means be understood except from the points that are in line with the equinoctial and solstitial hours. It also happens that men hesitate over these places, because it is unknown which of those four is more suitable to be placed first. For according to a flat circular nature, none of them precedes another, so that one would be more fit for beginning than another. However, those who have attempted to treat this in their books have placed these four seasons in different ways, and have established each one of them as the place of the beginning, led to this by their fitting reasoning and the natural effect of them. For to each of these times there is a certain property, through which we ought to consider it to be the beginning of the new year. For this reason, [[margin: The four seasons of the year.]] they placed the beginning at the vernal equinoctial time, because in it the day begins to overcome the night, and because it is moist; for much of a moist nature is in every beginning of a thing when it is procreated [[notes: A reference to the ancient theory of the four humors/qualities, where "moist" and "warm" were the qualities of life and growth.]], as we have shown in the preceding [pages]. But the summer solstitial time is placed as the location of the beginning because in it the day is perfected, and it is its furthest length, and because in that time among the Egyptians is the rising of the Nile, and in it rises *t’aschere algemenia* [[notes: This is a Latinized transliteration of the Arabic *ash-shi’ra al-yamaniya*, referring to the star Sirius, the "Dog Star." Its "heliacal rising" coincided with the annual flooding of the Nile.]], and the autumnal equinoctial time took the beginning because in it is the collection of all fruits [[margin: al alhabor [[notes: Another name for Sirius, from the Arabic *al-Abur*.]]]] and those things which are to come begin to be sown in it. The winter solstitial time, however, is established as the beginning because after the shortening of the days, the lengthening of those days begins in it. And what we find to be more suitable and closer to natural reason in the observation of the year’s affairs is the observation of these four beginnings, as well as of the conjunctions and "preventions" [[notes: *Praeventio* here refers to an opposition or Full Moon]] of the Sun and Moon which occurred near these aforesaid times, especially those in which there were eclipses. Thus, through the beginning which is grasped from the Sun’s existence in Aries, we know the vernal [spring] quality; and through the beginning grasped from its existence in Cancer, the summer quality; through the beginning known from its entry into Libra, the autumnal quality; and the beginning which is taken through its entry into Capricorn demonstrates the winter quality. This is because the general qualities of the seasons and all their modes are only through the Sun, of which qualities knowledge is anticipated not only by those expert in the teachings, but even by others. It also suits the knowledge of these [seasons] to know the properties of the signs, through which we may signify the blowing of the winds, and generally observe all their nature. We shall signify the variations of increase or decrease happening in certain hours from the conjunctions and oppositions that occur after the aforementioned points, and from the fellowship of the wandering stars [[notes: The "wandering stars" (*stellae erraticae*) are the planets.]] with them in the figures generally. We shall designate the particular matter from the conjunctions and oppositions of the Sun and Moon which occur in each of the signs, and from the places of the stars; this, therefore, is what can be called the observation of the months.

### -> On the particular natures of the signs suited to the qualities of the year: Chap. XI. <-

**I**t is fitting that we have related these aforementioned things which are necessary for this matter, and that we show the particular natural properties of each sign from that which suits the qualities of the year, and the properties of each of the stars. Therefore, we have shown in the preceding [pages] the likeness of the wandering stars and the non-wandering [fixed] stars—whose temperaments are likened to the temperaments of the wandering ones—with the air and winds, namely when they are in them, as well as the likeness of all the signs with the winds and seasons. It remains, therefore, to assign their particular natures. The nature of the sign of Aries, therefore, generally [[margin: ♈︎]] because of the equinox occurring in it, brings thunder and lightnings. But it perceives the nature of its parts in increase and decrease from the properties of the fixed stars that are in it. For the beginnings of this sign produce rains and winds, its middle exists as a temperate complexion [[notes: "Complexion" refers to the specific mixture of the four primary qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry.]], and its extreme part burns and generates mortality. And those parts which are northern are heating and destructive, but those which are southern are congealing and cooling. The sign of Taurus, truly, universally [[margin: ♉︎]] signifies both complexions, but nevertheless it is more prone to the signification of heat. And of its [parts]...

### ->**On the investigation of particular qualities. Chapter XII**<-

[[insert: **W**]] ith these things having been premised, let us subsequently speak of the modes of particular significations. One of these modes, therefore, is the observation of a matter generally, which is grasped through the observation of each of the four quarters [[notes: Referring to the four seasons of the solar year]]. In this, it is necessary that we observe the nearest conjunction [[notes: The New Moon]] or prevention [[notes: *Præuentio* here refers to the Full Moon, or the opposition of the luminaries]] of the Sun and Moon which precedes the solstitial and equinoctial points, as we have said before. And, as is proper, let us arrange the angles of the hour of the conjunction or prevention in each climate [[notes: A "climate" in ancient geography was a zone of latitude]] for which we wish to investigate, just as they are arranged in a nativity [[notes: A birth chart]]. Afterward, we should observe the planets that are the *almudhebir* [[notes: From the Arabic *al-mudabbir*, meaning the "governor" or "ruler" of the chart]] of the places in which the conjunction or prevention occurred, as well as the disposition of the angle that follows these places, just as we showed in the matter of eclipses. moved by observation. The second method is the observation of monthly matters, in which [[margin: Second.]] 
it is necessary to observe the conjunctions and oppositions [[notes: *Præuentiones* (literally "preventions") refers to the Full Moon or the syzygy preceding a specific event]] which occur in each month and in each sign, according to that same method which we described previously, following the knowledge of those things we shall say. Therefore, when a conjunction occurs near a solstitial or equinoctial point, we shall observe the conjunctions that preceded it until the completion of that same quarter; and when an opposition occurs near any of these points, we shall attend to the oppositions until that same quarter is completed. Likewise, we ought to observe the angles and stars of each of the aforesaid places of the *Almudhebit* [[notes: The *Almuten*, or the planet holding the most mathematical dignity/power over a specific point in the zodiac]], so that we may investigate the appearance of the approaching stars, the *alictisal* and *alintisef* [[notes: These are Latinized Arabic terms for the "application" (approaching an aspect) and "separation" (moving away from an aspect) of planets]] of the wandering stars [[notes: The planets]], and the properties and qualities of those stars—namely, which winds they themselves move—as well as the parts of the signs in which they reside. The third method, however, is that we should observe the stronger [[margin: Third.]]
significator, which indicates the weakness and strength of a matter. This is found from the fellowship of the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and Moon]] in particular figures, not only in the figures of conjunction and opposition, but even in those which are detected in the dichotomy [[notes: The quarter-moon phases, when the disk is half-illuminated]] of the Moon. And the beginning of the alteration will more frequently be shaped three days before the Moon is with the Sun, and perhaps this work will last three days, which happens upon an equal length. Likewise, it is detected from the fellowship of these two with the wandering stars, in these or other qualities, such as in trine and sextile [[notes: Astrological aspects of 120 and 60 degrees respectively]], and that these imitate the natural order. We shall arrive at the quality of variation when the natural similarities held by the signs and stars are observed, as they are surrounded by air and imitate the winds. Truly, the strength of these particular qualities, which occurs daily, will then be appropriate when the non-wandering stars [[notes: The fixed stars]], which are of greater brightness and stronger effect, appear in the morning or evening, in the east or west, according to their affinity with the Sun; for this reason, in the greater part, they change and alter particular qualities according to their own natures. Likewise, this will be no less the case when the luminaries are in any of the angles. For the weaknesses and strengths of the qualities of each hour happen when the luminaries have proceeded into these places. Just as the ebb and flow [[notes: *Accessus et recessus*, likely referring to the tides]] are proven to happen when the Moon is in these angles, so the change in the disposition of the winds is specifically only at the course of the two luminaries toward these cardines [[notes: The four pivotal points of the sky: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven]], and their change is toward the wind to which the latitude of the Moon declines. In every place, however, we ought to know that the first general occasion is stronger. Those which follow are the occasions of particular happenings, because the work is most certainly verified and corroborated when the stars of general natures are associated with the *Almudhebit* in the figure of particular natures.

### -> Concerning the significations which are received from other signs. Chapter XIII. <-

ALID indeed [[notes: The first word "VALET" (It is helpful/strong) begins with the large decorative 'V']] in the prognostication of particular significations is the observation of the marks which are around the Sun, the Moon, and the stars, as well as that which happens from them. For the Sun, the knowledge of the daily qualities must be investigated when it emerges [rises]; but in the scrutiny of the knowledge of the nightly qualities, it is appropriate to observe when it sets. To know the qualities whose spaces are prolonged, we shall consider the hours of the fellowships of the luminaries in the figure, because each of the figures signifies for the most part the quality that will exist from it until the hour in which the Moon is in the figure that follows it. Therefore, when the Sun rises or sets and is itself clear, so that it is not covered by anything and is free from clouds, it will signify serene weather. And if its [[margin: Prognostications of the weather from the Sun]] circle should be of diverse colors, or decline toward a fiery redness; or if the rays of the Sun which proceed from it, or those which are around it, should be red; or if clouds which [surround?] the Sun appear in one part of the Sun and have the color of clouds declining to [that] color, and its rays are extended in length and separated from one another outside the circle, they will signify very strong winds, whose blasts proceed from the angles in which these signs we have mentioned appear. -> **56 CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM** <-

[[notes: The *Quadripartitum* is the Latin name for Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of Western astrology.]]

...if the sun sets, or if one or two circles appear around it, or if it has those clouds which are called "Mock Suns" [[notes: Also known as parhelia, these are atmospheric optical phenomena where bright spots appear on either side of the sun.]], and if their rays are slanting toward a greenish or black color, they indicate wintery weather and rain. Likewise, regarding the Moon, we ought to observe its location on the day three days before the conjunction [[notes: The New Moon]], three days before the opposition [[notes: The Full Moon]], and three days before the dichotomy [[notes: The half-moon or quarter phases]], as well as the three hours following these times. For when it appears, if it seems thin and clear, and nothing surrounds it, it signifies fair weather. But if it is thin and red, and the entire part that is not illuminated appears clear, and it seems as if it is moving, it signifies that gusts of wind will come from the direction toward which the moon itself leans. However, if it is black, or green and thick, it announces wintery weather and rains. 

[[margin: Signs of Storms.]] 

Likewise, it is fitting that we attend to the circle [[notes: A lunar halo]] that forms around it; for if there is one, and it is clear and gradually diminishes, it designates clear weather. But if there are two or three, they demonstrate wintery weather; and if they lean toward a bright red and appear as if they are broken, they announce wintery weather that will come through powerful winds. If, however, they are murky and thick, they indicate wintery weather characterized by wind and snow. And if they lean toward a black-green and are broken, they signify wintery weather occurring through both causes. When there are many circles, the effects will be greater according to these things we have predicted. 

Similarly, the circle that appears around the wandering stars [[notes: The planets]] and around the bright ones among the non-wandering stars [[notes: The fixed stars]] will signify things that resemble the colors of the circles themselves and the natures of the stars they surround. It is also fitting for us to observe the non-wandering stars, such as the Pleiades, Alphecca [[notes: The brightest star in the constellation Corona Borealis]], and those similar to them, so that we may inspect their clusters where many stars approach one another, and so that we may perceive their colors regardless of their size. For when they appear and are of greater light and greater size than usual, they signify gusts of wind from that part of the sky in which they are situated. 

In a similar way, the stars that are specifically compared to "Aladcha"—such as those they call "Nathta," which are also called the Manger [[notes: *Praesepe*, a star cluster in the constellation Cancer]]—and those similar to them, when they are in clear weather yet seem invisible or thick, they indicate much rain and wintery weather. But if they are clear and shining, they announce powerful winds. The manner of those things which happen at certain times from other conditions is similar. 

[[margin: Tailed stars (Comets).]] 

For "Tailed Stars" [[notes: Comets]], which resemble Aladcha, always show winds and dryness of the air; the strength of what results from this will be according to the number of those things and the length of their duration. And the "shooting of stars" [[notes: Meteors]] and their paths: if they come from one of the angles, it signifies gusts of wind coming from that direction; and if they appear from different angles, it announces disordered winds. But if they are seen from four angles, it indicates wintery weather of many varieties, so that we will not doubt that thunder, lightning, and similar things will result from it. In the same way, when the qualities of the clouds resemble fleeces of wool [[notes: Likely referring to cirrocumulus clouds, often called a "mackerel sky"]], they perhaps signify wintery weather. 

[[margin: The Rainbow.]] 

Also, **the Rainbow** which is sometimes seen: when it appears in fair weather, it will prefigure wintery weather; and when it is formed in times of wintery weather, it will announce fair weather. Generally, however, we say that for the most part, the specific colors that appear in the air will indicate qualities similar to the events signified by the aforementioned colors. Therefore, the things stated above have been investigated in a general way for both universal and particular matters. In the following sections, we shall explain the forecasting of nativities [[notes: The casting of individual birth charts]], just as the order of the work requires.

of the [stars], and the movement of the stars is the occasion [[notes: Latin *occasio* here refers to a cause or formative influence]] for each individual and general occurrence. However, the difference between the natures of those things previously mentioned, and their similar movements, and the observation of those things which the heavens move—as well as those things that surround them—is the means through which the forecasting of these occurrences is made. Beyond this, general occurrences are greater and do not require the support of another, whereas particular occurrences [[notes: "Particular occurrences" refers to the horoscopes of individuals as opposed to "general" ones like eclipses or the fate of nations]] are not so. Nor should we think that there is one and the same beginning for the hours in which we place the qualities of the heavens, and by which we strive to foreknow what is signified by the assembly of figures formed in those hours; rather, we ought to consider that there are many beginnings for general occurrences, because we cannot find a single beginning for the whole. These beginnings are not always found from the subjects themselves, but from the surrounding things [[notes: *Rebus circundantibus* (surrounding things) is a standard phrase for the celestial environment or the influence of the heavens]], which are the causes of future events. For we, for the most part, investigate all occurrences through the greater eclipses and through the stars that move with manifest motion. In individual humans, however, one and many beginnings are found: for one beginning is the start of the gathering [[notes: *Collectionis* refers to the gathering of seed at conception]], which is within us, but the many beginnings, in respect to the first, are the alterations which happen afterward from the surrounding things. Therefore, one beginning is more suitable for setting forth in this place, because all other things arise only by occasion of this one. Wherefore, since these things are so, the general properties of the conception are apprehended from the observation of the first beginning; from the remaining beginnings, we shall learn what will happen in each of the hours from increase or decrease, according to what we shall subjoin from the divisions of time.

### -> *Concerning the Falling of the Seed and the Birth of the Infant. Chapter 1.* <-

[[margin: The beginning of the infant is twofold.]]
[[insert: **Q**]] uoniam [[notes: The decorated initial 'Q' begins the word 'Quoniam' (Since).]] Since the temporal beginning of humans is held to exist, this beginning occurs naturally when the seed falls [[notes: *Sperma cadit* refers to the moment of conception]], but potentially and accidentally when the infant comes forth at the hour of birth. It is appropriate for those who have grasped the hour of the falling of the seed—whether by chance or by observation—to take their investigations from what the figure of the stars performs specifically at this hour (that is, the hour of the falling of the seed), when they wish to know the specific qualities of the body and soul. For when it happens that the seed once receives a quality in the beginning which comes to it from the surrounding things, although that quality might later vary as the body develops in these hours, nevertheless the very increase of the matter will naturally attract to itself only what is similar, and when that matter of things has grown, it will be assimilated to the first quality which is specific to the seed. However, when the hour of the falling of the seed is unknown, as has been found to happen many times, it is necessary to observe the beginning which is the coming forth of the infant. This is the greatest beginning, nor does it differ from the first, except in what follows. For through the first beginning, it is possible for that which is before birth to be foreknown. For that there is one first beginning, and another similar to the beginning, can be sufficiently stated, because the last of them is second in time, and perhaps its magnitude is more perfect in strength than the first. It is also necessary that the first beginning be more frequently called the "being of the seed" of the human, but the second be called the "being of the human," because the infant then acquires those things which it did not have while it was enclosed in the womb, and when it also acquires the properties which are only in the nature of a human, and the quality which happens to its body. Likewise, although the environment that surrounds us at the hour of birth is thought to help nothing in making the newborn exist as a certain quality, it nevertheless helps so that its appearance and its coming forth may be according to the specific quality of the surrounding environment. This is because nature, after its perfection, makes it move toward its exit when the quality [of the heavens] is assimilated to the quality that formed it. It is necessary, therefore, that we consider the quality of the stars at the hour of the infant's exit to signify similar things again—not because the hour itself performs these things, but because it is necessarily and naturally assimilated in strength to the formative power. But since in this discourse our intention is to manifest this part of science with a skillful path, as we promised in the beginning of this book, where we proved that this mode of forecasting can be reached, and since the most ancient way of fore-

We shall place the beginning of our discourse upon universal things appearing at the beginning, which is at the emergence of the infant, as fits a suitable order; since through this beginning we can arrive at the nature of all things having this beginning, as we have said. **Since** in the first matter, which is the foundation—that is, the degree of the ascendant at the hour of the infant's emergence—uncertainty often arises, because in the majority of cases the hour of birth cannot be known without error, except by one who has observed it through the astrolabe alone among all the instruments of the hours. Indeed, other instruments of the hours, which many who engage in these matters look to, perhaps fail and deviate from the truth. For in those devices where the Sun indicates the hour, errors occur due to their declination in the positioning of *scioterorum* [[notes: shadow-measuring devices or sundials]] and from the distortion of the *scioterorum*. In instruments of the hours adapted by the flow of water [[notes: *clepsydrae* or water clocks]], errors occur from the retention of water and the difference in flow, which happens for various reasons or through whatever other occasion may occur. Therefore, it is necessarily fitting that we judge the way in which the ascending degree of the circle of signs [[notes: the Zodiac]], which according to natural logic must follow, can be found. After we have roughly found the degree of the ascendant through the path of ascensions for the hour assigned to us, it is then necessary that we find the degree of the conjunction or prevention [[notes: the New Moon or Full Moon]] which was closer to the birth, and learn it truly. If it was a conjunction, we shall take the degree of both luminaries [[notes: Sun and Moon in the same degree]]; but if it was a prevention, we shall observe the degree of the luminary existing above the earth. After this, we shall inquire which of the planets is suited to have the "disposition" of that degree at the hour of birth. Generally, the way in which a planet is granted disposition is explained by these five things: triplicity, house, exaltation, term, and appearance [[notes: also known as "Face" or "Decan"]], or affinity to the Sun in the figure. And the disposition of that place will belong to the planet which had more than one of these strengths in it, or all of them. But if we find all or most of these in one planet, we shall truly observe its degree in the sign in which it was at the hour of birth; and we shall say that the degree of the sign roughly accepted through ascensions, which is equal to it in number, is the degree of the ascendant. But if we find two or more planets associated together, we shall look at the number [[notes: the degree number]] which each one traveled at the hour of birth; and whichever number is closer to the ascending degree that appeared to us through ascensions, that shall be the ascendant of the hour of birth. If we find the number of degrees of two or more planets near the number of the ascending degree that came out for us, we shall follow the one which has more authorities in the angles and which has *Haiz* [[notes: An Arabic astrological term referring to a planet being in its preferred "sect" (day or night) and hemisphere]]. But if the distance of the *Almudhebit* [[notes: Latinization of the Arabic *Al-mubtazz*, the "Almuten" or ruling planet of a chart]] from the degree of the ascendant, without subtle observation, is greater than its distance from the degree of the Midheaven, by that same path of inquiry we shall establish that same number for the degree of the Midheaven, by which we shall equate the other angles.

### -> **On the division of the discourse on nativities. Chapter III.** <-

**P**-ollowing the presentation of those things previously set forth, we shall add that whenever anyone wishes to analyze the general observations of nativities [[notes: *Nativities* refers to birth charts or horoscopes calculated for the moment of birth]] through an organized and suitable division, he will find that among those things reached by a natural path, some are accidents that occur before birth—such as the discussion concerning parents—while some are accidents that occur both before and after birth, such as discourse concerning siblings. However, those things which happen at the very hour of birth are not entirely one and the same, nor as obvious as those things we have stated before. Indeed, the last category of accidents that can be known is said to be that which will happen after the birth. There is no doubt [[gloss: no doubt is held]] that this category contains many modes and many parts.

Therefore, among those things occurring at the very hour of birth which we wish to know, are: the discussion of males and females, whether the mother will give birth to twins or more, the discussion of monstrous forms [[notes: "Monstrous forms" in a Renaissance context referred to significant congenital birth defects]], and also concerning those who will never grow. Among those things occurring after birth, the things we seek to know are: the discourse on life (specifically regarding those whose lives do not last long enough to be recorded); after this, the discussion of the form of the body, and of the infirmities and impediments happening to the body; next, to discourse on the qualities of the soul and its accidents; then to speak of the good fortune and misfortune of the newborn, and of his sovereignty, exaltation, and his high rank; thereafter, to relate his state regarding what he shall achieve through his works [[gloss: works/deeds]], then to discourse on his marriage and the time to be spent with a wife, and what will happen to him regarding children, as well as his mixing and familiarity with men and his friends; then to show his travels; and finally, to indicate the manner of his death—which, in the strength of the discourse that is made, is likened [[gloss: is likened]] to the discourse on life, yet its order must be placed after these aforementioned things.

We shall generally relate the method for each of these, and we shall speak of these things only with the strengths of our narrative performing this work, as we have manifested above. Those things, however, which have been put forward foolishly and superfluously by many—in which there is no probable discourse that fits the circumstances existing through primary nature—we shall set aside. From these things, we shall investigate that which we can reach, not through lots [[notes: *Sortes* or "Lots" refers to calculated points in a chart, like the Part of Fortune, which the author here views with skepticism]] nor through numbers, where the reasons why a thing must be so are not held, but through the observations of the configurations of the planets and their similarities to their respective places.

Therefore, so that there is no need to repeat this word in every one of the prescribed chapters, it is fitting for us to put it forward here generally for all. From the chapters of the observation of nativities, let us consider the place in the circle of signs [[notes: the Zodiac]] which is similar to the nature of the specific chapter being sought—just as there is a similarity between the place of the Midheaven [[notes: *Medium Coeli*, the highest point in the chart, associated with career]] and one's works, and the place of the Sun and the matters of the father. Afterwards, let us observe the planets which, out of the five aforementioned types, ought to have the governance of that place.

And if one planet rules that place in all these ways, we shall attribute the disposition of the matter sought to it. If, however, two or three rule it, we shall give the disposition to the one who holds the strength of the greater number of factors. Then, let us consider the quality of the future, the investigation of which will be from the natures of those stars to which the disposition belongs, and from the natures of the signs in which the planets were, as well as from similar places. After this, we shall take up the investigation of the quantity of the future from their powers, considering whether they were strong in their qualities in the world and in the nativities, or if the opposite was the case.

Indeed, they are said to be stronger in the world when they are in their own or similar places, and when they are "oriental" [[notes: Rising before the sun]] and increasing in number. In nativities, however, they will be stronger when they are in the "angles" [[notes: The four most powerful points in a horoscope: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]] or in places ascending toward an angle—most especially in the first two, which are the Ascendant and the Midheaven. They will be weaker in the world when they are in foreign or dissimilar places, or when they are "occidental" [[notes: Setting after the sun]] or diminished in their journey; but in nativities, they will then be weaker when they have receded from the angles. We shall also consider the span of future time by investigating whether they were morning or evening stars with respect to the Sun and the Ascendant. For the first two quarters of each of them, and the two opposite by diameter, are morning-like [[gloss: morning-like]], and the rest are evening-like. We shall also consider [[gloss: We shall consider]] if they were in the angles, or ascending toward the angles. If they were morning stars, therefore, or in the angles, the operation will be of a sharper nature; if indeed
