->**On Parents. Chapter IV.**<-

# **F**or the first path which we must always follow in the investigation of each of these species
# is of this kind. We shall therefore now make our beginning from the first chapter, which
# is the chapter on the discourse of parents, as it seems to fit the order which
# we have just announced. We say then that the Sun and Saturn are naturally likened to fathers,
# but the Moon and Venus to mothers. Therefore, just as the qualities of these stars are found in relation to each other and with others, so we ought to estimate the qualities of the parents; for their good and bad fortune, and even their sovereignty, is fitting for us to consider from the proximity of the stars to the luminaries [[notes: The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.]]. For when both are surrounded by the fortunes [[notes: "Fortunes" (benefics) refers to the favorable planets, Jupiter and Venus.]] that are in their *haiz* [[notes: *Haiz* is an Arabic astrological term adopted into Latin, referring to a planet being in a favorable "sect" or position relative to the horizon and the Sun.]], and in two signs of the same, or in the signs following them, they will signify that the parents are distinguished. Especially so when the planets surrounding the Sun are rising in the morning, while those surrounding the Moon are appearing in the evening, for then their position will be favorable. Likewise, if Saturn and Venus are oriental in their own *almugea* [[notes: *Almugea* (from Arabic *al-muwayahah*) refers to a specific relationship between a planet's distance from the Sun or Moon compared to its own house.]], or if they are in the angles, we ought to signify from this a manifest good fortune for the parents, according to the quantity fitting to each of them. But if the contrary of these should occur, such as the luminaries being "void of course" [[notes: A planet is "void of course" when it makes no further aspects to other planets before leaving its current zodiac sign.]] and surrounded by no stars, they will signify the decline and lowliness of the parents, especially if the position of Venus and Saturn is unfavorable. But if planets not in their *haiz* surround them, as happens when Mars rises after the Sun, or Saturn after the Moon, and the places of the fortunes are not favorable in respect to the luminaries, nor in their *haiz*, it is not unfitting for us to signify from this a miserable life and the destruction of the parents themselves. But if the "Part of Fortune" [[notes: A mathematical point in the chart calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant.]], of which we shall make mention, is found in favorable agreement with the stars surrounding the Sun or Moon in the nativities of the parents, their substance will be preserved and endure. But if the Part of Fortune is not as we have said, or if the opposite occurs, and the "fortunes" do not surround the luminaries, or if those surrounding are "infortunes" [[notes: The "infortunes" or malefics are the planets Mars and Saturn.]], the parents' possession will not profit, but will cause harm. 

The length of the parents' life, [[margin: The father’s life.]] and its shortness, we shall consider from the associations of the stars in the figures [[notes: "Figures" here refers to the astrological charts or configurations.]]. Let us speak first of the father’s life. Whenever Jupiter and Venus are associated in the figure [[notes: The horoscope or chart layout.]] in any way with the Sun or Saturn, or when Jupiter is associated with Venus, and there is a fitting association of the Sun and Saturn—either if they are joined, or in trine or sextile aspect [[notes: A "trine" is an angle of 120 degrees; a "sextile" is 60 degrees. Both are considered harmonious and supportive.]], and both are strong—we shall announce a long life for the father. But if they are not strong, this will not be so, though they will not truly signify a shortness of life. If this does not happen, but Mars is elevated above the Sun or Saturn, or if he follows them, and Saturn is not favorable to the Sun but in a fourth aspect [[notes: A "fourth aspect" is a square, or 90 degrees, considered a point of tension or conflict.]] or diametrically opposite, or if both are far from an angle, the father’s weakness will be signified. But if they are in the angles, or in places rising toward the angles, they will signify a short life for the parents or some injury; for when they stand in the first two angles, which are the Ascendant and the Midheaven, they will indicate shortness of life. But when they are in the other two, which are the West [[notes: The Descendant.]] and the Angle of the Earth [[notes: The *Imum Coeli* or the bottom of the sky.]], or in places rising toward them, they are said to be impeded. When Mars also beholds the Sun [[notes: "Beholds" is the traditional term for forming an astrological aspect.]] in the aforementioned way, the father will depart by a sudden death, or an impediment will happen to his eyes; but if he beholds Saturn, it will signify death for the father or a fever with trembling, or an injury to come from cutting or burning. Again, when the figure of Saturn is unfavorable in respect to the Sun, death will come to the father by occasion of diseases happening from harmful humors [[notes: In ancient medicine, "humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) were the bodily fluids that governed health; an imbalance caused disease.]]. Likewise, let us deal with the mother's life: When therefore in the figure of the Moon or Venus, Jupiter or Venus is again associated with the Moon, whether with her, or in her trine or sextile aspect, [[margin: The mother’s.]] and both are strong, they will lengthen the mother's life. But if Mars beholds the Moon, or follows Venus, or remains in a square or diametrically opposite aspect, or if the quality of Saturn in respect to the Moon is of this kind, if they are slow in course or have receded from an angle, they will designate that the mothers are entangled only in diseases and illnesses. But if they are increased in course, or in the angles, they will shorten the mothers' life, or bring injury upon them.

If Mars looks upon Venus, their death will be by fevers and illnesses resulting from the darkening of sight, and through humors suddenly flowing down. And when Saturn looks upon the Moon, he will produce death or sickness; indeed, when the Moon is oriental, he will announce death through fevers with shivering, and when she is occidental, that [death] will happen by occasion of corroding ulcers and "eating" sores [[notes: Likely referring to gangrene or cancer]], or those occurring in the female members. 

But it should be known that if we wish to know the specific types of impediments, or infirmities, or of death which happen to the parents, it is fitting for us to observe the qualities of the signs—along with those things we have already said—in which the planets who are the "makers" [[notes: *Opifices*, the planets responsible for a specific effect in the chart]] of that particular quality are found. We must also observe the qualities of the signs of which we shall make mention, and whose nature we shall explain, when we relate the matters of nativities. In the day, we should specifically observe the Sun and Venus, but in the night, Saturn and the Moon. 

Furthermore, that which we must observe to investigate the remaining particular matters of the parents is this: that we place the "place" of the father or mother—whichever is according to the *haiz* [[notes: *Haiz* is a technical term for a planet's "sect" or dignity, being in a favorable position relative to the sun and horizon]]—in the position of the Ascendant, and we observe all their affairs just as we do in the nativities of the parents themselves, in the same way we have proved in the following sections regarding accidental and "maker" modes which are found in general types. However, it is fitting for us to keep a memory here and everywhere of the combination of causes with one another: we should consider that when the planets which rule the designated places are not of one type, but of different types, or planets working toward opposites, we shall take that one which has the greater authority among the planets whose powers are over it. This is done so that the planet itself matches the future event, and the nature of those things happens through it. But if their authorities should be equal, and stars have risen with them, we shall easily arrive at the knowledge of the combined matter from the mixture of these differing natures. If, however, they are separate, we shall attribute to each of them that which is assimilated to it from the events, according to the particular hours. To those which are matutine [[notes: Rising in the morning before the Sun]], we shall attribute [the events] first; to those which are vespertine [[notes: Rising in the evening after the Sun]], we shall attribute them later. Yet it is necessarily required that it be assimilated to them from the beginning; for if it is not so, it can do nothing of the future, since they retained no fellowship in the beginning. For the first disposition is not the cause of the future time, but the quality of the star which, in respect to the Sun and the angle of the world, was the mistress of the disposition at the time of birth.

-> ## *Concerning brothers and sisters. Chap. V.* <-

### **F**rom the things said previously, we have therefore proved the "place" of the parents. If anyone should examine the "place" of siblings by a general investigation, and in his search does not exceed the possible quantity which can truly exist for inquiring into the knowledge of the number of siblings, he will be able to know the matter of siblings who are of the same mother in a natural way from the sign of the Midheaven [[notes: *Medium Coeli*, the highest point of the zodiac at the moment of birth]], or the "place" of the mother—we call the "place" that in which Venus is by day and the Moon by night. And because this sign, and the sign which ascends to it, is the "place" of the mother from which the affairs of her children are grasped, it is fitting that this be the place of the siblings. If, therefore, the planets of fortune [[notes: The "benefics," usually Jupiter and Venus]] are associated with this place in the figure [[notes: The birth chart]], we shall judge a multitude of siblings therefrom; we shall take the estimation of this matter from the number of those planets. We shall also consider if they are in signs of a "single image" or of "two bodies" [[notes: "Two bodies" refers to bicorporeal or mutable signs like Gemini or Pisces, which often signified plurality]]. But if the planets of misfortune [[notes: The "malefics," Saturn and Mars]] are elevated above this place, or look upon it from opposition, they will indicate a small number of siblings, especially if the Sun is with them.

[[margin: The givers of males and females.]]

[[notes: In astrology, "givers" (datores) are the specific planets or points in a birth chart that "give" or determine information about a specific area of life—in this case, siblings.]]

If indeed they [the planets] are found in the angles, and specifically in the ascendant, and if Saturn is the planet residing in any of these places, he will signify this regarding older brothers [[notes: The Latin text mentions *uirginibus*, which usually means "virgins" or refers to the sign Virgo, but in this context of birth order, it likely refers to the "seniority" or "primacy" of the siblings ruled by Saturn]]. If, however, it is Mars, he will shorten the number of other brothers by death. If the quality of the planets which are the givers of siblings is in a favorable position, we should judge the siblings to be powerful and exalted. But if it is in the opposite position, they will be weak and powerless. Furthermore, if malefic planets [[notes: "Infortunæ" refers to planets like Mars and Saturn, traditionally thought to bring challenges or "ill fortune"]] are elevated above the givers, or if they follow them, the siblings will likewise be short-lived. The givers of males are masculine planets in their worldly qualities, while the givers of females are feminine in their worldly qualities. Likewise, those in the East grant the first-born siblings, and those in the West grant the last-born. Again, when the givers are associated in the chart with a sign that is favorable to the matter of siblings, they will signify harmony among them; and if they also agree with the "Part of Fortune," they will indicate a partnership among the siblings in their affairs. But if they are in signs that have no relationship to one another, or if they possess a quality contrary to the aforementioned quality, they will signify a tendency toward discord and envy among the siblings, and prove them to be deceivers. If anyone wishes to investigate each matter regarding siblings more deeply than what has been said above, they can sufficiently do so by setting the giver-planets in the place of the ascendant, and then let us observe all their conditions just as we do in nativities [[notes: Ptolemy is suggesting that one can cast a new "derived" horoscope for a sibling by treating their representative planet as the starting point (the ascendant) of a new chart]].

## -> *On Males and Females.* <-
### -> Chapter VI. <-

> [[insert: P]] ostquam [[notes: The historiated initial 'P' begins the word *Postquam* (After).]] after we have explained the account of siblings by the natural path—that which will happen to the newborn—it is necessary to subjoin what follows, and first indicate the consideration of males and females. The observation of this is not of one single kind, nor is it taken from only one thing, but from both luminaries [[notes: The "Luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon]], from the ascendant, and from the planets holding authority over these. Since the male and female are generated in the womb, it is fitting that the judgment of this matter properly belongs to the beginning, which is the hour of the falling of the seed [conception]; and what we can know of this is that the beginning, which is the emergence of the creature [birth], is general because of the participation which this beginning has with the first [[notes: Ptolemy argues that while conception is the true start, the moment of birth is a valid proxy because it shares the same astrological "blueprint" as the conception]]. It is fitting for us to observe generally: if these three aforementioned places [Sun, Moon, and Ascendant] and the planets ruling all or most of them are masculine, the child will be male; if they are feminine, it will be female; and according to this, we shall judge the newborn. We must also consider the masculine and feminine places and planets, just as we showed at the beginning of this book—I mean, demonstrating from the natures of the signs in which they are, from the natures of the planets themselves, and from their qualities with respect to the world. For when they are Oriental [[notes: Rising in the east before the sun]], they "masculinize," but they "feminize" when they are Occidental [[notes: Setting in the west after the sun]]. Likewise, from their qualities with respect to the Sun: for they masculinize when they are "matutine" [morning stars], and they feminize when they are "vespertine" [evening stars]. From all these things, therefore, we must conjecture which gender occurs in the constitution of the newborn according to the majority of factors.

And if the dominant places are signs of two bodies...

If the planets are associated with more than two in the chart, there will be more than two children born. Their number is also sometimes increased by a planet that possesses this specific property. Furthermore, the knowledge of the child's gender is increased by the type of planets associated with the Sun, the Moon, and the Ascendant sign in the figure, which adds masculine or feminine qualities according to the previously mentioned manner of strength at birth. Indeed, if this quality does not include the ascending sign and the Luminaries [[notes: The "Luminaries" refers to the Sun and the Moon]], but the location of the *Medium Coeli* [[notes: The Midheaven, or the highest point in the sky at the moment of birth]] is found in its place, the births of these mothers will mostly result in twins or more. 

Specifically, regarding the birth of three males, it happens just as it does in the case of the *albetatram* [[notes: An astrological term, likely derived from Arabic, referring to a specific configuration of royal or noble triplets]], who are kings; this occurs when Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars are positioned in the aforementioned places in "double-bodied" signs [[notes: Double-bodied signs (mutable signs) include Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces]]. In the birth of three females, it happens as it does in the *alchatis* [[notes: Likely another Arabic-derived term for a specific triple birth configuration]], namely that the Moon, Venus, and a feminine Mercury remain in the aforesaid places. In the birth of two males and one female, it is characteristic for it to happen as it does for those called *diasaccora* [[notes: A corruption of "Dioscuri," the mythological twins Castor and Pollux]], when Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus are in those places. They will also give birth to two females and one male when that which is said to have happened to those called *dimantatcoris* occurs, namely that the Moon, Venus, and Mars are present in those places. 

In this manner, it frequently happens that the child is not fully formed, or that certain physical impediments occur at the moment of birth. In some of the child's members, things may occur for which there is no cause for fear, happening without a clear reason, or there will be some of these accidents affecting a part of the body that is not visible.

-> ### **On monstrous signs.** <-
-> ### **Chapter VIII.** <-

[[insert: Large decorative initial letter 'I' containing floral or classical motifs.]]

That which by no means departs from our understanding is the description of **monstrous forms** [[notes: In this context, "monstrous" (monstruosus) refers to what we would now call congenital birth defects or significant physical deformities]]. We say first that the two Luminaries are mostly found in the births of such individuals falling away from the "angles" [[notes: The 'angles' are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]] or, if not, having some harmony with the Ascendant, while the "unfortunate" planets [[notes: The "malefics," traditionally Saturn and Mars]] are powerful in the angles. When it is found thus, it follows that this might occur, which is often said to happen in miserable and unfortunate births. 

Even if those births do not result in monstrous forms, let us observe the preceding conjunction or prevention [[notes: These refer to the New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth]] so that we may grasp the ruling planets of the hour of birth at the place of the conjunction or prevention, as well as the place of the Luminaries. For if their places in the births—and the place of the Moon or the Ascendant—are not bound to the planet in the place of the conjunction or prevention, the child will be of a **monstrous form**. 

If these things are so, and in addition we find the Luminaries in "quadruped" [[notes: Four-legged signs like Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, or Capricorn]] or "feral" signs, and the "unfortunate" planets are existing in the angles, the offspring will not be human. If no "fortunate" planet [[notes: The "benefics," Jupiter and Venus]] gives testimony to the Luminaries, but the "unfortunate" ones testify to them, the offspring will not be a domestic creature, and its nature will be of the nature of impeding wild beasts. But if Jupiter or Venus testifies to the Luminaries, the offspring will be of the domestic animals, such as dogs, ferrets, and similar things. If Mercury testifies, the offspring will be of the animals which humans use and have need of, such as chickens, pigs, oxen, goats, and similar things. 

But if the Luminaries are moving in signs whose images are **human**, and all other things are similar, we do not doubt that the offspring will be human, or of those who live with humans, except that we say he will have a monstrous form. The knowledge of this quality and its specific property will be found in this place again from the figures of the signs in which the "unfortunate" planets stood, which held the Luminaries or the angles. Likewise, if the signs of the "fortunate" planets in this place testify to none of the aforesaid places, the child will be unable to speak, and its form...

->### On those who are not reared. Chapter IX.<-

# A
fter the discussion concerning those who are not reared [[notes: This refers to "infant mortality." In the ancient world, "rearing" a child was the active decision to raise them; many infants died shortly after birth due to various astrological (and physical) causes.]] has preceded, it remains to speak of their condition, the knowledge of which we seek to have through the hour of birth. It should be known that this investigation is not far removed from the two modes of inquiry mentioned before, sometimes adhering to the discussion of life, and sometimes being contrary to it, because the force of this kind of investigation is altered by certain variations. For the discourse on life applies only to all those who have experienced life. These are those whose life is found to be no less than a solar circuit, which is the space of one year; but "life in its strength" is that which is said to be less, such as months, days, and hours. The discussion of those who are not reared is the account of those who do not reach any of these aforementioned times, but die in a short time because of an excess of evil and harm. Therefore, the investigation of life has many parts, but that of those who do not grow is single and plain.

Generally, therefore, when one of the Luminaries [[notes: The "Luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.]] is in one of the Angles [[notes: The "Angles" are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.]], and one of the Unfortunate planets [[notes: The "Infortunes" or "Unfortunate planets" are Mars and Saturn.]] is joined to it in longitude, being degree for degree with it, or is in an isosceles figure [[notes: *Figura equicruria* refers to a geometric configuration where the planets form equal "legs" or aspects, such as a square or opposition.]], and none of the Fortunate planets [[notes: The "Fortunes" are Jupiter and Venus.]] are joined to it in the figure, and the ruler of the place of the Luminaries is in the places of the Unfortunate planets, the child will not live, but will die soon. 

But if it is in an isosceles figure, but in the projection of rays of the Unfortunate planets ascending to it from the places of the Luminaries, and there are two Unfortunate planets, one or both harming the Luminaries, ascending to the places of these two or one of them, or if it is in opposition to him or them, or if one of the Unfortunate planets harms one of the Luminaries while the other is in opposition, and the other indeed ascends to the place of the Luminary, it is not at all doubted that the child will have no life. Since the greatest harm in this—health and progress—which arises in the span of life from the longitude of the place ascending to the place of the Luminaries, is destroyed and hidden. 

However, that which specifically hinders the Sun, from those things in the place which ascends to its own place, is said to be Mars; but Saturn hinders the Moon. But in their opposition, or when it ascends to it, the contrary happens: for Saturn hinders the Sun, and Mars the Moon, especially when they rule as the dispositors of the places of the Luminaries and the Ascendant. 

And if it has two oppositions, and the Luminaries and the Unfortunate planets are in the Angles or in an isosceles figure, the infants are born dead or half-dead. But if it happens so, and the Luminaries are separated from one of the Fortunate planets, or are joined to it in a figure, and the rays reach the preceding parts, the child will live according to the significance of the number of degrees that are between the *Alhileg* [[notes: The *Hyleg* or *Alhileg* is the "Giver of Life," a specific point in the chart used to calculate longevity.]] and the nearest Unfortunate planet, the rays [giving] the number of months or days or hours according to the quantity of their misfortune, which are the occasion of this. 

But if the rays of the Unfortunate planet reach the preceding parts of the Luminaries, and the rays of the Fortunate planets reach the following parts, the child will grow and live. Likewise, when the Unfortunate planets are elevated above the associating Fortunate planets in the figure, the child will be of a miserable quality and weak. But if the Fortunate planets are elevated, the child will not stay with its parents. And if one of the Fortunate planets rises together with the Moon, or has an *ictisal* [[notes: A Latinization of an Arabic astrological term (ittisal), meaning "application" or the coming together of two planets.]], and one of the Unfortunate planets sets, the child will be nourished by [foster] parents. 

In this way again, the observation of many births will be made. When any of the stars are in the West in two or more ways of having fellowship in the figure, the infant will be born half-alive, or like a piece of flesh, or of imperfect creation. And if one of the Unfortunate planets is elevated over it, the child will not be nourished, or will not have life, according to what happens through this.

-> On the span of life. Chapter X. <-

[[insert: decorative box containing an initial E and a figure of a scholar at a desk]] OF those events, indeed, which occur after birth, the first is the discourse on the length of life. For it would be a matter of ridicule for us to treat those things which rarely occur for one who does not reach the years of life in which those things can be completed—since the primary order of all things must be established first. This observation is neither slight nor simple; nevertheless, it is received and grasped from the powers of the dominant places, which are observed in many ways. The method, however, which has come down to us according to our estimation, and which imitates the natural path, is as we shall narrate. This observation is considered from the place of the *alhileg* [[notes: *Alhileg* (or Hyleg) is a medieval astrological term derived from the Arabic *haylaj*, referring to the "Giver of Life"—the specific point or planet in a birth chart used to determine a person's lifespan.]], and from those planets which have power over the *alhileg*, as well as the places of the killing planets [[notes: Referring to the *Anareta*, or "destroyer," the planet or point that signifies the end of life by its difficult aspect to the Hyleg.]]. The knowledge of each of these matters is as follows. First, it is necessary for you to know that the places of the *alhileg* are those in which a planet, which possesses dominion, must be the *alhileg*; here, however, it is above the sign of the ascendant, from five degrees which have ascended above the horizon before the ascendant itself, up to the twenty-five degrees which remain to ascend [[notes: This defines the "Hylegiacal places," traditionally the 1st, 11th, 10th, 9th, and 7th houses, where the "life-giver" must be located to be valid.]], and after these degrees, those which consist in a right-hand hexagonal radiation [[notes: A sextile aspect (60 degrees), here referring to the 11th house.]] of these thirty degrees, which are the house of good fortune. [[margin: Alhileg.]]
And those which are in their square [[notes: *Tetragono*, meaning a 90-degree square aspect.]] aspect, which is the midheaven above the earth, and also the degrees which are in their opposition, which is the west [[notes: The descendant or 7th house.]]. Among these, however, that which is suitable to be preferred, because it exists with stronger authority, is said to be the midheaven above the earth, [[margin: dētheos [[notes: Likely a corruption of "Agathos Daimon" (Good Spirit), the Greek name for the 11th house.]]]] and after this the ascendant, then that which follows the midheaven [[notes: The 11th house.]], and after it the west, and after that, the house which precedes the midheaven [[notes: The 9th house.]]. For we have decreed that everything which lingers under the earth in this so noble and excellent a matter should be passed over, except for that part of the ascendant which has appeared above the earth. Of those signs which are above the earth, those which do not connect with the ascendant are not to be observed, nor even the sign ascending before the ascendant [[notes: The 12th house.]], which is called the house of labor [[notes: Traditionally the *Mala Fortuna* or house of "Bad Fortune/Enemies."]], for the reason that besides being removed from the angle, a thick and dark vapor, which ascends to it from the moisture of the earth, disturbs and destroys its strength as it reaches the earth; therefore, that which appears from the colors and qualities of the planets existing in this house has a nature that is doubted. Afterwards, it is fitting that we establish the four dominants, which are the Sun, Moon, Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune, as the dispositors of the *alhileg*. We shall know the Part of Fortune if we take the number which we find from the place of the Sun to the place of the Moon, by day and night, and by beginning from the ascendant, we compute the quantity of that number according to the succession of the signs. In this way, therefore, we learn the place of the Part. This we do so that the quality of the Sun, with respect to the ascendant, may be like the quality of the Moon with respect to the Part of Fortune [[notes: The Part of Fortune is a mathematical point in the chart that represents the "Lunar Ascendant," balancing the solar and lunar influences.]]. For the Part of Fortune will be like a lunar ascendant. Those who say that in nocturnal births we ought to count from the Moon to the Sun seem to imitate this same reasoning. Then, initiating from the ascendant, let us compute the quantity of the same number in the contrary direction to what we said before—that is, according to the ordered precedence of the signs: when we have done this, the same place of the Part of Fortune which had come out for us will appear according to this method, and the quality of the figure's association will be the same. It is also fitting that from these, by day, we should primarily choose the Sun if it be in a place of the *alhileg*; if not, then the Moon; but if we cannot choose her, we shall choose the planet which has the greatest authorities in the disposition of the place of the Sun, and the place of the preceding conjunction, and also of the ascendant—that is, the planet which has, out of the five powers [[notes: The five essential dignities: House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, and Face.]] through which a disposition consists, three or more authorities in any of the aforesaid places, is to be chosen. If this does not happen, we shall take the degree of the ascendant. But at night, it is fitting that we first choose the Moon, then the Sun, then the planet which has the greatest authorities in the disposition of the place of the Moon, and the place of the preceding prevention [[notes: *Praeventio* refers to the Full Moon (opposition) occurring before birth.]], and the place of the Part of Fortune. When, however, this dominion does not occur, if a conjunction preceded the birth, we shall take the ascendant. But if a "prevention" [[notes: Full Moon]] preceded, we take the Part of Fortune. But if both luminaries and the dispositor which is according to the suitable *alaiz* [[notes: A technical term, likely a Latinization of an Arabic term referring to the "Almutes" or the victor of the chart.]] are in the places of the *alhileg*, it is fitting that we take from the luminaries that one which is in the place of greater and stronger power; however, choosing a dispositor over the luminaries is not...

-> ## THE FOUR BOOKS OF CL. PTOLEMY <-

...it is by no means suitable, unless it is in a place of greater and stronger dignity, having authority in its disposition according to the two **alahiz** [[notes: From the Arabic *al-hiz*, referring to the "portions" or "shares" of planetary strength/dignity]]. And when the **alhileg** [[notes: More commonly known today as the *Hyleg*, this is the "Life-Giver" or the specific point in a birth chart used to determine the length of a person's life]] has been identified, it is appropriate for us to observe its two types. One of these is solely according to the succession of the signs [[notes: Zodiacal motion, following the order of Aries, Taurus, etc.]], while the other is both according to that succession and also in the contrary direction of the succession [[notes: This refers to "mundane" motion, caused by the daily rotation of the Earth (the Primum Mobile), which appears to move planets from the East toward the Midheaven]]. We should observe the type that is solely according to the succession in quality, which is called the **projection of rays** [[notes: This is the method of calculating aspects or "hits" from other planets to the Hyleg]]. This is said to occur when the **alhileg** is in oriental places—that is, from the Midheaven [[notes: The highest point of the chart]] to the Ascendant [[notes: The eastern horizon]]. But that type which exists both in succession and contrary to succession we shall consider in the quality which is called **utine** in Greek [[notes: Likely a corruption of *aphesis* (direction/release) or *horimaia* (hourly direction)]]. This happens when the **alhileg** is in a place receding from the Midheaven. And when these things are perceived in such a way, the degrees signifying death according to the **alhileg** (which is of the species we find according to the precedence of the signs) will be the degree of the setting horizon [[notes: The Descendant]]. This is because it obscures the lordship of life according to the degrees of the stars applied to that same **alhileg** found in this way, or those testifying to it; namely, because they add to or subtract from the collected numbers until the hour at which the **alhileg** falls. Except for the fact that they do not "set" because they do not go to the place of the **hyleg**, but rather the **hyleg** itself goes to their places. 

[[margin: alchorima]] [[notes: This marginal note is an Arabic-derived term (often *alkochoden* or *al-gharib*) referring to the "Giver of Years" or the mathematical process of directing the Hyleg toward an "anaeretic" (killing) point.]] 

Those stars which always add are called the **Fortunes** [[notes: The benefics: Jupiter and Venus]], while those that subtract are called the **Infortunes** [[notes: The malefics: Saturn and Mars]]. **Mercury**, again, will be with the stars with which he is associated in the figure [[notes: Mercury is considered "neutral" and takes on the character of the planets he is aspecting]]. Moreover, the number of increase or decrease will be detected from the places of the degrees of each one of them. For it will be found according to the number of the temporal hours which each of those degrees possesses: for when it is a daytime birth, we shall attribute the times of the diurnal hours; and when it is a nighttime birth, we shall attribute the times of the nocturnal hours. According to their quantity will be the number of completed years. This must be understood to be the case when they are in the Ascendant; after this, according to its distance from the Ascendant, the number is reduced so that when we reach the point of the West [[notes: the Descendant]], nothing remains. 

But according to the **alhileg** of the species which we investigate through the succession of the signs, the places of the **infortune** stars—that is, **Saturn** and **Mars**—are the arrivals, whether they reach the **hyleg** bodily [[notes: by conjunction]] or when they project rays from any of those places. That is, from the places of the **quartile** [[notes: 90-degree square aspect]] and **opposite** radiation [[notes: 180-degree opposition aspect]], and perhaps from the **sextiles** [[notes: 60-degree aspect]] which "obey" or "behold" and are equal in strength. Likewise, the **quartile** aspect of the place of the **alhileg** (following the succession of signs) will also be a "killer," and perhaps the **sextile** will work the same when it is an Infortune and when it comes from a sign of "many ascensions" [[notes: Signs that take longer to rise over the horizon, also called signs of long ascension]]. Similarly, the **trine** [[notes: 120-degree aspect]] will do this when it is in an Infortune and remains in a sign of "few ascensions" [[notes: Signs of short ascension]]. 

And when the **Moon** is the **alhileg**, the place of the **Sun** sometimes kills; for when the Sun comes to the place of the **alhileg** of this species, it will have the power of killing and saving, for it will go to the place of the **alhileg**. Nor should we think that these places necessarily always kill, for they will by no means kill except when they are only **unfortunate** [[notes: afflicted by malefic planets]]. This is prohibited when there is a term [[notes: An Egyptian "term" or "bound," a specific subdivision of a sign]] of one of the Fortunes, or when one of the **Fortunes** projects rays—from a quartile, trine, or opposition—to that very degree which kills, or to the degree which follows after it. In this case, in the projection of rays, **Jupiter** must not pass more than 12 degrees beyond it, nor **Venus** more than eight. Similarly, this will happen when the **alhileg** is joined to a star and adheres to it in a bodily condition, and the latitude of those two is not the same. 

When, however, the stars that save or help or kill are two or more, in each of these two cases, it is appropriate that we observe which of those two is stronger, according to the multitude of helping things and their strength. Thus, according to multitude: when one of the two species is more than the other by a manifest increase. According to strength: when the stars which help or kill are in places suitable to themselves, and no others remain in such places—especially when the stars of one species are **oriental** and the stars of the other species are **occidental**. On which account, regarding those which are "under the rays" [[notes: Combust, or so close to the Sun that they are invisible]] in setting, helping, or saving, we generally need observe nothing, unless the **Moon** be the **alhileg**. For then that same place of the Sun will be the killer; and even then, we shall consider if the Infortune which was with it hindered it, and if none of the Fortunes helped it. 

Moreover, as for the numbers which are according to the distance we find between the place of the **alhileg** and the **abscisor** [[notes: The "cutter," the planet or point that ends the life]], it is by no means appropriate to take them loosely or in any old way. Just as...

->**BOOK II.**<-

Just as many used to do, who said that this was always according to the quantity of the times of the ascensions of the degrees of that longitude, nor should we even consider this at any time except when the place of the Alhileg [[notes: Also known as the Hyleg; the "giver of life" or the point in a birth chart used to determine a person's lifespan.]] itself was ascending, or one of the places ascending toward the ascendant. Therefore, those who have observed this type [of calculation] by natural consideration, it is fitting that they observe one thing in all ways: namely, how many times [[notes: "Times" (tempora) here refers to degrees of the celestial equator passing a point, where 1 degree = 1 year of life.]] of the equinoctial circle [[notes: The celestial equator.]] there will be from the place of the star or figure following to the place of the star or figure preceding in the nativity. This is because the times of the equinoctial circle travel equally across the circle of the horizon and the line of the meridian. These are the two [lines] through which similar local longitudes are taken; indeed, each single time of the equinoctial circle constitutes the place of one solar year. 

It is fitting, therefore, that when the place of the Alhileg itself has preceded, and was upon the eastern circle of the horizon, the times of the ascensions of the degrees should be taken from that very hour until the hour which "kills" [[notes: Referring to the *Interfector*, the planet or point that symbolically ends the life.]]—because after this quantity of time of the equinoctial circle, the "killer" will be in the place of the Alhileg, which is the eastern circle of the horizon. 

And when the Alhileg is on the line of the midday [[notes: The Meridian or Midheaven (Medium Coeli).]], one must take the ascensions of the right circle [[notes: Right Ascension; the movement of stars as seen from the Earth's equator.]], according to which will be the time of the transit of that part of the circle of signs [[notes: The Zodiac.]] in the circle of the midday. 

However, when it is on the western circle of the horizon, we shall take the number of times in which each of those longitudes falls and sets, which is just like the number of degrees of the ascensions of the parts of the circle of signs which are opposite to them. 

But if the place of the Alhileg, when it preceded, was not in any of these three [points], but was established in places situated between them, the aforementioned time of accessions, and the time of setting, and the time of transit through the midheaven, will not be those in which the following places [reach] the preceding places, but will be those in which they arrive at different places. This is because the place toward which the "follower" goes is judged to be neither similar to, nor of such a kind as, the place where the "preceder" had been—unless its position is made similar to the [original] position, and its part in respect to the horizon and midheaven is just as the [original] part was. 

And it also happens that, in respect to these two, its position is the same when it is near the places which are above the semicircle, from the circles passing through the place common to the circle of the midday and the circle of the horizon; and these are those of which each one produces one temporal hour [[notes: Unlike our modern hours of 60 minutes, "temporal hours" divided the day and night into 12 equal parts each, meaning their length changed depending on the season.]], nearly equal to one another. 

However, when this semicircle has rotated around the aforementioned common place, its position will sometimes be like the position of the hemisphere, and sometimes truly like the position of the circle of the midday; and the times in which the parts of the circle of signs pass through these two places will be unequal. Truly, the times in which the parts of the circle of signs cross this semicircle, when it stands in certain other places which are of different longitudes, will be different. 

But we shall set down the general method through which we shall work as that which follows: namely, whether the preceding of the two aforementioned places was in the ascendant, or in the circle of the midday, or in the west, or in another place, the following place alone will go to the preceding one, according to the times which pass through that same antecedent place. For when the degree of the midheaven is known, as well as the degree of the preceding and also the following [points], we shall consider the place of the antecedent degree by first investigating how many temporal hours it is distant from the circle of the midday. This is done by counting the ascensions which are under the degrees between this and the degree of the midheaven, which is established above the earth or below the earth in the right circle; after this, we divide them by the number of the times of the hours which the preceding degree had. 

If it was above the earth, [divide] by the times of the diurnal hours; and if [below] the earth, by the times of the nocturnal hours. What results will be the hours of its longitude from the circle of the midday. 

Therefore, because the parts of the circle of signs, whose longitude from the circle of the midday is one and the same quantity of the number of temporal hours, are falling upon one and the same semicircle from the aforementioned circles, it is necessary that we know in longitude: how much time from the times of the equinoctial circle the longitude of the following degree from the line of the midday will return temporal hours equal in number to the hours of the longitude of the preceding degree from the circle of the midheaven. 

And when we know this, we shall consider how many times from the times of the equinoctial circle the longitude of the following degree was from the degree of the midheaven, when the position of the following degree was the first position. This, moreover, [is found] from the ascensions of the right circle...

[[page number: 48]]

->**BOOK III: PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM**<-

...we shall find it correctly. After this, we shall observe how great its longitude [[notes: In this context, "longitude" refers to the distance measured along the celestial equator, often called "ascensional difference" in modern spherical astronomy]] is, based again on the fact that the number of its temporal hours [[notes: A "temporal hour" is 1/12th of the time between sunrise and sunset. Unlike our modern 60-minute hours, these hours grow longer in summer and shorter in winter]] which exist between it and the meridian circle [[notes: The *medium coeli* or Midheaven]], will be the same as the hours of the preceding degree. We calculate this by multiplying the number of these hours by the number of the "times" [[notes: "Times" (*tempora*) refer to degrees of the celestial equator; 15 degrees equals one equinoctial hour]] of the following hour. 

But if the hours we have obtained are taken in respect to the Midheaven which is above the earth, the values by which we multiply will be the "times" of the diurnal (daytime) hours. If, however, they are in respect to the Midheaven which is below the earth (the *Imum Coeli*), we shall multiply by the "times" of the nocturnal hours. Then, we take the result of the difference between the two longitudes—the amount by which one exceeds the other—because this will be the number of years sought [[notes: This is the core of "Prorogation": calculating the distance a planet must travel to reach a certain point, with each degree representing one year of life]]. 

To make what we have said more evident, let the beginning of Aries be placed as the "preceding" place [[notes: The *Locus Praecedens* is the starting point or Hyleg, the giver of life]], and let the "following" place be the beginning of Gemini. Also, let the climate [[notes: "Climate" refers to a specific latitude of the earth, defined by the length of its longest day]] in which we are located be that where the longest day is fourteen hours. In this case, the "times" of the hours for the beginning of Gemini will be approximately 17 [[notes: This means each temporal hour at this latitude covers 17 degrees of the equator]]. 

First, let the beginning of Aries be ascending, so that the beginning of Capricorn is at the Midheaven. Then, the longitude of Gemini from the Midheaven which is above the earth will be 148 times (degrees) of the equinoctial circle. Since the longitude of the beginning of Aries from the Midheaven (above the meridian circle) is six temporal hours, when we multiply these by the 17 times—which is the quantity of the times of the hours for the beginning of Gemini—the result is 102 times. (This is because the longitude of 148 times is only in respect to the Midheaven above the earth). 

Therefore, the "following" place will move to the "preceding" place after as many times as there are in the difference, which is 46. Thus, the times of the ascensions of Aries and Taurus are roughly equal to these times. 

This is set up so that if the *Alhileg* [[notes: Also known as the *Hyleg*, this is the planet or point in a horoscope that represents the life force of the newborn]] is the ascending place itself, the Midheaven is again the beginning of Aries; so that in the first position of the beginning of Gemini, the longitude from the Midheaven above the earth is 58 times of the equinoctial circle. 

Wherefore, in this second position, it is appropriate for us to observe when Aries and Taurus intersect the meridian circle. For this reason, we take the midday, just as we did when we placed the *Alhileg* there. 

Likewise, let the beginning of Aries be setting in the same manner, so that the beginning of Cancer is in the Midheaven. The longitude of the beginning of Gemini from the Midheaven above the earth, following the succession of the signs, would be 32 times of the equinoctial circle. Again, because the longitude of the beginning of Aries from the Midheaven circle toward the west is 6 temporal hours, when we multiply these by 17, we get 102 times. These are the "times" from the meridian circle to the beginning of Gemini when it sets; and its longitude toward this same part, when it was in its first position, was 32 times. 

It is proven, therefore, that it moves to the western place in the difference between these two times, which is the time of the setting of Aries and Taurus, and the time of the ascensions of the two signs opposite to them, which are Libra and Scorpio. 

Furthermore, if the beginning of Aries is not in any of the "angles" [[notes: The "angles" are the four most powerful points of a chart: the Ascendant (East), Midheaven (North), Descendant (West), and Imum Coeli (South)]], and we place its longitude toward the aforementioned part from the meridian circle at three temporal hours (so that the Midheaven is at 18 degrees of Taurus), the longitude of the beginning of Gemini in its first position from the Midheaven above the earth would be 13 times of the equinoctial circle, according to the precedence of the signs. 

However, when we multiply 17 times by three hours, the longitude of the beginning of Gemini from the Midheaven circle—when it reaches the second position—will be 51 times according to the succession of the signs. All these times together will be 64. 

The *Alhileg* has already traveled through 46 times when it was in the Ascendant, 58 in the Midheaven, and 70 in the West. Therefore, the number of "times" that occurs when its place is between the West and the Midheaven differs from each of the numbers that occur when its place is otherwise than what we have now said. For it is 64 times, and its difference is according to the 3 hours of addition; because the difference of times which appeared to us when we worked through the angles (which are from one quarter to the next) will undoubtedly be of the times of the circle. And when the longitude was three hours, the difference was 6 times. 

If we continue to follow a method suitable to all these matters, we may proceed by this other easier and clearer way [[margin: which soon]] [[notes: This margin note likely refers to a following chapter or section where a simpler calculation is provided]].

It uses complex ratios involving temporal hours and equatorial degrees across various positions in the sky, such as the Ascendant and Midheaven.]]

->**B O O K   I I I.**<-

...which we shall soon describe, we are able to use appropriately. Therefore, when the approaching degree is the ascendant [[notes: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], we shall observe the ascensions which occur from that degree up to the following one. However, when they are in the midheaven [[notes: 'medium coeli,' the highest point the sun reaches in the sky that day]], we shall consider the ascensions of the right circle; and when it is in the west [[notes: the descendant, where the sun sets]], we shall look at the settings of those degrees. But when they stand between these locations—for example, in the aforementioned longitude of Aries—we will first take the times of the difference of one to the other, namely those which are owed to each of the two angles formed on either side of Aries. For this reason, because the beginning of Aries is between the angle of the midheaven and the angle of the west (for its beginning was placed after the midheaven which is above the earth), we will take the times which are owed to the sign of Gemini. If Aries were in the midheaven, they are 58; we shall take the times owed to it if Aries were in the west, which are 70. When this has been done, we shall take their differences, and then we will observe how great the length of the temporal hours [[notes: 'Temporal hours' were a historical way of measuring time where the day and night were each divided into 12 equal hours; thus, an 'hour' changed length depending on the season.]] of the preceding point is found to be from each of the two angles positioned within it, and what part that is of the 6 temporal hours. We shall then take the amount of that part from the difference which we found between the two angles. Furthermore, whatever was taken from the angle to which we made the relation, we have determined it must be subtracted or added.

For example: Since the increase that occurs through these 6 established hours was 12 times, and because we have placed the length of the preceding place from each of the two angles at three temporal hours (which is half of 6), we take half of 12, which we add above 58, or subtract from 70; we find the increase to be 60. But if the length of this place from any of the two angles were two temporal hours (which is a third part of those 6 hours), we take a third part of 12, which is the difference, which is 4. If, however, those hours of length are from the midheaven, we add those 4 times above 58. If indeed they were the length from the west, we shall subtract those same 4 from 70. It is suitable, therefore, that by this method we should learn the quantities of time of the aforesaid lengths, just as is fitting and necessary.

It remains for us to notify you of each type of the aforementioned things meeting the *alhileg* [[notes: The Hyleg, or 'Life-Giver,' the most important point for determining vitality and lifespan]] itself; those which are of shorter time shall be the settings, and those which are among what are called †*felimecatura* [[margin: otherwise *climatiertos*]] [[notes: These are corrupted technical terms likely referring to 'interfictors' or 'climacterics'—specific degrees in the sky believed to 'cut off' or end life]], and others also which are said to meet it. The knowledge of this matter will come from the science of the harmful meeting which hinders, and the good meeting which helps, which are said to happen according to the recently mentioned method, as well as from the beginnings of the following years, over which there is no doubt that the place which met the *alhileg* holds significance. For when the places of the meeting are harmful and unfortunate, and the places of the stars in the beginnings of subsequent years are hindering the dominant places, it is not improper for us to know that what comes from there will truly be death. But if only one of these two is good, we do not doubt that what happens from it will be a great stroke of luck, though there are great obstacles causing great fear. If, however, both should be good, it is manifest that laziness and weakness, or an obstacle, or exile and pilgrimages will happen from there. We shall grasp the specific types occurring in each of these matters from the similarity of the place of the meeting thing to the matters of the nativity [[notes: the birth chart]]. And whenever we might doubt which of their places ought to be the 'killers' [[notes: 'interfectores,' planets or points that signal the end of life]], nothing can prohibit us from considering and observing the things which come to the *alhileg* in each person born; and in that which is to come, we will follow that which resembles it, which has already happened and appeared from the accidents, and we will consider the manner of them all, because the manner in the perfection of those things which happen through them is of equal strength in all. According to this, therefore, we shall establish our investigation and their increase and diminution.

->### On the form and figure of the body of the newborn, and of its temperament. Chapter XI.<-

**A**fter the completion of the choosing of life [[notes: determining the lifespan]], we shall first begin to describe the form and figure of the body from particular things, as is fitting in order; this is because the qualities of the body naturally precede the qualities of the soul, since the body is denser, and more things are apparent in it which are proper to its assembly as they are born with it. In the soul, however, they do not appear, except for those which are through the first occasion after
->**the birth.**<-

It then transitions into Chapter 11, which discusses the physical appearance and temperament of the person born, arguing that physical traits are easier to discern than those of the soul at birth.]]

[[meta: This page continues from the introductory sections of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos (here titled Quadripartitum), moving into the specific techniques of natal astrology. Having established the general influences of the heavens, the text now focuses on Book III, Chapter 11, which deals with "The Form and Temperament of the Body"—essentially how planetary positions at birth determine a person's physical appearance and health.] ]

-># CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM<-

...at birth and creation, it happened step by step. Those things which are outside the body happen much later in the future time after these. It is fitting for us, in the universality of the matter, to observe the eastern horizon [[notes: Known today as the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]] and the wandering stars [[notes: The planets]] which follow it, or the lords of their disposition in the manner we have previously described. In the particularity of the matter, the state of the Moon is also to be considered.

[[margin: Whence the form of man comes.]]
As it is fitting for us to consider here again, the form and manner of bodies are apprehended only from the nature of the configurations of these two places [[notes: The Ascendant and the Moon]], and from the configurations of the planets who are their dispositors [[notes: The planets that "rule" or have authority over those signs]], as well as from the mixture of those things which are in each of their species, and also from the configuration of the fixed stars rising with them. Indeed, those whose powers precede the powers of others are the stars dominating the disposition, which are then aided again by the quality proper to those same places. The particular matter, which can be easily and absolutely declared from their manners, is that which follows.

[[margin: Saturn’s complexion.]]
The first thing we say regarding the stars is that when **Saturn** is oriental [[notes: "Oriental" refers to a planet rising in the morning before the Sun; "Occidental" refers to it setting after the Sun as an evening star. This position was believed to change the planet's physical influence.]] and is the sole dispositor, the nature in figure will be of a **honey color** [[notes: A sallow or dark yellowish-tan complexion]], of moderate thickness, his hair will be black, the hair of the head curly, the hair of the chest thick, the eyes moderate, the body of temperate magnitude, and in his complexion [[notes: In this period, "complexion" referred to the balance of the four humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which determined health and temperament]], coldness and moisture will prevail. And when he is occidental, the native will be blackish, lean, of a small body, having flat and thin hair, well-proportioned, his eyes black, and in his complexion dryness will prevail.

[[margin: Jupiter’s.]]
When **Jupiter** is the lord of the disposition of the aforesaid places and is oriental, the native will be of a white color and of a pleasing and moderate hairiness, his eyes moderate, of a fitting stature and moderate quantity; in his complexion, heat and moisture will prevail. But if he is occidental, he will be white, except that he will not be of such a pleasing whiteness as we said above; his hair will also be flat, and he will be **bald on the front part of his head**, his eyes moderate, and he himself of a moderate body; moisture will prevail in his complexion.

[[margin: Mars’.]]
And when **Mars** is oriental, his form will be of whiteness and redness [[notes: A ruddy or "florid" complexion]], participating in a good quantity and a suitable fleshiness, his eyes varied, his hair thick and moderate; in his complexion, heat and dryness will prevail. But if he is occidental, the native will be of a purely red color and of a body of moderate quantity, having small eyes and thin, flat, and yellowish hair; dryness will prevail in his complexion.

[[margin: Venus.]]
Indeed, the works of **Venus** are likened to the works of Jupiter, except that those things which happen through her are more beautiful and more pleasing; her beauty is more likened to the beauty of women; he will also be of a better figure and a more suitable quality of soul, and the body is softer. Likewise, it is among her properties to make the eyes somewhat reddish and attractive.

[[margin: Mercury.]]
When **Mercury** is also oriental, the native is likened to the color of honey, and will be of a moderate quantity of body, well-proportioned, of small eyes, having moderate hair, and heat will prevail in his complexion. But if he is occidental, the native will participate in blackness and a saffron color, being lean, having a thin voice and hollow sockets; the pupil of the eyes will be like the **pupil of a goat’s eye** [[notes: Likely referring to a pale or yellowish iris, or perhaps an unusual shape]], declining toward redness. In his complexion, there is no doubt that dryness prevails.

[[margin: The Sun & Moon.]]
The **Sun** and the **Moon** aid each of these stars when they are associated with them in a configuration. For the Sun aids in figure and shapeliness, and in the fatness of the body; the Moon generally helps in temperament and leanness or moisture, but especially when she is separating from the Sun; her help will also be particularly according to her properties from the light that is in her, just as we related in the beginning of this book.

Likewise, stars generally, when they are matutinal [[notes: Rising in the morning]] and appearing, make large bodies; when they are in their first station [[notes: The point where a planet appears to stand still before turning retrograde]], they bestow vigor and strength upon them; when they precede the Sun, they temper these things; and when they move in their second station, they make those things weaker; but when they set, they work their misery, impediments, and burdens.

Again, the same places in which they are will aid the form and figure of the native, and the complexion of the same, as we said before. Universally also, the **quarter** which is produced from the vernal equinoctial point [[notes: Spring Equinox]] up to the summer solstice will demonstrate the native to be of a good color, of fitting stature, and of suitable fleshiness, with good eyes; and in him, heat and moisture will prevail. But the quarter which is from the summer solstice up to the equino...

...the point of the autumnal equinox [[notes: The moment in September when day and night are of equal length, marking the start of the "third quarter" of the astrological year]] is reached, it will grant the native a moderate and middling body size, a fitting fleshiness, large eyes, and thick, curly hair; in such a person, heat and dryness will prevail. But the fourth quarter, which extends from the autumnal equinox point to the winter solstice, will designate that the native has a honey-colored complexion, a lean frame, a slender voice, broad shoulder-blades, and average hair and eyes; in this person, coldness and dryness shall prevail. Furthermore, for the quarter which is placed from the winter solstice to the vernal equinox point [[notes: The spring equinox in March]], we shall not doubt that it gives the native a black complexion, a moderate body size, straight and thin hair, and a well-proportioned composition; in this person, coldness and moisture will prevail. In particular, however, those places whose shapes are likened to human forms—namely, those shapes formed within and without the circle of signs [[notes: The Zodiac]]—will produce bodies of fitting and moderate composition. But those whose forms do not lean toward a balanced temperament of the body are proven to imitate their own likenesses; they cause their members to be similar to their own members in some likeness, for they make them more prone to greatness or smallness, to strength or weakness, and to a fitting or unfitting physical composition. For those signs which produce greatness are **Leo**, **Virgo**, and **Sagittarius**; those that produce smallness are **Pisces**, **Cancer**, and **Capricorn**. Likewise, that which comes from **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Leo**, toward their beginnings and in their higher degrees, will make the limbs better and more prone to fatness. However, that which is located toward the lower and extreme parts of these signs applies them more to leanness. In the opposite case, that which is placed toward the beginnings of **Sagittarius**, **Gemini**, and **Scorpio** causes a decline toward leanness, and that which claims the ends of these signs for itself makes them more prone to fatness. Likewise, **Virgo**, **Libra**, and **Sagittarius** produce a body leaning toward balance and a good composition. **Scorpio**, **Pisces**, and **Taurus**, however, remove the body from such balance. It is therefore appropriate for us to observe the qualities of other figures in another way, to compare them with one each other, and to conjecture from there the properties united in the form of bodies, their complexion, and the mixture of all these things.

## ->*Concerning the impediments and infirmities occurring to the body of the native. Chapter XII.*<-

Since in this place we wish this to be generally known again, it is appropriate for us to observe two angles of the hemisphere, which are the Ascendant and the West [[notes: Also known as the Descendant, the point where stars set]], but specifically the West itself and that which is before it, which we say is clearly that which has no connection with the angle of the Ascendant; we must also observe the two malefic stars [[notes: Usually Saturn and Mars, considered "infortunas" or unlucky in traditional astrology]] and what their quality is in respect to these places. For when both of them, or one of them, are in that same place or in its fourth or opposite aspect [[notes: Astrological "aspects" or angles of 90 or 180 degrees, believed to be tense or difficult]] in respect to the degrees ascending toward the aforementioned places, we shall not doubt that infirmities and impediments will happen to the body of the native. This is most especially true when either or both of the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]] are in the angles in the manner we have said—namely, that both are in the same second angle or in two opposite to each other. For then, not only does one malefic star gain strength when it has ascended toward them after the luminaries and is located in an angle to cause some of the aforementioned infirmities—such as the infirmities which the places of the hemisphere signify, along with the places of the signs and the nature of the malefic and afflicted stars, and the stars associated with them in figure—but it is also strengthened again when it has ascended before the luminaries. This is because the parts of each sign surrounding the receiving part—I say the part receiving the light from the parts of the hemisphere, the part sustaining the impediments—signify that part of the body in which the event will occur; they also designate whether that which will happen is an impediment, or an infirmity, or both. -># 52 CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY'S QUADRIPARTITUM<-

[[notes: The *Quadripartitum*, also known as the *Tetrabiblos*, is Ptolemy's foundational 2nd-century work on astrology.]]

[Satur-]nus [[notes: Saturn]] governs, among the more important parts of a human, the right ear, the spleen, the bladder, and phlegm. Jupiter, however, governs touch, the lungs, the ribs, cartilages, and semen. Mars governs the left ear, the kidneys [[notes: Latin *rigones* is an archaic/variant spelling related to *renes*]], the veins, and the testicles. The Sun governs sight, the heart, the brain, the nerves, and all the members of the right side of the body. Venus governs smell, the liver, and the flesh. Mercury governs speech, deliberation, memory, the tongue, bile, and the nostrils. The Moon governs taste and swallowing, the stomach, the belly, the female reproductive organs [[notes: *pudenda*]], and all the members of the left side of the body. 

Generally, physical impediments [[notes: *impedimenta* here refers to permanent disabilities or birth defects]] will occur for the most part when the "unfortunate" stars [[notes: Malefic planets, specifically Saturn and Mars]], which are the cause of them, are Oriental [[notes: Rising in the east before the Sun]]. However, infirmities [[notes: *infirmitates*, referring to temporary or recurring illnesses]] will happen when these same stars are Occidental [[notes: Setting in the west after the Sun]]. The reason for this distinction is that impediments usually happen only once and do not change, whereas infirmities either last forever or recur in cycles. 

In matters where specific accidents are discerned, once the proper charts have been tested and the figures and qualities that signify infirmities and impediments are observed, we can understand the accidents that follow. These occur in the majority of cases according to similar positions of the stars. For instance, there will be a loss of sight in one of the eyes when the Moon is alone in the aforementioned "angles" [[notes: The four primary houses of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]] and is in conjunction or opposition at that hour, or when it is in another aspect with the Sun and has an *alictisal* [[notes: An Arabic-derived term meaning "application," or moving toward an astrological aspect]] with certain *asaceha* stars [[notes: Arabic *al-sa'qa*, referring to nebulous star clusters that appear "cloudy"]] which are in the zodiac circle. These include the nebulous star in Cancer [[notes: Praesepe, the Beehive Cluster]], the *athoraie* in Taurus [[notes: The Pleiades]], the tip of the arrow in Sagittarius, the tail of Scorpio, the area around the *aldhafeta* in Leo [[notes: Likely *Al-Dafirah*, the Tuft of the lion's tail]], and the *calbez* of Aquarius [[notes: Possibly *Al-Kalb*, the Dog or the Heart star of that region]]. 

Whenever the Moon is in an angle and is Occidental, and Mars alone is Oriental, or both Mars and Saturn are Oriental and approaching it from a distance; or if the Sun is in an angle and these two stars rise before it; or if the two luminaries [[notes: The Sun and Moon]] are joined in a figure and both are in the same sign or opposite signs; and if they are "morning stars" in respect to the Sun and "evening stars" in respect to the Moon, then the loss of sight will occur in both eyes. Through Mars, the predicted loss of sight will happen through some trauma, or by iron [[notes: Likely a blade or tool]], or by fire. If Mercury is associated with it in the figure, this will happen from a struggle, or in sport, or by an attack from criminals. Saturn, however, causes this through a "whiteness" of the eyes [[notes: Likely cataracts]], or by cold, or by a strike from a projectile, and things of this nature. 

Likewise, when Venus is in one of the aforementioned angles, and specifically in the Occidental one, and is with Saturn or associated with it in a figure, and they have changed places, and Mars is elevated above it or in opposition to it, this results in men having no children, and in women, abortions and premature births. Sometimes it results in the "cutting off" of children [[notes: This may refer to early childhood death or physical defects]], especially in Cancer, Virgo, and Capricorn, and when the Moon from the east has an *alictisal* with Mars. 

If Venus is associated with Mercury and Saturn in this way, and Mars is elevated above it or diametrically opposite to it, the child will be born without testicles, or as a hermaphrodite, or "closed" [[notes: Potentially referring to an imperforate anus or vaginal atresia]]. If the Sun is also associated with this figure, and the luminaries and Venus are masculine, and the Moon is Occidental while the malefics are in the following degrees, if the child is male, he will be unmanned [[notes: *ementulabitur*, emasculated or castrated]] or have impediments in his testicles. This happens most often in Leo, Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius. If the child is female, she will be sterile, and perhaps some of these individuals will not escape impediments of the eyes. 

Those whose tongues are tied in speaking and who are [[margin: Stuttering / children.]] stutterers are those for whom Saturn and Mercury are in the aforementioned angles with the Sun, especially when Mercury is Occidental and both are associated with the Moon. If Mars is with these two stars and associated with the Moon, he will, for the most part, "untie" the stiffness of their tongues. 

Furthermore, when the luminaries approach the malefic stars in "unfortunate" angles, or when the malefics are opposite the luminaries—especially when the Moon is in one of its two nodes, or in *casmon* [[notes: Likely a corruption of an Arabic term for a specific lunar degree or "cazimi" (in the heart of the Sun)]], or in "infirm signs" such as Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Scorpio, and Capricorn—this results in hunchbacks or the destruction of a limb, such as lameness...
