But if the **malefic planets** [[notes: In astrology, "infortunatrices" refers to Saturn and Mars, traditionally believed to bring hardship]] are positioned with the **luminaries** [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]], these same impediments will occur as a result of their influence. If, however, they are in the **midheaven** [[notes: The highest point in the sky at the time of birth, representing one's public life and actions]] and are elevated above the luminaries, and their positions are aligned in longitude with them, these impediments will arrive through major accidents full of terror—such as falling from a height, falling into the hands of thieves, or being harmed by four-footed beasts. And if **Mars** is elevated and dominant, these accidents will happen through fire and burning, or from great wounds, or because one falls into the hands of thieves. But if **Saturn** is elevated and dominant, these same accidents will occur through falling, drowning, or paralysis.

The impediments that occur most frequently when the **Moon** exists in the two equinoctial points and the two solstitial points are these: When the Moon is in the **vernal equinoctial point** [[margin: The Moon in the equinoctial points.]] [[notes: The point where Spring begins]], the resulting impediment will specifically be **morphea** [[notes: A condition causing discolored patches of skin]]. If it is in the **summer solstitial point**, it will be **impetigo** [[notes: A contagious skin infection characterized by crusting sores]]. In the **autumnal equinoctial point**, it will be **albaras** [[notes: An old term derived from Arabic for white leprosy or vitiligo]]. But if it is in the **winter solstitial point**, the most frequent result will be **lentigo** [[notes: Freckles or pigmented spots on the skin]] and similar conditions.

Diseases also occur when the "malefics" are associated in a certain way with the **Sun** or **Moon**, but in an opposite manner—that is, when they are associated with the Sun in the morning (matutinal) and with the Moon in the evening (vespertinal).

Regarding what generally follows from these diseases: **Saturn** will make the constitution of the belly of the newborn cold and very phlegmatic; or, because of humors [[notes: The four fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—once thought to govern health]] flowing to the limbs, the person will be emaciated, sickly, and jaundiced (**icteric**). It also causes afflictions in the intestines, coughing, spitting, colic, and **lepta** [[notes: A wasting disease or extreme thinness]]. Along with all these, women will experience pain of the womb.

**Mars**, however, brings the spitting of blood and **melancholia** [[notes: Thought to be caused by an excess of "black bile," resulting here in physical ailments]], which arises from dark colors; it causes abscesses in the lungs and **scabies** [[notes: A skin disease causing intense itching]]. When these occur, the person will always face hardships from incisions [[notes: Surgeries]] and cauterizations performed because of hidden ailments like **ficus** [[notes: "Fig-like" growths, often hemorrhoids]] and **fistulae**, or things that grow and expand in the body, such as hot, fiery ulcers, or even ulcers that spread by "eating" the flesh. For women, these conditions also lead to miscarriages and the loss of limbs in children.

The aforementioned natures of the stars, when associated with one another in the horoscope, sometimes cause specific diseases in the limbs of the body, which **Mercury** assists in making more malicious. For Mercury aids Saturn in cooling, specifically in the flow of humors to the limbs and in their damage—especially those flowing to the palate, chest, and stomach. But Mercury aids Mars in drying and in conditions arising from dryness, such as the crusts of ulcers, **eschars** [[notes: Pieces of dead tissue that fall off a wound]], **dubailet** [[notes: A medieval corruption of an Arabic medical term, likely referring to an internal abscess or boil]], **erysipelas** [[notes: A skin infection known as "St. Anthony's Fire"]], wicked skin eruptions, melancholy, frenzy, epilepsy, and the like.

These conditions sometimes have specific traits based on the differences of the **Zodiac signs** in which the planets are joined. For **Cancer**, **Capricorn**, and **Pisces**, and all signs whose figures resemble wild animals and fish, specifically generate diseases that grow by eating away at the flesh, as well as mange, skin abrasions, **scrofula** [[notes: A form of tuberculosis affecting the lymph nodes]], fistulae, leprosy, and similar things. **Sagittarius** and **Gemini**, however, cause falls, epilepsy, and the like.

And when the stars are in the final degrees of the signs, the resulting disease will appear specifically in the extremities of the body—this happens because of the impediments occurring there and the flow of humors, through which leprosy arises, and for the most part, **podagra** [[notes: Gout in the feet]] and **chiragra** [[notes: Gout in the hands]] result.

When things are thus, if the **benefic planets** [[notes: Jupiter and Venus]] are not associated with the malefic stars that cause these things, and are not with the luminaries in the "angles" [[notes: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart]], the diseases and resulting impediments will be very grave and incurable. The same will happen even if the benefics are associated with them, but the malefics are "elevated" or more powerful.

However, when the benefics are in their more dignified positions and are stronger than the malefics that cause these works, then the impediments will not be shameful or a cause for embarrassment; the diseases will be light and quickly settled. This also occurs when the benefics are "oriental" [[notes: Rising before the Sun]]. For **Jupiter** hides the impediments and causes the diseases of others to cease, providing help through wealth or his attributed virtue. And when he is with Mercury, he will erase diseases with medicines or through the cures of...

## -> On the Qualities of the Soul of the Newborn. Cap. XIII. <-

**M**ethodology for prognosticating the accidents of the body is as we have just described. Regarding the qualities of the soul, however, that which properly pertains to the intellect and reason is always recognized through the qualities of Mercury. But that which concerns the "irrational" part [[notes: In ancient philosophy, the "irrational soul" referred to emotions, instincts, and sensory perceptions, as opposed to the "rational soul" or intellect]]—the height of unreason—is perceived from the Moon, being the more substantial body nearest the two luminaries [[notes: The "two luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon]], as well as from the stars associated with her in the chart, and those joined with her by [[markup: alictisal]] and [[markup: alin chiref]] [[notes: These are Latinized versions of the Arabic astrological terms *attisal* (application) and *inshiraf* (separation), describing planets moving toward or away from an aspect]] conditions. For this reason, since the movements and qualities of the soul are of many kinds, it is by no means appropriate to investigate them by a single, simple path. Instead, they must be observed through many observations and diverse considerations, because the differences between the signs in which the Moon, Mercury, and their rulers are located greatly assist in determining the qualities of the soul’s properties. Furthermore, the configurations of the stars associated with the aforementioned, in respect to the Sun and the significant angles, also aid the movements of the soul according to the specific natures of each star. 

Generally speaking, **Movable signs** [[notes: These are what modern astrologers call "Cardinal signs": Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn]] make the soul focused on unity and universality, and make it love life in cities. Likewise, they compel one to seek praise, to think on divine matters, and to be of sharp wit, an inquisitive and praiseworthy nature, liberal, well-regarded by others, and skilled in the judgments of the stars [[notes: i.e., astrology]]. 

**Common signs** [[notes: These are "Mutable signs": Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces]] make the soul multiform, prone to easy change, difficult to know, agile, loving, unstable, deceitful, having many desires, a lover of music, possessing a quick intellect, and prone to regret. 

**Fixed signs** [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius]] make the soul upright, infallible, steady, of good wit, quiet, intelligent, patient in labors, tolerant, rigid, restraining of pleasures, envious of will, effective, imitative, loving, contentious, law-breaking, and unchangeable. 

From the qualities of the stars and their configurations: that which is oriental and ascending, or particularly that which is in its own [[markup: almiua]] [[notes: Likely *almugea*, a specific planetary dignity or relationship to the Sun]], will make the soul free, capable, confident in its own counsel, rigid, sharp-witted, generous, and open. 

Stars in their **morning stations** [[notes: When a planet appears to stand still in the morning sky before changing direction]], and when they are in the Midheaven [[notes: The highest point of the sky in a chart, representing career and public life]], make souls thoughtful, steady, possessing good memories, quiet, intelligent, magnanimous, immobile, unchangeable, infallible, knowledgeable, industrious, inquisitive, and skilled in the true sciences. 

**Risings of the stars** at the beginning of the night, and their settings, make souls light, agile, weak, intolerant of labor, easily affected, unfortunate, small-minded, fickle, "great" only in a small-minded way [[notes: Meaning someone who puts on airs but lacks true character]], hesitant, weary, slow to move, and solitary. 

**Evening stations** of stars, and when they are in the Midheaven that is under the earth [[notes: The *Imum Coeli* or IC, the lowest point of the chart]], as well as the evening settings of Venus and Mercury during the day, and their morning settings when it is night, will render the soul clean, pure, and sensible, though with an inconsistent memory. These configurations make one an orator, a lover of no labor, an investigator of secret things, and an inquirer into the occult—such as [[markup: nigtomantię]] [[notes: Necromancy or "black magic," though here used more broadly for hidden or forbidden knowledge]]—hidden things, the highest matters, the science of instruments and machines, and the marvelous works of the judgments of the stars. It also makes the soul prophetic, a promoter of the arts, an interpreter of dreams, and similar things. 

Likewise, when the stars that rule the disposition of the soul are in their proper places and in their own [[markup: haiz]] [[notes: From the Arabic *hayyiz*, a condition where a planet is in a sign and "sect" (day or night) that matches its nature]], as we explained in the preceding sections, they make the properties of the soul clear, so that nothing can hinder their effects, and each part will remain distinct and prosper. This is especially true when one and the same star rules two places—that is, when they are associated with the place of Mercury in any configuration and are separated from the Moon, or have [[markup: alictisal]] with her, which if—

But if it should not be as has been said, or if their own proper natures exist in places not appropriate to them, they will make the qualities of the soul not open, but hidden and imperfect, and they shall not prosper. Indeed, the natures of the stars ruling over them, or elevated above them [[notes: In astrology, "elevation" refers to a planet being closer to the Midheaven or "above" another planet in terms of zodiacal order, giving it more power over the other]], make the works of human souls rigid and harmful to their subjects—much like unjust and iniquitous men, to whom these things happen because of a resemblance to the "infortunes" [[notes: The "infortunes" or "malefics" are traditionally Saturn and Mars]]. When these rule, they make their movements toward hindering others easy, and nothing shall prohibit it, nor will there be any difficulty in it. However, when those stars which are of the *haiz* [[notes: *Haiz* is an Arabic astrological term referring to a planet's dignity. A planet is in its *haiz* when it matches the "sect" of the chart (e.g., a masculine planet in a masculine sign above the horizon in a day chart)]] are ruled by stars contrary to their *haiz*, they make the natives have a weak reputation, and they shall not prosper, and they shall suffer punishments. Furthermore, just as with just and equitable men—to whom this happens through a resemblance to the "fortunes" [[notes: The "fortunes" or "benefics" are traditionally Jupiter and Venus]]—when nothing is elevated above them, they will rejoice in doing good to others, and they will be praised for it, nor will any loss come to them from it; indeed, their very goodness will be the occasion of their own profit. But when stars contrary to them are elevated above them, the opposite of the aforesaid will happen: on account of their softness and quietude, and even their love and piety toward men, they will be little valued by people, and they will be blamed, and violence will be done to them.

This, therefore, is the general way in which the qualities of the sensory and rational soul are predicted. We shall teach the particular properties which occur from the natures of the stars according to their lordship through a general discourse, until we arrive at the mixing of influences, which is grasped through the general path. 

Therefore, when Saturn alone rules the disposition of the soul’s affairs [[margin: Saturn alone is the ruler of the disposition]], and is the ruler of the Moon and Mercury—if he is well-placed in respect to the world and the "angles" [[notes: The "angles" are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli]]—the native will love just men, and will be of rigid and profound counsel; he will persist in his own deliberations. He will be industrious and a debater, though sometimes he will deviate slightly from the truth; he will be wealthy, a seeker of power, a "turn-skin" [[notes: *Versipellis*, meaning a shapeshifter or one who changes his mind/appearance to suit his needs]], a hoarder, secretive [[notes: *Subterraneus*, literally "underground" or hidden]], and envious. 

But if he exists in the contrary of what we have said (that is, if he is inconveniently placed), the native will be filthy, vile, small-minded, ignorant, persisting only in his own counsel, envious, and timid. He will be separated from men, deceitful in words, a lover of concealment and mourning, shameless, unfortunate, a lover of toil, loving no one, a deceiver of friends, never rejoicing, and malevolent toward good things.

But if Saturn is associated with Jupiter according to what we have said, and his quality is commendable, the native will be just and will honor his elders; he will be of sound counsel, a helper of the kingdom, a man of knowledge, magnanimous, well-known, a lover of friends, quiet, intelligent, patient, and a philosopher. But if the quality of this star is contrary to the aforesaid, the native will be ignorant of how to do good and senseless; he will converse about diabolical things and linger in places of prayer; he will predict the future, loathe having children, and have no friends. He will dwell in vaults and caves and will not associate with men; no one will trust him. He will be foolish, evil, weak, a hater of honor, regretful, poorly received, of bad choices, and a sufferer of toil.

But if Saturn is associated with Mars, and he himself is of good and laudable quality, the native will be unacknowledging, very industrious, wretched and weak; he will attempt great things with much fear. He will be a heavy brawler, impious, and will think little of all things; immoderate and warlike, he will place his soul in fear and love disturbances. He will be a traitor and a disturber of others, possessed of the worst envy; his soul will be changed by any event. He will make men labor and will rule others by force; a transgressor, he will hold kings and princes in hatred. He will love hypocrisy and victory, being envious and of an evil depth. He will be heavy to tolerate, full of rusticity, intolerable, a boaster of himself, and iniquitous. He will harm men, vilify them, and hold them in hatred; he will not be changed or altered. He will involve himself in many things but will easily withdraw from them; he will be a craftsman and generally studious, and he will even prosper.

But if this star is in the contrary of the aforesaid, it will make the native a plunderer, a highwayman, wretched, of evil quality and evil profit. He will not fear God nor love anyone; he will be a blasphemer, a disturber, a thief, a deceiver, a traitor, a murderer, incestuous, evil, impious, a homicide, a practitioner of the dark arts [[notes: *Nigromanticus*, a "necromancer" or one who works with "black" magic]], a plunderer of temples, a fornicator, a violator of tombs, and generally wicked in all things.

But if Saturn is associated with Venus, and she is of good quality, the native...

He will be peaceful, modest, a lover of knowledge, faithful, and temperate. He is a careful deliberator who keeps himself from impurities, though he may be tedious and prone to jealousy regarding women. 

However, when this star [[notes: Saturn]] is in a condition contrary to the aforesaid [[notes: meaning the planet is "afflicted" or poorly positioned in the birth chart]], the native will be a fornicator and unclean. He will be a necromancer [[notes: *nigromanticus*—one who practices "black" or forbidden magic]] and will meddle in everything.

He will be a thief, a practitioner of necromancy and incantations, crafty,

and he shall not prosper. 

When Jupiter alone is the ruler of the soul’s disposition, if he is of a laudable quality, the native will be magnanimous, generous, just, modest, and cheerful. He will love people and beautiful things; he will be liberal, fair, a man of great thought, gentle, and excellent. Pious in his works, he will do good for men and be a lovable leader. 

But if Jupiter is in the contrary state, the quality of the native's soul will be similar to the above, except that in these traits he will be weaker and more hidden, lacking good intellect. For instead of being magnanimous, he will be a spendthrift; instead of just, he will serve the devil [[notes: *diabolo*—a Christianized translation of a "malignant spirit"]] or be of ill repute. Instead of modesty, he will be a coward; instead of gentle, he will be proud. Instead of loving people of good quality and beauty, he will delight in [crass] pleasures. Instead of great thought, he will be stubborn; he will be ignorant of true liberty, and other such things. 

If Jupiter is associated with Mars, and is of laudable quality, the native will be crafty, a pleader of cases [[notes: *placitator*—likely a lawyer or advocate]], warlike, and an organizer. He will be a most powerful actor who humbles himself to no one. He will be a man of armies and great works, desiring vengeance and total victory. He will make himself a master and be an inventor of things. He will not be ignorant of the truth; he will be provident, magnanimous, and will prosper. He will seek to be honored, though he is wrathful; he will be a knower of many things and will command many people. 

But if this same star is in the contrary state, the native will be a blasphemer, a disturber of words, impudent, and one who can hide nothing. He will be a despiser of others, a hypocrite, a beggar, proud, disobedient, and a plunderer. He will be easily changed, fickle, prone to regret yet unstable, vile, unfaithful, and lacking in knowledge or counsel. Senseless, he will be a snatcher of goods, a loser of his own property, and generally of diverse and mutable character. 

If Jupiter is associated with Venus and is of laudable quality, the native will be simple, a lover of elegance, mastery, and the investigation of things. He will seek out songs, jokes, and banquets. He will be of a good soul, pious, of a healthy heart, and will love and serve God. He will desire to be hardworking for the love of God. He will be sensible, loving, humble, of a splendid soul, and generous. He will by no means abhor the reading of books. He will be a knower of things and temperate in lawful sexual acts. He will love his relatives and desire the appearance of honor and a good name; generally, he will be just and upright. 

But if this star is in the contrary state, the native will be lazy, living a delicate life, and of a womanish soul. He will be a dancer, and his anger will be like the anger of women. He will be a spendthrift and senseless in the affairs of women. He will be a suitor, libidinous, and a delinquent. He will love hair ornaments and extol himself, being ignorant of his own losses...

He will be senseless, perhaps desiring to over-adorn himself, impetuous, committing foul acts, and will be horrid.

He will be full of regret, of disordered movement, a liar, a thief, and will ignore God. He will swear false oaths and be crafty—a man of contradiction. Though wise [in a worldly sense], he will be a hypocrite, manifestly wicked, a blasphemer, a highwayman, a burglar [[notes: Literally "a digger through walls"]], a slayer, an enchanter, a traitor, a necromancer, and a murderer. 

When Venus alone is the mistress of the soul's disposition and exists in a praiseworthy quality, the native will be just and quiet, a man of many delights, sensible, and a man of deliberation. He will love dancing and be very [[margin: ♀]] [[notes: The symbol for Venus]] jealous. He will also be of beautiful form, of good quality, and have good dreams. He will be lovable, pious, and beneficial; he will prosper and generally serve the virtues of Venus.

He will have no courage and no reputation; he will be of the lowest name, and one who trips his feet easily over a stone [[notes: A metaphor for being clumsy or easily thwarted by small obstacles]]. ...is assimilated to them, and if it be of a suitable quality, the native will love mastery and the sciences, will be learned and of sharp wit, a poet, a lover of music and of all things commendable. He will also be of an adaptable soul, a man of luxury and quiet, cheerful, a lover of his friends, and possessed of a good understanding of the law. He will be a lover of horses, of good character and reputation, and will proceed upon the straight path. He will learn willingly and will improve himself through study, imitating the manners of good and honest men, and will liken himself to such men. He will be eloquent and cheerful in speech, lovable, of a temperate soul, a just defender, a man of discernment and magnanimous; he will place less importance on women [[notes: In the gendered social context of the time, this implies a focus on public or intellectual life over domestic or romantic pursuits]], will associate with youths, and will be prone to jealousy. But if the position be to the contrary, the native will be shiftless and of great craftiness, a slanderer, double-faced, double-tongued, of evil counsel, a deceiver, a liar, a troublemaker, and false. He will do unclean things, be profoundly wicked, a traitor in counsel, and will neither love nor be loved. He will deceive women and abandon youths; he will be a man of evil deeds, blaming and censuring others, seeking to do all things—sometimes for good, but often for evil—which he will perpetrate over a long time, and [[margin: Mercury.]] will be blamed in many and diverse matters.

When Mercury alone is the lord of the disposition, and is of a suitable quality, the native will be of good intellect and sharp wit, a reporter of ancient things, and possessed of much integrity and experience. He will be a logician [[notes: Latin *dialecticus*, referring to the art of investigating the truth through reasoned argument]], a speaker on the nature of things, an investigator of the sciences, a benefactor, a man of deliberation, of good reputation, learned in the **quadrivium** [[notes: The four liberal arts of the medieval and Renaissance curriculum: arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy]], a keeper of secrets, and he shall prosper greatly. But if he stands in the contrary position to the aforementioned, the native will be a deceiver and base, making others err; he will proceed according to his own counsel, being frivolous, of hasty movement, and easily changed. Though healthy, he will be ignorant, of great deceit, a liar, of disordered quality, unstable, unfaithful, and disobedient to his master; he will commit injustice, and generally will be of great deceitfulness.

And since these things are so, it is fitting for us to know that the quality of [[margin: The Moon.]] the Moon, which we have spoken of, will assist in some way; for when she is in the places of the **anecas** [[notes: Likely a Latinization of the Greek *anabibazon*, referring to the Moon’s nodes or its "ascending" steps in latitude]], at the northern or southern limits, she will aid in the variations of the qualities of the soul and cause them to alter suddenly. But if she stands in either of these two modes, she will aid the sharpness of the soul's qualities and cause the native to act with haste. Likewise, when the Moon is ascending and increasing in light, she will increase the significations, making them clearer and more essential. But if she is diminished in light, or stands under the rays of the Sun [[notes: Known as being "combust," where the Sun's proximity was thought to weaken or hide a planet's power]], she will cause them to be more hidden, and she will not operate with such force.

The Sun also assists in some way in these things which have been said, if it exists in a similar state with the stars that dominate the disposition of the soul. For when it is assimilated to them, if its quality is commendable, the qualities of the soul will be more direct, further removed from what is crooked, and also more powerful, more generous, and more faithful, as well as of better law. But when the Sun is in the contrary position, and is not assimilated to the star, the qualities of the soul will be worse; the native will be more wretched and base, of greater labor in his own counsel, and will remain so. He will be foolish, of a heavy will, and generally difficult to improve.

->### On the Impediments of the Soul. Chapter XIV.<-

[[insert: Decorative drop-cap **Q**]] **S**ince the descriptions of the soul's own impediments [[notes: *Impedimentis animae* refers here to mental disturbances, illnesses, or "afflictions of the mind" like epilepsy or madness]] follow the narration of its properties, we should generally know and observe the qualities of Mercury and the Moon in relation to one another, and their relation to the **angles** [[notes: The four critical points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]] and to the **malefic stars** [[notes: Literally "unfortunate stars," referring to Mars and Saturn]]. For when the Moon and Mercury are not connected to each other, or when any of the stars whose qualities they impede are elevated above them at the eastern horizon, or surround them, or remain in opposition to them, they signify that impediments of many kinds will come upon the qualities of the soul. This indeed we can know and explain aptly enough from the aforementioned properties of the stars which are assimilated to those places. Moreover, in those things which we have set forth in demonstrating the properties of the soul, we have again explained many impediments from the weaker afflictions of the soul, and perhaps their increases and strengths from the ->abundance<- [[notes: The text cuts off here at the bottom of the page; "superabundantia" likely continues on the next page.]]

[[summary: This page details the character traits produced by Mercury (both alone and in aspect), how the Sun and Moon modify these traits, and begins a chapter on mental illnesses caused by planetary conflicts.]]

--- Page 322 ---
[[meta: This page continues the astrological discourse from Book III, transitioning into Book IV of what appears to be a Renaissance edition of Claudius Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos*. The text focuses on the "diseases of the soul" (mental and behavioral disorders) caused by the positions of the planets at birth.]]

->**B O O K   I V.**<- [[page number: 95]]

...we shall discern the abundance of the works of the "infortunate" [[notes: The "infortunate" or malefic planets are Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship.]] stars. For this reason, if anyone should name those qualities of the soul that cannot be restrained as "impediments"—whether they are intensified or relaxed around a moderate quality—he will name them well and properly. However, that which is less abundant, and is like a weakness, and that which entirely exceeds nature, is found partly in the intellect of the soul and partly in the body receiving the impression, as will be shown.

[[margin: **Epileptics.**]]
Thus, **Epileptics** are most often those in whose births the **Moon** and **Mercury** are not joined to each other (as we said before) nor to the eastern horizon [[notes: The "oriental horizon" refers to the Ascendant, the sign rising in the east at the moment of birth.]]. Furthermore, if in a daytime birth **Saturn**, or in a nighttime birth **Mars**, should be in the "angles" [[notes: The "angles" or pivots are the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven.]], provided that this planet dominates this specific quality.

Those who are **Insane**, however, are those in whom the conditions are the opposite of what we just said: that is, the lord of the quality is **Saturn** by night or **Mars** by day, especially when they are in *Castro* [[notes: Likely a typographical error in the Latin for *Cancro* (the sign of Cancer).]], or in **Virgo**, or **Pisces**.

[[margin: **Demoniacs.**]]
**Demoniacs** [[notes: In this period, "demoniacs" could refer to those suffering from what we now call severe mental illness or neurological conditions.]], and those called *aurōtafelis* [[notes: A corruption of the Greek *hydrokephalous*, referring to hydrocephalus or "water on the brain."]], that is, those in whose heads there is an excess of "humidity," are those in whose births the quality of the infortunates [[notes: Saturn and Mars.]] exists as we described, and they dominate the **Moon**. This occurs when the **Moon** itself is ascending under the **Sun’s** rays, and its lord is in conjunction with **Saturn**, or in "prevention" [[notes: Likely referring to a preceding aspect or opposition.]] with **Mars**, especially in **Sagittarius** and **Pisces**.

If both infortunate planets together prevail in this quality, the diseases of the soul will be incurable, though they will not be ferocious and will remain unnoticed. But if both "fortunes" [[notes: The "fortunes" or benefic planets are Jupiter and Venus, associated with growth and harmony.]]—that is, **Jupiter** and **Venus**—are similar to them, and both infortunates remain in the western angle while the fortunes remain in the eastern angle, they will produce diseases that, although very ferocious, are nonetheless curable. 

If it is **Jupiter** that is aligned with them, the weaknesses will be cured by medicines, whether through diet or antidotes. If **Venus** is similar, they will repel the sicknesses through prophecies or divine aid [[notes: This reflects the Renaissance belief that Venus governed "divine frenzy" and spiritual healing.]]. But if the infortunates are in the eastern angle and the fortunes in the western, the diseases will be incurable, ferocious, and less obvious; the infirmities of epilepsy will endure always with shouting and fear of death. 

The insane, indeed, being devoid of sense, can in no way be restrained; they will hinder their own kinsmen, speak foul things, and similarly the demoniacs. Their infirmities and the excess of humidity which harms the head [we shall consider], and being too exposed, they will strike people with impetuous leaps and similar actions.

Certain places in which that quality exists will sometimes help with their own particular aid. For the places of the **Sun** and **Mars** specifically aid insanity. The places of **Jupiter** and **Mercury** aid the infirmities of epilepsy. The place of **Venus** aids through prophecies and the speaking of occult things. The places of **Saturn** and the **Moon** aid demoniacs and the impediments of the humors [[notes: Referring to the "Four Humors" of ancient medicine; an imbalance of fluids was thought to cause disease.]]. 

These, then, are the many species of infirmities happening in the active part of the soul which we have foretold, which arrive generally according to their nature through qualities of this kind. But the differences which specifically happen in the part [of the body] receiving the disposition will appear greatly in the increase or decrease of natural things in males and females. We shall arrive at their prognostication by a path similar to the one already mentioned. 

When we have placed the **Moon** and the **Sun** (just as we placed the **Moon** and **Mercury** there), and we have observed the similarity of **Venus** and **Mars** to them: after the explanation of these things, we shall show that if the "luminaries" [[notes: The Sun and the Moon.]] alone are in masculine signs, men will excessively exercise that which is natural to them. Women, however, will perform too much of what is "against nature" for them [[notes: In the gender norms of the 16th century, this refers to women taking on traditionally masculine roles or traits.]], and those things which are natural to them will be converted into the strength and masculinity of the soul. 

Likewise, if **Mars** and **Venus** (or one of them) are masculine, men will be greatly occupied with the natural things of **Venus** and will be excessively troubled by that vice. Even from matters of "shameful intercourse," they will hastily desire to do things that are against the law. 

Women, however, will perpetrate unnatural acts of desire more than is right, and will be *thahaherat* [[notes: A corruption of the Greek *tribadas*, meaning "tribades" or women who engage in same-sex sexual activity.]], that is, they will intermingle with one another in the [sexual] act. If **Venus** alone is masculine, that which they perpetrate will be hidden and unknown. But if **Mars** is masculine, it will be so manifest that sometimes the women who live with them will be shown as if they were their own proper wives.

But if these same stars are contrary to the aforementioned qualities—that is, if only the luminaries [[notes: The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.]] with the predicted qualities exist in feminine signs—the women will perform those actions which are natural to them. Men, however, will commit those acts which are against their nature, and will cross the boundaries of what is natural with a softness and femininity of soul. [[margin: Venus alone is feminine.]] Likewise, if only Venus is feminine, women will excessively fulfill illicit acts of Venus [[notes: "Acts of Venus" refers to sexual intercourse.]], yet they will more frequently incline toward natural acts, and will do so with anyone, to the point that they deny intercourse to no one, whether the person be deformed or the act against the law. Men, however, will be effeminate and soft, and more inclined toward unnatural acts of Venus; they will also prohibit no one from illicit intercourse, except that they will perform it in secret. Likewise, if Mars is feminine, they will perform both of these things—that is, fornication and baseness—and perform illicit acts openly and without a blush on their face, so that because of their excessive openness, they will be blasphemed and reviled. The Oriental and morning qualities of Venus and Mars help with openness in masculinity. However, their evening and Western quality in femininity helps with concealment. Similarly, if Saturn is with them, he will help strike them with horrors, foulness, pollutions, and great shame, because his nature usually assists each of these things. But if Jupiter is with them, he will increase the beauty and decorum of things, as well as an appropriate sense of shame. And if Mercury is with them, he will assist in the public disclosure of matters, the haste of future events, and the multitude and increase of their various kinds.

->## CL. PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM<-
->### PREFACE TO BOOK IV<-

| [[meta: Historiated woodcut initial 'R' depicting a figure and architecture.]] | **R**eturning, therefore, to those things in which matters before birth, and those which happen at the very hour of birth, as well as all things after birth, can be observed—that which is proper and natural to the person, and by which their whole being is naturally proven—we have demonstrated these as much as possible. Now we turn to those things which happen extrinsically [[notes: "Extrinsically" refers to external circumstances of life, like wealth or career, rather than the person's character or body.]], the explanation of which follows appropriately. The first is to judge the prosperity of the native in substance and health, and to describe their prosperity in substance collectively with things pertaining to the body, as well as to explain their prosperity in health alongside things pertaining to the soul. |

->*On the Prosperity and Substance of the Native.* **Chap. I.**<-

| [[meta: Historiated woodcut initial 'Q' depicting a seated figure.]] | **Q**ualitatively, we ought to grasp knowledge of how the quality of a person’s substance [[notes: "Substance" here means material wealth or property.]] comes about from the "Part of Fortune" alone. This we shall always learn by observing the space between the Sun and the Moon, and by projecting it from the Ascendant in both day and night births, for the reasons we showed in our discourse on life. The way of this observation is as follows. We shall observe the stars that rule the disposition of that sign. And we shall consider what their strength and likeness is, just as we said before. Likewise, we shall observe the stars that are associated with them in the figure, or those that rise above them, whether they are of their own *haiz* or from a contrary *haiz*. [[notes: *Haiz* is a technical Arabic astrological term meaning a planet is in its preferred "sect" (day or night) and in a sign of its own gender.]] For when the dispositors of the aforesaid Part are strong, the native will be of great wealth. Indeed, those stars which are of the [[gloss: haiz]] [[notes: "Haiz" is a technical term in medieval astrology referring to a planet being in its preferred "sect" (day or night) and in a sign of its own gender, which strengthens its influence.]] and which possess the arrangement of the stars, when they bear witness with them, will signify that the native’s disposition remains with him and shall signal his safety. But if the stars which are contrary to the [[gloss: haiz]] are elevated above the places of authority, or follow after those same places, they shall demonstrate the loss of one's substance. Generally, however, the time in which this shall happen is discerned from the aspects of the stars that are to come, relative to the angles [[notes: The "angles" are the four most powerful points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.]] or the places ascending toward the angles.

->### On the prosperity and standing of the native. Chapter II.<-

[[meta: Large decorative woodcut initial R]]
**R**egarding the matter of standing [[notes: The Latin "valetudo" typically means health, but in this astrological context, it refers to the "vitality" or "strength" of one's social status and power.]], and the prosperities of that same standing, we must attend to and observe them from the qualities of the luminaries [[notes: The "luminaries" refer specifically to the Sun and the Moon.]] and the stars surrounding them, just as we observe their likeness in other matters. For when both luminaries are in masculine signs, and both, or one of them, resides in the angles—most especially that one which is the lord of the [[gloss: haiz]]—and five wandering stars [[notes: The "erratic" or wandering stars are the five planets known to the ancients: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.]] surround them, and if those surrounding the Sun are morning stars, and those encompassing the Moon are evening stars, we shall not doubt that the native will be a king. 

But if the stars that surround them also reside in the angles, or share a fellowship in the figure with the angles existing above the earth, the native shall be of great standing and most powerful, even a king of the world. His fortune will also be increased when the surrounding stars are on the right and are associated with the angles above the earth. However, when the qualities of the other stars are like this quality, but only the Sun revolves in a masculine sign while the Moon is in a feminine one, and one of them is in the angles, the native will be a man of solitary rule and a slayer. 

If, along with this, the surrounding stars do not appear in the angles, nor testify to them, the native will be of great name only, and his standing will appear like that of one who rules a single region, or like the dominion of a bailiff or the command of an army, and not like the dominion of an Alcaide [[notes: "Alcaide" is a term derived from Arabic meaning a governor, judge, or commander who manages an entire territory or kingdom.]] who organizes the whole realm. But if the luminaries do not, but many of those surrounding stars do reside in the angles or have a fellowship in the figure with them, he will not be of such great standing, nor even of great name, and he will remain unknown. Nevertheless, he will prevail in the management of cities, and in the affairs of the arrangement of life, he will be mediocre. 

If, however, the stars which surround the luminaries have no likeness to the angles, the native will appear wretched and unhappy in his works. And if the luminaries reside neither in the angles nor in masculine signs, and the fortunes [[notes: The "fortunes" or "benefics" are the planets Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring good luck.]] do not surround them, he will be in the extreme of misery and lack of prosperity. Therefore, the path that must be walked in the investigation of these things is this which we have shown in the increase and decrease of standing. We must observe the many qualities which exist between increase and decrease through those things found in that species of particular alteration which the luminaries and the stars surrounding them possess, and which they have arranged for those surrounding them. For when the dispositors [[notes: A "dispositor" is a planet that rules the sign in which another planet is located, thereby exerting influence over it.]] are the lords of the [[gloss: haiz]] or of fortune, the native will endure longer in his standing. But if those contrary to the [[gloss: haiz]] dominate, or if they are "infortunes" [[notes: The "infortunes" or "malefics" are Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship.]], his standing will appear weak and will pass away easily. 

The matters of future standing are to be observed from the specific qualities of the stars that surround the luminaries. For when Saturn is the dispositor of this matter, the strength of standing will consist in the multitude of substance and in the gathering of money. But if it be Jupiter or Venus, his strength will be in pleasures and gifts, and in honor and magnanimity. If it be Mars, it will be in the command of expeditions, in victories, and in the fear of his subjects. And if it be Mercury, it will be in intellect, discipline, and the management of affairs.

we shall observe. If, however, one of them happens to belong to one planet, and the other to none, we decree that the one to which only one condition applies must be observed. But if the same planet, having emerged from under the Sun's rays [[notes: "Under the rays" refers to a planet being so close to the Sun that it is invisible; here it refers to its first appearance as it moves away]], has appeared slightly in the morning, and is in the mid-heaven [[notes: The *Medium Coeli* or Tenth House, representing the highest point in the sky and one's career]], and another planet besides it has aspected the Moon, both must be considered. We shall give preference, however, to the one which, according to the multitude of its numerical authorities and its own disposition, as previously mentioned, prevails over the other. But if we do not find any of the planets emerging from under the Sun's rays to appear slightly in the morning, or to be moving in the mid-heaven, we shall take the lord of the mid-heaven; though it is clear that this happens in slow-moving works, for whatever the quality of such a person may be, they will remain idle for the greater part of their life. This, then, is the way by which we arrive at the knowledge of the qualities of the stars which govern the disposition of work and mastery, as well as those which signify idleness. The quality of the work and mastery is grasped only from the properties of three stars: Mars, Venus, and Mercury, as well as from the qualities of the signs in which they are located.

[[margin: *Mercury, author of the profession*]] For if Mercury is the author of the work and mastery, the subject will be a negotiator [[notes: The Latin *baratator* usually implies a shrewd dealer or someone involved in exchange]], a computer [[notes: A *computator* was a professional accountant or someone who calculated dates/numbers]], and a teacher; also a merchant and a bookkeeper, a connoisseur of things and a sacrificer [[notes: *Immolator*, likely referring to those involved in religious rites or temple administration]]; he will also judge by the powers of the stars, and generally will be occupied in the reading and exposition of books, and in giving and receiving. But if Saturn testifies to him, he will be a manager of other people's affairs, and an interpreter of dreams, or he will dwell in the houses of God [[notes: Temples or churches]] by occasion of some knowledge or divination that is in him. But if Jupiter testifies to him, the subject will be an author of law, and wise, and will associate with honorable men.

[[margin: *Venus.*]] If the authority of the work and mastery belongs to Venus, the subject will involve himself with the scent of flowers and spices, or with wine, or dyeing, or pigments, or with those things which pertain to adornment, such as the trade of spices, and medicines, and the varieties of flowers; or in decorating, and inn-keeping, or weaving, or trading in pigments, or painting and varying colors, or silk-weaving. And if Saturn testifies to her, his trade will be in luxuries and soft things, and he will be a receiver [[notes: Likely a middleman or fence for goods]] and a necromancer, and things similar to these. But if Jupiter testifies to her, he will be a wrestler, and a maker of crowns; he will also be suited for riches, and his wealth will flow by the occasion of women.

[[margin: *Mars.*]] If Mars is associated with the Sun in the figure [[notes: The birth chart or "horoscope"]], his work and mastery will be concerned with fire, such as the work of a cook, a smelter of metals, as well as the work of copper-smithing and gold mines. But if he is not associated with the Sun, the subject’s mastery will be conducted in iron, such as building ships, plowing, architecture, cutting stones, engraving seals in the stones of rings, splitting trees, and things similar to these. If Saturn testifies to him, he will be a navigator and a swimmer, a carrier of water, and a cook; also a painter, and one who stays in the baths. But if Jupiter testifies to him, he will be a soldier, and a minister of punishments, and a tax-collector, also an innkeeper and a *lamo* [[notes: This may be a contraction or error for *lanius* (butcher) or *lanio* (one who tears)]].

Likewise, if two planets have dominion over the mastery, and they are Venus and Mercury, he will practice music, or games, or singing, or the invention of songs, or any kind of finding of chants. Especially when they are in each other's places, then the subject will be a juggler [[notes: *Ioculator* can mean a jester, minstrel, or entertainer]], a dealer in stars and women [[notes: Likely an astrologer specializing in relationships or an entertainer of women]], a master of humorous instruments, a maker of lutes; and he will be a painter, a preacher, a mocker, and an inventor of incantations. If Saturn testifies to them, his work and mastery will be in those things mentioned above, in trades, and he will sell those things with which women are adorned. If Jupiter testifies to them, he will be a pleader and an accountant, and will always stay in places where people congregate, and around the royal gates; he will teach children, and be concerned with the affairs of the common people.

But if Mars and Mercury have dominion over the work and mastery, he will be learned in the composition of images and arms; he will be a sculptor of things used by divine houses [[notes: Temple or church statuary]], and will make images of animals; he will be a wrestler, a physician, a surgeon, a sorcerer, a fornicator, and a forger of documents. But if Saturn testifies to them, the subject will be a killer, and will snatch the clothes of others; he will be a highwayman and live in caves, and will also be a deceiver. But if Jupiter testifies to them, he will love arms and duels; he will also be a ruler and a manager, and a "skin-turner" [[notes: *Versipellis*, a term for a shape-shifter or a very crafty, adaptable, and often untrustworthy person]]; he will love his work, and be concerned with foreigners, and will profit from such things. ...and a master of lead [[notes: In alchemy and astrology, lead is the metal associated with Saturn]], he will be a farmer, and will dally with arms, and will prepare medicines, and will be a physician. Specifically, however, the differences in the mastery of work are aided in every way by the figures of the signs [[margin: The power of the figures of the stars.]] in which the stars that dominate are moved. For the signs whose figures are likened to the forms of men aid all the mastery of the sciences which men need for perfection. But the signs whose figures are likened to the forms of quadrupeds aid the masteries of mining, merchandising, building, and wood-cutting. Moreover, the solstitial and equinoctial signs [[notes: These are the "cardinal" signs—Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn—which mark the changing of the seasons]] aid the masteries of transport and variation, as well as geometry, agriculture, and matters concerning houses of prayer. But the signs whose figures are likened to the forms of wild and aquatic animals aid the masteries which pertain to moisture, and in which moistening agents are placed; they also aid the skill of herbs, the construction of ships, as well as the trade of salting and salted goods. 

But if the Moon should specifically dominate the place of mastery, and after its conjunction goes toward Mercury, and is in Capricorn, Taurus, or Cancer, the native [[notes: The person for whom the birth chart is cast]] will be wise, and a sacrificer, and an observer of water vessels. If, however, she should be in Sagittarius or in Pisces, he will divine through the dead [[notes: This refers to necromancy]], and will even compel wicked spirits to be moved from place to place. But if she should be in Virgo or Scorpio, he will be a necromancer and an astrologer, he will reveal hidden things and predict the future. If she should be in Leo, Aries, or Libra, he will be a prophet, and an interpreter of dreams [[gloss: interpreters]], and a wise man. 

This, therefore, is the way which it is fitting for us to observe in order to rationally know the qualities of masteries and their kinds. Furthermore, the quantities of their virtue are to be observed through the strengths of the stars which dominate the disposition. For when they are oriental [[notes: Rising in the east before the Sun]], or situated in the "angles" [[notes: The most powerful points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]], his masteries will be of dignity, dominion, and strength. But if they are occidental or "falling" from the angles, the masteries will be established under the power of others. 

But if the fortunes [[notes: Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus]] prevail over them, his mastery will be suitable, commendable, and quiet, nor will he ever be deceived in it. But if the misfortunes [[notes: Malefic planets, Saturn and Mars]] prevail over them, they will be vile, contemptible, and damaging, and he will be deceived in them. If Saturn should be the impeder, coldness, delay, and sluggishness will happen there. If Mars should be the impeder, fear and destruction will occur there. And if both should be impeders, there will be many inconveniences in the whole time of his life. Their increase and decrease will be perceived from the qualities of the stars, which are the occasions of the future according to their relationship to the angles, whether they be matutinal or vespertine [[notes: Rising in the morning or appearing in the evening]].

[[margin: Concerning wives.]] ...if [the Moon] has an *itisal* [[notes: *Itisal* is a Latinized Arabic term (from *ittiṣāl*) used in medieval translations of Ptolemy to mean "application," or the movement of the Moon toward an aspect with another planet.]], he will be joined to only one wife. But if she remains in a sign of two bodies [[notes: These are the "bicorporeal" or mutable signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces—which often signify plurality in traditional astrology.]] or of many figures, and in that same sign she has an *itisal* with more than one planet, he will be betrothed to many. But if the planets with which she has an *itisal* by conjunction or aspect are benefics [[notes: *Fortunæ* (fortunes), referring specifically to Jupiter and Venus.]], the wives will be suitable and fit; if, however, they are malefics [[notes: *Infortunæ* (misfortunes), referring to Saturn and Mars.]], the opposite will be true. For if she has an *itisal* with Saturn, his wife will be hardworking, but her character will be savage. If she has an *itisal* with Jupiter, she will be suitable, capable, and of a learned disposition. But if with Mars, she will be bold and indomitable. And if with Venus, she will be beautiful and very cheerful. If, however, with Mercury, she will be of good intellect. Likewise, if Venus is present with Jupiter, Saturn, or Mercury, she will be quite useful to him in matters pertaining to life, and she will greatly love both him and their children. But if she is with Mars, she will be destructive, unstable, and lacking in understanding.

In the marriages of women, however, the solar qualities at the hour of the woman's birth must be observed. For when the Sun is in either of the two eastern quadrants [[notes: The "oriental" quarters of the chart, usually meaning the space between the Ascendant and the Midheaven, or the Descendant and the IC.]], she will be betrothed to a husband in her youth, or in her old age she will take a young man for a husband. But if he is in either of the two western quadrants, she will be joined to a husband late in life, or in her first youth she will be betrothed to an old man. If the Sun is in a sign of one figure, and we find a morning planet in it, she will be given to only one husband. And if he is in a sign [[margin: To a husband.]] of two bodies or many figures, or is associated with more than one morning planet in the figure, she will have many husbands. 

Likewise, if Saturn is associated with the Sun in the figure, her husband will be upright, just, and hardworking. If the Sun has a partnership with Jupiter, he will be humble and magnanimous; but if with Mars, he will be cruel, without affection, and will not humble himself; and if with Venus, he will be upright and handsome; but if associated with Mercury, he will be successful in the affairs of life and hardworking. But if Venus is with Saturn, her husband will be weary and will abstain from Venusian [sexual] acts; and if she is with Jupiter, her husband will be good, just, and modest; and if with Mars, he will be of a sharp temperament, very preoccupied with Venusian acts, and will be a fornicator; but if she remains with Mercury, he will be very pious toward his own children.

Furthermore, what we said above regarding the two eastern quadrants for the Sun should be understood as being said of the two quadrants of which one precedes the point of the ascendant and the other precedes the point of the descendant of the zodiacal circle. In the case of the Moon, however, we should understand this as being of the two quadrants between the conjunction and the prevention [[notes: *Præuentionem* here likely refers to the Full Moon (opposition).]] until half of that light is reached. By the two western quadrants, we shall understand those which are opposite to these aforementioned.

And when the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon.]] are suitably associated with each other in both nativities [[notes: Meaning the birth charts of the man and the woman.]] by aspect—that is, they behold each other by a trine or sextile [[notes: Favorable astrological aspects of 120 and 60 degrees.]]—and especially when this is by *extabdil* [[notes: A corruption of the Arabic *itbiḍāl*, meaning mutual reception, where two planets occupy each other's signs.]], and most especially when the Moon in the woman’s birth is suitably associated with the Sun in the man’s birth, their marriage will never be dissolved. It will be dissolved for any reason when the aforementioned places of the luminaries are in signs that are not connected to each other, or which are diametrically opposed, or which behold each other by a tetragonal radiation [[notes: A square aspect (90 degrees), traditionally considered a source of conflict.]]. 

But if the benefics direct their rays toward the luminaries which agree in a suitable figure, the marriage will remain in mutual affection, joy, and health. But if the malefics behold them, it will indeed remain, but in litigation, hatred, and loss. A similar thing happens when their qualities are incompatible; for if the benefics testify to the luminaries, the marriage will not be entirely untied, but after a separation they will be reconciled and will remain together with lasting affection. But if the malefics testify to them, there will be a separation full of litigation and savagery. But if only Mercury is present with them, they will be manifestily separated with accusations and com- [[margin: Divorce.]] plaints. But if Venus is with them, this will happen because of adultery or sorcery [[notes: *Nigromantiam* (necromancy/black magic), often used in this period to describe "love potions" or charms used to cause infidelity.]], or because of similar things. 

Furthermore, how marriage is formed through Venusian, Martial, and Saturnine qualities will be demonstrated. These figures are indeed the beginnings of Leo and Aries, as well as what is called by the Greek letter λ [[notes: Lambda]], and this is its form λ, one of whose stars is called Aldebaran; there is also that which is called *calcas* in Greek, which is the end of Leo; the face of Capricorn is also numbered among these same figures. But if this quality is found in the first two angles, which are the oriental [[notes: 1st House/Ascendant]] and the meridian [[notes: 10th House/Midheaven]], he will be manifest in his works and will reveal them in places where men come together. If, however, it is in the last angles, which are the occidental and the northern, he will be a eunuch, and will distinguish various voices with a reed-pipe [[notes: Possibly suggesting a career in music or a change in vocal pitch due to castration]], or he will be sterile, or without an opening in his rod [[notes: A reference to a physical deformity of the penis]]. But if Mars is with them in these, if he is male, his rod will be cut off with the testicles, and if it is a female, her womanly parts will be exceedingly deep. In masculine nativities, it is fitting for us to investigate the qualities of those born in venereal acts from Mars generally in this way: When, therefore, he is separated from Venus or Saturn, and Jupiter bears witness to him, the one born will be gentle in coitus and not impure, nor will he serve Venus unless compelled by nature alone. But if he is with Saturn alone, he will be kept far from Venus, and in this, he will be lazy and cold. If he is associated in the figure with Venus and Jupiter, he will be easily moved to these things and will have a great desire for them, yet he will reprove and restrain himself, and will be very cautious of base and impure things. But if he is with Venus alone, or with Jupiter alone without the aspect of Saturn, he is said to have a great desire for debauchery and will wish to live delicately. ->## On Children. Chapter V.<-

[[margin: **q**]] Since we must subsequently treat the matter of children after marriage, it is fitting that we observe the planets that are in the place of the **zenith** [[notes: The Midheaven or 10th House]] of our heads, or in the following place, which is that of **Fortune** [[notes: The 11th House, traditionally called the 'Good Spirit' or 'Good Fortune']], or in the place associated with these in the figure. For if we do not find planets in these places, we must consider those which are diametrically opposite to them. We shall consider the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus in the granting of children, but the Sun, Saturn, and Mars in the denial of children or in their scarcity. We shall assign Mercury to whichever of these he is associated with in the figure. If he is eastern, he will give children; if he is western, he will take them away. If the giving planets are alone, there will be one child. If they are in signs of "two bodies" [[notes: Mutable signs like Gemini, Sagittarius, or Pisces]] and are feminine, there will be two. Similarly, if they are in signs of many children—such as Pisces, Cancer, and Scorpio—two or more will be born. If the planets are masculine in the signs and figures they hold with respect to the Sun, that which is born will be of the male sex. But if they are in feminine signs and figures, there is no doubt that what is born will be of the female sex. But if the "malefics" [[notes: Unlucky planets, specifically Saturn and Mars]] overcome them, or if they are in sterile signs like Leo and Virgo, there will indeed be a child, but it will be unfortunate and will not live. But if the Sun and the malefics dominate the aforesaid places and the "benefics" [[notes: Lucky planets, Jupiter and Venus]] do not look upon them, this signifies that there will be no child; and if they exist in masculine or sterile signs and the malefics overcome them, they signify that the person will have no child at all. And if they are in feminine signs, or signs of many children, or if the benefics testify to them, they will announce a child who will suffer some defect or who will live for a short time. But if every **alaiz** [[notes: A Latinized Arabic term, likely referring to the *Hyleg* or 'Alcocoden'—the planetary significators or "Lot of Children"]] has a part in signs designating children, all or some of those children will be held in abhorrence by men; the extent of this will appear according to the greater strength of the planets over the other **alaiz** testifying at the time. This occurs if their power is greater according to the multitude of planets, or according to greater dignities, or if they are more eastern, or closer to an "angle" [[notes: The four cardinal points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]], or higher, or ascending toward the angles. And if the ruling stars of the aforementioned signs that give children are eastern in their own proper places, the offspring will be powerful and of great name. But if they are western in places of the **alaiz** contrary to them, the offspring will be wret-

->## On Friendships and Enmities. Chapter VI.<-

[[margin: q]] **The qualities** of friendship and enmity—of which those that are more durable are called "friendships and enmities," while those that are less durable, involving applications and repulsions [[notes: "Application" and "repulsion" are technical terms for when planets move toward or away from an "aspect" or significant angle with each other]] in another context, are called "common"—should be investigated in this way. Therefore, in those qualities that we trust in greater matters, it is necessary for us to observe the places that most correspond to the lordship of power in the birth of both individuals: that is, the places of the Sun and Moon, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune. For when all these are in the same sign, or have exchanged places either partially or entirely—and especially when there are nearly seventeen degrees between the Ascendant of both—we shall say that there will be a fixed love between them, which will neither be separated nor disturbed. But if they rotate in places that are not joined to each other, or which are positioned in direct opposition (by diameter), they will be in the highest discord, or will be adversaries for a long time. But if it exists in neither of these ways, but only in signs that are associated in turn: if they regard each other from a trine [[notes: A harmonious astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart]] or sextile [[notes: A harmonious aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart]], there will be a lesser affection between them. If, however, they see each other from a quartile [[notes: Also known as a "square," an aspect of 90 degrees that usually indicates tension]], we have no doubt that there will be lesser discords between them. Thus, sometimes in their affection, "cuttings off of words" [[notes: Meaning arguments or falling out]] will occur, and they will alternately think little of one another; these things will happen when the "unfortunate" planets [[notes: Often called "malefics," such as Mars or Saturn]] pass through the places of the figures. But in times of discord, peace and concord will be interposed when the "fortunate" planets [[notes: Often called "benefics," such as Jupiter or Venus]] run through the places of the figures. Therefore, since the mode of friendship and enmity exists in three ways—that is, because the masters of these two qualities are compelled [to act] from birth, or for the sake of profit and loss, or because of anger and joy. When all these aforementioned places, or as many of them as possible, are assimilated to each other, friendships will be gathered from all these types; but if they do not agree with each other, enmities will be collected from them. But if the agreement of their affection, or the opposite of agreement, is only between the two places of the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]], a "necessary" affection will be produced from it, which is called true and supreme friendship, in which one must trust most. Conversely, a "necessary" enmity—as bad as can be—which will never cease, will be born from it. Likewise, when their agreement or its opposite is between the two places of the Part of Fortune of each, what results will come from the cause of profit or loss. If it is between the two Ascendants, we shall say that which is produced happens because of anger and joy. We should also observe the modes of the places in which this association of the chart exists, and also that which is elevated above them, as well as the planets that regard them. For in births where the planets elevated above the places of the common figure are in nearly the same sign, or in that which is elevated above it, we should assign the strength, durability, and sincerity of the friendship or enmity to those elevated planets. In births where the aspect of the planets appears fruitful and suitable, it is not unfitting to attribute the occasion of the fruit of friendship, or the improvement of enmity, to the planets regarding them. In the qualities of common friendship and enmity, which become contemporaneous...

...whether it be temporal, and in some cases hourly, or even momentary, found in each of these two nativities, it is not useless to observe the planetary modes—that is, the times in which the *alhileg* [[notes: *Alhileg* (Hyleg) is the planet or point in a chart that acts as the "giver of life" and signifies the person's physical existence]], moving away from the stellar positions of one nativity, passes through to the stellar positions of the other nativity; for according to this, there will be particular friendships and enmities. Those friendships which have not known a shorter limit of their permanence before that separation will not find an end to the duration of their time until the planet joins another star.

Therefore, **Saturn** and **Jupiter**, when one of them reaches the place of the other, will judge friendship between them arising from agriculture and inheritances.

**Saturn** and **Mars**, when one occupies the place of the other, will generate spontaneous brawls and discords between them.

But from **Saturn** and **Venus**, an alliance and affection on account of relatives will be produced, though it will be terminated very quickly.

**Saturn** and **Mercury** will signify their alliance and mixing in the affairs of life, as well as in giving and receiving, and trading, and things similar to these.

Through **Jupiter** and **Mars**, by the occasion of wealth, or by any dominion or arrangement, alliance and love will be produced between them.

Through **Jupiter** and **Venus**, they will love one another on account of women, or for the sake of divine service, or through houses of prayer, or from prophets, or from things similar to these.

**Jupiter** and **Mercury** will indicate a spontaneous alliance by the occasion of the dialectic sciences [[notes: Logic and philosophy]] and prophecy.

**Mars** and **Venus**, so to speak, will associate them together through *drueria* [[notes: From the Old French *druerie*, meaning gallantry, courtship, or an illicit love affair]] or adultery, or fornication, or "Sodomitic crime" [[notes: A standard legal/moral term in the 16th century for non-procreative or "unnatural" sexual acts]], except that this will have a brief durability, because one of them is a fortune and the other is a fortune [[notes: This likely refers to the "fortuitous" or "benefic" nature of the planets involved, or a specific condition of their strength]].

**Mars** and **Mercury** will signify enmities and deceptions and brawls between them, by the occasion of incantations and necromancy.

**Venus** and **Mercury** will bring about an alliance between them in the affairs of life for the sake of mastery, or music, or books, or women.

Furthermore, it is fitting for us to know the increase and decrease in the vigor of common friendship and enmity from the qualities of the places in which they exist with respect to the four primary places [[notes: The four "angles" or cardinal points of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]] which hold dominion and power. For if they are in the angles, or with the *Part of Fortune* [[notes: An Arabic part or calculated mathematical point signifying prosperity and well-being]], or with the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]], that which they signify will be clearer and more evident. But if they remain far removed from these, it will by no means appear; however, its health and injuries are perceived according to the property of the favorable or unfavorable quality of the stars looking upon the aforementioned places.

Indeed, the matter of servants regarding the love or hatred of their masters toward them is indicated from the sign specifically which is in the place of misfortune [[notes: Often referring to the 6th House of the zodiac, which governed servants and illness]], by the natural likeness which the planets have to one another—those which look upon that place in the very hour of birth, or those which are in that same place or in its opposite—but especially if the planets which dominate that sign agree in the fellowship of the figures with the places of their dominion and power, or if they are of the same kind as them.

->### On Foreign Travel. Chapter VII.<-

[[meta: Large decorative initial 'R' depicting a figure or landscape within the letterform.]]

**R**eally, the matter of foreign travel is perceived from the qualities of the luminaries with respect to the angles, but especially from the qualities of the **Moon**. For when the Moon is occidental [[notes: Setting in the west]] and remote from the angles, she will judge foreign travels and changes from place to place. Similarly, **Mars** also will sometimes work this effect when he is occidental, or when he declines from the zenith of the heads [[notes: The Midheaven or highest point of the sky]], and when his distance from the luminaries is the distance of opposition or the "aspect of the fourth" [[notes: A "quartile" or 90-degree square aspect]].

But if the *Part of Fortune* should again fall in signs that signify travel, his whole life, and his works and acts themselves, will be in foreign places. And if the "fortune-bearing" locations [[notes: The benefic planets Jupiter and Venus]] look upon the predicted places, or reach them, or follow them, those things which he performs in his travels will be suitable, as well as few and profitable; his return from foreign travel will also be hurried and easy, nor will he ever be contradicted by anything. But if the "unfortunate" locations [[notes: The malefic planets Saturn and Mars]] look upon them, those works of his will be laborious and harmful, full of fear, and the return from foreign travel will be slow...

...he will return from his travels. The combination of this matter according to the planets that are associated with these places in the figure [[notes: The "figure" refers to the astrological birth chart]], as we have shown in the preceding sections, will always be apparent. And when the luminaries [[notes: In astrology, the "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon]] are in either of the two eastern quarters, he will more frequently undertake journeys toward the regions of the east and south. But if they are positioned in either of the two western quarters, or in the west itself, his travel will appear to be toward the north and the west. Furthermore, if the signs that signify travel, or their lords [[notes: The "lord" or "ruler" is the planet associated with a specific zodiac sign]], are of a single form, the journey will happen only occasionally. But if they are of two bodies or two figures [[notes: These are "bicorporeal" or double-bodied signs, such as Gemini, Sagittarius, and Pisces]], the travel will be continuous and endure for a long time. 

Now, if Jupiter and Venus are the rulers of the places signifying travel and the places of the luminaries, there will be no fear in the journey; instead, it will be desirable, because he will carry out embassies [[notes: Diplomatic or official missions]] for the rulers of lands for the sake of his friends. This will be aided by a favorable temperament of the air and an abundance of things beneficial to him. If Mercury is present with them on this aforementioned occasion, he will achieve great profit and bring his embassy to its conclusion; gifts will also be given to him, and he will be honored. 

If Saturn and Mars should rule the places of the luminaries, and especially when they are in opposition by longitude, that which happens to him will be called ill health, and he himself will be greatly hindered. If both should dwell in humid signs [[notes: The "water signs": Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces]], this hindrance will come to him from the dangers of a sea voyage, such as shipwreck; or, because of misfortune, the journey on dry land will occur through passages in desert places. But if they are in fixed signs [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius]], this will happen from falls or from powerful blasts of wind. If they are in the solstitial or equinoctial signs [[notes: Also known as "cardinal signs": Aries, Libra, Cancer, and Capricorn]], we do not doubt that this happens to him through a lack and deprivation of necessary things, or through the qualities of corrupted air that brings on sickness. 

If, however, they are in signs of human form [[notes: Signs depicted as humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius]], we say it will happen from highway robberies, or betrayals, or plundering. But if they are in signs whose forms resemble those of wild animals, it will happen from the ferocity of wolves or from an earthquake. If Mercury is among them, it will proceed from attacks that cause fear, or from the bites of beasts, or the occasion of poisonous animals. In the properties of these occurring events—that is, in the differences of future circumstances, whether they help or harm—it is appropriate for us to observe the locations of dominion, which are the circumstances of works, substance, and the matters of the body and health according to the aforementioned occasions. Truly, the knowledge of the times in which these future things will happen will be gathered from the qualities appearing at the beginnings of subsequent years. Let it suffice, then, that we have treated these matters in this chapter.
