->## On the Quality of the Native’s Death. Chapter VIII.<-

[[meta: A large decorative initial Q containing a figure (possibly a scholar or deity) begins the text.]]

**S**ince [[notes: The original Latin begins with a large decorative **Q** for *Quia* (Since/Because)]], after this brief explanation of the things mentioned above, we must observe the qualities of death for those whose lives we have predicted. It is appropriate for us to know whether death will come from the projections of rays [[notes: "Ray projections" refer to astrological aspects or the influence of one planet's light upon another]] or from the arrival of the significator at the western angle [[notes: The "western angle" is the Descendant, where the sun sets, traditionally associated with the end of life]]. For if death occurs through the projection of rays, or because of any conjunction with that planet to which it is joined, it is not unfitting to consider the places of those planets to which it is joined when we wish to know the qualities of death. 

But if death is present because of the movement of the significator toward the western angle, that western angle itself must be observed. This is because the quality of death will be determined according to the planets that follow those aforementioned places (if any follow), or according to the planets that reached them first (if no following planets are found), provided we have accepted the properties of the stars in the chart according to their natures in the science of occurring differences. We shall also consider the specific qualities of the aforementioned place of the west, which they take from the signs and the natures of the terms [[notes: "Terms" or *termini* are specific sub-divisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets]]. 

Therefore, when Saturn is the lord of death [[margin: *Saturn as lord of death*]], it will occur by occasion of a long infirmity, or consumption [[notes: *Phthisis*, often referring to tuberculosis]], or catarrh [[notes: Excessive buildup of mucus or inflammation]], or through the dissolution of the body, or a hectic fever [[notes: A wasting fever]], as well as from bowel obstructions, or dropsy [[notes: *Hydropisi*, or edema/fluid retention]], or a loosening of the belly [[notes: Diarrhea or dysentery]], or disease of the womb, and other infirmities which arise more from the occasion of cold...

**♃** [[notes: The symbol for Jupiter.]] If death proceeds from Jupiter, it will be said to come from quinsy [[notes: *synancia*, a severe inflammation of the throat or "suffocation of the neck"]], or from pneumonia, or stroke, or spasms, or from intense headaches, or heart ailments, and all those chills which arise by occasion of great windiness [[notes: "Windiness" or "flatulence" in Renaissance medicine referred to "pneuma" or gases moving through the body’s cavities]], or through foul odors; we do not doubt that death comes to him by these means. But if Mars be the lord of death,
**♂** [[notes: The symbol for Mars.]] it will be imposed at the end of life by the occasion of persistent fever, or continual tertian fever [[notes: A fever that recurs every three days, often associated with malaria]], or by a sudden stroke, or kidney disease [[notes: *nefresis*]], or "empyic" disease [[notes: *empici morbi*, likely empyema or internal abscesses producing pus]], or any flow of blood, or miscarriage, or childbirth, or erysipelas [[notes: *herisipile*, a bacterial skin infection]], or any deadly sickness coming from a febrile heat or excessive warmth.
**♀** [[notes: The symbol for Venus.]] But if Venus should be the lady of death, we pronounce that life is ended by a defect of the stomach, the liver, or the heart, or by the passing of blood [[notes: *sanguinis egestione*, possibly dysentery or hemorrhaging]], or by shifting abscesses or fistulas, or by poisonous drinks, and all diseases occurring from a superfluity or corruption of the humors. But if Mercury should be the lord of death, it will occur
**☿** [[notes: The symbol for Mercury.]] by disturbance of the mind, or mania, or melancholy, or by a fall, or epilepsy, or cough, or an overabundance of spitting, and all diseases proceeding from excessive or unsuitable dryness. Now, those upon whom nature has enjoined death in the manner aforesaid shall depart life when the planets who have the disposal of death are in accordance with their own proper and natural qualities, or similar to them,
[[margin: Death against the law of nature.]] and no planet whose influence causes an evil or sudden death is elevated above them. However, death that is brought about by force, and not by the law of nature, happens when both "Infortunes" [[notes: The "Infortunes" are Saturn and Mars, planets traditionally viewed as having a malefic or challenging influence]] fall into the place of death, so that they remain in that same place, or in a square [[notes: *aspectu quarto*, an aspect of 90 degrees]] or opposite aspect to it, or if either of them has lordship and power over the Sun or the Moon, or over the place of both. For an evil and unjust death happens because of the conjunction of the two Infortunes, and its magnitude will proceed from the testimony of the Luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]]. But the quality of the death itself will arrive according to the aspects of the other planets and the signs in which the Infortunes are found. For when Saturn is in square aspect to the Sun, or in its opposite, and is in a state contrary to his own *alaiz* [[notes: *Alaiz* refers to "Hayz," an Arabic astrological term for a planet being in a favorable position relative to its gender and the time of day]], if he remains in fixed signs, the person will be crushed by the bonds of death by the stoning of a crowd, or will be afflicted by strangulation or deadly punishments. And when he is occidental [[notes: Setting in the west after the sun]], and the Moon follows him, let us not be unaware that the same thing happens. But when he is in signs whose figures are likened to the shapes of wild beasts, he will be covered with the diseases [[notes: Or perhaps "injuries"]] of wild beasts. But if Jupiter testifies to him and is unfortunate, he will be condemned to be devoured by wild beasts in a gathering of men on a well-known and solemn day. But if he remains in opposition to the place of the other Luminary holding the Ascendant, he will be endangered by death in prison. But if Mercury is joined to him in the figure, especially in the figures of the serpents of the celestial sphere, or in signs whose figures are of rapacious wild beasts, he will be torn by the bites of venomous animals. If Venus, however, is with them, he will die by a deadly drink given through the fraud of women. But if he claims a place for himself in Virgo or in Pisces, or in the humid signs, and is associated with the Moon in the figure, he will end his life by drowning. But if he is in the "Ship" [[notes: The constellation Argo Navis]], he will be deprived of life by the tempestuous tossing of the sea. And if he is in any of the solstitial signs, or in quadrupedal signs with the Sun, or remains in opposition to Mars in place of the Sun, he will be killed by a falling ruin. If, however, he is in the Midheaven [[notes: *coeli medio*, the highest point of the sky]], or its opposite, he will be hurled from a height and die. Mars, however, when he is in square or opposite aspect to the Sun or Moon, and in a state contrary to his *alaiz*: if he revolves in signs of human form [[notes: Such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius]], he will perish by the cutting off of his head because of wars and disturbances occurring among his kinsmen, or by fighting, or he might lay his own hand upon himself because of women, or be killed by the hands of women. That, however, will happen when Venus again testifies to him. But if Mercury is associated with him in the figure, he will be torn apart by the hands of robbers, pirates, or ambushers. But if he is in signs of "mutilated limbs" or "imperfect fortune," or in the "Head of the Chain" [[notes: *cathenae capite*, likely referring to a specific star or point in a constellation like Andromeda]] with its lord, he will depart by the cutting off of his head or limbs. And if he is in Scorpio or Taurus, he will pass the boundaries of life by burning, or by the piercing of limbs, or by incision, or by spasm. But if he remains in the Midheaven or its opposite, he will hang upon a cross [[notes: *in cruce suspendet*, which could mean crucifixion or hanging]], especially if he is with *Ficare* [[notes: Likely a corruption of "Phicares" or "Phikros," stars in the region of Andromeda/Perseus]] and Andromeda.

[[summary: This page details how the different planets govern the "quality" of a person's death, distinguishing between natural deaths caused by illness and violent or "unnatural" deaths caused by the malefic influence of Saturn and Mars in specific zodiacal signs.]]

[[meta: This page concludes the discussion on the quality and circumstances of death from the previous chapter and begins Chapter 9, which deals with the "Ages of Man"—the division of a person's life into periods ruled by different planets.]]

[[page number: 71]]

-># BOOK IV.<-

...should be. But if it should take place in a western sign, or in the Ascendant [[notes: The 'Ascendant' is the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]], he will be burned alive by fire. And if it should occur in the four-footed signs [[notes: Constellations depicted as animals with four legs, such as Aries (the Ram), Taurus (the Bull), or Leo (the Lion)]], he will be crushed by a fall. If, however, Jupiter gives witness [[notes: In astrology, a planet 'gives witness' when it is in a specific geometric relationship, or aspect, to another point]] to him, and he remains ill-fortuned, he will undergo a manifest judgment of death at the hands of the authorities or a king. But if both the malefics [[notes: Mars and Saturn, traditionally the planets associated with misfortune]] are joined, or one is opposed to the other, as we have said before, so that it becomes the occasion of death, it will worsen the evil deprivation of the vital spirit.

The lord of the quality of death is the lord of the "killing place." [[notes: The *anaretic* point or killing place is the specific degree in a birth chart calculated to determine the end of life.]] Indeed, the accidents leading to death will be multiplied in quantity or quality when both malefics have authority in the killing places. And when the qualities of the stars are of this kind, the body will lack burial and ceremony: it will be consumed by walking, ravenous, winged, and predatory creatures when these occur in the forms of such animals and no benefic planet [[notes: Venus or Jupiter]] gives witness to the killing places; and with these planets staying in the lower hemisphere, they shall feed upon the corpse itself. When the planets that are lords of the killing places are in declining houses [[notes: Houses that 'fall away' from the main angles of the chart, considered weaker]], and especially when the Moon is in the aforementioned places, and in the fourth house, or remains in opposition to these places, the native will succumb to the law of death among foreigners.

->## On the division of times in the life of the native. Chapter IX.<-

### [[insert: A]]fter we have generally explained the method of predicting each of these species [[notes: This 'P' in the OCR likely refers to the start of the word 'Postquam', but the drop-cap is often treated as an insert]] up to the perfection of the knowledge of those universal matters, as has been shown, it naturally follows that we should add, along that same path, those things which must be observed in the partition of births through the times of life, and which must be attended to in the particular matters by the aforementioned methods. Therefore, just as the judgments and estimations of particular things—which are taken from the aforementioned places in the narration of births—are set forth, so too are the judgments and estimations taken from those same regions. That is to say, those taken from the regions are the very judgments in which the particulars observed in births are generally contained, such as the forms and figures of bodies and their qualities, the properties of souls, and the differences in customs and laws.

It also behooves those who observe this naturally to always adhere to the primary occasion (which is more suitable than the rest) so that they are never deceived by similarities in births. For example, if they should say that one born in Ethiopia is adorned with whiteness and straightness of hair, or that the qualities of their souls are more domestic, or inclined toward reason, or that they are investigators of things. Or if they should affirm that the inhabitants of Germany [[notes: The text uses 'Aliemā', likely a shorthand or misprint for *Alemanniam*]] have wild souls, or are borrowers, and dissent from reason; or if they are again deceived regarding the customs and laws proper to each nation. For example, if regarding marriages they should decree that Italians marry their own sisters [[notes: Ptolemy is illustrating that an astrologer must know local laws; an Italian chart might 'suggest' an incestuous marriage, but the astrologer must know this is legally impossible in Italy]]; for it would be necessary for them to add to the judgment if they were born in Egypt (where they might marry sisters), or if they were born in Persia, they might marry their mothers.

It is proper first to observe universal qualities generally in one's judgments and estimations, and then to add to these the particular quantities by which they will judge, so that they may perceive the increases and decreases happening in these matters. Similarly, in the division of the times and hours of the native, let the temporal differences of the years and their similarities with each of the subsequent future events be set forth. They should inspect their qualities so that they are in no way deceived in the general accidents they have observed for the birth. It is necessary that they do not judge a boy to be working, or taking a wife, or doing that which can be done by no one unless he is of greater age; nor that they judge a man of decrepit age to be begetting offspring or performing acts possible only for youth. Rather, it generally behooves them to add those things which they have grasped through the observation of times, from the years themselves that are suitable to them, and which can happen in them. For the same way, the same method, and the same single order is held for all temporal differences, embracing the universal nature that contains all men, and maintaining a similarity with the order of the seven planets.

This path or order takes its beginning from the first years and from the sphere most akin to us, namely the lunar sphere, and in the final years is explained by the last sphere of the planets, which is called that of Saturn.

[[meta: This page continues the discussion of how celestial bodies influence human life, specifically detailing the "Seven Ages of Man." This is a famous passage from Book IV, Chapter 10 of the *Tetrabiblos* (here called the *Quadripartitum*). The translation maintains continuity with the astrological theory that planets govern specific periods of time based on their perceived "nature" and orbital cycles.]]

->[[page number: 72]] **CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM**<-

...is explained. It should also be understood that in individual years, events occur that take on a likeness to the nature of whichever planet happens to be in direct governance of that year. The observation of this matter is necessary for understanding the general quality of each of these time periods.

[[margin: *Infancy is ruled by the Moon.*]]
The particular differences of these ages are recognized from their inherent properties. Because the **Moon** [[notes: In ancient astrology, the Moon was associated with moisture and rapid growth, mirroring the "wetness" of an infant.]] governs the first 4 years, which correspond to the number of the moon's primary cycle, the infant takes on a tenderness and weakness of body, as well as rapid growth. The infant’s nourishment is primarily fluid and frequent, and their physical form changes easily. Furthermore, the soul itself is held to be weak and imperfect, which is appropriate for those who receive their soul-part from the "maker of infants" [[notes: A poetic reference to the Moon as the celestial body governing the formation of the physical body and early life]].

[[margin: *Mercury rules Childhood.*]]
And since the second planet, which is called **Mercury**, is the master of the disposition of the following ten years—which are the years of childhood and are called the "second" period—I say that he is the master because he rules the number ten (the midpoint of twenty years). Within this span of years, the child enters into the manifest effect of the intellect and the reasoning of the soul, just as if the plants of erudition and the roots of the soul's qualities were being planted within him. In these years, through those things that are adapted to his properties, discipline and learning begin to shine, and he rises up, awakened to the modes of his first exercises.

[[margin: *Venus rules Adolescence.*]]
But because **Venus** presides as the ruler over the disposition of the subsequent eight years—which are the years of adolescence and are called the "third" period—and because this matches the number of years in her own proper cycle [[notes: Venus has an 8-year cycle where it returns to the same position in the sky relative to the Sun and Earth]], the movement of the flow of the seed begins, and a gathering of its abundance takes place. The adolescent himself is moved toward the acts of Venus [[notes: A euphemism for sexual activity]]. We say this is a time in which the soul takes on a likeness to a sort of frenzy; barely touching a tiny portion of restraint, they reach the greatest impulse of desire in all things, falling into the possibilities provided by the affairs of Venus. They encounter tempestuous luxury, deception, and a blindness of the mind in all their wishes.

[[margin: *The Sun rules Youth.*]]
And because the **Sun**, the ruler of the middle sphere, is said to preside over the disposition of the next nineteen years [[notes: The 19-year Metonic cycle of the Sun and Moon]], which are noted in the fourth place and are the middle of the order, being assigned to youth, we decree that the soul in this time possesses a youthful concern for the works of power and the fruitful arrangement of life, as well as its direction. We say that the soul turns away from playful and deceptive diversions toward its own health, the preservation of modesty, and a desire for honor.

[[margin: *Mars rules Mature Age.*]]
After the Sun, because **Mars** rules for fifteen years, situated in the fifth place—which are the years of strength and vigor and equal the number of his own rotation cycle [[notes: 15 years is the "minor year" period of Mars in Hellenistic astrology]]—the gravity of life, as well as its obstacles and adversity, weigh upon the person. In truth, the soul and the body endure anxieties and impediments, and the decline of the body is almost felt and understood. Man will also perform great works from which great labor will come to him, seeking the completion of these things before the approach of his death.

[[margin: *Jupiter rules Old Age.*]]
Next, we assign to **Jupiter**, who claims the sixth place of the old man, the twelve years of old age—equal to his own proper rotation [[notes: Jupiter takes approximately 12 years to orbit the Sun]]. In these years, man withdraws from the works of the body and laborious tasks, and also from the anxiety of manual labor. He no longer commits his soul to danger, in exchange for which he puts on a healthy state of mind and strives for good preservation. Neglecting shameful things due to his magnanimity, he is providential and full of desire in all things, and he is held to be a speaker and a consoler. In this time, he will be especially concerned with freedom, honor, and a good reputation, along with modesty and reverence.

[[margin: *Saturn rules Extreme Age.*]]
After these, the years of **Saturn** follow in order, placed as if at the extreme. These are the years of "senium" [[notes: *Senium* refers to the final stage of life, characterized by decline or decrepitude]], and they are not terminated until the departure from the vital places. In these years, the movements of the body grow colder and heavier; there is a loss of pleasure and a diminishing of appetite, and the nature changes toward a swift decline. This quality strips the man of his life, imprinting impediment and sadness and a meager sustenance of things due to the weakness of his movements.

These, therefore, are the properties of the qualities of the times which appear according to the general things of nature. As for the particular properties of the times, since we ought not observe them except from the properties of the birth-chart (*nativitas*), we have considered that which appeared universal to us from the *alhileg* [[notes: Also spelled *Hyleg*, this is the "giver of life," a specific point or planet in a birth chart used to determine the length of life and its vital force]] the ruler. However, our observation in these matters brought us knowledge not from any one of them individually, but from all of them, just as in the span of life...

The text employs the "Profection" method—a system where one sign of the zodiac is assigned to a specific period of time (years, months, or days).]]

...is completed. For that **Hyleg**, which is taken from the **ascendant** [[notes: The 'Hyleg' or 'Alhyleg' is the 'Giver of Life,' a specific point in a birth chart used to determine vitality and longevity. The ascendant is the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.]], we use for events affecting the body and for travels. However, that which is considered from the **Part of Fortune** [[notes: An 'Arabic Part' or mathematical point in a chart representing material prosperity and well-being.]], we employ in matters of substance [wealth]. That taken from the **Moon** we observe for the qualities of the soul and for marriages. That which is found from the **Sun**, we take for matters of authority and high status; but that found from the **Midheaven** [the highest point of the sky] we follow for all other particular qualities, such as in one's work, friends, and children. For by doing this, we understand that there is only one single planet—whether it be a fortune or an infortune—ruling the matter, which we do not doubt to be both a just and suitable method. For often, contrary events [[margin: Contrary / events.]] happen at the same hour; for instance, when someone loses a relative but becomes their heir, or when a sickness settles in but one also becomes wealthy, or if one fathers a child while living a life of leisure. Similar things frequently happen to the body and the soul, in riches and in power, as well as in other good or bad accidents. One and the same quality necessarily arises so that a man may incur good or evil in all these things. Yet, in times of intense good or bad fortune, it is perhaps possible for something similar to happen when all the 'fortunes' or 'infortunes' [[notes: The 'fortunes' are the beneficial planets (Jupiter, Venus) and 'infortunes' are the malefic planets (Saturn, Mars).]] equally encounter all the Hylegs, or many of them. This clearly happens successively, because human nature, due to a sudden decline and an alteration from a balanced state of good and evil, can hardly reach the full intensity of both at once. In this aforementioned way, therefore, they determine the matters of all the Hyleg places. From the encountering Hyleg places, we judge that not only the end of life must be considered (as in the space of life), but indeed everything must be examined. Likewise, we should observe not only their bodily, opposite, or square encounters [[notes: Referring to the 'aspects' or angles between planets: Conjunction, Opposition, and Square (90 degrees).]], but also those joined to them by trine and sextile [[notes: The Trine (120 degrees) and Sextile (60 degrees) are considered harmonious or 'good' angles in traditional astrology.]].

We shall also first attribute the "times" in each Hyleg to the planet existing in that same degree as the Hyleg, or to the planet associated with it in the figure. But if no planet remains in that degree, and none is associated with it in the figure, it is appropriate to assign that degree to the closer preceding planet, until we reach the one who looks toward the aforementioned degree or the following degree. The aspect of this planet toward the other should be according to the succession of the signs, and thereafter the subsequent times are given to the one mentioned before, until it is applied to the one that follows it. And we decree that the same should be done in all cases. We shall also establish the planets existing in their own terms [[notes: 'Terms' (or *termini*) are subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by specific planets.]], some of which we have observed and some of which we have placed as "dispositors."

Furthermore, it is proper for the number of years to be given by the number of degrees of longitude. Therefore, for the Hyleg taken from the **ascendant**, a number of years equal to the number of the times of the **ascensions of the climate** [[notes: A complex calculation where the time it takes for a zodiac sign to rise depends on the 'climate' or latitude of the birthplace.]] in which the birth occurred will be assigned. For the Hyleg found from the **Midheaven**, years shall be provided whose number equals the number of the times of transit through the Midheaven. In other Hylegs taken from elsewhere, we proceed in this order, and according to their approach to the angles, we shall take the number of ascensions, or settings, or transits through the Midheaven, just as we explained in the narration of the span of life.

In this aforementioned manner, the "mistresses" of universal times shall be discovered. [[margin: Rulers / of the years.]] The mistresses [rulers] of the matters of the years will be known when we take the number of years from the birth and, starting from each of the Hyleg places, we project one year for each of the signs according to their succession; the lord of that sign in which the number ends shall be reserved. We shall do this same thing for the months; for by taking the number of months that have passed since birth, starting from the places which have the year's disposition (28 days), we shall project them to each of the signs. And we shall do similarly for the days. For taking the number of days from the day of birth, we shall project two and a third days to each sign from the places of the months.

Again, it is proper for us to observe the existence of the planets in the "places of the times." This helps not a little in the knowledge of future contingencies in those times. Thus, we shall observe the existence of **Saturn** in the places of universal times, **Jupiter** in the places of years, the **Sun** or **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** in the places of months, and the **Moon** in the places of days. Regarding the planets that are the lords of universal times...

-> ### CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM <-

[[notes: The *Quadripartitum* (Four Books) is the Latin title for the *Tetrabiblos*. This section concludes the final book, which deals with the timing of events and the quality of life.]]

...of things to come, and we shall consider the perfection of the same. We shall look upon the lords of the particular times in the increase or decrease of this [life], according to the likeness of things existing in their places, for this shall be the cause of the strength and weakness of accidents [[notes: In this context, "accidents" refers to events or external occurrences in a person's life, rather than mistakes]]. For the place of the *alhyleg* [[notes: A Latinized Arabic term, *hyleg*, referring to the "Giver of Life"—the specific point or planet in a birth chart that determines the duration of life]] is the significator of the properties of universal quality and the space of time; and the lord of universal times, who is the lord of the *terms* [[notes: "Terms" (or *fines*) are specific degrees of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet]], is so called because each of these stars, in the same nativity, had a likeness to the places of the stars that previously held the disposition. 

But whether an event is good or bad will be discovered from the properties of the qualities of the nature of the lords of the times, and their combination in doing good or evil, as well as from their likeness or contrariety in the beginning to the ruling matter. Furthermore, it will judge in which of the times the future event properly happens, based on the qualities of the signs ruling the year and the month (which have their causes according to the places where the future events are to be), and also from the qualities happening when the planets, the Sun, and the Moon appear in the signs ruling the years and months. For the planets which agreed with the aforementioned places from the hour of the beginning—which is called the nativity—and were suitably associated with them in the figure of the existing hour, will signify good in the future matter. But when they are in the contrary *alaiz* [[notes: This term likely refers to a specific "encounter" or planetary configuration, derived from the Arabic *al-ays*, meaning "existence" or a specific state]], they will announce evil to it. Those, however, who are unsuitably associated with them—as occurs, for instance, in their opposition across the diameter, or in a quartile aspect [[notes: A "square" or 90-degree angle, considered a stressful or challenging relationship between planets]], and in the contrary *alaiz*—will be the cause of adversity. In other qualities, they shall effect nothing. 

But if the same planets have power both in the times and in their essential state, they will experience an abundance and increase of future good or evil; this will necessarily happen more with power over the cause, so that they might rule the times alone. Rather, it is because they themselves were again the dispositors at the beginning of the nativity. And that good or evil should happen equally to the native [[notes: The "native" is the person for whom the horoscope is cast]] in all their affairs sometimes happens either because all species of the *alhyleg*, or many of them, have met in one and the same place, or because they were separated from one another, and at the same time things meeting them—all of which, or many of which, were fortunes or misfortunes—joined together in turn. In this way, therefore, according to the natural mode suitable to the matter, we prognosticate by the matters of the times. Of the particular ways by which the qualities of the temporal future are predicted, because the collection of things proceeding from them is multiform and the narration is difficult, we have judged it most suitable to propose the narration in this place; for from the start of this book, we proposed to explain the work of the general nature of the stars and its likeness, as is fitting, with particular things according to the estimation of a rational species in their mixing. Therefore, having explained the general matters of nativities, we think it not inappropriate to end this book in this place.

# -> CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S CENTILOQUIUM <-
## -> OR THE HUNDRED SAYINGS, <-
### -> Giovanni Gioviano Pontano, interpreter. <-

[[notes: The *Centiloquium* is a famous set of 100 aphorisms once attributed to Ptolemy, though modern scholars believe it was written later. Giovanni Gioviano Pontano (1426–1503) was a major Italian humanist who translated and commented on these works.]]

[[meta: The text below begins with a large woodcut decorative initial 'T' containing a figure in a landscape.]]

**T**o you and from knowledge. [[notes: This first aphorism usually reads "A te et a scientia," meaning "From you and from knowledge," suggesting that the astrologer's own judgment is as important as the science itself.]] For it cannot be that he who is knowledgeable should pronounce the particular forms of things, just as the senses do not perceive the particular, but rather some general form of a sensible thing; and it behooves the one treating these matters to use conjecture. Only those inspired by the divine predict particulars.
**2** When he who consults shall better examine himself, there will be no difference of things between that and his form.
**3** He who is fit for any particular task will surely have a star of this kind of significance quite powerful in his nativity.
**4** A soul fit for knowledge attains more of the truth than one who has exercised himself in the science in the highest degree.
**5** He who is knowledgeable can avert many effects of the stars when he knows their nature and prepares himself before their arrival.

--- Page 338 ---
[[meta: This page continues the *Centiloquium* (The One Hundred Sayings), a famous collection of astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy. This text was a cornerstone of medieval and Renaissance astrology, used as a handbook for practitioners to refine their judgments. Page 75 contains aphorisms 6 through 31, focusing on electional astrology (choosing the right time for an action), medical astrology, and mundane (political) astrology.]]

[[page number: 75]]

# ->THE CENTILOQUIUM<-
[[notes: The *Centiloquium* is a collection of 100 astrological rules. Although attributed to the 2nd-century astronomer Claudius Ptolemy, modern scholars believe it was likely written in the 10th century, possibly by an Arabic author, before being translated into Latin and becoming a standard textbook for centuries.]]

**6** The choice of days and hours is only useful when the time of birth [[notes: *Genitura* refers to the natal chart or the moment of birth]] is well-established. For if the natal chart is unfavorable, the chosen time will be of no benefit, even if it seems to look toward a good outcome.

**7** No one can truly perceive the mixtures of the stars unless he has first learned their natural differences and how they blend together.

**8** A wise soul assists the work of the heavens, just as the best farmer assists nature by plowing and weeding.

**9** In the cycle of birth and decay, forms are influenced by celestial forms. Therefore, those who create "images" [[notes: *Imagines* refers to astrological talismans or amulets engraved at specific times to capture planetary power]] use them by observing when the stars have entered into them.

**10** In choosing days and hours, make use of the "malefics" [[notes: The malefic planets are Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship]] just as a skilled physician uses poisons in moderation for a cure.

**11** Do not choose a day or an hour before you understand the true nature of the matter you are proposing.

**12** Love and hatred prevent true judgments, for they make great things seem small and small things seem great.

**13** When the celestial configuration signifies something, use the "assisting" and even the "corrupting" stars—that is, the secondary influences.

**14** To what great errors is the astrologer subject when the Seventh House and its Lord are afflicted. [[notes: In a consultation, the 7th house represents the relationship between the astrologer and the client; if this part of the chart is "afflicted" or poorly positioned, the reading is likely to be wrong.]]

**15** The "Ascendants" of enemy kingdoms are those signs that fall away from the Ascendant of your own kingdom. But the Ascendants of friends are the "angles" and the houses that follow them. The same applies to schools of thought. [[notes: The Ascendant is the sign rising on the eastern horizon. Astrologers mapped countries to specific signs to predict international relations.]]

**16** When "benefic" planets [[notes: The benefics are Jupiter and Venus, associated with good fortune]] rule in the Eighth House [[notes: The house associated with death and inheritance]], they bring loss through good men; but if they are well-placed, they will avert that loss.

**17** When you judge the life of an old man, do not give your verdict until you have measured how many years he is naturally capable of living.

**18** When both "luminaries" [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]] are at the same minute of the degree, if a benefic planet is rising, the child born will be fortunate in all things that happen to him. The same is true if they are opposite each other at sunrise and sunset. But if a malefic is rising, expect the opposite.

**19** The power of a "purgation" [[notes: A medical treatment intended to cleanse the body, often through laxatives or bloodletting]] is weakened when the Moon is joined with Jupiter.

**20** Do not pierce a limb with iron when the Moon is in the zodiac sign that rules that specific limb. [[notes: A fundamental rule of "Zodiac Man" medicine: for example, never perform surgery on the feet when the Moon is in Pisces.]]

**21** When the Moon is in Scorpio or Pisces, and the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a planet positioned below the earth, it is good to use purgations. But if it is joined to a planet positioned above the earth, the person who takes the potion will vomit it up.

**22** Do not put on a new garment for the first time, nor cut the cloth, when the Moon is located in Leo. It is even worse if the Moon is in a bad condition there.

**23** The Moon’s relationship to the stars makes the person born quite active; if the stars are powerful, it makes them an achiever; if they are weak, they indicate a lazy impulse toward action.

**24** An eclipse of the luminaries occurring in the "angles" [[notes: The four most powerful points of a chart: the East, West, Zenith, and Nadir]] of a birth chart or an annual revolution is harmful. The timing of the effect is taken from the distance between the Ascendant and the place of the eclipse. Just as you take years from the hour of a Solar eclipse, you take months from the hours of a Lunar eclipse.

**25** Calculate the "progression" of the ruler by the ascensions of the sphere when it is in the Midheaven, but by the ascensions of the "clime" [[notes: Geographic latitude]] when it is in the Ascendant.

**26** A matter is clearly hidden when the star signifying it is either below the earth or joined to the Sun in a foreign sign. On the other hand, it is out in the open when the star is raised from its "depression" [[notes: The "fall" or weakest point of a planet's influence]] into its height and placed in its own sign.

**27** Venus brings pleasure to a person in the limb ruled by the sign she is currently in. The same applies to the other stars.

**28** When you cannot manage to join the Moon to two planets, manage at least to join her to a fixed star that possesses a mixture of their natures.

**29** The fixed stars [[notes: Stars that do not move like planets, such as Sirius or Regulus]] bring irrational and wonderful strokes of luck, which nevertheless usually end in calamity unless the planets also agree to that good fortune.

**30** Look at the "creations" [[notes: This refers to the coronation or the start of a reign]] of the first kings of a dynasty. If the Ascendant of that creation matches the Ascendant of the King’s son at birth, he will be the successor to the kingdom.

**31** When the Ruler of a kingdom enters a "climacteric" place [[notes: A critical or dangerous degree in the zodiac, often occurring in cycles of seven or nine]], then either the King or someone great among the princes of the realm will die.

[[meta: This page continues the *Centiloquium*, a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy, though likely of medieval Arabic origin. These rules provide concise guidance for interpreting birth charts and predicting world events. This page covers aphorisms 32 through 55.]]

[[page number: 78]]

->**THE CENTILOQUIUM**<-
[[notes: Literally "The Hundred Sayings."]]

**32** Harmony between two people is created by a compatible arrangement of the stars that represent the nature of the matter, from which goodwill is established in the birth charts [[notes: Latin *genitura*; the map of the heavens at the moment of birth]] of both.

**33** Love and hatred are discerned both from the harmony or discord of the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]], and from the Ascendants of both birth charts. Moreover, "obedient" signs [[notes: Signs that share the same ruler or strength, such as Aries and Scorpio]] increase goodwill.

**34** If the ruler or the "host" of a new moon [[notes: *Interlunium*; the conjunction of the Sun and Moon]] falls on a cardinal point, it signifies whatever is to happen during that month.

**35** When the Sun reaches the position of any star, it excites the power which that star possesses in the atmosphere.

**36** In the founding of cities, use the fixed stars which have something to contribute; however, in the building of houses, use the wandering stars [[notes: The planets]]. The kings of any city who have Mars at their midheaven [[notes: *Culminantem*; the highest point of the sky in the chart]] usually perish by the sword.

**37** Those who have Virgo or Pisces as their horoscope [[notes: Here meaning the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon]] will be the cause of their own power; however, those whose Ascendant is Aries or Libra will be the cause of their own death. You shall reason in the same way regarding the other signs.

**38** When Mercury is positioned and powerful in the second house of Saturn [[notes: Capricorn or Aquarius]], it gives the native an intellect for conjectures and the investigation of things; but in the house of Mars, and especially in Aries, it gives eloquence.

**39** Affliction of the eleventh house in the crowning of a king signifies the loss of both his household and his money. But affliction of the second house signifies the loss of the money in his treasury.

**40** When the Ascendant is oppressed by "malefics" [[notes: Harmful planets, typically Saturn and Mars]], the person born at that time delights in filthy things and approves of foul odors.

**41** Beware of affliction to the eighth house and its lord at the time of departure; but beware of the second house and its lord at the time of return.

**42** A disease that begins when the Moon is in that sign which a malefic planet held at birth—or in a square or opposition to it—will be most grave. If a malefic planet regards it, it is dangerous. But if it is in the place where a "benefic" [[notes: Helpful planets, typically Jupiter and Venus]] was at the time of birth, it will be without danger.

**43** National characteristics [[notes: *Gentis figuras*]] can intensify contrary significations of the times.

**44** It is harmful when the Ascendant of a sick person's birth chart clashes with the current celestial figures, and no benefic planet intervenes at that time.

**45** Whoever does not have the rulers of his birth chart or his Ascendant in "human signs" [[notes: Signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius]] will be a stranger to humanity, even toward himself.

**46** Great fortunes are bestowed in birth charts by the fixed stars, by the cardinal points of the new moons, and by the locations of the "Part of Fortune" [[notes: A specific calculated point in a chart representing prosperity]] of the kingdom, when the horoscope is found within them.

**47** In a birth chart, when a malefic planet falls upon the place of a benefic in another person's chart, the one who has the benefic will be afflicted with harm by the one who has the malefic.

**48** When the midheaven of the master (that is, the prince) is the Ascendant of the subject, or if their rulers are arranged in a benevolent configuration, they will remain inseparable for a long time. The same is true when the sixth house of the servant is found to be the Ascendant of the prince.

**49** When the Ascendant of the subject is the midheaven in the master's birth chart, the master will place such trust in that subject that he will be influenced by him.

**50** Do not overlook the one hundred and ten "new conjunctions." For in these is placed the knowledge of those things which happen in the world, regarding both generation and corruption.

**51** Take the sign in which the Moon is at the time of birth and make it the Ascendant at conception. And take the sign in which the Moon was found at conception and make it (or its opposite) the Ascendant at birth.

**52** The rulers of the birth charts of tall men are in "sublimities" [[notes: High elevations or northern latitudes]], and their Ascendants are at the beginning of the signs. But those who are of short stature are found in "humilities" [[notes: Low elevations]]. In addition to these, inquire whether the signs are "straight" or "oblique."

**53** The rulers of the birth charts of thin men have no latitude [[notes: Distance from the ecliptic]], while those of fat men do. If the latitude is Southern, they will be agile; if Northern, they will be sluggish.

**54** Rulers of buildings where "subterranean" stars are joined hinder the raising of the structure.

**55** The harmful power of Mars against ships is diminished when it is neither in the midheaven nor in the e- [[margin: leventh]] [[notes: Text cuts off, indicating the next house of the chart.]]

It emphasizes the relationship between a master and subject's charts and the influence of specific signs on human character.]]

[[meta: This page continues a series of astrological aphorisms from the Centiloquium, a collection of 100 rules for divination. This page transitions from nautical astrology (shipwrecks) into medical, meteorological, and natal predictions. The Latin uses standard Renaissance abbreviations which have been expanded for this translation.]]

->CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY [page number: 77]<-

[[notes: This fragment concludes a rule from the previous page regarding travel by sea.]] is in the tenth house; for in these places he destroys the ship, with pirates seizing it by force. The ship will be set on fire if he [[notes: "He" refers to the planet Mars, discussed on the previous page]] ascends from any fixed star which is of the nature of Mars, and it will be distressed.

**56** When the Moon is in its first quarter—that is, from the time it has departed from its conjunction with the Sun [[notes: The New Moon]]—the moisture of bodies flows out until the second quarter [[notes: The Full Moon]]; however, in the remaining phases, they decrease.

**57** When you see the seventh house and its lord afflicted during a sickness, change the doctor. [[notes: In medical astrology, the first house represents the patient and the seventh house represents the physician. If the seventh house is "afflicted" by bad planetary aspects, the doctor may be incompetent or the treatment ineffective.]]

**58** Examine the place of the conjunction and where it falls in relation to the ascendant of the year; for when the *profection* reaches that point, then the event will occur. [[notes: A "profection" is an ancient timing technique where a point in the birth chart is moved forward by one zodiac sign for every year of life.]]

**59** Do not pronounce that someone who is absent has died before you have seen whether they have simply become drunk; nor that they have received a wound before you have inquired whether they have been bled [[notes: Bloodletting was a common medical treatment; a chart indicating "loss of blood" might just mean a scheduled surgery]]; nor that they have found a treasure before you have investigated whether they have perhaps received a deposit, since the astrological figures for all these things are similar.

**60** Regarding the sick, observe the "critical days" and the Moon's journey through the angles of a sixteen-sided figure. For where you find those angles well-disposed, it will go well for the person suffering; conversely, it will go poorly if you find them afflicted. [[notes: This refers to the "Crisis" points in an illness, calculated by the Moon's movement through 22.5-degree arcs (divisions of the 360-degree circle into 16 parts).]]

**61** The Moon signifies those things which belong to the body, as they are similar to her in their movement.

**62** When you establish the beginning of the minute of a conjunction, you can judge the change of the weather in that month. For the judgment will be according to the ruler of the angle of each figure; for this ruler dominates the nature of the air, taking on also the quality of the present time.

**63** When Saturn and Jupiter are in conjunction, see which of them is more elevated, and pronounce according to his nature. Do the same for the other stars.

**64** When you have inspected the lord of a query [[notes: The planet representing a specific question]], look at what power he holds in the revolution of the year, or in the ascendant of the New Moon, and pronounce according to these things.

**65** In the "minimal" conjunction is the difference of the "middle" conjunction, and in the "middle" is the difference of the "maximal" conjunction. [[notes: These refer to the "Great Conjunctions" of Jupiter and Saturn, which occur roughly every 20, 200, and 800 years, used to predict historical eras and the rise of empires.]]

**66** Do not use *profections* alone, but also the additions and subtractions of the stars.

**67** Years of life are diminished because of the weakness of the recipient.

**68** A malefic planet [[notes: Saturn or Mars]], when it rises in the morning, signifies an accident; however, in the evening, it signifies disease.

**69** There will be a defect in the sight of the newborn when the Moon is opposite the Sun and is joined to "cloudy" stars. [[notes: "Cloudy stars" or nebulae, such as the Pleiades or Praesepe, were traditionally believed to cause blindness or poor vision if they touched the luminaries (Sun/Moon) in a birth chart.]] Likewise, when the Moon is on the western horizon and both malefic stars are on the eastern horizon, and the Sun is also on one of the cardinal points, the newborn will be deprived of eyes.

**70** In the charts of the insane, the Moon is not joined to Mercury; and in the charts of the demon-possessed, neither is joined to the ascendant. In such a figure, Saturn will hold a cardinal point by night, but Mars by day—especially in Cancer, Virgo, or Pisces.

**71** In the births of men, when both luminaries are in masculine signs, their actions will be according to nature. But in the births of women, their actions will be intensified [[notes: Meaning more "masculine" or assertive]]. The same applies to Mars and Venus; for when they rise in the morning, they become more masculine; when they set in the evening, they become more feminine.

**72** Take things concerning upbringing from the lords of the "triplicity" of the ascendant; take things concerning the length of life from the lords of the "triplicity" of the luminary in charge. [[notes: Triplicities are groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water). Each triplicity has specific planetary "lords."]]

**73** When the Sun is found with the "Head of the Gorgon," if it is neither aspected by a beneficial star, nor a beneficial star rules the eighth house, and the lord of the luminary in charge is opposite Mars or squares him, the one who is born will be beheaded. [[notes: The "Head of the Gorgon" is the star Algol, historically considered the most "evil" star in the sky.]] But if the luminary is at the midheaven, his body will be mangled. If the conjunction is in Gemini or Pisces, his hands and feet will be amputated.

**74** Whoever has Mars in the ascendant will definitely have a scar on their face.

**75** When the Sun is joined to the lord of the ascendant in Leo, and Mars has no power in the ascendant, and no beneficial star is in the eighth house, the one who is born will be consumed by fire.

**76** When Saturn holds the midheaven and the luminary in charge is opposite him, and an earthy sign is on the bottom of the sky [[notes: The fourth house or Imum Coeli]], the one who is born will perish in the ruins of buildings. If it is a water sign, he will be suffocated by water. If it is a human sign [[notes: Signs like Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius]], he will be strangled by men, or perish by the noose or lashes. But if a beneficial star is in the eighth house, he will come close to these things, but will not die.

The previous page ended at aphorism 76. The text employs technical terminology of "profections" (symbolic movements of planets) and "houses" (twelve divisions of the sky).]]

-># THE CENTILOQUIUM OF PTOLEMY<-

77  Direct the profection [[notes: A "profection" is a symbolic technique where a point in the birth chart is advanced by one zodiac sign per year]] of the Ascendant for matters concerning the body; that of the Part of Fortune for external affairs; that of the Moon for the connection between body and soul; and that of the Midheaven [[notes: The highest point of the chart, associated with career and public life]] for one's actions.
78  A star often exerts its power in a place where it otherwise holds no dignity [[notes: "Dignity" refers to a planet's strength based on its position in the zodiac]], bringing unexpected gain to the one born under it.
79  When Mars is in the eleventh house [[notes: Traditionally the house of friends and hopes]], he is not mastered by the ruler of that house.
80  When Venus is joined with Saturn and has a host [[notes: A "host" or dispositor is the planet that rules the sign where another planet is currently located]] in the seventh house, the person born will engage in shameful sexual acts.
81  Times [of events] are determined in seven ways: by the interval between two rulers; by the interval of configurations between them; by the approach of one to another; by the interval between one and the place signifying the matter sought; by the setting of a star with addition or subtraction; by the change of a ruler; and by the entry of a planet into its own place.
82  When the figures of the new moon or full moon are equal, look to the horoscope; if that too is equal, do not be in a hurry to deliver a judgment.
83  The time of a petition indicates the affection between the petitioner and the king. The "throne," however, indicates the nature of the actions involved.
84  When Mars is the lord of the Ascendant at the time a possession is taken, and he rules the second house or is joined to the lord of the second, he will bring much loss.
85  When the lord of the Ascendant is configured with the lord of the second house, the prince will willingly undertake many expenses.
86  The Sun is the source of vital power; the Moon is the source of natural power.
87  The revolutions of the months consist of twenty-eight days, two hours, and approximately eighteen minutes. Some, however, judge by the passage of the Sun when it is exactly equaled to the degree and minute it held at the beginning.
88  When we wish to calculate the profection of the Part of Fortune for the entire year of a revolution, we take the distance from the Sun to the Moon and add an equal distance to the Ascendant.
89  Look for matters concerning grandfathers in the seventh house, and for uncles in the sixth.
90  When the ruler sees [[notes: In astrology, "seeing" means forming a geometric aspect or relationship between signs]] the Ascendant, the hidden thing will be according to the nature of the Ascendant; but if it does not see it, the thing will be according to the nature of the place where that ruler is master. The lord of the hour indicates its color, and the place of the Moon demonstrates the time. If it is above the earth, the thing is new; if below the earth, it is old. The Part of Fortune shows its quantity, whether it be long or short. The lords of the "Terms" [[notes: Specific subdivisions of zodiac signs]], the Imum Coeli [[notes: The lowest point of the chart, associated with hidden things and the end of life]], the Midheaven, and the Moon demonstrate its substance.
91  It is a bad sign when the ruler of a sick person is "combust" [[notes: A planet is "combust" when it is so close to the Sun that its light is obscured, signifying weakness or affliction]], especially if the Part of Fortune is also afflicted.
92  An "oriental" Saturn [[notes: Rising before the Sun]] does not harm the sick as much as an "occidental" Mars [[notes: Setting after the Sun]].
93  Do not judge from the figures before you have made a "conjunction" [[notes: Here meaning a synthesis of multiple factors]]. For principles are transformed in every conjunction; therefore, mix both, and you will not err.
94  The location of the most powerful of the rulers indicates those things which are in the mind of the person asking the question.
95  The things that rise with the individual decans [[notes: Ten-degree subdivisions of the zodiac signs]] confirm the will of the native toward the craft they practice.
96  The significance of an eclipse is determined by the planet nearest the "angles" [[notes: The four cardinal points: Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli]]. Consider also the nature of the stars standing with them—both the wandering stars [planets] and the fixed stars—and also the images rising with them; pronounce your judgment according to these.
97  The matter about which a question is asked is completed quickly when the lord of the new or full moon is on a cardinal point.
98  Meteors [[notes: "Traiectiones" or "shooting stars"]] and comets hold the second rank in making judgments.
99  Meteors indicate dryness in the air. If they move toward one part, they indicate wind from that corner; if they move in different directions, they indicate a decrease in waters, disturbances of the air, and incursions of armies.
100 Comets which are within eleven signs of the Sun: if they appear in the cardinal points, a king of some realm or one of the princes of the realm will die. If in a "succedent" house [[notes: Houses that follow the cardinal points: 2, 5, 8, 11]], his treasures will fare well, but he will change his governor. If in a "cadent" house [[notes: Houses 3, 6, 9, 12]], there will be diseases and sudden deaths. If they move from West to East, a foreign enemy will invade the regions; if they do not move, the enemy will be from within the province.

->**Cl. Ptolemy**<-

-> # THE BOOK OF THE HUNDRED <-
-> ## APHORISMS OF HERMES. <-

[[insert: [[meta: Large decorative woodcut initial S]]]] **S**un and Moon, after God, are the life of all living things. Indeed, the births [[notes: Latin *nativitates*, referring to natal horoscopes or the people born under them]] of many do not have a *hyleg* [[notes: The *hyleg* is the "giver of life," a specific planet or point in a chart used to determine a person's lifespan]], but because the Sun and Moon behold their Ascendant [[notes: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]] with favor, and are themselves unimpeded, their life is prolonged for a greater time.
**2** All day-time births are strengthened by the Sun, when it is well-configured with the benefics [[notes: The "benefics" are the "good" planets, traditionally Jupiter and Venus]]. Night-time births, however, are strengthened by the Moon, when she is beheld by the benefics; and if this is not the case, yet there are good planets in the angles [[notes: The "angles" are the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 10th (Midheaven), 7th (Descendant), and 4th (Imum Coeli)]], then the birth is fortunate.
**3** When Mars is the lord of the Ascendant and is in the 10th house, he grants the native [[notes: The person for whom the chart is cast]] dignity and power, which they will use with injustice and cruelty; and this is truly called a misfortune rather than a fortune.
**4** Jupiter, when configured with the malevolents [[notes: The "malevolents" or "malefics" are the "harsh" planets, traditionally Saturn and Mars]], changes their malice into good; Venus cannot do this unless she is aided by Jupiter, and therefore in increasing good and in prohibiting evil, Jupiter is considered much better than Venus.
**5** The astrologer cannot make a synthesis of the stars' significations before he knows their friendships and enmities. Their friendship and enmity is threefold: [[margin: *Friendship and* / *enmity of the* / *stars.*]] one according to nature, another according to their houses, and the third according to their aspects [[notes: "Aspects" are the geometric angles—like squares or triangles—formed between planets in the sky]].
**6** Venus is opposed to Mercury: for he embraces speech and disciplines, while she embraces pleasures and delights. Similarly, Jupiter is opposed to Mars: for he desires mercy and justice, while the other desires impiety and cruelty.
**7** You should make the Sun, or one of the superior planets [[notes: The "superior planets" are those further from the Sun than Earth: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn]], the significator of great princes. But for scribes and peasants, use the inferior planets, and especially the Moon.
**8** An aspect cannot diminish the significance of a conjunction. A conjunction, however, diminishes the significance of an aspect; for a conjunction is stronger than an aspect.
**9** Do not define or choose anything while Scorpio is in the Ascendant, nor when the angles are oblique; or if Mars should be in them, for the outcome of the definition will turn out false, especially because Scorpio is a sign of falsehood.
**10** A benefic planet brings forth bad things from the 6th or 12th houses when it is hindered there by malevolents.
**11** Rumors told while the Moon is in the first face [[notes: A "face" or "decan" is a 10-degree segment of a zodiac sign]] of Scorpio are lies and fabrications.
**12** Sometimes the judgments of astrologers result in untruths, either because of an error in their instruments, or because of the ignorance of the querent [[notes: The "querent" is the person asking the question]], or when the Sun is near the degree of the Midheaven, or when the figures that grant or deny the matter are equal.
**13** While the Moon is in the south, descending in Scorpio or Pisces, do not begin to build, for a building of this kind will quickly be destroyed.
**14** It is necessary for Mercury to be strong through harmonious places and through the configurations of other stars in natal charts for the native to have dignity. For Mercury by himself is a weak planet.
**15** A victory of two bodies [[notes: This likely refers to a conjunction or a struggle between significators in "double-bodied" or mutable signs]] is notably good, while defeat is bad; indeed, each is doubled.
**16** Do not define anything before you know the intention of the seeker. Many indeed do not know how to ask, nor can they express what they intend.
**17** When you are asked about the father, look to the 4th house; about a brother, the 3rd; about a son, the 5th; about a wife, the 7th. If, however, you are asked on behalf of a sick person, look to no other than the Ascendant.
**18** When the Moon comes to the squares [[notes: A "square" is a harsh 90-degree aspect]] of the benefics or the malevolents, both hindrance and help will be in doubt; and it is to be feared that the malevolents may hinder, while the benefics may be unable to help.
**19** At the beginning of journeys and returns, let the Moon not be in the Ascendant, nor in the 4th, nor in the 9th; and

-> H if not <- [[notes: This is a "catchword," a common feature in old printing where the first word(s) of the next page are printed at the bottom of the current one to ensure the binder puts pages in the correct order.]]

-> ## **THE CENTILOQUIUM** <-

[[notes: The *Centiloquium* (Hundred Sayings) is a famous collection of astrological rules. Although historically attributed to Ptolemy, modern scholars believe it was written by an anonymous Arabic or 10th-century author.]]

...if it has not been impeded. In the entry into a city, the Moon should not be in the Ascendant, nor in the 2nd or 4th houses. The same applies to the entry into a house.

**20** The accidents [[notes: In this context, "accidents" refers to the events or happenings in a person's life.]] of men are foreseen in three ways: from their own birth, from the birth of their firstborn son, or from an interrogation [[notes: A "horary" question asked of an astrologer.]] conducted with sincere emotion and care.

**21** Every undertaking begun while a planet is retrograde [[notes: Appearing to move backward in the sky from the perspective of Earth.]]—if the Moon is in conjunction with it—is quickly destroyed and turns for the worse, especially when the planet is impeded.

**22** The state of kings and princes is taken from Saturn and the Sun, and from the planet residing in the 10th house. The king’s helpers are known from the 11th house, and the helpers of the common folk from the 2nd house.

**23** A king or prince’s departure for a journey is utterly rejected when Cancer is in the Ascendant.

**24** Gemini and Sagittarius obey the **Head of the Dragon** and the **Tail** [[notes: These are the North and South Nodes of the Moon, points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path. They were often viewed as points of intense, often malefic, energy.]] more than other signs; therefore, they work greater evils in those signs than in others.

**25** In the nativities [[notes: Birth charts.]] of women, when the Ascendant is in one of the houses of Venus [[notes: Taurus or Libra.]] and Mars is located in them, or if it is in a house of Mars [[notes: Aries or Scorpio.]] and Venus is located in them, the woman will be immodest. The same occurs if she has Capricorn in the Ascendant.

**26** The Sun receives the virtues of the planets when it is in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven and joined with them. At night, the Moon does the same when joined with the aforementioned planets in those same places.

**27** Jupiter dissolves the malice of Saturn, just as Venus dissolves that of Mars.

**28** When a question is asked regarding a woman, take the general significance from Venus, but the specific significance from the 7th house. If it is regarding an enemy, take the absolute significance from the 12th house, but the specific from the 7th.

**29** In the departure of anyone for battle, but especially for kings, let the Ascendant be a house of the superior planets [[notes: Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn.]] or the Sun; and let both the Ascendant and its Lord be strong. Let the Lord of the 7th house [[notes: Representing the enemy.]] be weak and impeded by malefic influences.

**30** The Moon joined to Saturn or Jupiter, increasing in light and in number [[notes: Referring to its speed or its day in the lunar cycle.]], will be good for all things. If it is decreasing, it will be bad for all things. Understand the exact opposite for Venus and Mars.

**31** In matters of loans and deposits, beware lest Jupiter be **under the rays** [[notes: "Combust" or too close to the Sun to be visible, which weakens a planet’s power.]] or impeded by malefic planets. If this occurs, and it is not "received" from its impediment, no restitution—or only a small amount—will follow.

**32** Benefic planets moving toward a configuration with malefic ones diminish some of their malice, regardless of the aspect; they do so more through good aspects [[notes: Trines and sextiles.]] and less through bad ones. Malefic planets moving toward a configuration with benefics via a square or opposition diminish some of their goodness, but through other aspects, they do nothing.

**33** When Saturn passes from one sign into another, **diachohontes** occur in the sky—which the Arabs call **affub** [[notes: These terms refer to meteors, "shooting stars," or fiery atmospheric phenomena.]]—or other signs of a fiery nature.

**34** The tempering of the air occurs from the conjunction of Jupiter and the Sun, especially when that conjunction happens in air signs. From the conjunction of Saturn and the Sun comes cold. From the conjunction of the Sun and Mars in a **bicorporeal sign** [[notes: Also known as "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.]] during the springtime, darkness of the air and frequent illnesses occur.

**35** In the summer, when the Sun enters the **term** [[notes: An Egyptian or Chaldean subdivision of a zodiac sign.]] of Mars, heat occurs. In winter, drought and a lack of rain will be present.

**36** In birth charts and questions of life, you should calculate the **hyleg** and **alcocoden** [[notes: The *hyleg* is the "giver of life" (a point in the chart), and the *alcocoden* is the planet that rules it, used to predict the length of a person's life.]], as well as their directions—especially in questions regarding kings and nobles. For through these, their fortunes, whether good or bad, are known.

**37** When the Ascendant is in a good state but its Lord is in a bad one, it indicates health of the body but anxiety and sadness of the soul. If it is the other way around, judge the opposite.

**38** Always note the configuration of the stars not by the signs, but by their **rays** [[notes: The specific degrees of the aspects (angles) between planets, rather than just the signs they inhabit.]].

**39** Use the Moon for curing the eyes when it is increasing in light and free from the gaze [[notes: Aspect.]] of malefic planets.

**40** If the **Part of Fortune** [[notes: A mathematical point in the chart representing luck and prosperity.]] is with a malefic planet in the 4th, 9th, or 10th house, and the benefics are far away, it indicates death for a sick person.

**41** Good or evil things will be durable when the significator is **stationary** and in an **angle** [[notes: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, where planets are most active.]]. They will be easily changed when the same planet is retrograde and in the "cadent" houses [[notes: The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, which were considered weak.]] of the angles.

->HERMES<- [[page number: 87]]

**42** The lord of the 2nd house possesses the same power to hinder as the lord of the 8th. Similarly, the lord of the 6th has the same power as the lord of the 12th. [[notes: In traditional astrology, the 2nd, 8th, 6th, and 12th houses are often considered difficult or "unfortunate" because they do not "see" (aspect) the Ascendant, which represents the life and health of the individual.]]

**43** When Mars is occidental [[notes: Setting after the Sun]] in Cancer and is not aspecting Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, or the Sun, the person will be a phlebotomist [[notes: A bloodletter, a common medical profession in the past]]. However, if Mars is in Capricorn in the same manner, he will be a destroyer of men and a lover of bloodshed.

**44** It happens that a skilled astrologer errs when he is ignorant of the significator [[notes: The planet representing the person or topic in question]] of the person for whom he is making a selection.

**45** Saturn elevated above Venus by a square aspect [[notes: Positioned at a 90-degree angle and in a stronger position]] makes the children of that birth impudent, and in women, it makes them impatient. But if Venus is elevated over Saturn, it makes them easy and prone to the company of women.

**46** If Mercury is in the Ascendant at someone’s birth, being oriental and swift in motion, then the person born will be eloquent and learned in the liberal sciences. The same will occur if Mercury is in Sagittarius in its own terms [[notes: Specific degrees of a sign over which a planet has secondary rulership]] in that same manner.

**47** Of the Angles [[notes: The four most powerful points in an astrological chart]], the first is the horoscope [[notes: The Ascendant]], the second is the Midheaven, the third is the western point [[notes: The Descendant]], and the fourth is the angle of the earth [[notes: The IC or Imum Coeli]]. Of the remaining places, the first is the 11th house, then the 2nd, then the 5th, then the 9th, then the 3rd, and then the 8th. Truly, the 6th and 12th are the worst.

**48** Unless a benevolent planet [[notes: Jupiter or Venus]] forbids it, Mars takes back whatever he gives.

**49** You shall adapt the planets to the persons to whom you are making a petition. [[notes: Meaning, one should choose a time for a request when the planet ruling that type of person—like Mercury for a scholar or Jupiter for a judge—is well-placed.]]

**50** When the Ascendant or a planet is found at the 30th degree of a sign, its significance is in the following sign; but if it is at the 29th degree, it remains in that sign. For the power of a planet is considered across three degrees: specifically, the degree it is in, the one preceding it, and the one following it.

**51** One must consider future things from the conjunctions of the planets, but the present or the past from their separations.

**52** If Jupiter is in Cancer, far from the Ascendant and not hindered by anything, the person born will indeed be rational and very skilled in knowledge, yet he will love a solitary life and will not receive public praise for his knowledge.

**53** Many inconveniences occur in the world when an eclipse of both luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]] happens in a single month, and especially in those places where they have a special significance.

**54** If the Moon is in the *Via Combusta* [[notes: "The Burnt Way," a specific section of the zodiac (traditionally 15° Libra to 15° Scorpio) considered unlucky]] at the time a journey begins, the traveler will fall ill during his travels or suffer some grave troubles.

**55** In the directions of the wandering stars [[notes: The planets]] and the non-wandering ones [[notes: The fixed stars]], it is necessary to consider the time.

**56** Paternal property passes to the son when Saturn is fortunate and looks upon the lord of the Ascendant with affection [[notes: A harmonious aspect like a trine or sextile]], and even more so if he is the lord of the 4th house.

**57** When benevolent planets are in signs where they have no dignity [[notes: No special standing or "essential dignity" like being in their own sign or exaltation]], their kindness will be diffused or diminished.

**58** If Mars is the *almutaz* [[notes: The "Almuten," the planet with the most combined strength/dignity in a chart]] at a birth and is not joined to benevolent planets, it signifies that the native will suffer from fire or arson.

**59** A benevolent planet grants immense happiness when it is received in its own house; conversely, a malefic planet [[notes: Saturn or Mars]] refrains from much of its malice when it is received in such a way.

**60** The native will be sick and weak when Mars is elevated over Saturn. But if Saturn is over Mars, he will be strong and stout.

**61** If the "Part of Marriage" [[notes: An Arabic Part, a mathematical point calculated from planet positions]] for a man falls in obedient signs, but for the woman in commanding signs, the woman will rule the man, and the man will obey the woman; if it is the other way around, you may judge the opposite. [[notes: "Commanding" signs are the Northern signs (Aries-Virgo), and "Obedient" signs are the Southern signs (Libra-Pisces).]]

**62** Out of friendship, if the lords of the triplicity [[notes: The three signs of the same element]] of the conjunctional light [[notes: The Sun or Moon at the previous New Moon]] are joined to one another—the first to the second, and the second to the third—they signify lasting prosperity and freedom from sorrows.

**63** When Mercury is in Pisces in "pitted degrees," it makes those born foolish or mute. Jupiter in the houses of Mars [[notes: Aries or Scorpio]] and in "pitted degrees" makes them filthy, needy, and harmed by military people. In the houses of Saturn, however—especially in Capricorn—and in "pitted degrees," it makes them rigid and hated by everyone. [[notes: "Pitted degrees" (gradibus putei) were certain specific degrees in the zodiac thought to "sink" or weaken the planet's influence, like falling into a pit.]]
