-># THE HUNDRED APHORISMS<-

**64** Mercury takes on the nature of Mars when he is located in Mars's houses [[notes: The "houses" or signs ruled by Mars are Aries and Scorpio]]. If Mercury is configured with Mars and is "cadent" [[notes: Falling away from the powerful corners or "angles" of the chart, signifying weakness]] from an angle, the person born will be a lover of hunting and will delight in playing at dice. However, if he is not cadent, he will be warlike and a soldier.

**65** When planets are "under the rays"—meaning they are within 12 degrees of the Sun—they are weakened and afflicted, unless they happen to be in the exact same degree as the Sun [[notes: This rare exact alignment is known as "Cazimi," where the planet is thought to be in the "heart of the Sun" and thus highly empowered]]. However, when they have passed 12 degrees and are "oriental" [[notes: Rising before the Sun in the morning]], they are strong.

**66** The Head [[notes: "Caput Draconis" or the Dragon’s Head, the North Node of the Moon]] works terrible evils when paired with the malefic planets [[notes: Mars and Saturn]], for it increases their malice. Yet, it works much good with the benefics [[notes: Jupiter and Venus]], for through it their kindness is increased. The Tail [[notes: "Cauda Draconis" or the Dragon’s Tail, the South Node]], just as it is opposite in position, is also opposite to the Head in its meanings.

**67** If anyone has Mercury in the sixth house of their nativity [[notes: The house traditionally associated with illness and service]], they will turn from their own faith to another. And whoever has an afflicted "Part of Fortune" [[notes: An Arabic Part or calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and well-being]], they will not be firm in their faith.

**68** The first sign encountered holds dominion over the meaning of a matter when that matter is signified by two signs.

**69** The beginning of every matter is taken from the Moon, but every end is taken from the "Lord of her House" [[notes: The planet that rules the sign in which the Moon is located]].

**70** If Jupiter, in the "Revolution of the Years of the World" [[notes: A mundane chart cast for the beginning of the year to predict world events]], is in its own house or exaltation, oriental, in an angle, and free from the influence of the malefic planets, it signifies a scarcity of grain. [[notes: While Jupiter usually brings abundance, traditional texts sometimes suggest its heat can lead to drought or that its "exaltation" in certain contexts could lead to an over-ripening or scarcity in specific climates.]]

**71** There is fear for the sick when the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant are afflicted by the Lord of the Eighth House [[notes: The Eighth House is the house of death]].

**72** Do not begin a quarrel, a fight, or a lawsuit in any way when the Moon is in a bad state; for if it happens in such a way, you will undoubtedly be defeated.

**73** Every rebel who begins to rebel at the beginning of the year shall obtain dominion without difficulty.

**74** When the Moon is in the "ruminating signs" [[notes: Signs associated with animals that chew the cud: Aries, Taurus, and Capricorn]] or joined to a retrograde planet, it is not good to use purges [[notes: Laxative medicines]]; for these will cause vomiting or other injuries.

**75** Oriental planets, whether they show good or evil, give their effects quickly; occidental planets [[notes: Setting after the Sun in the evening]] give them slowly.

**76** The degree of the conjunction of the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and Moon]] marks the midpoint of the duration of an eclipse.

**77** In the Revolution of the Years of the World, there will be many difficulties and battles when Jupiter and Saturn are both in their exaltations [[notes: Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, and Saturn is exalted in Libra]].

**78** Be suspicious and anxious when a "benefic" planet is with a "malefic"; do not trust much that the malice of the evil planet has been entirely turned away.

**79** The twelve signs depend upon the Ascendant [[notes: The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]]. The Ascendant signifies the state of the body, but its Lord signifies the state of the soul. Therefore, strive in every way so that the Ascendant and its Lord are not afflicted.

**80** When planets are in "fixed signs" [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius]], they signify a durable matter; in "bicorporeal" signs [[notes: Also known as mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces]], the matter is doubtful; in "moveable" signs [[notes: Also known as cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn]], it is changeable for either good or evil.

**81** For secret matters, use the Moon not when she is entering "under the rays," but when she is coming out of them [[notes: Meaning when the Moon is moving away from the Sun and becoming visible again]].

**82** To cut or put on new clothes when the Moon is in a fixed sign, and especially in Leo, is horrible and dangerous; this is also true when she is in conjunction or opposition to the Sun, or afflicted by malefic planets.

**83** The Moon has great power in "interrogations" [[notes: Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question]], unless the Ascendant is Leo, Sagittarius, or Aquarius. In those cases, those signs take away her significance, and especially when she is in Leo or Aquarius.

**84** Saturn is still "under the rays" as long as a distance of 15 degrees exists between it and the Sun. Understand the same for Jupiter.

**85** The Moon in Cancer is utterly rejected for marriages. It is similar in Virgo, except in the marriages of widows.

**86** A malefic planet, when it is oriental and in its own house or exaltation, is better than a retrograde and afflicted benefic planet.

**87** There will be an impediment or ailment regarding that part of the body signified by the sign that was afflicted at the time of birth.

->**88 Then**<-

It emphasizes the importance of the Moon's condition and the relative strength of planets based on their relationship to the Sun and the "angles" of a chart.]]

The Latin text employs standard abbreviations of the period, such as the 'q;' for '-que' (and) and nasal macrons, which have been expanded for this translation.]]

->HERMETIS<- [[page number: 89]]

**88** Great prosperity occurs when the lords of the triplicity [[notes: The zodiac signs are divided into four "triplicities" based on the elements (Fire, Earth, Air, Water), each ruled by a set of planets]] of the luminary [[notes: The Sun or the Moon]] that holds authority are in the angles or the houses following the angles [[notes: The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart; "succedent" houses follow them and are also considered strong]], in their own proper places, and removed from the aspect of malefics [[notes: Specifically Saturn and Mars, traditionally viewed as bringers of hardship]]. And if the lord of the Ascendant is in a good state, the good will be even greater and more abundant.

**89** Planets do the same thing through a trine aspect [[notes: Planets 120 degrees apart]] as they do through a sextile [[notes: Planets 60 degrees apart]]; however, the sextile aspect brings less good or evil than the trine.

**90** Saturn brings evil with slowness, but Mars brings it suddenly; for this reason, Mars is considered worse than Saturn in the harm it causes.

**91** It is called a "Great Conjunction" when the three superior planets [[notes: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—those further from the Sun than Earth is]] are joined in one of the royal signs [[notes: Usually referring to the Fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius]]; they create very powerful kingdoms when they are aspected by the Sun.

**92** A secret word that is sought after is immediately revealed when the Moon and the planet she is applying to [[notes: Moving toward an aspect with]] are in vocal signs [[notes: The "human" signs—Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Sagittarius—thought to have "voices"]] and in the 5th or 3rd houses, or in opposition to them.

**93** A malefic planet increases its malice in the eighth house [[notes: The house associated with death and shared resources]], but a benefic planet in that same place exhibits neither good nor evil.

**94** Neither good nor evil will ever be fully realized unless the benefic or malefic planets in the birth chart—or in the yearly revolution—look upon the Moon through a square aspect [[notes: An aspect of 90 degrees, considered a point of tension or action]].

**95** If Mercury is hindered in the 6th house, the native [[notes: The person for whom the chart is cast]] will die in prison. If Saturn is enclosed in the 12th house and Venus is in the 8th, they will suffer a great fall.

**96** One must be fearful at the onset of an illness when the Sun (during the day) or the Moon (at night) is hindered.

**97** The meanings of the stars always vary when their latitudes change within their configurations to one another.

**98** The Moon in the 4th, 7th, 9th, or 12th houses indicates that the matter being asked about has already been questioned before. The same is indicated if she has separated from Mercury. However, if the Ascending sign is bicorporeal [[notes: "Double-bodied" or mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces]] and the Moon is likewise in a bicorporeal sign, the same matter will be sought after again.

**99** If a malefic is in its own house or exaltation [[notes: Signs where a planet is particularly strong]], even if it acts with slowness, it will nonetheless show a good end. But if that same planet is hindered in the Ascendant, even if it is in its own house or exaltation, it nonetheless brings hindrance and a bad end.

**100** The outcome of the events of every undertaking, and of all its uncertainties, is determined by these significators: namely, by the 4th house and its lord, and by any planet that happens to be in that house. Likewise by the luminary which holds authority and its lord, and by the planet to which that luminary is joined, and its lord.

> Use these and the other things I have handed down to you, most illustrious one, and by using them with sobriety, you shall never err, with the help of God.

## ->THE CENTILOQUIUM OF BETHEM<-
[[notes: Bethem is likely Al-Battani or Al-Bitruji, Arabic-era astronomers/astrologers whose works were translated into Latin and became staples of European science]]

# **1**
I shall now begin this book on the customs of judging the stars.
**2** Know that when planets are retrograde [[notes: Appearing to move backward in the sky]], they are like a man who is sick, stunned, and full of anxiety.
**3** A planet that is cadent [[notes: Falling away from the angles/strength]] is like a dead man who has no movement.
**4** A combust planet [[notes: A planet so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up"]] is like a captive, imprisoned and reviled without power.
**5** A planet standing still before retrogradation [[notes: Stationary]] is like a healthy man from whom health is departing, but a little of it still remains.
**6** A planet standing still before moving direct is like a sick man after he recovers and sees the beginning of his health.
**7** A planet "besieged" is like one fearing between two enemies; that is, when it is between two "infortunes" [[notes: Saturn and Mars]].
**8** When a planet is between two "fortunes" [[notes: Jupiter and Venus]], it is like a man eating and drinking, secure from all evil and fear.
**9** When the infortunes aspect a planet from the fourth house, or the planet aspects them, it is like a man for whom death, vengeance, and his final arrangement are already beginning.
**10** When a planet is in the aspect of its enemy, it is like a man fearing his enemy.
**11** When it is with its enemy, it is like a man fighting with his enemy.
**12** One who is with a planet that is a friend and similar to itself is like a man to whom hospitality and fellowship are shown.

[[page number: 90]]

-> **THE CENTILOQUIUM** <-
[[notes: *Centiloquium* translates to "The Hundred Sayings." These were highly popular collections of astrological rules in the Middle Ages and Renaissance, often attributed to famous figures like Ptolemy or Hermes Trismegistus.]]

**13** When a planet is in the house of its ally, it is like a man with his companion.
[[notes: In astrology, "houses" (domus) are the zodiac signs where a planet is said to "rule." An "ally" refers to a planet with a compatible nature.]]

**14** When it is falling away from its own house, or from the house of its exaltation, it is like a man absent from his own home or his city.
[[notes: "Exaltation" is a specific zodiac sign where a planet’s influence is considered particularly powerful, even more so than in its home sign.]]

**15** When it is in its own house, or the house of its exaltation, it is like a man in his own home; his judgment and will are perfected, and what he wishes to happen is completed.

**16** But when it is in its own house or the house of its exaltation while being retrograde, it is like a sick man in his own house.
[[notes: "Retrograde" refers to the optical illusion where a planet appears to move backward in the sky. It usually signifies delays, internal focus, or weakened external power.]]

**17** When it is combust in its own house, or house of exaltation, it is like a man whom his master or his king has imprisoned in his own home.
[[notes: "Combust" means the planet is so close to the Sun that its light and influence are "burned up" or hidden by the Sun's rays.]]

**18** When it is "falling," it is a man who is troubled and fearful.
[[notes: A "falling" (cadent) planet is located in a specific section of the sky that was thought to be weak or ineffective.]]

**19** A fortunate planet when it is retrograde is almost like an unfortunate one; and a fortunate planet falling from the angles or the ascendants is like a man hoping for good fortune but not finding it.
[[notes: "Fortunate" planets (benefics) are typically Jupiter and Venus. "Angles" are the strongest points in an astrological chart.]]

**20** When a fortunate planet is retrograde and is with an unfortunate one, the nature of the fortune is converted to misfortune, and the misfortune of the planet is strengthened.

**21** When an unfortunate planet is moving direct in its own house and is with a fortunate planet, it is converted from misfortune to fortune.
[[notes: "Direct" means the planet is moving forward normally, rather than retrograde.]]

**22** When a planet is in the final part of a sign, it is retreating or withdrawing.

**23** When it is in the first degree of a sign, it is of weak power in judgments and questions.

**24** From the first degree to the 15th it is approaching, but from the 15th to the 25th it is complete.

**25** If it is in the final part of a sign, it is receding, and then it is like a man leaving a house in which he has stayed.

**26** A "wild" planet in the ascendant, where it has authority, is singular in judgment and disposition.
[[notes: "Agrestis" (wild/of the field) likely refers to a planet in a sign not traditionally associated with "civilized" or human qualities.]]

**27** A planet in a house not its own is like a man knocking at a stranger's house; his judgment is suppressed, and he has no authority.

**28** When it is with the Sun, its powers are weak and its judgment is diminished.

**29** A planet existing in the final part of a sign while retrograde transmits its judgment, its light is weakened, and its brightness is taken from it.

**30** When it is in its own house while retrograde, and in the 7th degree from the Sun, it is like a man in his own house, but [[gloss: over]] over him there is a guard—namely, a man more powerful than he—and he desires to flee out of fear of him, and out of reproach and pride.

**31** A planet in the house of its enemy is like a man in the house of another between whom hatred and anger have already arisen.

**32** A planet in its own house moving direct, free from infirmity and misfortunes, signifies the [[gloss: perfection]] perfection of questions and investigations, and the fulfillment and attainment for the one asking.

**33** When the Moon is separated from the planets, it signifies things concerning the past.
[[notes: "Separation" occurs when the Moon moves away from an alignment (aspect) with another planet. This is a key technique in "Horary" astrology (answering specific questions based on the time they are asked).]]

**34** When the Moon is joined with the planets, it signifies that which is to be in the future.

**35** From the Moon separated from Saturn, there occur bindings and sorrows, the finding of evil, and downfalls.

**36** From the Moon separated from Jupiter, there occur joy and gladness, friendship, confirmation of gifts, increases in family, children, servants, and inheritances; also an addition to wealth, the multiplication of fortunes, and the dissolving of misfortune and downfall.

**37** From the Moon separated from Mars, there occur quarrels, oppositions, bad rumors, pains, bindings, deaths, the shedding of blood, false testimonies, children of fornication and of harlots, the removal of jealousy (as in the readings, the granting of what is forbidden), male intercourse, a woman in charge, the drinking of raisin wine and wine from any intoxicating thing, wounds, the cutting of children, and the preparation of syrups that make children descend from the womb to the vulva and the level ground.
[[notes: This passage links Mars to both violence and medical interventions, including those related to childbirth or the termination of pregnancy.]]

**38** From the Moon separated from the Sun, there occur illnesses, anxiety, fear, death, imprisonment, the finding of evil and disgrace, pains, downfalls, sickness, binding, captivity, horsemanship, armies, the populace, and terrible things.

**39** From the Moon separated from Venus, there occur fornications, jokes, laughter, gestures, songs, silk garments, colorings, and varieties.

**40** When the Moon has separated from Mercury, events occur according to the nature of Mercury’s **application** [[notes: "Application" refers to a planet moving toward a specific geometric relationship with another]] with a fortune or an infortune [[notes: "Fortunes" are beneficial planets like Jupiter and Venus; "Infortunes" are malefic ones like Saturn and Mars]].
**41** When the Moon is applied to any of the planets, it signifies the future according to the nature of that Moon’s **application** with those planets.
**42** If the Moon is fortunate in the morning, it is praiseworthy for whoever seeks to do business on that day, or for a birth; it will be pleasing to them and fortunate in every inquiry.
**43** If the Moon is unfortunate or corrupted in the morning, a request made on that day is not favored, and any child born then will not endure; if they do endure, they will be weak throughout their life.
**44** When the Moon is joined [[notes: "Joined" or "conjunction" means the planets are in the same degree of the zodiac]] to **Saturn**, that day is bad for every work and inquiry.
**45** When the Moon is joined to **Jupiter**, that day is good for every work and inquiry.
**46** When the Moon is joined to **Mars**, it is an unpleasant day for every work.
**47** When the Moon is joined to the **Sun**, that day is to be censured for every work, except for those things which one wishes to be hidden; if anyone should fall ill, they will die from that cause.
**48** When the Moon is joined to **Venus**, that day is pleasing for every work, especially when the inquiry concerns weddings or the return of a wayward woman [[notes: "Dissolutę" suggests a woman who has left her home or is living a scattered life]].
**49** When the Moon is joined with **Mercury**, that day is good for every work, especially to negotiate dowries, to meet with scribes and administrators; it is good to buy, sell, and calculate.
**50** When the Moon is in **opposition** [[notes: An aspect of 180 degrees, often considered tense or difficult]] to **Saturn**, the day is to be censured for every work; it is not fit to propose anything in it, nor is it profitable.
**51** When in opposition to **Jupiter**, it is a praiseworthy day for every work, especially in seeking the truth, bargaining for dowries, inquiring about agreements, imitating matters, calculating accounts for elders and administrators; going near or far is good.
**52** When it is in opposition to **Mars**, that day is worth nothing for any work.
**53** When in opposition to the **Sun**, that day is worth nothing; it is good for no work.
**54** When in opposition to **Venus**, it is a praiseworthy day for every work, especially in sexual union and the affairs of women, seeking their friendships and society; it is good for a separated woman to return, and also fit for undertaking a journey.
**55** When in opposition to **Mercury**, the day is mediocre for every work.
**56** When the Moon is in the **fourth aspect** [[notes: Also known as a "square" aspect (90 degrees), traditionally considered a challenge or obstacle]] from **Saturn**, that day is praiseworthy for every work, especially to meet with kings, princes of the realm, and nobles; it is not good for a journey in this aspect, as the departure will be ill-favored, and the sick will die on this day.
**57** When the Moon is in the fourth aspect of **Jupiter**, it is a praiseworthy day, especially in determining the truth, seeking marriage, and gaining access to nobles and those who rule the kingdom; it is good for laying foundations for buildings, and it is pleasing to go out on that day for any deed, for the doer shall rejoice.
**58** When the Moon is in the fourth aspect of **Mars**, it is ill-favored for every work, especially to meet a king or seek business; it is not good to marry then, and the sick will die, or blood or a wound shall come from it.
**59** When the Moon is in the fourth aspect of the **Sun**, the day is to be censured in every deed, especially to meet a king and nobles, or to seek what business or causes are among them.
**60** When the Moon is in the fourth aspect of **Venus**, the day is praiseworthy for every work, especially to sequester oneself with a woman, to put on new clothes, to practice noble things, for games, banquets, marriage, sexual union, the purchase of livestock or slaves, to enter the baths, to adorn oneself, or to go out seeking rest.
**61** When the Moon is in the fourth aspect of **Mercury**, it is a good day for proposing to sell or buy, to mix with kings, for the accounting of a great house or of books, and for reading books and sciences.
**62** When the Moon is in **sextile aspect** [[notes: A harmonious 60-degree aspect]] to **Saturn**, it is a good day to meet with elders and farm stewards, to look into one's causes, business, and affairs, to proceed in the arrangement of one’s things, to agree on every business being decided, and for a man’s hearing and certain friendship, and to mix with great men and be associated with their councils and other advisors.
**63** When the Moon is in sextile to **Jupiter**, it is a good day to agree in that meeting with **alcaldes** [[notes: From the Arabic "al-qāḍī," meaning a judge or magistrate]], to seek the judgment of the just, to deal with numbers and every good work, to marry, to undertake a journey, to mix with nobles and high men, to confirm great matters, to secure a kingdom, and to be present at banquets and weddings.
**64** When the Moon is in sextile to **Mars**, it is a good day; the best thing in it is to meet with leaders and providers.

**85** Saturn in the fourth from Venus, or in conjunction or opposition, completes every question in what is illicit and in disobedience; and if it should be according to a diversity of disobedience—I say, we say—it shall return, take away shame, and corrupt.
**86** Saturn in the fourth from Mercury, or in opposition or conjunction, corrupts the question, desolates business, and causes excess to overflow.

-> # THE PROPOSITIONS OF ALMANSOR. <-

**88** Jupiter in quartile [[notes: A "quartile" or square aspect occurs when planets are 90 degrees apart; it is usually considered a point of tension.]], or in opposition, or in conjunction with Saturn, prevents Saturn's corruption and turns the situation from misfortune to fortune.
**89** Jupiter in quartile, conjunction, or opposition to Mars, prohibits Mars' power of generation, corruption, and impression [[notes: "Impression" refers to the planet's ability to exert its influence on the physical world.]].
**90** Jupiter in quartile, conjunction, or opposition to Venus, signifies the fulfillment of the question and a pleasing end to the matter.
**91** Jupiter with Mercury in quartile, conjunction, or opposition, signifies the perfection of questions, the resolution of business, its completion, an increase in fortune, and good things.
**92** When a misfortune [[notes: An "infortuna" or malefic planet, typically Saturn or Mars.]] is in the ascendant [[notes: The "ascendant" is the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the query.]], but a fortune [[notes: A "fortuna" or benefic planet, typically Jupiter or Venus.]] is in the second house, the seeker will change from misfortune to fortune.
**93** When a fortune is in the ascendant and a misfortune is in the second house, the question will change from fortune to misfortune.
**94** When a strong planet is in the ascendant and another planet is in one of the angles [[notes: The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful positions in a chart.]], the question will change from fortune to misfortune.
**95** When the lord of the ascendant is in the *via combusta* [[notes: The "Burnt Way," a specific section of the zodiac (traditionally the end of Libra and beginning of Scorpio) considered highly unlucky.]], the business and the request will be ruined.
**96** When a misfortune is in the tenth or fourth house from the ascendant, hearts will tremble, misfortune will happen, and the question will be denied and fall away.
**97** When a misfortune is in the ascendant and a fortune is in the second house, the question will be fulfilled, and the business will be finished with joy and famous profit.
**98** When a misfortune is in the ascendant and a misfortune is in the second house, the question will fail and proceed toward misfortune.
**99** When the ascendant is decreasing in ascensions [[notes: This refers to "signs of short ascension," which rise more quickly over the horizon, often implying haste or instability.]], and its lord is in a descending place in the 6th or 12th house, the seeker will hope for things they will not obtain; and when a fortune is in the 3rd from the ascendant, and a misfortune is in the ascendant, the seeker will apply little effort to the business.
**100** When a planet occurs that loses its time of ascension, the seeker will encounter misfortune at the end of their business, even after its determination and attainment.

When a misfortune is in the angles and "received" [[notes: "Reception" is a dignifying relationship where one planet is in a sign governed by another.]], it will grant and apply the seeker's business; nevertheless, it will take back what it gave. The knowledge of reception is this: when a planet is in its own house or the house of its exaltation, safe from misfortune.

-> ## THE PROPOSITIONS OF ALMANSOR THE ASTROLOGER, <-
-> ### TO THE KING OF THE SARACENS. <-

[[insert: A]] short compendium of aphorisms you requested of me, my king; that I might satisfy your wishes, I have by no means refused to undergo the labor. I have written them; I ask that you receive them with a favorable mind.
**1** Regarding the disposition of the signs, let us begin with Aries: one sign is diurnal (of the day), another is nocturnal (of the night); one is masculine, another feminine; one is light, another heavy.
**2** The exaltation [[notes: A sign where a planet's influence is most harmoniously strengthened.]] of any of the seven planets is said to be in that place where it is substantially the opposite of another. For example, the Sun's exaltation is in Aries, which is the "fall" [[notes: The "fall" is the sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where its influence is weakened.]] of Saturn. For the Sun possesses clarity, while Saturn possesses darkness. Likewise, Jupiter's is in Cancer, where Mars falls; one of these desires justice, while the other signifies injustice. So too Mercury in Virgo, which is the fall of Venus; for one signifies knowledge and philosophy, while the other causes merriment and whatever is flavorful to the body.
**3** The significance of the parts of the circle [[notes: The Zodiac circle.]], O great king, is singular: just as a sign of the fiery part signifies fire, the earthy signifies earth, the airy signifies air, and the aquatic signifies water.
**4** Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius make up the hot, dry, bitter, fiery, diurnal, and masculine triplicity [[notes: A "triplicity" is a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element.]]...

The text focuses on the "triplicities" of the zodiac signs and specific planetary placements that determine health, character, and destiny.]]

-># PROPOSITIONS<-

[[notes: This section begins mid-sentence, concluding a description of the first triplicity (Fire signs: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius).]]
...masculine, and signifies red choler [[notes: Choler, or yellow bile, was one of the four "humors" in ancient medicine, associated with a fiery, irascible temperament]]. Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn are the earthy triplicity: cold, dry, nocturnal, feminine, and signify black choler [[notes: Associated with melancholy]]. Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are the airy triplicity: hot, moist, sanguine [[notes: Associated with the humor of blood and a cheerful disposition]], sweet, and diurnal.
**4** Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are the aquatic triplicity: cold, moist, phlegmatic [[notes: Associated with the humor of phlegm]], insipid, and nocturnal.
**5** The "Fortunes" [[notes: Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring good luck]] are generous and faithful. The "Infortunes" [[notes: Malefic planets, usually Saturn and Mars, thought to bring hardship]] are truly greedy and unfaithful.
**6** The Fortunes will grant things to a person without labor. The Infortunes, however, will shorten and take away whatever they give.
**7** When two Infortunes are joined together, a "perfect fortune" results from them, just as from a conjunction of two Fortunes; this is according to the sayings of Ptolemy [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy was the most influential astronomer and geographer of antiquity]].
**8** Of all planetary aspects [[notes: The geometric angles between planets]], the trine and sextile are better. The square and opposition are truly worse.
**9** The trine and sextile aspects of Infortunes do not benefit, just as the square and opposition of Fortunes do not cause harm.
**10** From many significations of life in the *hyleg* [[notes: The *hyleg* is the "giver of life," a specific point or planet in a birth chart used to determine longevity]], many years, a long life, a pure intellect, and the greatest vigor are signified.
**11** Whoever has Mercury in the *radix* [[notes: The "root" or original natal chart]] of their birth in the house of Mars will be prone to evil suspicion and hasty in their business.
**12** Whoever has Mercury in the *radix* of their birth in the house of Saturn will be of great intellect and long reflection—a wise man and a philosopher.
**13** He whose "lord of birth" [[notes: The planet ruling the sign on the horizon at the moment of birth]] is Jupiter shall never be poor or needy.
**14** Whoever has Infortunes in the Ascendant [[notes: The sign rising on the eastern horizon]] shall suffer a foul mark upon their face.
**15** His eyes cannot escape a heavy impediment whose "two luminaries" [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]] were both afflicted or "impeded" at birth.
**16** He will not lose his senses in whose birth the Moon was moving toward Mercury.
**17** When Fortunes preside over a birth, the child will be generous and lovable. If, however, Infortunes preside, he will be greedy and abhorrent.
**18** He whom Saturn presides over at birth will be filthy, and he whom Mars presides over will be foul-smelling.
**19** In whosever birth there are Infortunes in the eighth house [[notes: Traditionally the house of death]], they shall die a "bad death." But if Fortunes are in that same place, they shall pass away in their own bed.
**20** One will not gather money nor store up treasure unless the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the fourth house are the same planet; likewise, one will not gain money or riches, nor live splendidly, unless the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the tenth house are the same.
**21** Affection cannot exist between two people unless the luminaries are "commuted" in their birth charts—that is, the Sun or Moon of one is in the place of the Sun or Moon in the partner's chart. Truly, those are hateful to each other who are born when these points are in opposition, or in opposing signs, or in "square" aspects.
**22** The lord of the fifth circle, namely Venus, signifies moisture and rains, just as the lord of the sixth, namely Mercury, signifies journeys, changes, and pilgrimages.
**23** He who approaches a King while the Moon is in Aquarius will neither be received nor cared for by the King in any way. If he approaches him while she is in Pisces, the King will turn his face away from him.
**24** It is not good to perform bloodletting [[notes: *Minutio sanguinis*, a common medical practice of the era]] when the Moon is in Gemini, nor is it suitable to use cupping glasses when the Moon is in Taurus.
**25** The best signs for taking laxatives and purgatives are the aquatic signs; of these, Scorpio is considered the best, and Cancer the worst.
**26** The better sign for partnerships is Leo; the worse is Aries.
**27** The fixed stars give grand gifts and lift one from poverty to a high status, which the seven planets alone do not do.
**28** He will be a perfect physician who has Mars and Venus in the sixth house. He will be a good singer who has Mercury retrograde with Venus in the same sign.

-> ### THE APHORISMS OF ALMANSOR. <-
[[page number: 95]]

**29** The Lord of the fifth circle, namely Venus [[notes: In the Ptolemaic system, the "circles" or spheres are numbered from the outermost (Saturn) to the innermost (Moon). Venus is the fifth sphere.]], when she is in the first degree of Cancer, will bring rains.
**30** When the heavy planets [[notes: "Heavy" or "ponderous" planets are the slower-moving outer planets, Saturn and Jupiter.]] are occidental to the Sun [[notes: "Occidental" means setting after the Sun, which was traditionally thought to weaken their influence.]], they grant uprightness toward the end of life, and vice versa.
**31** Whoever buys something while the Moon is between the start of Cancer and the end of Sagittarius will buy at a high price and sell cheaply; however, it is the reverse when the Moon is from the beginning of Capricorn to the end of Gemini.
**32** Circumcision is not good when the Moon is in Scorpio, just as purging [[notes: *Vomitus* refers to the medical practice of inducing vomiting or purging to balance the humors.]] is not good when the Moon is in Leo.
**33** The nature of the sign in which Venus is found will be attributed to the person born under it: for when she is in Leo, she gives love; in Taurus, songs; and in Scorpio, sexual intercourse. The reason is that Leo governs the heart, Taurus the throat and neck, and Scorpio the genitals.
**34** To whomsoever Mercury is in the twelfth house, that person will be wise and a great philosopher.
**35** When the Moon is afflicted [[notes: "Impedited" or afflicted means the planet is in a poor position or negatively influenced by a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars.]] in the birth chart, and all the lords of the triplicities [[notes: Triplicities are groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).]] have fallen—
[[notes: A small character resembling a '5' or 's' appears at the start of the next line, likely a printer's mark or stray glyph.]]
5 particularly the first lord of the triplicity of the ascendant—and it is in one of the angles [[notes: The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful positions in a chart.]] with a fortune [[notes: A "fortune" is a benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus.]], it indicates a short life for the native.
**36** The Lord of the fifth circle, namely Venus, dissolves what the lord of the third binds, which is Mars. However, the lord of the second, namely Jupiter, dissolves what the lord of the first binds, namely Saturn; and this significance applies to great matters.
**37** When all the lords of the triplicities have fallen, but one of the fixed stars of the first or second magnitude of exaltation is in one of the angles—being of the same nature as the lords of the triplicities—the native's upbringing will be completed, and they will surpass it.
**38** The harm that falls upon the Moon from the malice of Mars when she is increasing in light is equal to the harm that falls upon her from the malice of Saturn when she is decreasing in light. This chapter, moreover, signifies great matters, nor will they be known to be of heretics, except by the lord of the second circle [[notes: Jupiter]]. And the lord of the fourth circle [[notes: The Sun]] signifies kings.
[[notes: 'quati' is likely a typo in the original for 'quarti' (fourth).]]
**39** In the elections [[notes: "Elections" are charts cast to choose an auspicious time for an event.]] of kings, the signs of the higher planets are commended, just as in the elections of the powerless, the signs of the lower planets are commended.
**40** Those things which indicate a higher fortune are Jupiter, the Part of Fortune, the Part of Giving, the second house (and whoever is in it and its lord), also the lord of the triplicity of the luminary [[notes: The Sun or Moon]] which holds authority, as well as the lord of the tenth house and whoever is within it.
**41** When the significator is between the ascendant and the tenth house, the timing will be in days and hours; when between the tenth and seventh, it will be weeks and months; but when it is between the seventh and fourth, it will be years.
**42** The Lord of the first circle, namely Saturn, when he is in fixed signs, causes mortality and famine; the wise have experienced this to be true.
**43** When you wish to choose a time for someone and you cannot delay, if the Moon is afflicted, place the afflicting planet as the lord of the ascendant.
**44** The best *istisal* [[notes: 'istisal' refers to the astrological concept of 'ittisal' (application), where a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one.]] is in longitude and latitude: the fortunes [[notes: Benefic planets]] strengthen the nature of good and weaken the nature of evil, while the infortunes [[notes: Malefic planets]] do the opposite.
**45** Whichever planet's nature is superior, its action will not cease until its contrary appears in that same place.
**46** When you cannot delay an election, you should place the ascendant and its lord in safety; also, place the names of the fortunes in an angle, and ideally in the tenth house. Mars does no harm in travels across water, just as Saturn does no harm in travels across land.
**47** In journeys, fixed signs are criticized, while movable signs are commended.
**48** When an infortune [[notes: A malefic planet]] aspects the significator while being retrograde and "falling" [[notes: In a cadent house, which is weak.]], and also in a place where it is peregrine [[notes: Having no essential dignity or "standing" in that sign.]], that is, in none of its dignities and in a sign contrary to its nature, it brings an evil upon the significator that no one can cure, except God alone.
**49** When Mars approaches the earth, he shall be at peace with Jupiter; Saturn likewise shall be at peace with Venus; and the Moon when she approaches the earth—this is the rising of two parts into one part.
**50** The Moon accords with the Sun when she is increased in light and number; every luminous star also accords with him.
**51** When Mars is weakened, Venus is strengthened, just as when Saturn is weak, Jupiter's

-> ## PROPOSITIONS <-

...the malice of the ill-fortunes [[notes: *Infortunae*, referring to the malefic planets Saturn and Mars]], when it exists in any of their dignities [[notes: "Dignities" are signs where a planet is particularly strong, like its "home" or "exaltation"]], and vice-versa.

**52** When an ill-fortune "receives" a good-fortune [[notes: "Reception" occurs when one planet is in a sign ruled by another; "good-fortunes" or *fortunae* are Jupiter and Venus]], it will not hinder it, especially when it does not aspect it from the fourth or the opposite [[notes: The square (90°) or opposition (180°) aspects, considered difficult or tense]], nor is in the same sign. The greatest impediment of the planets is when they are in "peregrine" places [[notes: A planet is "peregrine" when it is in a part of the zodiac where it has no traditional dignity, making it weak or wandering]].

**53** Every planet, when it is joined to the Sun at the exact same point [[notes: A state known as *cazimi*, or being in the heart of the Sun]], will move swiftly; but as it approaches him, it will move slowly.

**54** The application [[notes: Translating *ictisal*, a term from Arabic astrology referring to the "hitting" or coming together of two planets]] of the Moon to a planet is a stronger testimony than if it were in the *Medium Coeli* [[notes: The Midheaven, or 10th house of career]] or in the Ascendant [[notes: The 1st house of the self and the body]].

**55** Cancer is the significator over very moving waters; Scorpio, however, is over the flowing waters of rivers; Pisces likewise is over still waters, namely, such as pools and wells.

**56** Every matter which is quickly made, and quickly destroyed, and which is repeated, is under the significance of Mars.

**57** Everything that is quickly made and suddenly destroyed, and remains destroyed for a long time, is of the nature of Saturn and Mars.

**58** Whoever is of royal lineage, if in the root of their birth [[notes: The *radix*, or natal chart]] there are "two Suns" [[notes: This may refer to the Sun being in high dignity or reinforced by a specific planetary ruler]], he will be contrary to kings and will be separated from them in his deeds.

**59** To whomever the Moon is in Taurus at the minute of ascension at the hour of birth, and the Sun in Leo in the Ascendant at the minute of ascension, he shall arrive at great exaltation.

**60** Those things which happen in this world are known and investigated from the great strength of the superior significator and from its elevation; and if that is not present, it is sought from the planet toward which all other planets are moving.

**61** If any of the planets signified something in the root of birth, when the "division" [[notes: A method of timing events, often called "distributions"]] and its lord reach it, its significance will appear, whether it be good or evil.

**62** When the Lord of the 10th [House] moves retrograde away from the application [[notes: *ictisal*]] of the Lord of the Ascendant, the native [[notes: The person for whom the chart is cast]] will not be received by his lord; [but] when the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the Ascendant, and the two good-fortunes [[notes: Jupiter and Venus]] likewise behold each other, the native will be very strong and powerful, and no one shall bypass his command.

**63** From the degree of the Ascendant, the "accidents" [[notes: External events or physical traits]] of the body are known; from the degree of the Part of Fortune, the state of substance [[notes: Wealth]]. From the degree of the Moon, the state of the body and soul is perceived. From the degree of the Sun, his health; but from the degree of the *Medium Coeli* [[notes: Midheaven]], his mastery and works are distinguished. Give one year to each degree.

**64** He shall be fortunate, and of good being, and also powerful, whose year of revolution [[notes: The "Solar Return," a chart cast for one's birthday each year]] is similar to the root [natal chart], and whose circle is in the same likeness as the root was in that year.

**65** The daily state of the native is taken from the "direction" [[notes: A timing technique moving planets forward in the chart]]; otherwise from the motion of the Lord; otherwise, the day-to-day state of the native is taken from the motion of the Lord of the sign of the year's "profection" [[notes: Moving the chart forward one sign per year of life]] in the "bounds" [[notes: *termini*, or sub-divisions of a sign]] set forth by the Lord of the sign of the *alynthia* [[notes: Likely a technical term for a specific planetary ruler or period, possibly a corruption of *almugea* or *almuten*]] of the year to the bounds set forth.

**66** When Saturn ascends in the higher part of its circle—that is, in its apogee [[notes: The point where a planet is furthest from Earth]]—and the Moon joins the Sun at the end of the month, and she moves toward him [Saturn], it shall signify an increase of the thing which is of the nature of the sign in which he resides.

**67** When a planet is in the very minute of the eastern degree [[notes: Exactly on the Ascendant horizon]], and the Moon is joined to it in the same place, the action of that planet’s nature will appear, whether it be good or evil.

**68** When any planet shall rule any year (of the years of the world), its significance will appear in the very degree of its exaltation, and the king shall be elevated in that region and climate which is signified by it.

**69** An affliction [[notes: *Impedimentum*]] of Mercury by Saturn is bound to impede the tongue of the native; it is worse, however, if they are joined bodily [[notes: In a conjunction]].

**70** How great will be the fear for the sick person when the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon]] are below the earth at the hour of the interrogation [[notes: The time a question is asked in a "Horary" reading]].

**71** When both luminaries are in the same degree of their exaltation in their own dominion, free from ill-fortunes, the native will be the king of the whole world, and his seed shall inherit his lands and hold them for a long time.

**72** When the Ascendant of any birth is the *Medium Coeli* of the world [[notes: Referring to the start of the zodiac at Aries]], and it is a moveable sign—namely Aries or Cancer—and that degree which is upon the line of the *Medium Coeli* is the same degree,

It emphasizes the roles of the Sun, Moon, and "ill-fortunes" (Saturn and Mars) in determining a person's fate or the outcome of a year.]]

The text focuses on "interrogations" and "nativity" (birth charts), providing specific rules for predicting fame, health, war, and weather based on planetary positions.]]

the degree in which the Sun or Jupiter is exalted, his name shall be spread throughout the whole world, and his fame shall be broadcast. [[notes: "Exaltation" is a specific sign in the zodiac where a planet is thought to have its most potent or "noble" influence.]]
**73** These are the things which are to be prepared, or from which a judgment can be fashioned: namely, the Ascendant, the Part of Fortune, the Luminaries, the sign of the conjunction, and their lords, the sign of the lord, the hours, and also the location of the thing being sought, and its lord. [[notes: The "Luminaries" are the Sun and Moon. The "Part of Fortune" is a mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity.]]
**74** From the lord of the exaltation and the "divisor," as well as the lord of the other divisors of the rays, and from the lord of the year, and also from the movement of the planets into different places and their aspects, the events of the world are known during the revolutions of the years. [[notes: "Aspects" are specific angular relationships between planets, like 90 or 180 degrees, which astrologers believe trigger events.]]
**75** When the lord of the 10th house is in the 8th, it is to be feared that the mother of the child born from that birth will die. [[notes: In this specific tradition, the 10th house relates to the mother, while the 8th house is the house of death.]]
**77** When the lord of the 4th house is hindered by the lord of the Ascendant, there shall be fear for the father of the child. [[notes: The original text repeats the number 77 twice; the 4th house traditionally represents the father.]]
**77** Nothing benefits a warrior when the lord of the Ascendant is in a "fortune" but is retrograde, or "under the rays"; similarly, if he is with the 7th house or its lord, the one who first began the fight will prevail in battle. [[notes: "Retrograde" means a planet appears to move backward; "under the rays" means it is too close to the Sun to be seen, both considered signs of weakness.]]
**78** An "infortune" heats and hinders its own place; however, the Sun heats but does not hinder. [[notes: An "infortune" or "malefic" refers to Saturn or Mars, planets traditionally associated with hardship.]]
**79** Beware that you do not go out to battle when the lord of the Ascendant is moving toward the lord of the 7th.
**80** When Mars is with the Sun in Northern signs, there will be the greatest heat; likewise, when the Sun goes toward Saturn in Southern signs, there will be the greatest cold, and vice versa. [[notes: Northern signs are Aries through Virgo; Southern signs are Libra through Pisces.]]
**81** When the "infortunes" reach a favorable place, they will not do harm if their influence was not present in the original birth chart; likewise, the "fortunes" will not be profitable when there is no indication of them in the root of the birth. [[notes: This emphasizes that a planet's current movement (transit) can only trigger what is already promised in a person's birth chart (the "radix").]]
**82** Obstacles which are to come will happen in the "alynthæ" years, when the year of the world reaches the bodies of the malefics; give one year to each sign. [[notes: "Alynthæ" likely refers to "annos halica," a Latinization of an Arabic term for dangerous or climacteric years in a person's life.]]
**83** The greatest misfortune of Saturn is when it is in feminine signs, but for Mars, it is when it is in masculine signs.
**84** No one ought to attack a city whose lord is the lord of the Ascendant of the year of the world.
**85** It is necessary in every beginning to adapt the circle to the nature of that which someone is about to begin. [[notes: The "circle" refers to the horoscope or celestial map.]]
**86** The *ictisal* of the Moon to Mars from the houses of Venus is not recommended, nor to Jupiter from the houses of Saturn and Mercury, nor to the Sun from the houses of Saturn. [[notes: *Ictisal* is a technical term from Arabic astrology meaning "application," or the movement of a faster planet toward a slower one.]]
**87** It is among the greater fortunes when the day-planets are oriental of the Sun and in masculine signs, and the night-planets are occidental of the Moon. [[notes: "Oriental" and "Occidental" refer to whether a planet rises before or after the Sun/Moon.]]
**88** When the lords of the triplicity of the luminary of the day are diurnal and oriental, and the lords of the triplicity of the night are occidental and increased in light, it will be the greatest sign of fortune and happiness.
**89** The oriental point signifies young children and the beginnings of everything; the midheaven signifies kings, lords of the law, judges, and also the masters of battles. The seventh house signifies the old and the deceased, as well as women, enemies, and everything beautiful. The angle of the earth signifies fathers and lands, and also the place where an infant is born; it also shows the hour of death and the tomb. [[notes: These are the four "Angles" of a chart: Ascendant (East), Midheaven (Top), Descendant (West), and Imum Coeli (Bottom).]]
**90** The planets that give great riches are three: namely Jupiter, the Sun, and Mercury.
**91** Every undertaking by one who possesses great wealth is terrifying in all "middle points" in which a conjunction or "prevention" is hindered; let him therefore beware of this. [[notes: "Prevention" refers to the Full Moon (opposition) occurring before a conjunction.]]
**92** A universal question is likened to a birth; therefore, revolve its years and judge upon them.
**93** Saturn rejoices in Aquarius, just as Jupiter does in Pisces; Mars also rejoices in Scorpio, just as Venus does in Libra, and Mercury in Virgo.
**94** Just as the *Geuzahar* adds to the nature of every planet that is with it, so the Tail subtracts from the nature of every planet that is with it. [[notes: *Geuzahar* is the Dragon’s Head or North Node of the Moon; the Tail is the South Node. They were thought to amplify or diminish a planet's power.]]
**95** The strongest indication regarding the father's existence is the firstborn; those who follow will likewise give some indication.
**96** The *Algebuthar* is stronger in matters of life, but the *Alcocoden* is stronger in other things. [[notes: *Algebuthar* and *Alcocoden* are Arabic-derived terms for specific planets that "rule" a chart and are used to calculate the length of a person's life.]]

[[meta: This page continues a series of astrological aphorisms or 'propositions' likely derived from a mix of Arabic and Classical sources. The numbering suggests this is part of a larger compendium of judicial astrology, focusing here on kingship, wealth, and the timing of events.]]

# ->PROPOSITIONS<-

**96** The less of the rays is stronger than the *algebuthas* [[notes: An obscure term likely derived from the Arabic *al-mubattiz*, referring to a planet with the most dignity or "victor" of the chart]], and perhaps both are strong.
**97** When a newborn dies before one day and one night have passed, it is like a miscarriage, and it shall have no significance in any matter [[notes: This implies that no birth chart or "nativity" is calculated for infants who do not survive their first twenty-four hours]].
**98** Kings whose affairs are conducted quickly, and who avenge themselves quickly, and who also quickly achieve what they desire, are those for whom the Ascendant [[notes: The sign rising on the eastern horizon]] at the beginning of their reign was a fire sign, and likewise the Midheaven [[notes: The highest point of the zodiac at that moment]], or if one was fire and the other was air.
**99** When the lord of the Ascendant is in a good place, in the "terms" [[notes: Specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet]] of the fortunes [[notes: The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus]], and the lord of that term is of good condition, being joined to it, it will grant integrity, kingship, and every good thing.
**100** When the significator is in the Midheaven, it shall be directed by the ascension of the direct circle. In the Ascendant, however, by the ascensions of the region; but in that which is between both, by both; Alchindus [[notes: Al-Kindi, a 9th-century polymath known as the 'Philosopher of the Arabs']] indeed described this chapter.
**101** The cause of fortune and prosperity is that the lord of the house of the Sun, the lord of the house of the Moon, and the lord of the Ascendant are "oriental" [[notes: Rising before the Sun in the morning]], and in "angles" [[notes: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions]], and look upon one another from good places—that is, from a trine or sextile aspect [[notes: Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees]].
**102** He is very powerful whose Sun is in the Midheaven in a fire sign, and the Moon is in Taurus, and her aspect is "sinister" [[notes: An aspect cast 'to the left' or following the natural order of the signs, traditionally considered more forceful]].
**103** Those who will be very rich and abound in wealth, and are of great name, are those whose lord of the second house [[notes: The house governing personal finances and possessions]] is in its exaltation or its own house, moving toward the lord of the Ascendant, especially if it is Jupiter.
**104** The life of all living creatures is according to the degree of the Sun and Moon, and this is given by the Most High according to Astapham [[notes: Likely a corruption of an Arabic astronomical authority or a specific planetary configuration]].
**105** When a "fortune" [[notes: A lucky planet]] is in the places of Mars, and the significator goes toward it, or it toward the significator, it will cut off [[notes: "Abscission" or the cutting off of light/influence]] just like a "malefic" planet.
**106** Turn your eyes away from a figure in which Mars is in an angle, especially when the Ascendant is Scorpio.
**107** When someone wishes to withdraw or take something away, while the significator is aspecting Saturn, he will withdraw it with great difficulty.
**108** If anyone should petition for something while the Head [[notes: *Caput Draconis* or the North Node of the Moon, considered increasing and beneficial]] is in the Midheaven with Jupiter, and the Moon is moving toward him, or if—having separated from him—she goes to the lord of the Ascendant, or if the lord of the Ascendant goes toward him, it will not fail but that he shall quickly obtain what is sought.
**109** It is not good for one wishing to go to war, nor even for a king, to make a journey when the lord of the Ascendant is in the eighth house [[notes: The house associated with death and loss]], even if it is in its own exaltation.
**110** The Sun is not good in the Ascendant at the hour of war, nor with the lord of the Ascendant, unless the Ascendant is Aries or Leo [[notes: The signs where the Sun has the most dignity, being its exaltation and home sign respectively]].
**111** In 그 part in which the Sun and Moon are made fortunate, there will be victory for those asking questions; for example, if they are made fortunate from the Ascendant to the Midheaven, or from the Ascendant to the fourth house, the seeker wins; if they are in other places, the adversary will prevail.
**112** There must be a very great hindrance of things which are in the power of a sign in which a planet is "cadent" [[notes: Falling away from an angle, a weak position]], or retrograde, or in a bad state regarding the Sun.
**113** The signs signify bodies, but the planets signify those things which move the bodies; the places of the planets in the circle and their substances, and their places relative to the Sun, signify work and destruction.
**114** In whosever birth Jupiter is the receiver of the strengths of all the planets, and he himself commits them and his own to Saturn, and is received by him, and both are "oriental" and rising in an angle, the native shall be great and powerful in this world, and of good character; his name shall also rise throughout the earth.
**115** Beware lest Saturn be with the lord of the Ascendant, or in other elevated places, because he himself is worse than the Tail [[notes: *Cauda Draconis* or the South Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with decrease and misfortune]].
**116** Rumors are true if, at the hour of the news, the angles are "fixed" signs [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius]], and the Moon and Mercury are in fixed signs; and if the Moon is also separated from the fortunes, and a fortune is in any of the angles; when you find it so, this indication can neither deceive nor be deceived.

[[meta: This page continues a series of astrological and medical aphorisms attributed to "Almansor" (the Latinized name of the scholar Yahya ibn Abi Mansur). The text focuses on "mundane astrology"—the prediction of world events—and "natal astrology," which concerns the character and fate of individuals based on their birth charts.]]

[[page number: 109]]

-># THE APHORISMS OF ALMANSOR<-

**117** From the first hour of the day until the completion of three hours, the time belongs to the **blood**. The next three hours belong to **red bile**, the third three to **black bile**, and the final three to **phlegm**; it is the same during the night [[notes: This refers to the four "humors" of ancient medicine, which were thought to regulate health and temperament in cycles throughout the day]]. In the same way, this pattern applies to the quarters of the lunar month. The quarters of the year, however, belong to the **Sun**.

**118** He whose **Lord of the Ascendant** [[notes: The planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth]] is to the right of the Sun and elevated above it—that is, if it leads the Sun and is in its "oriental" phase—will be a friend to kings and powerful men, as well as wealthy and famous.

**119** Do not be in a hurry to pass judgment when planets are joined together (*in conjunction*) until you first consider the nature of the **sign** in which they are joined. See whether the sign matches their own nature or not; for if the sign is similar to them, it will strengthen their influence.

**120** When the lord of the 11th house of the Ascendant, or of the 11th house of the **Moon**, or of the 11th house of the **Part of Fortune** [[notes: An Arabic part or mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity]] is surrounded by **benefics** [[notes: "Fortunas"—lucky planets like Jupiter and Venus]], that person will be more fortunate than any other.

**121** When two **malefics** [[notes: "Infortunæ"—unlucky planets like Saturn and Mars]] are in the degree of the **fourth house** (the bottom of heaven), and in that same boundary, the person born will be unfortunate and truly miserable.

**122** When planets are in the **angles** [[notes: The four most powerful points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses]], the things they signify will manifest clearly, whether they be good or bad. The significance of the lord of the fourth circle is a year, but the seventh circle is a month.

**123** When the angles of the Ascendant are in **moveable signs** [[notes: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn—signs that mark the start of seasons and signify change]] and two malefics are in the angles, the entire life of the person born will be miserable.

**124** When the **Moon** is in the angles, she will strengthen her entire influence, especially if she has any authority in the Ascendant.

**125** A swift change cannot happen except through **Mars**, just as a long delay cannot happen except through **Saturn**.

**126** The state of all good things changes from good to bad, or from bad to good, when the signs and configurations of the planets change—specifically those that signify their movement from **ascent to descent** [[notes: Their rising or falling in power and visibility]] and vice versa.

**127** **Jupiter** and **Saturn** change and overturn affairs; the beginning of a variation occurs when they move from one **triplicity** [[notes: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, such as Fire or Earth]] to another in their conjunctions, or from one figure to another.

**128** The two best conjunctions are: one involving the **Luminaries** [[notes: The Sun and Moon]], and the other involving the two **heavy planets** [[notes: Saturn and Jupiter, the slowest-moving planets known at the time]]. Masculine planets are those that act; feminine planets are those acted upon; the same applies to the signs.

**129** Observe the **ascent** of a planet and the degree of its **exaltation** [[notes: The specific sign where a planet's power is most heightened]], as well as the degree of its **fall**; for these are the things that signify men and their works.

**130** If you find a masculine **significator** in a masculine sign in the angles, and the significator of an opponent is feminine in a feminine sign, the one whose sign and planet are masculine will act upon—that is, conquer—the other.

**131** Significance is of two kinds: **substantial** and **accidental**. In both ways, they signify the number of the seven planets.

**132** When two malefics are joined, and the Moon is with **Saturn** in latitude [[notes: Referring to the planet's vertical distance from the ecliptic]], there will be famine and death. If she is with **Mars**, kings will be overthrown, and there will be much bloodshed and battle in the place signified by that sign; and this does not fail.

**133** From the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter in **moveable signs**, a change in the state of the world will be known; and likewise from their conjunctions in **fixed signs**.

**134** When two benefics are joined, and the Moon is joined to **Jupiter** in latitude, there will be justice, and peace will be established on earth. If she is joined to **Venus**, there will be liveliness, joy, health of the body, and prosperity.

**135** When **Venus** and **Mars** are at the same point with the **Sun** in the place and "term" of Venus, the words of the person born will be accepted by men and rejected by no one.

**136** A hermit or a prophet, or one whose words are always received, is he in whose nativity **Jupiter** and **Venus** are in the same degree as the **Sun**.

**137** Famous kings in this age, whose commands are not despised, are those for whom **Jupiter** and the **Moon** are at the same point of the Ascendant at their **peak** [[notes: "Augem," meaning their point of greatest influence or highest altitude]].

It concludes the 150 aphorisms and begins a practical guide to "Planetary Hours," a system used to determine the best time for specific activities based on which planet rules the hour.]]

-> **B E T H E M** <-

**138** He who possesses the greatest vigor and power is the one for whom the Sun is in the Midheaven [[notes: the highest point of the chart, representing career and public life]] with Saturn in a masculine, oriental sign.
**139** When the Moon and the other significators [[notes: the planets representing the person or the subject of the inquiry]] are removed from the "angles" [[notes: the four most powerful points in a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli]], the matters themselves will not be completed, unless it be by means of travel, and not otherwise.
**140** When there is no *istisal* [[notes: an Arabic astrological term meaning "application," or when a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one]] aspect between any of the planets and the significator, but both are in the same circle, or in parallel circles at the *nadir* [[notes: the point directly below the observer]] or *anahat* [[notes: a point related to the horizon or altitude in medieval instruments]], or on the equinoctial path, this shall be better than an *istisal* aspect.
**141** Every planet possesses two signs as its homes, except for the luminaries [[notes: the Sun and Moon]], each of which has only one house, because their light is the opposite of Saturn’s darkness; therefore, their houses are placed in opposition to his.
**142** The "Fortunes" [[notes: the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus]] are faithful and prosperous when they are in their places of exaltation and moving "direct" [[notes: moving forward through the zodiac, rather than appearing to move backward in "retrograde"]], and also when they are increasing in light.
**143** In matters of great and exalted wealth or for new beginnings, it is praised to have the luminaries in the "terms" [[notes: specific degrees of a sign ruled by a particular planet]] of the Fortunes, beholding one another, and that the lords of those terms be of the same nature as the matter being started.
**144** The matters of the great cycle, which embrace all things and are the greatest, are seven—namely, the beginning of the creation of men, and the "Great Years" of the Sun, which are 1413 years [[notes: a reference to long-term historical cycles used in mundane astrology]]. Furthermore, when some beginning arises in the "term" of the Ascendant of any inception’s root, two minutes of the two heavy planets [[notes: Saturn and Jupiter]] will be found there. This is the science of the hour of the year in which they join in the signs: the Ascendant of the revolution of the world, the Ascendant of the conjunction or prevention, which also occurs in the hour of birth or of a question.
**145** Good or evil will not happen to anyone unless there is a change in the nature or the likeness of the "triplicity" [[notes: the grouping of signs by element—Fire, Earth, Air, Water]] of the signs of the planets, which are the significators of that place.
**146** When the "climates" [[notes: geographical zones of the Earth]] differ, the aspect of the planets and their rays also differ.
**147** Indeed, when the two latitudes differ, the circles of their circular motion differ. In this chapter, however, no one has spoken so perfectly.
**148** The obstructions of the two nodes [[notes: the North and South nodes of the Moon, often called the Dragon's Head and Tail]] are worse for the "inferior" planets [[notes: those closer to Earth: Moon, Mercury, Venus]] than for the "superior" ones [[notes: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn]].
**149** The figure of the circle [[notes: the astrological chart cast]] for questions of great similarity is like the likeness of the soul of the person asking the question.
**150** When Jupiter is in Aries moving direct, without any bad aspect from the Fortunes, it shall give strength and a kingdom in which no injustice will be committed.

# -> BETHEM ON THE HOURS <-
## -> O F  T H E  P L A N E T S. <-
### -> *Concerning the hour of Saturn.* <-

[[insert: Decorative woodcut initial 'C' depicting a crescent moon and stars in a night sky, framed by foliage.]] **W**hen it is the hour of Saturn, it is good to buy things of a heavy nature, such as iron, tin, lead, and all metals, as well as stone and black cloths. It is also good to begin digging gardens and to devise frauds against enemies. However, it is not good to undergo bloodletting, nor to take medicine, nor to speak to a person of power, nor to a prelate, a monk, a hypocrite, a fisherman, or a hunter. Do not speak to any friend, nor construct or build any wall. Indeed, it is not good for any man to begin anything, nor to form any partnership, nor to take a wife (for they will never be in harmony), nor to cut cloth, nor to put on new clothes.

### -> *Concerning the hour of Jupiter.* <-
In the hour of Jupiter, it is good to buy and exchange silver, and to handle all business pertaining to silver. It is good to trade azure-colored cloths, and to begin bridges and houses for the purpose of prayer. It is also good to begin a journey for the sake of the Lord, or even for the sake of business or seafaring. It is good to take medicine and to undergo bloodletting. It is a good time to speak of harmony, peace, friendship, and power, and to buy chestnut-colored horses and weapons of steel [[notes: Latin *azaro*, likely referring to *aciarium* or steel]]. It is good to set up looms for weaving, to plow the field, to sow seeds, to dig a well, and to construct or build a wall. Why say more? It is good to begin all good works in the hour of Jupiter.

->centered text<-
# ON THE HOURS OF THE PLANETS
[[page number: 111]]

->centered text<-
### *On the hour of Mars.*
In the hour of Mars, it is good to buy weapons and horses to be shod [[notes: "ferrandos" refers to fitting horses with shoes, a task associated with Mars's metal, iron]], and all horses suitable for war, to arm helmets, to begin a journey for the sake of war whether by land or by sea, and to buy all cloths of a red color. It is not good, however, to take medicine or to undergo bloodletting [[notes: "sanguinem minuere," literally to diminish the blood, was a standard medical treatment believed to balance the humors]]. To begin a journey for the sake of any business is not good. Furthermore, all works pertaining to fire are good, such as those of smiths, cooks, bakers, and kiln-workers. As we said regarding the hour of Saturn, it is not good to enter into a partnership, nor to confirm a wife or lead her in marriage.

->centered text<-
### *On the hour of the Sun.*
In the hour of the Sun, it is good to buy gold and all things of a golden color, and "golden" horses [[notes: likely referring to chestnuts or palominos]]. It is best in this hour to speak to a king and to all powerful men. It is good for authorities to begin a journey for the sake of war and to begin a battle. It is good to trade in cloths of a saffron color [[notes: "crocei coloris," a deep yellow-orange]]. As for taking medicine, bloodletting, beginning a journey for business, leading a wife, or entering into a partnership, to do or contract these things is neither good nor bad.

->centered text<-
### *On the hour of Venus.*
In the hour of Venus, it is good to buy women [[notes: in this historical context, this likely refers to domestic servants or enslaved persons, though the text immediately pivots to feminine finery]], pearls, and all ornaments of a woman. To pursue, betroth, and lead a wife in marriage is most perfect. It is also good to buy white horses and white garments, to take medicine, and to undergo bloodletting. It is good to speak to queens and noblewomen.

->centered text<-
### *On the hour of Mercury.*
In the hour of Mercury, it is good to buy all painted and written things, grain, millet, panic grass [[notes: a type of cereal crop similar to millet]], and all garments of various colors that pertain to the use of men. It is good to buy cotton, silk, and all works made of silk. It is good to begin a legal plea, to lead a wife, and to form a partnership. Taking medicine and bloodletting is excellent. It is also good to make a journey for business, to buy *baleian* horses [[notes: "equos baleianos" likely refers to piebald or dapple-grey horses]], to buy weapons of two colors (saffron and gold), and to buy garments of a green color. It is good to begin weaving a web [[notes: "telam ordiri," specifically to set up the warp on a loom]].

->centered text<-
### *On the hour of the Moon.*
In the hour of the Moon, it is good to buy honey, oil, figs, chestnuts, walnuts, almonds, wool, flax, hemp, barley, and the meat of pigs and of all animals except sheep. It is also good to buy birds pertaining to Mercury and all beasts that belong to the butcher’s shop. It is good to swear oaths, and to practice deceptions, betrayals, frauds, and clever tricks. It is not good to begin works in which you desire stability; however, it is good to begin those in which you desire speed.

->centered text<-
### *On the rising of the triplicities, and first on the rising of the first triplicity.*
**I**f Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius should be in the ascendant [[notes: the "rising" or "ortu" refers to the zodiac sign appearing on the eastern horizon]], because these signs are fiery, it is good under their rising to begin those things that pertain to fire, such as lighting a furnace, coloring gold, silver, lead, tin, and brass, and for blacksmithing. It is good for every work in which you desire speed: to sail, to hold horse races, to send a messenger, to raise sails, to dig a well, to find treasures, and many things that cannot be numbered.

->centered text<-
### *On the rising of the second triplicity.*
If Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn should be in the ascendant, because they are earthy signs, it is good under that same rising to do all works that pertain to the earth, such as plowing the land, buying lands and houses, measuring land, and dividing garments. It is good to buy wood from which you wish to make ships and all buildings, and to do all works in which you wish to have stability, perseverance, and durability.

->centered text<-
### *On the rising of the third triplicity.*
If indeed Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius should ascend, because they are airy signs, it is good under their ascent to do things that pertain to the air, such as placing a mast in a ship and raising it, and preparing and extending the yardarms and sails, and all works pertaining to a ship. It is also good to begin horse races, galley races, and journeys.

Here, the author concludes the discussion on the Water triplicity before beginning a major treatise on the theory of "Elections"—the art of choosing the right time for an action.]]
