-> ### ZAHEL ON ELECTIONS. [[notes: "Elections" or Electional Astrology is the practice of calculating the most auspicious planetary alignment for starting a specific task.]] <-

...if a benefic [[notes: A "fortuna" or benefic is a planet considered naturally lucky, traditionally Jupiter or Venus.]] is direct, and the Moon is joined to strengthened benefics, for it shall be increased; and beware lest Mercury be in a bad state, because if he is impeded—even if he is received [[notes: "Reception" occurs when a planet is in a sign governed by another, creating a sort of "hospitality" or mutual support between them.]]—it signifies trouble or sadness, hardship, and a second rejection of your petition. Therefore, set aside any foulness and place the Moon joined to the planet to which your business pertains: such as the Sun for a King, and Mars for generals and warriors, and similarly for the rest of the lords of the circles [[notes: "Lords of the circles" refers to the planetary rulers of the celestial spheres/zodiac signs.]].

-> *The twelfth sign, or the twelfth house, with its elections, and first concerning the buying of beasts.* <-

**W**hen you wish to buy a beast [[notes: "Bestia" here usually refers to large livestock, such as horses, oxen, or pack animals.]], let it be when the Moon is joined to the benefics, and let her be direct, oriental [[notes: Rising in the east before the Sun.]], and in the Ascendant. Beware the conjunction of the malefics [[notes: The "malorum" or malifics are Saturn and Mars, planets associated with challenge and decay.]], for then the beast is to be feared. If it is already tamed and ridden, buy it when a common sign [[notes: Also known as "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.]] is ascending, and the Moon is in a fixed sign [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius. Fixed signs suggest stability.]], except for Aquarius and Scorpio; and let that planet to which the Moon is joined be direct and in the Ascendant, so that the beast may increase in value and health. For if the planet is retrograde and in the Ascendant, there will be a wasting away in the beast's body, though the price may rise. If it is direct but descending, it will be physically robust, but its price will not be suitable. If the beast is wild and untamed, let the Ascendant be a common sign and the Moon be in a movable sign [[notes: Also known as "cardinal" signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. These suggest quick movement and change.]], joined to a benefic. After this, do as I told you in the first chapter.

-> *An election for going out to hunt.* <-

And if you wish to go out to the hunt, go under a common sign, and let the lord of the 7th house [[notes: In a hunting election, the 7th house represents the prey or the "other" being pursued.]] be weakening and descending, and let it be in the succedent houses [[notes: Houses that "follow" the angles, specifically the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th.]] of the angles; for if it is cadent [[notes: Cadent houses—the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th—were considered the weakest positions in a chart.]], it signifies that the prey will escape after you have caught it. Let the Moon be in the overall start of the hunt, separated from Mars, fortunate, and in the best location from the Ascendant. Do not go out to the hunt when the Moon is at the very end of a sign, nor when she is "void of course" [[notes: A period when the Moon makes no further aspects before changing signs, usually signifying that "nothing will come" of the effort.]], nor in a movable sign. Beware lest the lord of her house [[notes: The planet that rules the zodiac sign the Moon is currently in.]] does not look upon her; for if he does look upon her, it will signify his will and ease in that matter. Place Mercury clean of the malifics for hunting at sea. If you desire the hunt of the mountains, let the Moon be in Aries or its triplicity [[notes: The "Fire" signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.]]. If it is a hunt of birds, let the Moon be in Gemini or its triplicity [[notes: The "Air" signs: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.]], joined to Mercury or separated from the same Mercury, and let him be descending, for this is better. And if you wish for a hunt of the sea, let this be with a common sign ascending, and its lord in a water sign; and beware lest a fire sign be ascending. Let the Moon look upon the lord of her house, and know that the impediment of the Moon with Mars in a hunt of the sea will be worse and of little profit. Therefore, beware the impediment of Mars in a hunt of the sea, and beware the impediment of Saturn in a hunt of the shore. And know that when Venus and the Moon are in a good state, and Mars does not impede them in a hunt of the sea, the catch will be doubled for its master, and multiplied, and the master shall gain a very great profit, and the hunt will prosper for its master. Let the Moon therefore be joined to Venus, and let Mercury be with them also; but if Mercury is hindered by Saturn, this will not help. And beware lest Mars be in a water sign, and let not the Moon be joined to him, nor let Venus be separated from Mars.

-> *An election for fleeing, and whatever you wish to do secretly.* <-

If you wish to take flight, or perform a secret work—and for everyone who wishes to flee or be hidden—let it be when the Moon is joined to the benefics and separated from the malifics, and let the Moon be joined to Saturn "under the rays" [[notes: "Under the rays" (sub radiis) means a planet is very close to the Sun. In astrology, this makes the planet invisible, which is symbolically perfect for secrets or hiding.]], and let her be joined to the benefics at the time of her emergence from under the rays. For when the luminaries [[notes: The Sun and the Moon.]] have risen over any matter, they detect it and make it appear. Therefore, beware of their aspects in a similar way.

-> *An election for seeking a fugitive.* <-

And when you seek a fugitive, let the Moon be joined to the malifics, or let her emerge from under the rays and meet a malific during that emergence via a square aspect [[notes: A 90-degree angle, considered a point of tension or conflict.]], opposition, or conjunction; and do not place the Moon nor the planet receiving the disposition in the 4th house.

-> *An election for writing a letter, and this is of those elections which are not in the 12 signs.* <-

When you wish to write a letter, let it be when the Moon is joined to Mercury, clean of the malifics, and let Mercury be strong and fortunate, not retrograde, nor impeded; and let both he and the Moon be clean of the malifics.

# -> MESSAHALLACH ON THE ORDER <-
## -> OF THE ORBIT AND THE STARS; AND HOW <-
### -> they act upon this world. Chap. I. <-

[[margin: image: Historiated initial Q depicting a seated man, likely an astronomer or King, gesturing toward the heavens or a sphere.]] **B**ecause the Most High Lord made the earth in the likeness of a sphere, and made a higher orbit revolving in its circuit, and placed the earth fixed and immobile in the middle of that orbit—neither leaning to the right nor to the left—and placed the four elements in motion, and made them to be moved by the motion of the seven planets. The Head of the Dragon [[notes: The "Head of the Dragon" (Caput Draconis) refers to the North or Ascending Node of the Moon, a mathematical point where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic.]], as well as the signs and all the stars, participate with the seven planets in their works and their natures. Therefore, the work of the planets in this world is similar to a magnet stone and iron; for just as iron is drawn by this stone across a known distance, so too every creature and all things upon the earth are affected by the motion of the planets. For all things upon the earth, whether crops or animals, their good fortune or their hindrances, their preparation or their destruction, come from the motions of the planets and their workings. The greatest evidence of this is the diversity of men in their being, and in their fortunes and misfortunes. For since we see certain rational men deprived of goods, while certain fools enjoy them, surely this must have some signifying cause? Good and bad fortune occur without the choice or will of those who suffer them—namely the lucky and the unlucky—and all this, by the nod of God, is the work of the planets, as is all fortune and misfortune.

## -> On the diversity of the traces of the stars' influence in the regions of the earth. Chap. II. <-

**K**now that the work of the planets is diverse according to the diversity of the "climates" [[notes: In medieval geography, "climates" (climata) referred to seven latitudinal zones of the habitable world, each thought to be under the influence of a different planet.]], because in certain climates certain planets bring good fortune, and in another climate they are harmful in different orders. Therefore, every rational person ought to understand the reasons of the climates and regions—such as the region of the Ethiopians, where there is always heat, and the land of the Slavs [[notes: "Sclauorum" (Slavs) was used in medieval Latin to refer to the peoples of Northeastern Europe, representing the extreme cold of the North.]], where there is always cold. When the planets signify excessive cold to the citizens of Ethiopia, their air is merely tempered; but when this is signified to the Slavs, their air will be corrupted and their habitation will perish. Because of this, the science of the logic of climates, regions, and atmospheres is necessary. Know also that the science of the stars is very difficult, and that which is most worthy to be known from it is this: everything universal and plural, such as the revolutions of the years and eclipses. Understand the significations of all these things; and this cannot be done except through the knowledge of the natures of the signs, and what each one signifies regarding regions, provinces, and all things. We have already spoken of this in our other books, but now let us speak of a part of these things briefly, and now we begin with God's help.

## -> On the natures of the signs. Chap. III. <-

**T**here are 12 signs; in each sign there are 30 degrees, and in each degree 60 minutes, and in each minute 60 seconds, and so on down to the size of a point—that is, unto infinity. These are their names: Aries, Taurus, and the rest. They have significations over fire, air, water, and earth. For three of them are fiery: namely Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. Three are earthy: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. Three are airy: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. And three are aquatic: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. The fiery signs are hot, and the aquatic are cold. The earthy signs are also cold, and the airy are hot. Know also that all hot signs are masculine, and cold signs are feminine. All masculine signs are diurnal (of the day), and feminine signs are nocturnal (of the night). There are also four movable [[notes: These are now commonly called "Cardinal" signs, marking the start of the seasons.]] signs in which the season changes: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. There are four fixed signs in which the season is established: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. There are also four "bicorporeal" [[notes: Literally "two-bodied," these are now known as "Mutable" signs, representing the transition between seasons.]] or common signs in which two seasons are joined: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. These are the natures of the signs; understand them.

-># ON THE CONJUNCTIONS OF THE PLANETS<-

->### On the revolution of the years. Chapter IV.<-

**W**hen you wish to know what may happen in the world regarding rains, winds, and so forth: establish the **ascendant** [[notes: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon]] at the hour of the Sun’s entry into the first point of **Aries** [[notes: The Vernal Equinox, marking the start of the astrological year]], and arrange the seven planets for that same hour. Once the figure [[notes: The astrological chart]] is made, consider which of them rules over it. If that ruler be a **fortune** [[notes: A "benefic" planet, typically Jupiter or Venus]], the season will be well-ordered; but if it be an evil planet [[notes: A "malefic" planet, typically Saturn or Mars]] or hindered, the world will be corrupted. Do the same for the four quarters and months of the year. Know also that when many planets are conjoined in **watery signs** [[notes: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces]] during the revolution of the year, they signify a multitude of rain. In **fiery signs** [[notes: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius]] they signify an excess of heat and drought, or sterility of the earth; in **airy signs** [[notes: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius]] they signify a multitude of winds; and in **earthy signs** [[notes: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn]] they signify frost and snow. Likewise, in the quarters of the year, when planets are in cold places, they signify the severity of cold and a lessening of heat. Know also that when **Mars** and **Saturn** rule and the "fortunes" do not behold them [[notes: "Behold" refers to making a geometric aspect or connection]], they signify a multitude of war and the destruction of the world. So too, when Mars is the lord of the summer quarter and is in any of the houses of **Mercury**, it signifies a multitude of rains and pestilences. Know that the severity of drought and sterility of the earth, or the scarcity of the harvest, does not occur except from the conjunction of planets in fiery signs. Understand this and test it according to what has been told to you, and you shall find it so.

->### On the eclipse of the Moon, and its significance. Chapter V.<-

**Y**ou must consider the eclipses of the year, both lunar and solar, and know the ascendant of the middle of the eclipse, and the planet which rules that same ascendant and its figure. If the ruler be evil, it signifies hindrance and destruction; but if it be a "fortune," it signifies restoration. Know that an eclipse of the Moon, when it occurs in **cold signs**, signifies severity of cold; and in **watery signs**, an excess of rain—if the season assists it, that is, if it be winter. If, however, it be summer, it signifies a tempering of the air. Understand and test other things in this way. Understand also that when the "fortunes" behold the Moon and "receive" her [[notes: Reception occurs when one planet is in a sign ruled by another]], her significance in these matters will be for good and profit.

->### On the change of seasons through the movement of the planets. Chapter VI.<-

**W**hen you wish to foreknow the variety of the seasons upon the diverse things of this corruptible world, know the signs of the **heavy planets** [[notes: The "outer" planets which move more slowly—Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars]], whether they be hot or cold. If they be hot, they signify heat in summer and a tempering of the air in winter. If they be in cold signs, they signify cold in winter and a tempering in summer. Likewise, when planets are conjoined in watery signs, it signifies excessive rains and the corruption of the air through those same rains in winter, but a tempering of the air and a multitude of dew in summer; test according to this, for you shall not err. The heavy planets are **Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars**; you ought also to join the **Sun** with them. Know that
[[margin: The heavy planets.]]
the heavy planets, when they are directly over any region, signify drought as well as sterility of the earth; but when they are distant from it, they signify a multitude of rains. I wish "proximity" to be understood as being in the **northern signs**, and "distance" as being in the **meridional** [[notes: Southern]] signs. Know also that when the heavy planets are all **oriental** [[notes: Rising before the Sun in the morning]], they signify drought; and when they are **occidental** [[notes: Setting after the Sun in the evening]], they signify a multitude of rains in winter and a tempering of the air in summer. Likewise, at their rising, they signify a restoration of the air in winter and excessive drought in summer.

->### On the eclipse of the Sun, and its significance. Chapter VII.<-

**K**now that in an eclipse of the Sun, it cannot happen but that some great event is signified according to the magnitude of the eclipse itself—that is, if it be of a quarter of the Sun's body or more. To know what will happen from an eclipse of the Sun, you must know the ascendant of the middle of the eclipse and the planets prevailing over the figures of the eclipse. If they be evil, they will signify evil, and detriment, and the **death of kings**.

-> MESSAHALACH <-

...of kings and the wealthy. And if they are benefics [[notes: "fortunae," referring to the "fortunate" planets like Jupiter and Venus which were thought to bring good luck]], they will signify that good fortune and suitability attend all affairs. And know that when a solar eclipse occurs in Aries, it will signify the death of kings and the wealthy, as well as drought, or sterility of the land, and famine; and it is the same in the rest of the fiery signs [[notes: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius]]. In the watery signs [[notes: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces]], however, it will signify a great abundance of rain and harm resulting from them. Understand also that when the benefics cast an aspect [[notes: a specific geometric angle between planets that determines their influence]], they diminish the evil; but when the malefics [[notes: "mali," referring to Mars or Saturn]] cast an aspect, they will amplify the evil and diminish the good fortune. Know also that when the Sun or Moon are the *hyleg* [[notes: the planet designated as the "giver of life" in a birth chart]] or the *alcochoden* [[notes: the planet that determines the length of life]] of a person, and it is eclipsed, they signify great danger or grave illness for the person to whom that *hyleg* or *alcochoden* belongs, unless the benefics cast a favorable aspect.

-> On the conjunction of all planets, and their effect. Chapter 8. <-

**C**onjunction [[notes: an alignment where two or more celestial bodies appear in the same part of the sky]] of planets signifies the accidents of this world and its affairs, which are thus considered at the time of the conjunction of the higher and lower planets [[notes: "Higher" planets are those further from the Sun (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn); "lower" planets are closer (Moon, Mercury, Venus)]]. For the benefics signify good fortune and a good effect if they prevail over the figure [[notes: the astrological chart or "map" of the heavens]] of the conjunction; if however the malefics prevail, they will signify evil and a bad effect. You should also know that when they are joined in any of the signs, they signify a multitude of harm according to the nature of that sign; that is, if the conjunction occurs in watery signs, it signifies harm from rains, and so it is in the other signs. If, however, they are joined in feminine signs, they will signify pestilence and death among female animals, and the same is said of the masculine signs. And know that conjunctions and eclipses of the luminaries [[notes: the Sun and Moon]], when they occur in fixed signs [[notes: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius]], signify the long duration of the evil and its harm; if they are in moveable signs [[notes: also called "cardinal" signs—Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn]], they signify that the evil and its harm will be of short duration. If they are in common signs [[notes: also called "mutable" signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces]], they signify a moderate evil, and say the same regarding good.

-> On the conjunction of the superior planets. Chapter 9. <-

**K**now that the greatest and most wonderful things happen from the conjunction of the superior planets [[notes: Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars]], and this occurs because of the slowness of their motion. And when these three are joined in one term or face [[notes: specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign used for detailed analysis]] and the Sun beholds them, they signify the destruction of sects and kingdoms, and their transformation, and great events according to the power of the strongest among them, who prevails over their signs. And this is their "greatest conjunction," which signifies prophecy and the destruction of certain climates [[notes: a "climate" was an ancient geographical division of the world]] and the most significant affairs, especially if any of the inferior planets aids them. And know that the planet stronger than the rest will be the "significator." If it is a benefic, it will signify good fortune. And if it is a malefic, it will signify evil and tribulation. Understand also that these planets, when they are joined in their exaltations [[notes: the specific zodiac signs where a planet's power is heightened]], will signify good, the suitability of the time, a great commotion of wars, and the demonstration of miracles. If however they are joined in their falls [[notes: the signs where a planet is most weakened]], they signify harm, drought, sterility of the land, and famine, unless they are made fortunate by other planets. And know that when they are joined in a fiery sign, they signify sterility of the land. In a watery sign, an abundance of rain. In an airy sign, they signify the strength of the winds. And in an earthy sign, an excess of cold and harm. And when they are joined in masculine signs, they signify harm to male animals, and likewise for females.

-> On the greater conjunction. Chapter 10. <-

**W**e have already related that the principal events occur from the greater conjunction, which is the conjunction of the superior planets. But there are other conjunctions for these superior planets signifying even greater accidents. For the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter is the "greatest conjunction," and this signifies world-changing accidents and the rise of religious sects. Knowledge of these accidents is obtained by looking at the ascendant [[notes: the sign rising on the eastern horizon]] and the planets at the hour of their conjunction, and seeing which of them rules in the chart. If the ruler is a benefic, it will signify good and a suitable time. If it is a malefic, it signifies harm and drought, as well as sterility of the land and wars. Know therefore that when Jupiter is stronger than Saturn, it signifies prosperity in that same conjunction. If however Saturn leads, it will signify harm and tribulation. And know that their conjunction in fiery and airy signs signifies drought and sterility of the land, as well as severe hardship; and in earthy signs, destruction...

It specifically highlights the "Great Conjunction" of Saturn and Jupiter as a primary indicator of historical shifts, religious movements, and the fate of kingdoms.]]

...the destruction of seeds and famine. In aquatic signs, however, it will signify an excessive amount of rain and pestilence, provided that the planets are "impedited" [[notes: "Impedited" means a planet is weakened by a difficult mathematical relationship with a "malefic" planet like Mars or Saturn]]. If, on the other hand, they are "fortunate" [[notes: well-placed and supported by "benefic" planets like Venus or Jupiter]], they will signify an increase of good things in all their meanings, and a reduction of evil. Likewise, you should know that when a Great Conjunction occurs in any of the "angles" [[notes: The four most powerful points in an astrological chart: the East, West, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli]], and especially in the angle of the Midheaven, it signifies the appearance of a king or a prophet from the direction of that same sign. If that "sign" [[notes: the Latin text says 'lignum' (wood), likely an OCR error or variant for 'signum']] is fortunate and its Lord is in a good state, it signifies his triumph and dominion. If it and its Lord are hindered, it signifies his death and downfall; and the conjunction is to be feared after the known years of that same conjunction, which we have mentioned elsewhere.

-> On the Middle Conjunction. Chapter XI. <-

**T**he Middle Conjunction is the meeting of Mars and Saturn, and this signifies the occurrences of wars and the conflicts of strife. When you wish to know these occurrences, look to the ruler in the chart of their conjunction; if it is a "fortune" [[notes: a benefic planet]], it signifies goodness and restoration. If it is a "malice" [[notes: a malefic planet]], it signifies evil and its obstruction. Know also that their conjunction in "human signs" [[notes: Zodiac signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius]] signifies a multitude of infirmities among people. Their conjunction in any of the angles of the year signifies the opposition of the wealthy or of kings, and a multitude of wars; and this state of affairs will endure until they are joined another time. Their conjunction in fire signs signifies drought and the sterility of the earth; in air signs, winds; in water signs, a multitude of rains; and in earth signs, frost, snow, and a great deal of cold. Know also that when the "fortunes" look upon them [[notes: "look upon" refers to an astrological 'aspect' or mathematical angle]], they diminish the evil, and the "malices" increase it. Test this in the way I have told you, and you shall find it so, if God wills.

-> On the Minor Conjunction. Chapter XII. <-

**T**he Minor Conjunction is the meeting of Jupiter and Mars, and this signifies the occurrences that arise from rain and snow, the corruption of the air, and war. If a "fortune" prevails in their conjunction, it signifies good fortune; if a "malice," then evil. And know that when Jupiter and Mars are joined in the Ascendant of the year, or in any of its angles, it signifies the commotion and diversity of kings, unless the "fortunes" look upon them. Know also that whenever a "fortune" is joined with a "malice," the nature of the stronger one will appear. When a "malice" is joined with another "malice," evil will abound, unless the one presiding over the conjunction is a "fortune"—understand this. This is the last of what we have set forth in this book, and it is from the secrets of the science of the stars.

# ON NATIVITIES ACCORDING
## TO OMAR. BOOK ONE.

[[insert: Decorative woodcut initial 'M' showing a human figure holding a globe or circular object within floral scrolls.]] **M**ar Belnalfargdiani [[notes: A Latinized version of Umar ibn al-Farrukhan al-Tabari]] of Tiberias said: Know that the definitions of "nativities" [[notes: individual births]] regarding their "nourishment" [[notes: a technical term for whether a child will survive infancy]] are four. One concerns those who do not taste food, nor is there life in their souls. The second concerns those who taste food but are not nourished. The third concerns those who taste food and are nourished, but do not reach a long life. The fourth concerns those who are nourished and reach a long life—that is, old age. But now we must speak of the first definition: those who neither taste food nor are nourished. For this, you should look at the degree of the Ascendant and the angles, the degrees of the Luminaries [[notes: the Sun and Moon]], and the Lords of all these, as well as the three Lords of the Triplicity [[notes: The three signs belonging to the same element]] of the Ascendant, the Part of Fortune, and its Lord. Also, the Lord of the Conjunction or Prevention [[notes: The New or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth]] that occurred before the birth of the child. After this, look at the *Almutaz* [[notes: The 'Almuten,' or the planet that holds the most combined dignities/strength over a specific point in the chart]] over these places—that is, the planet itself which has dominion in these places, whether it be one, two, or three. If there is one, and you find it "falling" [[notes: located in a weak house]] and hindered by the degrees of some "malice"—that is, if it is in the same degree as a malefic planet—or if it is the degree of a sign...

[[summary: This page transitions from world astrology (predicting war, weather, and the rise of prophets through planetary conjunctions) to natal astrology. It begins "On Nativities," focusing first on the grim task of determining infant mortality through the "Almuten" and "Lords of Triplicity."]]

If the degree of the ascending sign is afflicted [[notes: *Impedimentus* (impeded or afflicted) usually refers to a planet or point being poorly placed or receiving "harsh" aspects from "malefic" planets like Saturn or Mars]], then the infant will taste nothing until it dies. And if the degrees of the luminaries [[notes: The "Luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon]] are afflicted in any way, and the degree of the ascendant is also afflicted, the child will not taste anything, if God wills it. Ptolemy [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the most influential astronomer and astrologer of antiquity]] also said that when the luminary which holds authority and the degree of the ascendant are afflicted, and the lord of the luminaries has retreated from the angles [[notes: The "Angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a zodiac chart, representing the strongest and most active areas of life]], the child will not taste food until it dies. This event will happen at the same hour when the luminaries reach a malefic point. Furthermore, all the ancient authorities said that when the lords of the triplicity [[notes: Triplicity refers to the grouping of zodiac signs by element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water), each ruled by a set of three planets]] of the ascendant—all three of them—have retreated from the angles, and the luminaries and their lords have retreated, and the conjunction or prevention [[notes: The New Moon or Full Moon that occurred immediately before the birth]] and its lord have retreated, then the newborn will not taste anything, if God wills it. Or, the newborn itself will not be a human, or it will be one of those who are born with certain signs, such as apes, or those who are called "changelings" by the country folk [[notes: *Mutati*, literally "changed ones," refers to the folkloric belief in babies swapped by fairies or spirits]]; that is, the birth will be a monster or a brute animal. If, however, it is a brute animal, and this occurred with the retreat of those points I mentioned and was afflicted by the malefics, and the malefics were dominant over them, the animal will be a "predatory wolf" which will not associate with humans. But if both malefics and benefics [[notes: Benefics are "helpful" planets, primarily Jupiter and Venus]] were dominant, especially if Mercury had some dignity in these places, it will be one of those animals that associate with humans and with which people play.

The second definition is that you should look at the ascendant, the angles, the degrees of the luminaries, and their lords. Look also to the three lords of the triplicity of the ascendant, the Part of Fortune [[notes: An Arabic Part or mathematical point calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant]], and its lord, as well as the conjunction or prevention and the lord of that conjunction or prevention which occurred before the birth of the child. If the *Almuten* [[notes: *Almutaz* (Almuten), the planet that holds the most "dignity" or power over a specific degree of the zodiac]], who has dominion in these places, is falling away from the angles, and the malefics are dominant over them, and there is some distance in degrees between the *Almuten* and the malefics, it signifies that the child may taste food and be nourished until the *Almuten* reaches the malefics by body [[notes: A physical conjunction]] or by rays [[notes: An aspect, such as a square or opposition]]; then it signifies the child will perish when it reaches the malefics by days, months, or years, according to the total of those degrees, if God wills it. Similarly, if the malefics are in the angles and the *Almuten* is falling away, and the degree of the ascendant is joined to a malefic, or if the degree is of an ill-placed Moon, then the newborn will perish at the years, months, or days according to the quantity of those degrees which were between them, if God wills it. And if all these things, or most of them, fall away from the angles, the child will taste food but will not be nourished. If you wish to know the hour, direct from the degree of the ascendant into the bodies of the malefics and their quartile aspects [[notes: A "quartile" or square aspect (90 degrees), considered a point of high tension]] or their oppositions to each sign, counting one month per equal degree. If a year passes, turn the profections [[notes: A timing technique where the chart is advanced by 30 degrees for every year of life]], giving one year to every 30 degrees, and then the newborn will perish, if God wills it. Look also in that hour to certain benefics; if they are in the angles or in an excellent place—that is, in their own dignities—or the planet which is most dignified in the degree of the ascendant, the year, and the Part of Fortune, this signifies (according to the measure of its strength or weakness) that the child will reach certain months of life according to the gift of that same planet from its "lesser" and "greater" years [[notes: In ancient astrology, each planet was assigned specific "years" of life it could grant]]; and perhaps there will be days according to its state of weakness or strength.

According to what Dorotheus [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet]] thinks, when the first and second lords of the triplicity of the ascendant "fall" [[notes: Move into weak houses]], it signifies the newborn will not be nourished, especially if Saturn is in an angle in a night birth, or Mars in a day birth; the hour of death will be when the profection of some other year reaches the angles. This is because when a malefic is in an angle, no year can come to any of the angles without the light of the malefic's quartile aspect, or its opposition, or its physical body being there. If the child has not died in the first year, and it is considered in the "Book of Likenesses" regarding the *Almuten*: if there are two of them and one is afflicted, the newborn will die and the other will not be sufficient to save it. Similarly, if there are three lords and one is afflicted while two are strong, the infant will endure, but its life will not be prolonged. If, however, three are afflicted and only one is useful, the child will not remain, if God wills it. Similarly, if there are four and one or two are afflicted while the others are "vital" [[notes: Healthy or well-placed]], the boy will remain, but his life will not be prolonged, if God wills it.

The third definition is when the newborn has no *Hyleg* or *Alcocoden* [[notes: The *Hyleg* is the "Giver of Life" and the *Alcocoden* is the "Giver of Years," specific planets used to calculate life expectancy]]. Instead, the luminaries and their lords, as well as the lord of the ascendant, are free from the malefics and from retrogradation or combustion [[notes: Combustion occurs when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" and hidden]], or they are falling away but free from the degrees of the malefics and their opposition or conjunction, and free from the dominion of the malefics over them. When births are of this kind, the newborn will be nourished, but it will not reach a 

-> long life. <-

. . . what sort of life, if God wills, and perhaps his life will be destroyed within 12 years: For when there are nativities according to what we have said, we delay speaking about those nativities because of the "fall" of the significators [[notes: Planets in "fall" are in signs where their influence is weakened]], until the Ascendant traverses one full circle—that is, twelve years, namely one year for each sign. For as often as the circle arrives from the Ascendant to the bodies of the malefics [[notes: Malefics are usually Mars or Saturn, planets associated with hardship]], or to their square aspects or their oppositions, there shall be fear for him until the Ascendant traverses one circle. And when one circle has passed, we direct him from the Ascendant at a rate of one year per degree according to the ascensions of the same climate [[notes: "Climate" here refers to the latitude of the birthplace, which affects how quickly signs rise]] in which he was born, until it reaches the malefics, if God wills. 

The fourth definition is of those who have a *hylech* and *alcochoden* [[notes: Technical terms for the "Giver of Life" and "Giver of Years" respectively]], and whose "Lords of Nutrition" are free, whom we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter, if God wills. 

Regarding the knowledge of the *hylech*: in daytime nativities, look to the Sun. If it is in the Ascendant, or in the 11th, or the Midheaven [[notes: The "Midheaven" or *Medium Coeli* is the highest point in the chart]], it will be the *hylech* in whatever sign it may be, whether feminine or masculine. But if it is in the 8th or 9th house, and it is a masculine sign, it will be the *hylech*. And know that the Sun or other places used for the *hylech* cannot be the *hylech* unless the Lord of their House looks upon it [[notes: "Looking upon" or "beholding" means the planets are in an astrological aspect to one another]], or the Lord of the Term, or of the Exaltation, or of the Triplicity; for if there is a *hylech* and one of the aforesaid—who are the Lords of the dignities in which they reside—does not behold it, their *hylech* status will be annulled. 

Similarly for the Moon by night and day, and the Part of Fortune [[notes: An Arabic Part or calculated point related to prosperity and health]], and the degree of the conjunction or prevention [[notes: The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth]], as well as the degree of the Ascendant. If the Sun is not the *hylech*, look to the Moon; if she is in an "angle" or in a "succedent" sign [[notes: Angles are houses 1, 4, 7, and 10; succedents are 2, 5, 8, and 11]] in a feminine sign, and any of the four aforementioned [Lords] beholds her, she will be the *hylech*. If it does not suit the Moon to be the *hylech*, and the birth was "preventional" [after a Full Moon]: start from the Part of Fortune and seek the *hylech* from there, just as was shown to you. If however the birth was "conjunctional" [after a New Moon], start from the Ascendant, seeking the *hylech* from it, and place it before the Part of Fortune. 

And know, as we said before, that it cannot be the *hylech* unless one of the four aforementioned behold it. If one of the four does not behold it, its "hylegia" [[notes: The quality of being a Hylech]] is destroyed. And if you have sent forward the Ascendant and it does not suit it to be the *hylech*, seek the *hylech* after it from the Part of Fortune. If these cannot be the *hylech*, seek the *hylech* from the degree of the conjunction which was before the birth: namely, in a conjunctional birth from the degree of the conjunction, and in a preventional birth from the degree of the Moon at the hour of the prevention. But if one of the four does not behold this, as we said before, it will be frustrated, if God wills. 

And if all four behold the *hylech*, that one which is closer to the degree of the *hylech* by the number of degrees—whether before or behind—and is in a stronger place, shall be the *alcochoden*, since each of them has one authority. But if any of them has two or three authorities, he himself shall preside, whether his aspect is closer or further away, provided only that he beholds the sign, if God wills.

[[margin: **Alcochoden.**]]
And when you know the *hylech* and *alcochoden*, know that the *alcochoden* signifies the 

[[margin: **Hylech.**]]
years of the life of the native, and its dangers; the *hylech* truly signifies the life of the native, if God wills. When the *hylech* arrives at the years determined by the degrees of ascensions—namely, one year for each degree—to the bodies of the malefics and their rays, and to the [Dragon's] Tail [[notes: The South Node of the Moon, considered unlucky]], and also to the four aspects of the Moon and to its degree or the opposition of its own degree, and those years are equal to or near the years of the *alcochoden*, and [the Part of] Fortune has not cast its rays to that same term in which the *hylech* reaches the malefic, then the native shall perish. But if it reaches the malefic and the years are not similar to the years of the *alcochoden*, he will be endangered by a peril similar to death, but he will escape, if God wills: this is the disposition of the order of the *hylech*. 

And know that the name *hylech* sounds like a word that in Latin can be called "wife" (*uxor*), and *alcochoden* similarly sounds like "husband" (*vir*) from this significance: because just as a woman cannot well-govern her house without the aid of a husband, so the *hylech* is not sufficient to signify the years of life without the authority of the *alcochoden*. Although some astronomers use only the *hylech* and do not care for the *alcochoden*. In another way, the *hylech* is called the "place of life" because the status of life is sought from it, and the *alcochoden* is called the "giver" or "significator of years." But let us return to the book. 

Dorotheus [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet]] thought the totality of their *hylech* was that the Sun is not the *hylech* in the 8th or 7th houses unless it is in a masculine sign; for if it is in these places in feminine signs, it is "effeminated," its strength is weakened, and it will be unequal—that is, tempered. Ptolemy [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy, the most famous astronomer/astrologer of antiquity]], however, thought that the Sun is not the *hylech* in the 8th house, because this place is turbid and dark, and no light of the Ascendant is in it; and he praised...

[[meta: This page continues a technical discussion of the *hylech* (the giver of life) and the *alcochoden* (the giver of years), two vital points in a medieval or Renaissance astrological chart used to predict the length of a native's life. -> ### BOOK ONE. <- [[page number: 125]]

...and he praised the ninth house [[notes: The 9th house in astrology is associated with wisdom, travel, and religion.]], because it is similar to the ascendant in its triplicity and is of the same nature. It is also the place of the **joy of the Sun**, which is its foundation; and when the Sun is tempered within it, a good life will be produced and shall endure, if God wills. The same **Ptolemy** [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), an astronomer and astrologer whose *Tetrabiblos* was the standard text for centuries.]] thought that when the authority of the Sun is by night in the investigation of the *hylech* [[notes: The *hylech* is the specific planet or point in a birth chart that represents the life force of the individual.]], and it is in the opposition of these places below the earth, it shall be the *hylech*. Moreover, **Dorotheus** [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer whose instructional poems influenced later Persian and Arabic astrology.]] said that when it is at night, in the opposition of these places below the earth, it shall be the *hylech*. Furthermore, Dorotheus also said that when it is at night in the opposition of these places in which we said it could become the *hylech*, by day it shall be the *hylech*, unless it is in masculine signs. 

If, however, the Sun is not in these places by day, it cannot be the *hylech*; seek then the *hylegia* [[notes: The status or quality of being the hylech.]] from the Moon. If the Moon is in an angle [[notes: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful "corners" of the chart.]] or in a house following an angle [[notes: Known as 'succedent' houses (the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th).]], it shall be the *hylech* without an examination of whether the signs are masculine or feminine. But it is more useful that it be feminine in feminine signs in the births of women, and masculine in masculine signs in the births of men. Indeed, everyone thought that the Moon is the *hylech* in the third house, because that is the place of its joy and foundation. But more recently, Dorotheus thought that when the Moon is in this place, it shall be hindered. 

Ptolemy, however, did not deny that the Moon could become the *hylech* in the ninth house, but he assigned to it the rule of the Sun: that if the Moon is not in these places and has fallen away, the *hylech* must be sought elsewhere. If the birth was *conjunctional* [[notes: Occurring near a New Moon.]], seek it from the degree of the ascendant of the birth. If indeed the birth was *preventional* [[notes: Occurring near a Full Moon.]], you shall begin from the **Part of Fortune** [[notes: A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being.]], which is the "ascendant of the Moon." They placed the degree of the ascendant afterward, and therefore prioritized the Part of Fortune in a preventional birth, because the Moon is then full, having the power of the night with its perfection. They began from the ascendant in conjunctional births because the Moon is then in conjunction without light, and then the light will be entirely that of the Sun—that is, the ascendant. 

If you begin from the Part of Fortune and it is in the angles, or in the houses following the angles, it shall be fit to be the *hylech*, and it will not be asked whether the signs are masculine or feminine. And if you begin from the ascendant, it shall be the *hylech* entirely, unless the Part of Fortune is there, or if it is hindered; and it is not considered whether it is "falling" [[notes: 'Cadent' houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) were generally considered weak or unfavorable.]] from the angles, because it is within it, and there is nothing further to seek. For what is feared to be lacking in other places of the *hylech* is regarding its advancement or lack thereof. For it is possible that the aforesaid places are in advancing positions. The ascendant, however, does not cease to be in advancement. 

If indeed the Sun, the Moon, the Part of Fortune, or the ascendant do not suit the *hylech*, look to the conjunction or prevention [[notes: The New or Full Moon]] which occurred before the birth; and whichever of these it regards, if it is in an angle or in a house following an angle, it shall be the *hylech*, and the nature of the sign and sex (whether it be masculine or feminine) is not to be considered. 

And when you know the *hylech*, and you wish to know the divider, the *alcochoden* [[notes: The *alcochoden* is the planet that "rules" the hylech. It is used to calculate the actual number of years a person is expected to live.]], according to the sayings of Dorotheus: Look to the lord of the house [[notes: The planet that rules the zodiac sign.]], and the lord of the term [[notes: Signs were subdivided into "terms" ruled by different planets.]], as well as the lord of the exaltation or triplicity. You shall begin from these with the **lord of the term**; if it should cast its rays toward that very term, regarding it, then that planet itself shall be the *alcochoden*. If, however, it does not cast its rays to that term, but the lord of the house, or of the exaltation, or of the triplicity does, then whichever of those casts its rays shall be the *alcochoden*, provided their dignity is equal—that is, if it has one dignity. But if one of them should have multiple dignities and casts its rays to that term, this one shall be the *alcochoden*. Similarly, the lord of three dignities is worthier, being stronger in that place. 

If indeed it is the same place, or similar, the one which is in an angle, or (in the case of the Sun) the one closer to the cusp at its rising, shall be stronger; and this is the explanation for them—that is, the *alcochoden*—being on the cusp. If the planets are in the angles, or in the houses following the angles, the one which is closer to the degree of the angles, or the houses following the angles, shall be stronger. And if one of them is "peregrine" [[notes: A planet with no essential dignity or 'home' in its current position, often viewed as a wandering stranger.]] and the other is in its own house, the latter shall be stronger. If indeed they are oriental [[notes: Rising before the Sun in the morning.]], the one which is closer to the Sun shall be stronger. 

And mix with the *hylech* the planet which is in the ascendant or in the *medium coeli* [[notes: The Midheaven, or the highest point of the chart.]]. The method of mixing it is to look at the planet in the ascendant or Midheaven: if it has any dignity in the *hylech* by house, exaltation, triplicity, or term, it shall be called a "partner"—that is, it shall be similar to it—and shall be considered worthier than one which has only one part, that is, one dignity. 

Regarding what Dorotheus said: that **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**, when they are oriental, or with the Sun in one degree, or in any of their stations, or seven days before or after these places...
[[margin: L]] ...thenceforward

...thence if they should have any testimony in the **hylech**, it tempers or perhaps will rule the **hylech** or **alcochoden**. [[notes: The *Hylech* is the "Giver of Life," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine longevity. The *Alcochoden* is the "Giver of Years," the planet that rules the Hylech and dictates the number of years the person might live.]] However, the lord of the **term** of the hylech is better and more worthy if it projects its rays to the term of the hylech. [[notes: A "term" is a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.]] But when there are many strong candidates, and their parts are equal, and they all aspect the hylech, that one which is closer in aspect to the hylech than the others shall rule the hylech. Moreover, **Ptolemy** named the aspect as if it were one of the other worthy parts. He said that when the lords of the dignities of the hylech—from the house, exaltation, triplicity, and term—aspect it, the one who has more dignity along with an aspect shall be the **alcochoden** who rules. But if there is a planet having one dignity in the hylech and it aspects it, and there is another having three dignities that does not aspect it, the lord of the three dignities shall rule. And he also said that the planet is more worthy to rule which has more dignity in the **Ascendant** and the **Luminaries** [[notes: The Sun and Moon]], and in the **Part of Fortune**, or in the degree of the conjunction or prevention [[notes: The New Moon or Full Moon]] which occurred before the birth.

**Q**VOD [[notes: Latin "Quod" (Because/But). The large drop-cap "Q" marks a new section on the *Almuten*.]] if there is a planet having dignity in three or four places, or in two of these aforementioned places, we shall establish it as the **almutaz** over the nativity who shall lead—that is, the one who holds dominion. [[notes: "Almutaz" or *Almuten* is the planet with the most essential dignity/power across various points in the chart.]] After this, to know the years of life, we look to the place of this same planet, the **almutaz**. If it is **oriental** [[notes: Rising before the Sun]] and in an **angle** [[notes: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, where planets are most active]], and with this it is in its **hayz**—that is, a masculine planet by day in a masculine sign above the earth, etc.—and it is in its own dignity (such as house, exaltation, triplicity, or term), and it happens to be in its hayz and in the angles (which are the Ascendant and the Midheaven), it will give its **greater years**. [[notes: Each planet was assigned three sets of years—greater, mean, and lesser—based on its strength. For example, the greater years of Saturn are 57, while its lesser are 30.]] But if it is oriental in its dignity, and in the houses following the angles [[notes: Succedent houses]], and especially in its hayz, though not in the degrees of an angle, the book will signify its **mean years**. And if it is "free" in the same way we described, but is **cadent** from an angle [[notes: Falling away from the angles, usually considered a weak position]], it signifies its **minor years**. If, however, it happens to be cadent and also **retrograde**, **peregrine** [[notes: Lacking any dignity; a stranger in its sign]], or in its **fall**, it will signify hours instead of the number of its minor years. When you have truly identified the author [of life], and you wish to know what the planets will increase or decrease from these years, look thus: If a **Fortune** [[notes: A beneficial planet, like Jupiter or Venus]] aspects it, it will increase its minor years, unless it is retrograde or **combust** [[notes: Too close to the Sun, thus weakened]], because then it adds months according to the number of its minor years. But if a **Malefic** [[notes: A harmful planet, like Mars or Saturn]] aspects it by a **fourth aspect** [square] or **opposition**, or is **conjoined** (that is, with it in one degree or sign), it decreases according to the minor years. And **Mercury**, when he is with the Fortunes and givers, will give his minor years; but when he is with the Malefics and diminishers, he will likewise diminish his minor years. And when you know the years of the native from the years of the significations of the alcochoden, you shall **direct** the hylech to the rays of the malefic planets by the fourth aspect, opposition, or conjunction in one sign; also from the third [trine] or sixth [sextile] aspect, by the degrees of the ascension of its region, counting one year for each degree. [[notes: "Direction" is a predictive technique where points are moved through the zodiac to time events.]] And when it reaches a malefic, without the rays of a Fortune being projected to that same degree, and these years are similar to the years of the alcochoden, that will be the year in which the native perishes. This is especially true if it is the year of the native, and the lord of the Ascendant of that year, and also the lord of its **profection** [[notes: Another timing technique that shifts the chart by one sign per year]], are impeded by that same malefic. And know that whenever the profection of the hylech reaches the rays or body of a malefic (that is, the degrees where the malefics were, and their rays in the root of the nativity), whether it projects its rays to that degree or not, it will be a year of danger and "cutting off." Among the malefics, the "cutters" [abscisores] are the malefic planets, and it is worse if the malefic is in the course of the hylech's degree in altitude and declination. For **Dorotheus** [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer]] thought that if the hylech were joined to a malefic by square or opposition, and the malefic was distant in latitude toward the North or South from the path of the hylech, it would not kill the lord of the nativity, but would cause him danger. Do not perform a direction without knowledge of the planet's latitude—that is, do not direct the hylech or any such thing unless you account for the latitude of the planets and fixed stars. After this, you should know in the oblique circle which degree the malefic planet travels through latitude from the path of the circle of signs [the ecliptic]. And when you know this, you shall project its rays from that same degree; then, when the hylech reaches its rays by trine, sextile, square, or opposition, or reaches its body, it will kill, if God wills it.

**I**nterfectors [[notes: From the Latin *Interfectores*, meaning "killers" or "slayers"; planets that end the life.]] indeed are **Saturn** and **Mars**, and the **Sun**, by opposition, square aspect, and conjunction. The **Moon** also, when she is in the fourth aspect [square] of the Sun, whatever hylech is [[margin: joined]]...

If [the planet] has been harmful, it kills. Similarly, when the Moon is in any opposition, and her body is joined to the degree of the ascending sign [[notes: The Ascendant, or the point rising on the eastern horizon at birth]], it kills when she is the *hylech* [[notes: The *hylech* is the specific planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life."]]. Furthermore, if she herself is joined to the degree of the ascendant when she is the *hylech*, she kills: because the Moon is the enemy of the ascendant. Similarly, the ascendant is an enemy to her because of the difference of their substances; for the ascendant is of the substance of the day—that is, the substance of heat and of the Sun—while the Moon is of the heat of the night and of cold [[notes: Astrology traditionally categorizes planets and points by "sect" (day or night) and temperament (hot, cold, moist, dry).]], and they are mutual enemies and contraries. Also, cloudy and dark places from the circle [[notes: Likely referring to nebulous clusters like the Pleiades or Praesepe, often associated with blindness or ill health in traditional astrology]] joined to these *hylech* points kill. For the Heart of the Scorpion [[notes: The star Antares]] and the Heart of the Bull [[notes: The star Aldebaran]], on account of their excessive and superfluous heat, kill if the *hylech* is joined to them.

Mercury also, when he is with the malefics [[notes: Usually Saturn and Mars]], namely in their fourth aspect [[notes: A square aspect (90 degrees)]] or opposition, or in a sextile [[notes: 60 degrees]] or trine aspect [[notes: 120 degrees]] in a "vessel" [[notes: *In vasu* likely refers to a specific planetary container or house placement]] away from the malefics without their aspect, and is joined to the degree of the body of the *hylech*, or its sextile, trine, square, or opposition, he kills. But if it should be the opposite of what I have said, he does not kill. If the *hylech* or the Moon is joined to the western degree—that is, the seventh house—or whatever you have directed toward it, it kills. And when the "direction" [[notes: "Primary direction" is a complex predictive technique where one degree of the sky's rotation equals one year of life]] is perfected at the end of a sign with half of the years of the *alcochoden* [[notes: The *alcochoden* is the planet that rules the *hylech*; it was used to calculate the actual number of years a person might live]], whether the "lesser," "middle," or "greater" years, it kills. And when the disposition changes from the *hylech*, from the term of a malefic into the term of a malefic [[notes: "Terms" or "Bounds" are sub-divisions of zodiac signs ruled by different planets]], by the very entry of some malefic, even if it does not kill, there will be fear concerning that which has already endured for a long time within that term.

## **A**ND know that it seemed to Ptolemy [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundation of Western astrology]] that the Moon should always be directed to the rays of the malefics and the benefics [[notes: *Fortunarum*, the "fortunes," usually Jupiter and Venus]] to know the state of the body in health or sickness, and the state of the mother; and the Part of Fortune [[notes: An Arabic Part or calculated mathematical point]] to know the acquisitions of a man—namely his riches and his poverty; and the Sun to know the state of the father, the kingdom, and the master. It also seemed to him that the direction of the degree of the Midheaven should be through the ascensions of the direct circle [[notes: Right Ascension]]. Again, it seemed to him and to all others that one should direct from the degree of the ascendant to know his being, because the divisions of the terms [relate] to the rays of the malefics and benefics. Likewise, if it happens that the "divisor" [[notes: The planet ruling a specific period of life]] is a malefic, and the division is in the rays of malefics, it foretells in this case distress, evil, and restraint, as well as infirmity of the body and corruption of the temperament according to the quantity of the natures of the malefic. But if the divisor is a malefic and the rays are of a benefic, his state will be common—that is, infirmities along with health, and poverty with abundance. If, however, the divisor is a benefic, and the rays are likewise of a benefic: if the native is from the children of the poor or the middle class in their condition, he will likewise be moderate in his division, and he will be moderate in his being and his condition, if God wills.

## **T**HE science of the projection of rays: know that whether it be the *hylech*, the Sun, the Moon, or anything else, when you wish to know the life of a person born and their state by the division of that same life, it is necessary for you to begin the work of the "projection of planetary rays" from them. And of the two modes from the sayings of the ancients, one is that through which almost all of us who divide the ray receive and work, which is the work of Dorotheus [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet]]. This is his work: beginning, look at the place of the planet, and the planet itself with its equal degrees and minutes. After this, know its sextile, square, or opposite aspect, because it projects its rays to them through similar equal degrees and minutes; and convert them into the degrees of ascension for that same sign, and these will be the rays of the planet. And in its own sign you will look at its degrees, and convert them into ascensions, and you will write them down, and this is the degree of its body. You shall do similarly for the ascendant and the twelve places [[notes: The twelve houses of the horoscope]] through the degrees of ascension; this is the work which the ancients performed, and this is the "word of degrees." If the *hylech* were in the tenth degree of Aries, and the malefic to which we wished to direct was in the twentieth degree of Scorpio, we direct from the place of the *hylech* in the degree of Taurus [[notes: Likely an error or specific calculation step in the Latin text]] to the rays and the malefic. We shall direct, however, as above by subtracting the ascensions which are in the line of the *hylech* from the ascensions which are in the line of twenty degrees of Taurus: and those which remain, they themselves will be the degrees of the direction, the number of which we ought to give as years, etc. Ptolemy, however, used another mode, and said that all rays gather in the cusp—that is, in the point of the earth—and it would be one thing; and he said that it is necessary for us to know the diversity of the rays according to the position of the place. For beginning to work the rays through the longitude of the planets from the angles, and through the ascensions of the city in which you are, just as you will work in this chapter, and when you have ordered the place of the planets, you will direct—

hyleg [[notes: The Hyleg is a specific point or planet in a birth chart designated as the "giver of life."]], and the degree of the Ascendant according to these lengths, just as I have told you. And when it reaches the "malefics" [[notes: Traditionally, Saturn and Mars are the "malefics," or planets that signify hardship or endings.]], there will be evil according to their nature and strength, if God wills. Know that when the Hyleg is the Sun or the Moon, or any other [planet] that is in those places between the Midheaven [[notes: The highest point of the chart.]] and the western degree [[notes: The Descendant, or point where the sun sets.]], it shall be directed backward—that is, toward the seventh [house], against the succession of the signs—and in a falling degree, which, taking the Ascendant from the start of the Ascendant's degree through the ascensions of the climate, and according to the light of the degrees which were between them through the ascensions, at a rate of one year for each degree, it "kills" [[notes: An astrological term for the point where the life-giving force is symbolically cut off.]]. And this method of direction is well explained in the *Introduction* of Alcabitius and Albumasar [[notes: Alcabitius (Al-Qabisi) and Albumasar (Abu Ma'shar) were famous 9th-century Arabic astrologers whose works were standard textbooks in Europe.]]. If, however, the direction is toward the Tail [[notes: The "Tail of the Dragon" or South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of depletion.]], direct from the degree of the Tail by the degrees of ascension, and according to the number of degrees between them, there shall be a year. If, however, the Hyleg is here between the Midheaven and the West, and you have spoken concerning them: direct backward against the succession of the signs toward the West, as I told you before. And know that the malefics cannot be more than six: the two [natural] malefics, namely Saturn and Mars; and Mercury when it is with them, or in their nature by aspect. And the fourth is the Sun, when it is specifically with Mars, or in its fourth aspect [[notes: A "square" aspect of 90 degrees.]], or its conjunction or opposition, or in its sextile or trine aspect of fortune to them [[notes: 60-degree or 120-degree angles.]], for then it becomes an evil similar to Saturn. The fifth of the malefics is the Head [[notes: The North Node of the Moon.]], and the sixth is the Tail [[notes: The South Node of the Moon.]]. And know that the malefics are necessarily six. For two are malefics by nature: Saturn and Mars; and two by accident: Mercury and the Sun; and two by location: the Head and the Tail. Know that all these things are so when they occur as I told you before. And when these six are gathered over Venus without the aspect of a fortune [[notes: A "fortune" refers to the beneficial planets Jupiter or Venus.]], the native will be a *spadus* [[notes: From the Latin *spado*, meaning a eunuch or someone who is sterile/impotent.]]; but if the first lord of the triplicity of Venus is strong, this will benefit him. Otherwise, he will be a man who has suffered laboriously, needing food for his belly all the days of his life. And when one wishes to know the life of the native, and his state in the division of his life, it is necessary for you to begin to calculate the projections of the rays of the planets. After this, you shall direct his Hyleg—that is, the degrees according to the work of this length, according to what was said in its procedure. And when you wish to direct the Hyleg to any degree of the malefics, or to their rays, take what is between the Hyleg and the degree of the malefic through the ascensions in the city in which the child was born, in degrees and minutes; and for every degree it yields, assign one year. The method for this is that you take from the first minute of the sign of Aries up to the degree and minute in which the Hyleg is, by the ascensions of that same city. Again, you take from the first minute of Aries up to the degree and minute in which the malefic and its rays were, and you take the remainder that is between them—that is, you subtract the smaller from the larger—and what remains from that is the length between them, and you assign one year to each degree; and this is the work of the Hyleg. And now I have many times repeated to you in this book, in order to know the state of the native, that you should always direct the degree of the Ascendant in nativities, because it is the "divider" itself, which is called the *Algerbuthar* [[notes: A Latinized Persian term for the "allotter" or "divider" of years in a lifespan calculation.]]. After this, look at what remains to him until he completes his term of degrees and minutes, and assign them by ascensions, one year for each degree. Then look, when the term is completed, at how many degrees the lord of the second term has, because you assign those also by ascensions: because it will dismiss years according to the number of those degrees. And when the division is in the rays of a fortune, and it is the divider, there will be tranquility and abundance in those years, or a largeness of life, and it pertains to the end of those things which it signified of good, when the degree reaches the degree of the fortune, if God wills. Similarly, do this until the work of the life is completed. Regarding the diversity of the *Alcochoden* [[notes: The planet that "rules" the Hyleg and is used to determine the specific number of years a person might live.]], Dorotheus [[notes: Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Hellenistic astrologer.]] said that if one planet has three dignities [[notes: "Dignities" are a planet's strength based on its position in the zodiac.]] and another has one, and the lord of the one aspects [the point], but the lord of the three does not aspect it, the one that aspects it would be more worthy. Ptolemy [[notes: Claudius Ptolemy, the most famous astronomer/astrologer of antiquity.]], however, said that whichever has more dignity will be more worthy and attentive, whether it aspects or not.

of the king, or of the wealthy, you shall direct them from the degree of the Midheaven [[notes: *Medium Coeli*, the highest point in the sky at birth, representing status]] through the ascensions of the direct sky for every 59 minutes and 8 seconds [[notes: This specific measurement represents the average daily motion of the Sun, used here to equate a tiny arc of the sky to one day of life]] until it reaches the malefics [[notes: Traditionally Saturn or Mars]], or for the fortunes [[notes: Traditionally Jupiter or Venus]], for one day. And in the revolution of the years of the world, for the common people and the peasants, you shall direct from the degree of the Ascendant to the malefics and fortunes, for every 59 minutes and 8 seconds for one day. And to know the state of the king from the degree of the Midheaven to the fortunes and malefics for every 59 minutes and 8 seconds. 

And in the revolution of the years of nativities [[notes: A "Solar Return" chart, cast on one's birthday]], you shall direct to know the state of the years of the native from the degree of the Ascendant to the fortunes and malefics for every 59 minutes and 8 seconds for one day. And when the "perfection" [[notes: *Profectio*, a technique where the chart is "rotated" by one sign per year]] reaches the fortunes of the sign, it signifies safety, prosperity, and progress. And when it reaches the malefics, it signifies sickness, loss, and a state of turmoil, if God wills it. From the profection in the revolution of the years of the native, you should look from the degree at which the profection arrives from the Ascendant, for every 30 degrees, one year. 

After this, you shall place from the degree at which the year arrives up to the completion of 30 degrees for the whole year; that is, you shall give 30 degrees to the whole year. Then you shall see how many degrees are between the degree at which the year arrives and the degree of the fortune or the malefic; and you shall take the remainder that is between them, and you shall multiply them by the 60ths and 70ths of a whole unit, and according to the quantity of those degrees you shall take from the days. And when there is a conjunction of the degree with a malefic, there will be hardship and a bad state of life; and when it reaches the fortunes, according to the quantity of that same number multiplied twelve times, it signifies the abundance and expansion of his being, and the balance of his temperament and his health, according to the quantity of the nature of that fortune in the circle. That is, if it is the Lord of Substance [[notes: The planet ruling the 2nd House of wealth]], it signifies wealth; and if it is the Lord of the House of the Queen, it signifies the kingdom or a house from the king.

### **M**essahallach said: When a king or a prince moves, and Mars is in the second house from the Ascendant, it indicates to him that he will have loss in those things which pertain to God [[notes: Possibly referring to religious duties or ecclesiastical property]], specifically in his relatives and children, or in his kingdom and substance. For this detriment will enter upon him from the contention of wars or by fire. If, however, it is Saturn, it will be what I said but from thieves or shipwreck, or sickness. 

But if the malefic is "received" [[notes: "Reception" occurs when a planet is in a sign or dignity ruled by another planet, suggesting cooperation]], it will not hinder him here; there will be some mention of it, but it will not be fulfilled, and things will improve. If, truly, it is not received, or is in its "fall" [[notes: *Dejectio/Descensio*, a sign where the planet is weakest]], it will be manifest and magnified until it is heard of by everyone—and all the more strongly if the planet is retrograde, because that signifies dissolution and destruction. Similarly, a fortune signifies fitness and good praise.

### **M**essahallach also said: In the election and constitution of princes [[notes: "Electional astrology" is the practice of picking the best time to start an endeavor]], when the Lord of the House of the Moon is retrograde, it signifies the hatred of the soldiers and the citizens of the region toward the one who is chosen when the prince enters upon his work. 

Furthermore, the years of life are from the **Alcochoden** [[notes: The planet that "gives" the number of years a person will live, based on the *Hylech* or "Giver of Life"]], according to what I shall tell you. Look at the planet which rules the **hylech**; if it is in its own house, or its exaltation, or its triplicity in the Midheaven, or in the Ascendant, or in the 11th house when it is a day-birth, and in the night—that is, in such strength in a day-chart in the 4th and 5th houses—it signifies its [greater] years. And if it is a "peregrine" [[notes: A planet with no essential dignity; a "stranger" in its current sign]] and western [[notes: Setting after the Sun]] in these places, it signifies its lesser years. 

And know that being peregrine, or "setting," or retrogradation, or "combustion" [[notes: Being so close to the Sun that its power is "burnt up"]] does not hurt the higher planets [[notes: Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars]] as much as it hurts the lower planets [[notes: Venus, Mercury, and the Moon]]. When, however, the higher planets are hindered by a heavy impediment, it signifies months or days instead of the number of their lesser years. When, however, the **Alcochoden** is outside—that is, the [ruling] house and these other places—in the "angles" or "succedent" houses [[notes: The houses of the chart that follow the four corners or angles]], it signifies its years whether it is peregrine or in whatever state it may be, unless it is combust: because combustion signifies a shortness of life. And if the **Alcochoden** is in the "cadent" houses [[notes: The weaker houses that "fall away" from the angles]], it signifies its lesser years. And in whatever way it signifies years, according to the quantity of those years, they will be days or months. If, however, it is combust, it signifies days or hours instead of the number of its lesser years, and some of them die and shall not taste life. And especially when the **Alcochoden** itself and the Ascendant are hindered by some impediment—that is, if they are hindered by malefics, and the Moon is hindered in the angles by malefics.
